body: [Lemma 2 of arXiv:2511.05218, 'On the Color Discrepancy of Spanning Trees in Random and Randomly Perturbed Graphs'] For any $d=d(n)=o(n),\,\alpha\in(0,1)$ and graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $\delta(G)\geq\alpha n$, there exists $U\subset V(G)$ such that $|U|=o(n)$ and each component of $G[V(G)\backslash U]$ is $d$ -connected and contains at least $\frac{\alpha}{2}n$ vertices.

[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2608.26300, 'Coordinate-Deletion Bundles from Composition Algebras: Hopf Defects, $KO$-Classes, and Rea'] The coordinate-deletion construction defines a continuous
	semialgebraic oriented rank-eight bundle
	\[
	E_{\Oct}\longrightarrow\RP^8
	\]
	with the following properties:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item $E_{\Oct}$ is trivial on the complement of the nine coordinate
		points by the matrix-determined trivialization $M_i^{-1}$;
		\item relative to the fixed coordinate and basis conventions, every
		coordinate point has local clutching map
		\[
		\sigma:S^7\longrightarrow\SO(8),\qquad u\longmapsto L_u,
		\]
		the standard octonionic Hopf clutching map associated with
		$S^7\to S^{15}\to S^8$;
		\item
		\[
		w(E_{\Oct})=1+x^8,
		\qquad w_8(E_{\Oct})=x^8\ne0;
		\]
		\item
		\[
		[E_{\Oct}]-8=8\bigl([\gamma]-1\bigr)
		\quad\text{in }\widetilde{\KO}(\RP^8);
		\]
		\item the stable identification cancels, and
		\[
		E_{\Oct}\cong\gamma^{\oplus8};
		\]
		\item the local map $\sigma$ is one of the two classical generators in
		\[
		\pi_7(\SO(8))\cong\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z,
		\]
		and its stabilization is a generator of
		$\pi_7(\SO)\cong\mathbb Z$.
	\end{enumerate}

DRAFT proof (unaudited), T421-W706-003 v1. For scalar uncorrected full-batch Adam on f(x)=lambda*x^2/2, lambda>0, eta>0, beta1=9/10, beta2=999/1000 and epsilon>0 outside the square root, put rho=epsilon/(eta lambda). For 0<rho<1/38 the known sign-alternating cycle has amplitude |x|=eta*(1/38-rho), momentum m=opposite-sign lambda*|x|/19, and v=lambda^2*x^2. Its local linear stability holds exactly when 358811/13673160 < rho < 1/38. For 0<rho<358811/13673160 it is linearly unstable; equality is a nonhyperbolic boundary. Therefore epsilon=eta and both eigenvalues of a positive diagonal quadratic in (38,13673160/358811) give locally attracting product cycles with eta active curvature and eta top sharpness tending to 38 in their full-state basin. This does not prove entry from standard m0=v0=0. With epsilon=eta^p, p>1, fixed lambda makes this particular cycle unstable for all sufficiently small eta. This does not exclude tracking by other attractors.

This concerns a whole epsilon/step ratio interval, but NOT the dossier's

Let beta1=9/10, beta2=999/1000 and f(x)=lambda*x^2/2, lambda>0.
Put X=x/eta, M=m/(eta lambda), V=v/(eta lambda)^2, rho=epsilon/(eta lambda).
Uncorrected Adam becomes
 M'=b M+(1-b)X, V'=d V+(1-d)X^2,

For 0<rho<1/38 its sign-alternating two-cycle is
 (X,M,V)=(a,-a/19,a^2) <-> (-a,a/19,a^2), a=1/38-rho>0.
The cycle's unnormalized preconditioned curvature satisfies eta C=38 exactly.
This cycle existence is known (Fong-Yang Prop.3.1), not new work here.

The explicit local stability interval computed here is
       rho_* < rho < 1/38, rho_*=358811/13673160.
In particular at p=1 (epsilon=eta) this means
       38 < lambda < 13673160/358811.
Both eigenvalues of a two-dimensional diagonal quadratic in this open interval
give an attracting product two-cycle (either relative sign), so every trajectory
in its local state-space basin has eta C_t ->38 and eta S_t ->38.
For p>1, rho=eta^(p-1)/lambda ->0, hence the same exact two-cycle is
linearly unstable for all sufficiently small eta. This rules out assuming
that cycle's attraction; it does NOT disprove curvature tracking via other orbits.

Derivative and exact test. At the positive phase, ordering (X,M,V),
J_+ = [[-1399/500-19*rho/250, -171/5, 18981/500],
       [1/10, 9/10, 0],
       [1/19000-rho/500, 0, 999/1000]].
For R=diag(-1,-1,1), J_-=R J_+ R, so D(F^2)=J_-J_+=(RJ_+)^2.
Thus Schur stability is equivalent to all roots of
 P(z)=z^3-(28970+760rho)/10000*z^2
          +(27999-684rho)/10000*z-8991/10000
lying in the open unit disk. All coefficients and calculations are rational.

Write P=z^3+A z^2+B z+C and define
 Q(z)=(P(z)-C z^3 P(1/z))/z=q0*z^2+q1*z+q2.
Here |C|=8991/10000<1,
 q0=19161919/100000000,
 q1=-(13749844rho+37960991)/100000000,
 q2=-9(151924rho-216897)/10000000.
Schur reduction gives P Schur iff Q Schur; for a real quadratic with q0>0,
this is equivalent to q0-q2>0, q0+q2>0, Q(1)>0 and Q(-1)>0.
Their exact factors are
 q0-q2=(13673160rho-358811)/100000000,
 q0+q2=1999(19351-6840rho)/100000000,
 Q(1)=360829(1-38rho)/50000000,
 Q(-1)=1009(19rho+18990)/25000000.
Over 0<rho<1/38, only the first can fail, giving the stated interval.
At rho=rho_* a conjugate pair lies on the unit circle; no hyperbolic
attraction or instability claim is made at this boundary.

Why the Schur test applies (proof, not a numerical eigenvalue test):
For monic real P with |C|<1, on |z|=1 its reciprocal polynomial P*(z)
has |P*|=|P|. If P is Schur, Rouché applied to P-C P* shows zQ
has all three roots in the disk, so Q is Schur. Conversely,
(1-C^2)P=zQ+C Q*, where Q*(z)=z^2Q(1/z).
If Q is Schur, Rouché compares zQ and C Q* on the unit circle and
shows P is Schur. The quadratic conditions follow by mapping the disk

criterion. Necessity and sufficiency follow also directly from a real
root pair or a complex conjugate pair. The extra q0+q2>0 is redundant
given Q(1),Q(-1)>0 but retained for a standard symmetric formulation.

The first quadratic has unit root product and negative discriminant.
For 0<rho<rho_* no root can lie on the unit circle: a non-real unit pair
would imply q2=q0, and real unit roots are excluded by P(1),P(-1)!=0.
Since Schur stability fails there, a root has modulus strictly above 1.

[Definition 14 of arXiv:2609.03248, 'Connections between colored restricted $b$-ary and ordinary partitions'] Let $b\geq 2$ and $\rho\geq 1$ be integers. For each $i=1, 2, \ldots, \rho$, 
let $(z_{i,1}, z_{i,2}, \ldots)$ be an infinite sequence of parameters 
satisfying $|z_{i,j}|\leq r^j$ for a fixed real $r\geq 1$, and let $Z$ denote 
the collection of all $z_{i,j}$. Then we define the sequence
$C_b^\rho(n;Z)$ by the generating function
\begin{equation}
\sum_{n=0}^\infty C_b^\rho(n;Z)q^n =\prod_{j=0}^\infty\prod_{i=1}^\rho
\left(1+z_{i,1}q^{b^j}+z_{i,2}q^{2\cdot b^j}+z_{i,3}q^{3\cdot b^j}+\dots\right).
\end{equation}
When $z_{i,j}=1$ for all $1\leq i\leq\rho$ and $j\geq 1$, we set
$C_b^\rho(n):=C_b^\rho(n;Z)$, so that
\begin{equation}
\sum_{n=0}^\infty C_b^\rho(n)q^n =\prod_{j=0}^\infty
\left(1+q^{b^j}+q^{2\cdot b^j}+q^{3\cdot b^j}+\dots\right)^\rho
=\prod_{j=0}^\infty\frac{1}{\left(1-q^{b^j}\right)^\rho}.
\end{equation}

body:
[Definition 9 of arXiv:2506.10494, 'Geometric Jensen-Shannon Divergence Between Gaussian Measures On Hilbert Space'] [\textbf{Alpha Log-Determinant divergences between positive definite trace class operators - \cite{Minh:LogDet2016}}]
			
			Assume that {$\dim(\H) = \infty$}. For {$-1 < \alpha < 1$},
			
			the Alpha Log-Det divergence 
			
			$d^{\alpha}_{\logdet}[(A+\gamma I), (B+ \mu I)]$ between  $(A+\gamma I) > 0, (B+\mu I) > 0$,
			$A, B \in \Tr(\H)$, $\gamma,\mu \in \R$, 
			
			is defined to be
			
			\begin{align}
				&d^{\alpha}_{\logdet}
				[(A+\gamma I), (B+ \mu I)]
				\nonumber
				\\
				& = \frac{4}{1-\alpha^2}  
				\log\left[\frac{\detX\left(\frac{1-\alpha}{2}(A+\gamma I) + \frac{1+\alpha}{2}(B+\mu I)\right)}{\detX(A+\gamma I)^{\beta}\detX(B + \mu I)^{1-\beta}}\left(\frac{\gamma}{\mu}\right)^{\beta - \frac{1-\alpha}{2}}\right],
				
			\end{align}
			where {$\beta = \frac{(1-\alpha)\gamma}{(1-\alpha) \gamma + (1+\alpha)\mu}$}.
			
			
			
			
			
			
			
			
			
			
			
				
				
				
				
				
				
				
				
			
				
				
				
				
				
				
				
				
				
			
			The limiting cases $\alpha \approach \pm 1$ are defined by
			\begin{align}
				&
				
				d^{1}_{\logdet}[(A+\gamma I), (B+\mu I)] = \left(\frac{\gamma}{\mu}-1\right)\log\frac{\gamma}{\mu} 
				\nonumber
				\\
				&\;\;\;\;\;+ \trX[(B+\mu I)^{-1}(A+\gamma I) - I] - \frac{\gamma}{\mu}\log\detX[(B+\mu I)^{-1}(A+\gamma I)].
				
				
				
				\\
				&
				
				d^{-1}_{\logdet}[(A+\gamma I), (B+\mu I)] = 
				\left(\frac{\mu}{\gamma}-1\right)\log\frac{\mu}{\gamma} 
				
				\nonumber
				\\
				&+ \trX\left[(A+\gamma I)^{-1}(B+\mu I) - I\right] - \frac{\mu}{\gamma}\log\detX[(A+\gamma I)^{-1}(B+\mu I)].
				
			\end{align}
title: Definition 9 of arXiv:2506.10494

body:
[Definition Quotient graph induces by graph of arXiv:2411.11341, 'Ultra high order cumulants and quantitative CLT for polynomials in Random Matrices'] Let $G_1,\dots,G_n$ be unoriented graphs with set of vertices and edges $(V_i,E_i)$ for $1\leq i\leq n$. Let $T=(V_T,E_T)$ be an unoriented graph with set of vertices $V_T=\{G_i:1\leq i\leq n\}$. For each edge $e=\{G_i,G_j\}\in E_T$ we also consider a pair of vertices $\{v_i,v_j\}$ where $v_i$ and $v_j$ are vertices of $G_i$ and $G_j$ respectively. We denote the vertices $\{v_i,v_j\}$ associated with the edge $e\in E_T$ by $V(e)$.  
We call the triple $T=(V_T,E_T,\{V(e)\}_{e\in E_T})$ a \textit{graph of the graphs} $G_1,\dots,G_n$. We let $\pi_T\in \mathcal{P}(\cup_{i=1}^n V_i)$ be the partition given by $u$ and $v$ being in the same block of $\pi_T$ whenever there is an edge $e\in E_T$ such that $V(e)=\{u,v\}$. Let $G=\cup_{i=1}^n G_i$ be the union of the graphs, that is, the graph with set of vertices $\cup_{i=1}^n V_i$ and set of edges $\cup_{i=1}^n E_i$. The quotient graph of $G$ under $\pi_T$ denoted by $G^T$ will be called the \textit{ quotient graph induced by the graph} $T$.
title: Definition Quotient graph induces by graph of arXiv:2411.11341

[Lemma NEW-l:pre-Gron of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Consider Lipschitz diffusion  coefficients $(b,\sigma)$ as defined in Definition~(NEW-d:lip_assum of the paper). Let $\{X[x]\}_{x\in{\cal X }}$ and $\{X'[x]\}_{x\in{\cal X }}$ be two families of  continuous  processes in $\mathbb{R}^{d'}$ adapted to the filtration generated by the family of i.i.d. standard Brownian motions $\{Z_x(\cdot)\}_{x \in {\cal X }}$ in $\mathbb{R}^{d'}$ on $[0,t_0]$ 
and $\mathbb{E} [\|X[x]\|^2]<\infty$, $\mathbb{E} [\|X'[x]\|^2]<\infty$ for all  $x\in{\cal X }$.
Consider  the family of stochastic processes $\{Y[x]\}_{x\in{\cal X }}$ on $\mathbb {M} $, defined on $[0,t_0]$ by
\begin{equation}
   
Y(x,t):= Y(x,0)+\int_0^t b(t, X[x], X[N_x])\, \mathrm{d} t + \sigma(t, X[x], X[N_x])\, \mathrm{d} Z_x(t),
\end{equation}
along with the family of stochastic processes $Y'(x,t)$ on $\mathbb {M} $ defined as above but with $X'$ instead of $X$.
These processes are indexed by the vertices $x\in{\cal X }$, they utilize the graph neighborhood $N_x=\{y\in{\cal X }:y\sim x\}$ on a given graph $\Psi({\cal X })$
and they share the same initial conditions $Y(x,0)=Y'(x,0)$.
Then for any $x\in{\cal X }$ and $t\in[0,t_0]$, we have
\begin{equation}

\mathbb{E}  [\| Y[x,t] - Y'[x,t] \|^2]
\le 32\max(t,1)K_t^2\int_{0}^t \max_{y\in\mathfrak{B}_1(x)} \mathbb{E}  [\| X[y,s] - X'[y,s] \|^2]\, \mathrm{d} s,
\end{equation}
where $\mathfrak{B}_1(x)$  is graph ball on  $\Psi({\cal X })$ of radius $1$ centered at~$x$
and where $K_t$ is the Lipschitz diffusion constant given in Definition \ref
{NEW-d:lip_assum}.
title: (Pre-)Gr\"onwall inequality for interacting diffusions

body:
[campaign result 2026-09-14, Author-checked only, no independent read.] This is a restricted negative answer to the question in Chapter 4 of David Aldous and James Allen Fill's Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, unfinished monograph (2002, recompiled 2014; official source https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/RWG/book.html), recorded as intake row I0024. The question asks whether the relaxation time can be characterized exactly as an infimum over flows, that is, whether one of the chapter's flow inequalities (Sinclair's bound, the Diaconis-Stroock bound) can be made an identity. For a finite irreducible reversible transition matrix P, let its eigenvalues be 1=lambda_1>lambda_2>=... and define the relaxation time tau_2=1/(1-lambda_2), equivalently the inverse spectral gap of the rate-one continuous-time generator P-I. Suppose Q(P) is the finite attained optimum of a finite linear program in flow variables whose objective and constraint coefficients are well-defined rational functions, with rational coefficients, of the entries of P. If P has rational entries, then Q(P) is rational. Such a rule cannot equal tau_2 for every rational reversible P. The witness is the simple walk on the path P_6 with vertices 0,...,5, which moves deterministically at the endpoints and with probability 1/2 to each neighbor in the interior. It has lambda_2=cos(pi/5)=(1+sqrt(5))/4 and tau_2=3+sqrt(5), which is irrational. A genuinely nonlinear flow characterization is not excluded. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
The flow optimization is finite, feasible, has finite optimum, and has rational data on rational P.
tau_2 uses the second-largest eigenvalue, not the absolute spectral radius.

[Definition def:dc-clean-dressing of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] We say that $K \colon \mathcal V \to \mathrm{End}(H)$ is \emph{dressing
compatible} with $(\Psi,\Phi)$ if: 
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*., leftmargin=*]
\item For every $u \in \mathcal{V}$,
\begin{align}
\partial_2K(u)
&= \Psi(u)\Phi(u),
 \\
\partial_1K(u)
&= \frac{1}{2}\bigl(\partial_2\Psi(u)\Phi(u)
   -\Psi(u)\partial_2\Phi(u)\bigr)
   +\Psi(u)C_1(u)\Phi(u),
 \\
K(S_3u)-K(u)
&= \Psi(u)C_2(u)\Phi(S_3u),

\end{align}
\item There exists $z \in \mathbb{F}$ such that the resolvent
exists at every vertex:
\[
R(u) \vcentcolon= (I - zK(u))^{-1} \in \mathrm{End}(H),
\qquad u \in \mathcal{V}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition def:dc-clean-dressing of arXiv:2608.02772

[Theorem 10 (Net with Hilbert--Schmidt approximation) of arXiv:2608.30722, 'Intermediate Singular Values of Random Matrices\\ under Second-Moment and Anti-Concentrati'] There exists an absolute constant $C_{\mathrm{net}}>0$ such that for every integer $m\ge1$ and every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ there exists a deterministic set
\[
  \mathcal N_\varepsilon
  \subset
  \frac32 B_2^m\setminus \frac12 B_2^m
\]
with
\[
  |\mathcal N_\varepsilon|
  \le
  \left(\frac{C_{\mathrm{net}}}{\varepsilon}\right)^m
\]
and the following approximation property: for every matrix $M$ with $m$ columns and every $y\in S^{m-1}$ there exists $y_i\in\mathcal N_\varepsilon$ such that
\begin{equation}
  \|M(y-y_i)\|_2
  \le
  \frac{\sqrt2\,\varepsilon}{\sqrt m}\|M\|_{HS}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem th:split:dynamical of arXiv:2608.19358, 'An optimal Poincaré inequality\\for the complex Ginibre log-gas'] Assume that $n\geq2$. Let $v$, $L$, and $L^\perp$ be as in Theorem
  (th:split of the paper). Consider the processes ${(S_t)}_{t\geq0}$ and
  ${(W_t)}_{t\geq0}$ with state space $\mathbb{C}$ and $L^\perp$ defined by
  \[
    S_tv=\operatorname{proj}_L(Z_t^n)=\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^n Z_t^{n,j}\Bigr)v
    \quad\text{and}\quad
    W_t=\operatorname{proj}_{L^\perp}(Z_t^n)=Z_t^n-\frac{S_t}{n}(1,\ldots,1)
  \]
  where $(Z_t^n)_{t\geq0}$ is the solution of (equation eq:intro-sde of the paper). Then there
  exist independent Brownian motions $B^S$ on $\mathbb{C}$ and $B^W$ on
  $L^\perp$ such that ${(S_t)}_{t\geq0}$ and ${(W_t)}_{t\geq0}$ solve the
  stochastic differential equations
  \begin{equation}
    \mathrm{d}S_t=\sqrt{\frac{2\alpha_n}{n}}\mathrm{d}B_t^S-\frac{2\alpha_n}{n}S_t\mathrm{d}t
    \quad\text{and}\quad
    \mathrm{d}W_t
    =
    \frac{\sqrt{2\alpha_n}}{n}\,\mathrm{d}B_t^W
    -\frac{2\alpha_n}{n}W_t\,\mathrm{d}t
    +\frac{2\alpha_n}{n^2}b(W_t)\,\mathrm{d}t,
  \end{equation}
  where $b_j(w)=\sum_{k\neq j}\frac{w_j-w_k}{|w_j-w_k|^2}$. In particular
  ${(S_t)}_{t\geq0}$ is a complex Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process and the
  transition semigroup of $Z^n$ is the product of the semigroups of
  ${(S_t)}_{t\geq0}$ and ${(W_t)}_{t\geq0}$. In particular, ${(S_t)}_{t\geq0}$
  and ${(W_t)}_{t\geq0}$ are independent whenever $S_0$ and $W_0$ are
  independent. Moreover, if we define
  \begin{equation}
    U_t=|S_t|^2,
    \quad
    R_t=n|W_t|^2
    =\sum_{1\leq j<k\leq n}|Z_t^{n,j}-Z_t^{n,k}|^2,
    \quad
    \kappa=\frac{(n-1)(n+2)}{2}.
  \end{equation}
  then there exist independent real Brownian motions $\beta^S$ and $\beta^R$
  such that ${(U_t)}_{t\geq0}$ and ${(R_t)}_{t\geq0}$ solve
  \begin{equation}
    \mathrm{d}U_t
    =
    \frac{4\alpha_n}{n}(1-U_t)\mathrm{d}t +2\sqrt{\frac{2\alpha_n}{n}U_t}\mathrm{d}\beta_t^S
    \quad\text{and}\quad
    \mathrm{d}R_t
    =
    \frac{4\alpha_n}{n}(\kappa-R_t)\mathrm{d}t +2\sqrt{\frac{2\alpha_n}{n}R_t}\mathrm{d}\beta_t^R.
  \end{equation}
  In particular ${(U_t)}_{t\geq0}$ and ${(R_t)}_{t\geq0}$ are
  Cox--Ingersoll--Ross processes with invariant distributions
  $\operatorname{Gamma}(1,1)$ and $\operatorname{Gamma}(\kappa,1)$,
  respectively. Furthermore, in the stationary case where $Z_0^n\sim\mu_n$,
  the processes $(S_t)_{t\geq0}$ and $(W_t)_{t\geq0}$, and hence
  ${(U_t)}_{t\geq0}$ and ${(R_t)}_{t\geq0}$, are independent and stationary.

[Proposition 5 of arXiv:2609.00209, 'Exit Times for Brownian Motion and Location Detection'] Let $\mathcal E_n$ denote the elliptic domain
\[
\mathcal E_n=\left\{(x,y)\in \mathbb{R}^2:\frac{2cx^2}{n}+\frac{(y-n)^2}{n^2}<1\right\}.
\]
Then $\mathcal E_n \subseteq \mathcal E_{n+1}$ for each $n\geq 1$ and $\bigcup\limits_{n=1}^{\infty} \mathcal E_n=\mathcal P$.

[Corollary 41 (Monomial Gaussian row) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] Let
\[
 F_{m,t}(x)=-\frac{x^2}{2}+\frac{it}{m}x^m,
 \qquad t>0,
\]
and orient the physical contour from \(-\infty\) to \(+\infty\).  Label
the decay sectors counterclockwise by the centres
\[
 \theta_j=\frac{\pi/2+2\pi j}{m},
 \qquad 0\leq j<m,
\]
using the Gaussian lateral prescription at the two boundary directions,
and put \(\ell=\lfloor m/2\rfloor\).  If \(L_j\) is an oriented
half-contour from a common finite base point to \(E_j\), define the
adjacent sector basis
\[
 \Gamma_j=-L_j+L_{j+1},
 \qquad 0\leq j\leq m-2.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 [\R]
 =
 L_0-L_\ell
 =
 -\sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1}[\Gamma_j].
 
\end{equation}
Hence in this basis the complete physical Betti row is
\[
 C_{\R}^{\mathrm{adj}}
 =
 (-1,\ldots,-1,0,\ldots,0),
\]
with exactly \(\ell\) entries equal to \(-1\).  If a distinguished
Lefschetz basis satisfies
\(\boldsymbol\Gamma^{\mathrm{th}}
=V\boldsymbol\Gamma^{\mathrm{adj}}\) with
\(V\in\operatorname{GL}_{m-1}(\mathbb Z)\), then
\begin{equation}
 C_{\R}^{\mathrm{th}}
 =
 C_{\R}^{\mathrm{adj}}V^{-1}.
 
\end{equation}

body:
[Corollary 12 (Mesh-point \(L^1\)-convergence) of arXiv:2608.16256, 'Error Distribution of the Local Linearization Method for Stochastic Differential Equations'] \label[corollary]{cor:local_L1_conv_mesh}
Let \(T>0\), and put
\[
    \varphi_n(s)
    \coloneqq
    \frac{\lfloor ns\rfloor}{n},
    \qquad
    0\le s\le T .
\]
Let \(Y^n\) and \(Y\) be measurable \(\mathbb R^d\)-valued processes on
\([0,T]\), and let \(h:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be continuous.  Assume that
\[
    \sup_{s\le T}|Y_s^n-Y_s|
    \xrightarrow{P}0,
    \qquad
    \sup_{s\le T}|Y_s^n-Y_{\varphi_n(s)}^n|
    \xrightarrow{P}0,
\]
and
\[
    \lim_{\rho\uparrow\infty}
    \limsup_{n\to\infty}
    \Prob*{P}{
        \sup_{s\le T}
        (|Y_s^n|\vee |Y_s|)>\rho
    }
    =
    0 .
\]
Then
\[
    \int_0^T
    |h(Y_{\varphi_n(s)}^n)-h(Y_s)|\,ds
    \xrightarrow{P}0 .
\]
Consequently,
\[
    \sup_{t\le T}
    \left|
        \int_0^t h(Y_{\varphi_n(s)}^n)\,ds
        -
        \int_0^t h(Y_s)\,ds
    \right|
    \xrightarrow{P}0 .
\]

    \theta_v^f=\frac{A+B}{2}.

[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2607.09246, 'Scaling limit of 1+1 dimensional directed polymer with power-law tail and spatial correlat'] Let \(\tau_N>0\).  Assume that, for all large \(N\), Lemma
\ref{lem:far-product-section2} can be applied at the scale \(h_1\).  Put
\[
        s_{1,N}:=C_{\mathrm{near}}\beta_NN|\mu_N|h_1^{1-r},
\]
where \(C_{\mathrm{near}}\) is fixed large enough that
\eqref{eq:near-centered-only-section2} implies
\[
        |\beta_N\Delta H_N^{\mathrm{near},h_1}(S)|
        \le s_{1,N},
        \qquad S\in\mathcal B_1,
\]
on \(A_{h_1}^c\).  When \(s_{1,N}\le1\), 
then, for every fixed \(\varepsilon,\delta>0\),
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb Q(F_N>\varepsilon\tau_N)
&\le
\mathbb Q(G_N(\delta)^c)
+
\mathbb Q(A_{h_1})
+
\mathbb Q(D_{h_1})                                     
+
\frac{C}{\delta\varepsilon\tau_N}
\left(s_{1,N}+\sqrt{\mathfrak d_N(h_1)}\right),
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}

body:
Let $S = \sum_i \lambda_i u_i u_i^T$ be the sample covariance of $n$ observations in $\mathbb{R}^p$ with population covariance $\Sigma$, $p/n \to c \in (0, 1)$, in the setting of the Marchenko-Pastur-Silverstein theorem. Consider rotation-equivariant estimators $\hat\Sigma = \sum_i d_i u_i u_i^T$ and the global minimum-variance portfolio $\hat w = \hat\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{1}/(\mathbf{1}^T\hat\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{1})$ built from them, scored by its true out-of-sample variance $\hat w^T \Sigma \hat w$. Ledoit and Wolf (2017) show: (i) the finite-sample oracle for this loss is $d_i^{\mathrm{mv}} = 1 / (u_i^T \Sigma^{-1} u_i)$ (the 'inverse' oracle), whereas the Frobenius-loss oracle is $d_i^{\mathrm{fro}} = u_i^T \Sigma u_i$; (ii) in the large-dimensional limit both oracles converge to the SAME nonlinear shrinkage $\tilde d_i = \lambda_i / |1 - c - c\lambda_i \breve m_F(\lambda_i)|^2$ (the Ledoit-Peche formula), because the Ledoit-Peche limits of the two quadratic forms $u_i^T\Sigma u_i$ and $u_i^T\Sigma^{-1}u_i$ are reciprocal to each other; so the nonlinear shrinkage estimator that is optimal for estimating the covariance in Frobenius loss is also asymptotically optimal for the minimum-variance portfolio - neither too much shrinkage (the linear shrinkage's) nor too little (the sample covariance's). In the ensemble-stacking application, this is the statement that the Ledoit-Peche cleaning of the error covariance is the right cleaning for the sum-to-one (unconstrained-sign) stack, whose weights are exactly a global minimum-variance portfolio.
the Marchenko-Pastur-Silverstein setting (i.i.d. rows with finite twelfth moments in Ledoit-Wolf's statement), p/n -> c in (0, 1)
estimators restricted to the rotation-equivariant class (sample eigenvectors kept)
the identity making the two oracles' limits reciprocal is cited from the paper, not re-derived above

[Lemma Lem:intersec_of_An of arXiv:2609.01501, 'Singularities of star cluster algebras'] Let $ n \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}_{\geq 2} $ be a positive integer with $ n \geq 2 $. 
	For $ a \in \{ 1, \ldots, n \} $, let
	\[
		g_a (\boldsymbol{t}^{(a)}) := \sum_{i=1}^{q_a} t_{2i-1}^{(a)} t_{2i}^{(a)} \in \kappa [\boldsymbol{t}^{(a)}] = \kappa [t_1^{(a)}, \ldots, t_{2q_a}^{(a)}]
	\]
	be the polynomial defining an $ A_1 $-hypersurface singularity in $ \Spec (\kappa [\boldsymbol{t}^{(a)}]) \cong \ensuremath{\mathbb{A}}_\kappa^{2q_a} $. 
	Let 
	\[
		\mathcal{X} :=  \mathcal{X}^{(n)} := V ( g_a (\boldsymbol{t}^{(a)}) - g_b (\boldsymbol{t}^{(b)}) \mid a, b \in \{ 1, \ldots, n\} )
		\subset \ensuremath{\mathbb{A}}_\kappa^{2(q_1+ \cdots + q_n)} =: \mathcal{Z} 
		\ .
	\] 
	Define $ \mathcal{Y}_0 \subset  \mathcal{Y}_1 \subset  \cdots \subset \mathcal{Y}_{n-2} \subset \mathcal{X} $
	by
	\[
		\mathcal{Y}_j 
		\ := \
		\mathcal{Y}_j^{(n)} 
		\ := 
		\bigcup_{(a_1, \ldots, a_{n-j})}
		\Big( V(\boldsymbol{t}^{(a_1)}, \ldots, \boldsymbol{t}^{(a_{n-j})}) \cap \mathcal{X} \Big)  
		\ , 
	\]
	where the union ranges over all $ (n-j) $-tuples $ (a_1, \ldots, a_{n-j}) $
	with $ a_1 < a_2 < \cdots < a_{n-j} $. 
	\\
	The following sequence of blow-ups is an embedded resolution of singularities for $ \mathcal{X} $:
	\[
		\mathcal{Z}_{n-1} \stackrel{\pi_{n-2}}{\longrightarrow}
		\cdots 
		\stackrel{\pi_2}{\longrightarrow}
		\mathcal{Z}_2 \stackrel{\pi_1}{\longrightarrow}
		\mathcal{Z}_1 \stackrel{\pi_0}{\longrightarrow}
		\mathcal{Z}
		\ , 
	\]
	where $ \pi_0 $ is the blow-up with center $ \mathcal{Y}_0 $
	and $ \pi_j \colon \mathcal{Z}_{j+1} \to \mathcal{Z}_{j} $ is the blow-up with center the strict transform of $ \mathcal{Y}_j $ in $ \mathcal{Z}_{j} $, for $ j \in \{ 1, \ldots, n-2 \} $. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 1 of arXiv:2607.16479, 'The Site Frequency Spectrum in an Exponentially-Growing Population with Selection'] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$ be a probability space and consider jointly-measurable, stochastic processes $X_t$ and $Y_t$. We further take $X_t$ to be non-negative and non-decreasing a.s. Suppose there exists $\lambda>0$ such that $e^{-\lambda t}Y_t \to \widetilde{Y}_\infty$ almost surely, where $\widetilde{Y}_\infty$ is a.s. finite and non-negative. If, in addition, the following condition is satisfied:

  \[\int_0^\infty \mathbb{E}[e^{-\lambda t}|X_t-Y_t|]dt<\infty\]
then $e^{-\lambda t}X_t\to \widetilde{Y}_\infty$ a.s.

[Proposition prop:xex of arXiv:2605.15545, 'Crossover from subcritical to critical decay: \\ random walk, self-avoiding walk, percolat'] Let $d=1$ and $p>  1$.
Consider the kernel
\begin{equation} 
D(x) = \frac{c_p}{|x|^p}e^{-|x|} \1\{x\neq 0\} ,
\end{equation}
where $c_p$ is the normalising constant.
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] [AIOV21PRE]
There exists $z_0 > 0$ such that for all $z \in (0, z_0)$,
\begin{equation} 
zD(x) \le S_z(x) \le 2 zD(x)
\qquad(x\ne 0).
\end{equation}

\item[(ii)]
Let $z_{\rm sat} = 1/ \sum_{x\in \mathbb{Z}} D(x) e^{x}  \in (0,1)$.
For every $z \in (z_{\rm sat}, 1)$,
Assumptions~(ass:Omega of the paper) and~(ass:J of the paper) hold.
If $p > 3$,
then Assumptions~(ass:Omega of the paper) and~(ass:J of the paper) also hold for $z=z_{\rm sat}$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2606.14564, 'Upper tails for irregular graphs \\ beyond the mean-field regime'] For every irregular, connected graph $H$ with maximum degree $\Delta \ge 2$ and all $0 < \varepsilon < \delta$, there is a constant $K$ such that the following holds.
  For all $p_H \cdot (\log n)^K \le p \ll 1$ and all large enough $n$,
  \[
    (1-\varepsilon) \cdot \psi_H^*(\delta-\varepsilon) \le - \log \Pr\big(X_H \ge (1+\delta)\Ex[X_H]\big) \le (1+\varepsilon) \cdot \psi_H^*(\delta+\varepsilon).
  \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:absolute-row-sum-sharpness of arXiv:2609.03264, 'Certified Spherical MUSIC for 3D Localization under Adversarial Subspace Perturbations'] There exists an absolute constant \(c>0\) such that, for arbitrarily
large \(s\), one can find a separated point cloud
\(X\subset B_1(0)\) and a wavenumber \(\kappa\) satisfying
\[
    \kappa\delta_X\asymp s^{2/3}
\]
and
\[
    \max_{\bm{x}\in X}
    \sum_{\substack{\bm{y}\in X\\\bm{y}\ne\bm{x}}}
    |K_\kappa(\bm{x}-\bm{y})|
    \ge c.
\]
More generally, the exponent \(2/3\) cannot be replaced by any
\(p<2/3\) in a uniform estimate of the form
\[
    \max_{\bm{x}\in X}
    \sum_{\substack{\bm{y}\in X\\\bm{y}\ne\bm{x}}}
    |K_\kappa(\bm{x}-\bm{y})|
    \lesssim
    \frac{s^p}{\kappa\delta_X}.
\]

[Theorem thm:first_coef_kernel of arXiv:2607.04514, 'Boundary-layer asymptotics for Gaussian-smoothed singular measures'] Let \(A>0\) and assume (ass:standing of the paper) with \(r\geqslant 1\). Then there exists \(\sigma_0 >
  0\) such that, for every \((y,\sigma)\in\mathcal Y_{A,\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}},\sigma_0}\), \(x=\pi(y)\),
  \(a = a(y,\sigma)\), it holds that
  \begin{align*}
    p_\sigma(y) &= \sigma^{-k}(2\pi)^{-d/2} \left[ \mathsf C_0(a,x)
    + \sigma\mathscr E_0(a,x,\sigma) \right], \\
    \log p_\sigma(y) &= - k\log\sigma - (d/2)\log (2\pi) + \mathsf L_0(a,x)
    + \sigma\mathscr E_{0, \log} (a,x,\sigma),
  \end{align*}
  where \(\mathsf L_0(a,x)=\log \mathsf C_0(a,x)\), and \(\mathscr E_0(a,x,\sigma)\), \(\mathscr
  E_{0,\log}(a,x,\sigma)\) have all mixed derivatives up to order \(r-1\), in the variables \((a,
  x,\sigma)\), uniformly bounded for \(x\in\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}\), \(\|a\|\leqslant A\), and
  \(0<\sigma\leqslant\sigma_0\). Derivatives in \(x\) are computed in the stratum coordinate
  \(\theta\), after writing \(x=\Phi(\theta,0)\); throughout, the precise meaning of these mixed
  derivatives in \((a,x,\sigma)\) --- over the closed ball in \(a\), and by pullback in \(\theta\)
  --- is fixed in (rem:parameter_variable_derivatives of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:encodeclosedorbit of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] Let \(F\) be a closed face of \(\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{Fr}}(\varphi)\) and let \(F^{\vee}\) be its dual open face in \(\mathcal{C}_{2}(\varphi)\).
Assume that \(\gamma\) is a closed orbit of \(\varphi\).
Then \([\gamma]\in F\) if and only if \(\gamma\) can be isotopic into \(\mathrm{Guts}(F^{\vee})\).
Equivalently, \([\gamma]\in F\) if and only if \(\pi_{1}(\gamma)\) and \(\pi_{1}(\mathrm{Guts}(F^{\vee}))\), as conjugate classes, have nonempty intersection.

body:
Consider i.i.d. first-passage percolation on Z^d, d >= 2, with edge-weight law nu. Assume the two conditions (i) E min{ t_1^d, ..., t_{2d}^d } < infinity, where the t_i are 2d independent copies of tau_e - equivalently E[Y^d] < infinity where Y is the MINIMUM of 2d copies, the two being the same because x -> x^d is increasing on [0, infinity) - and (ii) F(0) < p_c(d). Let B(t) = {x : T(0, x) <= t}, the random ball. Then there is a DETERMINISTIC, convex, COMPACT set B_nu in R^d with NON-EMPTY INTERIOR, symmetric about the axes, such that for every eps > 0, P( (1-eps) B_nu is contained in B(t)/t which is contained in (1+eps) B_nu for all large t ) = 1. The set B_nu is the unit ball of the time constant. Condition (i) is NOT merely convenient: if it fails then for every C > 0 the sum over x of P(m(x) > C|x|) diverges, where m(x) is the minimum weight over the edges at x, and Borel-Cantelli forces T(0,x)/|x| > C for infinitely many x almost surely, so the shape statement itself fails. Condition (ii) is what keeps the shape bounded: if F(0) >= p_c then zero-weight edges percolate, the time constant vanishes and B_nu is all of R^d. What is NOT known, and is repeatedly imported elsewhere as an unproven hypothesis: whether the boundary of B_nu is STRICTLY CONVEX, whether it is DIFFERENTIABLE, and whether it has uniformly positive CURVATURE. Those are open for every non-degenerate weight distribution in every dimension, which is why the Newman-Piza exponent bounds and the directed-geodesic results carry non-constructive curvature or differentiability hypotheses. B_nu is not computed explicitly for any non-trivial F. [Cox and Durrett (1981), verified against Auffinger, Damron and Hanson, 50 Years of First-Passage Percolation, Section 2.2]

F(0) < p_c(d), so the time constant is a norm and the shape is bounded
E min{t_1^d, ..., t_{2d}^d} < infinity, equivalently E[Y^d] < infinity for Y the minimum of 2d independent copies of tau_e - and this condition is necessary, not just sufficient
no curvature, strict convexity or differentiability of B_nu is asserted; those are open

Erdos (1947): R(k,k) > 2^{k/2} for every k >= 3. Colour the edges of the complete graph on n vertices red or blue independently and uniformly at random. The expected number of monochromatic k-cliques is C(n,k) 2^{1 - C(k,2)}; when n = floor(2^{k/2}) this expectation is below 1 for k >= 3, so some colouring has no monochromatic k-clique, and R(k,k) > n. This is the first-moment method (a union bound over the C(n,k) cliques); only linearity of expectation is used, and no clique needs to be independent of another. With Stirling's formula the same count gives R(k,k) >= (1 + o(1)) (k / (e sqrt 2)) 2^{k/2}; the Lovasz local lemma (Spencer 1975) improves the constant to (1 + o(1)) (sqrt 2 / e) k 2^{k/2} and nothing better than the exponent k/2 is known. The upper bound side is separate: R(k,k) <= 4^k from Erdos-Szekeres, improved to (4 - epsilon)^k by Campos, Griffiths, Morris and Sahasrabudhe (2023).
k >= 3 (for k = 2 the bound is trivial)
the random colouring is uniform and independent over edges; the argument uses only the expectation
the bound is on the diagonal Ramsey number; the off-diagonal case R(3,k) has a different order, of k^2 / log k

[Lemma lem:h-bernoulli-decomposition of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a send sequence $\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$. Let $j\ge 1$ be an integer, and suppose $j$ is sufficiently large. Fix an integer $\tau \ge 0$, a real number $\nu\ge 0$, and $\overline{a} \in (\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0})^j$. Let $E^+$ be a constant-escape process on $[j]$ with send sequence~$\overline{p}$, start time $\tau$, end-of-step arrival rate $\nu$, and $\overline{\mathrm{arr}}_{[j]}^{E^+}(\tau) = \overline{a}$. Then for all integers $t_1$ and $t_2$ with

[Theorem 12 of arXiv:2605.24445, 'Matrix concentration inequalities for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains'] \label[theorem]{thm:elo_augmented_point}
Let \(B\coloneqq 2\sqrt2\,\eta+2h_\rho+4\sqrt2\,h_q\).  There exists a
universal constant \(C>0\) such that, for every \(\epsilon>0\), if the burn-in
time satisfies
\[
t\ge C\kappa^{-1}\log(nM\epsilon^{-1}\eta^{-1}),
\]
then
\[
\Pbb\left(
\begin{aligned}
\|X^t-\rho^t\|_2
&\ge
\sqrt{\frac{\Delta}{\kappa}}
+(1+\epsilon)\sqrt{\frac{2\eta^2}{\kappa}}
+C\epsilon\,\frac{B}{\sqrt\kappa}
\end{aligned}
\right)
\le
2e^{-\epsilon^2}.
\]

[Lemma lem:weighted-subgraph-after-trimming of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] Work under the assumptions and notation of Proposition~(prop:average-degree-bridge-alternatives of the paper). Let $\delta_k\downarrow0$ and assume
\[
|B_0^{(k)}|<\delta_k n_k,
\qquad
|B_1^{(k)}|<\delta_k n_k.
\]
Fix a witness $\varepsilon_k\to0$ for \hyperref[def:local-sparse-four-cycle-incidence]{\textcolor{PineGreen}{\emph{local sparse four-cycle incidence}}}{}.
Set
\[
\widetilde n_k
:=
\min\left\{
\left\lceil c_{\ifmmode\text{\tiny(prop:produce-c4-good-subgraph of the paper)}\else{\tiny(prop:produce-c4-good-subgraph of the paper)}\fi}\varepsilon_k^{-1} k\right\rceil,
n_k
\right\}.
\]
Let
\[
\widetilde J^{(k)}\subseteq J^{(k)}
\]
be uniform with $|\widetilde J^{(k)}|=\widetilde n_k$.

Then, with probability $1-o(1)$, there is a set
$J_{\rm sub}^{(k)}\subseteq\widetilde J^{(k)}$ such that
\[
|J_{\rm sub}^{(k)}|\ge\frac23\widetilde n_k,
\]
the graph $G^{(k)}[J_{\rm sub}^{(k)}]$ is $C_4$-free, all right support
degrees in this subgraph lie between $2$ and $40d_{\rm av}$, and all its nonzero
weights have absolute value at most $10d_{\rm av}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma lem:f-track-jammed of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a positive integer~$j$, a send sequence~$\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$, a $\lambda\in (0,1)$, and a $j$-tuple $\overline{z}\in (\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0})^j$.
Fix non-negative integers~$\tau$ and~$\Delta$.
Let $Y$ be a $j$-jammed process with send sequence~$\overline{p}$, start time~$\tau$, birth rate~$\lambda$, and initial population size distribution $\mathsf{Po}(f_{[j]}^{\overline{0},\overline{z}}(\Delta))$.  

Then, for all $t\geq \tau$, 
$b_{[j]}^Y(t) \sim \mathsf{Po}(f_{[j]}^{\overline{0},\overline{z}}(\Delta+t-\tau))$.
Furthermore, the following positive correlation property holds.
Let $\mathcal{E}_1$ and $\mathcal{E}_2$ be any events 
determined by  
the random variables in 
$\{ b_\mathrm{tr}^Y \mid \mathrm{tr} \in \mathcal{T}^Y(t)\}$ such that $\mathcal{E}_2$ occurs with positive probability. 
If the indicator variables of  
$\mathcal{E}_1$ and $\mathcal{E}_2$ are increasing functions of 
these random variables   then $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E}_2 \mid \mathcal{E}_1) \geq \mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E}_2)$.

Let W,W_1,...,W_L be real D-by-D matrices, L>=1, and 1<=R<=D an integer. Put B=W_L...W_1 and E=W-B. Fix a singular value decomposition of E and use its nested truncations LR_j(E), with LR_0=0 and LR_j=E beyond the rank. Assume every W_l is nonsingular and B+LR_j(E) is nonsingular for every integer 0<=j<=R(L-1). Then min_{rank(Delta_l)<=R} ||(W_L+Delta_L)...(W_1+Delta_1)-W||_2 = sigma_(RL+1)(E), where ||.||_2 is the operator norm and singular values beyond D are zero. The minimum is attained with the product equal to B+LR_(RL)(E). In particular, R>=ceil(rank(E)/L) permits exact equality of the product with W. The target W itself need not be nonsingular unless the stated partial-sum hypothesis forces it.

Each frozen weight is invertible
All specified nested low-rank corrected full products are invertible

For the fixed $(\mathbf u,\boldsymbol{\delta})$ the space is further partitioned according to the values of $\boldsymbol{\delta}_{j,\ell}$.
 We equip each part with the product of Lebesgue measures over all parameters of blocks, except that whenever only a single value for a parameter is involved, then we assign weight $1$ for this value and for $\mathbb R_+\cup \{\varnothing\}$ in the definition of virtual blocks, $\varnothing$ comes with the Dirac delta measure of weight $1$, while $\mathbb R_+$ comes with the Lebesgue measure.

body:
[Proposition prop:edge_removal of arXiv:2608.15923, 'Universality of two-dimensional Markovian holonomy fields'] Let $\mathbb G=(V,E,F)$ be a topological map embedded in $\Sigma_{g,n}$.
Let $e$ be an internal edge incident to two distinct faces $f_1,f_2$, and
let $\mathbb G'$ be obtained by deleting $e$ and merging these faces into
$f_{12}$. Let $\mathcal R$ forget the variable attached to $e$. Then, for
every bounded measurable test function $\Phi$ on
$\Omega^1(\mathbb G',G)$,
\begin{align*}
 &\int \Phi(\mathcal R(U))\,
 d\mu_{\mathbb G,G,Q,\mathrm{vol},\mathfrak t}(U)\\
 &\quad=
 \int \Phi(U')
 (Q_{|f_1|}*Q_{|f_2|})
 \bigl(\Omega^{U'}(f_{12})\bigr)
 \prod_{f\in F'\setminus\{f_{12}\}}
 Q_{|f|}\bigl(\Omega^{U'}(f)\bigr)
 \prod_i\delta_{[t_i]}({\mathrm{Hol}}_{\partial b_i}(U'))\,dU'.
\end{align*}
In particular, if $(Q_t)_{t>0}$ is a convolution semigroup, then
\[
 \mathcal R_*\mu_{\mathbb G,G,Q,\mathrm{vol},\mathfrak t}
 =\mu_{\mathbb G',G,Q,\mathrm{vol},\mathfrak t}.
\]
If, in addition, $Q_{|f_1|+|f_2|}>0$ almost everywhere, the first identity
may equivalently be written as a Radon--Nikodym formula with quotient
$(Q_{|f_1|}*Q_{|f_2|})/Q_{|f_1|+|f_2|}$.

Rectangular spectral entropy is C1 under explicit bounded-density, spectral-gap, boundary-continuity and weak-transport hypotheses supplied by claim025. For gamma in (0,1), a=(1-gamma)/gamma, symmetric density rho_t and velocity V=H+a/(2x), E_gamma=gamma Sigma(rho_t)+(1-gamma) integral log|x|rho_t has derivative 2gamma integral V^2 rho_t=Phi_gamma(t)/2, continuous for t>0. Proof regularizes the logarithmic kernel, bounds its energy error by C*pi*epsilon, proves the smooth double-measure chain rule and passes to the boundary. This is a conditional supporting analytic lemma, not an MI-limit or full Target2 claim.
Every explicit regularity and weak transport hypothesis in the proof, including a common compact support separated from zero on compact positive heat intervals.

Claim draft w718-T287-026, version 1. Kind: moved; target: 2. Status: proof (unaudited). This is a supporting analytic lemma, not a completed MI calibration or Target 2 claim. Novelty is unestablished.

## Hypotheses and conclusion

Let gamma in (0,1), a=(1-gamma)/gamma. Suppose t maps to rho_t is a family of even probability measures on an open interval J, satisfying the conclusions of supporting claim 025. More explicitly, on every compact subinterval:

1. The laws have densities p_t, a common compact support in [-R,-epsilon] union [epsilon,R], and uniformly bounded Cauchy transforms up to the real boundary. Set H_t(x)=Re integral (x+i0-y)^(-1)rho_t(dy).
2. At each t0, p_t(x) and H_t(x) converge to p_t0(x) and H_t0(x) for almost every x as t tends to t0. Both are uniformly bounded on the common support.
3. With V_t(x)=H_t(x)+a/(2x), the integrated weak transport equation holds for every C1 test f:

integral f d rho_v-integral f d rho_u
 = integral_u^v integral f' V_t d rho_t dt.               (1)

Define Sigma(rho)=double-integral log|x-y|rho(dx)rho(dy) and

E_gamma(rho)=gamma Sigma(rho)+(1-gamma)integral log|x|rho(dx).

Then E_gamma(rho_t) is continuously differentiable and

d E_gamma(rho_t)/dt
 =2 gamma integral [H_t(x)+a/(2x)]^2 rho_t(dx)
 =Phi_gamma(t)/2,                                       (2)

where Phi_gamma(t)=4 gamma integral V_t^2 d rho_t is finite and continuous. These statements apply to the real Gaussian-product heat laws once claim 025 is accepted. They do not rely on equality of two definitions of rectangular free entropy or Fisher information.

## Smooth-kernel chain rule

Fix a compact time interval [u,v] inside J. Uniform boundedness and the gap imply |V_t|<=L on the common support. Equation (1) implies W1(rho_t,rho_s)<=L|t-s|: apply it to smooth tests of derivative norm at most one, approximate Lipschitz tests uniformly on the containing compact interval by convolution, and use the dual formula for one-dimensional W1 (equivalently its elementary distribution-function characterization).

For e>0 put K_e(x,y)=(1/2)log((x-y)^2+e^2) and Sigma_e(rho)=double-integral K_e d rho d rho. This kernel is smooth on the containing compact square. Let delta_h=rho_(t+h)-rho_t. Expanding the quadratic functional gives

Sigma_e(rho_(t+h))-Sigma_e(rho_t)
 =2 double-integral K_e(x,y)delta_h(dx)rho_t(dy)
  +double-integral K_e(x,y)delta_h(dx)delta_h(dy).         (3)

The last term is O(W1(rho_(t+h),rho_t)^2)=O(h^2). Indeed choose an optimal coupling pi of the two laws; write that term as the integral against pi tensor pi of the mixed difference K_e(x',y')-K_e(x',y)-K_e(x,y')+K_e(x,y). Its absolute value is bounded by ||partial_x partial_y K_e||infinity times integral |x'-x||y'-y|d(pi tensor pi), which equals that constant times W1^2.

The fixed test f_t(x)=integral K_e(x,y)rho_t(dy) is smooth, with derivative

f_t'(x)=H_e,t(x)=Re g(x+i e,t).

For any fixed C1 test, the right-hand integrand in (1) is continuous in time by hypothesis 2 and dominated convergence, since V_t p_t is bounded and supported in a common compact set. Hence its integral is differentiable at every t. Divide (3) by h and pass to zero to obtain

d Sigma_e(rho_t)/dt=2 integral H_e,t(x) V_t(x)rho_t(dx).  (4)

The derivative is continuous in t. For example H_e,t is jointly continuous and bounded on the compact support by weak continuity, which follows from (1), while V_t p_t converges almost everywhere and is uniformly bounded.

## Remove the logarithmic regularization

If p_t<=C, then uniformly in t,

0<=Sigma_e(rho_t)-Sigma(rho_t)
 <= C integral_R (1/2)log(1+e^2/x^2)dx
 = C pi e.                                             (5)

To check the integral, differentiate it in e>0 to get integral e/(x^2+e^2)dx=pi and use scaling, or monotone convergence to zero as e decreases to zero. Compact support and bounded density also show directly that Sigma is finite; its positive part is bounded by the support diameter and its negative logarithmic part is integrable.

The uniform Cauchy bound gives a bound on |H_e,t| on the common support, independent of small e and t. At each t, H_e,t converges almost everywhere to H_t. The functions involved are measurable in (t,x) (for H_t take a pointwise boundary limit where it exists and zero on the null complement). Fubini therefore permits dominated convergence over time and space. Integrate (4) over [u,v], use (5) at the endpoints, and let e tend to zero:

Sigma(rho_v)-Sigma(rho_u)
 =2 integral_u^v integral H_t V_t d rho_t dt.            (6)

The integrand is continuous in t by hypothesis 2, common support and uniform bounds. Thus (6) proves continuous differentiability, rather than simply an almost-everywhere derivative.

## The origin term and the square

On a neighborhood of the common support, log|x| is smooth and has derivative 1/x. Extend it to a global C1 test across the unused gap, and apply (1). This gives

d/dt integral log|x|rho_t(dx)=integral V_t(x)/x rho_t(dx), (7)

again continuously in t. Combining (6) and (7), and using gamma a=1-gamma, gives

E_gamma'=integral [2 gamma H_t+(1-gamma)/x] V_t d rho_t
         =2 gamma integral V_t^2 d rho_t.

The same pointwise convergence and uniform bounds show that integral V_t^2 p_t dx is continuous. This proves (2).

## Controls and exact scope

For dilation D_c rho (the law of cX, c>0), direct substitution in the two logarithms gives E_gamma(D_c rho)=E_gamma(rho)+log c. Consequently the pure rectangular Gaussian heat law rho_t=D_sqrt(t) rho_1 has E_gamma'=1/(2t), so (2) gives Phi_gamma=1/t. A Gaussian-entry signal with entry variance beta/n simply replaces t by beta+t and gives Phi_gamma=1/(beta+t). These controls check the factors of gamma and two. They do not establish MI convergence.

There is no claim here for gamma=1 under the gap hypotheses; that case was handled separately by claim 020. There is no claim for t=0. Removing the gap without another argument would invalidate (7). The principal dependency is every regularity and transport hypothesis of claim 025, whose algebraic physical-branch step requires external audit. body: The Gamma function Gamma(z) = integral from 0 to infinity of t^(z-1) e^(-t) dt, convergent for Re(z) > 0, extends the factorial to the complex plane. It satisfies the functional equation Gamma(z+1) = z Gamma(z) (integration by parts), so Gamma(n) = (n-1)! for positive integers n; it continues meromorphically to all of C with simple poles at the non-positive integers, and Gamma(1/2) = sqrt(pi). By the Bohr-Mollerup theorem it is the unique log-convex function on the positive reals with value 1 at 1 that satisfies the functional equation. Stirling's approximation is the asymptotics of Gamma (equivalently of the factorial) for large argument.

	\[

	\]

body:
[Lemma lem:concentration-mf of arXiv:2605.20697, 'Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for \\ Second-Order Consensus-Based Optimization'] Fix \(q>2\), and assume that the objective function \(f\) satisfies
    (assumption:bounded of the paper). Consider \(J\) independent mean-field processes
    \((\overline X_t^j,\overline V_t^j)\), initialized with i.i.d.\ samples from
    \(\overline\rho_0\in\mathcal P_{2q}(\mathbb R^{2d})\).

    Define
    \[
        \overline Y_t^j
        :=
        \overline X_t^j-m_{\overline X}(\overline\rho_t),
        \qquad
        \widehat{\overline Z}_t^j
        :=
        \bigl(\overline V_t^j-m_{\overline V}(\overline\rho_t)\bigr)
        -
        \frac1\gamma\overline Y_t^j,
    \]
    and let
    \[
        \overline L_2^j(t)
        :=
        \psi_2(\overline Y_t^j,\widehat{\overline Z}_t^j),
        \qquad
        \overline L_2^J(t)
        :=
        \frac1J\sum_{j=1}^J \overline L_2^j(t).
    \]
    Assume the parameter conditions needed for
    (prop:ito-mfl-centered-lyapunov-differential of the paper) at \(p=2\) and \(p=2q\).
    Let \(\kappa\) satisfy
    \[
        0<\kappa<\min\left\{\lambda_{2},\frac{\lambda_{2q}}q\right\},
    \]
    and assume the concentration noise absorption condition
    \begin{equation}
        \sigma^2
        \leqslant
        \frac{m^2 c_1^{(2)}(\lambda_{2}-\kappa)}
        {2\tau(S)(1+C_{\mathrm{lem}})}.
    \end{equation}
    Then, for every threshold \(A>0\) and every \(J\in\mathbb N_+\),
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbf P\left[
            \sup_{t\geqslant0}
            \e^{\kappa t}\overline L_2^J(t)
            \geqslant
            \mathbf{E}[\overline L_2^J(0)]+A
        \right]
        \leqslant
        \frac{C_{\mathrm{Bad}}^{\mathrm{MF}}}{A^q}
        J^{-\frac q2}\,
        \overline{\mathcal L}_{2q}(0).
    \end{equation}
    Consequently, by the coercivity bound for \(\psi_2\),
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbf P\left[
            \sup_{t\geqslant0}
            \e^{\kappa t}
            \mathfrak M_2(\mu_{\overline X_t^J})
            \geqslant
            \frac{\mathbf{E}[\overline L_2^J(0)]+A}{c_1^{(2)}}
        \right]
        \leqslant
        \frac{C_{\mathrm{Bad}}^{\mathrm{MF}}}{A^q}
        J^{-\frac q2}\,
        \overline{\mathcal L}_{2q}(0).
    \end{equation}
    The constant is
    \[
        C_{\mathrm{Bad}}^{\mathrm{MF}}
        :=
        3^q
        \left(
            \overline C_{\mathrm{MZ}}
            +
            C_{Z,q}
            +
            C_{\mathrm{Mart}}
        \right),
    \]
    where
    \[
        \overline C_{\mathrm{MZ}}
        :=
        \frac{C_{{\rm MZ},q} C_\phi^q 2^{q-1}}{c_{1,2q}},
    \]
    \[
        C_{Z,q}
        :=
        \frac{
            2(2K_{\mathrm{tr}})^q C_{{\rm WM},2q}
        }{
            c_{1,2q}\ell^{q-1}(\lambda_{2q}-q\kappa)
        },
        \qquad
        \ell
        :=
        \frac{\lambda_{2q}-q\kappa}{2(q-1)},
    \]
    and
    \[
        C_{\mathrm{Mart}}
        :=
        \frac{
            2^{q+1}C_{\mathrm{BDG},q}C_{\sigma,q}
        }{
            \lambda_{2q}-q\kappa
        }
        \left(
            \frac{q-2}{\lambda_{2q}-q\kappa}
        \right)^{\frac q2-1}.
    \]

[Lemma lm:pi-forward of arXiv:2507.08757, 'Strong existence and uniqueness of the tilt-indexed Busemann process in the planar corner '] Let $\pi^u:\Omega\to\mathbb{X}_u$, $u\in\mathbb{Z}^2$, be measurable maps such that $\pi^u\in\mathcal{G}_u^\omega$ $\mathbb{P}$-almost surely. Suppose the family $(\pi^u)_{u\in\mathbb{Z}^2}$ is shift-covariant, 
\[
\mathbb{P}\{\pi^u=u+\pi^0\circ T_u\}=1 \quad \text{for all } u\in\mathbb{Z}^2,
\]
and that $\pi^u\curlywedgeuparrow\pi^v$ holds with probability one for all $u,v\in\mathbb{Z}^2$. Then each $\pi^u$ is $\mathcal{F}^{+}_u$-measurable up to $\mathbb{P}$-null sets.

[Theo 7 of arXiv:2609.02261, 'Quantization and process'] i) If the two  operators  $A$ and $B$ 
  belong to $C_h$ then the composition  $A \circ B$ also  lies in $C_h$ and we have for every $V\in\R^{2n}$,
   
     $$  d_h (A \circ B) (V) \leq   (2 \pi h) ^ {-n} \int _{\R^{2n}}  
     ( d_h A) (V-U)  ( d_h B) (U) dU. $$
     
     ii) Take $F$ and $G$ in $D_{ h} ( \R^{2n})$ and set
    $A_h =  {\rm Op}_h^{\rm Wick}(F)$ and  $B_h =  {\rm Op}_h^{\rm Wick}(G)$. 
    Then, there exists a function in  $D_{ h} ( \R^{2n})$ denoted by $F \sharp _h ^{\rm Wick}G$ satisfying,
    
    $$ \sigma  _h ^{\rm Wick} (A_h \circ B_h) = F \sharp _h ^{\rm Wick}G. $$
    
   In addition,  we have the identity,    for all $X\in\R^{2n}$,
    
     \be   (F \sharp_h^{ Wick } G)  (X) = (2 \pi h)^{-n}
     \int _{ \R^ {2n}}  
   F  ^{\rm ext} ( X+T, X)   G  ^{\rm ext} ( X , X+T)   
   e^{ - \frac {1}   {2h} |T|^2 } dT.\ee (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 5 ({Lemma 3.5 in \cite{vanwerde2024recovering}}) of arXiv:2512.02661, 'Worst-case mixing estimates for Brownian motion with semipermeable barriers'] Suppose that $\delta < 1/2$.
	Then, for every $x_0 \in \bbR^2$, there is at most one barrier $B_i$ which intersects $\sB(x_0,r_{\delta})$.
	Moreover, if such a $B_i$ exists, then there exists a unit vector $ \hatn \in \bbR^2$ depending on $x_0$ and $B_i$ with the following properties:
	\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin = 2em, label = (\arabic*)]
		\item There exists some $\mathfrak{c}\in \bbR$ such that $\lvert \langle  y, \hatn\rangle - \mathfrak{c} \rvert <  4\delta r_\delta$ for every $y\in B_i\cap \sB(x_0, r_\delta)$.
		\item One has $\Vert \vec{n}_i(y)-  \hatn \Vert < 2\delta$ for every $y\in B_i \cap \sB(x_0, r_\delta)$.
		\item Every point $z \in \sB(x_0, r_\delta)$ on the positive side of $B_i$ satisfies $ \langle  z, \hatn\rangle > \mathfrak{c} -  4\delta r_\delta$.
		      Similarly, it holds for every $z\in \sB(x_0, r_\delta)$ on the negative side of $B_i$ that $ \langle  z, \hatn\rangle < \mathfrak{c}  +  4\delta r_\delta$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: {Lemma 3.5 in \cite{vanwerde2024recovering}}

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2604.24677, 'Local Limit of Random Regular Bipartite Planar Maps'] For any $n\geq 1$, denote by $\P^d_n$ the uniform probability measure on $\mathcal{M}^d_{n}$.

Then, the sequence $\left(\P^d_n\right)_n$  converges weakly, for the  local topology, to a limiting probability measure $\P^d_\infty$ supported on the set of one-ended infinite $d$-regular bipartite planar maps. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

				\[
					\mathbb{P}\left(P^m(u_n-\mathbb{E} u_n(0))(0)\leq -s\right)
					\leq
					C\exp\left\{
					-c\min\left(s^2m^{(d-4)/2}, s m^{(d-2)/2}\right)
					\right\}\, .
			\]

[Theorem thm:comonads of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] Let $F:\cC\leftrightarrows\cD:G$ be a comonadic adjunction of stable $\infty$-categories such that $T\coloneqq\mathrm{fib}(FG\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}1_{\cD})\circ [-1]$ is an autoequivalence of $\cD$, and let $\sigma\in\mathrm{Stab}(\cD,\Gamma,\mathrm{cl})$ be a stability condition preserved by $T$ and such that $\mathrm{cl}\circ K_0(T)=\mathrm{cl}$.
If we set $\cE\coloneqq \cC/G(\cD)$, then:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
    \item For any $X\in\cC$, the class $\mathrm{cl}([FX])\in \Gamma$ depends only on the isomorphism class of the image of $X$ in $\cE$. Moreover, this induces a well-defined map $\mathrm{cl}_{\cE}\colon K_0(\cE)\to \Gamma$.
    \item There is a stability condition $\sigma'$ on $\cE$ with respect to the map $\mathrm{cl}_{\cE}$ characterized by the following: The central charge is the same as for $\sigma$ and an isomorphism class of objects in $\cE$ is $\sigma'$-semistable of phase $\phi$ if and only if it admits a representative $X\in\cC$ such that $FX$ is $\sigma$-semistable of phase $\phi$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:comonads of arXiv:2609.00978

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2604.06516, 'From stochastic individual-based models to free-boundary Hamilton-Jacobi equations'] Let us consider $t\geq 0 $ and $f\in AC[0,t]$ such that $I_t(f)<+\infty$ and such that for all $s\leq t$, $F_s(f)>0$. Almost surely, for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$,

    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 14 of arXiv:2604.06516

body:
[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.27569, 'Laplace and Dolbeault operators on Sasakian manifolds'] Let $(M^{2n+1},g,\xi )$ be a Sasakian manifold. The Dolbeault Laplacians $\Delta
_{\partial }$ and $\Delta _{\overline{\partial }}$ are related by 
\begin{equation}
\Delta _{\partial }=\Delta _{\overline{\partial }}-2iH\mathcal{L}_{\xi }.

\end{equation}
The Hodge Laplace operator acting on differential forms on $M$ satisfies 
\begin{equation}
\Delta =2\Delta _{\overline{\partial }}-2iH\mathcal{L}_{\xi }+2i\eta \wedge
\left( \overline{\partial }^{\ast }-\partial ^{\ast }\right) +2i\xi
\lrcorner \left( \overline{\partial }-\partial \right) +4L\Lambda +4\eta
\wedge \xi \lrcorner H-\mathcal{L}_{\xi }^{2}.  
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.27569

[Propo moments_kesten_distance_finite of arXiv:2606.15339, 'Uniform integrability of the distance to the nearest leaf in random trees'] Let $\mathcal{T}_n$ be a sequence of size-conditioned simply generated trees. Then, for every $p>0$,
	\[
	\mathbf{E}\bigl[\partial(\hat{\mathcal{T}})^{p}\bigr] = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \bigl(k^{p} - (k-1)^{p}\bigr)\, c_k\,.
	\]
	In types~I and~II the series is finite by Lemma~(lem: exponential_c_k of the paper); in type~III we have $\partial(\hat{\mathcal{T}}) = 1$ almost surely and therefore $\mathbf{E}\bigl[\partial(\hat{\mathcal{T}})^{p}\bigr] = 1$.

[Proposition prop:mass of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] Let $A\to B\to C\xrightarrow{\delta}A[1]$ be an exact triangle, then
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
    \item $m(B)\leq m(A)+m(C)$,
    \item if $\phi_-(A)\geq\phi_+(C)$, then $m(B)=m(A)+m(C)$,
    \item if $\phi_+(A)<\phi_-(C)$ and $0\neq\delta\in\operatorname{Ext}^1(C,A)$, then $m(B)<m(A)+m(C)$.
\end{enumerate}

[Corollary 25 of arXiv:2608.18834, 'The Parabolic Anderson Model's Total Mass at Small Times: Geometry, Fluctuations, and Reno'] Let $\ka>0$ be fixed.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\rho=0$, then there exists a constant $\mf e_\ka\in\mbb R$ such that
\[\lim_{\eps\to0}\Big(\mbf E\big[\tfrac{\ka^2}{2}\be^\eps_t(B)\big]-t\ka^2\msf c(\eps)\Big)=-\ka^2\mf b\,t\log(1/t)+\mf e_\ka\,t.\]
\item If $\rho<0$, then
\[\lim_{\eps\to0}\Big(\mbf E\big[\tfrac{\ka^2}{2}\be^\eps_t(B)\big]-t\ka^2\msf c(\eps)\Big)=\tfrac{\ka^2\mf b}{(1+\rho)\rho}\, t^{1+\rho}.\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

AUTHOR-CHECKED PARTIAL OBSTRUCTION, NOT INDEPENDENTLY REVIEWED. For the heat semigroup with generator Delta on the unit two-torus, integral_0^infinity exp(-t)*||p_t(x,.)-p_t(y,.)||_2^2 dt is infinite when y-x=(1/2,0). Thus this illustrative metric formula can fail even when an ordinary Feller topology exists. For a symmetric Markov semigroup with finite integrated heat trace G(t) for t>0, the weight w(t)=exp(-t)/(1+G(2t)) instead yields finite Hilbert row norm almost everywhere. This alone does not establish the Feller-topology compactification conjecture.
Probability invariant measure
Symmetric heat kernels and semigroup identity
Generator Delta convention for the explicit torus calculation
No assertion about newly added completion states

The suggested unweighted heat-kernel metric can be infinite in a basic admissible example. For Brownian motion on the two-torus, the squared row-distance integrated against exp(-t)dt equals sum_(k in Z^2) |1-exp(2pi*i*k.h)|^2/[1+8pi^2*|k|^2]. At h=(1/2,0), every odd k1 has numerator4. Each dyadic annulus contains order N^2 such terms of order N^-2, so the series diverges. A repair is to use w(t)=exp(-t)/(1+G(2t)), where G is the integrated diagonal heat trace: Fubini gives finite weighted row norm for almost every state.

Second check. Parseval computes the row norm exactly; integrating the nonnegative Fourier series is justified by Tonelli. For the repaired weight, the average row squared norm is integral w(t)*G(2t)dt<=1. This produces an almost-everywhere finite Hilbert-space pseudometric after identifying indistinguishable rows.

Limits. Brownian motion already has a good usual topology, so the divergence refutes only the illustrative formula, not the existence conjecture. Completing a heat-kernel embedding can add states; proving valid transition kernels and the Feller property on that completion is still missing.

[Lemma lem: eigenspace of arXiv:2505.09839, '\textbf{Density Frankl–Rödl on the Sphere}'] For any $k \geq 0$ and $Y_k \in \mathcal{S}_k$, we have
\[
A_r(Y_k) = \mu_{k,r} Y_k,
\]
where $\mu_{k,r} = G_k(r)$, with $G_k : [-1,1] \to \mathbb{R}$ denoting the degree-$k$ Gegenbauer polynomial (see,e.g., [muller2006spherical]), given by
\[
G_k(r) = \mathbb{E} \left[ \left( r + i X_1 \sqrt{1 - r^2} \right)^k \right],
\]
where $X = (X_1, \dotsc, X_{n-1})$ is uniformly distributed on $\mathbb{S}^{n-2}$ and $X_1$ denotes any fixed coordinate.

body: In mathematics, Galois cohomology is the study of the group cohomology of Galois modules, that is, the application of homological algebra to modules for Galois groups. A Galois group G associated with a field extension L/K acts in a natural way on some abelian groups, for example those constructed directly from L, but also through other Galois representations that may be derived by more abstract means. Galois cohomology accounts for the way in which taking Galois-invariant elements fails to be an exact functor.
title: Galois cohomology

[Corollary cor:zero-info-consequences of arXiv:2609.02155, 'Exact Limits of Random Projections for Preserving Geometry:\\ Distance Recovery, Nearest-N'] Under the assumptions of (prop:zeroinfo of the paper), if $n\ge3$, define the
mean Kendall statistic for the replacement map by
\[
\overline\tau_n^{\mathrm{rep}}
=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\binom{n-1}{2}^{-1}
\sum_{\substack{j<k\\j,k\ne i}}
\operatorname{sgn}\!\left[
(D_{ij}-D_{ik})(D_{ij}^{\mathrm{rep}}-D_{ik}^{\mathrm{rep}})
\right].
\]
Then
\[
\E\overline\tau_n^{\mathrm{rep}}=0,
\qquad
\Pr\!\left(\abs{\overline\tau_n^{\mathrm{rep}}}>t\right)
\le2\exp\!\left(-\frac{\lfloor n/3\rfloor t^2}{2}\right).
\]
In the analogous setting with one query and $q\ge2$ candidates, let
$\mathcal N_k$ and $\mathcal N_k^{\mathrm{rep}}$ be the top-$k$ sets for the
original and replacement clouds, respectively, where $1\le k<q$. Then
\[
\E\frac{\abs{\mathcal N_k\cap\mathcal N_k^{\mathrm{rep}}}}{k}
=\frac{k}{q},
\qquad
\Pr\!\left(\mathcal N_1=\mathcal N_1^{\mathrm{rep}}\right)=\frac1q.
\]
title: Ranking consequences of the replacement map

 \deg(\operatorname{Id}-\Phi_t,\mathcal O_t,0)
\]
is well defined and independent of \(t\).  The degree of an empty
slice is understood to be zero.

[Theorem 12 (Maximum entropy triply augmented hive) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{thm:gaussian1}
Let \(\bar a,\bar b,\bar c\) be parameters in one of the following two regimes:
\[
\bar a,\bar b,\bar c>0,
\]
or
\[
\bar a,\bar b>0,
\qquad
-\bar c^2>\bar a^2+\bar b^2.
\]
Let \(\mathbb A^3\) denote the cone of triply augmented hives, where
\[
\mathbb A^3(\lambda,\mu;\nu)
:=
GT(\lambda)\times GT(\mu)\times GT(\nu)\times H_n(\lambda,\mu;\nu),
\]
for
\[
\lambda,\mu,\nu\in \Spec_n+\mathbb R\one,
\qquad
\sum_i\lambda_i+\sum_i\mu_i=\sum_i\nu_i.
\]
Define a probability density \(p\) on \(\mathbb A^3\), with respect to
Lebesgue measure, by
\[
p(g_\lambda,g_\mu,g_\nu,h)
=
Z^{-1}(\bar a,\bar b,\bar c)
\exp\left[
-\frac12
\left(
\frac{|\lambda|^2}{\bar a^2}
+
\frac{|\mu|^2}{\bar b^2}
+
\frac{|\nu|^2}{\bar c^2}
\right)
\right],
\]
for
\[
(g_\lambda,g_\mu,g_\nu,h)
\in
\mathbb A^3(\lambda,\mu;\nu).
\]
Then \(p\) is the unique probability density on \(\mathbb A^3\) that
maximizes differential entropy among all densities \(q\) satisfying
\[
\mathbb E_q |\lambda|^2
=
\frac{\bar a^2(\bar b^2+\bar c^2)n^2}
     {\bar a^2+\bar b^2+\bar c^2},
\]
\[
\mathbb E_q |\mu|^2
=
\frac{\bar b^2(\bar c^2+\bar a^2)n^2}
     {\bar a^2+\bar b^2+\bar c^2},
\]
and
\[
\mathbb E_q |\nu|^2
=
\frac{\bar c^2(\bar a^2+\bar b^2)n^2}
     {\bar a^2+\bar b^2+\bar c^2}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Maximum entropy triply augmented hive

[Theorem p-schuriff of arXiv:2609.03988, 'A $p$-summability approach to the weak maximizing property'] For a Banach space $Y$ and $1 < p < \infty$, the following are equivalent: \\
{\rm (1)} $Y$ has the $\mathrm{SP}_p$. \\
{\rm (2)} For every Banach space $X$ such that $B_X$ is relatively weakly $p$-precompact, every bounded linear operator $T: X \to Y$ is norm-attaining. \\
{\rm (3)} For every $1 \leq r < \infty$ and every Banach space $X$ such that $B_X$ is relatively weakly $p$-precompact, the pair $(X, Y)$ has the $\mathrm{SMP}_r$. \\
{\rm (4)} For every Banach space $X$ such that $B_X$ is relatively weakly $p$-precompact, the pair $(X, Y)$ has the $\mathrm{WMP}$.

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Transfer the branching-random-walk identification of the limit to the random model of zeta, and locate the arithmetic obstruction. Result: For the random Euler-product model (45) of the source, the maximum over h in [0,1] is a maximum of a log-correlated non-Gaussian field with the multiscale structure (47)-(50), and the general theory (Arguin's Section 3, and the DRZ-type universality for the maximum) gives convergence of the centred maximum to a randomly shifted Gumbel whose shift is the log of the total mass of the critical multiplicative chaos of the field, provided (i) the increments have exponential moments with the right Gaussian-like rate (true for the random model), and (ii) a second-moment computation at the level of the critical chaos with the derivative-martingale normalisation. For the random model this is plausibly within reach of existing tools (it is the content of what the random model's community calls the 'full FHK conjecture for the random model'), and I believe the identification of the limiting law for the random model is still not written; the Gumbel convolution structure would follow from the cluster structure at the maximum, which for a non-Gaussian field requires the local limit theorem for the increments, available via the prime-sum large deviations. For the actual zeta function the obstruction is arithmetic: the increments at different scales are only asymptotically independent, and the identification of the limit law needs the joint law of the increments at the finest scales (primes near T), which the moment method cannot control at the required precision. Recorded: for the random model the limit is predicted to be the standard randomly shifted Gumbel with the critical chaos of the Euler-product field; for zeta the same is conjectured and the finest-scale dependence is the gap. Obstruction: Fine-scale dependence of the prime sums prevents the local limit theorem needed to identify the cluster structure.

[Corollary thirdclasscordasg of arXiv:2504.15992, 'Repeated singular values of a random symmetric matrix and decoupled singular value estimat'] The proof of Theorem (mainquasiramdonmess2 of the paper) can be reduced to the following estimate: for a given constant $c_\Sigma>0$ and a (large, already fixed) $L>1$,
there exist $\alpha',\gamma,\mu\in(0,1)$ and $c_\Sigma'>0$ such that 
     $$\begin{aligned}
&\sup_{\epsilon_1,c,I,C_I^1,C_I^3,s_1,s_2}\sup_{w_0^1,w_0^2\in\mathbb{R}^n}\mathbb{P}^\mathcal{K}(\exists(v_1,v_2)\in\mathcal{P}_{\epsilon_1}(c)\cup\mathcal{P}_{\epsilon_1}^0(c): D_{\alpha',\gamma}((C_I^1v_1+C_I^3v_3)_I)\leq e^{c_\Sigma' n},\\&
\tau_{L,\underline{C}_I^3}(v_1,\underline{C}_I^1v_1+\underline{C}_I^3v_3)\leq e^{-c_\Sigma n} \text{ if }|\underline{C}_I^3|\geq e^{-c_\Sigma n},\quad\tau_{L,0}(v_1,\underline{C}_I^1v_1+\underline{C}_I^3v_3\left.\right)\leq e^{-c_\Sigma n} \text{else},
\\&
\|(A_n-s_1I_n)v_1-w_0^1\|_2\leq 2^{-n/3},\quad\\& \|(A_n-s_2I_n)(\underline{C}_I^1v_1+\underline{C}_I^3v_3)+(s_2-s_1)\underline{C}_I^1v_1-w_0^2\|_2\leq 2^{-n/3})\leq 2^{-600n},
\end{aligned}$$
where the supremum is over parameters of the same range as in Corollary (corollary1streduction of the paper) and (2ndreductionfirstsec of the paper).

[Deff sobolev-spaces of arXiv:2601.19145, 'Stochastic Persistence in Infinite Dimensions'] For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and $1 < p < \infty$ we define the Sobolev spaces recursively by $W^{0,p} \coloneqq L^p$ and
    $$W^{k,p} \coloneqq \{u \in L^p \mid \partial_iu \in W^{k-1,p} \text{ for } i = 1,\dots, N\}$$
    endowed with the norm
    $$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}} \coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^N\|\partial_i u\|_{W^{k-1,p}} + \|u\|_{L^p} \,.$$
    In the definition, it is implicit that the weak derivatives $\partial_i u$ exist. For $s > 0$ (not necessarily an integer), we define $W^{s,p}$ via complex interpolation, see [interpolation-simple] with the domain $\mathbb{R}^n$, but the results also hold for our domain $D$ via extension operators.

    If $D = \mathbb{T}^N$, we also define $W^{-s,p}$ to be the dual of $W^{s,p^*}$, where $1/p + 1/p^* = 1$.
title: Deff sobolev-spaces of arXiv:2601.19145

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2607.27786, 'Gaussian free field in annulus: \\BPZ equations and crossing probabilities for level lines'] Assume the same setup as in Definition~\ref{def::multiannulus_SLE}. 
Suppose $\bs{\gamma}=(\gamma^1, \ldots, \gamma^n)$ is $n$-annulus $\SLE_{\kappa}(\LFcro{n}^{(\kappa; \ell)})$. 
We denote $\dot{\bs{\alpha}}_1=(\alpha_2, \ldots, \alpha_n)$ and $\dot{\bs{\beta}}_1=(\beta_n, \ldots, \beta_2)$. 
Then the marginal law of $\gamma^1$ under $\Pcro{n}^{(\kappa; \ell)}$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\Pcro{1}^{(\kappa; \ell)}$ in $(\A_r; \ee^{\ii\alpha_1}, \ee^{\ii\beta_1-r})$ with Radon-Nikodym derivative given by~\eqref{eqn::rainbow_RN}.

[Lemma lem:smallphi of arXiv:2608.05089, 'Correlation decay in area-tilted line ensembles'] Let $\psi(t) = M \log(1 + |t|)$ for some $M > 0$ as in Lemma (lem:confinement of the paper).
Then for any $\alpha > 0$, there is some $H > 0$ for which there exists
a symmetric $C^1$ function $\phi$ on $\mathbb{R}$ such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=(A.\arabic*)]
    \item For all $t \in \mathbb{R}$, we have $\phi(t) \geqslant \psi(t)$, 
    \item For all $t \in [-\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}]$, we have $\phi(t) \leqslant \frac{H}{2} - \alpha M - 1$, 
    \item For all $t \in \mathbb{R}$, we have $|\phi'(t)| \leqslant 1$, 
    \item For all but two values of $t \in \mathbb{R}$, the function $\phi$ is twice differentiable
    and satisfies $\phi''(t) \leqslant \frac{1}{2}$. 
\end{enumerate}
title: Lemma lem:smallphi of arXiv:2608.05089

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2609.03830, 'Parabolic Poincar\'e inequalities and maximal function estimates for systems of partial di'] Let $1\le q<\infty$. Assume that $|F|\in L^q_{\loc}(\Omega_T)$ and that $u\in  L^q_{\loc}(0,T;W^{1,q}_{\loc} (\Om;\mathbb{R}^N))$ satisfies \eqref{weak_sol} for every $\varphi\in C_0^\infty(\Om_T;\mathbb{R}^N)$. 
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] If $1\le q<n+2$, then for $1\le q\le q^*<\tfrac{q(n+2)}{n+2-q}$, there exists a constant $c=c(n,q,q^*,L)$ such that 
    \[
    \left( \fiint_{Q } \frac{|u-u_{Q}|^{q^*}}{\rho^{q^*}}\,dz\right)^\frac{1}{q^*}
    \le c\left( \fiint_{Q } ( |\na u| + |F| ) ^q\,dz\right)^\frac{1}{q}
    \]
    for every parabolic cylinder $Q=Q_{\rho}\Subset\Omega_T$.
    \item[(ii)] If $q=n+2$, then there exists a constant $c=c(n,L)$ such that
    \[
    \fiint_Q\exp\left(\left(
   \frac{|u-u_{Q}|}{\displaystyle c\rho\left(\fiint_{Q}(|\na u|+|F|)^{n+2} \,dz\right)^{\frac{1}{n+2}}}\right)^{\frac{n+2}{n+1}}\right)\,dz\le c
    \]
     for every parabolic cylinder $Q=Q_{\rho}\Subset\Omega_T$.
    \item[(iii)] If $q>n+2$, then there exists a constant $c=c(n,q,L)$ such that
    \[
    \esssup_Q\frac{|u-u_{Q}|}{\rho}
    \le c\left( \fiint_{Q } ( |\na u| + |F| ) ^q\,dz\right)^\frac{1}{q}
    \]
     for every parabolic cylinder $Q=Q_{\rho}\Subset\Omega_T$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: The Arzelà–Ascoli theorem is a fundamental result of mathematical analysis giving necessary and sufficient conditions to decide whether every sequence of a given family of real-valued continuous functions defined on a closed and bounded interval has a uniformly convergent subsequence. The main condition is the equicontinuity of the family of functions. The theorem is the basis of many proofs in mathematics, including that of the Peano existence theorem in the theory of ordinary differential equations, Montel's theorem in complex analysis, and the Peter–Weyl theorem in harmonic analysis and various results concerning compactness of integral operators.

[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2608.09419, 'Left-tail expansions for Schr\"oder branching processes with explicit convergence rates'] \lb{T1} Suppose that the probability generating function $P(z)$ is analytic in some neighborhood of $z=1$, and $E=P'(1)>1$. Then the unique solution of the Poincar\'e functional equation 
\[\lb{111}
 \Pi(z)=P(\Pi(\frac{z}E)),\ \ \ \Pi(0)=1,\ \ \ \Pi'(0)=-1
\]
exists in some neighborhood of $z=0$. It can be computed by
\[\lb{111a}
 \Pi(z)=\lim_{t\to+\iy}\underbrace{P\circ...\circ P}_{t}(1-\frac{z}{E^{t}}).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 18 of arXiv:2605.03851, 'The Relay Random Tree:\\A stochastic geometry approach of multihop relay in an urban visib'] \textbf{Buildings being relayed by a given building.}
    
Conditional on $\zone(\alpha, \beta)$ the buildings in $\zone(\alpha, \beta)$ form an inhomogeneous PPP of intensity
\[\tilde{\lambda} = \lambda \rm{d}x\otimes \mathcal{L}. \]
The average number of such buildings is equal to:
\[\lambda\e[\ell_\theta(\zone(\alpha, \beta))] - \left(1-\exp(-\frac{\lambda}{\tan\theta}(\primi(\beta)-\primi(0)))\right).\]

		$b=b(d,\theta_0,K_0)>0$, $C=C(d,\theta_0,K_0)<\infty$,
		$c=c(d,\nu_0,\theta_0,K_0)>0$, and
		$t_0=t_0(d,\nu_0,\theta_0,K_0)<\infty$ such that, for every mean-zero
		i.i.d.\ field $(\zeta(x))_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}$ satisfying
		\[
			\Var(\zeta(0))\geq\nu_0^2\, ,
			\qquad
			\mathbb{E} e^{\theta_0|\zeta(0)|}\leq K_0\, ,
		\]
		and every $t\geq t_0$, the level set
		\[
			\{x:u_t(x)>c(\log t)^{2/d}\}
		\]
		contains an infinite nearest-neighbor component almost surely.
		Moreover, for every $t\geq t_0$,
		\begin{equation}
			\mathbb{P}\left(Q(0,1)\leftrightarrow\infty
			\textup{ in }\{x:u_t(x)>\mathbb{E} u_t(0)/2\}\right)
			\geq 1-Ce^{-b\mathbb{E} u_t(0)}\, .
		\end{equation}

body: Schwarz lemma: Let D = {z in C : |z| < 1} be the open unit disk and let f : D -> D be a holomorphic map with f(0) = 0. Then |f(z)| <= |z| for every z in D, and |f'(0)| <= 1. Moreover, if |f(z_0)| = |z_0| for some z_0 in D with z_0 nonzero, or if |f'(0)| = 1, then f is a rotation, i.e. f(z) = a z for some constant a with |a| = 1. (The Schwarz-Pick-Ahlfors generalization in complex differential geometry estimates the pointwise norm of a holomorphic map f : M -> N between Hermitian manifolds under curvature bounds: for instance, if M is complete Kaehler with Ricci curvature bounded below by -K_1 and N has holomorphic sectional curvature bounded above by -K_2 < 0, then the squared norm of df is bounded by K_1 / K_2.)
title: Schwarz lemma

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2608.12451, '2608.12451'] Fix $r\in\N$
and
let $(F_t, F)$ be the exchangeable pair of
Proposition~\ref{prop_P_pair} with $q=r$ or Proposition~\ref{prop_R_pair}
with $d=r$.
Assume $F$ lives in the $r$-th chaos 
and 
put
$D_t:=F_t-F.$
Then,

\noi
\begin{align}
 \cJ(F)
 :=\lim_{t\downarrow0}
 \frac{\E[D_t^2(D_t^2-1)]}{1-e^{-rt}}
 
\end{align}
exists  and  

\noi
\begin{align}
 \cJ(F)
 =8m_4(F)-\frac{6}{r}  \sum_{q=1}^{2r}  q\|J_q(F^2)\|_2^2
 -2m_2(F).
 
\end{align}
If in addition $F$  satisfies the lattice condition
\eqref{cond_La}, then $\cJ(F)\geq 0$.
title: Proposition 13 of arXiv:2608.12451

body:
[Lemma l:derbound of arXiv:2605.20587, 'Persistence and entropic repulsion of stationary Gaussian fields with spectral singularity'] Fix $\gamma > \gamma'  > 0$ satisfying $v \ge  (1+\gamma')/(1+\gamma)$, let $g_s$ denote an SGF with spectral measure $\phi_s^2 \mu$, and let $k$ be a multi-index. Then $g_s$ is almost surely smooth, and there exist $c_d > 0$ and $s_0 = s_0(d,\gamma,\gamma',v,k)$ such that, for all $s \ge s_0$, 
\begin{align*}  \textrm{Var} \big[ \partial^k g_s(0) \big]  &\le s^{-2|k|}  (\log s)^{2|k|(1+\gamma)}   \mu[ B( (\log s)^{1+\gamma} / s )] + \|\mu\| e^{-2(\log s)^{1+\gamma'} },  \\
 \mathbb{E} \Big[ \sup_{x \in B(s)} \partial^k g_s(x) \Big] &\le c_d s^{-|k|} (\log s)^{(|k|+1)(1+\gamma)}  \sqrt{ \mu[ B( (\log s)^{1+\gamma} / s )] } + \sqrt{ \|\mu\| } e^{-(\log s)^{1+\gamma'} } . 
 \end{align*}
The same result holds if $\phi_s$ is replaced by $\tilde{\phi}_s$.

[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2609.02850, 'Canonical-row Chern flow on Bott--Samelson towers:\\ realizable-volume models for Schubert'] Let $\rho:X\to B$ be a projective morphism from an integral projective
variety of dimension $d_X$.  Let $V$ be a globally generated vector bundle
of rank $R$ on $X$, and write
\begin{equation}
 \Xi(h):=\rho_*\bigl(c_R(V)\cap[X]\bigr)
 =\sum_{\gamma\le\mathbf m}\xi_\gamma h^\gamma
 \in A^c(B),
 \qquad c=\dim B-d_X+R.
\end{equation}
If $\Xi=0$, the conclusion below is understood to be the zero polynomial.
Otherwise $0\le c\le\dim B$, and
\begin{equation}
 \Dcomp_{\mathbf m}\Nrm(\Xi)
 =\sum_{\gamma\le\mathbf m}\xi_\gamma x^{[\mathbf m-\gamma]}
 \in\RV.
\end{equation}
If $X$ is smooth, the incidence variety used in the proof is smooth.
If $\operatorname{char}(\kk)=0$, the polynomial in
\eqref{eq:incidence-conclusion} also admits a smooth integral projective
realization.

body:
[Lemma 14 (Equivalence of $\tau$-norm and module norm) of arXiv:2608.30589, 'Vector-Valued Wavelet Bases as Hilbert $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-Module Bases: A Construc'] Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra and let $\tau$ be a faithful trace on $\mathcal A$.
Then there exist constants $0<c\le C$ such that for all $a\in\mathcal A$ with $a\ge 0$,
\[
c\,\|a\|\le \tau(a)\le C\,\|a\|.
\]
Consequently, for every $x$ in a Hilbert $\mathcal A$-module $(\mathbb H,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{\mathcal A})$,
\[
c\,\|x\|_{\mathcal A}^2\le \|x\|_{\tau}^2\le C\,\|x\|_{\mathcal A}^2,
\qquad
\|x\|_{\tau}^2:=\tau(\langle x,x\rangle_{\mathcal A}).
\]

body:
[Proposition 5 of arXiv:2608.26501, 'Explicit Bounds on the Entropy of Piecewise H\"{o}lder Graphon Models'] Let $W$ be piecewise H\"{o}lder with polytope domain, and write
\[W(x,y) = \sum_{t=1}^T f_t(x,y) \1_{A_t}(x,y),\]
where for each $t$, $f_t$ is H\"{o}lder continuous with constant $L_t$ and exponent $\alpha_t$. Define $L=\max_{t\in\set{1,\dots,T}}L_t$ and $\alpha = \min_{t\in\set{1,\dots,T}}\alpha_t$. Further, let 
\begin{equation}\rho = \max_{t,t'\in\set{1,\dots,T}}\sup_{\substack{(x,y)\in A_t\\ (x',y')\in A_{t'}}}|f_t(x,y)-f_{t'}(x',y')|.\end{equation}
Define
\[\Delta_n = \frac{1}{\binom n2}H(G(n,W)) - \iint_{\Omega^2}h\big(W(x,y)\big)\dd x\dd y.\]
Then
\begin{equation}0\leq\Delta_n\leq\frac{dn\log m}{\binom n2} +a_1 \frac{\log m}{m^\alpha}+a_2 \frac{1}{m^\alpha}+a_3\frac{1}{m}+a_4\frac{1}{m^2}\end{equation}
where $m = Cn^\gamma$ for $\gamma>0$ with $C\geq L^{1/\alpha}\ell\sqrt{2d}$ and the constants $a_i$ are given by 
\begin{align*}
a_1 &= \alpha L (\ell\sqrt{2d})^{\alpha}\ell^{2d}, & a_2 &=L(\ell\sqrt{2d})^{\alpha}(1/\ln 2 - \log(L(\ell\sqrt{2d})^{\alpha}))\ell^{2d},\\
a_3 &= 4d(T-1)\ell^{2d}\theta+2|\partial\K|\ell, & a_4 &= |\partial\K|^2\ell^2,
\end{align*}
where $\theta = -\rho\log\rho+\rho/\ln 2$. In the special case that $\Omega = [0,1]$, we can take $a_3 = 4d(T-1)\ell^{2}\theta$ and $a_4 = 0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 5 of arXiv:2608.26501

body:
[Lemma lem:correlation_init of arXiv:2608.05089, 'Correlation decay in area-tilted line ensembles'] For all $H > 0$ large enough,
there are some $C, c > 0$  such that for all $\lambda \geqslant 2$,
if $\mathbf{X}$ is the stationary infinite-line $\lambda$-tilted ensemble, then we have
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb{P} \mleft[ \mleft| \mathsf{LowEnds}^0_\ell(\mathbf{X}) \mright| \geqslant \tfrac{t}{16 H} \mright] \geqslant 1 - C e^{-ct},
\end{equation}
and the same holds with $\mathsf{LowEnds}^0_\ell(\mathbf{X})$ replaced by $\mathsf{LowEnds}^0_r(\mathbf{X})$, $\mathsf{LowEnds}^t_\ell(\mathbf{X})$,
or $\mathsf{LowEnds}^t_r(\mathbf{X})$.
