[Prop deffForWDRCM of arXiv:2411.10333, 'Subcritical annulus crossing in spatial random graphs'] Consider the interpolation model with a profile function with \(\delta\in(1,\infty)\).
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item 
            If \(\delta>2\), \(\gamma<1-1/\delta\), and \(\alpha<1-\gamma\), then
            \[
                \zeta = \max\big\{2-\delta, 1-\tfrac{\delta-1}{\gamma\delta}, \tfrac{\alpha+\gamma-1}{\gamma},\tfrac{2(\alpha+\gamma-1)}{\alpha+\gamma}\big\} <0.
            \]
        \item  
            If \(\delta=2\), \(\gamma<1-1/2\), and \(\alpha<1-\gamma\), or if \(\delta\geq 2\) and either \(\gamma<1-1/\delta\) and \(\alpha=1-\gamma\), or \(\gamma=1-1/\delta\) and \(\alpha<1-\gamma\), then \(\zeta=0\).
        \item   
            If either \(\delta<2\), or \(\gamma>1-1/\delta\), or \(\alpha>1-\gamma\), then
            \[
                \zeta= \max\big\{2-\delta, 1-\tfrac{\delta-1}{\gamma\delta}, \tfrac{\delta(\alpha+\gamma-1)}{\delta(\alpha+\gamma)-1}\big\}>0.
            \]
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:fc68a56dcc4d313155b2be68533d4ff0376888727be1c4560880e4646ea6c84a","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/fc/fc68a56dcc4d313155b2be68533d4ff0376888727be1c4560880e4646ea6c84a.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:b6b80062e37a23fca82e641d20dba351ce5b2a9b7c0adb121f8f3309c6a0ca51","bundle_entry_key":"tanh-sharp-mesoscopic-variance","bundle_id":"population.t244-critical-tanh-reciprocal-mean-rate-016","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks","draft":"w691/bundle_016.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:t244-tanh-sharp-mesoscopic-variance","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C046-C047: critical tanh mesoscopic law and reciprocal-mean correction

Version1, 20 October2026. Target3, kind moved. Proofs (unaudited).
These are direct finite-chain estimates and do not assume C026's functional
entrance limit. They use the independent positive-moment estimates of C027
and the exact inverse moments and drift calculations of C044/C045.
Literature novelty is not asserted.

Let K0>0 be fixed and

    K_(j+1)=n^(-1)sum_(i=1)^n tanh(sqrt(K_j)Z_(j,i))^2,

with independent standard Gaussian rows and layers. This is unshaped,
zero-bias tanh at weight variance1/n. Let V_j=1/(nK_j). These reciprocals
are finite almost surely; for sufficiently large n their required moments
are integrable by C044. No bounded replacement or extinction convention
is needed. Set Q=max(1,K0), so0<K_j<=Q at every layer.

## C046: quantitative mesoscopic variance law

For each finite T there are C_(K0,T),n0 such that for n>=n0,

    E|k K_k-1/2|<=C_(K0,T)[k^(-1/2)+sqrt(k/n)],
                                           1<=k<=floor(Tn).   (1)

Thus k_n K_(k_n)->1/2 in L1 when k_n->infinity and k_n/n->0.

Proof. C027's explicit positive moment bounds give, including k=0,1 by
increasing the constant,

    E K_j^p<=C_(K0,p,T)/(j+1)^p, p=1,2, j<=Tn.                (2)

The coarse reciprocal multiplier estimates C045(5) give

    E V_j<=C_(K0,T)(j+1)/n,
    E V_j^2<=C_(K0,T)(j+1)^2/n^2.                            (3)

Indeed, conditionally on K_j=q and V_j=v,
E V_(j+1)^p <=(1+C/n)v^p+(C/n)v^(p-1) for p=1,2.
Sum first for p=1, then for p=2, starting at V0=1/(nK0). All moments
are finite: conditional inverse sample moments are uniformly finite by
C044 on0<q<=Q, and iteration through finitely many layers preserves this.

Let M_k be the martingale of centered reciprocal increments. C045(5)
and (3) imply

    ||M_k||_2<=C[sqrt(k^3/n^3)+sqrt(k)/n].

The drift estimate C045(6), (2)-(3), and Minkowski give

    ||V_k-V0-2k/n-M_k||_2
        <=C[k(k+1)/n^2+log(k+1)/n+k/n^2
                                      +k(k+1)/n^(5/2)].

This is the C040 martingale argument with K replacing theta and a=2.
It uses no independence between the current state and its conditional
drift; only orthogonality of martingale differences across layers.
Consequently for Z_k=nV_k/k,

    ||Z_k-2||_2<=C[k^(-1/2)+sqrt(k/n)].

Since 1/Z_k=kK_k has a uniformly bounded second moment by (2), inversion
is controlled exactly as in C040: on Z_k>=1 the inverse map is Lipschitz;
on its complement Chebyshev and Cauchy-Schwarz bound the L1 contribution
by C||Z_k-2||_2. This proves(1).

In particular, for fixed t>0 and N=floor(nt),

    sum_(k=1)^(N-1) E K_k=(1/2)log(n)+O_(K0,t)(1),            (4)

because the absolute error term in E K_k is bounded by
C[k^(-3/2)+1/sqrt(nk)], whose sum is bounded through N<=tn.

## C047: a logarithmic bias for the exact reciprocal mean

For every fixed K0>0 and t>0,

    E[1/(nK_floor(nt))]
      = exp(2t)-1 -(5/6)exp(2t)log(n)/n+O_(K0,t)(1/n).        (5)

The limiting mean exp(2t)-1 is the mean of the reciprocal SDE
dV=(2V+2)dt+sqrt(2)VdW,V0=0. This numerical coefficient identifies the
leading logarithmic correction, not the coefficient of the remaining1/n
term. The statement concerns an exact integrable raw reciprocal mean,
unlike the ReLU angle reciprocal.

Proof. Write h=1/n. The exact conditional mean of the limiting linear
diffusion after time h from v is

    L_h(v)=(v+1)exp(2h)-1.

C045(4), subtracting the h^2 coefficient2v+2 of L_h(v)-v, gives on
K=q<=epsilon

    E[V_next | v]-L_h(v)
      =[2v-6-5/(3v)]/n^2+rho_n(v),
    |rho_n(v)|<=C[v/n^(5/2)
                   +(1+v+1/v+1/v^2)/n^3+v exp(-cn)].        (6)

On epsilon<q<=Q, v<=1/(n epsilon). The global inverse sample moment
bound gives E V_next<=C_Q v<=C/n. Both L_h(v)-v and the displayed main
correction in(6) are also O(1/n), since1/v=nq<=nQ. Hence the remaining
defect is bounded by C_Q/n on this large-variance range.

Along the exact chain, the expected number of large-variance visits is
bounded by epsilon^(-2)sum E K_k^2<=C_(K0,T), by (2). On the small range,
use (2)-(3) and1/V_k=nK_k in(6). Summation through N<=Tn yields

    sum_(k=0)^(N-1) E|rho_n(V_k)|<=C_(K0,T)/n.               (7)

For clarity, the inverse-square contribution is at most
n^(-1)sum E K_k^2=O(1/n); the inverse first-power contribution is
O(log(n+1)/n^2); the v/n^(5/2) term sums to O(n^(-3/2)); all remaining
terms are smaller or O(1/n). The large-variance bound was included
separately, so(7) does not apply the small-q Taylor series globally.

Let w_k=exp(2(t_n-(k+1)/n)), t_n=N/n. The affine nature of L_h makes
conditional-mean telescoping exact:

    E V_N - [(V0+1)exp(2t_n)-1]
      =sum_(k=0)^(N-1) w_k E[E(V_(k+1)|V_k)-L_h(V_k)].       (8)

All expectations are legitimate by (3). The weighted sum of the errors
in(7) remains O(1/n). The nonsingular correction2V_k-6 in(6) contributes
O(1/n), using (3). The singular correction contributes

    -(5/(3n)) sum_(k=0)^(N-1) w_k E K_k.

The k=0 term is O_(K0,t)(1/n). For k>=1,
|w_k-exp(2t)|<=C_t(k+1)/n, so (2) bounds the total weighted occupation
error by a constant. Equation(4) therefore gives

    sum_(k=1)^(N-1) w_k E K_k
                        =(exp(2t)/2)log(n)+O_(K0,t)(1).

Insert this into(8), and use V0=1/(nK0), |t_n-t|<=1/n. The initial-state
and fractional-layer effects are O(1/n). This proves(5).

## Scope

C047 is a first finite-width correction for an exactly critical unshaped
tanh scalar observable; it does not prove Target3's all-order uniform
finite-width cumulant expansion. Its proof does not require C026 and
never replaces the model by the shaped tanh model in Li-Nica-Roy.
Independent review is required for C044's inverse-tail deletion, the

body:
[Theorem thm:1 of arXiv:2608.05262, 'The law of $(1+1)$D SOS with an area tilt in a wedge'] Fix $\beta>0$, $\lambda>1$, $\mathfrak h > \theta_\star$ and $K\geq 1$. 
    Consider the line ensemble $\{\phi_k\}_{k=1}^K$ on $[-N,N]$ with a geometric area tilt,  as in  (eq:1d-sos-domain-many-phi,eq:1d-sos-many-curves-phi of the paper).  Then,
    \begin{enumerate}[(a), leftmargin=*]
\item \label[part]{part:a} 
As $N \to \infty$,  the $\mathbb R^K$-valued process of coordinates 
 \[ 
    \widehat\phi_k(t) := \frac{\phi_k(N t) - N\phi_k^\star(t)}{\sqrt {\alpha_k \,  N}}
 \]
(linearly interpolated),  converges weakly on $C([-1,1],\mathbb R^K)$ to rescaled,  independent Brownian bridges 
$(\mathsf{BB}_1, \ldots,\mathsf{BB}_K)$,  where for {\sc{\lowercase{iid}}} standard Brownian motions $W_k$,
\begin{equation} 
\mathsf{BB}_k (t) := \left\{
\begin{array}{ll}
W_k(v_\star(t/\alpha_k))-\frac{v_\star(t/\alpha_k)}{v_\star(1)}  W_k(v_\star(1))
\,,  & |t| \le \alpha_k \,,\\
0\,, & \alpha_k \le |t| \le 1 \,.
\end{array} \right.
\end{equation}
\item \label[part]{part:b} 
Fix $\varepsilon \in (0,\frac{1}{12})$ and consider the intervals
\[ 
I_N^{(-r)}:=-I_N^{(r)},  \qquad 
I_N^{(r)} := [\alpha_{r} N^{1/3} + 2 N^\varepsilon,\alpha_{r-1} N^{1/3} - 2 N^\varepsilon] \,,  \qquad 1 \le r \le K \,.
\]
Then,  for each $r=-K,\ldots,-1,1,\ldots, K$,  the $\mathbb R^{K+1-|r|}$-valued processes
\[ 
\underline{\psi}^{(r)}_N (u) := 
\frac{1}{\sqrt{\Lambda''(\theta_\star)}N^{1/3}} \big(\phi_{|r|} (N^{2/3} u),\ldots,\phi_K(N^{2/3} u) \big) 
 \]
converge 
subject to $I_N^{(r)}$-shifts
to the Brownian {\sc{\lowercase{gate}}} $\underline{X}^{(r)}$ 
of law 
$\mu^{\mathfrak o}_{\lambda,\mathfrak a_r,K-|r|+1}$.
Further,  the convergence
holds jointly over $r$,  with mutually independent limits.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let a<b be finite and f in C-infinity([a,b]). Let g(t)=product_i(t-t_i)^(k_i) be monic of positive degree, with distinct t_i in [a,b] and positive integer k_i. Write H(f,g) for the polynomial of degree<deg(g) matching f to order k_i at each t_i. The quotient Q(f,g)=(f-H(f,g))/g, defined at roots by smooth continuation, is C-infinity. If f^(r)(t)>=0 for every integer r>=0 and t in (a,b), then Q(f,g)^(r)(t)>=0 for every r>=0 on (a,b). If all these derivatives of f are strictly positive in (a,b), all derivatives of Q(f,g) are strictly positive there as well. The nonnegative conclusions extend to endpoints by continuity. The roots-in-the-interval and monic hypotheses are part of the statement. For functions smooth on [-1,1), the same conclusion on [-1,1) follows by applying the finite-interval statement on compact subintervals containing the roots and the evaluation point.
monic g has positive degree and all real roots in the specified interval
absolute monotonicity includes the zeroth derivative
strict absolute monotonicity means all derivatives positive in the interval interior
root values of Q are its smooth continuations

[Proposition of arXiv:2411.09257, 'Iterated Generalized Counting Process and its Extensions'] The state of $q$-iterated GCP are given as follows:
 For $q$ even, we have
{\footnotesize\begin{align*}
	\hat{p}^q(n,t)&=\sum_{s_q=0}^{\infty}\mathrm{Pr}\{M_q(t)=s_q\}\Big(\prod_{i=1}^{\frac{q}{2}-1}\sum_{\Omega(k_{2i},s_{2i})}\Big(\prod_{j_{2i}=1}^{k_{2i}}\frac{\lambda_{j_{2i}}^{n_{j_{2i}}}}{n_{j_{2i}!}}\Big)\exp(-\lambda_{2i+1}s_{2(i+1)})\sum_{\sum_{j_{2i+1}=1}^{k_{2i+1}}r_{j_{2i+1}}=z_{k_{2i}}}z_{k_{2i}}!\\
	&\ \ \cdot\prod_{j_{2i+1}=1}^{k_{2i+1}}\frac{j_{2i+1}^{r_{j_{2i+1}}}}{r_{j_{2i+1}}!}\exp(\lambda_{j_{2i+1}}s_{2(i+1)}\exp(-j_{2i+1})\lambda_{2i})\mathcal{B}_{r_{j_{2i+1}}}(e^{-j_{2i+1}\lambda_{2i}}\lambda_{j_{2i+1}}s_{2(i+1)})\Big)\\
	&\ \ \cdot\sum_{\Omega(k,n)}\Big(\prod_{j=1}^{k}\frac{\lambda_j^{n_j}}{n_j!}\Big)e^{-s_2\lambda_1}\sum_{\sum_{j_1=1}^{k_1}r_{j_1}=z_k}z_k!\Big(\prod_{j_1=1}^{k_1}\frac{j_1^{r_{j_1}}}{r_{j_1}!}\Big)\exp(e^{-j_1\lambda}\lambda_{j_1}s_2)\mathcal{B}_{r_{j_1}}(e^{-j_1\lambda}\lambda_{j_1}s_2)
\end{align*}}
 and for $q$ odd, we have
{\footnotesize\begin{align*}
\hat{p}^q(n,t)&=\sum_{s_{q-1}=0}^{\infty}\sum_{\Omega(k_{q-1},s_{q-1})}\Big(\prod_{j_{q-1}=1}^{k_{q-1}}\frac{\lambda_{j_{q-1}}^{n_{j_{q-1}}}}{n_{j_{q-1}}!}\Big)e^{-t\lambda_q}\sum_{\sum_{j_q=1}^{k_q}r_{j_q}=z_{k_{q-1}}}z_{k_{q-1}}!\Big(\prod_{j_q=1}^{k_q}\frac{j_q^{r_{j_q}}}{r_{j_q}!}\exp(\lambda_{j_q}te^{-j_q\lambda_{q-1}})\\
&\ \ \cdot\mathcal{B}_{r_{j_q}}(\lambda_{j_q}te^{-j_q\lambda_{q-1}})\Big)\bigg(\prod_{i=1}^{\lfloor\frac{q}{2}\rfloor-1}\sum_{s_{2i}=0}^{\infty}\sum_{\Omega(k_{2i},s_{2i})}\Big(\prod_{j_{2i}=1}^{k_{2i}}\frac{\lambda_{j_{2i}}^{n_{j_{2i}}}}{n_{j_{2i}!}}\Big)\exp(-\lambda_{2i+1}s_{2(i+1)})\sum_{\sum_{j_{2i+1}=1}^{k_{2i+1}}r_{j_{2i+1}}=z_{k_{2i}}}z_{k_{2i}}!\\

body:
[Theorem 17 (One-step nonconvex phase-atlas RG stability) of arXiv:2606.07931, 'Pointwise Complexity for Gaussian Fields:\\Upper Envelopes, Algorithmic Lower Bounds, and '] Under \eqref{eq:phase-chart-hessian-assumption}, the coarse marginal is again a finite phase-atlas mixture
\[
\nu_C(d\phi_C)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}w_a^+\nu_{C,a}(d\phi_C),
\qquad
\nu_{C,a}=Z_{C,a}^{-1}e^{-S_a^{\rm RG}(u)}\mathbf 1_{\Omega_{C,a}}\,du,
\]
where
\[
S_a^{\rm RG}(u):=-\log\int_{\Omega_{F,a}}e^{-S_a(u,v)}\,dv.
\]
Moreover \(S_a^{\rm RG}\) is \(H_a^{\rm RG}\)-strongly convex on \(\Omega_{C,a}\).  Hence every centered linear chart process
\[
Z_{a,x}:=\langle v_x,u\rangle-\mathbb E_{\nu_{C,a}}\langle v_x,u\rangle
\]
is sub-Gaussian with comparison metric
\begin{equation}
d_a(x,y)^2=\langle v_x-v_y,(H_a^{\rm RG})^{-1}(v_x-v_y)\rangle .
\end{equation}
Thus the usual sub-Gaussian chaining and the pointwise peeling argument give chartwise pointwise envelopes.  To make the event simultaneous over phases, one allocates failure probabilities \(\delta_a\), which adds the atlas code \(\log(1/\delta_a)\), for instance \(\log(1/w_a^+)\) or \(\log |\mathcal A|\).
title: One-step nonconvex phase-atlas RG stability

[Definition of arXiv:2606.13264, 'Interference Queueing Networks: A Replica Mean-Field Approach in the Symmetric Setting'] (K-Replica System)
    We denote by $Q^K=(q^{(K,l)}_i)_{l \in [1,K], i \in [1,N]}$ the K-Replica System which is a Markov chain on $(\mathbb{N}^N)^K$ defined by the generator : \begin{align}
        \mathcal{L}^Kf(q)
=
\lambda \!\sum_{i,l}\!\big(f(q + e_{(l,i)}) - f(q)\big)
-
\sum_{i,l}\!\mu^K_i(q)\big(f(q) - f(q - e_{(l,i)})\big)
\mathbf{1}_{\{q_{(l,i)}>0\}} ,
    \end{align}
where \begin{itemize}
    \item $e_{(l,i)}$ is the vector of $(\mathbb{N}^N)^K$ having a 1 position $l \times i $,
    \item $ \mu^K_i(t) = B \log_2\!\Biggl(1+\frac{1}{\,1+\frac{1}{K}\sum\limits_{k=1}^{K} I_i^k(t)}\Biggr)$,
    \item $I_i^k(t) = \sum_{j \neq i} \mathbf{1}_{\{q_j^{(K,k)}(t) > 0\}} \, l(d(i,j))$.
\end{itemize}

[Lemma 10 (Local Contraction Bound) of arXiv:2608.17374, '\textbf{On the Pseudo-Mixing of Kac's Walk}'] There is a universal constant $c_{\mathrm{loc}}>0$ such that the following holds. Let $X,Y\in \mathrm{St}(n,k)$ satisfy $\|X-Y\|\leq 1$, and let
\be
M = \max\left(\max_{a \in [n]} \| r_{a}(X)\|^{2}, \max_{a \in [n]} \|r_{a}(Y) \|^{2}\right).
\ee
Then there is a coupling $(X',Y')$ of one step of the $k$-column walk from $X$ and $Y$ such that
\be 
\mathbb{E}[\|X'-Y' \|^{2}\mid X,Y]
\leq \left(1 - \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{Mn^{2}} \right) \|X-Y\|^{2}.
\ee
After decreasing $c_{\mathrm{loc}}$ by a universal factor, the same coupling also satisfies the Frobenius-distance contraction
\be 
\mathbb{E}[\|X'-Y' \|\mid X,Y]
\leq \left(1 - \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{Mn^{2}} \right) \|X-Y\|.
\ee

body:
[Definition 1 (Geometric characteristic number of a THP) of arXiv:2608.03575, '2608.03575'] Let $P$ be a trivalent hyperbolic polyhedron in $\mathbb{H}^{3}$ and let $v$ be one of its vertices. Denote the three faces incident to $v$ by $f_{1}, f_{2}, f_{3}$, and write
\[
e_{ij}=f_{i}\cap f_{j}, \quad 1\le i<j\le 3.
\]
Let $\Theta_{ij}$ be the dihedral angle of $P$ along $e_{ij}$. For $\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}$, define
\[
\theta_{v}^{f_{i}}=\arccos\left(\frac{1+\cos\Theta_{ij}+\cos\Theta_{ik}-\cos\Theta_{jk}}{2\sqrt{1+\cos\Theta_{ij}}\sqrt{1+\cos\Theta_{ik}}}\right)
\]
Equivalently, $\theta_{v}^{f_{i}}$ is the angle at the vertex corresponding to $f_{i}$ in the auxiliary Euclidean triangle whose side lengths are $\ell_{ij}=\sqrt{2+2\cos\Theta_{ij}}$ for $1\le i<j\le 3$.

For a face $f$ of $P$, its geometric characteristic number is defined by
\[
L_{f}(P)=2\pi-\sum_{v\in f}\theta_{v}^{f}.
\]
The geometric characteristic number of $P$ is the collection $L(P)=(L_{f}(P): f\in F(P))$, where $F(P)$ denotes the set of faces of $P$.

[Thm 30 of arXiv:2607.13849, 'Rearranged Stochastic Heat Equation with an Entropy Gradient Structure'] Fix $T>0$ and assume that the parameter $\lambda$ in \eqref{eq:noise:1.8} belongs to $(1/2,1).$ Let $\left((X_t^{x^{*}})_{t\in [0,T]}\right)_{x \in L^2_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S})}$ denote the stochastic flow generated by \eqref{RHSE2} as constructed in Proposition \ref{propo:4.17}. Then there exists a constant $C_{\lambda}$ only depending on $\lambda$ such that, for any $t \in [0,T]$ and any bounded measurable function $f: L^2_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S}) \rightarrow \mathbb{R},$ the mapping $x \mapsto \mathbb{E}[f(X_t^{x^{*}})]$ is Lipschitz continuous on $L^2_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S})$ with Lipschitz constant given by $C_{\lambda}t^{-(1+\lambda)/2}$, that is, for all $x,y \in L^2_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S})$ we have
\[
|P_tf(x)-P_tf(y)|
\le C_\lambda t^{-(1+\lambda)/2}\|x-y\|_{L^2},
\quad \forall x,y \in L^2_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S}), t>0.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 30 of arXiv:2607.13849

[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Two variables $f,g:X\to\mathbb R$ are independent precisely when
$$E(\phi(f)\psi(g))=E(\phi(f))E(\psi(g))$$
happens, for any two measurable functions $\phi,\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$.

body:
[Theorem thm:pairwise-tail of arXiv:2607.00966, 'Dynamic Averaging on Regular Graphs'] There exists a universal constant \(c>0\) such that, for every finite connected \(d\)-regular graph \(G=(V,E)\), every deterministic sequence \(0\le w_t\le1\), every \(t\ge0\), every \(u,v\in V\), and every \(x\ge0\),
\[
\Pr\left(
|X_v(t)-X_u(t)|\ge x
\right)
\le
2\exp\left(
-c\min\left\{
\frac{x^2}{dR_{\mathrm{eff}}(u,v)+\Re_G+2},
\frac{x}{\Re_G+1}
\right\}
\right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Pairwise tail bound

body: [Definition of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $G$ be a compact Lie group, and let ${\mathcal{F}}$ be any collection of subgroups of $G$. We call a map $f\colon X\to Y$ of topological $G$-spaces an \emph{$\mathcal F$-equivariant weak equivalence} or \emph{${\mathcal{F}}$-equivariant fibration} if $f^H\colon X^H\to Y^H$ is a weak homotopy equivalence or Serre fibration, respectively, for every $H\in{\mathcal{F}}$.

body: [Lemma 10 (Counting the size of time-indexing sets) of arXiv:2607.14361, 'NeuralChaos: Optimal Adapted Approximation of Square Integrable Predictable Processes'] Let $T>0$ be a (fixed) time-horizon, $I_{\rm H}, J_{\rm H} \in \mathbb{N}$, and $i_{0} \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $J_{\rm H}\leq 2^{i_0}-1$. In addition, let $\Lambda_{I_{\rm H}, J_{\rm H}, i_0}\eqdef\{(i,k)\,:\,i_0 \leq i \leq i_0 + I_{\rm H},\,\,0 \leq k \leq J_{\rm H}\}$; in particular, $0 \leq k < 2^{i}$ for every $(i,k) \in \Lambda_{I_{\rm H}, J_{\rm H}, i_0}$. Let $\mathcal{S}_{I_{\rm H}, J_{\rm H}, i_0}^T\eqdef \bigcup_{i=i_0}^{i_0+I_{\rm H}}\left\{\frac{j T}{2^{i+1}}\,:\,j=0,\ldots,2 J_{\rm H}+2\right\}$ and $0=s_0<s_1<\ldots<s_{n_{\rm grid}} \leq T$ be the increasing enumeration of the elements in $S_{I_{\rm H}, J_{\rm H}, i_0}^T$.  Then $n_{\rm grid}=(J_{\rm H}+1)(I_{\rm H}+2)$. Moreover, for every Brownian component $r \in [D]_{+}$ the normalized Gaussian coordinate in Eq.~\eqref{eq:stochastic_haar_coordinate} can be computed from the Brownian samples on this finite grid. In particular, if $\mathbf{W}^{I_{\rm H}, J_{\rm H}, i_0} \eqdef [W_{s_0}^{\top},\ldots,W_{n_{\rm grid}}^{\top}]^{\top}$, then $\mathbf{W}^{I_{\rm H}, J_{\rm H}, i_0} \in \mathbb{R}^{(n_{\rm grid}+1)\times D}$.

[Theorem 17 (Heisenberg lower bounds) of arXiv:2605.27212, '2605.27212'] Fix an odd prime \(p\).  There are constants \(c_p>0\) and \(r_0(p)<\infty\)
such that, for every \(h=2m\ge2\) and every \(r\ge\max\{h+1,r_0(p)\}\),
the half-lazy PA-PRA walk on \(V_r(\Heis)\) satisfies
\[
    \tau_{\mathrm{mix}}
    \ge c_p\max\left\{r\log r,\,\frac{r(h+1)}{\log(e r)}\right\}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

associated with four distinct integer exponents.  The number of distinct
degree-$h$ Hilbert values $H_{C_A}(h)$ is $\Theta(h^3)$.  Moreover,
$\gg h^3$ such values already occur, inside the window in
(equation eq:localmain of the paper), among curves in the family from
Theorem~(thm:family of the paper) whose coordinate rings are arithmetically
Cohen--Macaulay of type two. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem Thm: prob of A_alpha of arXiv:2411.10296, 'Parking on a random rooted binary tree'] Let $T_\infty$ be a BGW(2,1/2) tree, conditioned on non-extinction, which is constructible as in Subsection 2.1. Assume that an independent Po$(\alpha)$ number of cars arrive at each of the vertices of $T_\infty$. Let $A_\alpha$ be the event that all of the arriving cars can park on the $T_\infty$. Then
    \[\mathds{P}(A_\alpha) = \begin{cases}
        e^{\alpha/2} \sqrt{\frac{\alpha^2 - 4\alpha + 2}{2(1-\alpha)}} & 0 \leq \alpha \leq 2-\sqrt{2} \\
        0 & \alpha > 2-\sqrt{2}.
    \end{cases} \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem Thm: prob of A_alpha of arXiv:2411.10296

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given complex random variables $f_1,f_2,f_3,\ldots$ whose real and imaginary parts are i.i.d., centered, and with common variance $t>0$, we have
$$\frac{f_1+\ldots+f_n}{\sqrt{n}}\sim C_t$$
with $n\to\infty$, in moments, where $C_t$ is the law of a complex variable whose real and imaginary parts are independent, and each following the law $g_t$.

[Proposition 18 of arXiv:2607.14948, 'Graph alignment in sparse inhomogeneous models via self-overlap'] \begin{enumerate}
        \item Let $\eps > 0$. Then, the subgraph $K[{V_{\leq(1-\eps)}}]$ is a union of connected components of $K$, each of which is a tree supported on a vertex set of size at most $\frac{1}{\eps}$.
        \item Let $k \geq 2$, and denote by $\Ker_k (K)$ the set of vertices inside the $k$-core of $K$. Then, $V_{\geq k} \subseteq \Ker_k(K) \subseteq V_{\geq \frac{k}{2}}$.
       
        \item Let $\rho_m = \max_{X \subseteq V} \dfrac{|K[X]|}{|X|}$. Then, $\rho_m = \max_{v \in V} w_K(v)$, and the set $X = V_{\geq \rho_m}$ maximises $\dfrac{|K[X]|}{|X|}$.

    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 36 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] Let $v_\sigma=c\sigma^{m-1}$, $s_\sigma=s(v_\sigma)$ and $\kappa_\sigma=s_\sigma/\sigma$. If $\phi(x)=e^{-\kappa_\sigma(x+L)}u(x)$, then
\[
\cA_{\sigma,m,L}\phi=e^{-\kappa_\sigma(x+L)}\left[\cB_\sigma u+a(x)u-\frac{\cH(v_\sigma)}{\sigma^m}u\right],
\]
where
\[
\cB_\sigma u=\frac1{\sigma^m}\left(\int_{-L}^{L}J_\sigma(x-y)e^{\kappa_\sigma(x-y)}u(y)\,dy-M(s_\sigma)u(x)\right)+cu'(x).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,L})=\frac{\cH(c\sigma^{m-1})}{\sigma^m}+\Lp(\cB_\sigma+a).
\]

[Definition 8 of arXiv:2603.26936, 'Sharp Riemannian heat kernel estimates on the cut locus and the Parabolic Anderson model'] A random field $\set{u(t,x)}_{t\geq 0,x\in M}$ is an It\^{o} mild solution to \eqref{eq: SHE} if all the following holds.
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item Every $u(t,x)$ is $\mathcal{F}_t-$measurable.
        \item $u(t,x)$ is jointly measurable with respect to $\mathcal{B}\otimes \mathcal{F}$, where $\mathcal{B}$ is the Borel $\sigma-$algebra on $\R_+\times M$
        \item For all $(t,x)\in (0,\infty)\times M$, we have $$\E \left[\int_0^t\iint_{M^2} \bm{G}_{\alpha,\rho}(z,z')P_{t-s}(x,z)u(s,z)P_{t-s}(x,z')u(s,z')m(dz)m(dz')ds\right]< \infty$$
        \item $u$ satisfies \eqref{pam:mild}.
    \end{enumerate}

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). Let f: {0,1}^n -> {0,1} be evaluated exactly by a randomized decision-tree algorithm T that, over its internal randomness, queries coordinate i with probability delta_i(T) (its revealment), and let Var(f) denote the variance of f under a product probability measure on the input. The OSSS inequality states Var(f) <= sum_{i=1}^n delta_i(T) Inf_i(f), where Inf_i(f) is the influence of coordinate i under the same measure. Consequently, exhibiting an algorithm with small maximal revealment forces the sum of influences to be large, giving lower bounds on total influence and noise sensitivity via algorithmic constructions; for critical planar percolation, an exploration-path algorithm gives revealments comparable to arm-event probabilities, and combined with quasi-multiplicativity this yields sharp bounds on noise sensitivity and, via the Duminil-Copin-Raoufi-Tassion route, on sharpness of the phase transition in all dimensions without reflection positivity or duality. The inequality does not directly compute Inf_i itself, does not apply to non-product (dependent-coordinate) measures without a separate generalization, and it is an inequality rather than an identity, so it can be loose or even vacuous if the algorithm chosen is not well matched to f's structure. Typical failure: Plugging in a naive, non-adaptive algorithm (e.g. querying coordinates in a fixed deterministic order) and expecting a sharp bound; the inequality is only informative when the algorithm is cleverly matched to the function's geometric structure, such as an exploration process for a crossing event, and a poorly chosen algorithm produces a valid but essentially vacuous bound that is easy to mistake for a genuine obstruction to sharper influence or sensitivity estimates. Canonical reference: O'Donnell, Saks, Schramm and Servedio, 2005, Proceedings of the 46th Annual IEEE Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science; Duminil-Copin, Raoufi and Tassion, 2019, Annals of Mathematics.

[Theorem thm:critical-toppling of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] Fix $\nu_0>0$ and $M<\infty$. For every $a\in(0,4/(4-d))$ there are $c>0$
	and $C<\infty$, depending only on $d$, $a$, $\nu_0$, and $M$, such that
	every i.i.d.\ mean-zero field with
	\[
		\Var(\zeta(0))\geq\nu_0^2,
		\qquad
		\mathbb{E}|\zeta(0)|^3\leq M\,\Var(\zeta(0))^{3/2}
	\]
	satisfies, for all $t\geq3$ and $L\geq2$ with $L^a\leq t/2$,
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbb{P}\Bigl(u_t(0)\leq \frac{t^{(4-d)/4}}{L}\Bigr)
		\leq CL^{-c}+C
		\begin{cases}
			(\log t)^{3/4}t^{-1/4}L^{a/4},&d\in\{1,3\},\\
			(\log t)^{7/4}t^{-1/2}L^{a/2},&d=2.
		\end{cases}
	\end{equation}

[Definition 11 (Interpolating metrics) of arXiv:2608.29427, '\small Positive mass and rigidity \\ for asymptotically flat tangent bundles'] Let \(\delta\) denote the Euclidean metric in the preferred coordinates near infinity. A Riemannian metric \(\widetilde g\) on \(TM\) is called an \emph{interpolating metric} if, on \(TU_\infty\),
	\begin{align*}
		\widetilde g_{(x,\y)}(X^h,Y^h)
		&=
		\bigl(
		\psi(x,\y)\,g_x
		+
		(1-\psi(x,\y))\,\delta
		\bigr)(X,Y),\\
		\widetilde g_{(x,\y)}(X^h,Y^v)
		&=
		a^c_{(x,\y)}(X,Y),\\
		\widetilde g_{(x,\y)}(X^v,Y^v)
		&=
		\bigl(
		\xi(x,\y)\,h_x
		+
		(1-\xi(x,\y))\,\delta
		\bigr)(X,Y),
	\end{align*}
	where \(g\) and \(h\) are Riemannian metrics on \(M\), \(a^c\) is a symmetric \((0,2)\)-tensor on \(TM\), and
	\[
	0\le\psi,\xi\le1
	\]
are smooth functions. We further assume that
	\[
	\psi(x,\y),\ \xi(x,\y)\longrightarrow0
	\qquad\text{as }|\y|\to\infty,
	\]
	and
	\[
	a^c_{(x,\y)}\longrightarrow0
	\qquad\text{as }|(x,\y)|\to\infty,
	\]
	with the latter convergence understood tensorially.
title: Interpolating metrics

[Theorem of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] Let $f \in \mathcal S_{1/2}$, the one-sided Gelfand-Shilov space, and let its Hermite polynomial expansion be denoted
 \[
   f(x)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_{n}\,h_{n}(x)

 \]
 in $L_2(N(0,1))$. 
The following two conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $f \in \mathcal S_{1/2}^{1/2}$, the two-sided Gelfand-Shilov space.
    \item The Hermite polynomial coefficients $a_n$ decay at an exponential rate, i.e. there exists $t > 0$ such that
    \[ |a_n| = O(\exp(-tn)). \]
\end{enumerate}
Either of the equivalent conditions implies that
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[3.] For any $r$-strictly-sub-exponential probability measure $\mu$, there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that the following is true. For any $\epsilon \in (0,1/2)$, there exists a polynomial $P$ of degree at most $C \log^r(1/\epsilon))$ such that 
    \[ \|f - P\|_{L_2(\mu)} \le \epsilon. \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 12 (Block biorthogonal identities) of arXiv:2608.30722, 'Intermediate Singular Values of Random Matrices\\ under Second-Moment and Anti-Concentrati'] Let $D$ be an invertible $n\times n$ matrix with columns $v_1,\dots,v_n$, and
let $[n]=S\sqcup T$ be a partition with $|S|=l$. Write
\[
  V_S := (v_j)_{j\in S},
  \qquad
  H_T := \Span(v_j:j\in T),
  \qquad
  P_T^\perp := P_{H_T^\perp}.
\]
Let $v_k^*=(D^{-1})^*e_k$ and $y_k^*:=P_{H_T}v_k^*$ for $k\in T$, and let
$B_T$ be the $(n-l)\times n$ matrix whose rows are $(y_k^*)^T$, indexed by
$k\in T$. Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item[\textnormal{(1)}] The matrix $B_T$ is determined entirely by the columns $\{v_j:j\in T\}$.
  \item[\textnormal{(2)}] For every $y\in\mathbb R^l$,
  \[
    \|D^{-1}P_T^\perp V_S y\|_2^2
    =
    \|y\|_2^2+\|B_TV_S y\|_2^2.
  \]
  In particular,
  \[
    \|D^{-1}P_T^\perp V_S y\|_2 \ge \|B_TV_S y\|_2.
  \]
  \item[\textnormal{(3)}] For every subcollection $V_J$ of columns of $V_S$,
  \[
    \|D^{-1}P_T^\perp V_J\|_{HS}^2
    =
    |J|+\|B_TV_J\|_{HS}^2.
  \]
  \item[\textnormal{(4)}] If $V_T:=(v_j)_{j\in T}$, then
  $B_TV_T=I$, $B_T$ vanishes on $H_T^\perp$, and
  \[
    \|B_T\|=s_{\min}(V_T)^{-1}.
  \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Block biorthogonal identities

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The chi squared laws have the following properties: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\chi_n^2=law(f_1^2+\ldots+f_n^2)$, with $f_i\sim g_1$, independent.

\item The density is given by $\chi_n^2=\frac{x^{n/2-1}e^{-x/2}}{2^{n/2}\Gamma(n/2)}\,dx$.

\item The moments are $M_k=n(n+2)\ldots(n+2k-2)$.

\item We have $E=n$, $V=2n$, $\gamma=\sqrt{8/n}$, $\kappa=3+12/n$.

\item The Fourier transform is $F(x)=(1-2ix)^{-n/2}$.
\end{enumerate}

[Definition def:URD of arXiv:2601.21762, 'Navier-Stokes with a fractional transport noise as a limit of multi-scale dynamics'] [URDog, EnergymethodRPDEs]
    Let $\alpha\in(\frac 13,\frac 12]$. An $\alpha$-continuous unbounded rough driver with respect to the scale $(H^{m})_{m>0}$ is a pair $(A^{1},A^{2})$ 
    of two index maps such that for any $s,t\in [0,T]$:
    \begin{align*}
        \norm{A^{1}_{s,t}}_{\mathcal{L}(H^{-m};H^{-(m+1)})} &\lesssim |t-s|^{\alpha}, \qquad m\in [0,2], \\
        \norm{A^{2}_{s,t}}_{\mathcal{L}(H^{-m};H^{-(m+2)})} &\lesssim |t-s|^{2\alpha}, \qquad
        m\in [0,1],
    \end{align*}
    and satisfies the Chen's relations: 
        $\delta A^{1}_{s,r,t}=0$ and $ \delta A^{2}_{s,r,t}=A^{1}_{r,t}A^{1}_{s,r}$  for all $ 0\leq s \leq r \leq t \leq T$.

body: Let G be a finitely generated group and, for a finite generating set, let gamma(n) count the elements of G expressible as a word of length at most n. G has polynomial growth if gamma(n) <= C n^d for constants C, d and all n. Gromov's theorem states that G has polynomial growth if and only if G is virtually nilpotent, i.e. has a nilpotent subgroup of finite index. Virtually nilpotent groups have polynomial growth by an earlier theorem of Wolf and Milnor; Gromov proved the converse using a compactness argument for rescaled Cayley graphs. Due to Mikhail Gromov, 1981.

[Lemma 9 (General Case Limit) of arXiv:2608.14143, 'Mod-$\phi$ convergence for random variables with cyclotomic generating functions'] Let $(s_N)_{N\in\N}$ be a sequence of positive integers. For each $N\in\N$, let $(a_{N,j})_{j=1}^N$ and $(b_{N,j})_{j=1}^N$ be sequences of positive integers. Define $h(w, z) := \log(\frac{1-e^{zw}}{-zw})$ for $w>0$, with $h(0, z) := 0$.
Recall the sequence
\[
K_N(z) := \Big( \prod_{j=1}^N \frac{a_{N,j}}{b_{N,j}} \Big) \Big(\prod_{j=1}^N \frac{1-e^{z b_{N,j}/s_N}}{1-e^{z a_{N,j}/s_N}}\Big).
\]
Define the sums $S_N^a(z) := \sum_{j=1}^N h(a_{N,j}/s_N, z)$ and $S_N^b(z) := \sum_{j=1}^N h(b_{N,j}/s_N, z)$. Assume there exist functions $I_a, I_b, C_a, C_b$ such that the following asymptotic expansions hold locally uniformly for $z$ in some domain $\mathscr{D} \subset \mathbb{C}$:
\begin{align*}
	S_N^a(z) &= N I_a(z) + C_a(z) + o(1),\qquad\text{and}\qquad S_N^b(z) = N I_b(z) + C_b(z) + o(1),
\end{align*}
as $N\to\infty$. Let $\phi(z) := I_b(z) - I_a(z)$. Then,
\begin{equation}
	\lim_{N\to\infty} \exp\big(-N \phi(z) \big) K_N(z) = \exp\big( C_b(z) - C_a(z) \big)
\end{equation}
locally uniformly on $\mathscr{D}$.

\]

Let phi, C: [0,T] -> R be continuous with C(t) >= 0 for all t, and let B >= 0 be a constant. If phi(t) <= B + integral_0^t C(s) phi(s) ds for all t in [0,T], then phi(t) <= B exp(integral_0^t C(s) ds) for all t in [0,T]. More generally B may be replaced by a nondecreasing continuous function B(t), with phi(t) <= B(t) exp(integral_0^t C(s) ds) pointwise. In particular, if phi >= 0 and phi(t) <= integral_0^t C(s) phi(s) ds, then phi is identically 0, which is the usual route to uniqueness and stability for ODE solutions.

[Lemma lem:kernel-sum of arXiv:2609.02544, 'A finiteness theorem for geodesic Leech wheels'] Let $M\ge3$, $R=\floor{(M-1)/2}$, and $\rho=\rho_R$, so that $R\ge1$ and the kernel $K_R$ of Lemma~(lem:kernel of the paper) is defined. Suppose $S\subseteq\{0,1,\ldots,M-1\}$ has $\abs S$ elements, of which $h$ exceed $R$. With $\zeta=\mathrm{e}^{2\pi i/M}$ and $F(z)=\sum_{a\in S}z^a$, if some $U>0$ satisfies $\abs{F(\zeta^t)}\le U$ for all $t\in\{1\}\cup\{2,4,6,\ldots,2R\}$, then
\begin{equation}
  \left(\frac\pi2+\rho\right)U
  \ge
  \sum_{a\in S}K_R\!\left(\frac{2\pi a}{M}\right)
  \ge\rho\abs S-\pi h.
\end{equation}

[Proposition 11 of arXiv:2604.09248, '\bfseries Limit laws for longest edges in empty region graphs'] For $d\in\mathbb{N}$ with $d\ge 2$, $u\in(0,\infty)$, and a continuous symmetric function $R:[-u,u]\to[0,\infty)$ let
$$
K := \Big\{ (x_1,\hdots,x_d)\in \RR^d: x_1\in[-u,u], \sum_{i=2}^{d} x_i^2\leq R(x_1)^2 \Big\}.

Assume that there exist $x_K\in K$ and $r_K>0$ such that $B^d(x_K,r_K)\subset K$. Then one can find a constant $c_K\in(0,\infty)$ only depending on $K$ and $d$ such that
\begin{equation}
\vol(K\setminus (\varrho K + x)) \geq c_K \|x\|    
\end{equation}
for all rotations $\varrho$ and all $x\in\RR^d$ with $K\cap(\varrho K+x)\neq\varnothing$.

body: Let f be holomorphic on some punctured neighborhood of a point z_0 in C, that is, on a disk around z_0 minus z_0 itself, and suppose z_0 is an essential singularity of f, meaning the Laurent series of f about z_0 has infinitely many negative-power terms. Then for every such punctured neighborhood, no matter how small, the image f(neighborhood) is dense in C: for every complex w and every epsilon > 0 there is a point z in the neighborhood with |f(z) - w| < epsilon. The great Picard theorem strengthens this to actual attainment of values.
title: Casorati-Weierstrass theorem

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2510.23130, 'Hidden regular variation for stochastic recursions with diagonal matrices\ \thanks{E.D. wa'] Assume \eqref{assump:alpha}, \eqref{assump:moments}, \eqref{assump:nondeg}, 
	 \eqref{assump:mixedmoments} and (as a sufficient condition for \eqref{assump:cramer}) that the law of $(\log |A_1|, \log |A_2|)$ has an absolutely continuous component with respect to the Lebesgue measure on $\R^2$.
	 Suppose $\P(|A_1|>1, |A_2|>1)>0$ and that $\supp(X)$ contains an open set.
	
		Assume that there is $\bb \xi^* \in D \cap (0,1)^2$ such that  $\nabla \phi(\bb \xi^*)$ is parallel to $(1,1)$. 
		Then there exists a non-zero Radon measure $\Lambda_2$ on $\R^2\setminus[\mathsf{axes}]$ such that for all $f\in \bfC (\R ^2\setminus[\mathsf{axes}])$, 
	\begin{equation}
	\lim_{t \to \infty}	(\log t)^{1/2}	t^{\xi^*_1+\xi^*_2}\E\big[ f(t^{-1/\alpha_1}X_1,t^{-1/\alpha_2}X_2) \big]= \int f(\bb x) \Lambda_2(d\bb x).
	\end{equation}
	In particular,
	\begin{equation}
		\lim_{t \to \infty}	(\log t)^{1/2}	t^{\xi^*_1+\xi^*_2}\P\big( |X_1|>t^{1/\alpha_1}, |X_2|>t^{1/\alpha_2} \big) \in (0,\infty).
	\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 3 of arXiv:2510.23130

[Theorem 24 (Coupling) of arXiv:2504.02435, 'Poisson-Voronoi percolation in higher rank'] Let $t_n\to\infty$, $\mu\in\mathbf M(\mathbf D)$ be such that $\mu_{t_n}\overset{v}\to \mu$ and let $\Upsilon$ be a Poisson point process on ${\bf D}$ with intensity $\mu$.
    There exists a coupling of $\Upsilon$ and $\Upsilon_{t_n}$, $n\in \mathbb{N}$, on the same probability space such that 
    $$
    \Upsilon=\sum_{i=1}^\infty \delta_{X_i} \quad \mbox{and} \quad \Upsilon_{t_n}=\sum_{i=1}^\infty \delta_{X_i^{(t_n)}},
    $$
    where $\{X_i(o)\}_{i\in \mathbb{N}}$ and $\{X_i^{(t_n)}(o)\}_{i\in \mathbb{N}}$ are strictly increasing, such that
    $$
    \lim_{n\to\infty} X^{(t_n)}_i= X_i
    $$
    for every $i\in \mathbb{N}$ a.s.

[Maintheorem 1 (Theorem~\ref{thm:h-equivalent}) of arXiv:2607.23526, 'Equivalence of Canonical and Microcanonical Ensembles for Euclidean Lattices'] Suppose the abelian group $\langle H(x):x\in\Lambda\rangle_{\Z}$ has rank $r$ and fix a $\Z$-basis $\{a_1,\cdots,a_r\}$. Write
\[H(x)=a\cdot F(x)^T,\quad a=(a_1,\cdots,a_r),\quad F(x)\in\Z^r.\]
For $\lambda\in\R^r$ such that $\lambda\cdot F(x)^T$ is positive definite, define
\[\bm{p}_{\lambda}(x):=\frac{e^{-\lambda\cdot F(x)^T}}{\sum_{y\in\Lambda}e^{-\lambda\cdot F(y)^T}},\quad\bm{m}(\lambda):=\E_{\bm{p}_{\lambda}}[F].\]
Let $E_N=a\cdot n_N^T$ with $n_N\in\Z^r$, and assume the exact shell
\[\left\{(x_1,\cdots,x_N)\in\Lambda^N:\sum_{i=1}^NH(x_i)=E_N\right\}\]
is non-empty. If there exist $\lambda_N\to\lambda$ such that $n_N-N\bm{m}(\lambda_N)=O(1)$, then for every $k\geq1$,
\[\left\|(\pi_k)_*\mu^{\sh}_{N,E_N}-(\pi_k)_*\bm{p}_{\lambda}^{\otimes N}\right\|_{\TV}\to0,\quad N\to+\infty.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem~\ref{thm:h-equivalent}

Lebesgue measure contained in the bounded open interval \(J\). There exists a constant \(c_{L,J,\beta}>0\) such that the following holds: if
\(v \in H^1_w(J^2)\) satisfies  that there exists an open neighborhood \(W\subset J^2\) of
\[
    \Delta_L\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\{(x,x):x\in L\}
\]
such that
\[

\]
then
\[
    \int_{J^2}
    \left(
        |v|^2+|\partial_x v|^2+|\partial_y v|^2
    \right)|x-y|^\beta\,dx\,dy
    \ge c_{L,J,\beta}.
\]

[Cor 35 of arXiv:2604.03777, 'Equilibrium fluctuations for a multi-species particle system with long jumps'] Let $\gamma \geq 1$, $0 \leq s \leq t \leq T$, $\delta \in [0, \; 1]$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}_+$. For $1 \leq \ell_n \leq L_n$, it holds
	\begin{align*}
	&	\mathbb{E}_{\nu_{\rho}} \Bigg[ \Bigg\{ \frac{\Theta(n) K_n}{n \sqrt{n} } \sum_{z=1}^{L_n-1} za(z)  \int_s^t \dd r \sum_{x}   \nabla H ( \tfrac{ \lfloor x - r v_n \rfloor }{n}  )    \big[   \Psi_{x, \ell_n}^{\alpha,\beta}(\eta_r^n) - \Psi_{x,L_n}^{\alpha,\beta}(\eta_r^n)  \big]  \Bigg\}^{2} \Bigg] \\
		\leq & \widetilde{C} \| \nabla H \|^{2}_{2,n} (t-s)^{1 + \delta} \Bigg( \frac{\big[ \Theta(n) K_n\big]^{\delta+1} }{n^{2}} +  \frac{\big[ \Theta(n) \big]^{1+\delta} (K_n)^2  }{n^{2}}  L_n^{(\gamma-1)(1-\delta)}  \ell_n^{ \delta} \Bigg)  \big\{ \mathbbm{1}_{ \{ \gamma > 1 \} } + \big[ \log(L_n) \big]^{2} \mathbbm{1}_{ \{ \gamma = 1 \} } \big\}.
	\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Prop 7 of arXiv:2608.23450, 'The Oldest Allele in a Moran Model'] For $n\geq1$, the transition kernel $Q_{n,k}^{(0,\theta)}=\Lambda_{n,k}T_n^{(0,\theta)}\psi_{n,k}$ satisfies 
    $$\Lambda_{n,k}T_n^{(0,\theta)}=Q_{n,k}^{(0,\theta)}\Lambda_{n,k}.$$
    Moreover, $Y_n^{(0,\theta)}$ is a time-homogeneous Markov chain with transition kernel $Q_{n,k}^{(0,\theta)}$ given explicitly by 
    \begin{align*}
        Q_{n,k}^{(0,\theta)}(\eta,\gamma)&=s_{w,w}^{(2)}\upsilon_{n-|\gamma|+\gamma_1}^{(0,\theta)}(\gamma_1)T_{|\eta|}^{(0,0)}(\eta, \gamma_2^k)\\
        &+s_{w,w}^{(2)}T_{|\eta|}^{(0,0)}(\eta, \gamma)\\
        &+s_{w,w-1}\upsilon_{n-|\gamma|+\gamma_1}^{(0,\theta)}(\gamma_1)p^{\downarrow}(\eta, \gamma_2^k)\\
        &+s_{w,w-1}p^{\downarrow}(\eta, \gamma)\\
        &+s_{w,w}^{(1)}\mathbbm{1}(\eta=\gamma)\\
        &+s_{w,w+1}p_{(0,0)}^{\uparrow}(\eta, \gamma)
    \end{align*}
    where $w=|\eta|$, when the initial distribution of $X_n^{(0,\theta)}$ is of the form $\mu\Lambda_{n,k}$.
title: Prop 7 of arXiv:2608.23450

body:
[Proposition propmain of arXiv:2605.01878, '\Large Random trade timing and power-law tails in realized prices'] Let $(X_t, t\ge 0)$ be a Markov-modulated L\'{e}vy process described in Section (smain1a of the paper), and let the trade time $T$, described in Sections (smain1b of the paper)--(smain1c of the paper), satisfy (equation iim of the paper) and (equation iimadd of the paper). Suppose that Assumption (asshol of the paper) holds and that there exists a positive real number $\alpha$ such that $r_D(A(-\alpha)) = -\log(1-p_{1})$. Then $\alpha$ is unique, and the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), ref=(\roman*)]
\item  There exist constants $0<C_1\le C_2<\infty$ such that
\begin{align} 
\widetilde{M}C_1 \le y^\alpha \mathbb{P}(P_T>y) \le \widetilde{M}C_2
\end{align}
for all sufficiently large $y$; that is, $P_T$ has a Pareto-type tail.
\item  Suppose, in addition, that either
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item the MGF $z\mapsto e^{\psi_j(z)}$ is nonlattice for some $j\in\mathcal E$, or
\item the transition-jump MGF $z\mapsto E[e^{zV_{jk}}]$ is nonlattice for some $j,k\in\mathcal E$ with $\varrho_{jk}>0$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, condition (a) holds whenever $\sigma_j^2>0$ for some $j\in\mathcal E$. Then
\[
\lim_{y \to \infty} y^\alpha \mathbb{P}(P_T>y) = \widetilde M/\alpha.
\]
\end{enumerate}
In (propmaina of the paper) and (propmainb of the paper), $\widetilde{M}$ is positive and given by
\[
\widetilde{M} = \left(\frac{q_{1}p_{1}}{1-p_{1}}\right) \frac{(w_0' x_{p})(y_{p}'1_N)}{-\,y_{p}' B^{(1)}(-\alpha)x_{p}},
\]
where $B(s) = e^{\log(1-p_{1})I+A(s)}$, $B^{(1)}(s) = \frac{d}{ds}B(s)$, and $x_p$, $y_p$ are right and left eigenvectors of $B(-\alpha)$ associated with the unit eigenvalue.
title: Proposition propmain of arXiv:2605.01878

[Lemma lem:trace.form.multicausal.cost of arXiv:2604.22453, 'Adapted Wasserstein Barycenters of Gaussian Processes'] Let \(\pi\in\mathrm{Cpl}_{\mathrm{mc}}(\mathbb{X}^1,\ldots,\mathbb{X}^K)\) be any multicausal coupling, not necessarily Gaussian. For each \(t\in[T]\), define
\[
\mathbf{P}_t:=\left(\mathbb{E}_\pi[\epsilon_t^k(\epsilon_t^\ell)^\intercal]\right)_{k,\ell=1}^K.
\]
Then \(\mathbf{P}_t\in\mathscr{P}_+(K,d)\) for every \(t\), and 
\begin{equation}

\mathbb{E}_\pi\left[\sum_{k=1}^K \lambda_k \left\|X^k - \phi^0(X^1, \ldots, X^K)\right\|_2^2\right]
=\Phi(\mathbf{P}) = \sum_{t=1}^T\Phi_t(\mathbf P_t).
\end{equation}
In particular every multicausal coupling satisfies
\begin{equation}

\mathbb{E}_\pi\left[\sum_{k=1}^K \lambda_k \left\|X^k - \phi^0(X^1, \ldots, X^K)\right\|_2^2\right]
\ge\sum_{t=1}^T\min_{\mathbf P_t\in\mathscr P_+(K,d)}\Phi_t(\mathbf P_t).
\end{equation}

body:
[Lemma lem:A1 of arXiv:2602.00988, 'Wealth exchange under ceiling and flooring constraints: a modified Bennati–Dragulescu–Yako'] Assume that ${\bf x} = (x_0,x_1,\cdots) \in \ell^1(\mathbb N)$ satisfies $\sum_{k\geq 0} (k+1)\,|x_k| \leq C$ and $\sum_{k\geq 0} (k+1)\,|x_k|^2 \leq \frac{C}{N}$ for some constants $C > 0$ and $N \geq 1$. Then there exists a universal constant $L > 0$ (independent of $N$ and ${\bf x}$) such that
$\|x\|_{\ell^1} \leq \frac{L\,\sqrt{\log N}}{\sqrt{N}}$.
title: Lemma lem:A1 of arXiv:2602.00988

[Definition d:lattice-inf of arXiv:2510.13659, 'On the energy image density conjecture of Bouleau and Hirsch'] Let $\Lambda$ be some $\sigma$-finite Borel measure on $(X,d)$ and let $\mathcal{F}$ be any collection of measurable functions. Then
		\[
		G= \bigwedge_{f\in \mathcal{F}} f 
		\]
		is a   measurable  function   that  satisfies the following properties. 
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item ($G$ is a lower bound for $\mathcal{F}$) For all $f \in \mathcal{F}$, we have $G(x)\le f(x)$ for $\Lambda$-a.e. $x\in X$, and
			\item ($G$ is maximal among lower bounds) For any other function $\widetilde{G}(x)$ which satisfies the condition in (1),  we have $\widetilde{G}(x)\le G(x)$ for $\Lambda$-a.e. $x\in X$.
		\end{enumerate}
title: Definition d:lattice-inf of arXiv:2510.13659

body: Consider finite rooted trees with vertices labeled from a fixed well-quasi-ordered set. One tree topologically embeds in another if there is an injective, ancestor-order-preserving map of vertices to vertices sending labels to weakly larger labels and sending each edge to a path, these paths being internally vertex-disjoint. Kruskal's tree theorem states that finite labeled trees, ordered by topological embeddability, form a well-quasi-order: in any infinite sequence of such trees, some tree embeds into a later one. The theorem is unprovable in the subsystem ATR_0 of second-order arithmetic. Its associated TREE function, bounding sequences of trees with at most n labels, grows far faster than the Ackermann function. Proved by Joseph Kruskal in 1960.
title: Kruskal's tree theorem

[Theorem 1 (Arizmendi and Perales {\cite[Proposition 3.3) of arXiv:2604.13819, 'Convolution, cumulants and infinitesimal generators in the formal power series ring'] {arizmendi2018cumulants-joctsa}}]
Given $d \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}$, the finite free cumulants $\kappa_{1}^{(d)}, \dots, \kappa_{d}^{(d)}$ are unique maps satisfying the following conditions. 
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (i)]
\item $\kappa_{i}^{(d)}(f)$ is a polynomial in $p_{1}(f), \dots, p_{i}(f)$ with leading term $\frac{d^{i-1}}{(d)_{\underline{i}}} p_{i}(f)$. 
That is, there exists a polynomial $F_{i}$ in $i-1$ variables such that 
$$
\kappa_{i}^{(d)}(f) = \frac{d^{i-1}}{(d)_{\underline{i}}}p_{i}(f) + F_{i}(p_{1}(f), \dots, p_{i-1}(f)).
$$ 
\item Homogeneity: $\kappa_{i}^{(d)}(D_{r}f) = r^{i}\kappa_{i}^{(d)}(f)$ for any $r \in \mathbb{R}$ and $i \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}$.
\item Additivity: $\kappa_{i}^{(d)}(f \boxplus_{d} g) = \kappa_{i}^{(d)}(f) + \kappa_{i}^{(d)}(g)$. 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Ding-Lee-Peres Question 5.2 (arXiv:1004.4371, Section 5: when t_hit = o(t_cov), are the cover-time fluctuations of order t_hit?) is answered in the negative. On the clique-star G_k (a k-clique with one pendant leaf at each clique vertex; t_hit = 2k^2 + k + 1) the cover time satisfies Var(tau_cov) ~ t_hit t_cov and (tau_cov - E tau_cov)/sqrt(Var tau_cov) converges to a standard Gaussian; on the double star D_k (t_hit = 6k + 3) the normalised fluctuations have a half-normal limit. The proofs use exact first-step hitting systems, an excursion transform f_k with mu = k^2 - k + 2 and sigma^2 = k^4 - 4k^2 + 5k - 2, stage and coupon-clock closed forms, a residual lemma (the trap is last with probability 1/(r+1)), second-order expansions with explicit error 3k log k + 5k, moderate deviations by Gartner-Ellis at speed a_k^2, an operational-time construction exact in law (tau = 2P + J - 1), and an occupation CLT with covariance (2/q) L^+.

[Definition def:A of arXiv:2605.15545, 'Crossover from subcritical to critical decay: \\ random walk, self-avoiding walk, percolat'] Let $d \ge 1$ and let $M,K_{\mathrm{IR}},\zeta > 0$ be given.
We define $\mathcal{Q}_{M,K_{\mathrm{IR}},\zeta}$ to be the set of pairs of functions $(Q,g)$,
each mapping ${\mathbb Z^d}$ into $\mathbb{R}$, such that the following bounds apply:
\begin{gather}

\norm{ Q(y) }_{1} ,\,
\bignorm{ \abs y ^{2+\zeta}  Q(y) }_{1}
	\le M ,
\\

\mathrm{Re}\,[ \hat Q(0)  - \hat Q(k) ]
	\ge K_{\mathrm{IR}} \abs k ^2 	
	\qquad (k\in {\mathbb T^d}) ,
\\

\norm{ g(y) }_{1} ,\,
	\bignorm{ \abs y ^{\zeta} g(y) }_{1}  ,\,
    \bignorm{ \abs y ^{2}  g(y) }_{ p_d \wedge 2  }
	\le M ,
\end{gather}
with $p_d=2$ for $d=1$ and $p_d=\frac{d}{d-2+(\zeta\wedge 2)}$ for $d \ge 2$.
For $d \ge 4$, we additionally assume that
\begin{equation} 
\bignorm{ \abs y^{d-1} Q(y) }_{ \frac d 3 \wedge 2},\,
\bignorm{ \abs y^{d-1} g(y) }_{ 2}
	\le M .
\end{equation}
title: Definition def:A of arXiv:2605.15545

[Definition 24 of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] The morphism $\pi:X\rightarrow X/G$ is an \emph{HKG cover} if the following conditions hold.

\medskip
{\bf (1)} We have $X/G\cong \mathbb P_k^1$ and the number of branch points is $\min(2,m)$.

\smallskip
{\bf (2)} There exists one branch point over which $\pi$ is totally and wildly ramified with inertia group $G$. 

\smallskip
{\bf (3)} If $m>1$, the second branch point is tamely ramified and has $\Sigma$ as an inertia group.

[Lemma lem:PF-vs-BE of arXiv:2605.16244, 'Analysis of a twisted Bose--Einstein Markov chain with applications to sampling Catalan st'] Let $K_{\mathrm{PF}}$ and $\pi_{\mathrm{PF}}$ be the transition kernel and stationary distribution of the Burnside process on $\mathrm{PF}_n$. \[
 K_{\mathrm{PF}}(x,y)=(n+1)K_{\mathrm{BE}}(x,y)

 \pi_{\mathrm{PF}}(x)=(n+1)\pi_{\mathrm{BE}}(x).
\]

[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2608.19151, 'Continuous-Time Reinforcement Learning for Controlled Hawkes Jump-Diffusions'] Fix $K\ge1$ and a deterministic Markov policy
$ \pi^\zeta\in\mathcal U$.
Suppose that
\[
    J_K^\zeta
    \in
    \mathcal C^{1,2,1}
    \left(
        [0,T]\times
        \mathbb R^{d_x}\times(\mathbb R^m)^K
    \right)
\]
where $\mathcal C^{1,2,1}$ means once continuously differentiable in time,
twice continuously differentiable in $x$, and once continuously
differentiable in each memory variable $\mathbf z^k$. Assume moreover that there exist $C>0$ and $\ell \in [1,p^*-2]$ such that,

\begin{align}
    &\norm{J_K^\zeta(u,x,\mathbf z^K)}
    +
    \norm{
        \partial_t
        J_K^\zeta(u,x,\mathbf z^K)
    }
    +
    \norm{\nabla_x J_K^\zeta(u,x,\mathbf z^K)} + \norm{\nabla_{\mathbf z^K} J_K^\zeta(u,x,\mathbf z^K)} \notag \\
    &+ \norm{\nabla_{xx} J_K^\zeta(u,x,\mathbf z^K)}\le
    C
    \left(
        1+\norm{x}^{\ell}
        +\norm{\mathbf z^K}_{\mathcal Z_K}^{\ell}
    \right),
    
\end{align}
 Then $J_K^\zeta$ satisfies
\begin{align}
    &
    \mathcal L_K^{
        \pi^\zeta(t,x,\mathbf z^K)
    }
    J_K^\zeta(t,x,\mathbf z^K)
    -
    \rho J_K^\zeta(t,x,\mathbf z^K)
    +
    c\left(
        t,x,
        \pi^\zeta(t,x,\mathbf z^K)
    \right)
    =
    0,
    
\end{align}
for $(t,x,\mathbf z^K)
    \in
    [0,T)\times
    \mathbb R^{d_x}\times(\mathbb R^m)^K,$
with terminal condition
\begin{equation}

    J_K^\zeta(T,x,\mathbf z^K)
    =
    g(x).
\end{equation} Conversely, any function $v$ satisfying the same smoothness,
growth, and integrability conditions and solving
\eqref{eq:fixed_policy_bellman_bold}--
\eqref{eq:fixed_policy_terminal_bold}
coincides with $J_K^\zeta$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 8 of arXiv:2608.19151

[Lemma replace_selection_sets_by_independent_copies of arXiv:2606.09386, 'High-degree vertices in uniform recursive directed acyclic graphs with freezing'] Fix $k\in\mathbb{N}$, $\alpha\in(0,m+1)$, $D>m(m+1)$, and set $t_n\coloneq \lceil(h_n^+)^{\gamma_0}\rceil$. Let $\mathbf x$ be a choice sequence that satisfies Assumption~$\hyperref[ass:A]{\mathbf{x}}$(item:geq1 of the paper) and~(item:lb of the paper) for $I_{\hyperref[ass:A]{\mathbf{x}}} \leq t_n$. [Theorem th:intro-Maria!! of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] (Theorem (Maria!! of the paper))
  Let $\varrho (N)$ be a sequence of probability measures on
  $\hat{U} (N)$ such that for every finite $r$ one has
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} N \left( \frac{1}{N} \log S_{\varrho (N)}^{U
    (N)} (u_1, \ldots, u_r, 1^{N - r}) - \sum_{i = 1}^r \Psi (u_i) \right) =
    \sum_{i = 1}^r \Phi (u_i), 
  \end{equation}
  where $\Psi, \Phi$ are analytic functions in a complex neighborhood of $1$ and the
  above convergence is uniform in a complex neighborhood of $1^r$. Then for every $k
  \in \mathbb{N}$ we have
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} N \left( \frac{1}{N} \sum_{\lambda \in
    \hat{U} (N)} \varrho (N) [\lambda] \sum_{i = 1}^N \left(
    \frac{\lambda_i + N - i}{N} \right)^k -\mathbf{m}_k \right)
    =\mathbf{m}'_k, 
  \end{equation}
  where 
  \begin{equation}
    \mathbf{m}_k = \sum_{m = 0}^k
    \frac{k!}{m! (m + 1) ! (k - m) !}  \left. \frac{\mathrm{d}^m}{\mathrm{d} x^m} (x^k
    (\Psi' (x))^{k - m}) \right|_{x = 1}, 
  \end{equation}
  \begin{equation}
    \mathbf{m}'_k = \sum_{m = 0}^{k - 1} \frac{k!}{m! (m + 1) ! (k - m - 1) !}
    \left. \frac{\mathrm{d}^m}{\mathrm{d} x^m} \left( x^k \left( \Phi' (x) -
    \frac{1}{2 x} \right) (\Psi' (x))^{k - m - 1} \right) \right|_{x = 1} .
    
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem th:intro-Maria!! of arXiv:2412.09290

[Definition 32 (Metric duality and musical notation) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] If $V$ is a spacetime vectorfield, then $V_{\flat}$ denotes the one-form that is
	$\gfour$-dual to $V$, i.e., $(V_{\flat})_{\alpha} = \gfour_{\alpha \beta} V^{\beta}$.
	Consistent with the conventions of Sect.\,\ref{SS:NOTATIONANDCONVENTIONS},
	we typically write $V_{\alpha}$ instead of $(V_{\flat})_{\alpha}$.
	
	If $Y = Y^B \geop{x^B}$ is an $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent vectorfield, 
	then $Y_{\flat}$ denotes the $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent one-form that is $\gtorus$-dual to $Y$,
	i.e., for $A=2,3$, $(Y_{\flat})_A = \gtorusdoublearg{A}{B} Y^B$. 
	Since $Y$ is $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent, $Y_{\flat}$ can also be viewed as the dual of
	$Y$ with respect to $\gfour$, i.e., 
	$(Y_{\flat})_{\alpha} \eqdef Y_{\flat} \cdot \partial_{\alpha} = \gfour(Y,\partial_{\alpha})
	= \gfour_{\alpha \beta} Y^{\beta}
	$.
	Similarly, if $\upxi$ is an $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent one-form, 
	then $\upxi^{\sharp}$ denotes the $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent vectorfield that is $\gtorus$-dual to $\upxi$,
	i.e., for $A=2,3$, $(\upxi^{\#})^A = (\gtorus^{-1})^{AB} \upxi_B$, where 
	$\upxi_B = \upxi \cdot \geop{x^B}$.
	Similarly, if $\upxi$ is a symmetric type $\binom{0}{2}$ $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent tensorfield, 
	then $\upxi^{\sharp}$ denotes the type $\binom{1}{1}$ $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent tensorfield
	obtained by raising one index of $\upxi$ with $\gtorus^{-1}$,
	while
	$\upxi^{\sharp \sharp}$ denotes the type $\binom{2}{0}$ $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent tensorfield
	obtained by raising both indices of $\upxi$ with $\gtorus^{-1}$.
title: Metric duality and musical notation

body: Sylvester's law of inertia is a theorem in matrix algebra about certain properties of the coefficient matrix of a real quadratic form that remain invariant under a change of basis. Namely, if is a symmetric matrix, then for any invertible matrix , the numbers of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues of are constant. This result is particularly useful when is diagonal, as the inertia of a diagonal matrix can easily be obtained by looking at the signs of its diagonal elements.

Let X_1, ..., X_n be INDEPENDENT random variables taking values in arbitrary measurable spaces - they need NOT be identically distributed and need not be real-valued - and let Z = f(X_1, ..., X_n) with E[Z^2] < infinity. Let X_i' be an independent copy of X_i, independent of everything else, and put Z^{(i)} = f(X_1, ..., X_{i-1}, X_i', X_{i+1}, ..., X_n). Then Var(Z) <= (1/2) sum_{i=1}^n E[ (Z - Z^{(i)})^2 ] = sum_{i=1}^n E[ ((Z - Z^{(i)})_+)^2 ]. Equivalently, and often more convenient, Var(Z) <= sum_{i=1}^n E[ (Z - Z_i)^2 ] for ANY random variables Z_i that are measurable functions of the n-1 variables other than X_i; taking Z_i = inf over the i-th coordinate of f gives the version used for suprema and for first-passage times. Equality in the replace-one bound (in either form) holds if and only if f is a sum of functions of the individual coordinates; equality in the bound with arbitrary Z_i holds if and only if, in addition, Z_i = E[Z | X_j, j != i] almost surely for every i. Independence is the only structural hypothesis and it is essential; the inequality is FALSE for dependent coordinates. Applied with a bounded-difference function it recovers the variance half of McDiarmid's inequality; applied to first-passage percolation with the geodesic length as the influence bound it produces the linear variance upper bound. [Efron and Stein (1981), Steele (1986); see Boucheron, Lugosi and Massart, Concentration Inequalities, Theorem 3.1]
X_1, ..., X_n independent (arbitrary measurable state spaces, not necessarily identically distributed)
E[Z^2] < infinity
X_i' an independent copy of X_i

Now let E^{(i)} denote expectation with respect to X_i alone, holding all other coordinates fixed. Own-work draft; T419-C006 v1, proof (unaudited), no novelty claim. Let Delta be any nonzero m-by-p matrix of rank at most r and X a fixed full-row-rank p-by-n design. For noiseless Y=Delta X, the global rank-r empirical least-squares estimate equals Delta, so its isotropic population parameter risk is zero. Simultaneous factor GD from B0=0 and nondegenerate Gaussian A0, with any step schedule fixed conditional on X independently of A0, almost surely has B_t A_t != Delta at every finite t. Each finite-iterate entry is a polynomial in A0; at A0=0 both factors remain zero, so a residual entry corresponding to nonzero Delta_ij has a nonzero constant term. Its zero set is Lebesgue-null, and a countable union over t remains null. This also excludes exact recovery at an almost-surely finite integer stopping time selecting these iterates. Consequently a finite-time constant-factor comparison to the noiseless zero-risk benchmark needs a limit, an additive optimization tolerance or other qualification. This does not cover arbitrary initialization-dependent adaptive step rules and does not refute the intended infinite-time or noise-dependent-stopping target.

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2604.10310, 'Weak convergence from projections along a positive-measure set of directions'] Let \((P_n)_{n\ge1}\) be Borel probability measures on
		\(\mathbb R^d\), with \(d\ge2\), and let \(A\subset\mathbb S^{d-1}\) be
		a Borel set with \(\sigma(A)>0\). Assume that, for every \(u\in A\),
		the sequence \(\bigl(\pi_u(P_n)\bigr)_{n\ge1}\) converges weakly to
		some probability measure \(N_u\) on \(\mathbb R\), and that each
		\(N_u\) has finite moments of all orders and is moment-determinate.
		Then there exists a Borel probability measure \(N\) on \(\mathbb R^d\)
		such that \(P_n\weakto N\). Moreover, \(\pi_u(N)=N_u\) for every
		\(u\in A\), and \(N\) is the unique Borel probability measure on
		\(\mathbb R^d\) with this property.

[2 17 of arXiv:2606.10058, 'Mean First Passage Times and Fundamental Tensors of Higher Order Markov Chains'] For the $(m-1)$th order ergodic chain $X$ whose transition tensor ${\cal P}$ is partitioned as (\ref{part0}), let $\tilde X$ be the modified absorbing chain whose transition tensor has the form (\ref{part}) with $A=\{n\}$.  Then, $\nu$ in (\ref{nu}) can be represented by 
\be

\nu={\cal E} \boxtimes \sigma = \sum_{k=0}^\infty  {\cal E} \boxtimes {\cal Q}^k,.
\ee
where $\sigma$ is the fundamental tensor of $\tilde X$ and ${\cal E} \in \mathbb R^{1 \times (n-1) \times n \times \cdots \times n}$ is an $m$th order tensor of all ones. In addition, as a linear system, (\ref{nu}) is nonsingular, and its unique solution yields $\nu$ in (\ref{nuser}). Once $\nu$ is available, $\omega$ can be determined from (\ref{ome}). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma lem:reunif of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] Let $w$ be a periodized kernel and $y$ an
		$\mathcal{F}_{n-1}$-measurable random variable. Then, conditionally
		on $\mathcal{F}_{n-1}$, the multiplier $w_{\alpha_{n}}(y)$ is
		distributed as $W := w(U)$ with $U$ uniform, independently of
		$\mathcal{F}_{n-1}$. Consequently, for every fixed $z$, the
		multipliers $V_{j} := w_{\alpha_{j}}(S_{j-1}(z))$ are independent
		copies of $W$, and
		\begin{equation}
			\log S_{n}'(z) = \sum_{j=1}^{n}\log V_{j}
			
		\end{equation}
		is a random walk with independent identically distributed steps.
		For every harmonic shape $w_{k}$ the step law is the same,
		$W = 2\sin^{2}(\pi U)$.

body:
[Lemma Lemma 3 of arXiv:2411.13419, 'Forest Fire Model on $\Z_{+}$ with Delays'] Assume $\Delta\equiv 0$ and fix some $\epsilon>0$.  Let
$$
F_n=F_n(\epsilon)=\{f_{n,1}\ge (1-\epsilon)\log n\}.
$$
Then 
$$
\mathbb{P}\left(F_n^c\right)<e^{-n^\epsilon}
$$  
and hence the event $F_n^c$ a.s.\ occurs only finitely often.
title: Lemma Lemma 3 of arXiv:2411.13419

[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2606.11389, 'Instability of a nonlinear oscillator with small friction and small additive noise'] (i)  $G_1(h)$ and $G_2(h)$ are analytic functions of $h$ in a
neighborhood of 0.  As $h \to 0$ we have
 \begin{align*}
 G_1(h) & =  \frac{3}{4} - \frac{87h}{32} +
 \frac{657h^2}{64} + O(h^3), \\
   G_2(h) & = h+\frac{15 h^2}{8}-\frac{25 h^3}{16}+ O(h^4).
 \end{align*}

(ii) As $h \to \infty$ we have
 $$
 G_1(h) \sim \frac{1}{4h}, \hspace{3em} G_1'(h) \sim
 -\frac{1}{4h^2},
   \hspace{3em} G_1''(h) \sim \frac{1}{2h^3},
 $$
 and
 $$
 G_2(h) \sim \frac{24}{5}\sigma^2 \gamma_1 h^{3/2}, \hspace{2em} G_2'(h) \sim
\frac{36}{5}\sigma^2 \gamma_1 h^{1/2},
   \hspace{2em} G_2''(h) \sim  \frac{18}{5}\sigma^2 \gamma_1 h^{-1/2},
 $$
where $\gamma_1 = 2E(2^{-1/2})/K(2^{-1/2}) - 1 \approx 0.457$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Theorem thm:oco-lower of arXiv:2608.25182, 'Minimax Alternating Regret \\for the Experts Problem and Online Convex Optimization'] There exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that, for every $d\ge2$ and $T\ge1$, there exists a $d$-dimensional compact convex set $\mathcal{X}$ with the following property: for every possibly randomized learner, there exists an oblivious sequence of continuous convex loss functions $f_1,\ldots,f_T:\mathcal{X}\to[0,1]$ such that \begin{align} \mathbb{E}[\operatorname{Reg}^{\mathrm{alt}}_T] \geq c\cdot d\log\left(1+\frac{T}{d}\right),  \end{align} where the expectation is over the learner's internal randomness. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:lyapunov-nonexplosivity of arXiv:2511.10223, 'Stochastic Reaction Networks Within Interacting Compartments with Content-Dependent Fragme'] Let $X$ be a continuous-time Markov chain on a countable state space $\mathbb S$ with generator $\mathcal L$. Suppose $V$ is a function on $\mathbb S$ which satisfies $V\to\infty$ in the sense that $\{x\in\mathbb S:V(x)<y\}$ is finite for every $y\in(-\infty,\infty)$. If there are constants $c,d\ge 0$ so that $\mathcal LV(x)\le cV(x)+d$ for all $x$, then $X$ is not explosive.

    See Theorem 2.1 in [Meyn_Tweedie_1993].

body:
[Theorem 26 (Benjamini--Schramm parabolicity) of arXiv:2608.03575, '2608.03575'] Let \(P_n\) be a sequence of finite trivalent hyperbolic polyhedra, and
let \(f_n\) be chosen uniformly from \(F(P_n)\). Assume that
\[
    |F(P_n)|\longrightarrow\infty
\]
and that the finite rooted marked dual triangulations converge locally in
distribution:
\[
    \bigl(G(P_n),\rho_n,\Theta_{P_n}\bigr)
    \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{\mathrm{law}}
    (G,\rho,\Theta).
\]
Suppose that \((G,\rho,\Theta)\) is almost surely infinite, locally
finite, simple, one-ended, tame, and satisfies
\emph{(Z1)--(Z4)}. Then \((G,\rho,\Theta)\) is unimodular and
\[
    \mathbb E[\deg_G(\rho)]=6,
    \qquad
    \mathbb E[L_\rho(G,\Theta)]=0.
\]
Moreover, every ergodic component of its law is RCP-parabolic and
invariantly amenable. Consequently, the infinite trivalent hyperbolic
polyhedron associated with the limiting RCP is almost surely
parabolic.

No moment or uniform-integrability assumption on the degrees is
required.

[Theorem 6 (transition density) of arXiv:2605.13648, 'Sticky CIR process with potential: invariant measure and exact sampling'] On $(0,\infty)$, the Lebesgue density $f$ of the CIR process defined by \cref{eq-CIR4} solves
  \[
  \partial_t f = -\partial_u\!\left(\left(\tfrac{\delta-1}{\beta u}
    -\lambda u\right)f\right) + \tfrac{1}{\beta}\partial_{uu}f.
  \]
  If $p$ denotes the density with respect to the speed measure $m$,
  then at $u=0$ the sticky (Wentzell) boundary condition holds
  \begin{equation}
    
    \partial_s p(t,0^+) = \tfrac{1}{\mu}\,\partial_t p(t,0),
  \end{equation}
  where $\partial_s = (1/s')\partial_u$ is the scale derivative.

body: Tarski's truth definition defines the satisfaction relation \mathcal{M} \models \varphi[s] by structural induction on formulas: an atomic formula R(t_1, \dots, t_n) is satisfied if the interpreted tuple belongs to R^\mathcal{M}; boolean connectives follow classical truth tables; and \mathcal{M} \models \exists x \, \psi[s] iff there is m \in M such that \mathcal{M} \models \psi[s[x \mapsto m]].
title: Tarski's Truth Definition (Satisfaction Relation)

[Lemma lem:retract_lim of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] Let $D$ be a simplicial set, $\cC$ an idempotent complete $\infty$-category, $X,Y\in\operatorname{Fun}(D,\cC)$ so that $Y$ is a retract of $X$.
If $\lim X\in \cC$ exists, then $\lim Y\in\cC$ exists and is a retract of $\lim X$.

[Proposition 8 of arXiv:2506.11707, 'Fluctuations of two-dimensional determinantal processes associated with Berezin--Toeplitz '] Suppose $V:\C\to \R$
  satisfies Assumptions \ref{ass:V}. 
Let $\mu>0$ and $\delta>0$ such that $\{V\le \mu(1+\delta)\}$ is compact.
For $\sigma>0$ and $\eta>0$, let 
\[\mathcal{D}_\eta^+(\sigma) :=\{z\in\C,\dist(z,\{V\leq \sigma(1+\eta)\})\le \eta\}.\]
Let $(\delta_N)_{N\ge 1}$, non-increasing, such that $\delta_N \ge
\varepsilon_N \log N $. There exists $C>0$ such that
the spectral counting function
\[
  \mathcal{N}(\sigma):=\tr[\1(H_N\leq \sigma)]
\]
satisfies, for all $0<\sigma \le \mu+\delta$,
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{N}(\sigma)\leq C N \bgamma(\mathcal{D}_{\delta_N}^+(\sigma)).
\end{equation}
Moreover, for any $\alpha >0$, there exists $C_{\alpha}$ and
$N_{\alpha}>0$ such that, for every $N\ge N_\alpha$ and $z\in
\C\setminus \mathcal{D}_{\delta_N}^+(\mu)$, 
\[
\Pi_N(z,z)  \le C_{\alpha} \exp(-\alpha\sqrt{N}\dist(z,\{V\leq \mu(1+\delta_N)\})) . 
\]

DRAFT source correction, pending independent review. In Hutchcroft's arXiv:1605.05301, the exponential-growth connectivity bound uses finite susceptibility only for p<p_c (Theorem 6). Supermultiplicativity of kappa_p(n)=inf{P_p(x connects to y):d(x,y)<=n}, followed by left continuity of sup_n kappa_p(n)^(1/n), transfers the rate bound to p_c. The proof does not require finite susceptibility at p_c or a branching-random-walk comparison. On the 3-regular tree the critical susceptibility is infinite, so an ordinary finite-critical-susceptibility interpretation of the old C0084 attempt is false. Its undefined qualifier 'spherically averaged' is not treated as a separate established theorem.

[Proposition prop:settlmentsphericalprocess of arXiv:2510.13733, 'Internal Diffusion Limited Aggregation \\ with Critical Branching Random Walks'] Let $d \geq 3$.  
There exist constants $c>0$, $J< \infty$ depending only on the dimension  such that the following holds.
Consider a RBG with integer  radii $R_2 >  R_1$,
starting from an initial particle configuration $\eta$
with support in $ \partial {B}_{ R_1 }$
and with $N_1 = \sum_{x \in  \partial {B}_{ R_1 }} \eta(x) $ particles.  
Then, with $H : = R_2 - R_1$, 
$$
\mathbb{E} \big [  N_2   \big]  \leq  N_1 \,  \Big ( 
J  \,  \frac{N_1}{H^{d}} + \, \,  \gamma_{H} \Big ) 
$$
where
$$
\gamma_{H}  := 
\begin{cases}
    1   - \frac{c}{\log H} & \mbox{ if $d=3$} \\
1 - c  & \mbox{ if $d>3$}.
\end{cases}
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:settlmentsphericalprocess of arXiv:2510.13733

    $$ and that

    $$
\mathbb{P}_{W_y}\{\operatorname{dist}(G_1y,V_{G_0,G_1}(E))\leq h_{(equation lemma3.10 of the paper)}h_{(equation lemma3.9 of the paper)}\sqrt{N})\}\leq 2\exp(-w_{(equation lemma3.10 of the paper)}N)
    $$ for constants $h_{(equation lemma3.10 of the paper)},w_{(equation lemma3.10 of the paper)}$ depending only on $\delta$. Here $E:=\operatorname{span}\{e_j\}_{j\in\operatorname{supp}y},$ and for any subspace $E\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, we denote by $V_{G_0,G_1}(E)$ the following subspace
    \begin{equation}V_{G_0,G_1}(E):=(G_0+G_1)(E^\perp)+G_0(E).\end{equation}

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Conservation, explicit coupling reduction, exact law comparison or spectral calculation Result: Compactness gives subsequential limits, but the new one-site theorem does not identify them. At density 1/2, compare iid Bernoulli occupation with a checkerboard having a uniform random phase on Z. Both are shift-invariant, ergodic under the full translation action, and have deterministic density 1/2. Both have the same one-site laws. Their adjacent covariance is respectively 0 and -1/4. Thus even the one-site theorem plus ergodicity would leave a real joint-distribution gap. Check: The shifted checkerboard has adjacent product identically zero and single-site mean 1/2. Translation swaps its two phases, so its only translation-invariant events have probability zero or one. These are auxiliary measures, not claimed ARW limits. Obstruction: Need uniqueness of all cylinder probabilities, or a coupling that suppresses differences between all subsequences. One-site flattening cannot provide it alone.

body: In computability theory, Kleene's recursion theorems are a pair of fundamental results about the application of computable functions to their own descriptions. The theorems were first proved by Stephen Kleene in 1938 and appear in his 1952 book Introduction to Metamathematics. A related theorem, which constructs fixed points of a computable function, is known as Rogers's theorem and is due to Hartley Rogers, Jr.
title: Kleene's recursion theorem

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2505.06187, 'Preferential Attachment Trees with Vertex Death: Persistence of the Maximum Degree'] Let $(E_i)_{i\in\N_0}$ and $(E_i')_{i\in\N_0}$ be independent exponential random variables, where $E_i$ and $E_i'$ have rate $\lambda_i>0$ for each $i\in\N_0$. Then, 
		\be 
		\sum_{i=0}^\infty (E_i-E_i')\text{ converges almost surely} \quad \Leftrightarrow \quad \sum_{i=0}^\infty \frac{1}{\lambda_i^2}<\infty. 
		\ee (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let d,m>=1 be integers and f:R^d->R^m continuous and affine on a finite polyhedral decomposition of R^d. For every integer L>=ceil(log_2(d+1))+1 and every -1<a<1, there is a finite-width depth-L network representing f exactly on all of R^d, with sigma_a(t)=t for t>=0 and a*t otherwise, activations after all but the final affine layer, and biases allowed. Widths may depend on f and a; no bounded-width or bounded-cost guarantee is asserted. This is exact representation, rather than approximation of arbitrary continuous functions.

Draft source correction awaiting referee w443: Let G=(V,E) be a finite graph, mu a probability law on {0,1}^E, and q in [0,1]. Fix an exploration e(omega) ordering every edge once, with deterministic first edge and each next edge determined only by previously revealed edge indices and bits. For each complete transcript (a,x) with positive mu probability, let Expl_k(a,x) denote agreement with its first k revealed edge indices and bits. Suppose mu(omega_{a_{k+1}}=1 | Expl_k(a,x))>=q for every such transcript and every k=0,...,|E|-1. Then iid Bernoulli-q on E is stochastically dominated by mu: for every increasing event A, P_q(A)<=mu(A).

body: [Lemma 28 of arXiv:2605.16868, '\ttl'] Let $N(t)$ be a Poisson process of rate 1. Let $\{Z(t)\}_{t\ge0}$ be a continuous increasing process  with $Z(0)=0$ and set $M(t)=N(Z(t))-Z(t)$. body: [Prop L1-branching of arXiv:2605.13004, 'Orientation in Poisson Cluster Processes via Imaginary Bispectra'] Let $C$ be a rooted branching cluster with a.s. finite genealogy, $\mathbb{E}[C(\mathbb{R})^3]<\infty$, and conditionally independent edge displacements admitting Lebesgue densities on $\mathbb{R}$. Then the reduced third factorial cumulant measure of the stationary Poisson cluster process generated by $C$ is absolutely continuous with some density $c_3\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$. The same conclusion applies, in particular, to one-sided branching clusters whose edge displacements have densities on $(0,\infty)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Continuous-displacement branching clusters lie in the $L^1$ regime

[Lemma 6 (uniqueness of neat r.v.'s) of arXiv:2604.04267, 'On Sharpest Tail Bounds for Functions \\ of Tail Bounded Random Variables'] Let $X,Y \in \mathcal{N}$ (definition~\ref{neatrvs}). 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item If $X, Y \in \mathcal{N}$ are both left continuous, or both right continuous, and $F_X = F_Y$, then $\forall s \in(0,1), \ X(s) = Y(s)$
\item The function $X'(s) = \lim_{s' \nearrow s} X(s'), \ \forall s \in (0,1)$ is neat, left continuous, and has the same distribution as $X$
\item The function $X'(s) = \lim_{s' \searrow s} X(s'), \ \forall s \in (0,1)$ is neat, right continuous, and has the same distribution as $X$
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma 7 (Soft-incidence Schur fibers) of arXiv:2606.26065, 'Localized Centered Second-Chaos Operators'] Let the cutoffs be as in Section~\ref{sec:setup}, with uniform $L^\infty$ bounds and supports of volumes $O(N^d)$, $O(Q^d)$, and $O(M^d)$ at the corresponding scales.  Then the following bounds hold uniformly in the dyadic parameters:
\begin{align}
 \sup_n \iiint |k(z)|\rho_N(\ell)^2\chi_Q(q)^2
 \rho_N(n-q-\ell-z)^2\dd z\dd\ell\dd q
 &\lesssim \norm{k}_{L^1}N^dQ^d,
 \\
 \sup_q \iiint |k(z)|\rho_N(\ell)^2\chi_M(n)^2
 \rho_N(n-q-\ell-z)^2\dd z\dd\ell\dd n
 &\lesssim \norm{k}_{L^1}N^dM^d,
 \\
 \sup_{\eta,n}\iint |k(z)|\chi_Q(q)^2
 \rho_N(n-q-\eta-z)^2\dd z\dd q
 &\lesssim \norm{k}_{L^1}Q^d,
 \\
 \sup_{\ell,q,z}\int \rho_N(\eta)^2
 \chi_M(\ell+q+\eta+z)^2\dd\eta
 &\lesssim M^d.
 
\end{align}
The same estimates hold with the two high-frequency variables exchanged.

[Cor 32 of arXiv:2609.03836, 'Koszul Orlik--Solomon Algebras from Non-supersolvable Arrangements'] Let $M$ be a round matroid of rank $r$ and $F$ a flat of rank $s \geq 2$. Then $\overline{T}_F(M)$ is supersolvable if and only if $M$ contains modular flats 
    $F = F_s \subsetneq F_{s+1} \subsetneq \dots \subsetneq F_r$ with $\rk_M F_i = i$.

body:
[Definition def:KPS of arXiv:2412.01381, 'Ergodicity and mixing for locally monotone stochastic evolution equations'] We say that $\{P_{t}\}_{t\ge0}$ is \emph{weak$^\ast$-mean
ergodic} if there exists a Borel probability measure $\mu_\ast$ on ${\mathcal B}(H)$, such that
\begin{equation}\text{w-}\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T P_t^\ast\mu\,\mathrm{d} t=\mu_\ast\quad\text{for every }\quad
\mu\in{\mathcal M}_1(H,{\mathcal B}(H)),
\end{equation}
where the limit is in the sense of weak convergence of probability measures.

We say that the \emph{weak law of large numbers} holds for $\{P_{t}\}_{t\ge0}$, for a function $F\in\operatorname{Lip}_{b}(H)$ and for a probability measure $\mu$ on ${\mathcal B}(H)$ if
\[\mathbb{P}_\mu\text{-}\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T F(X_t^\mu)\,\mathrm{d} t=\int_H F\,\mathrm{d}\mu_\ast,\]
where $\mu_\ast$ denotes the invariant probability measure of $\{P_{t}\}_{t\ge 0}$ and $\{X_t^\mu\}_{t\ge 0}$ denotes the Markov process related to $\{P_{t}\}_{t\ge 0}$ whose initial distribution is $\mu$ and whose path measure is $\mathbb{P}_\mu$, and where the convergence takes place in $\mathbb{P}_\mu$-probability.
title: Weak$^\ast$-mean ergodicity, weak law of large numbers

[Theorem of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'] {[ChenTshishiku2025]}
     Let $M$ be a closed, oriented 3-manifold M and $G$ a non-trivial subgroup of $\Twist(M)$. Then $G$ is realisable by diffeomorphisms if and only if $G$ is cyclic and $M$ is diffeomorphic to a connected sum of lens spaces. body:
[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] For a matrix $A\in M_N(\mathbb C)$ the following conditions are equivalent, and if they are satisfied, we say that $A$ is strictly positive, and write $A>0$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A=B^2$, with $B=B^*$, invertible.

\item $A=CC^*$, for some $C\in M_N(\mathbb C)$ invertible.

\item $<Ax,x>>0$, for any nonzero vector $x\in\mathbb C^N$.

\item $A=A^*$, and the eigenvalues are strictly positive, $\lambda_i>0$.

\item $A=UDU^*$, with $U\in U_N$ and with $D\in M_N(\mathbb R_+^*)$ diagonal.
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Definition Perfect fits of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] Two leaves \(F\in \mathcal{F}^{s}\) and \(G\in \mathcal{F}^{u}\), form a \emph{perfect fit} if \(F\) has a half ray \(F'\) and \(G\) has a half ray \(G'\), such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(F\cap G=\emptyset\), \(F'\) and \(G'\) converge to same ideal point \(p\),
\item there is leaf segments \(U\in \mathcal{F}^{u}\) and \(V\in \mathcal{F}^{s}\) such that \(F,G,U,V,p\) forms a rectangle with one ideal vertex \(R\),
\item the restriction of \(\mathcal{F}^{s}\) and \(\mathcal{F}^{u}\) on \(R\) is product (namely, conjugate to the vertical and horizontal lines on \([0,1]^{2}\setminus \{(0,0)\}\)). In particular, \(R\) contains no singular points.
\end{enumerate}

See the left side of Figure (fig:perfectfits of the paper).
title: Perfect fits

[Definition 20 of arXiv:2512.07202, 'Hitting Probabilities for Hypoelliptic Differential Equations Driven by Fractional Brownia'] Let $F\in \mathbb{D}^{1,2}_X(\mathbb{R}^N)$ be a random vector in $\mathbb{R}^N$. The \textit{Malliavin covariance matrix} (or simply \textit{Malliavin matrix}) of $F$ is the $N\times N$ random matrix $\gamma(F)$ whose $(i,j)$-entry is defined by 
$$
\gamma_{ij}(F):=\langle~\mathbf{D}_XF^i,\mathbf{D}_XF^j~\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_X}.
$$

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.03793, 'Typical martingale diverges on a co-$\sigma$-porous set'] Let $(X,\psi)$ be a metric space and let $x\in X$, $A\subset X$ and $\alpha>0$. Then $A$ is $2\alpha$-porous at $x$ if and only if
\begin{equation*}
\forall\varepsilon\in(0,\alpha)\exists r_0>0\forall r\in(0,r_0)\exists y\in X:B\bp{y,(\alpha-\varepsilon)\cdot r}\subset B(x,r)\setminus A.
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.03793

\[

\]

\[
\mathsf M_u'(t)=-q(t)
\]
for almost every $t\in(0,T)$.
