[Definition of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] Let \((\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})\) be a complete probability space supporting a family of \(d\)-dimensional
	Wiener processes \((W(\cdot,\xi))_{\xi \in [0,1]}\) and a family of initial random variables
	\((X_0(\xi))_{\xi \in [0,1]}\) taking values in \(\mathbb{R}^d\). A family of stochastic processes
	\(X=(X(\cdot,\xi))_{\xi \in [0,1]}\) is called a \emph{strong solution} to (equation eq:fibered-McKean-Vlasov-SDE of the paper) if
	the following conditions hold: 
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
		\item For almost every \(\xi \in [0,1]\), \(\mu^{\xi}=\mathrm{Law}(X(\cdot,\xi))\).  
		\item For almost every \(\xi \in [0,1]\), the process \(X(\cdot,\xi)\) has continuous paths, is adapted to the filtration generated by the Wiener process \(W(\cdot,\xi)\) and the initial condition \(X_0(\xi)\), and satisfies the following integral equation \(\mathbb{P}\)-a.s.:
		\[
			X(t,\xi) = X_0(\xi) + \int_{0}^{t} b_{\xi}(s,X(\cdot,\xi),\mu) \,ds + \int_{0}^{t} \sigma_{\xi}(s,X(\cdot,\xi),\mu) \,dW(s,\xi), \quad t \in [0,T].
		\]  
	\end{enumerate}
	We say that \emph{strong uniqueness} holds if any two strong solutions \(X\) and \(X'\), defined on the same probability space, driven by the same family of Wiener processes, and starting from the same initial conditions, satisfy \(X(\cdot,\xi)=X'(\cdot,\xi)\) \(\mathbb{P}\)-a.s.\ for almost every \(\xi \in [0,1]\).

	We say that \emph{uniqueness in law} holds if for any two strong solutions \(X\) and \(X'\), possibly defined on different probability spaces and driven by different Wiener processes but sharing the same fibered law for their initial conditions, one has that \(\mathrm{Law}(X(\cdot,\xi))=\mathrm{Law}(X'(\cdot,\xi))\) for almost every \(\xi \in [0,1]\).

Then the chain has a unique stationary law pi, is V-geometrically ergodic for V(x) = 1 + |x|^p (some p > 0), and lim t^alpha pi((t, inf)) = lim t^alpha pi((-inf, -t)) = c > 0, where alpha is the unique positive root of E|1 - (eta/b)Q|^alpha = 1. For each b there is a nonempty open interval of eta just above eta0 = 2b/(b+2) on which (S) holds and alpha < 2.

[Theorem {\cite[Theorem~1.1.4 and Remark~1.1.5 of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ I:\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple C'] {LevelLineGFFI}}]
Suppose that $h$ is a GFF on $\BH$ with piecewise constant boundary conditions that change only finitely many times. For all $u \in \BR$ and $x \in \partial \BH$, we let $\gamma_u^x$ be the level line of $h$ with height $u$ starting from $x$ and ending at $\infty$ (when it exists). Fix $x_2 \leq x_1$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $u_2 < u_1$, then $\gamma_{u_2}^{x_2}$ a.s.\ stays to the left of $\gamma_{u_1}^{x_1}$ (possibly touching it).
\item If $u_2 = u_1$, then $\gamma_{u_2}^{x_2}$ may intersect $\gamma_{u_1}^{x_1}$ and, upon intersecting, the two curves merge and never separate.
\item If $u_1 - u_2 \geq 2 \lambda$, then $\gamma_{u_1}^{x_1}$ and $\gamma_{u_2}^{x_2}$ do not intersect each other a.s.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prp 28 of arXiv:2608.13976, 'Boundary Harnack principle for diffusion with jumps on metric measure spaces'] Let $B=B(x_0, R)$ be a ball in $\R^d.$
Then $\xi_B$ is an excessive measure for $X^{b,B}$, that is, for every
Borel function $f \ge0$,
$$
\int_B f(x) \xi_B(dx) \ge\int_B \E_x[f(X^{b,B}_{t})]
\xi_B(dx).
$$
Moreover, $h_B$ is a strictly positive, bounded continuous function on $B$ and
there exists  $C=C(d, R)>1$ independent of $x_0\in\R^d$ so that
\begin{equation}
C^{-1}\leq h_B(x)\leq C \quad \hbox{for }   x\in \tfrac{1}{2}B.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Load-bearing hypotheses: A is densely defined, dissipative, AND Ran(λ_0 − A) = X (or at least dense) for some λ_0 > 0. What fails without the range condition: a dissipative operator can be closed and densely defined and still generate nothing. Counterexample: X = L²(0, 1), A f = f' with D(A) = {f ∈ H¹(0,1) : f(0) = f(1) = 0}. Then A is densely defined and closed, and Re⟨f', f⟩ = (|f(1)|² − |f(0)|²)/2 = 0, so A is dissipative (indeed both A and −A are). But solving λf − f' = g with f(0) = 0 gives f(x) = −∫_0^x e^{λ(x−s)}g(s) ds, and the second boundary condition f(1) = 0 forces the constraint ∫_0^1 e^{−λs} g(s) ds = 0: Ran(λ − A) is a closed subspace of codimension 1, not dense, for every λ > 0. Hence A is not a generator, although dropping one boundary condition (D = {f ∈ H¹ : f(1) = 0}) gives exactly the generator of the left shift semigroup. The range condition is what encodes 'the right number of boundary conditions'. What fails without density: X = C[0,1] with the sup norm, A f = f' on D(A) = {f ∈ C¹[0,1] : f(1) = 0}. Solving λ f − f' = g with f(1) = 0 gives f(x) = ∫_x^1 e^{λ(x−s)}g(s)ds, so ‖f‖ ≤ ‖g‖/λ: A is dissipative and Ran(λ − A) = X for every λ > 0. Yet the closure of D(A) is {f ∈ C[0,1] : f(1) = 0}, a proper closed subspace, so A generates no C_0-semigroup on C[0,1] (generators are densely defined); it generates one on the smaller space. Density is automatic only when X is reflexive, which C[0,1] is not. Related trap: for the norm inequality version, dissipativity means ‖(λ − A)x‖ ≥ λ‖x‖ for all λ > 0 - checking it for a single λ, or checking Re⟨Ax, x⟩ ≤ 0 only on a core without knowing the operator is closed or closable there, proves nothing about the closure being a generator unless the range condition is verified on that same core.
X is a Banach space
A is dissipative
the range condition Ran(λ_0 − A) = X (or dense) is the hypothesis at issue
title: Pitfall: Lumer-Phillips Needs the Range Condition (and Density) - Dissipativity Alone Is Not Enough

    \end{align*}

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2606.16164, 'A Low-Regularity Semigroup Sewing Lemma via Quotient Structures'] Let $\tau\in[0,T]$, $\beta\in\mathbb R$, and $\gamma\in(0,1]$. Then there exists a linear map
\[
\mathcal I_\tau^{\mathrm d}: \mathcal A^{\gamma}(\Delta_\tau^2;B_\beta) \to C([0,\tau];B_\beta),
\]
obtained from a dyadic recursion on $\mathcal D^\tau$ and continuous extension to $[0,\tau]$, such that, for every $A\in \mathcal A^{\gamma}(\Delta_\tau^2;B_\beta)$, $\mathcal I_\tau^{\mathrm d}(A)_0=0$. If we define the dyadic remainder $\mathcal R_\tau^{\mathrm d}(A):=A-\delta\mathcal I_\tau^{\mathrm d}(A)$, then
$
\delta \mathcal R_\tau^{\mathrm d}(A)=\delta A.
$
Moreover, if $\gamma\in(0,1)$, then
\begin{equation}

\mathcal R_\tau^{\mathrm d}(A)\in C^{\gamma}(\Delta_\tau^2;B_\beta)\ \text{\, and \, }\ \|\mathcal R_\tau^{\mathrm d}(A)\|_{\gamma,\beta;\tau}\le C_\gamma\|\delta A\|_{\gamma,\beta;\tau};
\end{equation}
if $\gamma=1$, then
\begin{equation}

\mathcal R_\tau^{\mathrm d}(A)\in C_{\log}^{1}(\Delta_\tau^2;B_\beta)\ \text{\, and \, }\ \|\mathcal R_\tau^{\mathrm d}(A)\|_{1,\log;\tau,\beta}\le C_{T}\|\delta A\|_{1,\beta;\tau}.
\end{equation}
while, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, $\|\mathcal R_\tau^{\mathrm d}(A)\|_{1-\varepsilon,\beta;\tau}\le C_{\varepsilon,T}\|\delta A\|_{1,\beta;\tau}$. Here the constants can be chosen independently of $\tau\in[0,T]$.

[Thm 135 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $\iota > 0$, there exists $\epsilon_0 = \epsilon_0(\alpha,\iota) > 0$ such that for all $\epsilon \in (0,\epsilon_0)$ and $L > 0$, there exists $C(L,\epsilon)$ such that the following holds.
  Consider any $q_0 \in [0,1)$. Given controls $(b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta,\zeta^\Ising)$,
recall from \eqref{e:s.sqrt.fn} that we denote $s(t) = ((tp)'(t))^{1/2}$. Let $B$ and $W$ be standard Brownian motions on the time interval $q_0 \le t\le 1$, and consider the SDEs (cf.\ Theorem~\ref{thm:BOGP-hardness-main})   \begin{align}
    
    \de X(t) &= p'(t)^{1/2} b(t,X(t)) \,\de t + s(t) \sigma(t,X(t)) \,\de B(t)\,, \\
    
    \de Y(t) &= w(t,Y(t)) \,\de W(t)\,,
  \end{align}
with initial values $X(q_0) \sim \zeta$ and $Y(q_0) \sim \zeta^\Ising$ independent of $B,W$. Suppose the controls satisfy the following conditions:
  \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item  $b(t,x) : [q_0,1] \times \bbR \to [-L,L]$ and $\sigma(t,x), w(t,x) : [q_0,1] \times \bbR \to [0,L]$ are $L$-Lipschitz in $(t,x)$.
    \item  $|\bbE[(w_t)^2] -1| \le \epsilon$ for all $t\in [q_0,1]$.
    \item  $p\in \incr([q_0,1];[0,1])$ (see Definition~\ref{d:incr.p}) is a twice differentiable function, with $p(q_0) \in [1/L,\epsilon]$ and $\|p\|_{C^2([q_0,1])} \le L$.
    \item  For all $t\in [q_0,1]$, the controls satisfy the approximate budget constraint:
    \begin{align}\nonumber
      \Cost(t)
      &\equiv
      \bbE\bigg[
      b_t(X(t))^2 + \bigg(
        \frac{s(t)^2}{p(t)}
        \bigg) \big(\sigma_t(X(t))-1\big)^2
      \bigg]\\
      &\leq 
      \budget(t)+\epsilon
      \equiv
      \frac{(\bbE w_t(Y(t)))^2}
        {\alpha}
      +\epsilon\,.
    \end{align}
    \item  The endpoint of the $Y$ process satisfies
    \beq
    \bbE\Big[\big(|Y(1)|-1\big)^2\Big]\leq \epsilon\,.
    \eeq
    \item  The initial measures $\zeta, \zeta^\Ising \in\cP_2(\R)$ are such that $|\bbE[X(q_0)^2]|\le \epsilon$ and $|\bbE[Y(q_0)^2] - q_0|\le \epsilon$.
  \end{enumerate}
We then have the following:
  \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
    \item  There exists a $C(L,\epsilon)$-Lipschitz algorithm $\cA_N$ (in the sense of Definition~\ref{d:Lip}) which agrees with the output of an efficient IAMP iteration with probability $1-e^{-cN}$, such that
    \begin{align}
      
      \bbP\lt(\cA_N(\bG,\bg^\aux) \in \Sigma(\iota) \rt) \ge 1-e^{-cN}\,, \\
      
      \bbP\lt(
        \bbW_2\Big(\mu_\bG(\cA_N(\bG,\bg^\aux)), \Law(X(1)) \Big) \le \iota
      \rt) \ge 1-e^{-cN}\,.
    \end{align}
    Moreover, for $\mu(\cA_N)$ and $\mu^{\Ising}(\cA_N)$ defined in \eqref{e:mu.of.Alg} and \eqref{e:mu.Ising.of.Alg}, we have
    \begin{align}
      
      \bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_N), \Law(X(1)) \Big) \le \iota\,, \\
      
      \bbW_2\Big(\mu^{\Ising}(\cA_N), \cP(\{\pm 1\}) \Big) \le \iota\,,
    \end{align}
    where in \eqref{e:IAMP-main-main-coords-averaged}, $\bbW_2$ denotes the point-to-set $\bbW_2$ distance.
    \item  Suppose that, in addition to the assumptions (\ref{i:IAMP-main-coefs})--(\ref{i:IAMP-main-init}) above, we have $w(t,x) = w(t,-x)$ for all $t,x$ and $\zeta^\Ising$ is symmetric, i.e. $\Law(-x : x\sim \zeta^\Ising) = \zeta^\Ising$. Then, there exists a $C(L,\epsilon)$-Lipschitz algorithm $\cA_N$ satisfying the conclusions of part (\ref{i:IAMP-main-main}) and furthermore $\bbE \cA_N(\bG,\bg^\aux) = \bzero$.
    \item

[Theorem thm:classical of arXiv:2507.01236, 'Disintegration theorem for multifunctions, \ with applications to empirical Wasserstein d'] Let $(\mathfrak{X},\mathcal{A})$ and $(\mathfrak{Y},\mathcal{B})$ be Polish spaces, assumed to be equipped with their Borel $\sigma$-algebras $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$, respectively, and let $f:\mathfrak{X}ightarrow\mathfrak{Y}$ be a Borel-measurable map. Given a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathfrak{X}$ and $
u:=f_*\mu$ on $\mathfrak{Y}$, there exists a measurable family $y\mapsto\mu_y$ of probability measures on $\mathfrak{Y}$ such that $\mu = \int\!\mu_y\,
u(dy)$ and such that $\mu_y$ is supported on $f^{-1}\{y\}$ for $
u$-almost all $y\in\mathfrak{Y}$.

[Theorem 103 of arXiv:2605.03236, 'Stochastic It\^o Equations and Parabolic Second-Order Equations with singular Drift'] For any 
$\kappa\in(0,1)$ there exists  
$N$, depending only on $\kappa,d,\delta$,
   such that, for any $R\leq  \rho_{b}$,
$x\in   B_{\kappa R}$, and closed set
$\Gamma\subset  C_{R}(R^{2},0)$, the $P_{0,x}$-probability that the process 
$(\sft_{s}, x_{s})$  
reaches $\Gamma$ before exiting from $C_{2R^{2},R}$
is greater than or equal to $N^{-1} (|\Gamma|/|C_{R}|)^{\gamma-1/
(d +1)}$:
\begin{equation}
                               
P_{0,x} (\tau_{\Gamma}  <\tau_{2R^{2},R}  )
\geq N^{-1} (|\Gamma|/|C_{R}|)^{\gamma-1/(d +1)},
\end{equation}
where $\tau_{\Gamma} $ is the first time $(\sft_{s}, x_{s})$
hits $\Gamma$, $\tau_{2R^{2},R} $ is the first exit time of
$(\sft_{s}, x_{s})$ from $C_{2R^{2},R}$,
   and $\gamma$ is taken from Theorem \ref{theorem 12.21.1}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Integrator-authored exact special-case argument and failure analysis after checking the incoming source Result: Put J=Q(I-Q)^(-1). Given the occupied set B outside e, the conditional odds of presence are s_B=J_ee-J_eB*(J_BB)^(-1)*J_Be. Schur-complement minimization makes s_B decrease as B increases. Its minimum is s_all=1/(J^(-1))ee=1/[(Q^(-1))ee-1]. The conditional probability, however, is s_all/(1+s_all)=1/(Q^(-1))ee. Equivariance makes (Q^(-1))ee=tr(Q^(-1)), with normalized trace, so this probability is the harmonic mean h of all eigenvalues counted with multiplicity. Sequential sampling with common independent uniforms couples the process above iid Bernoulli(h), since every conditional probability given a partial reveal is also at least h. Applying the same argument to the complement gives the upper density 1-HM(I-Q). AM-GM applied to the reciprocals gives HM(Q)<=FK(Q), exposing the exact remaining gap. Check: For a scalar Q=qI, s_all=q/(1-q) but the conditional probability is q; this catches the odds/probability confusion in the incoming record. In a finite group, equal inverse diagonal entries average to the full matrix trace divided by |Gamma|, irrespective of whether the group is abelian. No sum over one-dimensional characters is substituted for the nonabelian spectrum. Obstruction: No geometric-mean domination theorem or sharpness certificate. Numerical coupling feasibility is not exact proof, and the infinite-group extension of this particular calculation is not asserted.

body: In statistics, Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) is a class of algorithms used to draw samples from a probability distribution. Given a probability distribution, one can construct a Markov chain whose elements' distribution approximates it, i.e. the Markov chain's equilibrium distribution matches the target distribution. The more steps that are included, the more closely the distribution of the sample matches the actual desired distribution.

[Lemma lem:N-ball-type-2-3 of arXiv:2509.06273, 'Normalized Matching Property for Competing Urn Models'] Suppose that $e$ and $f$ are incident to $v_{d-1}$.
	 Then, for any 
	$S \subseteq X$, 
	\[
	\aM_{G,\ba}(S) \ = \ 2 \.\aM_{G-e-f,\ba'}(S), 
	\qquad \text{where } \ 
	\ba' := (\mathrm{a}_1,\ldots,\mathrm{a}_{d-1}-1) \in \mathbb N^{d-1}.
	\]
	
	Suppose instead that $e$ and $f$ are incident to $v_{d+1}$, with $d < n-1$. 
	Then, for any $S \subseteq X$, 
	\[
	\aM_{G,\ba}(S) \ = \ 2\. \aM_{G-e-f,\ba''}(S), 
	\qquad \text{where } \ 
	\ba'' := (\mathrm{a}_1,\ldots,\mathrm{a}_{d-1}) \in \mathbb N^{d-1}.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Defn 1 of arXiv:2506.15341, '\bf Superpositions for General Conditional Mckean-Vlasov Stochastic Differential Equations'] We define $\hC_b^2(\sM_1)$ to be the set of all bounded, continuous functions $F: \sM_1\rightarrow \hR$ such that:

{\rm (i)}  There exists a bounded function $\pa_{\m}F:\sM_1(\hR^d)\times\hR^d\rightarrow \hR$ such that 
\beaa 
\lim_{\varepsilon\rightarrow 0}\frac{F(\m+\varepsilon \xi)-F(\m)}{\varepsilon}=\int_{\hR^d}\pa_{\m}F(\m,x)\xi(dx),  \qq \m,\xi\in \sM_1(\hR^d). \eeaa 

\ss
{\rm (ii)} The function $x\mapsto \pa_{\m}F(\m,x)$ is continuously differentiable for $x\in\hR^d$, and the gradient $\nabla_x \pa_{\m}F(\m,x)$ is uniformly bounded in $(\m,x)$, denoted as $\bD_\m F(\m,x)$.

\ss
{\rm (iii)} The second order spacial derivative is defined as $\bD_{\m}^2 F(\m,x,x')$, and  is bounded and continuous for $x,x'\in\hR^d$.

\ss
{\rm {(iv)}} The mixed derivative $\bD_x\bD_{\m}F(\m,x)$ is defined as gradient of $\bD_{\m}F(\m,x)$ and assume that it is continuous and bounded in $(\m,x)$.
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2506.15341

$$
R^c(E_\alpha,E_{-\alpha})A = -\tfrac{g_\ag(A^{0,1},A_\alpha)}{x_\alpha}A_\alpha^{0,1} + \tfrac{g_\ag(A^{1,0},A_\alpha)}{x_\alpha}A_\alpha^{1,0},  \qquad\forall\alpha\in\Delta_\qg^+,   
$$
$$
R^c(E_\alpha,E_{-\alpha})E_\alpha = \left(-\tfrac{g_\ag(A_\alpha^{1,0},A_\alpha)}{x_\alpha} - \la\alpha,\alpha\ra\right)E_\alpha,  \qquad\forall\alpha\in\Delta_\qg^+,
$$
$$
R^c(E_\alpha,E_{-\alpha})E_\beta = \left(\tfrac{N_{\alpha,-\beta}^2x_{\alpha-\beta}}{x_\beta} 
- \tfrac{N_{\alpha,\beta}^2x_\beta}{x_{\alpha+\beta}} 
- \la\alpha,\beta\ra\right) E_\beta,  \qquad\forall\alpha,\beta\in\Delta_\qg^+,
$$
where in the last line, the term containing $N_{\alpha,-\beta}^2$ appears only if $\alpha-\beta\in\Delta_\qg^-$ and the term containing $N_{\alpha,\beta}^2$ appears only if $\alpha+\beta\in\Delta_\qg$.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Common-splice compatibility obstruction Result: Two independent standard Brownian half-paths attached at the same deterministic time give a two-sided Brownian motion. For a general process certified separately as forward and backward Brownian, the certifying random times can differ. Moving either certificate to another random time can bias its marginal law, as the selection-density calculation in P0032 demonstrates. Check: Independence of two halves at a proposed joining time is insufficient if their Brownian marginal laws have been lost there. Obstruction: No construction aligns both certificates at one time while preserving both marginal laws and their independence.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0030-compatibility-of-forward-and-backward-brownian-decompositions
No independent review
title: Attempt on Compatibility of forward and backward Brownian decompositions

body:
[Theorem thm:general-first-moment of arXiv:2609.02710, 'Asymptotic Mean Value Laplacian\\ on equiregular sub-Riemannian manifolds'] Fix $x\in O$ and a first-kind privileged chart $\Phi_x$. The following are
equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}, leftmargin=2em]
\item The unweighted limits $\Lambda_i(x)$ exist for $i=1,\ldots,k$.
\item The first-moment condition holds at $x$.
\item The limit $\lim_{h\downarrow0}A_hf(x)$ exists for every
  $f\in C_c^\infty(M)$.
\item The quantities $A_hf_i(x)$ converge for some horizontal coordinate
  test family.
\end{enumerate}
When these conditions hold,
\begin{equation}
  A_hf(x)\longrightarrow\mathcal A_\mu f(x)
\end{equation}
for every $f\in C_c^\infty(M)$, where
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal A_\mu f(x)
  =\frac1{\widehat V_x}\left(
    \frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^kM_{ij}(x)X_iX_jf(x)
    +\sum_{i=1}^k\Gamma_i(x)X_if(x)
  \right).
\end{equation}
title: First-moment criterion

body: [Lemma 16 of arXiv:2609.03750, '\bf Pullback Measure Attractors, Zero-Noise Limits, and Moderate Deviations for 2D Stochas'] Suppose Hypotheses \ref{PEeqAssum-2.2}, \ref{PEeqAssum-2.3}, \ref{PEeqAssum-2.4} and \eqref{PETNs-3.01} hold. Then, for every $\epsilon\in(0,\epsilon_0)$, the measure evolution process $S_\epsilon$ on $\mathcal P_{4,z}(H)$ is $\mathfrak{D}$-pullback asymptotically compact in the ambient topology $(\mathcal P(H),d_{\mathcal P(H)})$. More precisely, for every $\tau\in\mathbb R$, $t_n \to +\infty$, and ${\mu}_n\in D(\tau-t_n)$ with $D\in \mathfrak{D}$, the sequence $\{S_\epsilon(\tau,\tau-t_n){\mu}_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ has a subsequence converging in $\mathcal P(H)$, and every such limit belongs to $\mathcal P_{4,z}(H)$.

[Corollary CYT4 of arXiv:2608.30747, 'Compact homogeneous complex manifolds'] Under the hypothesis of Theorem (CYT2 of the paper), there exist $u<0<v$ such that for any complex structure $J=(J_\ag,J_\qg)$ with $c_1(M,J)=0$ and $J_\ag Z_{J_\qg}=aZ_{J_\qg}+bZ_2$, $b\ne 0$ admitting a CYT metric as in (equation g of the paper), the following inequalities hold:
$$
u<\tfrac{ab}{a^2+1}<v.  
$$
If $G$ is semisimple, $\dim{\ag}=2$ and these inequalities hold, then the corresponding complex C-space $(M=G/K,J)$ admits a CYT G-invariant metric as in (equation g of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:ae390e71f084a58224a6262239c239cef857bf014df3f91e5b0992163f86ed90","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/ae/ae390e71f084a58224a6262239c239cef857bf014df3f91e5b0992163f86ed90.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:8f7739103485ff3c36c8eb5e9a9175a6f7da25f25cd14393a16fb51b395d3617","bundle_entry_key":"2608-10415-theorem-420-theorem-420","bundle_id":"population.tex-extract-s1_054","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"tex-extract-v2-20260907/bundle_s1_054.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:harvest.arxiv.mathematics:arxiv-2608-10415-theorem-420-theorem-420","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Paper's own proof, opening: As before in the classical case, the 4 formulae in the statement are equivalent, via M\"obius inversion. Thus, it is enough to prove one of them, and we will prove the first formula, which in practice is the most useful one. Thus, we must prove that:
$$M_n(a)=\sum_{\nu\in NC(n)}\kappa_\nu(a)$$

(1) In order to prove this formula, let us get back to the construction of the free cumulants, from Definition 15.20. The Cauchy transform of $a$ is the following function:
$$G_a(\xi)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty\frac{M_n(a)}{\xi^{n+1}}$$

[Thm maingauss of arXiv:2412.00593, 'A new approach to strong convergence II.\\The classical ensembles'] Let $\boldsymbol{G}^N=(G_1^N,\ldots,G_r^N)$ be i.i.d.\ GUE/GOE/GSE random 
matrices of dimension $N$, and let $\boldsymbol{s}=(s_1,\ldots,s_r)$ be a 
free semicircular family. Let $\varepsilon\in (0,1]$ and $q_0\in\mathbb{N}$. 
Then for every noncommutative polynomial $P\in\mathrm{M}_D(\mathbb{C})\otimes 
\mathbb{C}\langle\boldsymbol{s}\rangle$ of degree $q_0$ with matrix 
coefficients of dimension $D\le e^{cN\varepsilon^2}$, we have
$$
	\mathbf{P}\big[
	\|P(\boldsymbol{G}^N)\|\ge (1+\varepsilon)\|P(\boldsymbol{s})\|
	\big] \le
	\frac{N}{c\varepsilon}
	\,e^{-cN\varepsilon^2},
$$
where $c$ is a constant that depends only on $q_0$ and $r$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 13 (Composition of cut majorants) of arXiv:2607.16724, 'Algebraic Transfer for Operator-Valued Gaussian Chaoses: Oriented Schatten Profiles and Si'] Cut majorants are closed under finite sums, external tensor products, and
multilinear composition.  More precisely, suppose
\[
 \Psi:\prod_{\nu=1}^{\ell}\cK_{q_\nu}^{\mathrm{alg}}
 \longrightarrow\cK_q^{\mathrm{alg}}
\]
and, for each $\nu$,
\[
 \Theta_\nu:\prod_{j\in J_\nu}\cK_{m_j}^{\mathrm{alg}}
 \longrightarrow\cK_{q_\nu}^{\mathrm{alg}}
\]
have $r$-cut majorants, where the finite input-slot sets
$J_1,\ldots,J_\ell$ are pairwise disjoint.  Then
$\Psi\circ(\Theta_1,\ldots,\Theta_\ell)$ has the majorant obtained by
summing the product
\[
 \mathsf M_\Psi^{(r)}(S;R_1,\ldots,R_\ell)
 \prod_{\nu=1}^{\ell}
 \mathsf M_{\Theta_\nu}^{(r)}
 (R_\nu;(T_j)_{j\in J_\nu})
\]
over the intermediate cuts $R_1,\ldots,R_\ell$.
For a finite sum of operations with the same source and target, the local
majorants add.  If $\Theta$ and $\Xi$ act on disjoint input families and have
output orders $q$ and $q'$, respectively, then an external-product majorant
is given by
\begin{align}

 &\mathsf M_{\Theta\boxtimes\Xi}^{(r)}
 \bigl(S\sqcup(q+S');\mathbf T,\mathbf T'\bigr)\notag\\
 &\qquad:=
 \mathsf M_{\Theta}^{(r)}(S;\mathbf T)
 \mathsf M_{\Xi}^{(r)}(S';\mathbf T').
\end{align}
Here $q+S':=\{q+s:s\in S'\}\subset[q+q']$, and $\sqcup$ uses the resulting
ordered identification of the two output leg sets.

Let Omega in R^n be bounded and open, A measurable and uniformly elliptic with constants lambda, Lambda, and b, c in L^infinity(Omega) with no sign condition. For u, v in H^1_0(Omega) put B[u,v] = integral ( A grad u . grad v + (b.grad u) v + c u v ) dx. Then: (i) |B[u,v]| <= alpha ||u||_{H^1} ||v||_{H^1} with alpha = Lambda + ||b||_infinity + ||c||_infinity (boundedness); (ii) B[u,u] >= (lambda/2) ||grad u||_{L^2}^2 - gamma ||u||_{L^2}^2 for all u in H^1_0(Omega), with gamma = ||b||_infinity^2/(2 lambda) + ||c^-||_infinity (the Gaarding inequality); in particular B + mu(.,.)_{L^2} is coercive for every mu >= gamma, so Lu + mu u = f is uniquely solvable in H^1_0 for such mu. (iii) Fredholm alternative: exactly one of the following holds: either for every f in L^2(Omega) there is a unique weak solution u in H^1_0(Omega) of Lu = f, or the homogeneous problem Lu = 0 has a nontrivial weak solution in H^1_0(Omega). In the second case the solution space N and the corresponding space N* for the formal adjoint L* have the same finite dimension, and Lu = f is solvable if and only if integral f v = 0 for every v in N*. (iv) There is an at most countable set Sigma of real numbers, with no finite accumulation point if it is infinite, such that Lu = mu u + f is uniquely solvable for every f exactly when mu is not in Sigma.
Omega bounded and open in R^n
A measurable and uniformly elliptic with constants 0 < lambda <= Lambda
b, c in L^infinity(Omega), no sign condition
all functions taken in H^1_0(Omega)

    \[

    \]

    \[
    \Sigma^\infty_\sQ G F \Omega^\infty_\sO \Rightarrow \Sigma^\infty_\sQ G \Omega^\infty_\sP \Sigma^\infty_\sP F \Omega^\infty_\sO
    \]
    of $\theta$ is given by the unit of the adjunction $(\Sigma^\infty_\sP, \Omega^\infty_\sP)$.

[Theorem thm:d4-critical-level-percolation of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] Fix $\nu_{0}>0$, $\theta_{0}>0$, and $K_{0}<\infty$. There are
$c=c(\nu_{0},\theta_{0},K_{0})>0$ and
$t_0=t_0(\nu_{0},\theta_{0},K_{0})<\infty$ such that, for every mean-zero i.i.d.\
field $(\zeta(x))_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^4}$ satisfying
\[
    \Var(\zeta(0))\geq\nu_{0}^2\, ,
    \qquad
    \mathbb{E} e^{\theta_{0}|\zeta(0)|}\leq K_{0}\, ,
\]
and every $t\geq t_0$, the planar set
\[
    \{x\in\Pi:u_t(x)>c\log t\}
\]
contains an infinite nearest-neighbor component almost surely. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Conjecture of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] Let $H_{2m}$ be the $2m$th harmonic number. Suppose a deck of $n$ cards is given an $m$-shelf shuffle, and $n/m$ is not too small. Then, the strategy, call it $\mathbf{G}$, discussed in [FDH] can be shown to be optimal in a high-probability case. Let $F^{\mathbf{G}}(n,m)$ be the expected number of correct guesses. We have, when $n/m$ is not too small,
    \[F^{\mathbf{G}}(n,m)\approx\frac{n}{2m}H_{2m}=\frac{n}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{2m}\frac{1}{k}\] (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Unnumbered conjecture of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'

We assume exponential decay of 
$R^{\emph{\tiny{birth-growth}}}$,
namely there is a constant $C>0$ such that
\begin{equation} 
\sup_{z \in \R^d} \PP(R_z \geq r) \leq \exp(-Cr), \ r > 0. 
\end{equation}
Fix $t_0 \in (0,\infty]$. Then  $H_\la$ satisfies the bounds
\[
\mathbf{d}_K \left(  \frac{H_\la - \E H_\la} {\sqrt{\Var H_\la}}, N \right) \leq C_K \cdot  \frac{\la^{1/2}}{\Var H_\la}
\]
and 
\[
\mathbf{d}_W \left(  \frac{H_\la - \E H_\la} {\sqrt{\Var H_\la}}, N \right) \leq C_K  \frac{\la^{1/2}}{\Var H_\la} + C_W  \frac{\la}{(\Var H_\la)^{3/2}},
\]
where $C_K,C_W$  are  constants depending only on $d$ and $C>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 62 (Metrics from regular pairs) of arXiv:2609.02267, 'Locally Conformally Flat Manifolds with Positive Scalar Curvature: Kleinian Groups, Moduli'] Let $n\ge3$, let $0<\mathfrak d\le a=(n-2)/2$, and let $(\Lambda,\mu)$ be a
$\mathfrak d$-regular pair in $S^n$ with
$\varnothing\ne\Lambda\subsetneq S^n$.  Define
\[
 \mathcal{K}_{\mathfrak d}(u)=
 \begin{cases}
  u^{-(\mathfrak d+a)},&\mathfrak d<a,\\[2mm]
  u^{-2a}\ell(u)^{-a/2},&\mathfrak d=a,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 V(x)=\int_\Lambda \mathcal{K}_{\mathfrak d}(\mathfrak q(x,y))\,d\mu(y),
 \quad x\in S^n\setminus\Lambda.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \widehat g=(1+V)^{4/(n-2)}g_{st}
\end{equation}
is smooth and locally conformally flat on $S^n\setminus\Lambda$; each
connected component is geodesically complete; and its scalar curvature
satisfies
\[
 0<\inf_{S^n\setminus\Lambda}\mathrm{Sc}_{\widehat g}
 \le\sup_{S^n\setminus\Lambda}\mathrm{Sc}_{\widehat g}<\infty.
\]

[Lemma lem:F-step-in-loop of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a real number $\lambda \in (0,1)$ and a send sequence $\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$. Let $j_0$ be a
sufficiently large integer.  
Let  
$\Psi_0$ be the initialising state with
$j^{\Psi_0} = j_0$ and $\tau^{\Psi_0} = \tau_0$.  
Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be  
the $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule from Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-rule of the paper).
Let $V$ be a volume process from~$\Psi_0$ with transition rule~$\mathrm{hls}$, send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and birth rate~$\lambda$. 
Fix any $t> \tau_0$ and any
$\psi_{t-1} \in \ensuremath{\Psi^{\mathrm{BB}}(\Psi_0)}$ with $j=j^{\psi_{t-1}}$.
Let $\psi_t = \mathrm{hls}(\psi_{t-1},{\overline{b}}, t)$ for some ${\overline{b}}$.
Suppose that the transition $\psi_{t-1}\rightarrow \psi_t$ is via (R(item:R2 of the paper))(ii), (R(item:R5 of the paper)), or (R(item:R6 of the paper)).
Then for all $k \in \Upsilon_{j+1,\ge j^2}$,
$\min \{F_k^{\psi_t}(t+1),\mu_k^{\overline{\gamma}}\} \geq \min \{F_k^{\psi_{t-1}}(t),\mu_k^{\overline{\gamma}}\} - 2\lambda$.

[Theorem 7 (\cite{manfred259ergodic}, Theorem 8.13) of arXiv:2604.07579, 'Topology of Percolation Clusters: Central Limit Theorems beyond the Lattice'] Let $G = \Cay(\Gamma, S)$ be an infinite, amenable Cayley graph, equipped
    with an independent Bernoulli bond percolation $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \Prob
    _{p})$. Then, for any F{\o}lner sequence $(A_{r})_{r\geq 1}$ in $V$ and any
    $L^{2}$ random variable $X:\Omega\to \mathbb{R}$, we have:
    \[
      \frac{1}{|A_{r}|}\sum_{x\in A_r}X\circ\varphi_{x^{-1}}\underset{L^2}{\longrightarrow}
      \E_{p}[X],
    \]
    as $r \to \infty$.

body:
[Theorem thmq of arXiv:2411.03942, 'Asymptotic expansions relating to the distribution of the product of correlated normal ran'] Let $\mu_X,\mu_Y\in\mathbb{R}$, $\sigma_X,\sigma_Y>0$, $-1<\rho<1$ and $n\geq1$. 

Let $q=1-p$. 

\vspace{2mm}

\noindent 1. Suppose that $r_X+r_Y\not=0$. Then, as $p\rightarrow1$,
\begin{align}Q(p)&=s(1+\rho)\bigg\{\ln(1/q)+\frac{|r_X+r_Y|\sqrt{n}}{\sqrt{1+\rho}}\sqrt{\ln(1/q)}+\frac{n-3}{4}\ln(\ln(1/q))\nonumber\\
&\quad+\ln\bigg(\frac{(1+\rho)^{(n+1)/4}}{2\sqrt{2\pi}}\bigg(\frac{1+\rho}{|r_X+r_Y|\sqrt{n}}\bigg)^{(n-1)/2}\bigg)+\frac{n}{8}\bigg(\frac{1+\rho}{1-\rho}\bigg)(r_X-r_Y)^2\nonumber\\
&\quad+\frac{n}{4}\frac{(r_X+r_Y)^2}{1+\rho}-\frac{n}{2(1-\rho^2)}\big(r_X^2+r_Y^2-2\rho r_X r_Y\big)\nonumber\\
&\quad+\frac{(n-3)\sqrt{n}}{8}\frac{|r_X+r_Y|}{\sqrt{1+\rho}}\frac{\ln(\ln(1/q))}{\sqrt{\ln(1/q)}}\bigg\}+O\bigg(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\ln(1/q)}}\bigg). 
\end{align}
\noindent 2. Suppose that $r_X+r_Y=0$. Then, as $p\rightarrow1$,
\begin{align}Q(p)&=s(1+\rho)\bigg\{\ln(1/q)+\frac{1}{2}(n-2)\ln(\ln(1/q))+\ln\bigg(\frac{(1+\rho)^{n/2}}{2^{n/2}\Gamma(n/2)}\bigg)-\frac{nr_X^2}{2}\bigg\}\nonumber\\
&\quad+O\bigg(\frac{1}{\ln(1/q)}\bigg). 
\end{align}
\noindent 3. Suppose that $r_X-r_Y\not=0$. Then, as $p\rightarrow0$,
\begin{align}Q(p)&=-s(1-\rho)\bigg\{\ln(1/p)+\frac{|r_X-r_Y|\sqrt{n}}{\sqrt{1-\rho}}\sqrt{\ln(1/p)}+\frac{n-3}{4}\ln(\ln(1/p))\nonumber\\
&\quad+\ln\bigg(\frac{(1-\rho)^{(n+1)/4}}{2\sqrt{2\pi}}\bigg(\frac{1-\rho}{|r_X-r_Y|\sqrt{n}}\bigg)^{(n-1)/2}\bigg)+\frac{n}{8}\bigg(\frac{1-\rho}{1-\rho}\bigg)(r_X+r_Y)^2\nonumber\\
&\quad+\frac{n}{4}\frac{(r_X-r_Y)^2}{1-\rho}-\frac{n}{2(1-\rho^2)}\big(r_X^2+r_Y^2-2\rho r_X r_Y\big)\nonumber\\
&\quad+\frac{(n-3)\sqrt{n}}{8}\frac{|r_X-r_Y|}{\sqrt{1-\rho}}\frac{\ln(\ln(1/p))}{\sqrt{\ln(1/p)}}\bigg\}+O\bigg(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\ln(1/p)}}\bigg). 
\end{align}
\noindent 4. Suppose that $r_X-r_Y=0$. Then, as $p\rightarrow0$,
\begin{align}Q(p)&=-s(1-\rho)\bigg\{\ln(1/p)+\frac{1}{2}(n-2)\ln(\ln(1/p))+\ln\bigg(\frac{(1-\rho)^{n/2}}{2^{n/2}\Gamma(n/2)}\bigg)-\frac{nr_X^2}{2}\bigg\}\nonumber\\
&\quad+O\bigg(\frac{1}{\ln(1/p)}\bigg). 
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 56 of arXiv:2504.02435, 'Poisson-Voronoi percolation in higher rank'] Let $G$ be a connected semisimple real Lie group, $X$ be its symmetric space  and $\Gamma\subseteq G$ be a discrete subgroup.
    Then the following holds.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[{\rm(1)}] There is $k\in \mathbb{N}$ such that the restriction $p_\Gamma$ of the projection $p:G\to X$ to $\Gamma$ is $k$-to-$1$.
        Moreover, if $\Gamma$ is torsion-free, then $p_\Gamma$ is injective.
        \item[{\rm(2)}] The set $p_\Gamma(\Gamma)\subset X$ induces a $\Gamma$-equivariant Voronoi diagram $\{V_\gamma\}_{\gamma\in \Gamma}$ as a multi-set.
        Moreover, if $\Gamma$ is co-compact, then there is $R>0$ and $d\in \mathbb{N}$ with the property that $V_\gamma\subseteq \mathcal{B}_R(\gamma o)$ for every $\gamma\in \Gamma$ and every cell intersect $k(d+1)-1$ many other cells (where $k\in \mathbb{N}$ is from {\rm(1)}).
        \item[{\rm(3)}] Let $\mathbf Z=(Z(\gamma))_{\gamma\in\Gamma}$ be a collection of iid ${\rm Unif}[0,1]$ random variables and $\lambda>0$ and $p\in(0,1]$.
        Then $\omega_p^{(\lambda)}$ may be realized as a $\Gamma$-equivariant factor of $\mathbf Z$.        
    \end{enumerate}

body:
[Definition of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] For an f-model $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$, we define a \emph{hybrid satisfaction relation} $\Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M}$ on $W \times \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$ by:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item $x \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi_1 \to \psi_2 \mathrel{\;\ratio\Longleftrightarrow\;} \forall x' \geq x\, (x' \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi_1 \mathrel{\Rightarrow} x' \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi_2)$
    \item $x \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \Box \varphi     \mathrel{\;\ratio\Longleftrightarrow\;} \forall x' \geq x\, \forall y' \sqsupset x'\, (y' \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \varphi)$
    \item $x \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \varphi \mathrel{\;\ratio\Longleftrightarrow\;} \exists y \sqsupset x\, (y \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \varphi)$
    \item The other cases are identical to the classical $\Vdash_\mathfrak{M}$.
  \end{enumerate}
  We write $\mathfrak{M} \vDash^{\text{h}} \varphi$ (``$\varphi$ is \emph{(h-)valid in} $\mathfrak{M}$'') to mean $\forall x \in W\,(x \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \varphi)$,
  and $\mathfrak{F} \vDash^{\text{h}} \varphi$ (``$\varphi$ is \emph{(h-)valid on} $\mathfrak{F}$'') to mean that $\mathfrak{M} \vDash^{\text{h}} \varphi$ for every f-model $\mathfrak{M}$ based on $\mathfrak{F}$.
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical M'

body:
[Proposition 34 (Finite-cutoff Wick decomposition) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] For every $(a;b,c)\in\mathfrak L$, every finite cutoff $\Lambda$, and every
localized dyadic tuple $(N,R,L,Q,M)$ with $L\sim_{\mathrm{ap}}R$,
\begin{equation}
 T^{a;b,c}_{\Lambda,N,R,L,Q,M}=
 \begin{cases}
  \cD^{a;b}_{\Lambda,N,R,L,Q,M}
   +\cB^{a;b,b}_{\Lambda,N,R,L,Q,M},
   &(a;b,c)=(a;b,b)\in\mathfrak L_{\mathrm{diag}},\\
  \cB^{a;b,c}_{\Lambda,N,R,L,Q,M},
   &(a;b,c)\in\mathfrak L_{\mathrm{off}}.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
The centered term is a second homogeneous Gaussian chaos.  Its
two-localizer frequency kernel is displayed in
\eqref{eq:two-localizer-kernel}.  If $b=c$, the deterministic
contraction satisfies $r=-\ell$; hence $L\sim N$, and the resonant relation
$L\sim_{\mathrm{ap}}R$ also forces $R\sim N$.  The strict relation $n=q$ of
the translation-invariant reference core is replaced after localization by a
Schwartz kernel rapidly decaying away from $n=q$ in $n-q$.  If $b\ne c$, the deterministic
branch is absent.

body:
[Theorem thm:Birk along poly of arXiv:2411.00663, 'Ergodicity and Mixing of invariant capacities and applications'] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},P,T)$ be a measure preserving system, and let $p(x)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients. If $f \in L^r(\Omega,\mathcal{F},P)$, $r>1$, then
	$$
	\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} f(T^{p(i)} \omega)
	$$
	exists for $P$-a.s. $\omega \in \Omega$. Furthermore, if $T$ is weakly mixing, then
	the limit is equal to $\int fdP$, for $P$-a.s. $\omega\in\Omega$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:Birk along poly of arXiv:2411.00663

body:
[Lemm l:ZBdelta-moment-formula of arXiv:2607.18194, 'Temperature chaos in directed polymers'] For any Borel set $A\in\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^2)$, 
    we have (writing $\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{F}_A}[\,\cdot\,]\coloneqq \mathbb{E}[\,\cdot\,|\,\mathcal{F}_A]$)
    \begin{multline}
        \mathbb{E}\left[
            \mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{F}_A}[\mathcal{Z}_{B,\delta}^S]^2
        \right]\\
        =
        \int_{[a,b]^4}
        \left(
            \int_{(S^-\times S^+)^2}
            \mathbb{E}\left[
                \mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{F}_A}[\mathcal{Z}^-_{x'}(\mathbf{x}^-)
                \mathcal{Z}^+_{x''}(\mathbf{x}^+)]
                \mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{F}_A}[\mathcal{Z}^-_{y'}(\mathbf{y}^-)
                \mathcal{Z}^+_{y''}(\mathbf{y}^+)]
            \right]
            d\mathbf{x}^- d\mathbf{x}^+ d\mathbf{y}^- d\mathbf{y}^+
        \right)\times\\
        \times
        \left(
            \int_{(S^0)^2}
            \left\{
                \sum_{n_0,n_1,\dots,n_{m^0} \geqslant 0}
                \beta^{2(n_0+\cdots+n_{m^0})}
                \prod_{i=0}^{m^0}
                \mathbb{E}\left[
                    I_{n_i}\left(
                        \1_{A}^{\otimes n_i}\,
                        p^{(n_i)}_{(t_i^0, x_i^0), (t_{i+1}^0, x_{i+1}^0)}
                    \right)
                    I_{n_i}\left(
                        \1_{A}^{\otimes n_i}\,
                        p^{(n_i)}_{(t_i^0, y_i^0), (t_{i+1}^0, y_{i+1}^0)}
                    \right)
                \right]
                \right\}
            d\mathbf{x}^0 d\mathbf{y}^0
        \right)\\
        dx'\,dx''\,dy'\,dy''.
    \end{multline} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemm l:ZBdelta-moment-formula of arXiv:2607.18194

body:
[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2606.24090, 'Sparsity-adaptive concentration inequalities for random polynomials'] Let $A=(A_{i_1,\ldots,i_{2d}})$ be a $2d$-tensor. Fix
$I=\{k_1,\ldots,k_l\}\subseteq[d]$ with $k_1<\cdots<k_l$, and fix
$\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^l$. Let $T_{I,\varepsilon}A$ be defined by
\eqref{eq:B_T_I_epsilon_A}, and let $\rho_{I,\varepsilon}$ be defined by
\eqref{eq:B_rho_I_epsilon}.

Let $I_2\subseteq[2l]$ and set
\[
    F:=\rho_{I,\varepsilon}(I_2)\subseteq[2d].
\]
For a fixed $j_{I_2}$, denote by $j_F^\rho$ the corresponding fixed coordinates
of $A$, namely
\[
    i_{\rho_{I,\varepsilon}(s)}=j_s,
    \qquad s\in I_2.
\]
If $\mathcal J=\{J_1,\ldots,J_\kappa\}\in
\Pi([2l]\setminus I_2)$, define
\begin{equation}
    \mathcal K
    :=
    \rho_{I,\varepsilon}(\mathcal J)
    \cup
    \bigl\{\{t,d+t\}:t\in[d]\setminus I\bigr\}.
\end{equation}
Then $\mathcal K$ is a partition of $[2d]\setminus F$, and
\begin{equation}
    \bigl\|
    (T_{I,\varepsilon}A)_{j_{I_{2}^{c}}}
    \bigr\|_{\mathcal J}
    \le
    n^{(d-l)/2}
    \bigl\|A_{(j_F^\rho)^{\,c}}\bigr\|_{\mathcal K}.
\end{equation}
In particular, if $I_2=\varnothing$, then
\begin{equation}
    \|T_{I,\varepsilon}A\|_{\mathcal J}
    \le
    n^{(d-l)/2}
    \|A\|_{\rho_{I,\varepsilon}(\mathcal J),\,\{\{t,d+t\}:t\in[d]\setminus I\}}.
\end{equation}
title: Lemma 10 of arXiv:2606.24090

body: In mathematics, the Cartan–Hadamard theorem is a statement in Riemannian geometry concerning the structure of complete Riemannian manifolds of non-positive sectional curvature. The theorem states that the universal cover of such a manifold is diffeomorphic to a Euclidean space via the exponential map at any point. It was first proved by Hans Carl Friedrich von Mangoldt for surfaces in 1881, and independently by Jacques Hadamard in 1898. Élie Cartan generalized the theorem to Riemannian manifolds in 1928. The theorem was further generalized to a wide class of metric spaces by Mikhail Gromov in 1987; detailed proofs were published by Ballmann (1990) for metric spaces of non-positive curvature and by Alexander & Bishop (1990) for general locally convex metric spaces.
title: Cartan–Hadamard theorem

[Definition 8 (Action on measures) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] For a finite signed measure $h \in \Sign$ and a number $n \in \Nz$ we define
the finite signed measure $T^{n} \circ h \in \Sign$ by
\[
  (T^{n} \circ h)(A) := \int_{\XX} T^{n}(A \mid x)\, h(\dd x)
  \qquad (A \in \XXA),
\]
the integral of a bounded measurable map against $h$ being defined, as usual, as its
integral against $h^{+}$ minus its integral against $h^{-}$.
The map $h \mapsto T^{n}\circ h$ is a linear map $\Sign \to \Sign$ which
maps $\Prob$ into $\Prob$, and it satisfies
\[
  T \circ (T^{n} \circ h) = T^{n+1} \circ h \qquad (n \in \Nz),
\]
because for every bounded measurable map $g : \XX \to \R$ one has
$\int g \dd(T^{n}\circ h) = \int \bigl( \int g(z)\,T^{n}(\dd z \mid x) \bigr)
h(\dd x)$. That identity holds for indicator maps by the displayed formula, hence for
nonnegative simple maps by linearity, hence for every measurable
$g : \XX \to [0,\infty]$ by monotone convergence, applied to $h^{+}$ and to $h^{-}$
separately; a bounded measurable $g : \XX \to \R$ is then treated by writing
$g = g^{+}-g^{-}$.

[Theorem Integral formula for Green functions of arXiv:2606.06187, 'How to Study Reflected Brownian Motion in a Quadrant via Kernel Functional Equations?\\ \m'] The Laplace transform $\widehat g_1^{z_0}$ can be written as follows:
$$
\widehat g_1^{z_0} (y)=
\frac{-F (w(y))}{2i\pi} \int_{\mathcal{R}^-} \frac{g(t)}{Y^+ (w(t))}
\left(
 \frac{w'(t) }{w(t)-w(y)}
 + \chi
  \frac{ w'(t) }{w(t)} 
  \right)
  \mathrm{d}t
$$
where $\chi=0$ or $1$, and
$$
F (w(y))=w(y)^{\chi} 
\exp  \left(
\frac{1}{2i\pi} \int_{\mathcal{R}^-} \log(G(t))\left(\frac{ w'(t)}{w(t)-w(y)}- \frac{ w'(t)}{w(t)} \right) \mathrm{d}t
\right),
$$
where $Y^+$ is the boundary value on $\mathcal{R}$ of the function $X$ defined on $\mathcal{D}_\mathcal{R}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Integral formula for Green functions

[Definition d:minimal-energy-dominant of arXiv:2510.13659, 'On the energy image density conjecture of Bouleau and Hirsch'] {hinoenergymeasures}}]
		Let $(X,d,\mu,\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F})$ be an MMD space and let $\Gamma(\cdot,\cdot)$ denote the corresponding energy measure. A $\sigma$-finite Borel measure
		$\nu$ on $X$ is called a \textbf{minimal energy-dominant measure}
		of $(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F})$ if the following two conditions are satisfied:
		\begin{enumerate} 
			\item[(i)](Domination) For every $f \in \mathcal{F}$, we have $\Gamma(f,f) \ll \nu$.
			\item[(ii)](Minimality) If another $\sigma$-finite Borel measure $\nu'$
			on $X$ satisfies condition (i) with $\nu$ replaced
			by $\nu'$, then $\nu \ll \nu'$.
		\end{enumerate}
		The existence of minimal energy dominant measure is due to Nakao [Nak] (see also [hinoenergymeasures]).  It is immediate that any two minimal energy dominant measures are mutually absolutely continuous.

[Lemma 28 of arXiv:2606.11271, '\LARGE The $K$-th nearest neighbor random walk on a Poisson point process gets trapped'] Fix $p\in (0,1)$ and let $(Z_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be the Markov chain on $\mathbb{Z}$ starting from $0$ with transition probabilities:
\[
\P(Z_{n+1}=j \mid Z_n=i) = \begin{cases} 
(1-p)\mathbf{1}_{j=1}+p\mathbf{1}_{j=-1} & \text{if } i= 0 \\
(1-p)\mathbf{1}_{j=i-1}+p\mathbf{1}_{j=i+1}  & \text{if } i\neq 0. \end{cases}
\]
Let $U \coloneqq \inf\{n\ge 0 : |Z_n|=3\}$. Then 
\[ \P(Z_U=3) = 1 - \P(Z_U=-3) = p. \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lem 16 of arXiv:2605.23659, '2605.23659'] Let \(f_n,f:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) be non-decreasing functions and suppose
\[
f(0)=0,
\quad
f(\infty)=\infty.
\]
Assume that there exists a dense subset \(D\subset[0,\infty)\) such that
\[
f_n(x)\to f(x)
\quad (n\to\infty)
\]
for every \(x\in D\).
Then, for every continuity point \(t\ge0\) of \(f^{-1}\),
\[
f_n^{-1}(t)\to f^{-1}(t)
\quad (n\to\infty),
\]
where \(f_n^{-1}\) and \(f^{-1}\) denote the right-continuous inverses.
Moreover, if \(f\) is strictly increasing,
\[
\sup_{u\in[0,T]}|f_n^{-1}(u)-f^{-1}(u)|\to0
\quad (n\to\infty)
\]
for every \(T>0\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lem lemequiv of arXiv:2608.25865, 'Instability of Böhm's Einstein metrics'] Let $\eta$ and $\delta>0$ be as in Lemma (lemqtilde of the paper). Let $v_\delta(s)=\phi_\delta(e^s)e^{\beta s}$. We define for all $v\in H^1(\mathbb{R})$ $$S(v)=\frac{\displaystyle\int_\mathbb{R} v'^2}{\displaystyle\int_\mathbb{R} v^2}.$$
    Then, $$\tilde Q(\phi_\delta)<0 \quad \text{if and only if} \quad S(v_\delta)<\alpha^2,$$
 where $\alpha^2=2(\Lambda-1)-\beta^2=\frac{(9-\Lambda)(\Lambda-1)}4>0$ since $4\leqslant \Lambda \leqslant 8$.

[Lemma 27 of arXiv:2609.04033, 'From configuration spaces to graph complexes via $\mathbf{FA}$-modules'] If $d\equiv 0$ mod $4$ then there exists an $S_n$-equivariant quasi-isomorphism
	$$
 \mathsf{T}^{1,1}_\Gamma(n)_d  \stackrel{\sim}\to\Sigma^{d+1}\Omega(\mathsf{C}_{(d/2)^\ast}\circ^{S_2} \mathsf{C}_{(d/2)^\ast})(n) \oplus \ds\bigoplus_{\substack{ r > s \geq 2\\ r,s \text{ both even }  \\ r+s =d}}\Sigma^{d+1}\Omega(\mathsf{C}_{(r)^\ast}\circ \mathsf{C}_{(s)^\ast}) (n).
	$$

body:
Let (X_n)_{n=1}^\infty be independent random variables with \mathbb{E}[X_n] = 0. Let \phi: [0, \infty) \to [0, \infty) be a strictly increasing, convex function such that \phi(0) = 0, \phi(x)/x \uparrow \infty and \phi(x)/x^2 is nonincreasing on (0, \infty). If \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\mathbb{E}[\phi(|X_n|)]}{\phi(n)} < \infty, then \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=1}^n X_k \to 0 almost surely.
(X_n) independent, mean zero
\phi convex, strictly increasing, \phi(x)/x \to \infty
\phi(x)/x^2 nonincreasing on (0, \infty) (without it the law fails: \phi(x) = x^4, X_n = \sqrt{n}\,\varepsilon_n)
\sum \mathbb{E}[\phi(|X_n|)]/\phi(n) < \infty

[Definition def:three of arXiv:2607.09946, 'Statistics on Yau's conjecture: Variance asymptotics'] {cgv2025StecconiTodino}}{}]
We define three deterministic positive real numbers associated to $M,g,\phi$: the \emph{average variance $\sigma$}, the \emph{average frequency $\lambda$} as follows.
\begin{equation} 
\sigma^2=\sigma(\phi)^2:=\fint_M 
\mathbb{E}\left\{ \phi(x)^2\right\} dx,\quad \lambda^2=\lambda(\phi)^2:=\frac{1}{\sigma^2}\fint_M \mathbb{E}\left\{ \|d_x\phi\|^2\right\} dx,
\end{equation} 
and the \emph{maximal eccentricity} of $\phi$:
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned} 
\varepsilon=\varepsilon(\phi):=\max_{x\in M,\ u\in S(T_xM)}\left|\frac{\sqrt{\mathbb{E}\left\{ |\langle d_x\phi,u\rangle|^2\right\}}}{\sigma\lambda}\sqrt{n}-1\right| 
\\
+\max_{x\in M}\left|\frac{\sqrt{\mathbb{E}\left\{ \phi(x)^2\right\}}}{\sigma}-1\right|
+
\max_{x\in M,\ u\in S(T_xM)}\left|\langle d_x\frac{\sqrt{\mathbb{E}\left\{ \phi(\cdot)^2\right\}}}{\sigma}, u\rangle \right|\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\lambda}.
\end{aligned}\end{equation}
When $\varepsilon(\phi)=0$, we say that $\phi$ is a \emph{homothetic field}.

[Lemma 60 (Logarithmic Schatten selection) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Fix $p\ge2$, $\delta>0$, and $C\ge1$.  For dyadic
$1\le Q,M\le CN$, choose
\[
 r_{N}:=\max\left\{p,\,2,\,\delta^{-1}\log(2+N)\right\}.
\]
Then $p\le r_N<\infty$ and
\begin{equation}
 r_N\bigl(1+N^{3/r_N}+Q^{3/r_N}+M^{3/r_N}\bigr)
 \lesssim_{p,\delta,C}N^\delta.
\end{equation}
The same assertion holds with $p$ replaced by any prescribed finite moment
$p_0$.  Thus a logarithmically growing Schatten exponent converts all finite
shell-volume remnants and the linear Khintchine factor into an arbitrarily
small power of the principal shell.

body:
Let Z be standard normal, g(z)=phi(z)+z Phi(z), a=1/sqrt(pi), and v=1/3+(sqrt(3)-2)/(2*pi). Then E[g(Z)]=a and Var(g(Z))=v. W=(a-g(Z))/sqrt(v) has support (-infinity,a/sqrt(v)] and no atom at its finite endpoint. For w<a/sqrt(v), with z=g^{-1}(a-sqrt(v)w), its CDF is 1-Phi(z) and its density is sqrt(v)*phi(z)/Phi(z). This non-Gaussian law is the standardized-degree limit only conditional on the earlier degree/moment convergence being established in a stated regime.

Let Z be standard normal, phi its density, Phi its distribution function, and g(z)=phi(z)+z*Phi(z). Put a=1/sqrt(pi), v=1/3+(sqrt(3)-2)/(2*pi), and W=(a-g(Z))/sqrt(v).     P(W<=w)=1-Phi(z),
    density_W(w)=sqrt(v)*phi(z)/Phi(z).

Proof: differentiation gives g'=Phi>0 and g''=phi. Also g(z)=E[(z-Y)_+] for an independent standard normal Y, so g is positive; it tends to zero as z tends to minus infinity and diverges at plus infinity. Thus it is a continuous increasing bijection onto (0,infinity). The distribution and density follow by reversing its monotone change of variables. No finite Z maps to the upper endpoint, so that endpoint has no mass.

For the constants, normal integration by parts gives E[phi(Z)]=1/(2*sqrt(pi)) and E[Z*Phi(Z)]=E[phi(Z)], hence E[g(Z)]=a. Write A=E[phi(Z)^2]=1/(2*pi*sqrt(3)) and B=E[Z*phi(Z)*Phi(Z)]=A/2, by integrating the derivative of phi^2. Since Phi(Z) is uniform, E[Phi(Z)^2]=1/3. Applying E[Z^2*h(Z)]=E[h(Z)]+E[h''(Z)] to h=Phi^2 gives E[Z^2*Phi(Z)^2]=1/3+2A-2B=1/3+A. Therefore E[g(Z)^2]=A+2B+(1/3+A)=1/3+sqrt(3)/(2*pi). Subtracting a^2 gives v. All integrations have Gaussian tails, so the boundary terms vanish. A nondegenerate Gaussian has no finite upper endpoint; W does.

This consequence does not extend the packet to other k regimes. The saved attempt's error O(k^2/n+k^5/n^2) tends to zero, for example, when k tends to infinity and k=o(n^(2/5)); that observation alone is not a proof of the whole graph limit.

[Proposition prop_omega_rk1 of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] Suppose that $E$ is a complex of ``rank 1'' representations of $Q$, i.e.\ $\dim E_i^n\leq 1$ for all $i\in Q_0,n\in\bZ$.
Then the component of $\Omega$ on $E_i^n$ (complex scalar) is given by
\begin{align*}
\Omega_i^n= \,&(-1)^n  e^{-\beta_i^n-\beta_i^{n+1}}\Bigg(z_i \\
&+\sum_{a\colon i\to j}\left(\alpha_a^n +(\alpha_a^n-\alpha_a^{n-1})(\beta_i^n-\beta_j^n)\varphi_2(\beta_i^n-\beta_j^n+\beta_i^{n+1}-\beta_j^{n-1})\right) \\
&+\sum_{a\colon k\to i}\left(-\alpha_a^n+(\alpha_a^{n+1}-\alpha_a^{n})(\beta_i^{n+1}-\beta_k^{n+1})\varphi_2(\beta_i^{n+1}-\beta_k^{n+1}+\beta_i^{n}-\beta_k^{n+2})\right)\Bigg)    
\end{align*}
where
\[
\alpha_a^n\coloneqq\rho^n(a)\rho^n(a)^\dagger,\qquad \beta_i^n\coloneqq d^n_i(d^n_i)^\dagger,\qquad \varphi_2(s)\coloneqq\frac{e^s-s-1}{s^2}.
\]
Here, $d_i^n\colon E_i^{n-1}\to E_i^n$ and $\rho^n(a)\colon E_i^n\to E_j^n$ for $a\colon i\to j$ and $\alpha_a^n$, $\beta_i^n$ are considered as non-negative real scalars.

Own-work draft; status: independently checked proof. For a fixed pair of internally compatible nearest-neighbor path halves under independent iid fair two-color scenery, let V^- and V^+ be their observed spatial sites, and K=|V^- intersect V^+|. Let A mean that the two records prescribe the same color at every shared site. The joint record likelihood equals L^- L^+ 2^K 1_A, where each half likelihood is 2^(-|V^sign|) and is zero for internal incompatibility. Because the two increment halves are independent before color conditioning, their joint two-sided posterior is the product of the separate half-posteriors reweighted by 2^K 1_A and normalized by its positive expectation. Spatial zero is included in K if both halves revisit it; the origin color is not fixed in this identity. Bounding this overlap reweighting uniformly is an unproved input for transferring one-sided escape estimates.

[Corollary 16 (Absorption of multiplicative noise) of arXiv:2609.02728, 'Momentum in large-batch training: Polyak enlarges the critical batch size, Nesterov improv'] For $\sigma > 0$, under the stability condition $\eta \lesssim \min\{1,B(1-\rho)\}$, the multiplicative gradient noise is strictly bounded by the additive label noise up to a constant factor:
\[
    \frac{\eta^2}{B}\sum_{\tau=0}^{k-1}\mathcal{K}_{\polyak}(\tau)\EE[\cE(\btheta_{k-1-\tau})] \le \frac{M}{\sigma^2} \left( \frac{\eta^2\sigma^2}{B}\sum_{\tau=0}^{k-1}\mathcal{K}_{\polyak}(\tau) \right).
\]
Consequently, the multiplicative noise can be absorbed, and the expected excess risk is asymptotically equivalent to the sum of the deterministic bias and the label noise:
\[
    \EE[\cE(\btheta_k)] \eqsim \cS_{\polyak}(k) + \frac{\eta^2\sigma^2}{B}\sum_{\tau=0}^{k-1}\mathcal{K}_{\polyak}(\tau).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Absorption of multiplicative noise

[Lemma 33 of arXiv:2609.02808, 'Minimizers of Laplace eigenvalues under a lower curvature bound'] For each fixed $\theta\in(0,\pi)$, the map
$\mu\mapsto\bar\gamma(\theta;\mu)$ is strictly increasing. Moreover, for
every $j\ge1$,
\begin{equation}
\bar\gamma(\theta;j(j+1))
+
\bar\gamma(\pi-\theta;j(j+1))
=
j\pi.
\end{equation}
In particular, if $\mu<j(j+1)$, then
\[
\bar\gamma(\theta;\mu)
+
\bar\gamma(\pi-\theta;\mu)
<j\pi.
\]

body:
Let (X, B, mu, T) be a measure-preserving system on a STANDARD Borel (Lebesgue) probability space, and let I be the sub-sigma-algebra of T-invariant sets.

ERGODIC DECOMPOSITION. There is a measurable family x -> mu_x of T-invariant Borel probability measures on X such that (i) mu_x is a version of the conditional measure of mu given I, so mu(A) = integral of mu_x(A) d mu(x) for every A in B and integral of f d mu = integral over x of (integral of f d mu_x) d mu(x) for f in L^1(mu); (ii) mu_x is ERGODIC for mu-a.e. x; (iii) the family is essentially unique. Writing P for the law of the random measure x -> mu_x, one gets mu = integral of nu dP(nu) supported on the ergodic T-invariant measures -- the Choquet representation of mu in the simplex of invariant measures.

AFFINITY OF ENTROPY. Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy is affine in the measure, with values in [0, +infinity]:
  for every finite measurable partition Q,   h_mu(T, Q) = integral of h_{mu_x}(T, Q) d mu(x);
  and                                        h_mu(T)    = integral of h_{mu_x}(T) d mu(x).
In particular, for T-invariant mu and nu and t in [0,1],  h_{t mu + (1-t) nu}(T) = t h_mu(T) + (1-t) h_nu(T).

SHARP EDGES. (1) AFFINE IS NOT CONTINUOUS: nu -> h_nu(T) is affine on the simplex of invariant measures but is in general NOT weak-* continuous; for expansive homeomorphisms it is upper semicontinuous, and in general it can fail even that. Do not use affinity to pass to weak-* limits. (2) The decomposition genuinely needs a standard/Lebesgue space; on a pathological measure space conditional measures need not exist and the statement can fail. (3) The convex combination must be of INVARIANT measures -- entropy is undefined for a non-invariant measure, so there is no affinity statement along an arbitrary path in the space of measures. (4) The identity holds in [0, +infinity]; if h_mu(T) = +infinity the integral is +infinity, and no finiteness is assumed anywhere. (5) The affinity is a property of measure-theoretic entropy, not of topological entropy: the variational principle gives h_top(T) = sup over invariant nu of h_nu(T), which is a supremum over the simplex, so it is attained (if at all) at ergodic measures precisely BECAUSE h is affine -- but h_top itself is not an average.
(X, B, mu, T) is measure-preserving on a standard Borel (Lebesgue) probability space
mu is T-invariant; entropies are Kolmogorov-Sinai entropies with values in [0, +infinity]
the ergodic decomposition is taken over the sigma-algebra of T-invariant sets
convex combinations are of T-INVARIANT measures only
no finiteness of entropy and no continuity of the entropy map is assumed or asserted

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:517281da6fc4fded44e85d52dcf610db117316849f2f169c606a5b7dd0cefac8","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/51/517281da6fc4fded44e85d52dcf610db117316849f2f169c606a5b7dd0cefac8.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:6dfc6007a8df781d09125f492dcccf14d7708dde09a4ec3265fdaa6178c78c83","bundle_entry_key":"ergodic_decomposition_entropy_affine","bundle_id":"population.pivot2-dynamics-b","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"ergodic theory, entropy","draft":"claude-pivot2-dynamics-b/bundle_pivot2-dynamics-b.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:dynamics.ergodic:ergodic-decomposition-and-affinity-of-entropy","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Existence and uniqueness of the ergodic decomposition is the disintegration of mu over the factor map onto the invariant sigma-algebra I, available on a standard space (Rokhlin); ergodicity of almost every fibre measure follows since the conditional measures are, almost surely, invariant and their own invariant sigma-algebra is trivial -- concretely, by the Birkhoff ergodic theorem the limits of ergodic averages of a countable dense family of continuous functions are I-measurable, and they identify mu_x-a.e. with the corresponding mu_x-integrals.

Affinity, finite convex combinations first. Let phi(s) = -s log s (concave on [0,1]). For any finite partition Q and t in [0,1]:
  lower bound: H_{t mu + (1-t) nu}(Q) >= t H_mu(Q) + (1-t) H_nu(Q) by concavity of phi applied atom by atom;
  upper bound: H_{t mu + (1-t) nu}(Q) <= t H_mu(Q) + (1-t) H_nu(Q) + log 2, obtained by adjoining a Bernoulli(t) label L that records which of the two measures a point is drawn from and using H(X) <= H(X, L) = H(L) + H(X | L), with H(L) <= log 2.
Apply both bounds to Q_n = the join of T^{-i} Q for 0 <= i < n, divide by n and let n go to infinity: the additive log 2 disappears and h_{t mu + (1-t) nu}(T, Q) = t h_mu(T, Q) + (1 - t) h_nu(T, Q).

The integral version (Jacobs' theorem) is the same estimate with the two-point mixture replaced by the integral decomposition: the concavity bound integrates directly, and the label term is replaced by the entropy of a finite measurable partition of the index space, whose contribution is again O(1) and is killed after dividing by n; measurability of x -> h_{mu_x}(T, Q) holds because each H_{mu_x}(Q_n) is a measurable function of x.

From partitions to the entropy itself: on a standard space choose an increasing sequence of finite partitions Q_1 < Q_2 < ... generating B modulo mu. Since a mu-null set is mu_x-null for a.e. x and the algebra generated is countable, the same sequence generates modulo mu_x for mu-a.e. x. By the Kolmogorov-Sinai theorem h_mu(T) = lim_k h_mu(T, Q_k) and h_{mu_x}(T) = lim_k h_{mu_x}(T, Q_k) for a.e. x, both limits increasing. Apply the partition-wise identity for each k and pass to the limit by monotone convergence. (This last step is where a bare supremum over all partitions would not suffice: a supremum of affine functions is only convex, so the generating sequence is doing real work.)","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:d37b643574863d0d87862b211345cdbd8fa1472dd80b325dff599f991ba15499","revision_digest":"sha256:c423ff08a284a7ccfc7dc1d8f089019abb153806f7c00355fd50d003464125fc","source_id":"wikipedia:Measure-theoretic_entropy","source_revision":"as-read-2026-09-12","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2603.26217, 'On associative neural networks for sparse patterns with huge capacities'] Consider Amari's model with fixed interaction order $n$, defined by
	\eqref{multdyn} and \eqref{multhebb}, and choose
	\[
	h=\gamma \log^{n-1} N
	\]
	for some $0<\gamma<1$. Then there exists $\alpha_0=\alpha_0(n,\gamma)>0$ such that
	for every $\alpha<\alpha_0$, the choice
	\[
	M=\alpha \frac{N^n}{(\log N)^n}
	\]
	satisfies
	\[
	\mathbb P\bigl(T(\xi^\mu)=\xi^\mu\bigr)\longrightarrow1
	\qquad\text{as }N\to\infty
	\]
	for every fixed stored pattern $\xi^\mu$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2603.26217

[Proposition 10 (Persistence through reset) of arXiv:2608.16701, 'Order-Sensitive Fast-Synapse Limits in Sparse Excitatory--Inhibitory Threshold--Reset Netw'] Fix $\rho>0$ and $T_P>\rho$.  There are uniformly bounded-degree,
Dale-compatible networks with the same initial data in both orderings such
that, for every $t_*>T_P$ and every $\varepsilon_N\downarrow0$,
\begin{equation}
 F_N^{\varepsilon_N,\E}(\rho/2)
 -F_N^{\varepsilon_N,\I}(\rho/2)\longrightarrow\frac14,
 \qquad
 F_N^{\varepsilon_N,\E}(t_*)
 -F_N^{\varepsilon_N,\I}(t_*)\longrightarrow\frac12.
 
\end{equation}
For all sufficiently large $N$ along the stated sequence, every nonisolated
target has fired twice by $t_*$ under E-first and has not fired under
I-first.

Method: Deterministic limits for trace-reinforced ants structural argument Result: If two parallel edges connect N directly to F, an ant crosses exactly one and reinforces it. Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). After the optimism reading was refuted (P20), the gain was located row by row: the per-evaluation-row relative-score gain of the long-only stack over least squares against the bootstrap variance of the least-squares stack at that row. P22 (a) REFUTED at the pre-registered 0.2: the within-cell median Spearman between a row's gain and the least-squares variance load at that row is 0.13 over the 40 EMIT cells (positive in 36 of 40; 0.37 on Y2, 0.01 on Y1); (b) HELD on Y2, REFUTED as an every-group claim: the top-decile-load rows carry 47 pct of Y2's gain (a uniform spread gives 10) but only 11 pct on Y1 (20 on Y3, 32 on Y4); (c) HELD: across the 40 EMIT cells the gain rank-correlates 0.54 with the variance-load share of least squares' error, and 0.65 with the share the constraint removes (least squares minus nn1) - the between-cell statistic that optimism (P20) failed to be; (d) REFUTED as written: the OCO-2 top-decile share reaches 0.40 on sco2, but as the share of a gain of -0.55 pct it is the ratio of two near-zero numbers and does not test the clause; falsifier (within-cell correlation at or below zero) not triggered. Reading: where the gain is large (Y2, +18) it sits where least squares is uncertain - row-level rank correlation 0.37, 47 pct of the gain on the tenth of rows with the largest variance; where it is modest (+5 to +6) it is spread over the rows; between cells the variance-load share of least squares' error predicts the gain (0.54) and the variance the constraint removes predicts it better (0.65). The calibration and evaluation rows share the same target-norm distribution, so this is not a split shift; the gain leans toward the small-norm evaluation rows the reported metric weights most. Cell level: the variance the constraint removes (least squares' bootstrap variance share minus the long-only stack's) predicts the gain within every output group (Spearman 0.79, 0.87, 0.54, 0.43 on Y1-Y4; 0.69 across 40 cells with the group effect removed), while the L1 norm of the least-squares weights does not survive the group adjustment (0.02): the constraint pays what it saves in estimation variance at the rows it is scored on. Fresh-split replication (split C, SPLIT_SEED 11): P23 (a) REFUTED at the per-group 0.5, HELD in the aggregate: on split C the within-group Spearman between the gain and the variance removed is +0.59, +0.49, +0.64, +0.22 on Y1..Y4 and +0.74 across the 40 cells with the group effect removed (split B: +0.69); (b) REFUTED: the split-B variance-removed share predicts the split-C gain only on Y1 and Y2 (+0.72, +0.47; Y3 +0.09, Y4 -0.24; demeaned +0.17), and the split-B gain itself predicts the split-C gain only weakly (Y1 +0.82, Y4 +0.47, Y2 +0.15, Y3 -0.14); (c) HELD: the long-only stack beats least squares on 35 of 40 split-C cells (mean +9.59 against +8.83 on split B); falsifier (any group at or below 0.2, or the demeaned correlation at or below 0.3) not triggered. Fresh-split check of the calibration-side correlates (P32, the P20 driver on split C): P32 (a) HELD: on split C the between-cell Spearman of the gain with the least-squares L1 is +0.55 and with n_eff -0.44; (b) REFUTED: group-demeaned, L1 +0.29 and members kept +0.21; (c) HELD: the nn0 RMSE gain with the smallest relative eigenvalue +0.29 and with the condition number -0.31; falsifier (L1 above +0.3 after the group adjustment) not triggered. The gain off the tail (P36, the top tenth of evaluation rows by |gain| removed): P36 (a) HELD for the sign, REFUTED for the size: the trimmed gain is positive on 36 and 36 of 40 EMIT cells (splits B, C) but reads +7.67 and +8.30 against untrimmed +8.83 and +9.59 - the body keeps 87 pct of the gain, not less than half; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the trimmed gain is +0.25 against -0.18 untrimmed; (c) REFUTED: the smallest trimmed gain is on Y4, not Y1; falsifier (negative trimmed gain on EMIT) not triggered. Removing the two-sided tail leaves 87 pct of the EMIT gain: the constraint pays broadly across the rows, and the non-transfer between splits comes from the tails' noise, not from where the gain sits. P46: the mechanism on the third family (P46): P46 (a) REFUTED: within-family Spearman(gain, variance removed) = burgers +0.55, darcy +0.80, pkanrtm -0.12 (families with at least ten cells; threshold 0.3); (b) HELD: family-demeaned across 55 cells +0.65 (threshold 0.4); (c) HELD: the family with the most negative gain is pkanrtm, the family with the smallest variance removed is pkanrtm; falsifier (demeaned correlation at or below 0.1) not triggered.

[Definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The orthogonal polynomials with respect to $d\mu(x)=f(x)dx$ are polynomials $P_k\in\mathbb R[x]$ of degree $k\in\mathbb N$, which are orthogonal inside $H=L^2(\mathbb R,\mu)$:
$$\int_\mathbb RP_k(x)P_l(x)f(x)dx=0\quad,\quad\forall k\neq l$$
Equivalently, these orthogonal polynomials $\{P_k\}_{k\in\mathbb N}$, which are each unique modulo scalars, appear from the Weierstrass basis $\{x^k\}_{k\in\mathbb N}$, by doing Gram-Schmidt.

A real-valued random variable X is called sub-Gaussian if there exists a constant sigma^2 >= 0 such that for all lambda in R, E[exp(lambda * (X - E[X]))] <= exp(lambda^2 * sigma^2 / 2). The parameter sigma^2 is called a variance proxy (or sub-Gaussian parameter) for X.
X is an integrable real-valued random variable

body: Let f : M -> N be a C^k map between smooth manifolds of dimensions m and n respectively, with k >= max(1, m - n + 1). Call x in M a critical point if the differential df_x : T_xM -> T_(f(x))N fails to be surjective, and call f(x) a critical value for such x. Then the set of critical values of f has Lebesgue measure zero in N, measured in any smooth chart, so almost every point of N is a regular value, even though the critical set in M can itself be large, even all of M in degenerate examples.
title: Sard's theorem

body:
[Theorem 39 of arXiv:2608.17374, '\textbf{On the Pseudo-Mixing of Kac's Walk}'] There is a universal constant $C<\infty$ with the following property. Let $Q$ be an $\So{n}$-valued random matrix whose law is $(d_{\mathrm{ph}},L)$-pseudo-Haar in the sense of \eqref{EqJLPseudoHaarDef}. Let $\mathcal X\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ have $N\geq2$ points, and let $0<\varepsilon,\delta<1$. Set
\be 
r=\left\lceil C\log\frac{N}{\delta}\right\rceil.
\ee
Assume
\be 
4r\leq d_{\mathrm{ph}},\qquad
\ell\geq C\varepsilon^{-2}r,
\qquad
L\log n\geq \log\frac{2\binom{N}{2}}{\delta}+2r\log\frac{n}{\varepsilon\ell}.
\ee
Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$ over $Q$,
\be 
(1-\varepsilon)\|x_i-x_j\|_2^2
\leq
\|A_Q(x_i-x_j)\|_2^2
\leq
(1+\varepsilon)\|x_i-x_j\|_2^2
\ee
for every pair $1\leq i<j\leq N$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 39 of arXiv:2608.17374

[Theorem 1 (\cite{efron1981jackknife}, \cite{steele1986efron}) of arXiv:2605.05388, 'The Efron-Stein inequality for identically distributed pairs'] Let \(X_1,\ldots, X_n,Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\) be \(2n\) independent random variables with \(X_i\stackrel{d}{=} Y_i\) for all \(i\). Let \(f\) be a measurable function, and let \(Z_i=f(X_1\ldots X_{i},Y_{i+1},\ldots Y_n)\) for \(i=0,\dots,n\). Then
$$
E(Z_n-Z_0)^2\le \sum_{i=1}^n E(Z_i-Z_{i-1})^2.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{efron1981jackknife}, \cite{steele1986efron}

body:
Let H be a complex Hilbert space and T a compact operator on H. List its nonzero eigenvalues lambda_1, lambda_2, ... with |lambda_1| >= |lambda_2| >= ... , repeated according to algebraic multiplicity and padded with zeros if there are finitely many, and let s_1(T) >= s_2(T) >= ... be the singular values. Then for every n, the product of |lambda_1| ... |lambda_n| is at most the product of s_1(T) ... s_n(T). Consequently, for every p > 0 and every n, sum_{k <= n} |lambda_k|^p <= sum_{k <= n} s_k(T)^p; in particular, if T is Hilbert-Schmidt then sum_k |lambda_k|^2 <= ||T||_2^2 (Schur's inequality), and if T is trace class then sum_k |lambda_k| <= ||T||_1. The inequalities are equalities for normal T.
H is a complex Hilbert space
T is a compact operator on H
eigenvalues are listed with algebraic multiplicity in nonincreasing order of modulus
p > 0

Using the Riesz-Schauder theory, the generalized eigenspaces for lambda_1, ..., lambda_n span a T-invariant subspace, and inside the last generalized eigenspace one can choose a T-invariant subspace of the right dimension (a Jordan flag), so there is an n-dimensional T-invariant subspace M with the eigenvalues of the matrix T|_M equal to lambda_1, ..., lambda_n. Then the absolute value of det(T|_M) is the product of |lambda_1| ... |lambda_n|. On the other hand, for an n-dimensional subspace the absolute value of the determinant of the compression P_M T|_M equals the product of the n singular values of that compression, and the singular values of a compression are dominated by those of T (s_k(P_M T|_M) <= s_k(T) by the min-max / approximation-number characterisation). Since M is T-invariant, P_M T|_M = T|_M, giving the multiplicative inequality. The additive form follows from multiplicative majorization: if a nonincreasing nonnegative sequence (a_k) satisfies the partial-product inequalities against (b_k), then sum f(a_k) <= sum f(b_k) for every function f with f(e^t) convex and nondecreasing in t, and f(t) = t^p is such a function for p > 0 (Weyl's lemma).","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:2225456d23e042d16fa41a4883a1acf0ad8f28160beb6e99ce53d176a31bf47b","revision_digest":"sha256:c446db4b2e55b169d304622d0d2097308ab3105e60f4e040b228bd1ee13f692e","source_id":"wikipedia:Singular value","source_revision":"as-known-2026-09-12","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body:
[Lemma lem:exp-affine of arXiv:2605.03703, 'Scaling Limits of Bivariate Nearly-Unstable Hawkes Processes and Applications to Rough Vol'] Let $X$ be an integrable solution with input $f$, let
$u:[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ be bounded measurable (of arbitrary sign), and
suppose $\varpi\in C([0,1])$ solves~(equation eq:riccati of the paper); set
$\chi:=-u(1-\cdot)+\tfrac{\nu^2}{2}\varpi^2$.  Define, for
$0\le t\le s\le 1$, the forward curve
\[
\xi_t(s):=f(s)+\nu\int_0^tK(s-r)\,dM_r,
\qquad M_r=\int_0^r\sqrt{X_v}\,dW_v,
\]
and the exponent process
\[
H_t:=-\int_0^tu(s)X_s\,ds+\int_t^1\chi(1-s)\,\xi_t(s)\,ds .
\]
Then, almost surely, for all $t\in[0,1]$,
\begin{equation}
H_t=H_0+N_t-\tfrac12\langle N\rangle_t,
\qquad
N_t:=\nu\int_0^t\varpi(1-s)\sqrt{X_s}\,dW_s .
\end{equation}
Consequently $G:=e^{H}=e^{H_0}\,\mathcal E(N)$ is a positive local
martingale and supermartingale with
\[
G_0=\exp\Bigl(\int_0^1\chi(1-t)f(t)\,dt\Bigr),
\qquad
G_1=\exp\Bigl(-\int_0^1u(t)X_t\,dt\Bigr),
\]
so that
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}\Bigl[\exp\Bigl(-\int_0^1u(t)X_t\,dt\Bigr)\Bigr]
\ \le\
\exp\Bigl(\int_0^1\chi(1-t)f(t)\,dt\Bigr),
\end{equation}
with equality if and only if $\mathcal E(N)$ is a true martingale on
$[0,1]$.

body:
[Definition Def_UniformlyFredholmMap of arXiv:2609.02848, 'The universal moduli space of non-degenerate $\Z/2\Z$~harmonic spinors'] Let ${\mathbf{X}},{\mathbf{Y}}$ be tame Fréchet manifolds.
  A tame smooth map $f \mskip0.5mu\colon\thinspace {\mathbf{X}} \to {\mathbf{Y}}$ is \defined{uniformly Fredholm} if for every $x \in {\mathbf{X}}$ there are
  a tame Fréchet space ${\mathbf{F}}$,
  a chart $\phi \mskip0.5mu\colon\thinspace U \to \tilde U \subseteq {\mathbf{F}} \times \mathbb{R}^k$ of ${\mathbf{X}}$ with $x \in U$,
  a chart $\psi \mskip0.5mu\colon\thinspace V \to \tilde V \subseteq {\mathbf{F}} \times \mathbb{R}^\ell$ of ${\mathbf{Y}}$ with $f(x) \in V$, a smooth map
  $F \mskip0.5mu\colon\thinspace \tilde U \to \mathbb{R}^\ell$ such that
  \begin{equation*}
    \psi \circ f \circ \phi^{-1}(y,z) = (y,F(y,z)).
    \qedhere
  \end{equation*}
  In this case, $k - \ell$ is independent of the choice of charts and defines the \defined{index} of $f$ as a locally constant map
  \begin{equation*}
    \ind f \mskip0.5mu\colon\thinspace {\mathbf{X}} \to \mathbb{Z}.
  \end{equation*}
title: Definition Def_UniformlyFredholmMap of arXiv:2609.02848

[Cor 3 of arXiv:2506.12145, 'Functional central limit theorem for dependent models with finite memory'] We have, as $n \to \infty$,
\[\left\{\sqrt{n}\left(\frac{S_{\lfloor nt\rfloor}^M}{\lfloor nt\rfloor} - \frac{q}{1-r+q}\right) \ , \ t\geq 0 \right\} \overset{d}{\longrightarrow} \left\{W_t \ , \ t\geq 0\right\},\]
where $\E[W_sW_t] = \frac{1}{t}\sigma^2_{r,q,k}$ for all $0<s\leq t$.

Moreover, as $n \to \infty$, we have that its center of mass $C^M_n \to \frac{q}{2(1-r+q)}$ almost surely and
\begin{equation}
\sqrt{n}\left(\frac{C^M_n}{n}-\frac{q}{2(1-r+q)}\right) \overset{d}{\longrightarrow} N\left(0,\frac{\sigma^2_{r,q,k}}{3}\right).
\end{equation}
The details of $\sigma_{r,q,k}^2$ are given in Section \ref{sec:MRW}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:generatorXt of arXiv:2411.14876, 'Limit theorems for stochastic exponentials of matrix-valued L\'evy processes \\'] Let $L=(L_t)_{t\geq 0}$ be a Lévy process in $\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ with characteristics $(\Sigma_L,\gamma_L,  \nu_L)$ fulfilling (equation eq-nonsingular of the paper), and let $X=(X_t)_{t\geq 0}$ be its stochastic exponential. Then $X$ is a rich Feller process in $\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ and  its extended generator is given by
		\begin{align*}\mathcal{A}_{X} f(x) &= \sum_{i,j=1}^d \ell(x)^{(i,j)} \frac{\partial}{\partial x^{(i,j)}} f(x) + \frac12 \sum_{i,j, k,l=1}^{d} Q(x)^{(i,j,k,l)} \frac{\partial}{\partial x^{(i,j)}}\frac{\partial}{\partial x^{(k,l)}} f(x) \\
			&\quad  + \int_{y\in \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}\setminus \{0\}} \Big( f(x+y) - f(x) -  \sum_{i,j=1}^d y^{(i,j)} \frac{\partial}{\partial x^{(i,j)}} f(x)\mathds{1}_{\{\|y \|\leq 1\}}  \Big) N(x, dy), \end{align*}
		for all $f\in C_c^2(\mathbb{R}^{d\times d})\subseteq D(\mathcal{A}_{X})$, the latter denoting the domain of $\mathcal{A}_X$. For any $x\in \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$, the triplet $(\ell(x), Q(x), N(x,dy))$ is given by
		\begin{align*}
			\ell(x)&=  x \gamma_L +  \int_{y\in \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}\setminus\{0\}}  x y  \left(  \mathds{1}_{\{ \| x y  \| \leq 1\}}- \mathds{1}_{\{ \|y \| \leq 1\}} \right) \nu_L(dy),  \\
			Q(x)^{(i,j,k,l)} &= \sum_{n,m=1}^{d} 	x^{(i,m)} \sigma_{(m,j),(n,l)} x^{(k,n)} , \, i,j,k,l=1,\ldots, d,\quad \text{and} \\
			N(x,dy)&= \nu_L(T_x^{-1}(dy)),
		\end{align*}
		being the image measure of $\nu_L$ under the transform $T_x$ defined by
		$$T_x(y): \mathbb{R}^{d\times d} \to \mathbb{R}^{d\times d} , y\mapsto x y, \quad x\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:generatorXt of arXiv:2411.14876

       \leqslant c \frac{R_n(\delta,x)}{\sqrt{n}},

body: [Lemma 52 of arXiv:2603.00353, 'Aldous-type Spectral Gaps in Unitary Groups'] Assume that $c_1>c_2>\ldots>c_n>0$. For any $0\ne t<1$, denote by $h(t)$\marginpar{$h(t)$} the largest eigenvalue of $D_t$, namely, the largest root of $P(\under,t)$. Then the set $\{t\in(0,1)\,\mid\,h(t)>c_1\}$ is an open interval of the form $(t_c,1)$  and $h(t)$ is strictly increasing in it.\footnote{As for now, this interval is possibly empty. We will shortly show it is the entire $(0,1)$.} Likewise, the open set $\{t<0\,\mid\,h(t)>c_1\}$ is an open ray of the form $(-\infty,t_c)$, and $h(t)$ is strictly decreasing in it.\footnote{Again, the ray is possibly empty, but we will shortly show it is the entire ray $(-\infty,0)$.}

[Theorem homo multilinear recursion of arXiv:2412.07936, 'Simple Norm Bounds for Polynomial Random Matrices via Decoupling'] [Homogeneous Multilinear Recursion]

Let ${\bf x} = \{x_i\}_{i = 1}^n$ be a sequences of i.i.d random variables with ${\mathbb E} x_i= 0$,  ${\mathbb E} x_i^2= 1$ and $|x_i| \leq L$ for all $1\leq i \leq n$. Let $\{{\bf A}_{{\bf i}}\}_{{\bf i} \in {\mathcal T}^d_n}$ be a multi-indexed sequence of deterministic matrices of the same dimension. Define a permutation symmetric, homogeneous multilinear polynomial random matrix of degree $d$ as
$$
{\bf F}({\bf x}) =  \sum_{{\bf i} \in {\mathcal T}^d_n} \left( {\bf A}_{{\bf i}} \cdot \prod_{j \in \{i_1,\dots, i_d \}} x_j\right).
$$
Let $a,b,c\in {\mathbb Z}_{\geq 0}$ and $d = a+b+c$. Then for $2 \leq t \leq \infty,$
$$
{\mathbb E} \norm{{\bf F}({\bf x}) - {\mathbb E} {\bf F}({\bf x})}_{4t}^{4t} ~\leq~ \sum_{\substack{a,b,c: \\ a+b+c=d}} (48dt)^{4dt} \cdot L^{4ct} \norm{{\bf F}_{a,b,c}}_{4t}^{4t}.
$$

body: In mathematics, the connective constant is a numerical quantity associated with self-avoiding walks on a lattice. It is studied in connection with the notion of universality in two-dimensional statistical physics models. While the connective constant depends on the choice of lattice so itself is not universal, it is nonetheless an important quantity that appears in conjectures for universal laws. Furthermore, the mathematical techniques used to understand the connective constant, for example in the recent rigorous proof by Duminil-Copin and Smirnov that the connective constant of the hexagonal lattice has the precise value , may provide clues to a possible approach for attacking other important open problems in the study of self-avoiding walks, notably the conjecture that self-avoiding walks converge in the scaling limit to the Schramm–Loewner evolution.
title: Connective constant

[Thm critical_weights_unique of arXiv:2506.12171, 'The multinomial dimer model'] {KenyonPohoata}}]
    Fix a finite graph $G = (V,E)$, a weight function $w: E \to \mathbb{R}_+$, $\alpha_v \in [0,1]$ feasible and a sequence of multiplicites ${\mathbf N}$ with $N_v/K\to \alpha_v$ as ${\mathbf N}\to \infty$ for all $v\in V$. Then there exist a \textit{critical weight function} $\mathbf x:V\to \mathbb{R}_+$ such that for each $v\in V$,
\begin{equation}
\sum_{u:(u,v)=e\in E} w_e x_u x_v  = \alpha_v P(\mathbf x).
\end{equation}
Further, the critical weights $\mathbf x$ are unique up to the operation of multiplying by a constant on all black vertices,
and the inverse of this constant on white vertices. In particular, the \textit{critical edge weights} $w_e x_u x_v$ for $(u,v)\in E$ are unique. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
