[Lem 11 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\ge0$, 
and for $(\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda$, 
the mapping
$(\lambda,\mu)\mapsto S_\star(\lambda,\mu;\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$,
is continuous with respect to the Hausdorff metric $d_H$.

\begin{proof} Fix $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\ge0$.
Recall the notation \eqref{e:lam.mu.delta.ball}, and suppose
$(\lambda',\mu')\in\Lambda$ and 
 $(\lambda,\mu)\in B_\delta(\lambda',\mu')$. Given $\YY'\in S_\star(\lambda',\mu';\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$, we will construct $\YY\in S_\star(\lambda,\mu;\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$ which is $o_\delta(1)$-close to $\YY'$. We set $\vwww$ as in Lemma~\ref{l:D.mu.continuity.w}, so that we have the bound $\|\vwww-\vwww'\|_1 \le \delta/\iota^2$. Recalling Lemma~\ref{l:p.polytope.bd.local.aux}, we see that
 $\vwww,\vwww'$ are confined to a compact domain $[0,9/\iota_0]^s$.
The $\Budget$ function is uniformly continuous on the compact domain
$[0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s}\times\Lambda$, so
	\[\sup\bigg\{
	\begin{array}{l}
	|\Budget(\YY;\mu)
	-\Budget(\YY';\mu')|
	:\YY,\YY'\in[0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s},
	(\lambda,\mu),(\lambda',\mu')\in\Lambda,\\
	\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad
	\|\mu-\mu'\|_\infty \le \delta,
	\|\YY-\YY'\|_1 \le \delta/\iota^2
	\end{array}
	\bigg\} \le o_\delta(1)\,,
	\]
where $o_\delta(1)$ denotes an error tending to zero as $\delta\to0$. 
For the purposes of this proof, let us abbreviate
	\begin{align*}
	c(\YY;\lambda)
	&\equiv \Cost(\YY;\lambda)
	+ \epsilon_1\alpha^2\iota^2(\|\vBBb\|_2)^2\,,\\
	g(\YY;\lambda,\mu)
	&\equiv c(\YY;\lambda) - \Budget(\YY;\mu) - \epsilon_2\,.
	\end{align*}
Then we can similarly bound
	\[\sup\bigg\{\begin{array}{l}
	|c(\YY';\lambda)
	-c(\YY';\lambda')|
	: \YY'\in[0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s}, 
	(\lambda,\mu),(\lambda',\mu')\in\Lambda,\\
	\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad
	\|\lambda-\lambda'\|_\infty \le \delta,
	\end{array}
	\bigg\}
	 \le o_\delta(1)\,.
	\]
Combining the above bounds gives
	\beq
	c(\YY';\lambda)
	-\Budget(\YY;\mu) - \epsilon_2
	\le g (\YY';\lambda',\mu') + o_\delta(1)
	\le o_\delta(1)\,,
	\eeq
uniformly over 
$(\lambda,\mu),(\lambda',\mu')$ in $\Lambda$ within distance $\delta$,
and
$\YY,\YY'\in [0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s}$ within distance $\delta/\iota^2$.
If the above left-hand side is in fact $\le0$ then we are done, since we can then set
$\YY=(\vBBb',\vvvv',\vUUu',\vwww)$
 to achieve
$g(\YY;\lambda,\mu)\le 0$. If the above left-hand side is
 strictly positive, then it remains to choose 
 $\YY=(\vBBb,\vvvv,\vUUu,\vwww)$
 close to 
 $\YY(0)\equiv(\vBBb',\vvvv',\vUUu',\vwww)$ to make $g(\YY;\lambda,\mu)\le 0$.
In this case, consider the path in $\cD_\mu$ given by the line segment joining $\YY(0)\equiv(\vBBb',\vvvv',\vUUu',\vwww)$
to $\YY(1)\equiv(\vec{0},\vvvv'-\vUUu',\vec{0},\vwww)$. If we parametrize this segment as a linear function $\YY(t)$ of $t\in[0,1]$, then along the segment we have
	\[\Cost(\YY(t);\lambda)
	-\Cost(\YY(0);\lambda)
	=-(\lambda,\vBBb'+\vUUu')t
	\equiv -A(\YY')t\,.
	\]
Recall from \eqref{e:surplus.small.error.bound} that at the start of the line segment we have $g(\YY(0);\lambda,\mu) \le o_\delta(1)$.  Let $\eta = g(\YY(0);\lambda,\mu)$. We then divide into several cases:
\begin{itemize}
\item If  $A(\YY')\ge\eta^{1/2}$, then we can choose $t_0= \eta / A(\YY') \le \eta^{1/2}$ such that
	\[
	g(\YY(t_0);\lambda,\mu) 
	\le  \eta^{1/2} - A(\YY') t_0 
	\le 0\,,
	\]
and (since $\YY,\YY' \in [0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s}$) $\|\YY(t_0)-\YY(0)\|_2 \lesssim \eta^{1/2}$. In this case, we can conclude by setting $\YY = \YY(t_0)$.
\item Otherwise, if 
$A(\YY')\le \eta^{1/2}$, then
assumption~\eqref{e:def-Lambda} implies that 
\[
    \max\Big(\|\vBBb'\|_1,\|\vUUu'\|_1\Big) \le \frac{\eta^{1/2}}{\iota}\,,
\]
so that we have 
\[
    \|\YY(1)-\YY(0)\|_2
    \le \|\vBBb'\|_2 + 2\|\vUUu\|_2

\]
If

then we can conclude by setting $\YY = \YY(1)$.

[Theorem thm:one-dimensional-phase-diagram of arXiv:2608.05105, 'Cluster-Cluster model in $\mathbb{Z}^d$'] For the fully occupied one-dimensional Cluster-Cluster model ($p=1,d=1$), the following bounds hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If \(\alpha>0\), then \(T_\alpha=\infty\) and
\[
   \mu(t) := \mathbb{E}[|\mathfs{C}_0(t)|]\asymp (1+t)^{1/\alpha}.
 \]
\item If \(\alpha=0\), then \(T_0=\infty\) and 
\(\mu(t)=e^t\). 
\item If \(-1<\alpha<0\), and let $q=-\alpha$, then \(0<T_\alpha<\infty\). More explicitly,
 \(\exists \kappa_q>0\) such that
\begin{equation*}

    \frac1q
    \le
    T_q
    \le
    \min\left\{
        \frac1{\kappa_q},
        \frac1{1-2^{-q}}
    \right\}.
\end{equation*}

\item If \(\alpha=-1\), then \(T_{-1}=1\) and
\(\mu(t)=(1-t)^{-1}\).
\item If \(\alpha<-1\), then \(T_\alpha=0\).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:one-dimensional-phase-diagram of arXiv:2608.05105

[Theorem thm:one-dimensional-coding of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] Let $T:Z\to Z$ be a Borel automorphism of a standard Borel space.
There is a Borel family of sets
\[
    z\longmapsto P_z\subset\mathbb R
\]
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item
the sets $P_z$ are uniformly Delone;

\item
\[
    P_{Tz}=P_z-1
    \qquad
    (z\in Z);
\]

\item
if $z,w\in Z$ and $u\in\mathbb R$ satisfy
\[
    P_w=P_z-u,
\]
then
\[
    u\in\mathbb Z
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    w=T^u z;
\]

\item
for every $z\in Z$,
\[
    \widehat{\delta}_{P_z}
    =
    4\delta_0
    \qquad\text{on }(-1,1)
\]
in the sense of tempered distributions.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: One-dimensional coding theorem

[Corollary cor:poisson-noisy of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a real number $\lambda>0$.
Fix a send sequence $\overline{p}$. Fix a real number $W\geq 1$.  Let $S$ be a set of positive integers such that, for every $k\in S$, $W_k \geq W$. Let $\{ P_k : k\in S\}$ be a set of   independent Poisson variables 
such that, for each $k\in S$,
$\mathbb{E}(P_k) \ge  \lambda W_k/10$.   Then \[

[Definition 76 (Connes--Kreimer extraction-contraction coproduct) of arXiv:2605.14630, '2605.14630'] The \emph{Connes--Kreimer extraction-contraction 
co\-product} $\DeltaCK: \spanF \to \spancFminus \otimes \spanF$ is defined by 
\begin{equation}
  
 \DeltaCK(\Gamma) = \Gamma\otimes\unit + \unit\otimes\Gamma 
+ \sum_{\substack{\unit\neq\overline\Gamma\subsetneq\Gamma, \overline\Gamma \in \Fminus}} 
\overline\Gamma\otimes(\Gamma/\overline\Gamma)\;, 
\end{equation} 
where the sum ranges over all \emph{divergent} subgraphs $\overline\Gamma$, and 
$\Gamma/\overline\Gamma$ denotes the graph obtained by replacing $\overline\Gamma$
by a single vertex. The subgraphs have to be \emph{full}, in the sense that if an edge
$e$ belongs to $\overline\Gamma$, all edges connecting the same vertices also belong 
to $\overline\Gamma$.
title: Connes--Kreimer extraction-contraction coproduct

[Proposition prop:periodic-finite-volume-compatibility of arXiv:2607.04264, 'Macroscopic Feynman Cycles and Poisson--Kingman Universality in Bose Condensation'] The process \(\Xi_{L,N}^{\mathrm{per}}\) is obtained from the finite-volume
periodic ideal Bose Feynman--Kac measure
(equation eq:periodic-spatial-permutation-measure of the paper) by decomposing the
permutation into cycles, disintegrating each cycle into a rooted Brownian
loop, describing the marks defined in
(sssec:periodic-rooted-loops-marks of the paper), and adding independent uniform
labels.  Consequently:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item the unmarked cycle-count marginal is
  (equation eq:periodic-canonical-cycle-law of the paper);
  \item conditionally on the cycle counts, the marks attached to distinct
  cycles are independent;
  \item for a cycle of length \(j\), the single-loop mark has law
  \[
    (R,Y_{L,j},\zeta_{L,j})
    \sim
    \mathsf J_{L,j}^{\mathrm{per}}
    =
    \mathsf H_{\mathbb T^d}\otimes
    \mathsf G_{L,j}\otimes
    \mathsf B_{j/V_L};
  \]
  in particular, the rescaled root, the scaled winding endpoint, and the
  winding-corrected bridge fluctuation are independent;
  \item cutting each rooted loop of duration \(\beta j\) into its \(j\)
  consecutive time-\(\beta\) legs and forgetting the marks recovers the
  spatial-permutation measure
  (equation eq:periodic-spatial-permutation-measure of the paper).
\end{enumerate}

[Lem lem-monotone-lim of arXiv:2411.06301, 'Inverting the operation of conditioning a branching process on extinction'] Let $\lambda \in [0,\infty)^d$.
If there exists $ m \in \mathbbm N$ such that $g^{(m)}(\lambda) < \lambda$, then $\lim_{n\to\infty} g^{(n)}(\lambda) = 0$. 
Moreover, if there exists $m \in\mathbbm N$ such that $g^{(m)}(\lambda) > \lambda$, then $\lim_{n\to\infty} |g^{(n)}(\lambda)| = \infty$.
title: Lem lem-monotone-lim of arXiv:2411.06301

body:
Aldous and Janson, The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II (arXiv:2303.02529), Open Problem 14 (pp. 54-55) asks to prove that L_n, the expected drawn length of DTCS(n) under their recursion (73) l(chi_m) = l(chi_i) + l(chi_{m-i}) + 2 + |h(chi_{m-i}) - h(chi_i)|, grows roughly like n log^4 n. Our result (id P0340, 2026-09-08): the drawn length is Theta(n), so the conjecture is FALSE. For every full binary tree the drawn length is at most the sum of all leaf depths, because the increment 2 + |h_R - h_L| is at most n_L + n_R (a full binary tree with k leaves has height at most k-1); with the authors' own Theorem 3 (the expected depth of a random leaf is asymptotic to (1/(2 zeta(2))) log^2 n = 3 pi^-2 log^2 n) this gives E[drawn length] <= n E[leaf depth] ~ (3/pi^2) n log^2 n = o(n log^4 n). The heuristic's error is a missing factor m: their heuristic (75) uses n a(n,m) as the mean count of size-m subclades where the correct count is (n/m) a(n,m); with the wrong count the conjecture is reproduced exactly, with the right one the scale sum converges (sum log^3 m / m^2) instead of diverging (sum log^3 m / m). Verification as the source words it: machine-checked in P0340.lean, together with the exact decomposition drawn(T) = sum of internal subtree heights + height(T); simulation gives L_n/n = 4.71, 4.78, 4.84, 4.83, 4.86 at n = 10^3 to 4 x 10^5 - flat across a 400x range while log^4 n grows 12x - with the sampler validated first against the paper's own clade counts and leaf-depth law. Prior art not cleared.

[Corollary 34 (Conditional convergence) of arXiv:2607.24561, 'Range convergence and sharp one-arm asymptotics\\for the critical percolation cluster in h'] Let either $W(\mu):=\mu(\varphi_0)$, with $\varphi_0\in\Cc$, $\varphi_0\not\equiv0$, fixed
and $\eps$ admissible in the sense of Theorem~\ref{thm:restricted} and small
enough that $\bN(\mu(\varphi_0)>\eps)>0$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:PZ}); or
$W(\mu):=\mu(\R^d)$, with $\eps>0$ arbitrary --- every $\eps$ being admissible
here, since $\mu(\R^d)$ has no atoms under $\bN$ and
$\bN(\mu(\R^d)>\eps)\in(0,\infty)$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:totalmass}). Then
\[
\bP\bigl(\mu_n\in\cdot\;\big|\;W(\mu_n)>\eps\bigr)
\;\xRightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\;
\bN\bigl(\,\cdot\,\big|\;W(\mu)>\eps\bigr)
:=\frac{\bN(\,\cdot\,;\,W(\mu)>\eps)}{\bN(W(\mu)>\eps)}
\]
weakly as probability measures on $\cM$, and
$n^{2}\,\bP\bigl(W(\mu_n)>\eps\bigr)\to\bN\bigl(W(\mu)>\eps\bigr)\in(0,\infty)$.

[Definition of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] We say that $Z \in_R \mathbb{R}^d$ is \emph{symmetric about zero} if for any measurable $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, $\mathbb{P}(Z \in E) = \mathbb{P}(Z \in -E)$. 
If $Z - w$ is symmetric about zero (for some fixed $w \in \mathbb{R}^d$) then we say $Z$ is \emph{symmetric about $w$}. 
We say that $Z$ is \emph{symmetric} to mean that it is symmetric about \emph{some} $w$; 
we say that $Z$ is \emph{asymmetric} if it is not symmetric about \emph{any} $w$.

body: [Lemma 8 of arXiv:2609.03171, 'Factorization patterns and fields of definition of $\ell$-torsion points on the Jacobians '] Suppose that $\tilde{P}(X)\in\mathbb{F}_{\ell}[X] $ has linear irreducible factors of the form $(X-\alpha)^3(X-\beta)^2$, for some nonzero $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{F}_{\ell}$. Then its factorization pattern is necessarily  $[1]^4[1]^2$ or $[1]^3[1]^3$.

[Lemma lem:ineqs of arXiv:2607.22291, 'Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declum'] Let $H_n$ be integer-valued and let $N_n(h),L_n(h)$ be nonnegative random
variables such that
$$
\{H_n\ge h\}=\{N_n(h)\ge1\},
\qquad
\{L_n(h)\ge1\}\subseteq\{H_n\ge h\}.
$$
If $\mathbb{E}[N_n(h_n)]\to0$, then $\P(H_n\ge h_n)\to0$. If
$L_n(h_n)\to\infty$ in probability, then $\P(H_n\ge h_n)\to1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 25 of arXiv:2607.18862, 'Tamed Euler Schemes for Singular SDEs with Multiplicative L\'{e}vy Noise'] A measurable function $u:[0,1]\times \mR^d\mapsto\mR$ is considered a solution to Eq. (\ref{EquationA.1}) if $u\in \mH_{1,p}^q([0,1])$, $\partial_su\in \mH_{-1,p}^q([0,1])$, $u(1,\cdot)=0$ and Eq. (\ref{EquationA.1}) holds in $\mH_{-1,p^*}^{q^*}([0,1])$. Specifically, for every $\phi\in\mH_{1,p^*}^{q^*}([0,1])$, the following equality must be satisfied
	\be
	\int_{0}^{1}\langle(\partial_t+a^{i,j}\partial_{i,j}+\sL_{\upsilon,R}^g)u_t,\phi_t\rangle_{\mH_{-1,p}(\mR^d),\mH_{1,p^*}(\mR^d)} dt=\int_{0}^{1} \langle f_t,\phi_t\rangle_{\mH_{-1,p}(\mR^d),\mH_{1,p^*}(\mR^d)} dt.
	\ee 
	
	Likewise, a measurable function $v:[0,1]\times \mR^d\mapsto\mR$ is considered a solution to Eq. (\ref{EquationA.2+1}) if $v\in \mH_{1,p^*}^{q^*}([0,1])$, $\partial_sv\in \mH_{-1,p^*}^{q^*}([0,1])$, $u(1,\cdot)=0$ and Eq. (\ref{EquationA.2+1}) holds in $\mH_{-1,p}^{q}([0,1])$. Specifically, for every $\phi\in\mH_{1,p}^{q}([0,1])$, the following equality must be satisfied
	\be
	\int_{0}^{1}\langle(\partial_t v_t-\partial_{i,j} (a^{i,j} v_t)+\sL_{\upsilon,R}^g v_t,\phi_t\rangle_{\mH_{-1,p^*}(\mR^d),\mH_{1,p}(\mR^d)} dt+\int_{0}^{1} \langle h_t,\phi_t\rangle_{\mH_{-1,p^*}(\mR^d),\mH_{1,p}(\mR^d)} dt=0.
	\ee
title: Definition 25 of arXiv:2607.18862

body:
[Theorem thm:CM_OU of arXiv:2510.18106, 'Law equivalence for Ornstein--Uhlenbeck dynamics\\ driven by L\'evy noise'] Let $B$ generate a $C_0$-semigroup and let $h\in\mathcal{H}_{B,T}$. Then
\[
        \mathcal{L}\big(Y_B(W)+h\big)\sim \mathcal{L}\big(Y_B(W)\big)
        \quad\hbox{on }D_{H,T}.
\]
Equivalently, if $h=\mathcal{R}_{B,T}u$ for some $u\in L^2(0,T;H)$, the shift is implemented by the usual Cameron--Martin density. If $u$ is random but independent of $W$, the same conclusion holds after conditioning on $u$; no unconditional Novikov estimate is needed in this conditional situation. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cameron--Martin theorem for OU convolutions

[Openproblem 13 of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186'] Do suitable analogues of Theorem \ref{Theorem: Main} and Corollaries \ref{Corollary: Spectral Geometry},
\ref{Corollary: Fractal Dimension}, and \ref{Corollary: Variance} still hold if one or several of the following changes are made?
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item $D$ is replaced by a compact Riemannian manifold of any dimension.
\item $\xi$ is replaced by a more general singular noise
(e.g., $\xi$ could be Gaussian with covariance $\mbf E[\xi(x)\xi(y)]=\mf K(x,y)$
for the Riesz kernel $\mf K(x,y)=|x-y|^{-\om}$, $\om>0$, or the fractional
kernel $\mf K(x,y)=\prod_{i}|x_i-y_i|^{-\om_i}$, $\om_i>0$).
\item Assuming there is a boundary, the Dirichlet boundary condition is replaced by
another boundary condition (e.g., Neumann, Robin, or mixed).
\end{enumerate} (Stated as a problem by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Problem 13 of arXiv:2507.06186

Let mu and nu be laws of countably many zero-one indicators X_i, pairwise negatively correlated under each law. Suppose delta_i=E_mu X_i-E_nu X_i>=0 and sum_i delta_i^2=infinity. Then mu and nu are mutually singular. The criterion needs no common invariant group action. Its application to distinct free and wired spanning-forest laws requires checking the ordered-marginal, negative-correlation and divergent-squared-gap hypotheses; that divergence is not proved for arbitrary networks here.

[Lem 16 of arXiv:2609.03653, 'The derived set of multiple star polylogarithms'] Let $G$ be a domain and let $f,g$ be holomorphic on $G$.  Suppose that $g$ is univalent, $g(G)$ is convex, and
\[
\mathrm{Re}\,\frac{f'(z)}{g'(z)}>0,
\qquad z\in G.
\]
Then $f$ is univalent on $G$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 1 (Jiang-Qi) of arXiv:2604.13134, '\bf From Gaussian to Gumbel: extreme eigenvalues of complex Ginibre products with exact ra'] Let $k_n$ and $\alpha_n$ be defined as above. The following holds.

(a). If \(\alpha=+\infty\), then 
\[\sqrt{\alpha_n \log \alpha_n}\big( n^{-k_n/2} \max_{1 \leq j \leq n} |Z_j| - 1 \big) - (\log \alpha_n - \log(\sqrt{2\pi} \log \alpha_n))\]
converges weakly to the Gumbel distribution.

(b). If \(\alpha \in (0, \infty)\), for any $x>0,$ we have 
\[\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}(\max_{1 \leq j \leq n} |Z_j|\le x n^{k_n/2})=\prod_{j=0}^{+\infty}\Phi(\frac{j}{\sqrt{\alpha}}+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{\alpha}}+2\sqrt{\alpha}\log x).\] 

(c). If \(\alpha=0\), then
\[\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}(\max_{1 \leq j \leq n} \log |Z_j|\le  \frac12 k_n \psi(n)+\frac{x}{\sqrt{2\alpha_n}})=\Phi(x).\]
Here, $\Phi$ is the distribution function of standard normal and $\psi(n)$ is the digamma function. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Jiang-Qi

[Corollary holub-1-Y-reflexive of arXiv:2609.00794, 'On operators whose adjoints or second adjoints attain their norms'] Let $X$ and $Y$ be Banach spaces. 
\begin{enumerate}
        \itemsep0.25em
        \item If $\operatorname{NA}(Y,X^*) = \mathcal{L}(Y,X^*)$, then $\operatorname{NA}_1 (X,Y^*) = \mathcal{L}(X,Y^*)$.
\item If $\operatorname{NA}_1(Y,X^*) = \mathcal{L}(Y,X^*)$, then $\operatorname{NA}_2 (X,Y^*) = \mathcal{L}(X,Y^*)$.
        \end{enumerate}
If $Y$ is reflexive, then the converses of both implications also hold. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2505.21774, 'The friendship paradox for trees'] {\bf [Correlations of vertex types for infinite trees]}

\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] 
Let $\mathcal{T}_\infty$ be the infinite Galton-Watson tree with offspring distribution $p$ satisfying \eqref{eq:pcond}. Then, for each $\tchi,\chi \in S$, there exists $f^{\tchi\chi}$ such that 
\[
\lim_{m\to\infty} \frac{N_m^{\tchi\chi}}{N_m} = f^{\tchi\chi} \quad \PP\text{-}\mathrm{a.s.}
\] 
\item[(b)] 
For $k \in \N$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
f^{\tchi\chi} &= \sum_{\tk \in \N_0} \sum_{k \in \N_0} \tilde{p}_{\tilde{k}}\, p_k\,
\PP\Big({\rm sign}\big[\tX+{S}_{\tilde{k}-1}+k-\tilde{k}(\tilde{k}+1)\big]=\tchi\Big)\\
&\qquad \times \PP\Big({\rm sign}\big[\tilde{k}+S_k-k(k+1)\big]=\chi\Big),
\end{aligned}
\]
where $S_k$ and $\tilde{X}$ are as defined in Theorem \ref{thm:densities-on-infinite-trees}.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma lem:t0-asymptotics of arXiv:2609.00556, 'Higgs--Demailly System and Positivity of Higgs Bundles'] Fix $\lambda_*>0$.  Uniformly for all $\lambda\geq\lambda_*$ and all
admissible solutions $(f,g)$ at $t=0$, with $u=\log g$, one has
\begin{equation}
 \lambda\|f\|_{C^0}=O(\alpha^{-1}),
 \qquad \|u\|_{C^0}\leq C,
 \qquad
 \frac{\|\Delta_\omega^{\mathbb C} f\|_{C^0}}{\alpha}=o(1)
 \quad (\alpha\to\infty).
\end{equation}
More precisely,
\[
 \sup_{\lambda\geq\lambda_*}
 \sup_{(f,g)\in\mathcal S_{\alpha,\lambda}}
 \frac{\|\Delta_\omega^{\mathbb C}f\|_{C^0}}{\alpha}
 \longrightarrow0
 \qquad\text{as }\alpha\to\infty,
\]
where \(\mathcal S_{\alpha,\lambda}\) denotes the set of admissible
solutions at \(t=0\).

body:
[Dfn of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{The product functor}]
  Fix $N \in \mathbb{N}$.
  Let $(\tau^{(k)})_{k=1}^{N}$ be 
  a sequence of functors.
  The \textit{product functor} $\tau = \prod_{k=1}^{N} \tau^{(k)}$ is defined as follows:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item
      For every $(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}$, 
      we set $\tau(S) \coloneqq \prod_{k=1}^{N} \tau^{(k)}(S)$.
      We equip $\tau(S)$ with the max product metric (cf.\ (equation 2. eq: max product metric of the paper)).
    \item 
      For every $(S_{i}, d^{S_{i}}, \rho_{S_{i}}),\, i=1,2$ 
      and root-and-distance-preserving map $f: S_{1} \to S_{2}$, 
      we set $\tau_{f} \coloneqq \prod_{k=1}^{N} \tau_{f}^{(k)}$, that is, 
      $\tau_{f}: \tau(S_{1}) \to \tau(S_{2})$ is a distance-preserving map given by 
      \begin{equation}
        \tau_{f}\bigl( (a_{k})_{k=1}^{N} \bigr) \coloneqq \bigl( \tau^{(k)}_{f}(a_{k}) \bigr)_{k=1}^{N}.
      \end{equation}
  \end{enumerate}

body:
[Prop prop-single-type of arXiv:2411.06301, 'Inverting the operation of conditioning a branching process on extinction'] Let $X= \{X(n)\}_{n \geq 0}$ be a single-type branching process started from a single individual and let $f$ be its generating function. Assume that 
\begin{enumerate}[I.]
\item $X$ is subcritical, i.e., $\mathbbm E[X(1)] < 1$.  
\item We have $\mathbbm P[X(1) \geq 2] > 0$.   
\item $f$ is continuous from $(0,\infty]$ to $(0,\infty]$ (with $(0,\infty]$ equipped with the topology of a half-open interval). 
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a unique conjugate branching process for $X$. Equivalently, there exists a unique value of $ q > 1$ for which $f(  q) =  q$.

[Definition 29 of arXiv:2511.02725, 'Mixing of general biased adjacent transposition chains'] Let $\cB=\{B_1,\dots,B_\ell\}$ denote any collection of subsets of $[N]$ where $\bigcup_i B_i=[N]$.  
The heat-bath block dynamics 
is the {discrete-time} Markov chain which, from a configuration $X_t$, chooses a block $B_i$ with probability $|B_i|/(\sum_i |B_i|)$ from $\cB$, and resamples the entire configuration $X_t(B_i)$ 
according to the stationary distribution conditioned on $X_{t}(B_i^c)$.

 \Psi(r+h)-\Psi(r)=r^3h+o(1).

\(\Phi(s_n)-\Phi(r_n)\to y\), then
\(\Psi(s_n)-\Psi(r_n)\to y\).

[Theoremc 3 (Coordinate and diagonal extremizers for all smoothing times) of arXiv:2605.11451, '2605.11451'] Let $1\le p<2$, $n\ge2$, and $t\ge0$. Then for every $\theta\in\sphere$,
\[
 \widetilde A_{p,n,t}(\diag)
 \le
 \widetilde A_{p,n,t}(\theta)
 \le
 \widetilde A_{p,n,t}(e_1).
\]
The right equality occurs exactly for coordinate directions $\{\pm e_i\}$, and the left equality occurs exactly for diagonal directions
\[
 \left\{\frac1{\sqrt n}(\pm1,\ldots,\pm1)\right\}.
\]
The same statement holds for the unstandardized profile $A_{p,n,t}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem.mathcalYCN of arXiv:2605.11785, 'Regularization of a mean-field SDE by an additive common noise: the conditional expectatio'] There exists a unique probability measure $Q(d\bm{x}^0,d\bm{y}) = Q^{\bm{x}^0}(d\bm{y}) {\mathcal W}^{\overline\mu_0}(d\bm{x}^0)$ on $({\mathcal C}^2, \overline{\mathcal F})$ (with $Q^{\bm{x}^0}$ denoting the conditional law of $\bm{y}$ given $\bm{x}^0$ under $Q$),  such that 
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] under $Q(d\bm{x}^0,d\bm{y}) 
$, the process
$$
\Bigl( {\bm{x}}^0_t\; , \; \bm{y}_t-\bm{y}_0 - \int_0^t  \left(b(\bm{y}_s+{\bm{x}}^0_s,{\bm{x}}^0_s)ds - \overline b(s,\bm{x}^0_s,\bm{x}^0)\right)ds \Bigr)_{t\in[0,T]}, 
$$
 is a $2d-$dimensional Brownian motion starting from $(\overline\mu_0,0)$ for the canonical filtration generated by $(\bm{x}^0,\bm{y})$, and $\bm{y}_0$ is distributed according to $(Id-\overline \mu_0)\sharp \mu_0$, 
\item[(ii)] ${\mathcal W}^{\overline \mu_0}(d\bm{x}^0)\otimes dt$-a.e., 
  $\bm{y}_t\sharp Q^{\bm{x}^0}= \mu^{\bm{x}^0}_t$. 
\end{itemize}

[Corollary cor:jackson-rescale of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] For any $f\in C^k([-R,R])$ such that $f^{(l)}(-R) = f^{(l)}(R)$ for all $l\le k$ and $\norm{f^{(k)}}_\infty \le M$, there exists a trigonometric polynomial of the form 
\begin{align}
    T_D(x) &= \sum_{m\le D} a_m \cos\Big(\frac{m\pi (x+R)}{R}\Big) + b_m \sin\Big(\frac{m\pi (x+R)}{R}\Big), \text{ for } x\in [-R,R],  
\end{align}
such that $\norm{T_D - f}_\infty \le C_k D^{-k} M (R/\pi)^k$. 
Additionally, it holds that 
$$\sum_{1\le m\le D} |a_m| + |b_m| \le  \frac{2^{k+2}\,MR^k}{\pi^{k+1}} \sum_{1\le m \le D} m^{-k}.$$

Garg, Gunn and Wang, arXiv:2506.01854v2, Corollary 4: relative to any crypto oracle, there are no statistically secure pseudorandom codes robust to any constant rate of independent random binary errors. This already holds for secret-key zero-bit PRCs with negligible soundness and completeness errors and polynomial query complexity. Their noise parameter rho is correlation: N_rho refreshes each bit independently with probability 1-rho, equivalently flips each bit with probability (1-rho)/2; constant positive noise means rho is bounded away from 1. Section 1.1 interprets this as a fully black-box separation from primitives implemented by crypto oracles; footnote 3 specifies the additional PSPACE oracle used in that interpretation. The statistical oracle impossibility must not be read as an unconditional impossibility from existence of one-way functions.
Binary channel with a constant positive independent bit-flip rate below one half
Statistical security in the oracle model of the source
Polynomially many oracle queries and polynomial block length
Negligible completeness and soundness errors

Let (X, mu) and (Y, nu) be sigma-finite measure spaces, 1 <= p < infinity, and F: X x Y -> [0, infinity] measurable for the product sigma-algebra. Then ( int_Y ( int_X F(x,y) dmu(x) )^p dnu(y) )^{1/p} <= int_X ( int_Y F(x,y)^p dnu(y) )^{1/p} dmu(x), both sides in [0, infinity]. Consequently, for complex measurable F with the right-hand side (computed with |F|) finite, int_X F(x,y) dmu(x) converges absolutely for nu-a.e. y and its L^p(nu)-norm is at most the right-hand side. In words: the L^p norm of an integral is at most the integral of the L^p norms. (For p = infinity the analogous statement with ess sup holds for F >= 0.)

Stated in arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy' (prob environment labelled eq:tuple-of-Phis).] When $\phi$ is unital, Theorem~(thm:pre-LDP) says that the value $E_n$ gives the rate function in the large deviations principle obeyed by the random element
\[(\Phi^\pi_V)[B_n] \in \S^\rm{u}_k(B_n).\]
The values $E_n'$ should have an analogous interpretation, but this time for the random $S$-tuples
\begin{equation}
\big((\Phi^\pi_V)[B_n\cup sB_n]:\ s \in S\big)
\end{equation}
taking values in the space
\[\Big\{(Q_s:\ s \in S) \in \prod_{s \in S}\S^\rm{u}_k(B_n\cup sB_n):\ (Q_s)[B_n]\ \hbox{is the same for all $s$}\Big\}.\]
If this is true, then both inequalities in Lemma~(lem:1-2-ineqs) become instances of the contraction principle.

I believe one can prove this along the same lines as Theorem~(thm:pre-LDP) without any really new ideas, but working with the the tuples in~(eq:tuple-of-Phis) is sure to be more complicated than working with $(\Phi^\pi_V)[B_n$ alone. [Lemma lem:LG-kernel of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] We have
\[
\mathbb{P}_y\Bigl(\bigcap_{i=1}^m
\{Y_{n_i}(t) > a_i\}\Bigr)
= \det(I - K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}})_{\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})},
\]
where
\[
K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}(x, x')
= \sum_{1 \le j \le i \le m}
  \sum_{r \le a_i} \sum_{r' \le a_j}
   \psi_{t, r, n_i}(x)
  \bigl[\delta_{ij}\delta_{r,r'}
  + [B_{\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}]_{ij}(r, r')\bigr]
  \phi_{t, r', n_j}(x').
\]
This identifies $K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}$ with the
kernel~(equation eq:K-def of the paper) on the product graph
$\mathcal{G}^m$, with $\psi, \phi$ as the seed data and

[Definition of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] A map $f\colon X\to Y$ of closed orthogonal $G$-spaces is called a \emph{$G$-global ${\mathcal{F}}$-weak equivalence} if $f({\mathcal{U}}_H)\colon X({\mathcal{U}}_H)\to Y({\mathcal{U}}_H)$ is a $\mathcal G_{H,G}$-weak equivalence for every $H\in{\mathcal{F}}$ and some (hence any) complete $H$-universe ${\mathcal{U}}_H$. 

    A map $f\colon X\to Y$ between general orthogonal $G$-spaces is called a $G$-global ${\mathcal{F}}$-weak equivalence if in some (hence any) commutative square
    \[
        \begin{tikzcd}
            X'\arrow[d,"\sim"']\arrow[r,"f'"] & Y'\arrow[d,"\sim"]\\
            X\arrow[r,"f"'] & Y
        \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    where the vertical maps are $G$-global equivalences and $X',Y'$ are closed, the map $f'$ is a {$G$-global ${\mathcal{F}}$-weak equivalence} in the sense defined above.

Own work draft, status independently checked proof, E0018-C3 v1 (w667 PASS, w668 PASS). For symmetric-rate switching of real 2x2 matrices Ai, set Bi=Ai-(tr Ai/2)I. The exponent obeys L_A(r)=L_B(r)+(tr A0+tr A1)/4. If one traceless part has nonzero imaginary eigenvalues +-i omega, a fixed real similarity and time scaling transform the traceless pair into J=[[0,-1],[1,0]] and eta H+sJ, H=diag(1,-1), eta>=0, s real; normalized rate rho=r/omega and the original traceless exponent equals omega times the normalized exponent at rho. For unscaled traceless matrices with spectral abscissae ki=sqrt(max(-det Bi,0)), there exist scalar shifts Ai=Bi-ai I making both individually Hurwitz with prescribed damping average abar iff abar>(k0+k1)/2. This places no requirement on the averaged matrix. No rate monotonicity or unimodality is asserted.
Real 2x2 matrices
Symmetric switching rate r>0
A nonzero traceless elliptic part for the canonical-form clause

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:fe9deef0fb4c1dc2fd37af05e0411297191295e99ba0bd9b9fd07f9a34beeaa3","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/fe/fe9deef0fb4c1dc2fd37af05e0411297191295e99ba0bd9b9fd07f9a34beeaa3.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:4e9f642e9691b8ace067e6decf99dc0f5e89614d9e79d9526f32a2fe17bfd0b7","bundle_entry_key":"canonical","bundle_id":"population.w658-hurwitz-disconnected-instability-002","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"randomly switched planar linear systems","draft":"w658/bundle_002_resubmit.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.switched.linear:elliptic-planar-pair-canonical-form-and-trace-shift","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# E0018-C3 v1: scalar traces and canonical elliptic-pair reduction
Status: proof (unaudited), 2026-10-14.

Let symmetric-rate switching alternate two real 2x2 matrices Ai. Put
Bi=Ai-(tr Ai/2)I, so Bi is traceless. Let tau=(tr A0+tr A1)/4.
The top Lyapunov exponent satisfies L_A(r)=L_B(r)+tau whenever one exists.
This is an exact pathwise scalar factorization plus the two-state occupation law.
If B0 has purely imaginary nonzero eigenvalues +-i omega, omega>0, then after a
single fixed real similarity and time scale omega the pair is
B0/omega=J=[[0,-1],[1,0]],
B1/omega=eta H+s J=[[eta,-s],[s,-eta]], eta>=0, s real, H=diag(1,-1).
The transformed switching rate is rho=r/omega. Thus (after removing traces) every
pair with a nonzero elliptic matrix reduces to two real parameters eta,s.

Proof of trace shift. Let c_i=tr Ai/2 and C(t)=integral_0^t c_{I_s}ds.
The fundamental matrix equals exp(C(t)) times the one for Bi: differentiate on
sojourns and use the commuting scalar factor and continuity at jumps.
The two-state symmetric occupation law gives C(t)/t->(c0+c1)/2=tau almost surely.
Fixed similarity preserves exponential norm growth since its condition number is
constant. Rescaling time t'=omega t divides both matrices and rate by omega and
scales the original exponent by omega.

Proof of elliptic canonical form. Cayley-Hamilton for a traceless real B0 gives
B0^2=-omega^2 I. Choose any real nonzero vector v; vectors v, B0v/omega are linearly
independent, since dependence would give a real eigenvalue. In that basis B0=omega J.
Every real traceless B1 in this basis decomposes uniquely into s0 J+R, where
s0=(B1_21-B1_12)/2 and R is symmetric traceless, R=[[a,b],[b,-a]].
Any real symmetric traceless R has eigenvalues +-eta0 with eta0=sqrt(a^2+b^2)>=0.
There is a determinant-one orthogonal matrix O (a plane rotation) with
O^T R O=eta0 H: select an orthonormal eigenbasis, flip its second eigenvector if
necessary to make determinant one. Every plane rotation commutes with J, so the
same O leaves B0 unchanged. Divide by omega to obtain eta=eta0/omega,s=s0/omega.
This transformation is fixed, independent of r, so preserves the full rate curve.

Exact diagnostic identities. Half the trace of (B1/omega)^2 equals eta^2-s^2;
half the trace of ((B0+B1)/(2omega))^2 equals [eta^2-(1+s)^2]/4.
Let k1=sqrt(max(eta^2-s^2,0)), kavg=(1/2)sqrt(max(eta^2-(1+s)^2,0)).
The symmetric occupation average of the individual spectral abscissae is k1/2.
Comparing these algebraic endpoints, kavg>k1/2 is possible only for s<-1/2
and eta>|1+s|; those two conditions are also sufficient. This statement compares
spectral abscissae only; it does not assert a stochastic slow/fast limit theorem.
For any traceless real Bi its eigenvalue spectral abscissa is sqrt(max(-det Bi,0)).
A scalar shift Ai=Bi-ai I is Hurwitz exactly when ai exceeds that abscissa.
Consequently a fixed scalar damping average abar can make BOTH Ai Hurwitz if and
only if abar>(k0+k1)/2: necessity by summing ai>ki; sufficiency choose
ai=ki+abar-(k0+k1)/2. No condition on the averaged matrix is required.

Non-result: the two-parameter curve is not proved unimodal. This reduction helps

[Proposition 14 (Persistent supercritical misalignment) of arXiv:2608.20638, 'Provable Edge-of-Stability for Adam on a One-Dimensional Quadratic'] Suppose that $0<\beta_1<1$ and $w_{\max}>2$.  For every $v_0>0$ satisfying
$w_0=c\eta/(\sqrt{v_0}+\varepsilon)>2$, there exist $x_0\ne0$ and
$m_0\in\R$ such that
\begin{equation}
    x_t(m_t+cx_t)<0
    \qquad\text{for every }t\ge0.

\end{equation}
Along this trajectory,
\begin{equation}
    w_t\ge w_0,
    \qquad
    \abs{x_t}\le(w_0-1)^{-t}\abs{x_0},
    \qquad t\ge0.

\end{equation}
In particular, $(x_t,m_t,v_t)\to(0,0,0)$ and $w_t\to w_{\max}$,
although the trajectory remains uniformly supercritical for all time. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Persistent supercritical misalignment

body: The number of primes up to x satisfies pi(x) ~ x / log x, equivalently pi(x) ~ Li(x), as x grows. Proved independently by Hadamard and de la Vallee Poussin (1896) by showing zeta(s) has no zeros on the line Re(s) = 1; elementary proofs (Erdos, Selberg 1949) avoid complex analysis. The error term in the theorem is governed by the zero-free region - under the Riemann hypothesis the error is O(sqrt(x) log x).

[Lemma lem:prime-deleted-character-sum of arXiv:2609.00777, 'Universal murmuration and Hecke augmentation'] Let $X\geq2$ and $1\leq Y\leq X$.  Let $m,w,D\geq1$, and let $q,t\in\mathbb Z$ satisfy $(t,D)=1$ and $wt\equiv q\pmod D$.
Let $P$ be a prime with $P\nmid D$, and put $\chi_m(\cdot)=(\frac{\cdot}{m})$.
Define
\[
\mathcal P(m;w,D,q)
=
\{\ell\mid m:\ \ell\text{ odd},\ v_\ell(m)\text{ odd},\
\ell\nmid q,\ (D,w,\ell)=1\}
\]
and
\[
\mathfrak m
=
\frac{m}{\displaystyle
\prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(m;w,D,q)}(\sqrt\ell/2)}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{\substack{M\in[X,X+Y]\\M\equiv t\ (\bmod D)\\P\nmid M}}
\mu^2(M)\chi_m(M)
\chi_m\left(\frac{wM-q}{D}\right)
&\ll
\sqrt X+\frac{\mathfrak mY}{mD}
+\frac{\log(2X)\sqrt{\mathfrak mY}}{\sqrt D},
\end{aligned}

\end{equation}
with an absolute implied constant.

In the Gaussian linear-regression setting y=<x,theta*>+z, with independent x~N(0,diag(v_1,...,v_d)) and z~N(0,sigma^2), let n,d be positive integers, v_i>0, sigma^2>0, and theta*_i nonzero. Put a_i=v_i(theta*_i)^2 and b=sigma^2/n. For coordinate learning rates 0<=eta_i<=1/v_i define the deterministic surrogate risk of equation (2), Rbar_eta(t)=sigma^2+sum_i [a_i(1-eta_i v_i)^(2t) +b(1-(1-eta_i v_i)^t)^2], for integer t>=1. For any prescribed integer t_*>=1, choose eta_i=[1-(b/(a_i+b))^(1/t_*)]/v_i. Then each coordinate summand attains its minimum at t=t_*, and Rbar_eta(t_*)=sigma^2+sum_i a_i b/(a_i+b), the global minimum over all admissible coordinate rates and integer stopping times. These are oracle rates using the true signal coefficients and feature variances. This statement optimizes the source surrogate; approximating the random finite-sample prediction risk requires the separate hypotheses and conclusion of Theorem 1.

[Lemma lem:expmom of arXiv:2607.12564, 'Power-law and log-periodic degree tails for a family of probability generating function eq'] There exist $\theta>0$ and $M<\infty$, depending only on $p$, such that
\[
  \sup_{n\ge0}\mathbb{E}\exp\!\Bigl\{\theta\,\frac{D_n}{\lambda^{n}}\Bigr\}\le M,
  \qquad
  \sup_{n\ge0}\mathbb{E}\exp\!\Bigl\{\theta\,\frac{D^*_n}{\lambda^{n}}\Bigr\}\le M^{j}.
\]
Consequently there are constants $C,c>0$ with
\[
  \mathbb{P}(D_n\ge x\lambda^{n})\le C e^{-cx},\qquad
  \mathbb{P}(D^*_n\ge x\lambda^{n})\le C e^{-cx},\qquad n\ge0,\ x\ge0 .
\]
title: Lemma lem:expmom of arXiv:2607.12564

[Corollary 19 of arXiv:2604.25470, 'A mathematical analysis of hierarchical Hopfield models'] Assume that $L_\alpha$ are i.i.d.\ with exponentially decaying tails,
	for instance Poisson or Poisson conditioned on $\{L_\alpha\ge1\}$.
	Since $L_\alpha$ has an exponentially decaying tail, there exist
	constants $c_1,c_2>0$ such that
	\[
	\mathbb P(L_\alpha>n)\le c_1 e^{-c_2 n}
	\]
	for all sufficiently large $n$. Hence, for $u_M=C\log M$,
	we have
	\[
	\mathbb P(L_\alpha>u_M)\le c_1 M^{-c_2 C}\to0.
	\]
	Suppose moreover that, for some fixed integer $t_*\ge0$,
	$
	t_M:=t_{\ell_*,u_M}\ge t_*
	$
	for all sufficiently large $M$, and that
	$
	\max_{\alpha\le P}\mathbb P\bigl(\mathcal G_\alpha(\delta,\rho)^c\bigr)\to0.
	$
	If
	\[
	P\,\frac{(\log M)^{2(t_*+1)}}{M^{t_*+1}}\to0,
	\]
	then
	\[
	\max_{\alpha\le P}\mathbb P(\widehat\alpha(x)\neq\alpha,\ 
	\alpha\in\mathcal A_{\ell,u})\to0.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 12 ({Lower bound for binomials}) of arXiv:2604.25470, 'A mathematical analysis of hierarchical Hopfield models'] Let $\{\xi^\mu\}_\mu$
		be i.i.d.\ {Bernoulli}$(p)$-random variables with $p=\log N_f/N_f$, and set
		$\theta=\kappa\log N_f$ with $\kappa\in(0,1)$. Then with
		$a=\tfrac12(1-\kappa)^2$,

		\[
		\min_{1\le\mu\le M} |\xi^\mu|_1 \ge \theta
		\]
		with probability $1-o(1)$ as $N_f\to\infty$.

body:
[Defi 15 of arXiv:2511.10535, 'Eigenvalues of Brownian Motions on $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$'] A {\bf Ginibre Brownian motion} of size $N$ is an $\M_N(\C)$-valued diffusion process $Z^N(\cdot)$ of the form
    \[ Z^N(t) \equaldist \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(X^N(t) + \i Y^N(t) ) \]
    where $X^N,Y^N$ are independent Hermitian Brownian motions of size $N$.  Entrywise, this can be described simply: for $1\le i,j\le N$, 
    $\{\sqrt{2N}\,\mathrm{Re}Z_{i,j}^N, \sqrt{2N}\,\mathrm{Im}Z_{i,j}^N\}_{t\ge 0}$ are all independent standard Brownian motions on $\mathbb{R}$.

    The random matrix $Z^N(1)$, whose entries are all i.i.d.\ complex normal random variables, is called a {\bf Ginibre Ensemble} first introduced in \cite{Ginibre1965}. Equivalently, the law of $Z$ has a density with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\M_N(\C)$ which is proportional to $Z\mapsto \exp(-N\mathrm{Tr}_N[Z^\ast Z])$.  Note that this density is invariant under $Z\mapsto UZV^\ast$ for any deterministic unitary matrices $U,V\in\mathrm{U}(N)$; thus, the law of the Ginibre ensemble is unitarily bi-invariant.

body:
At a fixed parameter theta, let a single-example gradient g have finite second moment, mean G=grad L(theta) and covariance Sigma=E[(g-G)(g-G)^T]. Let H=grad^2 L(theta), and assume G^T H G>0. McCandlish et al. define B_noise=tr(H Sigma)/(G^T H G). When G!=0, they also define B_simple=tr(Sigma)/||G||_2^2. These are different statistics in general. They coincide when H is a positive scalar multiple of the identity. For the mean of B independent identically distributed gradients, the gradient covariance is Sigma/B. Interpreting B_noise as a local quadratic turning-point scale requires the one-step quadratic model; identifying it with a global empirically optimal critical batch size is an additional modeling step. In particular a common scalar step size does not make curvature isotropic.
finite second moment per-example gradients at a fixed parameter
H is the loss Hessian; positive G^T H G for B_noise
iid draws for the stated Sigma/B covariance identity

[Theorem 42 (Batch-size-dependent data scaling) of arXiv:2609.02728, 'Momentum in large-batch training: Polyak enlarges the critical batch size, Nesterov improv'] For \(B=D^{b+o(1)}\) with \(b\in[0,1)\), 
\[
r_{\sgd}(b)=
\begin{cases}
\frac{s}{s+1}, & 0\leq b<b_1,\\[2mm]
s(1-b), & b_1\leq b<1,
\end{cases}
\qquad
r_{\polyak}(b)=
\begin{cases}
\frac{s}{s+1}, & 0\leq b<b_3,\\[2mm]
2s(1-b), & b_3\leq b<1,
\end{cases}
\]
and
\[
r_{\nesterov}(b)=
\begin{cases}
\frac{s}{s+1}, & 0\leq b<b_1,\\[2mm]
\frac{s(1+(\beta-1)b)}{s\beta+1}, & b_1\leq b<b_2,\\[3mm]
2s(1-b), & b_2\leq b<1.
\end{cases}
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def-frac-Gaus-field of arXiv:2411.09614, 'Moment estimates for the stochastic heat equation on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds'] Consider  $\alpha>0$ and the following Hilbert space of space-time functions:
\begin{align}
\mathcal{H}_\alpha=L^2(\mathbb{R}_+, \mathcal{W}^{-\alpha}(M)),  
\end{align}
    where $\mathcal{W}^{-\alpha}(M)$ is the Sobolev space introduced in Definition (sobo_def of the paper). On a complete probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{G},\mathbf{P})$ we define a centered Gaussian family $\{W(\phi); \phi\in \mathcal{H}_\alpha\}$, whose covariance is given by 
\begin{align}
\mathbf E\left[ W(\varphi) W(\psi)\right]
=&
\int_{\mathbb{R}_+}\ \left\langle \varphi (t,\cdot) , \psi (t,\cdot)\right\rangle_{\mathcal{W}^{-\alpha}(M)}  dt \notag\\
=&
\int_{\mathbb{R}_+} \int_{M^2} \varphi (t,x)  \psi (t,y)G_{2\alpha}(x,y)dxdy dt
\, ,
\end{align}
for $\varphi$, $\psi$ in $\mathcal{H}_\alpha$. This family is called the fractional Gaussian fields on $M$.
title: Definition def-frac-Gaus-field of arXiv:2411.09614

\xrightarrow{d}\mathcal N(0,1).
$$

[Definition 12 (Riemannian $p$-harmonicity residual) of arXiv:2609.00571, '\textbf{Shape Optimization and Bernoulli Free Boundary Problems\\ for the Riemannian $p$-L'] For a diffeomorphism $\Psi:U\to V$, define the residual of the transported
function $U^\Psi=u\circ\Psi^{-1}$ by
\begin{align}
\mathcal R_{\Psi,g}[u](\widehat\varphi)
:={}&
\int_U
|\nabla_h u|_h^{p-2}
\left\langle
\nabla_hu,\nabla_h\widehat\varphi
\right\rangle_h\,dV_h
\nonumber\\
&-
\int_U
|\nabla_g u|_g^{p-2}
\left\langle
\nabla_gu,\nabla_g\widehat\varphi
\right\rangle_g\,dV_g,

\end{align}
where $h=\Psi^\ast g$.
If $u$ is $p$-harmonic with respect to $g$, then
\[
\mathcal R_{\Psi,g}[u]
\]
measures exactly the failure of $U^\Psi$ to be $p$-harmonic with respect
to the fixed metric $g$.
title: Riemannian $p$-harmonicity residual

[Proposition Sharpness of the inverse-square correction of arXiv:2608.12376, 'A Heat Kernel Expectation Approach to Boundary-Corrected Li--Yau Estimates for the Dirichl'] The boundary correction term

\[
-\frac1{|x|^2}
\]

in Theorem~3.1 is of optimal order near the Dirichlet boundary.

More precisely, for the Dirichlet heat kernel itself, the quantity

\[
\Delta \log K_D(x,y,t)
+
\frac n{2t}
\]

has an inverse-square singular behavior as
$x\rightarrow \partial\mathbb R^n_+$.

\item Let $E_0(T_n)$ be the set of all parallelograms $e_0\subseteq T_n$ whose vertices are $\{(v_1, v_2),  (v_1 + 1, v_2),  (v_1 + 1, v_2 + 1),  (v_1 +2, v_2 + 1)\}.$

\item Let $E_1(T_n)$ be the set of all parallelograms $e_1\subseteq T_n$ whose vertices are $\{(v_1, v_2),  (v_1 + 1, v_2),  (v_1, v_2 + 1),  (v_1 +1, v_2 + 1)\}.$ 
\item Let $E_2(T_n)$ be the set of all parallelograms $e_2\subseteq T_n$ whose vertices are $\{(v_1, v_2),  (v_1 + 1, v_2+1),  (v_1, v_2 + 1),  (v_1 +1, v_2 + 2)\}.$ 
\eit

We define the discrete Hessian $\hess(f):E(T_n) \ra \R$ to be a  real-valued function on the set $E(T_n) = E_0(T_n) \cup E_1(T_n) \cup E_2(T_n)$ and the $\De_i$ from $\R^{T_n}$ to $\R^{E_i(T_n)}$ by 
\beq\lab{eq:A}
\hess f(e_0) := \De_0 f(e_0) :=  f(v_1, v_2) - f(v_1 + 1, v_2) - f(v_1 + 1, v_2 + 1) + f(v_1 +2, v_2 + 1).\nonumber\\
\hess f(e_1) := \De_1 f(e_1) :=  - f(v_1, v_2) + f(v_1 + 1, v_2) + f(v_1, v_2 + 1) - f(v_1 + 1,  v_2 + 1).\nonumber\\
\hess f(e_2) := \De_2 f(e_2) :=  f(v_1, v_2) - f(v_1+1, v_2+1) - f(v_1, v_2 + 1) + f(v_1 + 1, v_2 + 2).\nonumber\\
\eeq

[Lemma lem.girsanov-lambda of arXiv:2605.26082, 'Quantitative Einstein relation for reversible diffusions in a random environment'] There exists $C=C(d,\Lambda)<\infty$ such that, for every environment
		$\omega$, every $\lambda,\lambda'\in(0,1]$, every $t>0$, and every
		nonnegative, possibly $\omega$-dependent, path functional $F$ measurable
		with respect to $\sigma(X(s):0\le s\le t)$,
		\begin{equation}
			E_0^{\lambda',\omega}[F]\le \exp\bigl(C(\lambda'-\lambda)^2 t/2\bigr) \bigl(E_0^{\lambda,\omega}[F^2]\bigr)^{1/2}\, .
		\end{equation}
		If in addition $|\lambda-\lambda'|^2 t\le 1$, then for every
		square-integrable, possibly $\omega$-dependent, path functional $G$
		measurable with respect to $\sigma(X(s):0\le s\le t)$,
		\begin{equation}
			\bigl|E_0^{\lambda',\omega}[G]-E_0^{\lambda,\omega}[G]\bigr|\le C|\lambda-\lambda'|\sqrt t \bigl(E_0^{\lambda,\omega}[G^2]\bigr)^{1/2}\, .
		\end{equation}
		The same estimates hold with the expectations $\widehat E_0^{\lambda,\omega}$ whenever $F$ and $G$ depend only on the diffusion path. For every integer $q\ge1$, the second estimate also holds for $\mathbb{R}^q$-valued $G$, with a constant depending additionally on $q$ and with $|G|^2$ in place of $G^2$.

body: [Defi stationary of arXiv:2411.04157, 'Stochastic homogenization of dynamical discrete optimal transport'] We call $(\mathcal X_\omega,\mathcal E_\omega,\sigma_\omega,\theta_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}$ \emph{stationary} if for every $z\in\mathbb{Z}^n$ the law of the weighted graph $(\mathcal X_\omega,\mathcal E_\omega,\sigma_\omega,\theta_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}$ is the same as the law of the translated weighted graph $(\mathcal X_\omega+z,\mathcal E_\omega+z,\sigma_\omega(\cdot - z),\theta_\omega(\cdot - z))_{\omega\in\Omega}$. We call $(\mathcal X_\omega,\mathcal E_\omega,\sigma_\omega,\theta_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}$ \emph{ergodic} if all events $A\in \mathcal{A}$ that are invariant under translations in $\mathbb{Z}^n$ have probability $\mathbb{P}(A)\in\{0,1\}$.

[Lemma lem:hypoexponential_derivative_properties of arXiv:2604.09509, 'An Improved Bipartition Cover Bound for the Multispecies Coalescent Model'] If we have positive, distinct rates $\{\lambda_i\}_{i = 1}^\infty$:

    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item At zero, the one-sided derivatives $F_k^{(m)}(0) = 0$ for $0 \leqslant m \leqslant k-1$. The nonzero derivatives take the form
        
        \[F_{k}^{{(k + r)}}(0) = (-1)^r \left(\prod_{i=1}^k \lambda_i\right) \left(h_r(\lambda_1,..., \lambda_k)\right),\]
        
        \noindent where $h_r$ are the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials
        
        \[ h_r(\lambda_1, ..., \lambda_k) := \sum_{1\leqslant i_1\leqslant i_2 \leqslant ...\leqslant i_r\leqslant k} \prod_{j=1}^r \lambda_{i_j}.\]
        
        \noindent In particular, for $r=0, 1$ we have
            \[F_k^{(k)}(0) = \prod_{i=1}^k \lambda_i, \qquad F_k^{(k+1)}(0) = -\left(\sum_{i=1}^k \lambda_i\right)\left(\prod_{i=1}^k \lambda_i\right).\]
        
        \item The derivatives are uniformly bounded. Namely, for fixed $m$
        
        \[||F_k^{(m)}||_\infty \leqslant M_m = \max_{i=1, ...,m} |F_i^{(m)}(0)|.\]

    \end{enumerate}
title: Lemma lem:hypoexponential_derivative_properties of arXiv:2604.09509

Exact proof SHA256 f367eed1f9fb01baee0dabd6f699b418c16bcc3a5ecdfc7182dae660291f3339. No novelty or Lean certification is claimed. # Target 1: accelerated finite-feature GP prediction

Claim T336-w727-C002 v1. Rung: proof (unaudited), subject to recorded checks. The full theorem is not Lean-checked and no independent audit or novelty certification is claimed.

The hardest step is realizing both Chebyshev recurrences in normalized ReLU attention, including the previous-iterate registers and variance readout. Section 4 specifies every head.

## 1. Statement

Fix integers p>=1 and n>=0, reals s>0, B>=0, R>0, eps>0, and a feature map z:X->R^p with ||z(x)||<=R. The zero-mean GP prior has kernel k(x,x')=z(x)^T z(x'). Observations have independent N(0,s) noise. A prior scale tau^2 is absorbed into z. The prediction concerns a new **noisy observation**, not the latent function value.

Input tokens supply any t<=n context pairs (z_i,y_i), |y_i|<=B, and one query q=z(x_*). Zero padding fixes N=n+1 tokens. The supplied feature encoding is specified in Section 4. Its computation from arbitrary raw inputs is not included in the size bound.

Use the bidirectional residual normalized ReLU-attention architecture of Bai, Chen, Wang, Xiong and Mei, arXiv:2306.04637v2, Definition 1, PDF page 5, Eq. (1):

    h_i^+ = h_i + (1/N) sum_heads sum_j ReLU(<Q h_i,K h_j>) V h_j.

Q,K,V are real D-by-D matrices. There is no softmax, layer normalization, or causal mask. Feed-forward blocks are identities. Define

    n_+=max(1,n), L=s+n_+R^2, kappa=L/s, M=nR^2B/s,
    delta=min(1/2, s/(2R^2), sqrt(s eps)/(1+M), s sqrt(eps)/R^2),
    T=ceil((sqrt(kappa)/2) log(2/delta)).

An attention-only transformer of width D=7p+4, depth T+2, and at most five heads per layer outputs (mhat,vhat) with vhat>=s and

    KL(N(m,v) || N(mhat,vhat)) <= eps

uniformly over all these contexts and queries. Here (m,v) are the exact posterior noisy predictive mean and variance. A dense parameter bound is 15(T+2)D^2+2D, including a linear readout. All weights depend only on the fixed bounds, never the observed inputs or labels. They are explicit in Section 4.

If R=0, (mhat,vhat)=(0,s) is exact and the formulas dividing by R are unnecessary. No training, ERM generalization, arbitrary raw-feature complexity, softmax approximation, or infinite-rank truncation theorem is asserted.

## 2. Posterior and spectral interval

Set A=s I+sum_i z_i z_i^T and b=sum_i z_i y_i. Completing the square in the standard-normal weight prior and Gaussian likelihood gives posterior weight mean A^{-1}b and covariance s A^{-1}, hence

    m=q^T A^{-1}b, v=s+s q^T A^{-1}q.

For every r, s||r||^2<=r^T A r<=(s+nR^2)||r||^2<=L||r||^2. Thus A is symmetric positive definite, spec(A) is contained in [s,L], v>=s, and

    ||A^{-1}b||<=nRB/s, ||A^{-1}q||<=R/s.

These are deterministic bounds and use no independence among context features.

## 3. Accelerated iteration and its error

Put c=(L+s)/2, d=(L-s)/2, a=c/d. Since n_+>=1 and R>0, d>0,a>1. Define Chebyshev polynomials C_0(x)=1,C_1(x)=x,C_{j+1}(x)=2xC_j(x)-C_{j-1}(x).

For a right-hand side f start x_0=x_{-1}=0. Let eta_0=1/c,beta_0=0 and, for j>=1,

    eta_j=2C_j(a)/(d C_{j+1}(a)), beta_j=C_{j-1}(a)/C_{j+1}(a).

Take T updates

    x_{j+1}=x_j+beta_j(x_j-x_{j-1})+eta_j(f-Ax_j).

Every denominator is positive: for zeta=a+sqrt(a^2-1)>1 the polynomial recurrence gives C_j(a)=(zeta^j+zeta^{-j})/2>0.

For x*=A^{-1}f, induction gives

    x*-x_j=r_j(A)x*,
    r_j(lambda)=C_j((c-lambda)/d)/C_j(a).

At j=0 this is the identity; at j=1 it is 1-lambda/c. For the induction, C_{j+1}(a)+C_{j-1}(a)=2a C_j(a) gives 1+beta_j=eta_j c. Substitution in the error recurrence then gives exactly the recurrence for C_{j+1}. All coefficients are fixed independently of A and f.

For lambda in [s,L], (c-lambda)/d is in [-1,1]. By the cosine addition formula and induction, C_j(cos theta)=cos(j theta); thus |C_j(x)|<=1 there. Also

    zeta=(sqrt(kappa)+1)/(sqrt(kappa)-1), rho=zeta^{-1} in (0,1).

Orthogonal spectral decomposition gives ||r_T(A)||_op<=1/C_T(a)<=2rho^T. With u=1/sqrt(kappa) in (0,1),

    log((1+u)/(1-u))=integral_0^u 2/(1-x^2) dx>=2u.

The denominator is positive throughout the integration interval. Hence 2rho^T<=2exp(-2T/sqrt(kappa))<=delta by the stated T.

Apply the iteration simultaneously to f=b and f=q, with final iterates w_T,u_T. It follows that

    ||w_T-A^{-1}b||<=delta nRB/s,
    ||u_T-A^{-1}q||<=delta R/s.

Furthermore u_T=g_T(A)q, where g_T(lambda)=(1-r_T(lambda))/lambda. Since |r_T(lambda)|<=delta<=1/2 and lambda>=s>0, g_T(lambda)>0, so q^T u_T>=0.

## 4. Explicit attention heads

Each token contains seven p-dimensional registers

    (z_c,z_q,qbar,w,u,w_old,u_old)

and four scalars (y,one,mout,vout), for D=7p+4. Every token has one=1. Context i has z_c=z_i,z_q=0,y=y_i. The query has z_c=0,z_q=q,y=0. Padding has z_c=z_q=0,y=0. All working registers and mout start at zero; vout=s. This is a fixed role-dependent feature encoding with no query label.

Specifying linear Q and K coordinate lists of equal length and a linear V output defines ordinary D-by-D matrices, with all unspecified coordinates zero. Constant scores use the register one.

**Broadcast layer, one head:** Q=one,K=one, and V writes N z_q into qbar. Exactly one token supplies z_q, so after the normalized sum qbar=q on every token.

The four iterate registers are identical on all tokens at initialization. The following layers preserve that invariant.

**Solver layer j, five heads:** All expressions below use pre-layer registers; eta=eta_j,beta=beta_j.

1. Q=(w,one), K=(-z_c,y). V writes N eta z_c into w. Its score is y_j-z_{c,j}^T w_i.
2. Q=-(w,one), K=(-z_c,y). V writes -N eta z_c into w.

Together these write eta sum_i z_i(y_i-z_i^T w), by ReLU(r)-ReLU(-r)=r.

3. Q=u,K=z_c. V writes -N eta z_c into u.
4. Q=-u,K=z_c. V writes N eta z_c into u.

Together these write -eta sum_i z_i z_i^T u.

5. Q=one,K=one. V writes the following, with **no N factor**:

       beta(w-w_old)-eta s w        into w,
       beta(u-u_old)+eta(qbar-s u)  into u,
       w-w_old                     into w_old,
       u-u_old                     into u_old.

The normalized sum in head 5 is the average of identical registers and equals the displayed expression. The residual connection makes the old registers equal to the pre-layer w,u. Summing all five heads produces exactly the recurrences of Section 3 for f=b,q. Context, feature, label, constant, and output registers are unchanged. Query and padding contribute zero to the data sums because z_c=y=0. This proves the invariant and exact implementation by induction.

**Readout layer, four heads:** Q=qbar,K=w,V writing one into mout, and Q=-qbar,K=w,V writing -one into mout, together produce q^T w_T. The factors 1/N cancel the sum over N identical w registers. Likewise Q=qbar,K=u,V writing s one into vout, paired with Q=-qbar,K=u,V writing -s one into vout, produces s q^T u_T. The preexisting vout=s supplies the noise floor. Thus the query token outputs are exactly

    mhat=q^T w_T, vhat=s+s q^T u_T>=s.

This is T+2 layers and at most five heads. Counting three D-by-D matrices per head gives the parameter bound. There is no nonlinear readout computing products or inverses outside the transformer.

## 5. Uniform forward KL

The errors obey

    |m-mhat|<=M delta<=sqrt(s eps),
    |v-vhat|<=R^2 delta<=min(s/2,s sqrt(eps)).

For the mean inequality use M/(1+M)<=1, also when M=0. Both variances are >=s. Put h=(v-vhat)/vhat, so |h|<=1/2 and 1+h>0. The exact Gaussian formula is

    KL=(h-log(1+h))/2+(m-mhat)^2/(2vhat).

For h in [-1/2,1/2], h-log(1+h)=integral_0^h x/(1+x) dx<=h^2. If h>=0, use x/(1+x)<=x. If h<=0, reverse the integral and use |x/(1+x)|<=2|x| on [h,0]. All denominators remain >=1/2. Consequently

    KL<=|v-vhat|^2/(2s^2)+|m-mhat|^2/(2s)<=eps.

All estimates hold for every admissible context and query. There is no conversion from a prior-averaged loss to uniform KL.

## 6. Prior work and boundaries

Bai et al., arXiv:2306.04637v2, Definition 1 (PDF page 5), supplies the architecture. Theorem 4 (PDF page 7) and Appendix D.1 supply known GD ridge point prediction with three heads and depth proportional to the condition number. Those facts are settled and are not claimed anew. The construction here combines classical Chebyshev iteration with exact attention operations to obtain simultaneous mean/variance and an explicit uniform KL budget. Novelty remains subject to literature and independent review.

The feature-input qualification is essential. A bounded finite-rank kernel on a compact set alone imposes no continuous or efficiently computable feature map on the raw inputs. A raw-input theorem needs additional regularity and an explicit feature-computation cost. The dossier's feature-map formulation motivates the feature-input reading used here; the reviewer must decide whether it closes Target 1 as intended.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:d607636f8bb63d92aae86ebe87bc095c863378e40c7757b232a3caebfaf4f168","revision_digest":"sha256:c83f32d096597a983c216b5023e30dce732c0e384663e77937b4e82999fca6e8","source_id":"owner:T336-w727-C002-v1","source_revision":"C002-v1-2026-10-20T20:00:48.215724+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Prop local-critical-thermal-mass of arXiv:2607.00311, 'Thermal Concentration and Poisson--Dirichlet Edge Statistics for Random-Lattice Gibbs Ense'] Let $L_n$ be distributed according to $\mu_n$ on $\mathbb X_n$.
Assume $0<c<1$ and put
$$
y_c=\frac{1}{2}\log\frac{1}{c}.
$$
For $t\in\mathbb R$, define
$$
H(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi}}\int_{-\infty}^{t}e^{-x^2}dx.
$$
This is the distribution function of the centered Gaussian law with density
$\pi^{-1/2}e^{-x^2}$, or equivalently of a normal random variable with
variance $1/2$.
Then
$$
\frac{
B_{n,c}((-\infty,y_c+t/\sqrt{n}],L_n)
}{
B_{n,c}(L_n)
}
\longrightarrow H(t)
$$
in probability as $n\to\infty$.

Method: Planar uniform lattice-tree diameter and scaling limit structural reduction or obstruction Result: Every such planar tree has Euclidean diameter at most n-1. If its diameter is D, all its vertices lie in an axis-aligned square of side at most2D around any chosen vertex, containing at most(2D+1)^2 lattice points. [Proposition combi_estimate_rooted_middle of arXiv:2603.05491, '\textbf{Local limits of uniform triangulations with boundaries in high genus}'] Fix $\theta \in [0,\frac{1}{2})$, $\displaystyle \frac{g_n}{n} \to \theta$ and $\mathbf{p}^{n} = (p^n_{1},\cdots,p^n_{\ell_n})$ such that $|\mathbf{p}^{n}|= o(n)$. For any $r_1,r_2 \ge 0$ and any $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists $a > 0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$,
\[
(n\tau_{\mathbf{p}^{n}}(n,g_n))^{-1}
\sum_{((n_1,g_1,I),(n_2,g_2,J)) \in \mathcal{M}(n,a)}
\tau_{(r_1,\mathbf{p}_{I}^{n})}(n_1,g_1)\,
\tau_{(r_2,\mathbf{p}_{J}^{n})}(n_2,g_2)
\le \varepsilon.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\frac{\tau_{r_1,r_2,\mathbf{p}^{n}}(n,g_n-1)}{n\tau_{\mathbf{p}^{n}}(n,g_n)} \longrightarrow 0.
\]
In particular,
\[
\frac{\tau_{\mathbf{p}^{n}}(n,g_n-1)}{\tau_{\mathbf{p}^{n}}(n,g_n)} = o(n^{-1}).

Status: independently checked proof; reviewer PASS on the listed claim version. Target 1, technical support: removes the atomic degeneracy obstacle to a stopped/conditioned-kernel diffusion argument. This is one technical step, not a proof of the proposed SDE.

Assume a zero-bias width-n network with independent Gaussian weight matrices and ReLU, n>=2. Initial inputs are nonzero with angle theta_0 in (0,pi). Given nonzero nonproportional inputs with angle theta, define q=(pi-theta)/(2*pi). Let D be the event that one output vector is zero, or both output vectors are nonzero and have zero angle.

**One-step identity.**

    p_n(theta) = P(D|theta) = 2^(1-n) + (n-1) q^n <= (n+1) 2^-n.

Proof. P(X=0)=P(Y=0)=2^-n, and their intersection has probability q^n. Thus extinction contributes 2^(1-n)-q^n. Conditional on any fixed pattern of strict signs, the positive coordinates have an absolutely continuous density. Two nonzero nonnegative vectors can be proportional only if their positive supports agree. If that common support has size >=2, proportionality is a nontrivial polynomial equality (for two coordinates, X_i Y_j-X_j Y_i=0) and has probability zero. If the support is a singleton, proportionality is automatic. There are n such sign patterns, each with probability q^n. Add these disjoint probabilities. The bound uses q<=1/2. After the first surviving layer the angle is in (0,pi/2].

**Conditioned-kernel coupling.** Let P_n(theta,.) be the exact kernel, sending D to an absorbing cemetery state. Let Q_n(theta,.) be P_n conditioned on D not occurring, well-defined for n>=2 and theta in (0,pi). For any integer L, the path laws of P_n and Q_n started at the same angle satisfy, in the convention d_TV=sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|,

    d_TV(path_0:L(P_n), path_0:L(Q_n)) <= min(1, L (n+1) 2^-n).

Construct a step coupling while the chains agree: sample the P_n step. If it survives, use the same value for Q_n. If it dies, draw Q_n independently from its conditioned kernel and count a disagreement. The Q_n marginal is correct since its law is (1-p)Q_n+pQ_n. Each agreeing step disagrees with conditional probability at most (n+1)2^-n. The union bound proves the assertion. This is a per-step conditioned chain; it is not asserted to equal the original path law conditional on survival through L.

For L<=Tn the bound is T n(n+1)2^-n. Thus proving a weak path limit for Q_n is sufficient to prove the same weak path limit for the killed P_n chain (with any common embedding of its cemetery state).

**Limit of this repair.** Removing the atom does not ensure inverse-angle integrability. On the positive-probability event that both vectors have exactly the same two-coordinate support, the continuous angle density is positive near zero, and E[1/theta' | D^c] is still infinite. A proof must use bounded test functions or a further truncation. In particular, this coupling theorem is not permission to reuse the dossier's untruncated inverse-angle generator estimates.

Independent finite check: scripts/localization_check.py enumerates all sign patterns at theta=pi/2 for n=1,...,7, using integer counts. logs/localization_exact.txt records agreement with the formula. The proof above covers every theta, without numerics.

[Defi change of specialization of arXiv:2412.05999, 'Non-Archimedean GUE corners and Hecke modules'] Let $\theta=(a_1,\ldots,a_n),\psi=(b_1^2,b_2^2,\ldots)$ be specializations ($\psi$ is a finite or infinite sequence) and $t$ a parameter. Also, we write $p_k$ as the $k$th power sum.
\begin{enumerate}
\item(Alternating case) We denote the specialization $\theta'=(a_1,a_1t,\ldots,a_n,a_nt)$. This makes the below equality hold:
$$p_k(\theta')=(1+t^k)p_k(\theta),\quad\forall k\ge 1.$$
\item(Hermitian case) We denote the specializations $\theta'=(a_1^2,\ldots,a_n^2),\psi^*=(b_1,-b_1,b_2,-b_2,\ldots)$. This makes the below equality hold: 
$$p_k(\theta')=p_{2k}(\theta),p_{2k-1}(\psi^*)=0,p_{2k}(\psi^*)=2p_k(\psi),\quad\forall k\ge 1.$$
\end{enumerate}
title: Defi change of specialization of arXiv:2412.05999

[Lem 1.1-CP of arXiv:2412.00708, 'Stochastic PDE approach to fluctuating interfaces'] For some $C, c>0$, we have
\begin{align*}
\|e^{-tKL^\varepsilon}w - \pi_\tau w\| \le C \Big\{(t+1) e^{-c/\varepsilon} + e^{-tc/\varepsilon^2}\Big\} \|w\|
\end{align*}
for every $t\ge 0$ and $w\in L^2\equiv L^2({\mathbb{T}})$, where 
$\|\cdot\|=\|\cdot\|_{L^2({\mathbb{T}})}$ and

If one deletes all rounds in which neither distinct-coupon count changes, then the induced sequence of nonself transitions is a Markov chain whose transition probabilities are proportional to the three weights displayed below.  Consequently all hitting probabilities of these absorbing sets are unchanged by self-loop erasure.

Moreover, the changed-state chain is absorbed after at most $2d-(2s+g)$ nonself transitions when started from an interior state $(s,g)$.  In particular, all stopping times below are almost surely finite and bounded by $2d$.

body:
[Definition 5 of arXiv:2608.00449, 'First-order phase transitions in the hard-core model'] \label[definition]{def:finitebasics}
    For a finite graph $G$ and $\lambda\ge 0$, the \emph{hard-core model on $G$ at fugacity $\lambda$} is the probability measure $\mu_{G,\lambda}$ on $\cI(G)$ such that
    \[ \mu_{G,\lambda}(I) = \frac{\lambda^{|I|}}{Z_G(\lambda)}. \]
    
    When the graph and fugacity are clear from context, we consider $I\sim\mu_{G,\lambda}$, identify a vertex $u$ with the indicator random variable for the event $u\in I$, and write $\overline{u}$ for the indicator of $u\notin I$. Then $\mu_{G,\lambda}(u)$ is the marginal of $u$ and $\mu_{G,\lambda}(\overline{u})=1-\mu_{G,\lambda}(u)$.
    
    In keeping with statistical physics terminology, we refer to the state of a vertex $u$ being in or out of an independent set as the \emph{spin} of $u$. One can think of an independent set $I\in\cI(G)$ as an assignment of spins in $\{0,1\}$ to the vertices of $G$ such that vertices in $I$ receive spin $1$ and vertices in the complement of $I$ receive spin $0$.
    For convenience when working with this formulation, we write $\Omega(G)$ for the set of functions $\sigma:V(G)\to\{0,1\}$ such that $\sigma^{-1}(1)\in\cI(G)$.

Convention $\hat f(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R}f(x)e^{-2\pi i x\xi}dx$. (a) (Always, as an $L^1$ identity) If $f\in L^1(\mathbb R)$, the periodization $Pf(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}f(x+n)$ converges absolutely for a.e. $x$, $Pf\in L^1(\mathbb T)$ with $\|Pf\|_{L^1(\mathbb T)}\le\|f\|_1$, and $\widehat{Pf}(k)=\hat f(k)$ for all $k\in\mathbb Z$. (b) (Pointwise identity) If in addition $\sum_nf(x+n)$ converges for every $x$ to a continuous function and $\sum_k|\hat f(k)|<\infty$, then $\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}f(x+n)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}\hat f(k)e^{2\pi i kx}$ for every $x$; taking $x=0$, $\sum_nf(n)=\sum_k\hat f(k)$. (c) (Convenient sufficient condition) If $f$ is continuous and there are $C,\delta>0$ with $|f(x)|\le C(1+|x|)^{-1-\delta}$ and $|\hat f(\xi)|\le C(1+|\xi|)^{-1-\delta}$, then (b) applies and both series converge absolutely; this holds for every $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R)$. (d) Scaled and multidimensional forms: for $T>0$, $\sum_nf(nT)=T^{-1}\sum_k\hat f(k/T)$; for $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ and the lattice $\mathbb Z^d$, $\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^d}f(x+n)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}\hat f(k)e^{2\pi i k\cdot x}$; more generally for a full-rank lattice $\Lambda$ with dual $\Lambda^*$ and covolume $|\Lambda|$, $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}f(\lambda)=|\Lambda|^{-1}\sum_{\mu\in\Lambda^*}\hat f(\mu)$. Classic application (Jacobi theta transformation): $\sum_ne^{-\pi n^2t}=t^{-1/2}\sum_ne^{-\pi n^2/t}$ for $t>0$.

(b): the periodization converges everywhere to a continuous function AND the Fourier transform is absolutely summable over the integers

[Theorem 31 (Combined clumsy-careless collector) of arXiv:2605.14511, 'Clumsy and Careless:\\ Stationary-Entry Flux in Non-monotone Coupon Collectors'] For fixed $\alpha\in[0,1)$ and $\beta\in(0,1)$,
\[
        \mu_n^{\alpha,\beta}
        \sim
        \frac{1}{(S;S)_\infty}
        \frac{n!}{n^n}Q^nS^{n(n+1)/2}.
\]
If $T_n^{\alpha,\beta}$ is the first post-thinning completion time from the empty collection, then
\[
        \mu_n^{\alpha,\beta}T_n^{\alpha,\beta}
        \Rightarrow \Exp(1).
\]
Moreover, for every fixed $r\ge1$,
\[
        \Ebb\bigl(\mu_n^{\alpha,\beta}T_n^{\alpha,\beta}\bigr)^r\to r!.
\]
Consequently,
\[
        \Ebb T_n^{\alpha,\beta}
        \sim
        (S;S)_\infty
        \frac{n^n}{n!}Q^{-n}S^{-n(n+1)/2},
\]
and
\[
        \Var(T_n^{\alpha,\beta})
        \sim
        (S;S)_\infty^2
        \left(\frac{n^n}{n!}\right)^2
        Q^{-2n}S^{-n(n+1)}.
\]

Let T be a triangulation of an n-dimensional simplex Delta^n with vertices v_0, ..., v_n. Suppose the vertices of T are colored with {0, 1, ..., n} such that each vertex of T lying on a face of Delta^n is colored with the index of one of the vertices spanning that face. Then T contains an odd number of fully colored n-simplices (simplices whose vertices receive all n+1 colors).
T is a simplicial triangulation of Delta^n
Coloring satisfies Sperner boundary condition

body:
[Theorem thm:generalcoupling of arXiv:2506.10765, 'A General Coupling for Ising Models and Beyond'] Let $\Omega$ and $\Sigma$ be two finite sets, $\rho$ and $\gamma$ be probability measures on $\Omega$ and $\Sigma$ respectively, and $f: \Omega \to 2^{\Sigma}$ be a function\footnote{Here, $2^{\Sigma}$ is the power set of $\Sigma$.}. For each $\eta \in \Sigma$, let
    $f^{-1}(\eta):=\{\omega \in \Omega \mid \eta \in f(\omega)\}.$
     Suppose that $ \sum_{\omega \in \Omega, \eta \in \Sigma} \rho[\omega] \gamma[\eta] 1\! \!1[\eta \in f(\omega)] > 0$ and then define a coupling probability measure on $\Omega\times\Sigma$ by
	\[\mathscr{P}[\omega,\eta]\propto \rho[\omega] \gamma[\eta] 1\! \!1[\eta \in f(\omega)],~\forall (\omega, \eta)\in\Omega\times\Sigma. \] 

	\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(a)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Omega$, denoted by  $\mathscr{P}_{\Omega}$, satisfies $ \mathscr{P}_{\Omega}[\omega]  \propto \gamma[f(\omega)]\rho[\omega]$ for each $\omega \in \Omega$. 
		\item[(b)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Sigma$, denoted by $\mathscr{P}_{\Sigma}$, satisfies $ \mathscr{P}_{\Sigma}[\eta] \propto  \rho[f^{-1}(\eta)] \gamma[\eta] $ for each $\eta \in \Sigma$.   

\item[(c)] For each $\omega\in\Omega$ with $\mathscr{P}_{\Omega}[\omega]\neq 0$,  the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\cdot | \omega]$ on $\Sigma$ is $\gamma[\cdot \mid f(\omega)]$.
        \item[(d)]   For each $\eta\in\Sigma$ with $\mathscr{P}_{\Sigma}[\eta]\neq 0$, the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\cdot|\eta] $ on $\Omega$ is $\rho[\cdot \mid f^{-1}(\eta)]$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:generalcoupling of arXiv:2506.10765

body: Every square complex n by n matrix A can be written as A = U T U*, where U is unitary (U* U = I) and T is upper triangular. body: Z^2 bond FPP with iid weights in [a, b], 0 < a <= b. Let T_+ denote the passage time between two wall points confined to the upper half-plane H. Then for every r >= 1, P(T_+ - E T_+ >= t sqrt(r)) <= exp(-a t^2 / (8 b^3)) for t in (0, 4 b^2 sqrt(r)/a). Derivation: modified log-Sobolev tensorization over the edge weights (BLM Theorem 6.15 applied conditionally), the deterministic bound #G_+ <= (b/a) r on the number of edges lying in every H-geodesic (from subpath optimality and the weight band), and Herbst-Chernoff with lambda in (0, 1/b]. The deterministic edge-count bound makes any variational choice of an auxiliary parameter redundant; the earlier form of this lemma carried such a parameter and a constant of a/(16 b^3), and an independent referee (2026-08-10) confirmed all constants and derived this two-fold improvement by removing the parameter outright. The lower tail is NOT covered by this route.

body:
For probability mass functions p and q on a finite set and an event A with p(A) > 0 and q(A) > 0, d_TV(p(.|A), q(.|A)) <= d_TV(p, q) / max(p(A), q(A)). In particular, if p(A) = q(A) = a, conditioning on A multiplies the total variation distance by at most 1/a. The constant is sharp: for all masses a, b in (0, 1] and every conditional distance c with max(a, b) c >= |a - b| there are laws with these values for which equality holds.

[Corollary 11 of arXiv:2609.01996, 'Baumslag--Solitar Subgroups Obstruct Model Companions for Fields with Group Actions'] Let \(K\) be a \(G\)-field and let \(\chi:G\to K^\times\) be a \(1\)-cocycle.
  If \(z\) is transcendental over \(K\), then the formula
  \[
    \gamma(z)=\chi(\gamma)z\quad(\gamma\in G)
  \]
  extends the action on \(K\) to a \(G\)-field structure on \(K(z)\).
  If \(D\trianglelefteq G\), \(\chi|_D=1\), and \(D\) acts trivially on \(K\), then \(D\) acts trivially on \(K(z)\).

[Proposition prop:Hurstinvariant of arXiv:2601.10359, 'An Operator It\^o Formula for Volterra Gaussian Processes:\\ The Intrinsic Bracket via Cau'] Let $X$ be a centered Gaussian process with stationary increments and covariance $R(t,s) = \tfrac{1}{2}(t^{2H}+s^{2H}-|t-s|^{2H})$. Then for any Volterra representation $(K,W)$ satisfying the Decreusefond--\"Ust\"unel conditions, the classical Hurst exponent $H$ is equivalently characterized by the intrinsic bracket scaling
\[
\langle X\rangle^{(D^K,\Pi^K)}_t \sim t^{2H} \quad \text{as } t\to 0^+,
\]
and this characterization is independent of the representation.

[Proposition 10 of arXiv:2608.29152, 'Uniform Statistical Convergence of Empirical Sinkhorn Potentials\\ with Exponential and Po'] Let $\mathbb B_\cX=C(\cX)/\R$ with the quotient sup norm, and define $\mathcal G_\eps([u])=[u-\Phi_\eps u]$.
Assume $\mathcal G_\eps$ is Fr\'echet differentiable at $[f_\eps]$, its derivative $\mathcal L_\eps := D\mathcal G_\eps([f_\eps])$ is invertible, and satisfies $\|\mathcal L_\eps^{-1}\|_{\mathbb B_\cX\to\mathbb B_\cX} \le K_0\eps^{-r}$.
Further assume a quadratic remainder bound $\|\mathcal G_\eps([f_\eps+h])-\mathcal L_\eps[h]\|_{\mathbb B_\cX} \le M_0\eps^{-s}\|[h]\|_{\mathbb B_\cX}^2$ inside a local ball $\|[h]\|_{\mathbb B_\cX}\le\rho_\eps$.
Then, on the smaller ball defined by $\|[h]\|_{\mathbb B_\cX} \le \bar\rho_\eps := \min\{\rho_\eps, \frac{\eps^{r+s}}{2K_0M_0}\}$, we have the local stability bound $d_\infty([f_\eps+h],[f_\eps]) \le 2K_0\eps^{-r} d_\infty([f_\eps+h],[\Phi_\eps(f_\eps+h)])$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

$v,w\in C_0^{\infty}(\cR,\bR^d)$. 
Then for $\P\otimes dt$-almost every $(\omega,t)$
we have 
\begin{align}
|b(u,v,w_t)|
&\leq N\hat w \big(|Du|_{L_2}+|u|_{L_2}\big)|Dv|_{L_2}  \nonumber\\
&\quad+N\bar w_t|Dv|_{L_2}|Dv|_{L_2}             \nonumber
\end{align}
with a constant $N=N(d,r)$.

[Lemma lem:gauge-identity of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] For every mean-zero $b$ and $a$,
		\begin{equation}
			\gamma^{(b)}_{2}(x_{1})
			= \int_{0}^{F_{1}(x_{1})}(Pb)(s)\,ds,
			\qquad
			\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\Big|_{0}
			\Big(\text{marginal 2 of } \big(1 + \varepsilon a(F_{1})\big)f\Big)
			= f_{2}\cdot(P^{*}a)(F_{2}):
			
		\end{equation}
		the cross-talk of the coordinate modulations, both in the bracket
		and at the level of marginals, is exactly the gauge
		field~(equation eq:gauge-P of the paper). For the Gaussian copula of correlation
		$r$, Mehler's expansion diagonalizes $P$ in the Hermite basis with
		spectrum $\{r^{k}\}_{k \ge 1}$~[lancaster1969], so

body: For a real parameter delta >= 0 the SQUARED BESSEL PROCESS of dimension delta started at y >= 0, written BESQ^delta, is the unique strong solution of dY_t = 2 sqrt( |Y_t| ) dW_t + delta dt with Y_0 = y; the solution is nonnegative, and pathwise uniqueness holds despite the non-Lipschitz diffusion coefficient by the Yamada-Watanabe criterion, which requires only Holder continuity of exponent 1/2. The BESSEL PROCESS of dimension delta, BES^delta, is X_t = sqrt(Y_t); for X > 0 it solves dX_t = dW_t + ((delta - 1)/(2 X_t)) dt. When delta = d is a positive INTEGER, BES^d started at |x| has the law of the radial part |B_t| of a d-dimensional Brownian motion started at x - a fact that makes the family the natural interpolation of radial Brownian motion to non-integer dimension. ADDITIVITY: BESQ^delta started at y and an independent BESQ^{delta'} started at y' add to a BESQ^{delta + delta'} started at y + y'; this holds for the SQUARED process and is false for the Bessel process itself. The index nu = delta/2 - 1 is the other common parameterisation and is the one that appears in the modified Bessel functions of the transition density; delta and nu must not be confused. For delta < 2 the boundary point 0 is reached and a boundary convention (absorbing or instantaneously reflecting) must be specified; for delta >= 2 the point 0 is never reached from y > 0 and no convention is needed. [standard; e.g. Revuz and Yor, Continuous Martingales and Brownian Motion, 3rd ed., Chapter XI]

body:
Fix finitely many inputs x^1,...,x^m in R^n_in and a finite T>0. For clarity restrict to a positive definite input Gram matrix V_0^{alpha beta}=<x^alpha,x^beta>/n_in. All layers have width n, zero biases, and mutually independent standard Gaussian weight entries. Equivalently, start from this deterministic V_0 and, conditional on V_l, draw n independent Gaussian m-vectors G_i with covariance V_l; update V_{l+1}^{alpha beta}=(c_n/n) sum_i phi_n(G_i^alpha)phi_n(G_i^beta). This is the covariance Markov chain of the Gaussian network, up to the harmless first-layer index shift. Let d_n/n tend to T. Choose fixed real c_+,c_-, slopes s_+=1+c_+/sqrt(n), s_-=1+c_-/sqrt(n), phi_n(x)=s_+ max(x,0)+s_- min(x,0), and c_n=(E[phi_n(g)^2])^(-1) for standard Gaussian g. Then V_{floor(nt)}, with upper-triangular entries viewed as a vector, converges in distribution on finite time intervals in the Skorohod topology to the covariance diffusion dV=b(V)dt+Sigma(V)^(1/2)dB, started at V_0. For alpha<=beta and gamma<=delta, Sigma_{alpha beta,gamma delta}(V)=V^{alpha gamma}V^{beta delta}+V^{alpha delta}V^{beta gamma}. Set rho_{alpha beta}=V^{alpha beta}/sqrt(V^{alpha alpha}V^{beta beta}), nu(rho)=(c_+-c_-)^2/(2pi) [sqrt(1-rho^2)-rho arccos(rho)], and b_{alpha beta}(V)=sqrt(V^{alpha alpha}V^{beta beta})nu(rho_{alpha beta}). The limiting scalar outputs at time T, conditional on V_T, form a centered Gaussian vector with covariance V_T; their unconditional law is the resulting Gaussian mixture. This result concerns width-dependent shaped activations and does not assert the same covariance diffusion for ordinary fixed ReLU.
A fixed finite collection of inputs with positive definite normalized Gram matrix (explicit restriction of the source)
Independent iid N(0,1) weights, no biases, constant width n
Fixed c_+,c_-; slopes 1+c_+/sqrt(n),1+c_-/sqrt(n)
Exact Gaussian variance normalization c_n; depth/width tends to finite T
