[Lemma mainlemma of arXiv:2411.06006, 'Mixing time of the torus shuffle'] Suppose $n \geq 4$ and consider the torus shuffle on an $n \times n$ grid.
Fix $l \geq 2$. 
  There exist universal constants
  $C>0$ and $D>0$ such that if
  $T'$ is the smallest even integer that is at least $C\ell^2 n$,
  then for any triplets of positions
  $(i, j, k)$ and $(i', j', k')$ in an $\ell \times \ell$ box $B_l$ within
  the $n \times n$ grid, the probability that tile $i$ travels to position $i'$, tile $j$ travels
  to position $j'$,
  and tile $k$ travels to position $k'$ in $T'$ steps is at least $\frac{D}{\ell^6}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma mainlemma of arXiv:2411.06006

[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2606.11389, 'Instability of a nonlinear oscillator with small friction and small additive noise'] Suppose $h > 0$.  We have
  \begin{align*}
  T(h) & =  4(1-2m^2)^{1/2} K(m), \\
  G_1(h) & =  -\frac{T'(h)}{T(h)} =  \left( \frac{1}{m(1-2m^2)}-\frac{E(m)}{m(1-m^2)K(m)} 
     \right) \frac{dm}{dh}> 0,  \\[1ex]
  G_2(h)  & =  \sigma^2\left(\frac{8}{15}h + \left(\frac{7}{15}+ \frac{12}{5}h\right)\left((1+4h)^{1/2}\left(\frac{2E(m)}{K(m)} -1\right) - 1\right) \right)
     \end{align*}
where
 $$m^2 = \frac{1}{2}\left( 1 - \frac{1}{\sqrt{4h+1}}\right)
 $$
and $K(m)$ and $E(m)$ denote the complete elliptic integrals of the
first and second kind (see \cite[Sect.\ 22.7]{WW62}). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 6 of arXiv:2606.11389

[Theorem thm-detprocess of arXiv:2411.14876, 'Limit theorems for stochastic exponentials of matrix-valued L\'evy processes \\'] Let $L=(L_t)_{t\geq 0}$ be a Lévy process in $\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ with characteristic triplet $(\Sigma_L, \gamma_L, \nu_L)$ and fulfilling (equation eq-nonsingular of the paper) and let $D=(D_t)_{t\geq 0}$ be the determinant process of its stochastic exponential defined in (equation eq-detprocess of the paper). 
	Then $D$ is a left (and right) Lévy process taking values in $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$. In particular, $D_t=\mathcal{E}(\check{L})_t$ for the real-valued (additive) Lévy process $\check{L}=(\check{L}_t)_{t\geq 0}$ given by
	$$\check{L}_t= \operatorname{tr}(L_t) + \frac12 \sum_{\substack{m,n=1\\m\neq n}}^d (\sigma_{(m,m),(n,n)} - \sigma_{(m,n),(n,m)})\cdot  t  + \sum_{0<s\leq t} (\det(\Id + \Delta L_s)-1- \operatorname{tr}(\Delta L_s)), \quad t\geq 0,$$
where $\sigma_{(m,j),(n,\ell)}$ denotes the covariance between the Gaussian components of $L^{(m,j)}$ and $L^{(n,\ell)}$.

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2609.01346, '2609.01346'] Suppose a solution of \eqref{eq:profile-system} approaches, as $s\to s_0$,
\[
 (x,r,\theta)\longrightarrow(x_0,r_0,\theta_0),
 \qquad r_0>0,
 \qquad \theta_0\in\{\pi/2,-\pi/2\},
\]
and assume
\begin{equation}
 x_0\sin\theta_0\neq0.
\end{equation}
Then the solution has a unique local continuation through $s_0$ in the class of
nondegenerate crossings.  If $u=(\theta-\theta_0)^k$, then $u$ is strictly
monotone near $s_0$, and
\begin{equation}
 \theta(s)-\theta_0
 \sim
 \left(\frac{k r_0^{k-1}x_0\sin\theta_0}{A}\right)^{1/k}
 (s-s_0)^{1/k},
\end{equation}
where the real $k$-th root is understood.  In particular,
\begin{align}
 x(s)-x_0&=O(|s-s_0|^{(k+1)/k}),\\
 r(s)-r_0&=O(|s-s_0|),\\
 \left|\frac{d\theta}{ds}(s)\right|&\sim
 \frac1k\left|\frac{k r_0^{k-1}x_0\sin\theta_0}{A}\right|^{1/k}
 |s-s_0|^{-(k-1)/k}.
\end{align}
Writing $\gamma=(x,r)$, there are constants $C>0$ and $\eta>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \left|
 \frac{d\gamma}{ds}(s)-\frac{d\gamma}{ds}(t)
 \right|
 \leq C|s-t|^{1/k}
 \qquad
 \text{whenever }|s-s_0|<\eta\text{ and }|t-s_0|<\eta.
\end{equation}
Consequently the profile curve is $C^{1,1/k}$ near the crossing, and the
exponent $1/k$ is optimal.  It is also locally $W^{2,p}$ for every
$1\leq p<k/(k-1)$, but it is not $W^{2,k/(k-1)}$ at the crossing.
title: Lemma 5 of arXiv:2609.01346

body: [Cor 3 of arXiv:2608.26698, 'Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion '] The mapping class group $\mathrm{MCG}(S^2 \times S^3)$ is isomorphic to $(\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}) \rtimes \mathbb{Z}/2$, where the action of the nontrivial element of $\mathbb{Z}/2$ on $\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}$ is given by sending an element to its inverse. In other words, $\mathrm{MCG}(S^2 \times S^3)$ has the following presentation: \[\left\langle a, b, v | ab = ba, v^2 = 1, vav = a^{-1}, vbv = b^{-1} \right\rangle,\] where $a$ and $b$ can be represented by the Dehn twists $\mathbf{t}_{S_1, \alpha}$ and $\mathbf{t}_{S_1 \# S_1, \alpha}$ respectively, and $v$ can be represented by $R$. It follows that $\mathrm{MCG}(S^2 \times S^3)$ is residually finite and virtually torsion-free, and has trivial center. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor 3 of arXiv:2608.26698

body:
[Lemma 25 (Eigenvalue rigidity) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{lem:rigidity}
Let \(A\) be a matrix such that \(A/\sqrt n\) has the distribution of GUE.
Let
\[
\lambda_1 \leq \lambda_2 \leq \cdots \leq \lambda_n
\]
denote its eigenvalues, and let \(\gamma_i\) be the corresponding classical
location for the semicircle law, defined by
\[
\int_{-\infty}^{\gamma_i}
\frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{(4-x^2)_+}\,dx
=
\frac{i}{n}.
\]
Then for every \(1\leq i\leq n\),
\[
\mathbb P\left(
n^{-1/3}\min(i,n-i+1)^{1/3}
\left|\lambda_i-\sqrt n\,\gamma_i\right|
\geq T
\right)
\ll
n^{O(1)}\exp(-cT^c)
\]
for all \(T>0\), where \(c>0\) is an absolute constant.

In particular, with overwhelming probability,
\[
\lambda_i
=
\sqrt n\,\gamma_i
+
O\!\left(
n^{1/3}\min(i,n-i+1)^{-1/3}\log^{O(1)} n
\right),
\]
and the same estimate holds with \(\lambda_i\) replaced by
\(\mathbb E\lambda_i\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Eigenvalue rigidity

[Lemma lem:leave-one-out-upper-bound-het of arXiv:2510.11015, 'An interpretable universal bound for multiserver queues via a leave-one-out technique'] Consider the modified $GI/GI/n$\xspace queue with heterogeneous servers.
    For each $j=1,2,\dots n$,
    the queue length of the $j$-th leave-one-out system pathwise dominates the queue length of the main system under study, i.e., 
    \[
        Q_{-j}(t) \geq Q(t) \quad \forall t\geq 0.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2608.19832, 'Sharp Convex Concentration for Symmetric Random Tensors with Subgaussian Coordinates'] Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\R$ with
$\int e^{x^2/K^2}\,d\mu\le2$. Let $\nu\ll\mu$, and assume
\[
 h=D(\nu\Vert\mu)<\infty.
\]
There is a coupling $(U,V)$ of $\mu$ and $\nu$ such that
\begin{align}
 \E\left[\E(\abs{U-V}\mid U)^2\right]
 &\le C K^2h\log\left(e+\frac1h\right),
 \\
 \E\left[\E(\abs{U-V}\mid V)^2\right]
 &\le C K^2h\log\left(e+\frac1h\right),
 \\
 \E\abs{U-V}^2
 &\le C K^2(\sqrt h+h).
 
\end{align}
The right sides are interpreted as zero when $h=0$.

body:
[Theorem 36 of arXiv:2604.04267, 'On Sharpest Tail Bounds for Functions \\ of Tail Bounded Random Variables'] The reversed CDF (section~\ref{preliminaries}) of $\mathscr{S}_R(f_k,G^k)$ is 
\begin{equation}
P(\mathscr{S}_R(f_k,G^k) \geq t) = f_k\Big(\inf \big(G^k\cup (-\infty, \inf G^k]\big)_{\geq t}\Big), \ \forall t \in \mathbb{R}
\end{equation}
with the conventions $\inf \emptyset = + \infty$ and $f_k(+\infty) = 0$. 
\begin{proof}
For convenience, we may replace $G^k$ with $G^k \cup (-\infty, \inf G^k]$ WLOG. \eqref{SRXkeq} becomes
$$
\mathscr{S}_R(f_k,G^k)(s) = \sup G^k_{\leq \widetilde{X}_k(s)}, \ \forall s \in (0,1).
$$
One finds
$$
\mathscr{S}_R(f_k,G^k)(s) \geq t \iff \exists t' \in G^k \cap [t, \widetilde{X}_k(s)].
$$
The RHS holds iff $\widetilde{X}_k(s) \geq \inf G^k \cap [t,\infty) = \inf G^k_{\geq t}, \ G^k_{\geq t} \neq \emptyset$. Thus, 
\begin{equation}
\mathscr{S}_R(f_k,G^k)(s) \geq t \iff \widetilde{X}_k(s) \geq \inf G^k_{\geq t}, \ G^k_{\geq t} \neq \emptyset. 
\end{equation}
So $P(\mathscr{S}_R(f_k,G^k) \geq t) = 0$ if $G^k_{\geq t} = \emptyset$ (i.e.\ if $\inf G^k_{\geq t} = +\infty$, because the greatest lower bound of the empty set is $+\infty$). For $G^k_{\geq t} \neq \emptyset$, define
$$
I_t := \big\{ s \in (0,1) \ \big| \ \mathscr{S}_R(f_k,G^k)(s) \geq t \big\} \stackrel{\eqref{gamma1}}{=} \big\{ s \in (0,1) \ \big| \ \widetilde{X}_k(s) \geq \inf G^k_{\geq t} \big\}.
$$
This gives
\begin{align*}
P(\mathscr{S}_k(f_k,G^k) \geq t) = m(I_t) &= P(\widetilde{X}_k \geq \inf G^k_{\geq t}) \\ 
&= f_k(\inf G^k_{\geq t})
\end{align*}
where the last step is because $P(\widetilde{X}_k \geq t) = f_k(t), \ \forall t \in \mathbb{R}$ \ (lemma~\ref{Xtilde} (ii)).
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 30 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recall from Lemma~\ref{l:freeprob.V.convex} that $z_{\min}$ is the unique minimizer of $V$ on the interval $[z_0,\infty)$.
    We have $z_{\min} = z_0$ if and only if
    \beq
        
        \alpha \le \mu_1 \textup{ and } \hv_1 < 0\,.
    \eeq
    If \eqref{e:zmin-equal-z0} does not hold, $z_{\min}$ is the unique solution to the equation $V'(z) = 0$ for $z\in(z_0,\infty)$.

\begin{proof}
Recall that if $\hv_1 > 0$, then $V(z)\uparrow\infty$ as $z\downarrow z_0$, so in this case clearly $z_{\min} > z_0$.
If instead $\hv_1 < 0$, then $z_0 = \hw_1$, so we have $z_{\min}=z_0$ if and only if the derivative $V'$ stays nonnegative as $z\downarrow \hw_1$. To this end, recall that as $z\downarrow \hw_1$ we have $m(z)\uparrow\infty$, so
    \[\sum_{j=1}^r \lambda_j \bigg(
        \frac{\hv_j m(z)}{\alpha - \hv_j m(z)}\bigg)^2
        \longrightarrow \sum_{j=1}^r \lambda_j = 1\,.\]
We also have $m_2(z)/m(z)^2 \to 1/\mu_1$, and substituting into
\eqref{e:fp-V-pr} gives
    \[
        V'(z)
        \longrightarrow 1 - \frac{\alpha}{\mu_1}
    \]
   as $z\downarrow\hw_1$. This is nonnegative if and only if $\alpha \le \mu_1$, which yields the condition \eqref{e:zmin-equal-z0}. Otherwise, we must have $z_{\min} > z_0$; in this case, since $V$ is strictly convex and twice differentiable, the value $z_{\min}$ must be the unique solution to the equation $V'(z) = 0$ for $z\in(z_0,\infty)$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[campaign result 2026-09-14, author_checked_exact_integer_arithmetic_no_independent_read] This refutes the literal p=d condition in M. Neri and P. Pinto's Remark 3.7 in Quantitative limit theorems for generalized Polya urns with applications to random tree models, arXiv:2607.07309. Let R be a real d-by-d replacement matrix with each row sum equal to lambda, let I_d be the identity matrix, and define symm(A)=(A+A^T)/2. Set C_d=J_d=I_d. The real symmetric matrix G=symm(C_d J_d(R^T-lambda I_d) C_d^T)=symm(R^T-lambda I_d) has largest eigenvalue at least zero. Thus the strict inequality lambda_max(G)<0 cannot hold on the full d-dimensional space for any balanced replacement matrix. This statement concerns the full-space matrix in the remark; it does not assert failure of every possible restriction to mean-zero vectors. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
All row sums of R equal lambda; d>=1.

body:
Ansatz 20, stated inside Open Problem 8 of Aldous and Janson (arXiv:2303.02529), claims for nonnegative f with f(j) = O(j^k) that (i) if sum_i a(i) f(i) converges then sum_{i <= n} a(n,i) f(i) tends to it, and (ii) if it diverges then sum_{i <= n} a(n,i) f(i) is asymptotic to sum_{i <= n} a(i) f(i); here a(n,j) is the probability that the tagged harmonic descent chain started at n visits j and a(j) = 6 H_{j-1} / (pi^2 (j-1)) is its fixed-j limit. Our result (id P0341, 2026-09-08): BOTH parts are FALSE, on the single observation that a(n,n) = 1 exactly - the chain starts at n, so it visits n surely. For (i), take f(j) = 1{j = 2^r}: f is bounded (hence of polynomial growth) and a(2^r) = O(r 2^-r), so S = sum a(i) f(i) converges; but at n = 2^K the truncated sum contains the top term a(2^K, 2^K) = 1, forcing liminf >= 1 + S against the predicted S. For (ii), take g(j) = j 1{j = 2^r} (so g(j) <= j): since a(j) j ~ (6/pi^2) log j the truncated limiting sum at n = 2^K is of order K^2 while the actual sum is at least its root term 2^K, so the ratio diverges. The refutation is scoped to the displayed Ansatz, not to Open Problem 8 as a whole - explicit bounds on |a(n,m) - a(m)| remain open. Verification as the source words it: each piece re-derived (the asymptotics of a(j) and a(j) j, the summability of a(2^r), the polynomial-growth hypothesis for both test functions, and a(n,n) = 1 from the definition); no rate of convergence and no numerical evaluation is needed anywhere. Prior art not cleared.

[Theorem thm:erm-fragile of arXiv:2608.20480, 'When Clean Data Hurts: Learning with Monotone \\ Corruptions Beyond Binary Classification'] There is a countable, closed class $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{frag}}$ of finite coordinatewise range, with $d_{\mathrm{DS}}(\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{frag}})=1$, that is ordinarily PAC learnable by a proper ERM.  Nevertheless, for every fixed $\alpha>0$ and every possibly randomized ERM rule $A$, an oblivious adversary using at most $\alpha n$ additions can force
\[
    \liminf_{n\to\infty}
    \sup_{D,h^\star,\mathsf{Adv}}
    \mathbb{E} L_D(A(T),h^\star)
    \geq
    c_\alpha>0,
\]
where the supremum ranges over oblivious adversaries of budget at most $\alpha n$, and $c_\alpha$ may be taken of order $e^{-1/\alpha}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Oblivious additions destroy ERM

[Lemma lastlemma of arXiv:2411.06006, 'Mixing time of the torus shuffle'] Fix $k$ with $2 \leq k \leq m+1$ and let $T$ and $t$ be as defined in Claim (bigclaim of the paper). 
Let $B_{\ell_k}$ be a box of side length $l_k$ in the $n \times n$ grid. 
Let $x, y$ and $z$ be distinct tiles in $B_{\ell_k}$ and 
let $T_{xyz}$ be the time of the first
$3$-collision in the time interval $\{T, \dots, t\}$
that involves either $x, y$ or $z$. There is a universal constant $d >0$ such that
\[
  { \mathbb P}( \mbox{$x$, $y$ and $z$ collide at time $T_{xyz}$}) \geq
  \left(\frac{t}{n^2} \wedge 1 \right) \frac{d}{\ell_k^4} \,. 
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary 29 (Pythagorean identity for the martingale projection) of arXiv:2604.22159, 'Adapted optimal transport between filtered Gaussian processes'] Let $L\in\mathscr{L}(N,d)$, and let $L^{\mathrm{mgle}}\in\mathscr{L}_{\mathrm{mgle}}(N,d)$ be the martingale projection defined in Theorem~\ref{thm:mgle.proj}. Then, for every $M\in\mathscr{L}_{\mathrm{mgle}}(N,d)$,
\begin{equation}
\|L-M\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2
=
\|L-L^{\mathrm{mgle}}\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2
+
\|L^{\mathrm{mgle}}-M\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2.
\end{equation}
In particular, $L^{\mathrm{mgle}}$ is the orthogonal projection of $L$ onto $\mathscr{L}_{\mathrm{mgle}}(N,d)$.
Moreover, the projection map $P_{\mathrm{mgle}}:L\mapsto L^{\mathrm{mgle}}$ is $1$-Lipschitz with respect to the Frobenius norm and is $\dist_{\AW}$-contractive:
\[
\|L^{\mathrm{mgle}}-M^{\mathrm{mgle}}\|_{\mathrm{F}}\leq \|L-M\|_{\mathrm{F}},
\qquad
\dist_{\AW}(L^{\mathrm{mgle}},M^{\mathrm{mgle}})\leq \dist_{\AW}(L,M),
\]
for all $L,M\in\mathscr{L}(N,d)$.

body: [Theorem thm:plaw of arXiv:2412.01381, 'Ergodicity and mixing for locally monotone stochastic evolution equations'] Assume $p=1+\frac{d}{2}$ for $d\ge 2$, and that Hypotheses~(hyp:regularity of the paper),~(hyp:reg2 of the paper),~(hyp:quant of the paper) hold true. Then the Markovian Feller semigroup $(P_t)_{t\ge 0}$ of the stochastic shear thickening power-law fluid equations~(equation eq:plaw of the paper) with degenerate additive Wiener noise possesses a unique invariant measure $\mu_\ast$ with finite $p$-moments in $W^{1,p}_{\operatorname{sol},0}({\mathcal O};\mathbb{R}^d)$. If, additionally, Hypothesis~(hyp:mixing of the paper) holds, then $(P_t)_{t\ge 0}$ is exponentially ergodic and exponentially mixing, with a quantitative upper bound for the $\varepsilon$-mixing time given in Theorem~(thm:mixing of the paper).

[Lemma 4 (Order statistics) of arXiv:2506.09333, 'On the Dimension-Free Concentration of Simple Tensors via Matrix Deviation'] Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent random variables satisfying $\norm{X_i}_\psitwo \le 1$ for all $i$. Let $t>0$, $q \ge 2$ and 
    $k \coloneqq t/\ln_+(en/t)$.
    Then,\footnote{By convention, we set $1/0=\infty$ in defining $k$, and the sum over an empty set is zero.} with probability at least $1-2e^{-t}$, we have
    \begin{equation} 
        \sum_{i \le 3k} (X_i^*)^2 \lesssim t
        \quad \text{and} \quad 
        \sum_{i > k} (X_i^*)^q \lesssim_q n.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Order statistics

[Theorem 10 (Uniform concentration of LOO) of arXiv:2608.30261, 'Estimating Population-Risk Curves Along Nonconvex Gradient Flows from the Training Sample'] Assume \eqref{eq:loss-range-length}, finite $\beta_{n-1}$ in
\eqref{eq:uniform-stability}, the size-$(n-1)$ modulus
\eqref{eq:hyper-modulus}, and \eqref{eq:loo-joint-measurability}.  For
$r>0$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$, let $s_n(r,\delta),c_n^-\in[0,\infty)$ be the
finite deterministic concentration radius and bounded-difference coefficient
defined in \cref{eq:sn-definition,eq:bounded-difference-c}.  Then, with probability
at least $1-\delta$,
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{u\in\mathcal U}
 |\Score_{n,\mathcal U}^{\LOO}(u)-\Risk_{S,\mathcal U}^-(u)|
 \leq s_n(r,\delta),
\end{equation}
where
\begin{align}
 s_n(r,\delta)
 &=2\omega_{n-1}(r)
 +c_n^-\sqrt{\frac n2
 \log\frac{2\mathcal N(\mathcal U,\rho,r)}{\delta}},\\
 c_n^-&=\frac{B_{n-1}^{\rm rng}}n+\frac{2(n-1)}n\beta_{n-1}.
 
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Uniform concentration of LOO

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2608.16752, 'Absorption Probabilities for Random Convex Hulls: Distribution-Freeness via the Wall-Cross'] For integers $n,d\geq 1$ we have
$$
\sum_{\ell=1}^{n}
\stirling{n}{\ell}\,
2^{\,n-\ell}
\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}
\binom{\ell-1}{j}
=
\sum_{q\geq 0}
\stirlingb{n}{d-1-2q},
$$
where the numbers $\stirlingb{n}{k}$ with $n\in \{1,2,\ldots\}$, $k\in \mathbb Z$,  are defined by the generating function
$$
\sum_{k\in \mathbb Z} \stirlingb{n}{k} t^k
=
(t+1)(t+3)\cdots(t+2n-1).
$$
title: Lemma 12 of arXiv:2608.16752

[Prop PropCarlo of arXiv:2506.08202, 'Stochastic dissipative systems in Banach spaces driven by L\'evy noise'] Let $T>0$, $d\in{\mathbb N}$, $H=L^2([0,1]^d)$, let $A$ be the realization of the Laplacian operator in $H$ with Dirichlet boundary condition and let $R=(-A)^\delta$ with $\delta\in{\mathbb R}$. Then the following assertions hold true. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\delta=0$ then $\{W_{A}(t)\}_{t\geq 0}$ is a continuous process (with values) in $H_\gamma$ with $\gamma<1/4$.
\item If $\delta > (d-2)/4$ then $\{W_{A}(t)\}_{t\geq 0}$ is a continuous process in $C([0,1]^d)$. Moreover for every $p\geq 2$
\[
\mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{t\in [0,T]}{\left\|W_A(t)\right\|}_{C([0,1]^d)}^p\right]<+\infty.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop PropCarlo of arXiv:2506.08202

body:
[Lemma circular_law of arXiv:2606.16609, 'On stability of outliers from the circular law'] Let $\{ \lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_N \}$ the spectrum of a complex Ginibre matrix conditioned on $\{ \lambda_1 = z \}$ with fixed $z \in \mathbb{C}$; almost surely, the empirical spectral distribution
$$
\frac{1}{N-1} \sum_{k=2}^N \delta_{\lambda_k}
$$
converges weakly to the circular law. That is to say that, for any continuous bounded function~$\phi$, we have
$$
\frac{1}{N-1} \sum_{k=2}^N \phi(\lambda_k) 
\xrightarrow[]{N \rightarrow \infty} 
\frac{1}{\pi} \int_{\mathbb{D}} \phi(z) \mathrm{d} z.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Conditional Circular Law \cite{Thomas2026}

[Definition 5 of arXiv:2604.19220, 'Split merge dynamics for expanding intervals and point processes on the real line.'] For $ r,s > 0, $ a random variable has a distribution $\beta_{r, s}(0,1)$ if its density 
with respect to the Lebesgue measure  $ dx $ on $ [0,1]$ is 
$$ \beta_{r, s}(0,1)(x)=  \frac{x^{r-1} (1-x)^{s-1}}{\int_0^1 x^{r-1} (1-x)^{s-1} dx}{\mathbf 1}_{x \in [0,1]}.$$ For $ a <  b $ we denote $ Y \overset{d}{=} \beta_{r, s}(a,b) $
if $ \frac{Y - a }{b- a } $ has $\beta_{p, q}(0,1)$ distribution. We often drop 
$ (0,1) $    in $\beta_{p, q}(0,1).$ The density of $ \beta_{r, s}(a,b) $ is $ (b-a) \beta_{r, s}(0,1)(\frac{x-a}{y-b}).$  By convention we set $ \beta_{r, s}(a,a)= \delta_a (dx). $

L_{i}^{0}(x)\;\leq \;x,\quad \forall \,x\in (0,1),\quad i=1,2.  
\end{equation}
Consequently, for all $n\geq 1$, $L_{i}^{n}(x)<x$ on $(0,1)$.

[Lem 58 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $\cA_N$ and $\tilde\cA_N$ be $L$-Lipschitz algorithms with 
	\beq
	\frac{1}{N} \bbE\bigg[

		\bigg]

    \[\WERR(\cA_N,\tilde{\cA}_N)

        \max\bigg\{
        \bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_N),
        \mu(\tilde \cA_N)
        	\Big)^2,
        \bbW_2\Big(
        	\mu^{\Ising}(\cA_N),
        \mu^{\Ising}(\tilde \cA_N)
        \Big)^2
        \bigg\}
        \le C_1 \delta + C_2e^{-c_0N}\,.
    \]

body:
[Lem 76 (Kolmogorov continuity lemma for distributions) of arXiv:2510.22155, 'Random walks in space-time random media in all spatial dimensions: the full subcritical fl'] Let $(t,\phi) \mapsto V(t,\phi)$ be a map from $[0,T]\times \mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ into $L^2(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ which is linear and continuous in $\phi$. Fix a non-negative integer $r$. Assume there exists some $\kappa>0, q>d/\kappa$ and $\alpha<-r$ and $C=C(\kappa,\alpha,q,{T})>0$ such that 
		\begin{align*}\mE[|V(t,S^\lambda_{x}\phi)|^q]^{1/q}&\leq C\lambda^{\alpha },\\  \mE[|V(t,S^\lambda_{x}\phi)-V(s,S^\lambda_{x}\phi)|^q]^{1/q}&\leq C\lambda^{\alpha -\kappa} |t-s|^{\kappa },
		\end{align*}uniformly over all smooth functions $\phi$ on $\mathbb R$ supported on the unit ball of $\mathbb R$ with {$\|\phi\|_{C^r}\leq 1$}, and uniformly over $\lambda\in(0,1]$ and $0\leq s,t\leq T$. Then for any $\tau>1$ and any $\beta<\alpha-\kappa$ there exists a random variable $\big(\mathscr V(t)\big)_{t\in[0,T]}$ taking values in $C([0,T],C^{\beta,\tau}(\mathbb R^d))$ such that $(\mathscr V(t),\phi)=V(t,\phi)$ almost surely for all $\phi$ and $t$. Furthermore, one has that $$\mE[\|\mathscr V\|^q_{C([0,T],C^{\beta,\tau}(\mathbb R^d))}]\leq C',$$ where $C'$ depends on the choice of $\alpha,\beta,q,\kappa,$ and the constant $C$ appearing in the moment bound above but not on $V,\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Kolmogorov continuity lemma for distributions

\[

\begin{equation}
        f_j^H(H(y))=\widetilde f_j(y),
        \qquad j=1,\ldots,m.
\end{equation}
Consequently, if $\rho_H=H_{\#}\widetilde\rho$, then
\begin{equation}
        \rho_H F_H=\widetilde\rho\,\widetilde F.
\end{equation}

\bal
(X_{1,k}(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta), X_m(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta), T_1(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta), T_m(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta), Y_m(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta)) \xrightarrow{D} N(\bm{0}, \bm{\Sigma})
\eal
as $\theta_0, \theta \to \infty$ such that $\frac{\theta_0}{\theta} \to c$, where the covariance matrix is given by
\bal
\bm{\Sigma} = \begin{pmatrix}
1 - \beta & B_k(\alpha, \beta, c, m, L) & 0 & 0 & 0 \\

[Lem boundstheta of arXiv:2605.06488, 'Continuous-state branching processes with L\'evy-Khintchine drift-interaction: Laplace dua'] Assume $\neg \Htwo:\ \int_1^{\infty}\frac{\mathrm{d} u}{\Sigma(u)}<\infty$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $\Phi$ be the Bernstein function with triplet $(\gamma^+, \pi_{|[1,\infty)}, \lambda)$. One has \begin{equation} \underline{\theta}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Phi, \hat{\Sigma}}=\underset{x\rightarrow \infty}{\liminf}\, x\int_1^{\infty}\frac{\bar{\pi}(h)+\lambda}{\hat{\Sigma}(x+h)}\mathrm{d} h,\end{equation}
and similarly for $\overline{\theta}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Phi, \hat{\Sigma}}$ replacing $\liminf$ by $\limsup$.
\item
If $\Phi\sim \Phi_1$ at $0$, then $$\overline{\theta}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Phi, \hat{\Sigma}}=\overline{\theta}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Phi_1, \hat{\Sigma}},\text{ and } \underline{\theta}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Phi, \hat{\Sigma}}=\underline{\theta}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Phi_1, \hat{\Sigma}}.$$ 
\item One has
\[\underline{\theta}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Phi,\hat{\Sigma}}=\underset{x\rightarrow \infty}{\liminf}\,\mathbb{E}[A(\mathbbm{e}_x)], \quad \overline{\theta}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Phi,\hat{\Sigma}}=\underset{x\rightarrow \infty}{\limsup}\,\mathbb{E}[A(\mathbbm{e}_x)],\]
where $$A:(0,\infty)\ni z\mapsto\frac{\Phi(z)\hat{W}(z)}{z} \text{ and } \mathbbm{e}_x \text{ is an exponential r.v. with parameter }x.$$ The following hold: $A(z)\asymp \frac{\Phi(z)}{z^2\hat{\Sigma}(1/z)}$ and
\[\liminf_{z\rightarrow 0}A(z)\leq \underline{\theta}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Phi, \hat{\Sigma}}\leq \overline{\theta}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Phi, \hat{\Sigma}}\leq \limsup_{z\rightarrow 0} A(z).\]    
In particular if $\theta:=\underset{z\rightarrow 0}{\lim}\frac{\Phi(z)\hat{W}(z)}{z}\text{ exists in } [0,\infty]$, then $$\theta=\underline{\theta}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Phi, \hat{\Sigma}}=\overline{\theta}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Phi, \hat{\Sigma}}.$$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:rho-convexity-subcritical-interval-paper of arXiv:2606.08683, 'Exact Fourier dimensions of dyadic Mandelbrot cascades under minimal integrability'] Assume the vector law is energy-admissible. Then the following hold.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item For \(0<q\le1\), one has 
\(
\rho(q)<\infty
\).

\item The function 
\(
q\mapsto \log_2\rho(q)
\)
is convex on every interval on which 
\(
\rho(q)<\infty
\).

\item One has
\[
\rho(1)=1,
\qquad
\left.\frac{d}{dq}\right|_{q=1-}\log_2\rho(q)=\gamma(X)<0.
\]

\item For every \(0<q<1\), one has \(\rho(q)>1.\)

\item The set
\[
I_X=\{q\in(1,2):\rho(q)<1\}
\]
is either empty or an initial interval of \((1,2)\), namely one of
\[
(1,q_*),\qquad (1,q_*],\qquad (1,2),
\]
where \(q_*\in(1,2)\) in the first two cases.
\end{enumerate}

[Definition 16 of arXiv:2606.29512, '2606.29512'] A $\cV$-valued optional process
$u=(u_t)_{t\in[0,T]}$
is called a solution of \eqref{SNS5}--\eqref{div5}--\eqref{bin5} on $[0,T]$ if
$u\in L_2([0,T],\cV)\cap L_\infty([0,T],\cH)$ (a.s.),  
and for every $\varphi\in\cV$, 
\begin{align}
(u_t,\varphi)=&(u_0,\varphi)-
\int_0^t\Big[\big(a_s^{ij}D_j u_s+\frf_s^i(u_s),D_i \varphi\big)
+(u_{s(u_s)},\varphi)\Big]\,ds                                                                   \nonumber\\
&+\int_0^t\big(\gamma_s^{ki}D_i q_s^k+f_s(u_s,Du_s),\varphi\big)\,ds  \nonumber\\
&+\int_0^t\big(\sigma_s^{ik}D_i u_s+h_s^k(u_s),\varphi\big)\,dw_s^k    \nonumber\\
&+\int_0^{t}\int_{Z}\big(\frh_s(u_{s-},z),\varphi\big)\,\tilde\pi(ds,dz)                       
\end{align}
holds for $\mathbb P\otimes dt$-almost every
$(\omega,t)\in\Omega\times[0,T]$. In addition 
equation \eqref{pressure_assumption} is assumed to hold. 

As before, we call
$u=(u_t)_{t\in[0,T]}$
an $\cH$-solution if it is an $\cH$-valued 
$\cF_t$-adapted c\`adl\`ag process such that
$u\in L_2([0,T],\cV)\ \text{(a.s.)}$, 
almost surely \eqref{1.19.6} holds for all
$t\in[0,T],\,\varphi\in\mathcal V$, 
and equation \eqref{pressure_assumption} is satisfied. 
Recall that a solution is called an admissible solution if it is 
an admissible function.

Fix a positive integer k and a constant mu in(0,1). For integer d>=k, let U_d be uniform on{-1,1}^d and let P_mu have independent binary coordinates of mean mu. For0<=rho<=1 set D=(1-rho)*U_d+rho*P_mu. Let P_F be uniform over the binom(d,k) parity functions chi_S(x)=product_{j in S}x_j with |S|=k. There exists C_k>0 depending only on k such that, for all sufficiently large d (the threshold may depend on k and mu), uniformly over rho in[0,1], CP_infinity(P_F,D)<=1/binom(d,k)+C_k*rho^2*mu^(4k). Here CP_infinity is the average squared D-correlation of two independent P_F draws. This is a fixed-k asymptotic interpretation of source Lemma16; no degree-uniform constant for k=k(d) is supplied.
Fixed k>=1 and fixed0<mu<1; d tends to infinity.
Two supports are sampled independently and uniformly among all k-subsets.
Input mixture weight0<=rho<=1; product coordinates have common mean mu.

[Theo moments_vertex of arXiv:2606.15339, 'Uniform integrability of the distance to the nearest leaf in random trees'] Let $\mathcal{T}_n$ be of type~I, II or~III, and let $\mathcal{T}^{*}$ denote the corresponding
pointed local limit. Then, for every $p>0$,
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbf{E}\bigl[\partial(\mathcal{T}_n,v_n)^{p}\bigr]
=\mathbf{E}\bigl[\partial(\mathcal{T}^{*})^{p}\bigr]
=\sum_{k\ge 1}\bigl(k^{p}-(k-1)^{p}\bigr)\,\mathbf{P}\bigl(\partial(\mathcal{T}^{*})\ge k\bigr).
\]

Let $(Z_1,Z_2)$ be standard bivariate normal with correlation $\rho \in [-1,1]$, and write $z_+=\max\{z,0\}$. Then $\mathbb{E}[(Z_1)_+(Z_2)_+] = \frac{1}{2\pi}\left(\sqrt{1-\rho^2}+(\pi-\arccos\rho)\,\rho\right)$. At $\rho=1$ this gives $\mathbb{E}[Z_+^2]=\tfrac12=\tfrac12\mathbb{E}[Z^2]$, and at $\rho=0$ it gives $\mathbb{E}[Z_+]^2=1/(2\pi)$. The normalized map $\rho \mapsto 2\pi\,\mathbb{E}[(Z_1)_+(Z_2)_+]/\pi$ has derivative $1$ at $\rho=1^-$, so the correlation dynamics it induces is marginal at perfect correlation. This is the degree-one arc-cosine kernel; sources defining that kernel often carry a compensating factor of two, so the constant should be checked against the convention in use rather than copied.
(Z_1,Z_2) is centered bivariate normal with unit variances and correlation rho

[Lemma 14 (Tail bounds are preserved under convergence in distribution) of arXiv:2604.04267, 'On Sharpest Tail Bounds for Functions \\ of Tail Bounded Random Variables'] Let \\ $(X^m)_{m \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of real r.v.'s (not necessarily neat) that converges to the real r.v.\ $X$ in distribution.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item If $f \in \mathcal{B}_R$ \eqref{BRTR} and $\forall m \in \mathbb{N}, \forall t \in \mathbb{R}, \ P(X^m \geq t) \leq f(t)$, then $$\forall t \in \mathbb{R}, \ P(X \geq t) \leq f(t)$$
\item If $f \in \mathcal{B}_L$ and $\forall m \in \mathbb{N}, \forall t \in \mathbb{R}, \ P(X^m \leq t) \leq f(t)$, then $$\forall t \in \mathbb{R}, \ P(X \leq t) \leq f(t)$$
\item If $f \in \mathcal{B}$ \eqref{absolutetails} and $\forall m \in \mathbb{N}, \forall t \geq 0, \ P(|X^m| \geq t) \leq f(t)$, then $$\forall t \geq 0, \ P(|X| \geq t) \leq f(t)$$
\item If $f=(f^-,f^+) \in \mathcal{B}_2$ \eqref{B2T2} and $\forall m \in \mathbb{N}, \forall t \geq 0, \ P(X^m \geq t) \leq f^+(t)$, also $\forall t \leq 0, P(X^m \leq t) \leq f^-(t)$, then $$\forall t \geq 0, P(X \geq t) \leq f^+(t) \text{ and } \forall t \leq 0, P(X \leq t) \leq f^-(t)$$
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Prop prop_parity of arXiv:2608.29914, 'Fixed points in abstract provability structures'] Let $S$ be an APS and let $\triangle v$ be a one-variable APS term. 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item If $d(\triangle)$ is even, then $\triangle v$ is an order-preserving operation on $L$. 
    That is, for any $x, y \in L$, $x \leq y$ implies $\triangle x \leq \triangle y$. 

    \item If $d(\triangle)$ is odd, then $\triangle v$ is an order-reversing operation on $L$. 
    That is, for any $x, y \in L$, $x \leq y$ implies $\triangle y \leq \triangle x$. 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: A partially ordered set (poset) is a pair (P, <=) where <= is a binary relation on P that is reflexive (x <= x), antisymmetric (x <= y and y <= x implies x = y), and transitive (x <= y and y <= z implies x <= z). A subset C of P is a chain if every two elements of C are comparable, that is, for all x, y in C, x <= y or y <= x. A subset A of P is an antichain if no two distinct elements of A are comparable. [standard, e.g. Stanley, Enumerative Combinatorics, Volume 1]
title: Partially Ordered Set, Chain, and Antichain

Own-work draft, proof (unaudited), no novelty claimed. Let X in R^(p-by-r) satisfy X^T X=I_r with p>r>=1, and let M be SPD r-by-r. On T_X St(p,r), set g_R(xi,xi)=tr(xi^T xi M). For any SPD p-by-p A, set g_A(xi,xi)=tr(xi^T A xi), and let c_A,C_A be the infimum and supremum of g_A/g_R over nonzero tangent vectors. Then C_A/c_A >= kappa(M), and equality is attained for every A=a I_p, a>0. Thus the optimal ambient-row metric distortion is exactly kappa(M); proportional representation on the entire tangent space is possible iff M is scalar. For p=r>=2 this obstruction disappears: A=X M X^T represents g_R exactly. This concerns metric comparison, not algorithmic iteration lower bounds or Gaussian LoRA convergence.
Real orthonormal p-by-r frame, p>r>=1 for distortion theorem
M SPD r-by-r; A SPD p-by-p, allowed to depend on X

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:a7083406f33c5a057a0bc3f88c5afe6fa80bf5d0c1c4eae070a3db5f9de683e0","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/a7/a7083406f33c5a057a0bc3f88c5afe6fa80bf5d0c1c4eae070a3db5f9de683e0.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:162562ad4878057f1e3c2d3f8f129b53522d4f66a642b4132d98a03923fdaec7","bundle_entry_key":"stiefel-metric-distortion","bundle_id":"population.t419-stiefel-optimal-metric-distortion-021","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Stiefel manifold metric comparison","draft":"w705/bundle_021.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.riemannian:stiefel-column-weight-ambient-row-optimal-metric-distortion","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T419-C035 v1: exact distortion of column-to-row metric transfer

Kind: route-failure. Target: 1. Status: proof (unaudited).
This is an auxiliary geometric obstruction, not a LoRA iteration lower bound,
new convergence regime, or claim of novelty. The hardest remaining piece is
a quantitative Gaussian entry time for the actual C029 dynamics.

Let X be a real p-by-r matrix with X^T X=I_r, where p>r>=1.
Let M be SPD r-by-r. At X the Stiefel tangent space is
T={xi: X^T xi+xi^T X=0}. Define

    g_R(xi,xi)=tr(xi^T xi M),
    g_A(xi,xi)=tr(xi^T A xi),

where A is any SPD p-by-p matrix. It may depend on X; the assertion is
pointwise. Let c_A and C_A be respectively the infimum and supremum of
g_A(xi,xi)/g_R(xi,xi) over nonzero xi in T. Both are positive and finite
by compactness of a unit sphere in this nonzero finite-dimensional space.
Write kappa(M)=lambda_max(M)/lambda_min(M).

**Theorem.** C_A/c_A >= kappa(M) for every A. Equality is attained by
every A=a I_p, a>0. Consequently the optimal distortion over ambient-row
SPD metrics is exactly kappa(M). A metric proportional to g_R can be
represented by an ambient-row SPD metric on the entire tangent space
if and only if M is scalar.

**Proof.** Since p>r there is a unit v with X^T v=0. For every nonzero
z in R^r, xi=v z^T is tangent, and direct multiplication gives

    g_A(xi,xi)/g_R(xi,xi)=(v^T A v) ||z||^2/(z^T M z).

Taking z to be unit eigenvectors for lambda_max(M) and lambda_min(M)
shows c_A <= (v^T A v)/lambda_max(M) and
C_A >= (v^T A v)/lambda_min(M). Their quotient is at least kappa(M).
For A=a I_p, the eigenvalue bounds on M imply that all tangent ratios
are between a/lambda_max(M) and a/lambda_min(M). The same two rank-one
directions attain the endpoints. This proves optimality. Proportionality
would give distortion one, forcing kappa(M)=1. Conversely if M=m I_r,
take A=m I_p to obtain equality of the two metrics. QED.

**Why the strict dimension hypothesis matters.** For p=r and r>=2,
X is orthogonal and tangent vectors have the form xi=X Omega with
Omega skew-symmetric. In this case A=X M X^T represents g_R exactly:

    g_A=tr(Omega^T M Omega)=tr(M Omega Omega^T),
    g_R=tr(Omega^T Omega M).

Since Omega Omega^T=Omega^T Omega, these quadratic forms agree, and
polarization gives agreement of their bilinear forms. Thus the proper
bottleneck hypothesis cannot be discarded. For p=r=1 the tangent space
is zero and a nonzero-vector distortion quotient is not defined.

**Application and limit.** C029's row-frame metric tr(dY^T M dY), after
X=Y^T, is g_R. Shustin--Avron's equation (3.10) (arXiv1902.01635v4,
PDF p9, as checked in C034) is of ambient-row form. For a proper
bottleneck, identifying these metrics without a condition-number loss
is impossible unless M is scalar. This statement concerns comparison
constants for metrics only. It does not imply a lower bound on the
iterations of any particular algorithm or exclude other transfers of
the primary source's techniques. Neither target is solved.

Sources: direct tangent-space and trace calculation above; C034 for the
primary source's metric convention. Independent audit and novelty
assessment remain pending.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:43f0988bc53898d9f4b11fcd2d5bb198784f611806a1e732e4c01e09a706dc01","revision_digest":"sha256:cc8d4366cc5fa1bb9aaef1012fe8034fc902315bfde051c4b67c12ab8bcf4053","source_id":"own-work:T419-C035:v1","source_revision":"v1-2026-10-20","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

Let 0 < alpha < 1 and let Omega in R^n be a bounded C^{2,alpha} domain. Let Lu = sum a^{ij}D_{ij}u + sum b^i D_i u + c u be strictly elliptic in Omega (sum a^{ij} xi_i xi_j >= lambda|xi|^2, lambda > 0) with a^{ij} = a^{ji} and all coefficients in C^{0,alpha}(closure of Omega) with norms at most Lambda. (a) A priori estimate: if u in C^{2,alpha}(closure of Omega) satisfies Lu = f in Omega and u = g on the boundary with f in C^{0,alpha}(closure of Omega) and g in C^{2,alpha}(closure of Omega), then ||u||_{C^{2,alpha}(closure of Omega)} <= C ( sup |u| + ||g||_{C^{2,alpha}} + ||f||_{C^{0,alpha}} ) with C = C(n, alpha, lambda, Lambda, Omega). (b) If moreover c <= 0 in Omega, then the Dirichlet problem Lu = f in Omega, u = g on the boundary, has exactly one solution u in C^{2,alpha}(closure of Omega), and the term sup|u| in (a) may be dropped, because the maximum principle gives sup |u| <= sup over the boundary of |g| + C(diam Omega, lambda, sup|b|) sup |f|.

[Prop 5 of arXiv:2604.02129, 'Realisation of constraints in underdamped Langevin dynamics'] Given $\eps>0$, let $(Q_t,P_t)$ be the solution to~\eqref{eq:abc-slow},\eqref{eq:intro-0Mass-Fast}, with corresponding initial data $(Q^i_0,P^i_0)$ for $i=1,2$. Recall the definition of the potential $V$ from~\eqref{eq:Valpha} and the parameter $\alpha\geq 0$. 
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item 
        For any $t\geq 0$ 
        \begin{align}
          
            \E\Bigl[|P_t^{1}|^2\Bigr] \leq 
            \begin{dcases} C_1 \bigl(\eps +  e^{-\frac{C_2}{\eps}t} |P_0^{1}|^2\bigr) \  &\text{if $\alpha=0$}, \\
            C_3 \left(\eps +\eps |Q^1_0|^2  + (e^{-\frac{C_4}{\eps}t} + \eps)  |P^1_0|^2    \right) &\text{if $\alpha>0$},
             \end{dcases}
        \end{align}
        where the constants $C_1, C_2, C_3, C_4>0$ are independent of $\eps$ and $t$.

        \item Let $(\hat q_t,q_t,p_t)\in \R^{k}\times \R^{d-k} \times \R^{d-k}$ with initial data $(\hat q_0,q_0,p_0)=(Q^1_0,Q^2_0,P^2_0)$  evolve according to~\eqref{eq:0Mass-q1} and~\eqref{eq:limit-gen}. 
        We have for any $t\leq 0$
        \begin{align}
        \E\biggl[\Bigl|(Q^{1}_t,Q^{2}_t,P^{2}_t)^\top - (\hat q_t,q_t,p_t)^\top\Bigr|^2\biggr] \leq \begin{dcases}C_5 e^{C_6 t^2}\Bigl(\eps + 
        \bigl|P_0^{1}\bigr|^2  \Bigr) \ &\text{if $\alpha=0$}, \\
        C_7 e^{C_8 t^2}\Bigl(\eps t^2+\eps^2 t^2 \bigl|Q_0^{1}\bigr|^2 + |P^1_0|^2\Bigr)  &\text{if $\alpha>0$},
        \end{dcases}
        \end{align}
        where the constants $C_5,C_6, C_7,C_8>0$ are independent of $\eps>0$ and $t>0$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 5 of arXiv:2604.02129

body: Theorem (campaign status: audited-pass): For a rank-r, size-k = r+j component, the ternary basis-mass encoding has exponent -(n-r)*ell + O(d_cb*k + j*log r + r + n) (tag 29). Substituting Theorem 2 gives -(n-r)*ell + O((4^ell + ell)*k + j*log r + r + n) (tag 30). Notes: This is the exact interface at which a deterministic d_cb bound becomes a probabilistic component saving; the coefficient on d_cb is k (component size), which is why an o(log n) coefficient suffices at the endpoint.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Invariant monotone coupling under an amenable action Result: Start with a monotone coupling of the two invariant forest laws under a countable amenable action. Average its translates over a Folner sequence. The product space of two edge configurations is compact, the prescribed marginals are unchanged, and the order relation is closed. A subsequential weak limit is therefore still a monotone coupling and is invariant because translation changes each average by at most its Folner boundary ratio. Check: The argument averages probability measures, not individual configurations, so convexity preserves the marginals and the monotone support. Compactness is available for a countable locally finite edge set. Obstruction: For a nonamenable acting group there is no Folner averaging sequence. Existence of an arbitrary monotone coupling does not by itself produce an invariant one.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0044-invariant-monotone-coupling-of-free-and-wired-uniform-spanning-forests
No independent review

[Lem 1d-uncovered-tails of arXiv:2411.14336, 'Finding the root in random nearest neighbor trees'] For a $1$-NN tree with $K + 1$ uncovered vertices, the size of the remaining uncovered interval $L_{K+1}$ satisfies 
    \[-\log L_{K+1} \overset{d}{=} \sum_{j=1}^{K} E_j,\]
    where $E_j$ are i.i.d.\ truncated exponential $\mathrm{TEXP}(1,\log 2)$ random variables, i.e., $E_j = \Tilde{E_j}\ind{\Tilde{E_j} \leq \log 2}$ for i.i.d.\ $\Tilde{E_j} \sim \mathrm{Exp}(1)$.

body:
[Thm large-deviations-time-constant of arXiv:2606.01627, 'The geometry of the giant component of random geometric graphs'] Fix $\lambda > \lambda_c(d)$.   Let $G^\lambda = G^{\lambda}_{\mathbb{R}^d}(1)$ and let  $d_\lambda$ denote the graph distance
        on $G^{\lambda}$. Then, for any $\xi > 0$ there exists 
        $c(\lambda,\xi,d)>0$ such that for all $x,y \in \mathbb{R}^d$ we have
        \[
            \mathbb{P}_{x,y}\left( x \xleftrightarrow{G^{\lambda}} y,
            \frac{d_\lambda(x,y)}{\mu(\lambda)\|x - y\|}
            \notin [e^{-\xi}, e^\xi] 
            \right)
            \le \exp(-c\|x - y\|).
        \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lemm:derniersaut of arXiv:2606.24793, '\LARGE Random sequential nearest-neighbor coloring on trees'] Let $v\in \mathcal{T}$. We have
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)]  If $\tilde{\Gamma}(v)$ is finite, then for $\ell$ large enough, 
    $$\tilde{\Gamma}^{(\ell)}(v)=\tilde{\Gamma}(v).$$
    \item[(ii)]  If $\tilde{\Gamma}(v)$ is infinite, then, for any vertex $w\in \mathop{dir} \tilde{\Gamma}(v)$ and for all $\ell$ large enough, the penultimate vertex of $\tilde{\Gamma}^{(\ell)}(v)$ is in $\mathcal{T}_w$, \emph{i.e.},
    $$\tilde{V}^{(\ell)}_{n_\ell(v)-1}\in \mathcal{T}_w.$$
\end{itemize}

Let n>=2, alpha in (0,1], and A be an n x n symmetric random matrix with A_ii=0 and mutually independent upper-triangular entries A_ij~Bernoulli(p_ij). Set P=E A. Suppose p_ij<=alpha and there exist 0<nbar_min<=nbar_max such that alpha nbar_min<=sum_j p_ij<=alpha nbar_max for every i. Write mu=nbar_max/nbar_min. For a nonnegative symmetric matrix B define L(B)=D(B)^(-1/2) B D(B)^(-1/2), where D(B)_ii=sum_j B_ij and inverse square roots at zero degrees are zero. For every nu>0 there exist constants C_nu,Cprime_nu depending only on nu such that, if alpha>=Cprime_nu mu log(n)/nbar_min, then P(||L(A)-L(P)||_op <= C_nu mu sqrt(n)/(nbar_min sqrt(alpha)))>=1-n^(-nu). This normalized matrix is adjacency normalization, not I minus the normalized adjacency. The constants do not give convergence for a general bounded-degree static graph sequence.

p_ij<=alpha; every expected degree lies between alpha nbar_min and alpha nbar_max
mu=nbar_max/nbar_min; logarithmic sparsity condition with constants depending on nu
normalized adjacency convention; inverse square root is zero at zero degrees

In the multi-season stochastic epidemic framework of Britton and Pugliese, successive epidemic seasons k = 1, 2, ... are driven by an independent and identically distributed sequence of bivariate random vectors (delta_k, tau_k) with joint probability density q(delta, tau) supported on [0, 1] x [0, infinity). The component delta_k in [0, 1] represents seasonal random genetic drift reducing homologous antibody immunity by 1 - delta_k, while tau_k >= 0 represents seasonal transmissibility governing the baseline reproduction number R_0^{(k)} = tau_k.
Sequence of pairs (delta_k, tau_k) is i.i.d.
delta_k in [0, 1] and tau_k >= 0
title: Seasonal Epidemic Genetic Drift and Transmissibility Distribution

DRAFT AUTHOR MODEL CHECK; independent review pending. In the simple C_2*C_3 triangle graph with one a-edge per unordered pair, the forward branching mean is 2p^2+2p^3-2p^4. Replacing every a-edge by two independent parallel Bernoulli(p) bonds changes its connection probability to 2p-p^2 and the branching mean to 4p^2+2p^3-6p^4+2p^5. Its critical equation is 2p^5-6p^4+2p^3+4p^2-1=0, with root in (0.51,0.53), rather than the simple-graph root in (0.63,0.64). These polynomials are checked by 32 and 128 exact local configurations respectively. Kozakova 2008 reports the latter polynomial with Cayley edge multiplicity; that published number must not be transplanted into the simple graph at the same p.
Independent bond model, not site percolation
Parallel bonds are distinct random variables
Published-model interpretation is identified as an inference in MODEL_CONVENTIONS.md

[Lemma 6 (Finite-chaos Stein estimate) of arXiv:2608.12492, 'Weak Limits of Wiener Chaos: Primitive--Fock Classification and Hilbert--Stein Extraction'] Fix positive integers $q_1,\ldots,q_d$.  Let
$F_{n,a}=I_{q_a}^{(n)}(f_{n,a})$, assume that the kernels are bounded,
and let $C_n=\Cov(F_n)$.  Put
\[
 \Gamma_{n,ab}
 =\ip{DF_{n,a}}{-DL^{-1}F_{n,b}}_{H_n}.
\]
There is a constant $c=c(q_1,\ldots,q_d)<\infty$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{a,b=1}^d
 \norm{\Gamma_{n,ab}-C_{n,ab}}_2^2
 \le c\sum_{a,b=1}^d
 \sum_{\substack{1\le r\le q_a\wedge q_b\\
 (r,q_a,q_b)\ne(q_a,q_a,q_a)}}
 \norm{f_{n,a}\otimes_rf_{n,b}}^2.
 
\end{equation}
Moreover, if $Z_n\sim N_d(0,C_n)$, then for every $t\in\R^d$,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\E e^{it\cdot F_n}-\E e^{it\cdot Z_n}\right|
 \le\frac{|t|^2}{2}
 \left(
 \sum_{a,b=1}^d
 \norm{\Gamma_{n,ab}-C_{n,ab}}_2^2
 \right)^{1/2}.
 
\end{equation}

[Lemma le:mono-init of arXiv:2604.21142, 'Gaussian fluctuations for Internal DLA on cylinders'] Let $\mathcal{B}_1 \subseteq \mathcal{B}_2 \subsetneq V_N \times {\ensuremath{\mathbb Z}} $ be two proper subsets of the cylinder, and let $\o = (\o_1, \o_2, \ldots)$ be a sequence of infinite cylinder walks with prescribed starting sites. Assume that for each $i \in \{1, 2\}$ and each $k \geq 0$, the first exit time of $\o_{k+1}$ from $\Phi_k(\mathcal{B}_i)$ is almost surely finite. Then
\[
  \Phi_k(\mathcal{B}_1) \;\subseteq\; \Phi_k(\mathcal{B}_2) \qquad \text{for every } k \geq 0\,.
\]

[Lem localconcentration of arXiv:2412.00593, 'A new approach to strong convergence II.\\The classical ensembles'] Let $Z\sim N(0, \mathbf{1}_d)$ be a 
$d$-dimensional
standard Gaussian vector. 
Let $\Omega\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a measurable set with 
$\mathbf{P}[Z\in \Omega] \geq \frac{3}{4}$, and let $f: \mathbb{R}^{d}\to \mathbb{R}$ be a
function whose restriction to $\Omega$ is $L$-Lipschitz.
Then
$$
	\mathbf{P}[|f(Z)-\mathrm{med}(f(Z))| > \varepsilon] 
	\leq \mathbf{P}[Z\notin \Omega] + C e^{-c \varepsilon^2/L^2}
$$
for any $\varepsilon>0$, where $C, c>0$ are universal constants.

[Proposition 28 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] The two estimates on which the critical compactness argument rests are the following.

\textup{(i)} Let $\phi_0>0$ be the normalized local Dirichlet principal eigenfunction. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\sigma_\varepsilon>0$ such that
\[
\cA_{\sigma,2,L}\phi_0+(\lambda_0+\varepsilon)\phi_0\ge0\;\hbox{in }(-L,L)
\]
for $0<\sigma<\sigma_\varepsilon$. Consequently $\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,2,L})\le\lambda_0+\varepsilon$.

\textup{(ii)} There exist constants $c_J,C_J>0$ such that
\[
c_J\min\{\eta^2,1\}\le1-\widehat J(\eta)\le C_J\min\{\eta^2,1\}\;\hbox{for all }\eta\in\R.
\]
Consequently, if $\sigma_n\to0$ and $u_n$ are supported in a fixed bounded interval with $\|u_n\|_2\le C$ and $E_{\sigma_n}(u_n)\le C$, then a subsequence converges strongly in $L^2(\R)$ to a function in $H^1(\R)$ supported in the same interval. The estimate is proved directly below from the Fourier symbol. In particular, the proof does not invoke the Sobolev-norm approximation/characterization theorems of \cite{BBM,Brezis02,PonceCV,Ponce}; retaining the zero-extension support is essential for recovering the missing inflow boundary condition in the advective problem.
For every such strongly convergent subsequence, with limit $u$, one also has the sharp lower-semicontinuity estimate
\[
d_J\int_\R |u'(x)|^2\,dx\le \liminf_{n\to\infty}E_{\sigma_n}(u_n).
\]

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2609.00988, 'Covering Projective Height Balls by Subspaces in Rigid Adelic Spaces'] Let $C_2$ be the constant in Lemma~\ref{lem:representatives}.  There are
constants $0<c_8<1$ and $C_8\ge2$, effectively computable from $n, d, r_2, |D_K|, R_K$, with the following property.  Let $F$ be
an $n$-dimensional rigid adelic space over $K$, and write
\[
\lambda_i=\Lambda_i(F),
\qquad
R_i=\frac{1}{8nC_2\lambda_i}
\qquad(1\le i\le n).
\]
If $\mathfrak p\subset\cO_K$ is a nonzero prime ideal, $q=\Nm\mathfrak p$, and
\[
\lambda_n\le c_8,
\qquad
C_8\le q\le c_8\Psi_F(1)^d,
\]
then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $R_i\ge1$ for every $1\le i\le n$;
\item[(ii)] if, for each $1\le i\le n$, the set $S_i=S(R_i,\mathfrak p)$ is chosen as in Lemma~\ref{lem:residue}, then
\[
\prod_{i=1}^n|S_i|>q^{n-1}.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 9 of arXiv:2609.00988

[Lem 62 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For all $q_0 \in [0,1)$, we have $\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,q_0) \subseteq \sM^{\BOGP}(\alpha,q_0)$.
\begin{proof}
    This is a consequence of Theorem~\ref{thm:BOGP-hardness-main}.
    Consider any $\mu \in \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon)$, where $L$ is sufficiently large depending on $\alpha,q_0,\epsilon$. Recalling \eqref{e:cM.Lip.q0}, this means there exists a sequence of $L$-Lipschitz algorithms $(\cA_j)^\circ$ (acting in $N_j$ dimensions) such that
    \begin{align} \nonumber 
    &\WERR( (\cA_j)^\circ,\mu)
 \le \epsilon\,,\\
        
   &     q_0(j)
        \equiv \chi_{ (\cA_j)^\circ}(0)
         \stackrel{j\to\infty}{\longrightarrow} q_0\,.
    \end{align}
    Let $(\cA_j)_{j\ge 1}$ be the perturbations of the $( (\cA_j)^\circ)_{j\ge 1}$ given by Proposition~\ref{p:wlogable}, which are also $L$-Lipschitz.
    Proposition~\ref{p:wlogable} further yields
    \[
        \frac{1}{N} \bbE \Big[\| (\cA_j)^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) 
        	- \cA_j(\bG,\bg^{\aux})\|^2\Big]
        \le \frac{2}{(1-q_0(j))L^2}\,.
    \]
Thus Lemma~\ref{l:control.problems.approx} implies that for $c_0$, $C_1(\alpha)$ and $C_2(\alpha,L)$ given therein,
	\[
	\WERR(\cA_j,(\cA_j)^\circ)
	\le 
	\bigg\{
        C_1(\alpha) \cdot \frac{2}{(1-q_0(j))L^2} + C_2(\alpha,L) e^{-c_0N_j}
        \bigg\}^{1/2} 
        \le \epsilon \]
    where the last inequality holds if $L$ is sufficiently large depending on $\alpha,q_0,\epsilon$ (consistent with our assumptions), and $j$ sufficiently large depending on $q_0,\epsilon,L$. Hence, by omitting finitely many $j$, we can assume it holds for all $j$ that
    \beq
        
        \WERR(\cA_j,\mu)=
        \max\bigg\{
            \bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_j), \mu\Big),
            \bbW_2\Big(\mu^{\Ising}(\cA_j), \cP(\{\pm 1\})\Big)
        \bigg\}
        \le 2\epsilon\,,
    \eeq
By passing to a further subsequence of the $j$'s, we can assume that for all $j$ we have 
    \[
         \max\bigg\{
            \bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_j), \mu\Big),
            \bbW_2\Big(\mu^{\Ising}(\cA_j), \mu^\Ising\Big)
        \bigg\}
         \le 3\epsilon
    \]
for some fixed $\mu^\Ising \in \cP(\{\pm 1\})$.
    By passing to a further subsequence, we can assume (as in Theorem~\ref{thm:BOGP-hardness-main}) that $\chi_{\cA_j}$ converges to a limiting function $\chi$, both pointwise and in $L^1$.
    Since Proposition~\ref{p:wlogable} ensures 
    \[
        \chi_{\cA_j}(0) = \chi_{\cA^\circ_j}(0) = q_0(j)\,,
    \]
    by \eqref{e:Lip.in.BOGP.q0.limit} we have $\chi(0) = q_0$.

We now apply Theorem~\ref{thm:BOGP-hardness-main} to the sequence $(\cA_j)_{j\ge 1}$ where, treating $\epsilon$ as a function of $L$ tending to $0$ sufficiently slowly, the hypothesis \eqref{e:BOGP-hardness-main-hypothesis} holds by \eqref{e:Lip.in.BOGP.hardness.hypothesis}.
    Then, for some $\tilde\epsilon = \tilde\epsilon(\epsilon)$ tending to $0$ sufficiently slowly as $\epsilon\rightarrow 0$, Theorem~\ref{thm:BOGP-hardness-main} provides controls $(q_*,b,\sigma,w,p\equiv \chi^{-1},\zeta,\zeta^\Ising)$ satisfying the conclusions of that theorem, where all $o_L(1)$ error terms are replaced by $\tilde\epsilon$. We assume without loss that $\tilde{\epsilon}\le1$. 
    We will now verify that for $C(L)$ given by Theorem~\ref{thm:BOGP-hardness-main},
    \beq
        
         (q_*,b,\sigma,w,p\equiv \chi^{-1},\zeta,\zeta^\Ising) 
         \in \Adm^{\BOGP}\Big(
         \alpha,q_0;
         \tilde C = \max\{C(L),L^2\}, \tilde\epsilon 
         \Big)\,.
    \eeq
    Indeed, we verify each of the conditions from Definition~\ref{d:SDE.classification} specifying the $\Adm^{\BOGP}$ class:
    \begin{itemize}
\item Theorem~\ref{thm:BOGP-hardness-main}\ref{it:BOGP-hardness-main-Lip}
    implies condition~\ref{it:1.1bogp};

\item Theorem~\ref{thm:BOGP-hardness-main}\ref{it:BOGP-hardness-main-diffusivity}
    implies condition~\ref{it:2.1}; 

\item We have $p(q_0) = 0$ because we defined $\chi(0) = q_0$. 
        Theorem~\ref{thm:BOGP-hardness-main} asserts $p(q_*) \le \tilde\epsilo (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: A graph is bipartite if its vertices split into two parts X and Y with every edge joining X to Y - equivalently, it contains no odd cycle (Konig). A matching is a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges; it saturates a set S if every vertex of S is an endpoint of a matching edge, and it is perfect if it saturates every vertex. In a bipartite graph, Hall's marriage condition - |N(S)| >= |S| for every subset S of X, where N(S) is the neighborhood - is exactly the condition under which X can be saturated by a matching.
title: Bipartite Graph and Matching

body: In the mathematical discipline of graph theory, Menger's theorem says that in a finite graph, the size of a minimum cut set is equal to the maximum number of disjoint paths that can be found between any pair of vertices. Proved by Karl Menger in 1927, it characterizes the connectivity of a graph. It is generalized by the max-flow min-cut theorem, which is a weighted, edge version, and which in turn is a special case of the strong duality theorem for linear programs.
title: Menger's theorem

[Problem Average-energy Gaussian codes of arXiv:2607.14087, 'Stochastic Domination of Gaussian Maxima: A Resolution of the Weak Simplex Conjecture'] \label[problem]{prob:average-energy}
For fixed $M$, ambient dimension, noise level, and average-energy budget $E$,
maximize the average probability of correct decoding over equiprobable
Gaussian codebooks satisfying
\[
  \frac1M\sum_{i=1}^M\lVert c_i\rVert^2\leq E.
\]
Characterize the optimizers as a function of the signal-to-noise ratio.  Can an
optimizer always be chosen from a family consisting of a lower-dimensional
regular simplex together with coincident zero signals, or are additional
geometries unavoidable? (Stated as a problem by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Average-energy Gaussian codes

\[

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2607.18070, 'The Brownian loop-catcher'] For every \(0<\lambda\le 1\) (i.e.~\(-2\le c<0\)), there is a
unique probability law on compact connected sets
\(K\subset\overline D\) with
\(K\cap\partial D=\{a,b\}\) such that
\begin{equation}
        \mathbb{E}\left[\mathbf 1_{\{K\cap A=\varnothing\}}
        \exp\left\{-\lambda m_D(K,A)\right\}\right]
        =\mathbb P\left[\gamma_{\mathrm{BE}}^{D;a,b}\cap A=\varnothing\right],
\end{equation}
for every compact \(A\subset\overline D\) such that $A\cap\{a,b\}=\varnothing$ (with no requirement that \(A\) attach to \(\partial D\)).

For \(\lambda>1\) (i.e.~\(c<-2\)), no probability law on compact
connected sets satisfies~(equation eq:intro-main-id of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def: Berger_good_box_definition of arXiv:2608.00399, 'The Heavy-tailed Frog Model'] Let $Q$ be a $k$-block

    \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}, leftmargin=2.2em, itemsep=2pt]
    \item A $0$-block $Q$ is \textbf{good} if there is no directed edge $(u,w)$ with
    $u,w\in Q$ and $|u-w|>A_0/100$.

    \item For $k\ge1$, a $k$-block $Q$ is \textbf{good} if the following hold:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}, leftmargin=2.2em, itemsep=2pt]
    \item there is no directed edge $(u,w)$ with
    $u,w\in Q$ and $|u-w|>A_{k-1}/100$;
    \item among the $(k{-}1)$-blocks (children) of $Q$,
    all but at most one are good;
    \item for every
    $v\in\{0,\pm A_{k-1}/2\}^d$, the shifted inner block $Q^{\mathrm{int}}+v$
    also satisfies \textup{(b)} (i.e., among its $(k{-}1)$-subblocks, all but at most
    one are good).
    \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}
title: Good blocks

body:
[Lem 198 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $\cA$ be an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm, and let $\bx(q_d)$ be as defined by
\eqref{e:x.q.mean}. Then
    \[
    \P\bigg(\bigg|
    \frac{(\bx(q_d),\bx(q_\ell))}{N}-q_{\min\{d,\ell\}}
    \bigg|\ge
    \frac{1}{N^{1/3}}\bigg) 
    \le \exp(-N^{0.1})\,.
    \]

\begin{proof}
This follows easily from gaussian Lipschitz concentration (see e.g.\ Lemma~\ref{l:lip.subgaus}).
Indeed note that $\|\cA(\bG,  \bg^\aux)\|_2\leq N^{1/2}$ almost surely, while by definition $\bx(q_d)$
is an $L$-Lipschitz function of the gaussian vector $(\bG(q_d),\bg^\aux(q_d))$. It follows that for $\ell \le d$, the normalized inner product
    \[\frac{(\bx(q_d),\bx(q_\ell))}{N}\]
is an 
 $O(LN^{-1/2})$-Lipschitz function of 
    \[\Big(\bG(q_\ell),
    \bg^\aux(q_\ell),
    \bG(q_d) - \bG(q_\ell),\bg^\aux(q_d) - \bg^\aux(q_\ell)\Big)\,.\]
 Therefore it concentrates around its mean by Lemma~\ref{l:lip.subgaus}, which gives the conclusion.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 198 of arXiv:2608.29416

[Lemma 4 (Absolute Fourier estimate) of arXiv:2609.01413, 'Sharp Threshold for Universality of Rational Canonical Forms over a Finite Field'] Fix a positive integer $m$ and a constant $c>1$, and put
    $$
    \beta_n:=\frac{c\log n}{n}.
    $$
    Let $V$ be an $m$-dimensional $\F_p$-vector space, and let
    $\mu_{ij}$, $1\leq i,j\leq n$, be arbitrary
    $\beta_n$-balanced probability measures on $\F_p$. Fix a nontrivial
    additive character
    $$
    \psi:\F_p\longrightarrow\C^\times,
    $$
    and write
    $$
    \widehat{\mu}_{ij}(u)
    :=
    \sum_{a\in\F_p}\mu_{ij}(a)\psi(ua),
    \qquad
    u\in\F_p.
    $$
    Then
    \begin{align}
        
        &p^{-mn}
        \sum_{\substack{g_1,\ldots,g_n\in V\\
        \Span_{\F_p}\{g_1,\ldots,g_n\}=V}}
        \ \sum_{\substack{h_1,\ldots,h_n\in V^\vee\\
        (h_1,\ldots,h_n)\neq(0,\ldots,0)}}
        \prod_{i,j=1}^n
        \left|
        \widehat{\mu}_{ij}\bigl(h_j(g_i)\bigr)
        \right|
        =
        o(1),
    \end{align}
    where the estimate is uniform over the choices of
    $\mu_{ij}$.

[Lemma stability of arXiv:2603.15323, '\Large \bf Small-time heat decay for stable processes on fractal drums'] {[vB87]}
Let $D$ be a bounded $C^{1,1}$ open set in ${\mathbb R}^{d}$ with characteristic $(R_0, \Lambda_0)$ and define for $0\leq q <R_{0}$,
$$
D_{q}=\{x\in D : \delta_{D}(x)>q\}.
$$
Then
$$
\left(\frac{R_{0}-q}{R_{0}}\right)^{d-1}|\partial D|\leq |\partial D_{q}| \leq \left(\frac{R_{0}}{R_{0}-q}\right)^{d-1}|\partial D|,
\quad 0\leq q < R_{0}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition Wigner Matrix of arXiv:2411.11341, 'Ultra high order cumulants and quantitative CLT for polynomials in Random Matrices'] By a Wigner matrix $X\equiv X(N)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}(x_{i,j})\in \mathbb{C}^{N\times N}$ we mean a self-adjoint random matrix, i.e., $x_{i,j}=\overline{x_{j,i}}$, with independent (up to symmetry) entries which satisfy the moment conditions $\mathbb{E}x_{i,j}=0$ for all $i,j$ and $\mathbb{E}|x_{i,j}|^2=1$ for $i\neq j$. We further make the following assumptions. 

\begin{itemize}

 

\item[$\diamond$]
the entries above the diagonal, $\{x_{i,j}\}_{i<j}$, are
identically distributed as a complex random variable $x_o$ whose odd  cumulants are all $0$, that is, $K_{2n+1}(x_o^{\epsilon_1},\dots,x_o^{\epsilon_{2n+1}})=0$ for any $\epsilon_i\in \{1,-1\}$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Here $x_o^{1}=x_o$ while $x_o^{-1}=\overline{x_o}$ means its conjugate. We further assume $x_o\stackrel{d}= \overline{x_o}$. 

\item[$\diamond$] 
the diagonal entries, $\{x_{i,i}\}_{i}$, are identically
distributed as a real random variable $x_d$ whose odd cumulants are all $0$, that is, $K_{2n+1}(x_d)=0$ for any $n\in\mathbb{N}$;

\item[$\diamond$] For any $r$, any $i,j$ and $\epsilon_i\in \{1,-1\}$, 
$|K_r(x_{i,j}^{\epsilon_1},\dots,x_{i,j}^{\epsilon_r})|\leq \mathsf{C}^rr!$ for some constant $\mathsf{C}>0$. 

\end{itemize}
We call a Wigner matrix a  GUE if its off-diagonal entries are $\mathbb{C}\mathcal{N}(0, N^{-1})$ and the diagonal entries are $\mathcal{N}(0, N^{-1})$. We call a Wigner matrix a GOE if its off-diagonal entries are $\mathcal{N}(0, N^{-1})$ and the diagonal entries are $\mathcal{N}(0, 2N^{-1})$.

[Defi def:skew_gt_patterns of arXiv:2412.05999, 'Non-Archimedean GUE corners and Hecke modules'] For $\mu \in \Sig_n, \lambda \in \Sig_{n+k}$, we define $\GT_P(\lambda/\mu)$ to be the set of sequences of interlacing signatures $\mu = \lambda^{(0)} \prec_P \lambda^{(1)} \prec_P \cdots \prec_P \lambda^{(k)}= \lambda$. 

For $\lambda,\nu \in \Sig_n$, we define $\GT_{Q,k}(\lambda/\nu)$ to be the set of sequences of length $n$ interlacing signatures $\nu = \lambda^{(0)} \prec_Q \lambda^{(1)} \prec_Q \cdots \prec_Q \lambda^{(k)}=\lambda$. We refer to elements of either $\GT_P$ or $\GT_{Q,k}$ as \emph{Gelfand-Tsetlin patterns}.

For $T \in \GT_P(\lambda/\mu)$ with $\len(\lambda) = \len(\mu)+k$, set $\psi(T) := \prod_{i=1}^{k} \psi_{\lambda^{(i)}/\lambda^{(i-1)}}$. For $T \in \GT_{Q,k}(\lambda/\nu)$, set $\varphi(T) := \prod_{i=1}^{k} \varphi_{\lambda^{(i)}/\lambda^{(i-1)}}$. In both cases, let $wt(T) := (|\lambda^{(1)}|-|\lambda^{(0)}|,\ldots,|\lambda^{(k)}|-|\lambda^{(k-1)}|) \in \mathbb{Z}^k$.
title: Defi def:skew_gt_patterns of arXiv:2412.05999

body:
[Lemma forward estimate of arXiv:2605.03151, 'Giants through Higher-Order paths in Random Simplicial Complexes'] Let $k \geq 0$ and let $v$ be a vertex that can create a forward $d$-dimensional simplex with a $(d-1)$-simplex $\sigma_k$ that is being explored at Step $k$. Then, given $\mathcal{X}_{k-1}$, the probability that $\sigma_k \cup \{v\}$ appears at Step $k$ is lower bounded by
\[  \tag{3.2.3}
p_k^F := \left( 1 - (k-1) \frac{\lambda}{n} - \sum_{\ell = 1}^{d-1} \sum_{\rho \subseteq \sigma_k, \dim(\rho) = \ell-1} \deg_{\ell-1, d-1}^{\mathcal{X}_{k-1}} (\rho)  p_{d, \ell}  \right) \left( \frac{\lambda}{n} + o(1) \right).
\]
In particular, if the given MRSC model is the Linial-Meshulam model, the probability is exactly $\lambda/n + o(1)$.
title: Lemma forward estimate of arXiv:2605.03151

body: [Definition \cite{KMSVV99} of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] We say that $X \in_R \mathbb{R}^d$ is \emph{variance symmetrization resistant} with constant $c>0$ when every $f_Y \in \Sym(X)$ satisfies $\Var(f_Y) \ge c\Var(f_X)$.
title: \cite{KMSVV99}

[Lemma lem:BR_Hilbert of arXiv:2601.08184, 'Wasserstein-p Central Limit Theorem Rates: From Local Dependence to Markov Chains'] Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) be a probability space equipped with a
filtration \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge 0}\). Let \(H\) be a real separable Hilbert
space with norm \(\|\cdot\|\). Let \((d_k)_{k\ge 1}\) be an \(H\)-valued
martingale difference sequence, i.e., for each \(k\ge 1\),
\(d_k\) is \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, \(\mathbb{E}\|d_k\|<\infty\), and
\[
\mathbb{E}[d_k\mid \mathcal F_{k-1}]=0
\qquad \text{a.s.}
\]
Define
\[
M_n:=\sum_{k=1}^n d_k,\qquad n\ge 1,
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
M_0:=0.
\]
Then, for every \(p\ge 2\), there exists a constant \(C_p\in(0,\infty)\),
depending only on \(p\), such that for all integers \(n\ge 1\),
\[
\mathbb{E}\|M_n\|^p
\le
C_p\left\{
\mathbb{E}\Bigl(\sum_{k=1}^n \mathbb{E}[\|d_k\|^2\mid \mathcal F_{k-1}]\Bigr)^{p/2}
+
\mathbb{E}\sum_{k=1}^n \|d_k\|^p
\right\}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem~4.1 in \cite{pinelis1994optimum}

body: [Lem 53 of arXiv:2606.13459, 'Symmetric Cooperative Motion in Higher Dimensions'] Suppose $\x, m \in \mathbb Z^d$ and $|\x_i| \le m_i$ with $\sum_{i=1}^{d} m_i = n-2$. Let $\lapconst := (8d^4)^{-1}$. If $2 \le n \le \lapconst|\x|^2$, then $${n(n-1) \over d^3} \sum_{i=1}^{d} {1 \over ((m_i+2)^2 - \x_i^2)} \ge 1 + {1 \over n}.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem th:InfiniteVol-PhaseTrans of arXiv:2601.05798, '{I}mry-{M}a phenomenon for the hard-core model on $\mathbb{Z}^{2}$'] Consider the hard-core model
	on ${\mathbb{Z}}^2$ with activity field $\boldsymbol{\lambda}$,
	$0\le \lambda_v<\infty$ for all $v$.
	The even and odd infinite-volume measures
	are well-defined as the (unique) local weak limits of finite-volume measures along any exhausting sequence $\Lambda \uparrow {\mathbb{Z}}^2$:
	\begin{equation}
		\mu_{{\mathbb{Z}}^2,\boldsymbol{\lambda}}^{e} = \lim_{\Lambda \uparrow {\mathbb{Z}}^2} \mu_{\Lambda, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}^{e} \,, \quad \quad
		\mu_{{\mathbb{Z}}^2,\boldsymbol{\lambda}}^{o} = \lim_{\Lambda \uparrow {\mathbb{Z}}^2} \mu_{\Lambda, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}^{o}. \vspace{-.2cm}
	\end{equation}
	Furthermore,
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item[(i)]
		      If $\mu_{{\mathbb{Z}}^2, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}^{o}(v\in I) = \mu_{{\mathbb{Z}}^2, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}^{e}(v\in I)$ for every $v\in {\mathbb{Z}}^2$, then $\mathcal{G}_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}(\mathbb{Z}^2)$ is a singleton set.
		\item[(ii)] For any site $v \in {\mathbb{Z}}^2$, $
			      \mu_{{\mathbb{Z}}^2, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}^{e}(v \in I) - \mu_{{\mathbb{Z}}^2, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}^{o}(v \in I)\ge 0$ if $v$ is even and $\le 0$ if $v$ is odd.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem th:InfiniteVol-PhaseTrans of arXiv:2601.05798

D_\ell[R_{\ell+1},P_\ell]D_\ell
\bigr],
\\
T_\ell^{\mathrm{gate}}
&:=
\mathbb E_\mu
\bigl[
[D_\ell,P_\ell]S_{\ell+1}D_\ell

\end{align}

=T_\ell^{\mathrm{tr}}
+T_\ell^{\mathrm{imb}}
+T_\ell^{\mathrm{fluc}}
+T_\ell^{\mathrm{gate}}.
\end{equation}

[Lemma 13 of arXiv:2506.13347, 'Ergodic theorem for the differential equations with interaction'] Assume that for equation with Lipschitz coefficient $a: \mathbb{R} \times \mathfrak M_{0} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$,
$$
\left\{\begin{array}{l}
x\left(u,t\right)=a\left(x(u, t), \mu_{t}\right) d t \\
x(u, 0)=u \in \mathbb{R}, \\
\mu_{t}=\mu_{0} \circ x(\cdot, t)^{-1}
\end{array}\right.
$$
there exists a set $A$ of invariant initial measures,
that is $A=\left\{\mu \in \mathfrak M_{0}: \Phi_{t}(\mu)=\mu, \ t \geq 0\right\}$.
Then the measure $\varkappa$ on $\mathfrak M_{0}$ of the form
$$
\varkappa=\sum_{k=1}^{N} \delta \mu_{k} \cdot p_{k}, \quad \mu_{k} \in A
$$
is invariant with respect to $\Phi_{t}$ :
$$
\varkappa \circ \Phi_{t}^{-1}=\varkappa .
$$

[Lem 17 of arXiv:2605.23659, '2605.23659'] Let \(x_n,y_n,x,y\in D([0,\infty),\bR)\).
Assume the following:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \(x_n\to x\) on \(D([0,\infty),\bR)\) as \(n\to\infty\),
  \item \(y_n\) and \(y\) are non-decreasing, with
  \[
  y(0)=0,
  \quad
  y_n(\infty)=y(\infty)=\infty,
  \]
  \item \(y\) is strictly increasing,
  \item there exists a dense subset \(D\subset[0,\infty)\) such that
  \[
  y_n(u)\to y(u)
  \quad (n\to\infty)
  \]
  for every \(u\in D\).
\end{enumerate}
Then, for every \(t\ge0\) such that \(x\) is continuous at \(y^{-1}(t)\), we have
\begin{align}
x_n(y_n^{-1}(t))\longrightarrow x(y^{-1}(t))
\quad (n\to\infty),

\end{align}
where \(y_n^{-1}\) and \(y^{-1}\) denote the right-continuous inverses. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

viscosity supersolution
\[

\]
of the PIDE \eqref{eq:bubble-pide}.

[Lemma 27 (KMS small-particle lemma in discrete time) of arXiv:2607.13183, '2607.13183'] Let $Q$ be a finite irreducible reversible transition kernel on $N\ge2$ states
with stationary law $\pi$, and assume $Q(x,x)\ge1/2$ for all states. Let
$t_{\rm meet}^Q$ be the worst-case expected meeting time of two independent
synchronous $Q$-walks, and let $t_{\rm mix}^Q$ be the total-variation mixing
time with threshold $1/4$. Put
\[
        \alpha_Q:=\frac{t_{\rm meet}^Q}{t_{\rm mix}^Q}.
\]
There are universal constants $a_0,c_0,C_0\in(0,\infty)$ such that, if
$\alpha_Q\ge a_0$, then the expected coalescence time of the synchronous
coalescing $Q$-walk process started from any initial configuration with at most
$c_0\alpha_Q\log\alpha_Q$ particles is at most $C_0t_{\rm meet}^Q$.

body:
Load-bearing hypothesis: the Rankine-Hugoniot condition, and hence the whole notion of weak solution, is attached to a specific pair (conserved density, flux) — not to the PDE as an equation for smooth functions. Two equations with identical classical solutions can have different weak solutions. Counterexample: for smooth u, Burgers' equation u_t + (u^2/2)_x = 0 is equivalent to (u^2/2)_t + (u^3/3)_x = 0 (multiply the first by u; conversely divide where u ≠ 0). But a jump from u_l = 1 (left) to u_r = 0 (right) travels with speed [f]/[u] = (1/2 - 0)/(1 - 0) = 1/2 for the first form, and with speed (1/3 - 0)/(1/2 - 0) = 2/3 for the second: the two weak solutions are genuinely different. The same phenomenon makes the nonconservative form u_t + u u_x = 0 meaningless across a shock (the product u u_x is not a distribution for discontinuous u). Physically, the model must specify which quantity is conserved; numerically, only schemes written in the conservative form of the true conserved quantity (Lax-Wendroff theorem) converge to the correct shock speeds. Auditor's check: when a proof rewrites the flux (multiplying the equation by a function of u, changing variables u = φ(v), or using a chain rule), the manipulation is legitimate for smooth solutions only; across discontinuities it changes the answer.
Counterexample: u_t + (u^2/2)_x = 0 versus (u^2/2)_t + (u^3/3)_x = 0 with left state 1 and right state 0
Rankine-Hugoniot: σ = [flux]/[density], so both entries matter
Chain-rule manipulations of the flux are valid only where the solution is C^1

The first-order theory of real closed fields (RCF) admits quantifier elimination in the language of ordered rings (0, 1, +, -, \cdot, <). Consequently, every semialgebraic set is preserved under coordinate projections.
Axioms of Real Closed Fields

Let X_1, ..., X_n be independent random variables and let Z = f(X_1, ..., X_n) where f is (a, 0)-self-bounding with a >= 1. Then for all t >= 0, P(Z - E[Z] >= t) <= exp(- t^2 / (2 * a * E[Z] + 2 * a * t / 3)) and for 0 <= t <= E[Z], P(Z - E[Z] <= -t) <= exp(- t^2 / (2 * a * E[Z])).
X_1, ..., X_n are independent
f is (a, 0)-self-bounding
t >= 0

[Theorem main of arXiv:2604.12815, 'On ergodicity of the SAGA-LD algorithm\thanks{The author gratefully acknowledges the suppo'] Let Assumptions (init of the paper), (dissip of the paper) and (lip of the paper) hold. There is $\eta_{0}>0$ such that,
for $0<\eta\leq \eta_{0}$ 
there exists a probability $\mu_{*}=\mu_{*}(\eta)$ on $\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{Nd}$ such that 
$$
d_{TV}(\mathrm{Law}(X_{n},G_{n}),\mu_{*})\to 0,\ n\to\infty.
$$	
For all measurable 
functions $\phi:\mathbb{R}^{(N+1)d}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that 
\begin{equation}
|\phi(u)|\leq C(1+|u|)	
\end{equation} 
with some $C>0$,
\begin{equation}
E\left[\left|\frac{\phi(X_{1},G_{1})+\ldots+\phi(X_{n},G_{n})}{n}-\int_{\mathbb{R}^{(N+1)d}}\phi(u)\mu_{*}(du)\right|\right]\to 0,
\ n\to\infty.
\end{equation}
A fortiori, the averages converge in probability. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Tightness of the path via the exponential metric (Liouville first passage percolation) comparison. Result: The energy-minimising path between two points concentrates on paths of small total resistance, i.e. on near-geodesics of the discrete metric with edge weights e^{beta h}; this is the Liouville first passage percolation metric, whose scaling limit (the LQG metric) exists for beta below the critical value by Ding-Dubedat-Dunlap-Falconet and Gwynne-Miller. Tightness of P is then plausible via geodesic tightness in that metric, but P is not a geodesic: the current spreads over many paths and the minimiser of the quadratic energy is a flow, not a path; the notes' 'path' is the sampled path of the current. Its scaling limit would be a random path sampled from the limiting current, which requires the continuum current on LQG, an object not yet constructed. I record the reduction: existence of the limit of P is equivalent to existence of the continuum electrical current between boundary points on the LQG surface. Obstruction: No continuum electrical current on LQG has been constructed; the path is a functional of it.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0015-scaling-limit-of-the-current-minimising-path-in-the-dgff-network
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

At each fixed finite t for sparse critical parking on Z^d, d>=3, the common-Abel full-space potential V_t=lim_{a->1}G_a*(eta-(A_t-H_t)) exists in L2 and U_t-E U_t=V_t+M_t, where M_t is the C17 Green instruction martingale. The odometer mean is a harmonic mode; the two components are not asserted independent. In d4 the difference is well-defined although raw individual charge potentials diverge. Assumptions: Bounded sparse iid source law, 0<p<1/2; finite t; d>=3; Full-space discrete-time SRW, (I-P)G=delta; common Abel parameter; Source finite propagation gives finite-dependent centered U_t; C17 L2 Green instruction martingale. Limitation: No time-uniform potential variance, Gaussian law or independence; no nearest-distance conclusion. Novelty: KNOWN stationary Poisson/resolvent method; UNCHECKED exact parking decomposition. Status: proof (unaudited). The model is discrete-time uniform nearest-neighbor synchronous parking on Z^d with stationary capacity-one holes; A_t(x) is the active-particle count and H_t(x) the unfilled-hole indicator. In the sparse law eta(x) is initially +1 and -1 each with probability p, and zero otherwise, independently across sites. In this card V_t denotes the charge-difference potential, not the eligible-site indicator V_t in C23; these are separate local notations. No audit has been completed for this exact version. U_t(y) counts departures through time t, rho_j(y) is the destination of its jth used instruction, P is the nearest-neighbor averaging operator, G_a=sum_{n>=0}a^n p_n, and M_t(x)=L2-lim_{a->1}sum_y sum_{j<=U_t(y)}[G_a(rho_j(y)-x)-(P G_a)(y-x)].

Full-space discrete-time SRW, (I-P)G=delta; common Abel parameter
