Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty: KNOWN stationary Poisson/resolvent
method; UNCHECKED this exact parking Abel decomposition. The terms are
not assumed independent and no time-uniform variance bound follows.

For the sparse critical source process on Z^d, d>=3, 0<p<1/2, fix a
finite horizon t. Let S_t=A_t-H_t, m_t=E U_t(0), and

    N_t(x)=sum_y sum_{j<=U_t(y)}
                  [1{rho_j(y)=x}-p_1(x-y)].

This is accumulated arrival instruction noise. For 0<a<1 let
G_a(x)=sum_{n>=0}a^n p_n(x), the full-space discrete-time Abel Green
kernel. The limit

    V_t(x)=L2-lim_{a->1} [G_a*(eta-S_t)](x)

exists, and the exact centered identity is

    U_t(x)-m_t=V_t(x)+M_t(x),

where M_t is C17's deterministic Green-potential instruction martingale
with covariance m_t[2G(z-x)-1{x=z}]. All convolutions use the same full-space
SRW convention (I-P)G=delta. In d4 the raw eta and S_t potentials separately
have divergent variance (C24); their difference is regularized together.
The mean m_t is a spatially constant harmonic mode and cannot be recovered
by inverting I-P on mean-zero charges.

## 1. Exact finite-Abel algebra

Source conservation (19) and the definition of N_t give

    S_t=eta+(P-I)U_t+N_t,
    eta-S_t=(I-P)U_t-N_t.

At fixed t under the bounded sparse law, all local counts have a deterministic
finite bound. G_a is in l1, with total mass 1/(1-a), so these convolutions
are well-defined absolutely at a<1 and commute with P. Therefore

    G_a*(eta-S_t)=G_a*(I-P)(U_t-m_t)-G_a*N_t.

The constant was removed because (I-P)m_t=0. Expanding the arrival noise
and using symmetry of G_a shows

    (G_a*N_t)(x)=sum_y sum_{j<=U_t(y)}
                  [G_a(rho_j(y)-x)-(P G_a)(y-x)]
                =M_t^a(x).

The rearrangement is legitimate: at fixed t U_t(y) is uniformly bounded,
and the sum of neighbor Green weights is finite at a<1. C17 proves
M_t^a converges in L2 to M_t for d>=3.

## 2. Resolvent filter converges to the centered identity

Set Z_t=U_t-m_t. The field Z_t is stationary, square-integrable and
finite-dependent by source finite propagation from iid bounded initial
data and independent local motion randomness. Its covariance therefore
has finite support and an absolutely continuous spectral measure; in
particular there is no atom at frequency zero.

The SRW Fourier multiplier is lambda(theta)=d^(-1)sum_i cos(theta_i).
The filter G_a*(I-P) has multiplier

    b_a(theta)=(1-lambda)/(1-a lambda).

For lambda>=0, 0<=b_a<=1; for lambda<0 it is bounded by two.
At every frequency with lambda!=1 it tends to one as a tends to one.
The only frequency lambda=1 is zero, which has no spectral atom for Z_t.
Dominated convergence against its finite spectral measure yields

    G_a*(I-P)Z_t -> Z_t in L2.

Combining this with Step 1 and C17 gives convergence of the charge-difference
potential and the claimed identity. This also proves why centering is
required: b_a(0)=0 at every a and the mean mode is annihilated.

## 3. Scope of cancellation

The difference eta-S_t is a stationary current divergence; covariance
reindexing as in C19 shows its susceptibility is zero. This is consistent
with the existence of its potential even when the two individual raw
charge potentials diverge. It is not legitimate to subtract two separately
defined infinite-variance limits; the same Abel parameter regularizes their
difference before passing to the limit.

Both V_t and M_t depend on the same routing and final configuration.
No independence between them is claimed. The identity supplies a correct
potential decomposition at each finite time, not a bound on V_t as time
grows, a Gaussian approximation, or a conditional hole-influence estimate.
The remaining d4 nearest-distance problem still requires spatial control.

body: Two Latin squares of order n are orthogonal if superimposing them produces each of the n^2 ordered pairs of symbols exactly once; a family is a set of MOLS if every pair in it is orthogonal, and N(n) denotes the maximum size of such a family. For every n >= 2, N(n) <= n - 1, with equality whenever n is a prime power via the finite-field construction L_a(i, j) = a i + j over F_n for nonzero a. N(1) is infinite by convention, and N(2) = N(6) = 1.
title: Mutually Orthogonal Latin Squares (MOLS)

\left(
\fint_I \tvert{P_{2\tau}}_{A,B,q',q}\drm \tau

\inf_{\omega\in\ell^\infty(X)}
\sup_{A}\euler^{-\omega}
\sup_{B}\euler^{\omega}
\left(
\fint_I
\tvert{P_\tau^\omega}_{A,A,2,q}^q
\drm \tau
\right)^\frac{1}{q}
\left(
\fint_I
\tvert{P_\tau^{-\omega}}_{B,B,2,q}^q
\drm \tau
\right)^\frac{1}{q}.

[Proposition prop:BKtoL of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] Given the structure (A1-A5) one obtains (L1-L6) via the following:
\begin{enumerate}[(L1)]
\item $A^0=\cA$, $A^{0,1}=\Omega^1$, $A^{1,0}=\overline{\Omega^1}$, $A^2=\cA^\vee$.
The product $A^1\otimes A^1\to A^2$ is defined by
\begin{gather*}
A^{0,1}\otimes A^{1,0}\to A^2, \qquad x\otimes \overline{y}\mapsto -\sqrt{-1}h(\_ x,\overline{y}),     \\
A^{1,0}\otimes A^{0,1}\to A^2, \qquad \overline{x}\otimes y\mapsto \sqrt{-1}h(\_ y,\overline{x}).     
\end{gather*}
\item The differential $d\colon A^0\to A^1$ is $da=Da+\overline{Da^*}$ and the differential $d\colon A^1=A^{0,1}\oplus A^{1,0}\to A^2$ is 
\[
d(x,\overline{y})=\left(a\mapsto-\sqrt{-1}h(x,\overline{Da^*})+\sqrt{-1}h(Da,\overline{y})\right)
\]
where $x,y\in\Omega^1$ and $a\in\cA$.
\item $F=-2\eta\in\cA^\vee$.
\item $\tau=\operatorname{ev}_1\colon \cA^\vee\to\bC$.
\item The $*$-structure on $A^0$ and $A^2$ comes from the $*$-structure on $\cA$, and the $*$-structure on $A^1$ is given by $x^*=\overline{x}$ for $x\in A^{0,1}$.
\item See (L1).
\end{enumerate}

[Dfn 3. dfn: metric on frakMtau of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{The metrics $d_{\mathfrak{M}_{c}}^{\tau}$ and $d_{\mathfrak{M}}^{\tau}$}]  
  Let $\tau$ be a functor on $\mathfrak{M}$.
  For $\mathcal{S}=(S,d^{S}, \rho_{S}, a_{S}), \mathcal{T}=(T, d^{T}, \rho_{T}, a_{T}) \in \mathfrak{M}(\tau)$,
  we define
  \begin{equation} 
    d_{\mathfrak{M}}^{\tau} (\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{T})
    \coloneqq
    \inf_{f, g, M}
    \left\{
      \lHausdMet{M}{\rho_{M}} \bigl( f(S), g(T) \bigr) 
      \vee  
      d_{\tau}^{M,\rho_{M}} \bigl( \tau_{f}(a_{S}), \tau_{g}(a_{T}) \bigr)  
    \right\},
  \end{equation}
  where the infimum is taken 
  over all $(M, d^{M}, \rho_{M}) \in \mathfrak{M}$ 
  and root-and-distance-preserving maps $f : S \to M$ and $g : T \to M$.
  For a functor $\tau$ on $\mathfrak{M}_{c}$,
  we define $d_{\mathfrak{M}_{c}}^{\tau}$ similarly.

body: Let (mu_n) be a sequence of probability measures on a topological space X equipped with its Borel sigma-algebra, and let (a_n) be a sequence of positive reals with a_n tending to infinity (the speed). A function I: X -> [0, infinity] is a rate function if it is lower semicontinuous; it is a good rate function if in addition every sublevel set {x in X : I(x) <= alpha}, alpha < infinity, is compact. The sequence (mu_n) satisfies a large-deviation principle with speed a_n and rate function I if, for every Borel set B, -inf_{x in int(B)} I(x) <= liminf_n (1/a_n) log mu_n(B) <= limsup_n (1/a_n) log mu_n(B) <= -inf_{x in cl(B)} I(x), where int(B) and cl(B) denote the interior and closure of B. [Dembo and Zeitouni, Large Deviations Techniques and Applications]
title: Large-Deviation Principle and Rate Function

with the same coupling over $y\in\mathbb R^d$ and $s>0$.

[Definition 9 (Weak sub-solution) of arXiv:2608.26834, 'Small-time annealed large deviations principle for one-dimensional diffusions in a random '] A nonnegative function $u$ on $(0,S)\times D$ is called a bounded weak sub-solution  of the differential equation
		\begin{equation}
			\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}={\mathcal L}_W u
		\end{equation}
		if
		\[
		u\in L^\infty((0,S)\times D) \cap L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}((0,S);H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)),
		\]
		and, for every nonnegative $\varphi\in C_c^1((0,S);H_0^1(D)\cap L^\infty(D))$, one has
		\begin{equation*}
			-\int_0^S\!\int_Du\,\partial_s\varphi\,\dd \mu_W\dd s
			+\int_0^S\mathcal E_W(u(s),\varphi(s))\,\dd s\le0.
		\end{equation*}
		If equality holds for all such $\varphi$, then $u$ is called a weak solution.
title: Weak sub-solution

body:
[Definition 4 (Martingale representation problem) of arXiv:2608.03412, 'A McKean--Vlasov semigroup and its application to a martingale representation problem'] Let $G:\Pc(\R^d)\to\R$ be given. A pair of Borel maps
\[
Y:[0,T]\times\Pc(\R^d)\to\R,
\qquad
Z:[0,T]\times\R^d\times\Pc(\R^d)\to\R^d
\]
is called a solution of the martingale representation problem associated with
$G$ if the following property holds.

For every initial time $e\in[0,T]$, every initial law $m\in\Pc(\R^d)$,
and every admissible conditional law flow $(\nu_r)_{r\in[e,T]}$ generated by
a bounded Lipschitz drift $\beta$, namely
\[
\mathrm{d}X_r
=
\beta(r,X_r,\nu_r)\,\mathrm{d}r
+\mathrm{d}W_r+\sigma_\circ\,\mathrm{d}W^\circ_r,
\qquad
\nu_r=\Lc(X_r\mid\Gc_r),
\qquad
\nu_e=m,
\]
the following integrability condition is satisfied:
\[
\E\left[
\sup_{r\in[e,T]} |Y(r,\nu_r)|
+
\int_e^T
\left(
|Z(r,X_r,\nu_r)|
+
\left|
\E[Z(r,X_r,\nu_r)\mid\Gc_r]
\right|^2
\right)\mathrm{d}r
\right]
<\infty,
\]
and, $\P$-a.s., for every $t\in[e,T]$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
Y(t,\nu_t)
=
G(\nu_T)
-
\int_t^T
\E\Big[
Z(r,X_r,\nu_r)\cdot\beta(r,X_r,\nu_r)
\,\Big|\,\Gc_r
\Big]\mathrm{d}r
-
\int_t^T
\E\Big[
Z(r,X_r,\nu_r)
\,\Big|\,\Gc_r
\Big]\cdot\sigma_\circ\,\mathrm{d}W^\circ_r .
\end{aligned}
\]
title: Martingale representation problem

body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Controlled generators, exact finite-state diagnostic, coupling, renewal reward or capacity comparison Result: A finite-horizon input coupling suggests a cubic collision scale. Fix k tagged servers. Jobs arrive at rate Lambda=lambda*n/k and choose a uniform k-subset. If N is the number of tagged servers hit by an arrival, E[N(N-1)]=k*(k-1)*k*(k-1)/(n*(n-1)). Remove arrivals that hit at least two tagged queues and restore their lost marginal rates by independent Poisson streams. A union bound on removed events and added events is at most (3/2)*Lambda*T*E[N(N-1)], hence at most 3*lambda*T*k*(k-1)^2/(2*(n-1)). The resulting streams are independent with the correct marginal rates. With independent task marks and queues initially empty, this also bounds total variation of their workload paths on [0,T]. Extending the credited source coupling to stationary starts gives TV<=2*k*r(T)+3*lambda*T*k*(k-1)^2/(2*(n-1)), where r(T) is the stationary marginal emptying tail. With independent exponential service of rate mu>lambda, a stopped generator calculation gives r(T)<=(1+sqrt(lambda/mu))*exp(-(sqrt(mu)-sqrt(lambda))^2*T). Taking T=2*log(n)/(sqrt(mu)-sqrt(lambda))^2 gives sufficient k=o((n/log(n))^(1/3)). A conditional polynomial tail r(T)<=C*T^(-p) gives sufficient exponent p/(3*p+1). Check: The hypergeometric factorial moment follows by summing ordered pairs of tagged-server indicators. On N>=2, both 1<=N(N-1)/2 and N<=N(N-1), giving the factor 3/2. Small subset enumeration checks the moment exactly. Separate exact checks cover 77 hypergeometric/restoration cases, 81 generator identities, nine geometric exponential moments and five polynomial balancing identities. The complete packet explicitly checks stationary coupling, marginal rate restoration, PASTA and heavy-traffic limits; these are author checks, not independent review. Obstruction: Partial exponential-service sufficient regime only. No optimal threshold, boundary k of order n^(1/3), general-service improvement, correlated-mark result, uniform heavy-traffic result or novelty certification. The basic source coupling is credited.

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2609.02581, '\bfseries Interior Curvature Estimates for the Graphical Scalar Curvature Equation in All '] Let \(B_1\subset\mathbb R^n\), and suppose that
\[
 u,v\in C^2(B_1)\cap C^1(\overline{B_1}),
 \qquad
 \kappa[v]\in\Gamma_2,
\]
with
\[
 v\geq u\quad\text{in }B_1,
 \qquad
 v=u\quad\text{on }\partial B_1,
 \qquad
 \lVert Du\rVert_{L^\infty(B_1)}\leq K.
\]
Set
\[
 \tilde{d}(x):=\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial B_1)=1-|x|.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 0\leq v(x)-u(x)
 \leq (1+K)\left(\sqrt{2\,\tilde{d}(x)}+\tilde{d}(x)\right)
 \qquad\text{for every }x\in B_1.
 
\end{equation}

[Definition def:FktdAJs of arXiv:2609.02588, 'Ramsey-type results for Maker-Breaker games'] Let $k,t,d,s,r$ be positive integers with $t\geq d \geq 2$ and $k\geq r$,
let $\mathcal{A} \subseteq \binom{[t]\setminus \{1\}}{d-1}$
and $\mathcal{K}\in \binom{[t]\setminus \{1\}}{d-1} \setminus \mathcal{A}$.
We define $\mathcal{F}_s(k,t,d,\mathcal{A},\mathcal{K},r)$ to be the family of all 
$d$-uniform hypergraphs
$\mathcal{H}$ that satisfy the following property:
There exists a partition of the vertex set $V(\mathcal{H}) = V_1\cup \ldots \cup V_t$
such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $|V_i| = k$ for every $i\in [t]$,
\item[(ii)] $|e\cap V_i| \leq 1$ for every $i\in [t]$ and $e\in E(\mathcal{H})$,
\item[(iii)] for every $i\in [t]$, every vertex $v\in V_i$,

[Prop pr.Topo of arXiv:2411.13099, 'Long time behavior of killed Feynman-Kac semigroups with singular Schr{ö}dinger potentials'] Let $(L_t,t\ge 0)$ be a purely jump Lévy process over $\mathscr R^d$ such that its  Lévy measure $\nu$ has full topological support over $\mathscr R_0^d$, i.e. for all $y\in \mathscr R^d_0$ and all $r\in (0,|y|)$, $\nu(B(y,r))>0$, and such that for some $\beta >0$, 
 $$\int_{|u|\le 1}|u|^\beta \nu(du)<+\infty.$$  Let $\mathscr O$ be a subdomain of $\mathscr R^d$. 
 Let  $T>0$ and $x,z\in \mathscr O$. Then,  for all $\epsilon>0$, 
 \begin{equation}
 \mathbb P_x[|L_T-z|<\epsilon, T<\sigma _{\mathscr O}]>0,
 \end{equation}
 where $\sigma_{\mathscr O}:=\inf\{t\ge 0, L_t\notin \mathscr O\}$. 
 In addition, if $\mathscr R^d\setminus \overline{\mathscr O}$ is nonempty, for all $x\in \mathscr O$, $\mathbb P_x[\sigma_{\mathscr O}<+\infty ]>0$.

body:
[Prop number of components in MRSC of arXiv:2605.03151, 'Giants through Higher-Order paths in Random Simplicial Complexes'] Let $X_n \sim \MRSC_d(n; \bm{p})$ satisfying Assumption~(assumption: prob parameters of the paper). Let $C_n$ denote the number of $d$-dimensional connected components in $X_n$. Then, it holds that
\[
\frac{C_n}{s_{d-1}(X_n)} \overset{\mathbb{P}}{\to} \gamma_{\lambda} - \lambda \frac{d}{d+1} \gamma_{\lambda}^{d+1},
\]
where $\gamma_{\lambda}$ is the extinction probability of a branching process with offspring distribution $d \mathsf{Poi}(\lambda)$, i.e., $\gamma_{\lambda}$ is the smallest solution to $\gamma = e^{-\lambda(1 - \gamma^d)}$.
title: Prop number of components in MRSC of arXiv:2605.03151

[Proposition 11 of arXiv:2605.25715, '2605.25715'] Let $\Phi$, $A$, $\mathbf{P}$, $\mu$, $\mathbf{B}$, and $V$ be as in Theorem \ref{thm:polydifdrift} and let all conditions of Theorem \ref{thm:polydifdrift} except \eqref{prop:eq0} and \eqref{prop:eq2} be satisfied. Then a sufficient condition for \eqref{prop:eq0} and \eqref{prop:eq2} to hold is given by
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] $\mathrm{deg} (\mathbf{B})\le 2m-2$, where $m=\mathrm{deg}(\Phi)$, and
\item[(ii)] $-\Phi_m(x)>0$ for every $x\in S^{d-1}:=\{x\in \R^d\,| \, \|x\|=1\}$.
\end{itemize}
In particular, Theorem \ref{thm:polydifdrift} applies and in addition, the regularized semigroup associated with the
$L^1$-closed extension of $(L^{\widetilde{\mathbf P}},C^\infty_0(\mathbb R^d))$
is conservative.

The series converges uniformly there, and g is strictly decreasing with a unique zero r_* in (59/125,473/1000). Put theta_*=r_*/[4(1+r_*)^2] and p_raw=1/(1+theta_*). The constant-word whole no-cut coefficients satisfy sum_{l>=2}l h_l(theta)<infinity IF AND ONLY IF theta<theta_*, for theta>=0. Thus every exterior configuration is good for p>p_raw, in particular p>=135424/142799. Certified bounds are 2169729/2287979<p_raw<135424/142799. These rational bounds use 20 exact series terms plus an analytic bound on the ENTIRE remaining tail. Positive-axis continuation and nonnegative coefficients give summability below the root; a noncanceled E-zero pole gives divergence at and above it. This is the exact cutoff of a sufficient raw-profile METHOD, not the actual good/bad transition. It does not settle the conjectured all-good interval down to 4/5 or the low-drift side, and no novelty is asserted.

[Corollary Constant alternating regret for polyhedral OLO of arXiv:2608.24731, 'Optimal Alternating Regret for Online Learning and Games\thanks{Authors are alphabetically'] \label[corollary]{cor:polytope}
Let $\mathcal X=\operatorname{conv}\{\boldsymbol{v}_1,\ldots,\boldsymbol{v}_N\}$ be a  polytope. Consider  linear losses $f_t(\boldsymbol{x})=\langle \boldsymbol{c}_t,\boldsymbol{x}\rangle$, with $f_t(\boldsymbol{x})\in[-1,1]$ for every $\boldsymbol{x}\in\+X$. Running (alg:main of the paper) with $\mu$ being the uniform distribution on $\{\boldsymbol{v}_1,\ldots,\boldsymbol{v}_N\}$ gives
\[
  \max_{\boldsymbol{u}\in\mathcal X}\operatorname{Reg}_{\mathrm{Alt}}^T(\boldsymbol{u})\le8\log N.
\]
In particular, for $\mathcal X=\Delta_d$ and $\boldsymbol{c}_t\in[-1,1]^d$, (alg:main of the paper) coincides with (alg:variance hedge of the paper) and recovers the bound $8\log d$.

[Lemma 106 (Proportional distinct-speed phase gap) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let $\parvec$ satisfy \eqref{eq:parameter-vector}.  There exist
$\delta_0=\delta_0(\parvec)>0$, $N_{\mathrm{sp}}=N_{\mathrm{sp}}(\parvec)\ge2$,
and $c_{\mathrm{sp}}=c_{\mathrm{sp}}(\parvec)>0$ such that, whenever
\[
  |\ell|\sim N,\qquad N\ge N_{\mathrm{sp}},
  \qquad |q|\le\delta_0|\ell|,
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
  |\omega_a(\ell+q)-\omega_b(\ell)|
  \ge c_{\mathrm{sp}}N,
  \qquad a\ne b.
\end{equation}
Every sum phase in \eqref{eq:two-frequency-phases} has the same type of lower
bound.  Consequently
\begin{equation}
  |\Phi_{a|b}^{\eps_1,\eps_2}(q,\ell)|
  \ge c_{\mathrm{sp}}N
\end{equation}
for every sign branch generated by a same-color block.  The constants
$\delta_0$, $N_{\mathrm{sp}}$, and $c_{\mathrm{sp}}$ depend only on the
dispersive parameters and the Littlewood--Paley support constants; they are
independent of $\mathfrak h_{\W}$ and $\mathfrak h_{\K}$.
title: Proportional distinct-speed phase gap

body: [Lemma 5 of arXiv:2609.03951, 'Generalized Semi-Riemannian Submersions and Foliations'] Let $(M,g)$ be a semi-Riemannian manifold and let $\pi:M \to B$ be a surjective submersion. If the horizontal distribution $\mathcal{H}$ is locally generated by basic vector fields, then there exists a smooth singular distribution $\mathcal{D}$, locally finitely generated on $B$, such that $\mathcal{D}_{\pi(p)} = d\pi(\mathcal{H}_p) = d\pi(\mathcal{A}_p)$ for every $p \in M$.

[Proposition 29 ({\bf The Interval of Integers Principle}) of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] Suppose that $X\rightarrow X/G$ is an HKG cover. For each integer $j\in\llbracket0,s-1\rrbracket$ let the pair $(\l_{j,0},\l_{j,-1})\in (\mathbb N\cup\{0\})\times\llbracket0,m-1\rrbracket$ be such that 
$$\Big\lfloor\frac{l_{j+1}}{p^{j+1}}-(p-1)\sum_{i=1}^j\frac{l_i}{p^i}\Big\rfloor=m\l_{j,0}+\l_{j,-1};$$
e.g., $(\l_{0,0},\l_{0,-1})\in (\mathbb N\cup\{0\})\times\llbracket0,m-1\rrbracket$ is such that $\lfloor\frac{l_1}{p}\rfloor=m\l_{0,0}+\l_{0,-1}$. Let $b\in\llbracket1,p^s\rrbracket$ and let the pair $(\q_{s,b},\r_{s,b})\in \mathbb Z\times\llbracket0,m-1\rrbracket$ be such that $\delta_s(b-1)-\delta_s(b)=m\q_{s,b}+\r_{s,b}$.  Then the following properties hold.

\medskip
{\bf (1)} If either $a=[0]_m$ with $\delta_s(b)\ge 1$ (i.e., with $b\le p^s-2$) or $a\neq [0]_m$, then we have identities
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}\mu_X(a,b)=&\q_{s,b}+\Big\lfloor\frac{\delta_s(b)-1+\r_{-a}+\r_{s,b}}{m}\Big\rfloor-\Big\lfloor\frac{\delta_s(b)-1+\r_{-a}}{m}\Big\rfloor\\
=&\begin{cases}\q_{s,b}+1\quad\;\textup{if}\quad \r_{\delta_s(b)-1+\r_{-a}}+\r_{s,b}\ge m\\
\q_{s,b}\quad\quad\quad\textup{if}\quad \r_{\delta_s(b)-1+\r_{-a}}+\r_{s,b}<m.\end{cases}
\end{split}
\end{equation}
In particular, we have $\mu_X(a,b)=\q_{s,b}+1$ if and only if $\r_{s,b}\neq 0$ (i.e., $\r_{s,b}\in\llbracket1,m-1\rrbracket$) and $a\in [\delta_s(b)]_m+\{[i]_m|i\in\llbracket0,\r_{s,b}-1\rrbracket\}$.

{\bf (2)} We have identities 
\begin{equation*}
\q_{s,p^s-1}=\Big\lfloor\frac{\lfloor \frac{l_1}{p}\rfloor+1}{m}\Big\rfloor=\begin{cases}\l_{0,0}+1\quad\textup{if}\quad\l_{0,-1}=m-1\\
\l_{0,0}\quad\quad\;\;\,\textup{if}\quad \l_{0,-1}\in\llbracket0,m-2\rrbracket,\end{cases}
\end{equation*} 
$\r_{s,p^s-1}=\Big\lfloor \frac{l_1}{p}\Big\rfloor+1-m\Big\lfloor\frac{\lfloor \frac{l_1}{p}\rfloor+1}{m}\Big\rfloor$, and
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}\mu_X([0]_m,p^s-1)=\q_{s,p^s-1}+\Big\lfloor\frac{\delta_s(p^s-1)-1+\r_{s,p^s-1}}{m}\Big\rfloor-1-\Big\lfloor\frac{\delta_s(p^s-1)-1}{m}\Big\rfloor\\
=\l_{0,0}=\begin{cases}\q_{s,p^s-1}\quad\quad\quad\textup{if}\quad \r_{s,p^s-1}\ge 1\\
\q_{s,p^s-1}-1\quad\;\textup{if}\quad \r_{s,p^s-1}=0\end{cases}=\begin{cases}\Big\lfloor\frac{\lfloor \frac{l_1}{p}\rfloor+1}{m}\Big\rfloor\quad\quad\quad\;\;\textup{if}\quad m\nmid \lfloor \frac{l_1}{p}\rfloor+1\\
\Big\lfloor\frac{\lfloor \frac{l_1}{p}\rfloor+1}{m}\Big\rfloor-1\quad\;\;\;\textup{if}\quad m\mid\lfloor \frac{l_1}{p}\rfloor+1.\end{cases}
\end{split}
\end{equation}

{\bf (3)} For each $a\in C_m$ we have inequalities 
$$\mu_X([0]_m,p^s-1)\le\mu_X(a,p^s-1)\le \mu_X([0]_m,p^s-1)+1.$$

{\bf (4)} For each pair $(a_1,a_2)\in C_m^2$ and every $b\in\llbracket1,p^s-1\rrbracket$ we have inequalities $0\le |\mu_X(a_1,b)-\mu_X(a_2,b)|\le 1$.

\smallskip
{\bf (5)} Let $j\in\llbracket0,s-1\rrbracket$. We assume that $b\in A_{s;j}$; so $p^j\mid b$ but $p^{j+1}\nmid b$. Then the following properties hold.

\medskip\noindent
{\bf (5.a)} We have identities
$$\q_{s,b}=\begin{cases}\l_{j,0}+1\quad\quad\textup{if}\quad\l_{j,-1}=m-1\quad\textup{and}\quad \r_{s,b}=0\\
\l_{j,0}\quad\quad\quad\;\;\,\textup{if}\quad\l_{j,-1}=m-1\quad\textup{and}\quad \r_{s,b}>0\\
\l_{j,0}\quad\quad\quad\;\;\,\textup{if}\quad \l_{j,-1}\in\llbracket0,m-2\rrbracket.\end{cases}$$

\noindent
{\bf (5.b)} If $j=0$ we assume that $b\neq p^s-1$. Then for each $a\in C_m$ we have inequalities 
$$\l_{j,0}\le \q_{s,b}\le\mu_X(a,b)\le \l_{j,0}+1\le\q_{s,b}+1.$$

\noindent
{\bf (5.c)} If $\l_{j,-1}=m-1$, $\r_{s,b}=0$, and for $j=0$ we have $b\neq p^s-1$, then $\mu_X(a,b)=\q_{s,b}=\l_{j,0}+1$.

\noindent
{\bf (5.d)} There exists a uniquely determined subset $\mathbb J_{X;j}$ of $C_m\times A_{s;j}$ such that 
$$\mu_X(a,b)=\begin{cases}\l_{j,0}+1\quad\;\textup{if}\quad (a,b)\in\mathbb J_{X;j}\\

[Lem 18 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] In the setting of Proposition~\ref{p:polytope.bd.local}, 
we can construct a family of half-spaces $(\tilde{H}_j : j\in[\tilde{n}])$
such that for $\delta_0>0$ small enough, we have
	 \begin{align}
        
        P\supseteq 
        \tilde{P}_\mu &\equiv \cD_\mu \cap \bigcap_{j=1}^{\tilde n} \tilde H_j 
        \supseteq S_\star(\lambda,\mu)[\epsilon']\,, \quad \text{and} \\
        
        	\emptyset \ne 
        \tilde{P}_{\mu'} &\equiv \cD_{\mu'} \cap \bigcap_{j=1}^{\tilde n} \tilde H_j 
        \subseteq 
        S_\star\bigg(\lambda',\mu';
        	\frac\epsilon5,\frac\epsilon2-\delta_0
        	\bigg)\,.
    \end{align}
for all $(\lambda',\mu') \in B_{\delta_0}(\lambda,\mu)$. 

\begin{proof}Let $n = C(\lambda,\mu)$. Let $(H_j:j\in[n])$ be a collection of closed half-spaces of $\bbR^{3r+s}$ such that
	\[
        K_1=S_\star(\lambda,\mu)[\epsilon']
        \subseteq P
        \equiv \cD_\mu \cap \bigcap_{j=1}^n H_j
        \subseteq S_\star\bigg(\lambda,\mu;
        	\frac\epsilon5,\frac\epsilon2\bigg)
        =K_2\,.\]
Abbreviate $u_\mu\equiv (0^{3r},\mu)$, and recall from \eqref{e:D.mu.affine.closure} that the affine space $\mathcal{F}_\mu$ is defined by the constraint $(\YY,u_\mu)=1$. In the above definition of $P$, we can assume without loss that none of the $H_j$ have normal vector parallel to $u_\mu$: such $H_j$ are redundant because of the intersection with $\cD_\mu$. 

Recall that the function $f$ from \eqref{e:f.strictly.convex.surplus.relaxation}
is strictly convex on $\cD_\mu$.
We also have
	\[
	P\subseteq K_2
	=\bigg\{\YY \in \cD_\mu : f(\YY;\lambda,\mu) \le 	
	\frac\epsilon2
		\bigg\}\,.
	\]
The strict convexity of $f$ implies that the set 
    \[
        \cQ \equiv \bigg\{
        	\YY \in P : f(\YY;\lambda,\mu) = \frac\epsilon2
		\bigg\}
    \]
must be a subset of the extreme points of $P$ (the points that cannot be written as a convex combination of two other points in $P$). Therefore, $\cQ$ is a discrete set.
    Moreover, Lemma~\ref{l:S.star.nbd.in.S.star.eps} implies
    \[
        S_\star(\lambda,\mu)[\epsilon'] \subseteq
        \bigg\{\YY \in P : f(\YY;\lambda,\mu) \le 
        	\frac\epsilon3
        	\bigg\}\,,
    \]
and thus $\cQ \cap S_\star(\lambda,\mu)[\epsilon'] = \emptyset$. Enumerate the points of $\cQ$ as $\YY_1,\ldots,\YY_{\hat{n}}$, and for each $j\in[\hat{n}]$ let $\hat{H}_j$ be a closed half-space in $\R^{3r+s}$ whose interior contains $K_1$, and which does not contain $\YY_j$. We then construct the collection $(\tilde H_j : j\in[\tilde{n}])$ by appending these half-spaces to $(H_j:j\in[n])$, so that $\tilde{n}=n+\hat{n}$. Note that $\hat{H}_j$ strictly separates $\YY_j\in\cD_\mu$ from $K_1\subseteq\cD_\mu$, so the normal vector of $\hat{H}_j$ cannot be parallel to $u_\mu$. 

Recall from \eqref{e:polytope-tilde1} and \eqref{e:polytope-tilde2}
that we denote 
	\[
	\tilde{P}_{\mu'}
	\equiv \cD_{\mu'} \cap \bigcap_{j=1}^{\tilde{n}} \tilde{H}_j\,.
	\]
From the above construction combined with Lemma~\ref{l:p.polytope.bd.local.aux}, we have
	\[
	K_1\subseteq \tilde{P}_\mu \subseteq P\setminus\cQ
	\subseteq P
	\subseteq K_2
	\subseteq \cD_\mu
	\cap \bigg[0,\frac{8}{\iota_0}\bigg]^{3r+s}
	 \subseteq \mathcal{F}_\mu
	 \cap \bigg[0,\frac{8}{\iota_0}\bigg]^{3r+s}\,.
	\]
In particular, we know that $K_1$ has nonempty interior in the $\mathcal{F}_\mu$-topology, so $\tilde{P}_\mu$ also has nonempty interior in the $\mathcal{F}_\mu$-topology; we denote this set $\mathrm{int}(\tilde{P}_\mu;\mathcal{F}_\mu)$. If $\YY\in \mathrm{int}(\tilde{P}_\mu;\mathcal{F}_\mu)$, then for all $\YY'$ orthogonal to $u_\mu$ with $\|\YY'\|$ small enough, we must have $\YY+\YY' \in\tilde{P}_\mu$. We claim that any such $\YY$ must also belong to the interior of $\tilde{H}_j$ in the full space $\R^{3r+s}$. Indeed, in the full space $\R^{3r+s}$, we can express
	\[\tilde{H}_j
	= \Big\{\YY''\in\R^{3r+s}
		: (\YY'',v_j) \le c_j\Big\}\,.
	\]

body: In mathematics, specifically in homology theory and algebraic topology, cohomology is a way of attaching algebraic invariants to a topological space or other mathematical object that encode its properties in a way that is often computable. Cohomology is often related to questions of whether some local property of the space is obstructed when passing to a global property. For example, the Möbius strip is not the product space of a line segment with a circle, but locally on any segment of the circle it resembles an ordinary rectangle without the global twist. The obstruction to making the product structure global is encoded in the first cohomology of the underlying circle, which classifies the two inequivalent ways a line can twist around a circle. The fact that there are only two inequivalent ways of twisting a line around a circle is encoded in the relevant cohomology group which can be computed as isomorphic to the group where corresponds to an even number of twists, and to an odd number.
title: Cohomology

Suppose $\mathcal{C}_1\subset\mathrm{Interior}(\mathsf{Tri}_f(a,x))$ and $\mathcal{C}_2\subset\mathrm{Interior}(\mathsf{Tri}_f(x,b))$ are finite sets such that $\{\mathsf{A},\mathsf{X}\}\cup\mathcal{C}_1$ is in convex position, and $\{\mathsf{X},\mathsf{B}\}\cup\mathcal{C}_2$ is in convex position.
Then $\mathcal{C}_1\cup\mathcal{C}_2\subset\mathrm{Interior}(\mathsf{Tri}_f(a,b))$, and $\{\mathsf{A},\mathsf{B}\}\cup\mathcal{C}_1\cup\mathcal{C}_2$ is in convex position.

\end{enumerate}

K,\,({\underline N^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}}(\,\raisebox{0.4mm}{\scalebox{0.6}{\textbullet}}\,)))=\int_{0}^{\exp(K\,\alpha) }
\mathbbm{1}_{K*A^{c}}\big({\underline N^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}}(s)\big)\,ds\;.
$$
Then for any $\epsilon>0$
$$
\lim_{K\to\infty}{{\mathds P}}^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}_{\nu_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}}\left(\frac{\mathcal{T}(A,\,\alpha,\,
 K,\,({\underline N^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}}(\,\raisebox{0.4mm}{\scalebox{0.6}{\textbullet}}\,)))}{e^{\alpha\,K}}
\in\big[(1-\epsilon)\,\mu_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}\big(K*A^{c}\big),\,
(1+\epsilon)\,\mu_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}\big(K*A^{c}\big)\big]
\right)=1.
$$

[Definition defn:core of arXiv:2411.10829, 'Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble and its Laplace transform'] Take any $m\in \mathbb N$, $\vec \mathbf k \in \mathbb R^m_+ $, and $\vec \boldsymbol{\tau}\in \mathbb R^m$ such that $\boldsymbol{\tau}_1\le \cdots \le \boldsymbol{\tau}_m$, and denote $\mathbf Q_\ell = \sum_{\ell'=1}^\ell \mathbf k_{\ell'}$ for each $\ell\in\llbracket 1,m\rrbracket$.
We let
\[
\mathbf L_\beta(\vec\mathbf k, \vec\boldsymbol{\tau}) = \mathrm{p.v.}\int_{\mathscr K[\vec\mathbf k]} \exp\left(\sum_{\ell=1}^{m-1}
(\boldsymbol{\tau}_\ell-\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\ell+1}) \mathbf H(\mathbf Q_\ell)/2 \right)\mathbf I_{\beta,\vec\mathbf k}[\vec \mathbf p, \vec\boldsymbol{\upsilon}, \mathbf H] \mathrm d(\vec\mathbf p,  \vec\boldsymbol{\upsilon},\mathbf H),
\]
where the principal value integral is taken in the following sense.
For any small enough $\epsilon>0$, we let  $\mathscr K_\epsilon=\mathscr K_\epsilon[\vec\mathbf k]$ denote the space of all blocks $(\vec\mathbf p, \vec\boldsymbol{\upsilon}, \mathbf H)\in \mathscr K[\vec \mathbf k]$, such that for each $\ell\in\llbracket 1,m\rrbracket$, $\mathbf p^0$ is constant in $(\mathbf Q_{\ell-1}, \mathbf Q_{\ell-1}+\epsilon)$, and either $\boldsymbol{\upsilon}_\ell>\epsilon$, or $\boldsymbol{\upsilon}_\ell=\varnothing$.
We integrate over $\mathscr K_\epsilon$, then send $\epsilon\to 0+$.

[Lemma 23 of arXiv:2605.02002, 'Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph of maximal degree at most $\Delta$, and for each $(u,v)\in E$ we are given constants $\beta_{uv}$ where $|\beta_{uv}|\leq\beta$ for all edges. Fix an arbitrary external field $h=(h_u)_{u\in V}$, an arbitrary subset $A\subset V$ and configuration $\tau\in\{0,1\}^A$. Then whenever $\beta\leq\frac{1}{\Delta}$, the measure $\mu_{\beta,h}$ defined on $\{0,1\}^{V\setminus A}$ via
$$
\mu_{\beta,h}(\sigma)\propto\exp(\sum_{(u,v)\in E}\beta_{uv}\sigma_u\sigma_v+\sum_{u\in V\setminus A}h_u\sigma_u),\quad\forall\sigma\in\{0,1\}^V:\sigma|_A=\tau
$$satisfies approximate tensorization of variance and approximate tensorization of entropy with constant 2.

[Defn qcdens of arXiv:2411.14350, 'Randomized Geodesic Flow on Hyperbolic Groups'] [coornaert-pjm] 
For $(X,d)$ Gromov-hyperbolic, let $M(\partial_g X)$ denote the collection of positive finite Borel measures on $\partial_g X $. A $G$-equivariant map $X \to M(\partial_g X)$ sending $x \to \mu_x$ is said to be a $C$ {\bf quasi-conformal density} of dimension $v$ ($v\geq 0$), for some $C\geq 1$, if
\begin{equation}
	\frac{1}{C}\exp\big(-v\beta_\xi(y,x)\big)
	\leq
	\frac{{\rm{d}}\mu_{x}}{{\rm{d}}\mu_y} (\xi)
	\leq C \exp\big(-v\beta_\xi(y,x)\big)
\end{equation}
for all $x, y \in X$, $\xi\in \partial X$. If $C=1$, it is a {\bf conformal density}. Equivalently, we also call the family of measures $(\mu_x)_{x\in G}$ a (quasi)-conformal density.

[Lemma lem:quotient-properties of arXiv:2609.02845, 'Degeneracy bounds, stability, and a sharp gap for $B$-colorings'] The false-twin quotient $Q$ has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item Every false-twin class is an independent set in $G$.
  \item Between two distinct false-twin classes there are either all
        possible edges or no edges.
  \item For every $X\in V(Q)$,
        \[
          \sum_{Y\in N_Q(X)}w(Y)=\Delta.
        \]
  \item Distinct vertices of $Q$ have distinct open neighborhoods
        in $Q$.
  \item The graph $Q$ is nonbipartite.
  \item The graph $Q$ is connected.
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Prop bvp of arXiv:2411.05441, 'Sticky diffusions on star graphs : characterization and It\^o formula'] For every $\delta > 0$ and $f \in \bigoplus_{i=1}^N C_b([0,\delta))$, with $f_i(0) = f_j(0)$ for all $1 \leq i,j \leq N$, there is a unique $u \in \bigoplus_{i=1}^N C^2([0,\delta])$ such that
 \begin{equation}
  \begin{cases}
   L_i u_i(x) = f_i(x) \quad & \textnormal{for all } x \in (0, \delta), \, 1 \leq i \leq N, \\
	\eta L u (\mathsf{v}) - \sum_{i=1}^N \rho_i {u_i}'(0) = 0, \\
	u_i(\delta) = 0 \quad & \textnormal{for all } i \in \{1,\dots, N \}, \\
	u_i(0) = u_j(0) \quad & \textnormal{for all } i,j \in \{1,\dots, N \},
  \end{cases}
 \end{equation}
 given by
 \[
  u_i(x) = - \frac{\kappa_i  \alpha_i(x)}{\alpha_i(0)} - \beta_i(x) \quad \textnormal{for all } 0 \leq x \leq \delta,
  \]
  where
  \begin{align*}
  \kappa_i & = \left (\eta f(\mathsf{v}) - \sum_{j=1}^N \frac{\rho_j(\beta_1(0) - \beta_j(0))}{ \alpha_j(0)} \right ) \left (\sum_{j=1}^N \frac{\rho_j}{\alpha_j(0)} \right )^{-1} + \beta_1(0) - \beta_i(0) \\
  \alpha_i(x) & = \int_x^\delta \exp \left (-\int_0^y \frac{2b_i(z)}{\sigma_i^2(z)} dz \right) dy \\
  \beta_i (x) & = \int_x^\delta \left ( \int_0^y \frac{2 f(z)}{\sigma_i^2(z)} \exp \left (\int_0^z \frac{2b_i(s)}{\sigma_i^2(s)} ds  \right) dz \right ) \exp \left (-\int_0^y \frac{2b_i(z)}{\sigma_i^2(z)} dz \right) dy
 \end{align*}
 for all $1 \leq i \leq N$.
 Furthermore, we have 
 \[
  \max_{1 \leq i \leq N} \max_{x \in [0,\delta]} \left \lvert u_i''(x) \right  \rvert = O(1) \quad  \textnormal{as } \delta \downarrow 0,
 \]
 where the hidden constant only depends on $f$ through $\lVert f \rVert_{\infty}$.
title: Prop bvp of arXiv:2411.05441

body: In probability theory, Bernstein inequalities give bounds on the probability that the sum of random variables deviates from its mean. In the simplest case, let X_{1},..., X_{n} be independent Bernoulli random variables taking values +1 and −1 with probability 1/2 (this distribution is also known as the Rademacher distribution), then for every positive $\varepsilon$, $$\mathbb {P} \left(\left|{\frac {1}{n}}\sum _{i=1}^{n}X_{i}\right|>\varepsilon \right)\leq 2\exp \left(-{\frac {n\varepsilon ^{2}}{2(1+{\frac {\varepsilon }{3}})}}\right).$$

[Lemma 32 (Monotonicity of angles) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Fix a finite graph $G$, some $\beta\in[0,\infty)$.
    Let $u$ denote some vertex, and let $E_u$ denote the set of edges incident to $u$.
    Pick
    \[
        \tau'=(\alpha',\omega',\eta')\in [0,\pi/2]^{V\setminus\{u\}}\times\{0,1\}^{E\setminus E_u}\times\{0,1\}^{E\setminus E_u},
    \]
    Let $\mu_{\tau'}$ denote the measure
    $\mu_{G,\beta}$ conditioned on \[\{\tau|_{(V\setminus\{u\})\times (E\setminus E_u) \times (E\setminus E_u)}=\tau'\}.\]
    Then the density of $\alpha_u$ on $[0,\pi/2]$ under $\mu_{\tau'}$
      is proportional to
    \begin{align}
        \textstyle
        \left(
        \prod_{\Gamma\in C(\omega')}
        \textstyle
        2\cosh(\beta\cos\alpha_u\sum_{v \in \Gamma}\cos\alpha_v')
        \right)
        \left(
        \prod_{\Gamma\in C(\eta')}
        \textstyle
        2\cosh(\beta\sin\alpha_u\sum_{v\in \Gamma}\sin\alpha_v')
        \right),
\end{align}
where $C(\rho)$ is the partition of $\{v\in V:v\sim u\}$ into $\rho$-connected components.

In particular, if $\mu^{\alpha_u}_{\tau'}$ denotes the law of $\alpha_u$ under $\mu_{\tau'}$, then
\[
    \tau'\preceq\tau''
    \qquad
    \implies
    \qquad
    \mu^{\alpha_u}_{\tau'}\leqstoch\mu^{\alpha_u}_{\tau''}.
\]

body:
Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, paired). The per-output long-only stack on the relative-metric error covariance was shrunk toward the pooled simplex weights, $w_d \\mapsto w_g + (1 - s)(w_d - w_g)$. The ceiling of the family - the amount chosen by five-fold cross-validation on the calibration rows - adds $+0.59$ percent on EMIT and $+0.20$ on OCO-2 at full calibration (28 of 40 and 26 of 30 cells). A positive-part James-Stein amount $s = \\min(1, \\sum_d \\operatorname{tr} V_d / \\sum_d \\|w_d - w_g\\|^2)$ with $V_d$ the naive $n$-out-of-$n$ bootstrap covariance of the long-only weights over 20 resamples recovers $+0.10$ / $+0.15$ (worst cells $-2.6$ / $-0.0$) with amounts $0.18$ against the cross-validated $0.14$ on EMIT: it overshoots, because the long-only weights have coordinates at the boundary and the naive bootstrap is inconsistent there (Andrews 2000; resampled fits flip members between zero and positive weight). The $m$-out-of-$n$ subsampling repair ($m = n/2$, variance scaled by $m/n$; Politis-Romano) gives amounts $0.11$ / $0.12$ against $0.14$ / $0.57$ and gains $+0.43$ / $+0.09$ (worst $-1.3$ / $-0.0$). Reading: the residual pooling amount is not recoverable from resampling to the accuracy the ceiling requires and remains the one cross-validated quantity in the neighbourhood of the long-only estimator, which alone sits within that ceiling

[Proposition 17 of arXiv:2606.14564, 'Upper tails for irregular graphs \\ beyond the mean-field regime'] Suppose that $p \ll 1$ and let $G \subseteq K_n$ be a graph with $O(f \log(1/p))$ edges.
  Suppose further that either $\eps_H = \infty$ or $\eps_H < \infty$ and $p \gg n^{-1/\Delta - \eps_H} (\log(1/p))^K$ for some large constant $K$ that depends only on $H$.
  Then
  \begin{equation*}
    \Ex_G[X]-\Ex[X] \leq \sum_{J\in \cJ} \frac{|\Emb(J,H)|}{|\Aut(H)|} \cdot N(J,G)\cdot n^{v_H-v_J}p^{e_H-e_J}+o(n^{v_H}p^{e_H}).
  \end{equation*}
  Furthermore, if $p \le n^{-1/\Delta-\Omega(1)}$, then
  \[
    \Ex_G[X]-\Ex[X] \leq \sum_{J\in \cJ^*} \frac{|\Emb(J,H)|}{|\Aut(H)|} \cdot N(J,G)\cdot n^{v_H-v_J}p^{e_H-e_J}+o(n^{v_H}p^{e_H}).
  \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 14 (Uniform local bound for zero-truncated Poisson sums) of arXiv:2604.26298, 'The Expiring Coupon Collector\\ Sliding-Window Surjection Flux and Rare-Entry Laws'] Let \(N\ge2\), \(m\ge N+1\), and let \(\tau=\tau_{N,m}>0\) be the unique
solution of
\[
        \frac{\tau}{1-e^{-\tau}}=\frac{m}{N}.
\]
Let \(D_1,\ldots,D_N\) be iid zero-truncated Poisson variables with parameter
\(\tau\):
\[
        \Pbb(D_i=k)=\frac{\tau^k}{k!(e^\tau-1)},\qquad k\ge1.
\]
Write
\[
        \mu_\tau=\Ebb D_i=\frac{\tau}{1-e^{-\tau}},
        \qquad
        \sigma_\tau^2=\Var(D_i),
        \qquad
        B=N\sigma_\tau^2.
\]
Assume \(0<\tau\le C_0\log N\). If \(B\to\infty\), then
\[
        \Pbb(D_1+\cdots+D_N=m)
        =
        \frac{1+o(1)}{\sqrt{2\pi B}},
\]
uniformly in this range. Consequently, for some constants \(c,C>0\),
depending only on \(C_0\),
\[
        \Pbb(D_1+\cdots+D_N=m)\ge c\,m^{-C}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(N\). If \(B\) is bounded, the same polynomial
lower bound still holds.

body:
[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked; depends on the companion memo on Problem 20.2] This is the boundary and condensation part of the answer recorded for Svante Janson's Problem 20.3 in Simply generated trees, conditioned Galton-Watson trees, random allocations and condensation, Probability Surveys 9 (2012), arXiv:1112.0510. Use Janson's balls-in-boxes setting with weights w_j, generating function Phi, radius rho, Psi(t) = t Phi'(t)/Phi(t), nu = lim_{t up to rho} Psi(t), m/n -> lambda, pi the tilted law at tau = rho when lambda >= nu, and N_d the number of boxes with d balls. In the two regimes not covered by the finite-variance mean-conditioning theorem, (c) lambda = nu with sigma^2 = infinity and (d) lambda > nu, the natural analogue of the Gaussian limit has variance sigma_d^2 = pi_d(1-pi_d). In (d) the constraint is absorbed by the condensate rather than by the bulk. The record asserts that this analogue holds under regular variation of the tail, by the argument of Thevenin's Theorem 6.7 in case (d), and fails in general. The failure rests on two constructions, Theorems A and B of the companion memo on Problem 20.2. Theorem A is a subcritical law conditioned at lambda = 1 > nu, that is, sum of the xi_i equal to n-1, for which (N_1 - n pi_1)/sqrt(n) converges to a non-degenerate two-point law. Theorem B is a law with nu = 1 and sigma^2 = infinity, conditioned at lambda = 1, for which (N_1 - n pi_1)/sqrt(n) converges to a mixture of two Gaussians. Assuming those two theorems, a Gaussian limit for the box counts in regimes (c) and (d) does not hold without a further regularity condition on the tail. The record identifies local flatness of the tail at the scale the conditioning must supply as the dividing line. This is an unrefereed campaign result, and the counterexamples are proved in the companion memo, not in this record.
The conditioning events have positive probability.
The counterexample construction is reported, rather than proved within this record.

body:
[Definition 23 (Vertex condition) of arXiv:2608.15805, 'Spectral duality structures and the Fisher--Rao geometry of reset distributions'] The structure satisfies the \emph{vertex condition}
\textup{(V)} if there is $\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}$ such that for
every active orbit $O$ and both of its sites $z\in O$,
\[
\varepsilon\,\mathcal W\bigl[\varphi_O,\,s(z;\cdot)\bigr](\gamma)>0
\qquad\text{for all }\gamma\in(0,1).
\]
Equivalently, since
\[
\frac{\partial}{\partial\gamma}
\left(\frac{\varphi_O}{s_z}\right)
=\frac{\mathcal W[\varphi_O,s_z]}{s_z^{2}},
\qquad s_z>0,
\]
each ratio $\varphi_O(\gamma)/s(z;\gamma)$, $z\in O$, is strictly
monotone in $\gamma$, in the same direction for all orbits and both
orbit sites. Only these $2r$ scalar ratios
enter the theorem below, and the condition involves only scalar
functions of $\gamma$.

Two remarks on the shape of \textup{(V)}. First, it is stated
relative to the orbit representatives fixed once and for all in
Section~\ref{subsec:inherited-structure}: reversing the
representative of an orbit replaces $\mathbf d_O$ by
$-\mathbf d_O$, hence $\varphi_O$ by $-\varphi_O$ and both of that
orbit's Wronskians by their negatives. The genuinely invariant
content of \textup{(V)} is therefore the \emph{intra-orbit}
requirement that the two Wronskians of a given orbit share a sign;
the common value of $\varepsilon$ across orbits is a normalisation.
That it is always achievable is worth stating precisely: the choice
of representative is made \emph{independently in each orbit}, and
reversing it in a single orbit $O$ sends
$\mathbf d_O\mapsto-\mathbf d_O$,
$\varphi_O\mapsto-\varphi_O$, hence
$\mathcal W[\varphi_O,s(z;\cdot)]\mapsto
-\mathcal W[\varphi_O,s(z;\cdot)]$ at both $z\in O$ and leaves every
other orbit untouched. So if each orbit separately has a constant
Wronskian sign, the $r$ signs can be aligned one orbit at a time.
The substantive hypothesis is thus the intra-orbit one; the global
$\varepsilon$ follows. Second, and
consequently, the conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:vertex-sign} is
orientation-independent, since only the product
$\varepsilon\cdot\operatorname{sgn}[\mathbf d_O]_z$ appears there,
and that product is unchanged by a reversal.
title: Vertex condition

[Corollary 5 of arXiv:2608.17562, '2608.17562'] Moment bounds.
     Let $(X_{i})_{i \ge 1}$ be a sequence of nonnegative \iid random variables with common distribution function $F$. Assume that $\widebar{F} \in \SRV{\alpha}{\rho}$, with $\alpha > 0$, $\rho < 0$ and auxiliary function~$A$.
    Then, there exists $C>0$ such that for every $b \in (0,\alpha)$
 we have 
 \begin{equation}
   
	\vert \esp[Z_{n}^{b}] - \esp[Z^{b}] \vert \leq C\Big(\frac{1}{n} + A(a_n)\Big),
 \quad n \geq 1, 
\end{equation}
if the $X_{i}$ are continuous random variables.
 If not, then for every $b \in (0, \alpha)$ and
 $\delta \in (1, \alpha / b )$, there exists a constant $C_{\delta}$ such that 
\[
\vert \esp[Z_{n}^{b}] - \esp[Z^{b}]\vert \leq C_{\delta}\Big(\frac{1}{n} + A(a_n)\Big)^{1 - {1}/{\delta}}, \quad n \geq 1.
\]
title: Corollary 5 of arXiv:2608.17562

body:
Let T be a first-order theory satisfying all three hypotheses: (i) T is consistent; (ii) T is effectively axiomatized: its set of axioms is computably enumerable (equivalently, by Craig's trick, computably decidable after re-axiomatization), so theoremhood is computably enumerable; (iii) T interprets enough arithmetic - it suffices that T contains or interprets Robinson arithmetic Q. Then T is incomplete: there is a sentence G in the language of T (arithmetical under the interpretation) such that T proves neither G nor the negation of G. Consequently no consistent, effectively axiomatized theory interpreting Q is complete; in particular Peano arithmetic and ZFC, if consistent, are incomplete. Godel's original 1931 argument additionally assumed omega-consistency to rule out T proving the negation; Rosser's 1936 refinement, stated here, needs only consistency. All three hypotheses are necessary: complete consistent extensions of Q exist but are not effectively axiomatized (e.g. true arithmetic), effectively axiomatized complete consistent theories exist that do not interpret Q (e.g. the theory of dense linear orders, or Presburger arithmetic), and an inconsistent theory proves everything.
T is consistent
T is effectively axiomatized (computably enumerable axiom set)
T interprets Robinson arithmetic Q

the exponents defined in Chatterjee (2013) are assumed to exist
first-passage percolation on Z^d
NO nearly-Gamma assumption on the weight law
conclusion is the single inequality chi <= 2 xi - 1, not the equality

IN THE AUTHORS' OWN WORDS: 'we show that under the assumption that exponents defined in Chatterjee (2013) exist, one has the relation chi <= 2 xi - 1. One advantage of our argument is that it does not require the "nearly Gamma" assumption of Chatterjee (2013).'
WHY THE SPLIT MATTERS: quoting 'Auffinger-Damron proved the scaling relation' overstates it in two ways at once - it upgrades an inequality to an equality, and it hides that the exponents are still only assumed to exist. The other inequality's first proof appeared in a model of a Brownian particle in a Poissonian potential; in FPP a version of chi >= 2 xi - 1 goes back to Newman-Piza (1995).
SOURCE: Auffinger, A. and Damron, M. (2014), 'A simplified proof of the relation between scaling exponents in first-passage percolation', Ann. Probab. 42, no. 3, 1197-1211; arXiv:1109.0523v2.
VERIFICATION STATUS: theorem-checked-against-source. The v2 abstract states the hypothesis, the conclusion and the dropped assumption in full; the proof was not read.
title: Auffinger-Damron (2014) reprove only ONE of the two inequalities in the first-passage percolation scaling relation - they obtain chi <= 2 xi - 1, still assuming that the exponents defined in Chatterjee (2013) exist, but WITHOUT Chatterjee's 'nearly Gamma' assumption. So the nearly-Gamma hypothesis is removable for the '<=' direction and, as of the survey, not for the equality.

Equivalently, $X$ is almost surely a single tree-like equivalence class. Hence the expected signature is itself a signature only in the degenerate deterministic case; in general it lies in the tensor algebra but outside the group of group-like elements.

[Lemma lem_position_slopes of arXiv:2608.09105, 'Longest convex chains with i.i.d.\ points'] Let $f\colon[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}$ be continuous and convex.
Let us write $\mathsf{A} = (a,f(a))$ and $\mathsf{B} = (b,f(b))$.
Given a set
\eq{
\mathcal{C} = \{(x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_n,y_n)\}\subset\mathsf{Tri}_f(a,b)\setminus\{\mathsf{A},\mathsf{B}\} \quad \text{such that} \quad
a \leqslant x_1 \leqslant \cdots \leqslant x_n \leqslant b,
}
let us write $\mathsf{P}_i = (x_i,y_i)$.
Then the following two statements are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]

\item 
$\{\mathsf{A},\mathsf{B}\}\cup\mathcal{C}$ is in convex position.

\item 
$\mathrm{Slope}(\mathsf{A},\mathsf{P}_1)<\mathrm{Slope}(\mathsf{P}_1,\mathsf{P}_2)<\cdots<\mathrm{Slope}(\mathsf{P}_{n-1},\mathsf{P}_n)<\mathrm{Slope}(\mathsf{P}_n,\mathsf{B})$.

\end{enumerate}

body:
Let A be an INCREASING event depending on the states of a FINITE set E of edges, and let P_p be the product measure with density p. Then p -> P_p(A) is a polynomial in p, hence smooth, and d/dp P_p(A) = sum_{e in E} P_p( e is pivotal for A ) = E_p[ N(A) ], where N(A) is the number of pivotal edges. Equivalently the derivative is the TOTAL INFLUENCE. The monotonicity hypothesis matters: for a general event the correct statement is the Margulis-Russo formula d/dp P_p(A) = sum_e [ P_p(A with e open) - P_p(A with e closed) ], whose summands can be negative and which reduces to Russo's formula exactly when A is increasing. Russo's formula is the bridge from influence estimates - Kahn-Kalai-Linial, Talagrand, Friedgut-Kalai - to SHARP THRESHOLDS: a lower bound on the total influence of order log(1/(p(1-p))) forces P_p(A) to rise from eps to 1 - eps over a parameter window of width O(1/log n). [Russo (1981), Margulis (1974); see Grimmett, Percolation, 2nd ed., Theorem 2.25]

for general events use the Margulis-Russo form with signed summands

Lewin's 2022 review discusses finite-temperature Riesz phase transitions in Section VI through nonuniqueness and symmetry breaking of Gibbs point processes, and reports numerical BCC/FCC phase diagrams in three dimensions. Its Conjecture 38 in Section IV.B instead concerns zero-temperature equilibrium configurations. Proving that conjecture, or finite phonon variance around an assumed lattice, does not by itself construct a positive-temperature crystalline Gibbs state.
Lewin review version 2, 2022-04-30
The source's finite-beta Gibbs class is stated directly for short-range s>d; long-range Gibbs specifications require separate formulation.
title: Finite-temperature Riesz phase versus ground-state crystallization

[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked; the recursion is integrated exactly against two published closed-form values as a control] This is the campaign answer to Conjecture 1 of H. Stepanyants, P. L. Krapivsky, H. Hartle and D. Krioukov, The rank and layer distributions in random recursive trees, arXiv:2608.04303. Let the Poisson-weighted infinite tree have root position zero, with children of each vertex at the points of an independent rate-one Poisson process on (0,infinity), translated by their parent's position. Let M_k be the minimum position of generation k, and set M_0=0. Define s_0(y)=1 for y>=0 and s_k(y)=1-exp(-integral_0^y s_{k-1}(z)dz) for k>=1. Put bar_ell_k=integral_0^infinity s_k(y)exp(-y)dy and ell_k=bar_ell_k-bar_ell_{k+1}. In the source, ell_k is the limiting fraction of vertices in layer k of a random recursive tree, formed by joining each new vertex j uniformly to one of vertices 1,...,j-1; layer zero consists of the initial leaves, and subsequent layers are obtained by successive leaf removals. Let e be the base of the natural logarithm. There is a constant C_star in (0,infinity) such that bar_ell_k exp(k/e) k^(3/(2e)) -> C_star and ell_k exp(k/e) k^(3/(2e)) -> (1-exp(-1/e)) C_star. More precisely, if M_star denotes the distributional limit of M_k-[k/e+(3/(2e))log k] furnished by the cited branching-random-walk minimum theorem, then C_star=E[exp(-M_star)]. In particular both tails have order exp(-k/e) k^(-3/(2e)). The proof uses Addario-Berry and Ford's Poisson-Dirichlet branching random walks, Annals of Applied Probability 23 (2013), Theorems 1.1-1.2, and Aidekon's Convergence in law of the minimum of a branching random walk, Annals of Probability 41 (2013), as stated in the record. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
The stated published minimum-location, tail, and limit theorems apply to this Poisson branching walk.

That walk is not a generic one. It is the walk whose displacement vector has *exponential steps* (the $j$-th child sits at the sum of $j$ independent exponentials), which is exactly the class treated by Addario-Berry and Ford, *Poisson–Dirichlet branching random walks*, Ann. Appl. Probab. 23 (2013) 283–307. Their Theorem 1.1 states, for this class,
$$\widetilde M_n := \mathrm{median}(M_n) = \frac ne + \frac{3}{2e}\log n + O(1), \tag{2}$$
uniformly over the class, and their Theorem 1.2 gives uniform exponential tails: for every $c_1 < e$ and $c_2 < 1$,
$$\mathbb{P}\big(M_n \le \widetilde M_n - x\big) \ll_{c_1} e^{-c_1 x}, \qquad \mathbb{P}\big(M_n \ge \widetilde M_n + x\big) \ll_{c_2} e^{-c_2 x} \qquad (n \ge 1,\ x \ge 0). \tag{3}$$
Equation (2) is precisely the conjectured (A12), velocity selection included.

## Conjecture 1 is a theorem

**Theorem 2.** There are absolute constants $0 < c < C < \infty$ with
$$c \le \bar\ell_k\,e^{k/e}\,k^{3/(2e)} \le C \qquad (k \ge 1),$$
that is, $\bar\ell_k = \exp[-k/e - \tfrac{3}{2e}\log k - O(1)]$. The same holds for $\ell_k$, so Conjecture 1 holds as stated.

*Proof.* Write $D_k = M_k - \widetilde M_k$, so $\bar\ell_k = e^{-\widetilde M_k}\,\mathbb{E}[e^{-D_k}]$ by Theorem 1. For the upper bound take $c_1 = 2$ in (3), which is legitimate since $2 < e$: with $K$ the implied constant,
$$\mathbb{E}[e^{-D_k}] \le 1 + \sum_{j\ge 0} e^{\,j+1}\,\mathbb{P}(D_k \le -j) \le 1 + eK\sum_{j \ge 0}e^{-j} < \infty,$$
uniformly in $k$. For the lower bound, $\mathbb{E}[e^{-D_k}] \ge \mathbb{P}(D_k \le 0) \ge 1/2$ by the definition of the median. Now insert (2). For $\ell_k$: the upper bound is immediate from $\ell_k \le \bar\ell_k$, and the lower bound follows from Theorem 3 below; unconditionally it already follows for a positive density of $k$, since summing the telescoping identity $\sum_{k=j}^{j+L-1}\ell_k = \bar\ell_j - \bar\ell_{j+L}$ and choosing $L$ with $e^{-L/e} \le c/(2C)$ gives some $k \in [j, j+L)$ with $\ell_k \ge (c/2L)\,e^{-j/e}j^{-3/(2e)}$. $\square$

**Theorem 3.** $\bar\ell_k\,e^{k/e}k^{3/(2e)} \to C^* \in (0,\infty)$ and $\ell_k\,e^{k/e}k^{3/(2e)} \to (1 - e^{-1/e})\,C^*$.

*Proof.* Aïdékon, *Convergence in law of the minimum of a branching random walk*, Ann. Probab. 41 (2013), gives $M_k - (k/e + \tfrac{3}{2e}\log k) \Rightarrow M^*$ for a class of walks that includes this one (Addario-Berry and Ford say so explicitly in their Remark 2). The family $e^{-(M_k - \widetilde M_k)}$ is uniformly integrable by the computation above with $c_1 = 2 > 1$, so the exponential moments converge: $\bar\ell_k e^{k/e}k^{3/(2e)} \to C^* := \mathbb{E}[e^{-M^*}] \in (0,\infty)$. Let d>=1 and A,X be arbitrary real d-by-d matrices. Use full unnormalized linear attention Att(H)=H+sum_i V_i H (K_i H)^T(Q_i H), with the feedforward contribution set to zero. There exist two layers, each with two attention heads and hidden width 4d, that send the d-token state H=[X; A^T; 0_(d by d); I_d] to [X(2I_d-A X); A^T; 0_(d by d); I_d]. If A is symmetric, one such layer suffices. The matrices are encoded as input state blocks; this is an exact construction in the paper's linear-attention model.

[Lemma Lower Bound for correlation of arXiv:2411.09614, 'Moment estimates for the stochastic heat equation on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds'] Suppose $\sec_M\geq-K_2>-\infty$. Let $x,y\in M$, and let $z=d(x,y)$ denote the distance between $x$ and $y$. 
    The kernel $G_\alpha(x,y)$ satisfies the lower bound $$G_\alpha(x,y)\geq \overline{G}_{\alpha}(z)$$
    where the positive function $\overline{G}_\alpha$ which satisfies $\dv{\overline{G}_\alpha}{z}<0$ and the asymptotics \begin{align*}
        &\overline{G}_{\alpha}(z)\sim_{z\uparrow+\infty} e^{-z^2},& \alpha>0,\\
        &\overline{G}_{\alpha}(z)\sim_{z\downarrow0} z^{2\alpha-n},&\alpha<\frac{n}{2},\\
        &\overline{G}_{\alpha}(z)\sim_{z\downarrow0} \abs{\log z},&\alpha=\frac{n}{2},\\

body:
Let X_1, X_2, ... be independent and identically distributed real random variables with mean 0 and variance 1, and S_k = X_1 + ... + X_k. Define the rescaled random continuous path W_n(t) = n^{-1/2} ( S_{floor(n t)} + (n t - floor(n t)) X_{floor(n t) + 1} ) for t in [0, 1], the linear interpolation of the random walk with time scaled by n and space by sqrt(n). Then W_n converges in distribution, as a random element of C[0, 1] with the uniform norm, to a standard Brownian motion W on [0, 1]. Consequently, for every functional Phi : C[0, 1] -> R that is continuous almost surely with respect to the Wiener measure, Phi(W_n) converges in distribution to Phi(W): the law of the maximum of the walk, of its time spent positive, of its first hitting time of a level, all converge to the Brownian laws, whatever the increment distribution. The same holds in the Skorokhod space D[0, 1] for the uninterpolated step process. Finite variance is essential; with infinite variance the limits are stable processes under different scaling.
X_i independent, identically distributed, E X_1 = 0, Var X_1 = 1 (finite variance is essential)

Tightness in C[0, 1]: W_n(0) = 0, and the modulus of continuity is controlled by a maximal inequality for the partial sums. Cut [0, 1] into about 1/delta blocks of length delta; an oscillation larger than epsilon over some pair s, t with |s - t| <= delta forces an oscillation larger than epsilon/3 inside one block, and Ottaviani's inequality bounds the probability of that by twice the tail P(|S_m| > (epsilon/3) sqrt(n) - sqrt(2 m)) with m about n delta, which by the central limit theorem is of Gaussian size, of order exp(-c epsilon^2 / delta), for large n. A union over the 1/delta blocks is then of order (1/delta) exp(-c epsilon^2 / delta), which tends to 0 as delta -> 0 uniformly in n large, and the finitely many small n are handled by the continuity of each W_n. So the sequence is tight in C[0, 1]. By Prokhorov's theorem every subsequence has a further subsequence converging in distribution in C[0, 1]; every such limit has the finite-dimensional laws of Brownian motion and continuous paths, hence is Brownian motion (a law on C[0, 1] is determined by its finite-dimensional distributions), so the whole sequence converges. [Lemma lem:thinning-preserves-overlap of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] Let $G=(I,J,M)$ be finite with $|J|=n\ge2$. Choose $J_0\subseteq J$ uniformly from $\binom J{n_0}$, where $2\le n_0\le n$, and let $G_0:=G[J_0]$. Then
\[
\mathbb E\,\eta(G_0)=\eta(G).
\]
Consequently, for every $\alpha>0$,
\[
\mathbb P\big(\eta(G_0)>\alpha\big)\le\frac{\eta(G)}{\alpha}.
\]

[Prop 17 ({\cite[Proposition~9.4.26) of arXiv:2609.02561, 'NON-NEF LOCI IN MIXED CHARACTERISTIC'] {Laz}}]
With notation as above, let $A$ be a globally generated ample line bundle, $M$ be a line bundle on $X$, and $n$ be a positive integer such that $n\geq\max_{s\in S}\dim X_{s}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
If $M-(K_X +\Delta)$ is big and nef,
then $\J(X,\Delta)\otimes\sO_{X}(nA+M)$ is globally generated.
\item
If $M-(K_X +\Delta)-D$ is big and nef, then $\J(X,\Delta,\|D\|)\otimes\sO_{X}(nA+M)$ is globally generated.
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Proposition 10 of arXiv:2608.21551, '\bf Sparse Separable Factor Analysis in the Complex Domain with an Application to Local Fi'] For $j=1,\ldots,d$, let $\Lambdab_j\in\CC^{p_j\times k_j}$ denote the true loading matrix and $\widehat{\Lambdab}_j$ denote its estimate. Define the orthogonal projectors onto their column spaces by
\begin{align*}
  \Pb_j
  &=
  \Lambdab_j
  \left(
    \Lambdab_j^\star\Lambdab_j
  \right)^+
  \Lambdab_j^\star,
  \qquad
  \widehat{\Pb}_j
  =
  \widehat{\Lambdab}_j
  \left(
    \widehat{\Lambdab}_j^\star
    \widehat{\Lambdab}_j
  \right)^+
  \widehat{\Lambdab}_j^\star,
\end{align*}
where $+$ denotes the Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse. The null-space projection error is
\begin{align}
  \operatorname{err}_{\Pb_j}^2
  &=
  \left\|
    \left(
      \Ib_{p_j}-\widehat{\Pb}_j
    \right)
    \Pb_j
  \right\|_F^2.
  
\end{align}
Let
\begin{align*}
  r_j
  &=
  \operatorname{rank}(\Lambdab_j),
  \qquad
  \widehat{r}_j
  =
  \operatorname{rank}(\widehat{\Lambdab}_j),
  \qquad
  r_{\min,j}
  =
  \min(r_j,\widehat{r}_j).
\end{align*}
Denote the principal angles between the column spaces of $\Lambdab_j$ and $\widehat{\Lambdab}_j$ by
\begin{align*}
    0
  \leq
  \theta_{(j)1}
  \leq
  \cdots
  \leq
  \theta_{(j)r_{\min,j}}
  \leq
  \frac{\pi}{2}.
\end{align*}
Then,
\begin{align}
  \operatorname{err}_{\Pb_j}^2
  &=
  r_j-r_{\min,j}
  +
  \sum_{i=1}^{r_{\min,j}}
  \sin^2\left(\theta_{(j)i}\right),
  
\end{align}
where the sum \eqref{eq:appendix-null-err-proj-angle} is interpreted as zero when $r_{\min,j}=0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 10 of arXiv:2608.21551

body: In mathematics, philosophy, linguistics, and computer science, first-order logic (FOL), also called predicate logic, predicate calculus, or quantificational logic, is a type of formal system. First-order logic uses quantified variables over non-logical objects, and allows the use of sentences that contain variables. Rather than propositions such as "all humans are mortal", in first-order logic one can have expressions in the form "for all x, if x is a human, then x is mortal", where "for all x" is a quantifier, x is a variable, and "... is a human" and "... is mortal" are predicates. This distinguishes it from propositional logic, which does not use quantifiers or relations; in this sense, first-order logic is an extension of propositional logic.

[Theorem thm:potential-identities-results of arXiv:2608.18320, 'Asymptotics for Beta-Splitting Trees via Homogeneous Fragmentations and Meromorphic Potent'] For every $\beta>-2$ and $n\ge2$, the following identities hold.
    \begin{enumeratei}
    
    \item For every $t\ge0$, the continuous height and the expected total length satisfy
    \begin{equation}
            \mathsf P(D_n>t)=\mathsf E\bigl(F_n(\xi_t)\bigr),
            \qquad
            \mathsf E D_n=\mathcal U_\beta F_n,
            \qquad\text{and}\qquad
            \mathsf E\Lambda_n=\mathcal U_\beta H_n.
    \end{equation}
    
    \item The expected discrete height satisfies
    \begin{equation}
            \mathsf E L_n=\sum_{j=2}^n a_\beta(n,j),
            \qquad\text{where}\qquad
            a_\beta(n,j)
            =
            \phi_\beta(j-1)\binom{n-1}{j-1}
            \mathcal U_\beta G_{n,j}.
    \end{equation}
    
    \item Let $M_{n-1}$ be the maximum of $n-1$ independent exponential random
    variables of rate $1$, independent of $\xi$. Then
    \begin{equation}
            D_n\stackrel{d}=T_{M_{n-1}},
            \qquad\text{where}\qquad
            T_x:=\inf\{t\ge0:\xi_t\ge x\}.
    \end{equation}
    
    \end{enumeratei} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. Fix an integer K>=1. Let U_N in R^(N by M) and V_N in R^(P by M) be independent arrays with fixed centered symmetric iid real entry laws of variance one and finite absolute moments of order 2K+2. Assume P/N and M/N remain bounded above and away from zero. Put X_N=U_N V_N^T/sqrt(N), and let X_N^G use independent standard Gaussian factors of the same dimensions. For every j=1,...,K, the coefficient of s^j in the normalized finite-size Gaussian-channel MI I(X_N;sqrt(s)X_N+G)/(NP) differs from its Gaussian-factor counterpart by O_K(1/N), with constants allowed to depend on the fixed moments and aspect bounds. If both aspect ratios have positive finite limits, every coefficient has a finite prior-independent Gaussian limit. The unnormalized finite-size order-K Taylor remainder obeys |R_K(s)|<=[2^K(2K)!/(2(K+1)!)] E||vec X_N||^(2K+2) s^(K+1) for s>=0. The proof cancels articulation entropy graphs using chi_G derivative at one, then uses connected product-cumulant partitions and Euler surface power counting to show every higher factor cumulant loses a free index. This is not a size-uniform remainder or an expansion of the thermodynamic MI; asymmetric factor laws are not covered.
Fixed positive integer K
Fixed real symmetric iid unit-variance factor laws with finite absolute 2K+2 moments
Independent U_N,V_N and standard Gaussian observation noise
Positive aspect bounds; convergent aspect ratios only for the coefficient-limit conclusion
Finite-size coefficients, nats; no exchange of limits

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:d87f6a5266bf32d2a0fa38de889ccd6afb7ba56f079baf4df7d32c8b269866d4","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/d8/d87f6a5266bf32d2a0fa38de889ccd6afb7ba56f079baf4df7d32c8b269866d4.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:58dc3304a4b00a408b529761b6990c1ca2d7e3bc96d8ced9ee22a0ee2572b6a8","bundle_entry_key":"iid-product-mi-all-fixed-coefficients-w718","bundle_id":"population.t287-entropy-chromatic-and-all-fixed-coefficients-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian channels and extensive-rank matrix inference","draft":"w718/bundle_003.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.gaussian_channels:iid-product-mi-all-fixed-coefficients-w718","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# All fixed Taylor coefficients: symmetric iid factor laws

Target 1. Proof draft, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. This is
about finite-size Taylor coefficients, not a uniform expansion of
the thermodynamic mutual information. The planar dual lemma in
Section 4 is the step that most needs independent scrutiny.

## 1. Precise theorem

Fix a positive integer K. U_N in R^(N by M) and V_N in R^(P by M)
are independent arrays. Each array has iid entries from a fixed real
symmetric law of mean zero and variance one, and both entry laws
have finite absolute moments of order 2K+2. Let P/N and M/N stay
bounded above and away from zero. Put X_N=U_N V_N^T/sqrt(N). Let
X_N^G be the same product with independent standard Gaussian factors.
Independent channel noise is standard Gaussian in R^(N by P).

For j=1,...,K let a_j(N) and a_j^G(N) be the coefficients of s^j
in the right Taylor polynomials at zero of

 I(X_N;sqrt(s)X_N+G)/(NP),
 I(X_N^G;sqrt(s)X_N^G+G)/(NP),

respectively, with natural logarithms.

For the dossier's channel Y=X_N+sqrt(Delta)G, an invertible rescaling
of Y gives sqrt(s)X_N+G with s=1/Delta. Since UV^T and X_N differ
by a fixed invertible scaling, their mutual information with Y is
the same. These are therefore the finite-size 1/Delta coefficients.
The coefficient comparison is

                    a_j(N)-a_j^G(N)=O_K(1/N).       (1)

The implied constants may depend on the fixed entry laws' moments
and aspect-ratio bounds. If P/N->alpha and M/N->beta in (0,infinity),
each coefficient sequence has a finite limit. The limits depend only
on alpha,beta and coincide for all these symmetric factor laws.

In each finite dimension the polynomial through order K has the
explicit unnormalized remainder

 |R_K(s)| <= [2^K (2K)!/(2(K+1)!)]
                         E||vec X_N||^(2K+2) s^(K+1), s>=0.  (2)

The bound (2) is not uniform in N and does not prove an expansion
of the limiting MI. The same finite-size bound applies to X_N^G.

## 2. What remains after the entropy diagram cancellations

Write d=NP, b=M/N and a=s/(1+bs). The standardized output has
covariance I_d. Relative to the standard Gaussian, let its density
be 1+q. For bounded symmetric vector inputs its formal Hermite
generating series is

                  exp(sum_(k>=4 even) C_k:t^k a^(k/2)/k!).

Here C_k is the ordered cumulant tensor of vec X_N. At fixed SNR
order <=K this uses finitely many tensors and contractions only.
Normal-ordered Gaussian products are evaluated from the exact identity

 E product_h exp(t_h.G-|t_h|^2/2)
                         =exp(sum_(h<l) t_h.t_l).

Hence each full Wick pairing pairs endpoints in different Hermite
factors. Put a vertex at each cumulant tensor and an edge at each
paired pair of endpoints. Its loopless multigraph G has degrees
even and at least four. A graph with e edges carries a^e, with
e<=K in the coefficient calculation.

The finite algebraic lemma entropy_chromatic_identity.md proves:
after common endpoint factorials and tensor contractions are
extracted, the grouping weight of this graph is chi_G'(1).
The proof uses distinct formal labels on tensor vertices, proper
coloring partitions, and the scalar entropy expansion. It applies
before equal tensor labels are identified and summed.

Since there are no isolated vertices, every disconnected graph has
zero weight. A connected graph with an articulation vertex also has
zero weight. Thus only connected graphs with one block survive.
Parallel-edge two-vertex graphs count as one block. A single-edge
graph cannot occur because all tensor degrees are at least four.

The covariance-matched entropy identity is

 I(X_N;sqrt(s)X_N+G)=d log(1+bs)/2-D(output_standardized || gamma_d).

Its first term depends only on b. It suffices to compare the
finitely many retained cumulant contractions in D at each order.

## 3. Exact raw-factor cumulant expansion and index monomials

For a single rank-one summand W_ij=u_i v_j,

 C_k(W)=sum_(rho join sigma=1)
   product_(B in rho) kappa_|B|(u)
   product_(C in sigma) kappa_|C|(v)
                            delta_rho(i)delta_sigma(j).      (3)

The partitions rho,sigma are on the k tensor positions; delta_rho
requires equality of the row indices in each block, and delta_sigma
does the same for columns. This standard cumulant-of-products
identity has a short direct proof: first expand moments of the
independent raw u and v families in cumulants. In the outer
moment-to-cumulant inversion, a fixed raw partition pair is allowed
exactly in outer partitions pi above rho join sigma. Its coefficient
is sum_(pi>=rho join sigma) mu(pi,1), which equals one if the join
is 1, and zero otherwise by finite partition-lattice inversion.
That inversion also follows from
sum_l S(m,l)(-1)^(l-1)(l-1)!=1_(m=1), obtained by taking coefficients
in log(exp(x))=x. Thus (3) hides no probabilistic limit theorem.

Centering removes singleton blocks. Symmetry removes all odd blocks.
Every retained block has even size >=2. For each local term in (3),
make a bipartite multigraph H: its vertices are the row and column
blocks, and its k edges are the tensor positions. The join condition
makes H connected, and all vertex degrees are even.

Independence of the M rank-one summands gives

                        C_k(X_N)=(M/N^(k/2)) C_k(W).

Consequently, for a fixed contraction graph with v tensor vertices
and e Wick edges, and a choice of local terms (3), its index sum is
exactly a constant in the fixed raw cumulants times

                         M^v N^(c_i-e) P^(c_j),              (4)

where c_i,c_j are the free row and column equality classes.
Different free classes are allowed to take equal numerical values;
there is no distinct-label exclusion or asymptotic counting shortcut.

## 4. Surface lemma, including the strict loss for a higher cumulant

For every local connected even-degree H choose an Euler circuit.
Pair the two incident edges at every visit to a raw vertex along
that circuit. This refines each raw block into pairs. The refined
row and column pairings together form one cycle on all k positions.
Represent that cycle as a polygon with alternating row and column
corners. Each side is one tensor position, with one row and one
column endpoint.

Glue the two sides paired by each Wick edge, identifying row with
row and column with column. The result is a connected closed surface
map, possibly nonorientable. Locally each side belongs to two
polygons and each vertex link is a cycle: vertex equivalence classes
are generated by the adjacent-corner pairings and side gluings.
Thus this is a surface, not a pinched pseudomanifold. Its faces are
the v polygons, its edges are the e Wick pairs, and its vertices
are the refined equality classes c'_i+c'_j. Its dual adjacency graph
is precisely G. The original raw equalities can only merge refined
classes, so c_i<=c'_i and c_j<=c'_j.

For any connected closed surface map,

                   chi=c'_i+c'_j-e+v<=2.                     (5)

One elementary justification, valid without orientability, is to
choose a primal spanning tree. The dual edges complementary to that
tree are connected: otherwise a nonempty proper set of faces has
all its boundary edges in the primal tree. Around every primal vertex
the selected and unselected faces alternate an even number of times,
so this nonempty boundary is an even-degree subgraph and contains a
cycle. A tree cannot contain that subgraph. Choose a dual spanning
tree in the complement. Contracting the primal tree and then merging
faces along the dual tree leaves one vertex, one face, and
e-[(c'_i+c'_j)-1]-(v-1)=2-chi edges. This number is nonnegative.
If it is zero, the remaining cell is a disk with its whole boundary
collapsed to the single vertex, namely a sphere. Tree contractions
and face mergers preserve the underlying surface. Therefore chi=2
implies the original surface is a sphere.

We also need a planar-map fact with its relevant exceptions exposed:
in a connected sphere map whose dual is loopless and has no
articulation vertex, every primal face boundary is a simple cycle.
Here primal loops are additionally excluded by the row/column colors.
Indeed a primal bridge has the same face on both sides and hence
gives a dual loop, so there are no primal bridges. If the primal
has an articulation vertex, take a leaf block of its block-cut tree.
It contains a cycle because there are no bridges. The rest of the
map also contains a cycle, because it contains another non-bridge
block. The rest meets this leaf block at just its cut vertex and
lies in one face f of that block. The faces internal to the leaf
block communicate in the full dual with faces in the rest only
through f. Both sides contain a face other than f, so f is a dual
articulation, a contradiction. Thus the primal has no articulation.
Finally, a repeated vertex on a face boundary of a bridgeless plane
graph would be an articulation: joining the two boundary visits by
an arc within that face gives a separating Jordan curve through
that vertex, with graph edges on both sides. Deleting that vertex
disconnects the two sides. This proves the asserted simple-boundary
property. It includes a two-vertex parallel-edge block; no simplicity
of the edge graph was assumed.

Suppose now that the original term (3) involves a raw cumulant of
order >=4. At least one raw block was split into at least two visits
on the same polygon. If the refined map has chi<=1, then already

                       c_i+c_j-e+v<=1.

If it has chi=2, it is a sphere. Section 2 guarantees that its dual
G is loopless and has no articulation. Its polygon boundary is
therefore simple by the preceding paragraph. The two distinct visits
split from that raw block are distinct global map vertices.
Reimposing the raw block merges at least these two classes. Again

                       c_i+c_j-e+v<=1.                       (6)

For a pure Gaussian-pairing term only (5) is needed; its exponent
is at most two. This completes the surface power-counting lemma.

## 5. Coefficient comparison and analytic scope

Since P and M are comparable to N, equation (4) has size
O(N^(c_i+c_j-e+v)). Every term with a higher raw cumulant is O(N)
by (6); divided by NP it is O(1/N). At fixed K there are finitely
many contraction graphs, local set partitions and pairing choices,
with finite fixed cumulant coefficients. All pure-pairing terms
are exactly the same for U,V and for their Gaussian replacements.
Expanding a^e=s^e/(1+bs)^e adds only universal powers of b.
This proves (1). Pure-pairing exponents are integers <=2, so their
normalized monomials have finite limits when both aspect ratios
converge. The limits are the same for all the stated symmetric laws.

For bounded vector inputs the finite Hermite coefficient extraction
used above is analytic at each finite order, as in
bounded_prior_expansion.md and sixth_order_coefficients.md: Mehler
estimates and hypercontractivity control each fixed chaos truncation
in the L^p norm needed for its finite entropy expansion.

The posterior-replica streaming bound in finite_moment_expansion.md
gives |F^(K)(s)|<=2^K(2K)! E||X||^(2K+2), where
F(s)=E||E[X|sqrt(s)X+G]||^2. Since I^(K+1)=-F^(K)/2, Taylor's
integral remainder is (2). Symmetric vector truncation and covariance
whitening converge in L^(2K+2); the finite polynomial cumulant
contractions and moment bound converge, and Gaussian output entropy
is continuous. This extends the coefficient formulas and remainder
to the finite-moment inputs in Section 1, without assuming an
unbounded-input analytic series or exponential moments.
The truncated vector need not retain a product-factor representation:
only the general finite-vector coefficient identity is extended by
truncation. Formula (3) is then applied to the actual product input.

The proof establishes neither a uniform-in-N remainder nor a
nonzero radius of analyticity of the thermodynamic MI. It therefore
does not prove the conjectured universal low-SNR phase, and it does
not establish an expansion at the first prior-dependent thermodynamic
order. It shows why searching higher fixed finite-size coefficients
cannot reveal such an order for symmetric factors, if this draft's
finite diagram and surface arguments pass independent review.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:5f137222344a62a63677b52bd9ad3cd8fe51757cc1a2ca0ca661d913ec9b26ff","revision_digest":"sha256:ce3122784ffd46e433a9de1d97d722112f4fa6f5793b4706020c470f229a26fd","source_id":"owner:w718:T287:iid-product-mi-all-fixed-coefficients-w718","source_revision":"2026-10-20 claim w718-T287-011 version 2, proof unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma optimal-control-structure:finite-p of arXiv:2605.14149, 'The mean-field limit of online stochastic vector balancing'] Let $p\in[2,\infty)$ and $\delta>0$. Let $\alpha\in\mathbb{A}$ be the unique optimizer for $V_{p,\delta}^{\infty}$. Then, there exists $\hat{\alpha} : [0,1]\times{\mathbb R} \to {\mathbb R}$ such that
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\alpha(t)=\hat{\alpha}(t,X^\alpha(t))$ for all $t\in[0,1]$ almost surely,
        \item $\hat{\alpha}$ points inwards, i.e., $x\hat{\alpha}(t,x) \le 0$ for all $(t,x)\in[0,1]\times{\mathbb R}$,
        \item $\hat{\alpha}$ is odd, i.e., $\alpha(t,x)=-\alpha(t,-x)$ for all $(t,x)\in[0,1]\times{\mathbb R}$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma optimal-control-structure:finite-p of arXiv:2605.14149
