Let Omega in R^n be open. A nondivergence-form operator is Lu = sum_{i,j} a^{ij}(x) D_{ij} u + sum_i b^i(x) D_i u + c(x) u with a^{ij} = a^{ji} real (symmetry is no loss because D_{ij}u is symmetric) and b^i, c real. L is elliptic at x if the matrix (a^{ij}(x)) is positive definite; lambda(x) denotes its smallest eigenvalue. L is uniformly elliptic with constants 0 < lambda <= Lambda if lambda|xi|^2 <= sum a^{ij}(x) xi_i xi_j <= Lambda|xi|^2 for all x (a.e. x for measurable coefficients) and all xi in R^n. Sign convention: here L = +Laplacian when (a^{ij}) = I, b = 0, c = 0, so the maximum principle concerns Lu >= 0 and the favorable sign of the zeroth-order coefficient is c <= 0 (the opposite of the divergence-form convention -div(A grad u) + c u with c >= 0). A classical solution of Lu = f is u in C^2(Omega) with Lu = f pointwise; a strong solution is u in W^{2,p}_loc(Omega) for some 1 <= p <= infinity with Lu = f almost everywhere. If the a^{ij} are C^1 (or Lipschitz), a^{ij} D_{ij} u = D_i(a^{ij} D_j u) - (D_i a^{ij}) D_j u rewrites L in divergence form; for merely measurable a^{ij} the two forms are different theories (De Giorgi-Nash-Moser for divergence form, Krylov-Safonov for nondivergence form).
Omega open in R^n
a^{ij} = a^{ji}, b^i, c real functions on Omega
lambda|xi|^2 <= a^{ij} xi_i xi_j <= Lambda|xi|^2 for uniform ellipticity
title: Uniformly Elliptic Operator in Nondivergence Form and Strong Solutions

Let (X, d) be a metric space. A sequence of Borel probability measures (mu_n)_{n in N} in M_1(X) is sequentially tight if for each epsilon > 0 there exists a collection of compact subsets (K_epsilon^delta)_{delta > 0} of X such that: (i) liminf_{n -> infinity} mu_n(B_{K_epsilon^delta}(delta)) >= 1 - epsilon for every delta > 0, where B_A(delta) = {x in X : dist(x, A) < delta}; and (ii) the subspace K_epsilon := overline{bigcup_{delta > 0} K_epsilon^delta} subset X is complete in the metric d.
(X, d) is a metric space
(mu_n)_{n in N} in M_1(X)
title: Sequential Tightness on Metric Spaces

[Proposition 37 of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] The rate function \(J_a\) is real analytic and strictly convex on
\((0,\infty)\). Moreover, there exist \(\varepsilon_a>0\) and a function
\(h_a\), holomorphic on \(\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|<\varepsilon_a\}\), such that
\[
        J_a(x)
        =
        J_a(0)+x\log x+h_a(x),
        \qquad 0<x<\varepsilon_a,
\]
and, with the principal branch of the logarithm,
\(z\mapsto J_a(0)+z\log z+h_a(z)\) is holomorphic on
\(\{0<|z|<\varepsilon_a\}\setminus(-\varepsilon_a,0]\). In particular, as
\(x\downarrow0\),
\[
        J_a(x)
        =
        J_a(0)+x\log x+\gamma_a x+O(x^2)
\]
for some real constant \(\gamma_a\).

body: Hilbert's basis theorem: if R is a Noetherian ring, then the polynomial ring R[x] is Noetherian; by induction, k[x_1, ..., x_n] over a field k in FINITELY many indeterminates is Noetherian, so every ideal there is finitely generated. Finiteness of the variable set is essential: in k[x_1, x_2, ...] the ideal generated by all the variables has no finite generating set.
title: Hilbert's basis theorem

body: Aldous-Fill Open Problem 4.48(a) is answered in the negative: tau_1 <= tau_0 fails. On the continuous-time birth-and-death chain on {0,1,2} with rate 1 toward 0 and rate eps away from it, tau_0 = 2(1+eps)/(1+eps+eps^2) < 2 while tau_1 -> 2.14619 (the root of e^{-t}(1+t) = 1/e) as eps -> 0: the pair (2,0) separates until the sum of two unit exponentials has arrived. On the path of length k the limiting ratio tau_1/tau_0 is t_k/k with t_k the Gamma(k,1) tail threshold at 1/e (1.0731, 1.0861, 1.0880 at k=4, 1.0868, ...), so sup tau_1/tau_0 lies in [1.0880, 66]. Exact 30-digit check: k=2, eps=0.1 gives tau_0 = 1.981982, tau_1 = 2.010072.

[Prop 5 of arXiv:2608.23450, 'The Oldest Allele in a Moran Model'] For $n\geq1$, the transition kernel $Q_n^{(0,\theta)}=\Lambda_nT_n^{(0,\theta)}\psi_n$ satisfies 
    $$\Lambda_nT_n^{(0,\theta)}=Q_n^{(0,\theta)}\Lambda_n.$$
    Moreover, $Z_n^{(0,\theta)}$ is a time-homogeneous Markov chain with transition kernel $Q_n^{(0,\theta)}$ given explicitly by 
    $$Q_n^{(0,\theta)}(i,j)=r_{i,j}+r_{1,0}\mathbbm{1}(i=1)\upsilon_n^{(0,\theta)}(j)$$
    when the initial distribution of $X_n^{(0,\theta)}$ is of the form $\mu\Lambda_n$.

[Lemma l:remainder2case1 of arXiv:2605.22803, 'Persistence of asymptotic variance under transport:\\ from hyperfluctuation to stealthy hy'] Suppose that $\Phi$ is an invariant locally absolutely square-integrable random measure, and that $K$ is an invariant transport kernel. Let $p\geq 0$ and assume that Condition~(c:condition square-integrable general with p of the paper) is satisfied.
Then $K\Phi$ is locally absolutely square-integrable. Further, for $r>0$,
\begin{equation}
    \lim_{r\to\infty} \frac{1}{r^{d-p}} \BE\bigg[\bigg(\int_{B_{2r}^c} |K|(y, B_r) \, |\Phi|(dy) \bigg)^2\bigg] = 0. 
\end{equation}
\begin{proof}
First of all, by Lemma~(l:stronlgy log-dominating modification of the paper), without loss of generality, we can assume that $\rho$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
    \rho(2r) \leq 4 \rho(r), \quad r\geq 0.
\end{equation}
Further, by Lemmas~(l: simplification to lebesgue of the paper) and~(l:condition reduction lebesgue of the paper), there is an invariant nonnegative transport kernel $L$ such that $L(y)$ has support on $\overline{B_1}+y$ for $y\in\R^d$, that $|\Phi|=L\lambda_d$, and that the invariant nonnegative transport kernel $\tilde{K}:=|K|L$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
    \BE\bigg[\bigg(\int \sqrt{\|x\|^{d+p}\rho(\|x\|)+1}\, \tilde{K}_0(dx)\bigg)^2\bigg] < \infty.
\end{equation}
Let $r>2$. Then,
\begin{align*}
    \int_{B_{2r}^c} |K|(y, B_r) \, |\Phi|(dy) &= \iint_{B_{2r}^c} |K|(z, B_r)\, L(y, dz) \, dy\nonumber\\
    &\leq \int_{B_{2r-1}^c}\int |K|(z, B_r) \, L(y, dz) \, dy\nonumber\\
    &= \int_{B_{2r-1}^c} \tilde{K}(y, B_r)\, dy,
\end{align*}
which simplifies the problem. Now this inequality and a two-times application of the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality yield
\begin{align}
    \BE\bigg[\bigg(\int_{B_{2r}^c} |K|(y, B_r) \, |\Phi|(dy) \bigg)^2\bigg] &\leq \BE\bigg[\bigg(\int_{B_{2r-1}^c} \tilde{K}(y, B_r) \, dy \bigg)^2\bigg] \nonumber\\
    &= \int_{B_{2r-1}^c}\int_{B_{2r-1}^c} \BE\big[\tilde{K}(y, B_r)\tilde{K}(z, B_r)\big] \,dy\,dz \nonumber\\
    &\leq \int_{B_{2r-1}^c}\int_{B_{2r-1}^c} \sqrt{\BE\big[\tilde{K}(y, B_r)^2\big]\BE\big[\tilde{K}(z, B_r)^2\big]} \,dy\,dz \nonumber\\
    &= \bigg(\int_{B_{2r-1}^c}\sqrt{\BE\big[\tilde{K}(y, B_r)^2\big]} \,dy\bigg)^2\nonumber\\
    &= \Bigg(\int_{B_{2r-1}^c}\frac{\sqrt{(\|y\|^{d+p}\rho(\|y\|)+1)\BE\big[\tilde{K}(y, B_r)^2\big]}}{\sqrt{\|y\|^{d+p}\rho(\|y\|)+1}} \,dy\Bigg)^2 \nonumber\\
    &\leq \int_{B_{2r-1}^c} \frac{1}{\|y\|^{d+p}\rho(\|y\|)+1} \, dy\nonumber\\
    &\quad \ \ \times\int_{B_{2r-1}^c} (\|y\|^{d+p}\rho(\|y\|)+1) \BE\big[\tilde{K}(y, B_r)^2\big] \, dy.
\end{align}
For the first factor, we get
\begin{align*}
    \int_{B_{2r-1}^c}\frac{1}{\|y\|^{d+p}\rho(\|y\|)+1} \, dy &= d\kappa_d \int_{2r-1}^\infty \frac{s^{d-1}}{s^{d+p}\rho(s)+1} \, ds \nonumber\\
    &\leq \frac{d\kappa_d}{2^p r^p} \underbrace{\int_{2r-1}^\infty \frac{1}{s\rho(s)+s^{-(d+p-1)}}\, ds}_{a(r):=}.
\end{align*}
Because $\rho$ is strongly log-dominating, we can derive that $a(r)\to 0$ as $r\to\infty$ by the theorem of dominated convergence.
The second factor can be bounded by
\begin{align*}
    &\int_{B_{2r-1}^c}(\|y\|^{d+p}\rho(\|y\|)+1)\BE\big[\tilde{K}(y, B_r)^2\big] \, dy\nonumber\\
    &\quad\ \ = \int_{B_{2r-1}^c}(\|y\|^{d+p}\rho(\|y\|)+1)\BE\big[\tilde{K}_0(B_r-y)^2\big] \, dy\nonumber\\
    &\quad\ \ = \BE\bigg[\iiint(\|y\|^{d+p}\rho(\|y\|)+1)\,  \I\{y\in B_{2r-1}^c, x, z\in B_r-y\}\, \tilde{K}_0(dx)\, \tilde{K}_0(dz)\, dy\bigg]\nonumber\\
    &\quad\ \ \leq \BE\bigg[\iiint(\|y\|^{d+p}\rho(\|y\|)+1)\,  \I\{y\in B_{3\min(\|x\|, \|z\|)}\cap (B_r - x) \cap (B_r-z)\}\nonumber\\

    &\hspace{12cm}\phantom{\, dy} \tilde{K}_0(dx)\, \tilde{K}_0(dz)\bigg]\nonumber\\

[Lemma 18 of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] For a strictly increasing sequence $u_1<\cdots<u_s$ of positive integers, the following statements are equivalent.

\medskip
{\bf (1)} There exists a cyclic $C_{p^s}$-extension of $k((t))$ whose upper jumps are $u_1<\cdots<u_s$.

\smallskip
{\bf (2)} The following conditions hold.

\medskip\noindent
{\bf (2.a)} We have $p\nmid u_1$.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (2.b)} For each $i\in\llbracket2,s\rrbracket$, either $u_i=pu_{i-1}$ or $u_i>pu_{i-1}$ and $p\nmid u_i$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\[
E[S_{\alpha_*}^2]=1, \qquad E[S_{\alpha_*}^4]=3,
\]
while $S_{\alpha_*}$ is not Gaussian. In fact, $E[S_{\alpha_*}^3]\neq 0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:HDL_volume of arXiv:2505.10256, 'Stochastic Oscillators out of equilibrium:\\ scaling limits and correlation estimates'] Let $v_0$ be a bounded real-valued measurable function on $\mathbb T$ and let $\{\mu_N\}_{N\in\mathbb N}$ be a sequence of probability measures on $\Omega_N$ associated to $v_0$ and assume that $\{\mu_N\}_{N\in\mathbb N}$ satisfies Assumption (assump:initial_measure of the paper).  
Moreover, assume that the parameter $\alpha_N$ is taken under the weak asymmetry (equation eq:weak_asymmetry of the paper) with $\kappa=1$.
Then, for every $t\in [0,T]$, the sequence of empirical measures $\{\pi^{v,N}_t\}_{N\in\mathbb N}$ converges in probability to the absolute continuous measure $v(t,u)du$, that is, for any $\delta>0$ and for any $G\in C^2(\mathbb{T})$ we have 
\begin{equation*}
\lim_{N\to\infty}Q^{v,N}_m \bigg(\Big|\langle \pi^{v,N}_{t},G\rangle-\int_{\mathbb T} v(t,u)G(u)du \Big|>\delta\bigg) =0
\end{equation*}
provided $m>5/2$, where $v(t,u)$ is the unique weak solution of the first equation in (equation eq:hdl of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:HDL_volume of arXiv:2505.10256

[Lemma range_estimates of arXiv:2608.00399, 'The Heavy-tailed Frog Model'] Let $Q \in \mathcal{H}_{\alpha, K}$ for some $\alpha, K > 0$. Fix an arbitrary $\varepsilon \in (0, 1)$.
        Then, there exist positive constants $c_0 = c_0(Q, \varepsilon)$ and $c_1 = c_1(Q)$ such that the following holds:
        for 
        any $r \in \mathbb N^+$ and 
        any subset $D \subseteq B_x(r)$ with $|D| \le (1-\varepsilon) |B_x(r)|$, 
        we have 
        \begin{align} 
        \mathbf P_x \left( \, \left\vert \widetilde{\mathrm{R}}\left(\ell(r)\right) \right\vert \ge c_1 \varepsilon f(r) \, \right) &\ge  c_0,
        \end{align}
        where $\widetilde{\mathrm{R}}(k) := \mathrm{R}(k) \cap B_x(r) \setminus D$ and $f(r)$ and $\ell(r)$ are defined as above.
title: Lemma range_estimates of arXiv:2608.00399

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Test the conjecture's consistency by the boundary values and the contour relations alone. Result: The contour relations plus the known boundary values determine the discrete observable up to a subspace of dimension equal to the number of faces minus the number of independent contour relations, which is of the order of the number of vertices, so the observable is far from determined by what is proved; the conjecture is a statement about the actual random-cluster measure, not derivable from the relations alone. A weaker rigorous consequence that IS available: the contour relations imply that the integral of f_delta along any closed contour vanishes, so any subsequential limit of (2 delta)^{-sigma} f_delta, if tight, is holomorphic (Morera), and its boundary behaviour (modulus fixed on the boundary arcs by the boundary conditions) makes (phi')^sigma the unique candidate if the limit is bounded near a and b. Hence the conjecture reduces to tightness plus a priori bounds near the marked points. This reduction is standard for q = 2 and I confirmed it goes through for all q <= 4 given the contour relations; the a priori bounds are the missing input. Key identity: Contour relations + Morera => any tight subsequential limit is holomorphic with the prescribed boundary modulus; uniqueness then forces (phi')^sigma. Obstruction: Tightness and boundary a priori bounds for the observable are unproved for q not 2.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0050-convergence-of-the-parafermionic-observable-to-phi-sigma-for-q-4
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved
title: Attempt on Convergence of the parafermionic observable to (phi')^sigma for q <= 4

\begin{align}

 C_{T,r}\left(V_r(w_0)+1+\|\mathsf p\|_{H^1}^{d_r}\right).

The orders in $V_r$ and $d_r$ are independent of $T$.  The

[Corollary cor:polytope-learning-queries of arXiv:2606.19763, 'Optimal Sparsification of Gaussian Processes'] Let $r\geq1$, let $0<\eps<1/2$, and let $f:\R^n\to\zo$ be an unknown
	Boolean function. 
	There is an algorithm which, given black-box query access to $f$, runs in
	time
	\[
		\poly(n)\cdot
		2^{
			\poly\pbra{
				\log(\alpha(r,\eps/2))/\eps
			}
		}
		= \poly(n)\cdot 2^{\poly(r, 1/\eps)}
	\]

[Proposition 10 of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] Let~\(\chi\) be a Navier--Stokes potential and let \(I^\beta\) and \(I^{\beta\gamma}\) be algebraic source terms. Then the system
\bel{eq:pot-general-sources}
\nabla_\alpha T_\chi^{\alpha\beta}=I^\beta,
\qquad
\nabla_\alpha A_\chi^{\alpha\beta\gamma}=I^{\beta\gamma}
\ee
is symmetric hyperbolic in the interior of the state space, and the particle-number current satisfies
\bel{eq:pot-chain-identity}
\nabla_\alpha\vNumb_\chi^\alpha
=-\beta_\beta I^\beta
-\zeta_{\beta\gamma}I^{\beta\gamma}.
\ee
Moreover, let \(n\) be future timelike and set
\be
U^{\alpha A}
\coloneqq
\frac{\del^2\chi}{\del\beta_\alpha\del\Xi_A},
\qquad
Y^A\coloneqq-n_\alpha U^{\alpha A},
\qquad
\eta_n\coloneqq n_\alpha\vNumb_\chi^\alpha,
\qquad
\Xi=(\beta,\zeta).
\ee
Then \(\eta_n\) is strictly convex as a function of the normal conserved variables~\(Y\).
title: Proposition 10 of arXiv:2608.31171

[Prop UstatTail of arXiv:2609.02743, 'Sharp mean-field estimates for diffusive log/Riesz gases in the Hilbert--Schmidt regime'] There exists a universal constant $L>0$ with the following property.  Let $\{h_{ij}\}_{1\le i,j\le n}$ be bounded, completely degenerate kernels, let $\{\xi_{i}^{(1)},\xi_{j}^{(2)}\}_{1\le i,j\le n}$ be independent random variables in a measurable space $(S,\mathscr{S})$, and define
\begin{align}
A &\coloneqq \max_{1\le i,j\le n} \|h_{ij}\|_{L^\infty},
\qquad\qquad
C^2 \coloneqq  \sum_{1\le i,j\le n} {\mathbb{E}}\brak[\big]{h_{ij}^2(\xi_i^{(1)},\xi_j^{(2)})},\\
B^2 &\coloneqq \max_{1\le i,j\le n}\ \max\brac[\bigg]{\Big\|\sum_{i'=1}^n {\mathbb{E}}\brak[\big]{h_{i'j}^2(\xi_{i'}^{(1)},\cdot)}\Big\|_{L^\infty},\ \Big\|\sum_{j'=1}^n {\mathbb{E}}\brak[\big]{h_{ij'}^2(\cdot,\xi_{j'}^{(2)})}\Big\|_{L^\infty}},\\
D &\coloneqq \sup\ {\mathbb{E}}\brak[\Bigg]{\sum_{1\le i,j\le n}h_{ij}(\xi_i^{(1)},\xi_j^{(2)})\, f_i(\xi_i^{(1)})\, g_j(\xi_j^{(2)})},
\end{align}
where the supremum in $D$ runs over all $f_i,g_j:S\to{\mathbb{R}}$ with ${\mathbb{E}}[\sum_i f_i^2(\xi_i^{(1)})]\le 1$ and ${\mathbb{E}}[\sum_j g_j^2(\xi_j^{(2)})]\le 1$.  Then, for every $t>0$,
\begin{align}
\mathbb{P}\Bigg(\Big|\sum_{1\le i,j\le n}h_{ij}(\xi_i^{(1)},\xi_j^{(2)})\Big| \ge t\Bigg)
\le L\exp\pa*{-\frac{1}{L}\min\brac*{\pa*{\frac{t}{C}}^{2},\ \frac{t}{D},\ \pa*{\frac{t}{B}}^{2/3},\ \pa*{\frac{t}{A}}^{1/2}}}.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop UstatTail of arXiv:2609.02743

[Definition def:lipschitz of arXiv:2609.03980, 'Decay Rates and Domain Dependence of a Coupled Wave-Heat System with Spatially Dependant H'] \begin{enumerate}
    \item Let $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a non-empty domain. We call $\Omega$ a (strongly) \textit{Lipschitz domain} if $n=1$ or if for every $x\in \partial\Omega$, there is an open neighborhood $U_x \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ around $x$, an orthogonal matrix $O_x \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ and a Lipschitz function 
    $\phi_x: \mathbb{R}^{n-1}\to \mathbb{R}$ with 
    \begin{align*}
       O_x (U_x\cap \Omega) = \{(\xi,y) \in \mathbb{R}^{n-1}\times \mathbb{R}~|~ y < \phi_x(\xi) \}\cap O_x(U_x).
    \end{align*}

    
    \item Let $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a non-empty, bounded Lipschitz domain, and let $\Omega_w,\Omega_h\subset \Omega$ be two disjoint, non-empty Lipschitz domains. If 
    $\overline{\Omega}=\overline{\Omega_w\cup \Omega_h}$, we call $(\Omega,\Omega_w,\Omega_h)$ a \textit{Lipschitz interface triple} with interface $\gamma.$ 
    In this case, we set
    $$\Gamma_w  \coloneq  \partial\Omega\backslash\partial\Omega_h, ~~\Gamma_h \coloneq \partial\Omega\backslash\partial\Omega_w,~~ \gamma \coloneq  \partial\Omega_w\backslash\overline{\Gamma_h} = \partial\Omega_h\backslash\overline{\Gamma_w}.$$
    Furthermore, we denote by $\nu_w,\nu_h$ the unit outer normal vectors on $\Gamma_w,\Gamma_h$, which exist almost everywhere due to Rademacher's Theorem for $n\geq 2,$ and trivially everywhere in the case $n=1.$

    
Our assumptions on $(\Omega,\Omega_w,\Omega_h)$ are weaker than the assumptions imposed in  [ines,zuazualongtime].

    \item Let $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a non-empty Lipschitz domain, and let $\Gamma\subset \partial\Omega$ be a non-empty, relatively open subset of the boundary.
    We call $(\Omega,\Gamma)$ an \textit{admissible} Lipschitz pair, if there exists some domain $\Tilde{\Omega}\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ such that 
    $$(\Omega\cup \Gamma\cup \Tilde{\Omega}, \Omega, \Tilde{\Omega})$$ is a Lipschitz interface triple with interface $\Gamma$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Lipschitz interface triples

Guionnet-Huang Theorem1.1, existence and normalization assertion in the bounded-norm, log-regular case. Let m_n>=n, m_n/n->1+gamma for a finite gamma>=0, and rho=(1+gamma)^(-1). Let A_n,B_n be deterministic real n by m_n matrices with sup_n max(||A_n||_op,||B_n||_op)<=K for a finite K. For C=A,B let nu_hat_Cn=(1/(2n))*sum_{i=1}^n (delta_{s_i(C_n)}+delta_{-s_i(C_n)}) be its symmetrized empirical singular-value probability law. Suppose these laws converge weakly to symmetric probabilities nu_hat_A,nu_hat_B. Assume for both limits finite logarithmic energy Sigma(nu)=integral integral log|x-y| dnu(x)dnu(y)>-infinity and finite logarithmic moment integral log|x| dnu(x)>-infinity. Thus their second moments are bounded, and all the source logarithmic regularity conditions are imposed, including at the square endpoint. With independent normalized Haar U in O(n), V in O(m_n), set I_n,m(A_n,B_n)=integral exp(n*Tr(A_n^T*U*B_n*V^T)) dU dV. Then n^(-2)*log I_n,m_n(A_n,B_n) has a finite limit depending only on gamma and the two limiting symmetrized singular laws. In the notation of source equation1.5 that limit is (1/2)*mathcalI^gamma(nu_hat_A,nu_hat_B); this card extracts the existence and normalization assertion, under the displayed stronger bounded-norm/log-regular hypotheses. Consequently, with N=n,M=m_n and J_N,M(A,B)=log I_N,M(A,B)/(N*M), the limit of J is (rho/2)*mathcalI^gamma(nu_hat_A,nu_hat_B), where gamma=1/rho-1. The factor rho converts the source n^2 normalization to n*m. Here gamma is the source aspect parameter called alpha in Guionnet-Huang; rho is the reciprocal aspect ratio called alpha in the Pourkamali-Macris application. The stated case is real orthogonal Haar and uses the exponent n, without an additional beta factor.
Real rectangular deterministic matrices; m_n/n->1+gamma in [1,infinity); independent normalized orthogonal Haar matrices.
Uniform bounded operator norms and weak convergence of the two symmetrized singular-value empirical laws.
Both limiting measures have finite logarithmic energy and logarithmic moment, explicitly imposed for every gamma.

[Defn Chordal link pattern of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] Given $\boldsymbol{z}=\{z_1,z_2,...,z_n\}$ on the real line, a link pattern is a homotopically equivalent class of non-intersecting curves connecting pair of boundary points (links) or connecting boundary points and the infinity (rays). The link patterns with $n$ boundary points and $m$ links are called $(n,m)$-links, denoted by ${\rm LP}(n,m)$.

The number of chordal $(n,m)$-links is given by $|{\rm LP}(n,m)|=C_{n}^{m+1}-C_{n}^{m}$.
title: Chordal link pattern

If eps>0 and M=E|X|^(2+eps)<infinity, then E[|X|^2 1_{|X|>R}]<=M*R^(-eps) for R>0. The power eps is sharp as a scalar envelope: a symmetric atom law with total mass c*2^(-(2+eps)*j)/j^2 at +/-2^j has finite (2+eps)-moment and tail variance of order 2^(-eps*m)/m^2 at R=2^m. This proves neither a lower bound nor an optimal exponent for a circular-law convergence rate.

[Theorem thm:tailrl-finite-unbiasedness of arXiv:2609.02987, 'Tail Likelihood Reinforcement Learning'] The unbiased estimator of  $\nabla_\theta J_{\mathrm{TailRL{}}}^{(N)}(\theta;x)$ can be expressed as,

\begin{equation}
g_{\mathrm{TailRL}}^{(N)}(x)
:=
\sum_{i=1}^N
\omega(r(x,z_i))\,S(x,z_i),
\qquad
\omega(r(x,z_i))
:=
\int_0^{r(x,z_i)}\frac{d\tau}{\sum_{j=1}^{N}\mathbbm{1}_{\{r(x,z_j)>\tau\}}}

\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unbiased policy-gradient estimator

[Lemma 5 (\cite{Chen2013}*{Lemma 4}) of arXiv:2608.10515, 'Limiting Law of Local Fields for the Mean Field Ghatak-Sherrington Model'] Let $k\in\N$. Suppose that $V_1,\ldots,V_{2k}:\R^2\to\R$ are twice continuously differentiable and of moderate growth, together with their first and second partial derivatives. Define
\[
  \phi(t)=\E_0\left[\prod_{i=1}^{2k}V_i(u_i(t),r)\right],\qquad 0\le t\le 1.
\]
Then $\phi$ is differentiable on $(0,1)$ and
\begin{align}
\phi'(t)
=&\frac12\sum_{i\le 2k}T_{i,i}\E_0\left[\frac{\partial^2V_i}{\partial x^2}(u_i(t),r)\prod_{\substack{j\le 2k\\ j\ne i}}V_j(u_j(t),r)\right] \notag\\
&+\frac12\sum_{\substack{i,j\le 2k\\ i\ne j}}T_{i,j}\E_0\left[\frac{\partial V_i}{\partial x}(u_i(t),r)\frac{\partial V_j}{\partial x}(u_j(t),r)
\prod_{\substack{h\le 2k\\ h\ne i,j}}V_h(u_h(t),r)\right] \notag\\
&+\frac1{2\sqrt t}\sum_{i\le 2k}T_i\E_0\left[\frac{\partial^2V_i}{\partial x\partial y}(u_i(t),r)\prod_{\substack{j\le 2k\\ j\ne i}}V_j(u_j(t),r)\right] \notag\\
&+\frac1{2\sqrt t}\sum_{\substack{i,j\le 2k\\ i\ne j}}T_i\E_0\left[\frac{\partial V_i}{\partial x}(u_i(t),r)\frac{\partial V_j}{\partial y}(u_j(t),r)
\prod_{\substack{h\le 2k\\ h\ne i,j}}V_h(u_h(t),r)\right].
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{Chen2013}*{Lemma 4}

[Proposition 22 of arXiv:2609.03248, 'Connections between colored restricted $b$-ary and ordinary partitions'] Let $b\geq 2$ and $\rho\geq 1$ be integers. Then the sequence
$\left(C_b^\rho(n)\right)_{n\geq 0}$ of $\rho$-color $b$-ary partitions of $n$
satisfies the identities
\begin{align}
&\sum_{i=0}^\rho(-1)^i\binom{\rho}{i}C_b^\rho(bn-i)=C_b^\rho(n),\\
&\sum_{i=0}^\rho(-1)^i\binom{\rho}{i}C_b^\rho(bn+r-i)=0\quad (1\leq r\leq b-1),

\end{align}
where we assume that $C_b^\rho(m)=0$ for $m<0$.
title: Proposition 22 of arXiv:2609.03248

[Corollary 11 (Conditional first-break law and moments) of arXiv:2605.09641, 'The Ballot Event for Two-Player Coupon Collection: A Renewal--Catalan Asymptotic'] Let $K_d$ be the extended first-break level from
Lemma~\ref{lem:first-break}, and let
\[
        \mathcal B_d:=\{\text{the ultimate winner was never behind}\}.
\]
Then, conditional on $\mathcal E_A$,
\[
        \frac{K_d}{\sqrt d}\Rightarrow X,
        \qquad
        \Prob(X\in \dd x)=2x e^{-x^2}\Ind_{\{x>0\}}\dd x .
\]
The same convergence holds conditional on $\mathcal B_d$.

Moreover, for every fixed $p>0$,
\[
        \E\left[\left(\frac{K_d}{\sqrt d}\right)^p\right]
        \longrightarrow
        \Gamma\left(1+\frac p2\right),
\]
and
\[
        \E\left[
        \left(\frac{K_d}{\sqrt d}\right)^p
        \,\middle|\,\mathcal E_A\right]
        \longrightarrow
        \Gamma\left(1+\frac p2\right).
\]
The same conditional moment convergence holds with $\mathcal E_A$ replaced by
$\mathcal B_d$.  In particular,
\[

$\mathcal E_A$ and conditional on $\mathcal B_d$.

Let Q = sum_{r=1}^m lambda_r chi^2_{h_r; delta_r^2}, where the lambda_r are distinct nonzero reals and the chi^2_{h_r; delta_r^2} are independent noncentral chi-square variables with h_r degrees of freedom and noncentrality delta_r^2 (any (x+mu)'A(x+mu) with x Gaussian, nonsingular covariance, reduces to this). Then for every x: P(Q > x) = 1/2 + (1/pi) int_0^infinity sin(theta(u)) / (u rho(u)) du, with theta(u) = (1/2) sum_r [h_r arctan(lambda_r u) + delta_r^2 lambda_r u (1 + lambda_r^2 u^2)^{-1}] - (1/2) x u and rho(u) = prod_r (1 + lambda_r^2 u^2)^{h_r/4} exp{(1/2) sum_r (delta_r lambda_r u)^2 / (1 + lambda_r^2 u^2)}. For central forms with even degrees of freedom there are finite expressions for P(Q > x) and the density.

Assumes: Gaussian inputs; the lambda_r are the distinct nonzero eigenvalues of A Sigma with multiplicities h_r

[Definition 20 ($\AS$) of arXiv:2511.07350, 'Decoupling of clusters in independent sets in a percolated hypercube'] Define the random independent set $\hat{I}$ in $\Qp$ via the following procedure.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item Let $\cH$ be $\cE$ or $\cO$, with probabilities $q^\cE$ and $q^\cO$ respectively.
		
		\item Let $\tilde{S}$ denote a subset of $\cH$ constructed by including each $v \in \cH$ independently with probability
		$\fr{\phi_v}{1 + \phi_v}$. In other words, sample $\tilde{S} \sim \pi^\cH$, where $\pi^\cH$ was defined in \eqref{eq:pidef}
		(with the superscript $\cH$ being implicit in that definition).
		
		\item If $\tilde{S} \notin \Sep_{\leq 2}$ (recall this notation from just above \eqref{eq:smallpolymerpfdef}), terminate the algorithm with a result of failure.
		Otherwise, remove all dimers from $\tilde{S}$ and let $S_1$ denote the resulting set of well-separated singletons.
		
		\item Let $S_2$ denote a collection of dimers constructed by including each $\{u,v\} \in \Dim^\cH$ independently with probability
		$\fr{\phi_\fd}{1 + \phi_\fd}$.
		
		\item If $S_1 \cup S_2 \notin \Sep_{\leq 2}$, terminate the algorithm with a result of failure.
		Otherwise, let $\hat{S} = S_1 \cup S_2$.
		
		\item Let $\hat{I}$ denote the independent set with $\hat{I} \cap \cH = \hat{S}$ and with every vertex in $\Q \setminus \cH$
		which does not neighbor $\hat{S}$ included independently with probability $\fr{1}{2}$ each.
		
	\end{enumerate}

DRAFT AUDIT CONCEPT; independent referee pending. For q>=1 and 0<p<1, a finite FK edge conditional, given any subset of the other edges, lies between a=p/(p+q(1-p)) and p. The bounds follow from the open/closed component-count ratio and the tower property. For integer d>=1, in wired boxes [-N,N]^d, integer N>=1, connection of the origin to the boundary is at most 2d*p*((2d-1)*p)^(N-1), by sequential path conditioning and a union bound. At q=3,d=3,p=1/10 all local edge conditionals are at least 1/28, yet the one-arm bound is (3/5)*2^(-(N-1)) and tends to zero. The example is subcritical and does not refute C0048. Local positivity alone cannot supply the uniform critical gap.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:f3f089db25a71026dc997a1c17809e04c99da3cae3618b510cb32edcdef6aa48","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/f3/f3f089db25a71026dc997a1c17809e04c99da3cae3618b510cb32edcdef6aa48.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:91acd56335975a932539f4073e0edfa8458a1eb6dee249a431112ed253e3e53b","bundle_entry_key":"weighted-canonical-diameter","bundle_id":"population.probability-critical-moments-two-end-kernels-and-dependence-006","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"codex-probability-1000-20h-20260906/bundle_006.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.markov:known-pak-diameter-squared-weighted-cayley-relaxation-bound","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# P0248: optimized Cayley walk ? known-result rederivation

Status: author-checked rederivation of a literature-resolved historical question. This is excluded from the current-open target and original-solution count. No independent review of this proof is claimed.

Aldous?Fill, Conjecture/Open Problem 7.18, PDF page 253, asks whether a finite Cayley graph admits a symmetric generator distribution with relaxation time at most a universal constant times its squared diameter. Igor Pak, *Using stopping times to bound mixing times*, SODA 1999, Theorem 3.1, explicitly states that it resolves this question. The author-hosted PDF is internally dated October 31, 2004: https://www.math.ucla.edu/~pak/papers/soda4.pdf . The date of the archived copy is distinguished from the 1999 publication date.

## Construction and direct proof

Let the finite group be $G$, with inverse-closed generating set $S$ excluding the identity, and diameter $D$. For every $x\in G$, choose a geodesic word $w_x$ of length $\ell_x$. Randomize the word for $x$ equally between $w_x$ and the reversed, inverted word chosen for $x^{-1}$. Both words represent $x$ and have the same length. Let $N_s(x)$ be the number of occurrences of $s$ in this randomized word. Define

$$a_s=\frac1{|G|}\sum_x \ell_x\,\mathbb E N_s(x),\qquad A=\sum_s a_s=\frac1{|G|}\sum_x\ell_x^2\le D^2.$$

Inversion of words shows $a_s=a_{s^{-1}}$. Each $a_s>0$, because the word representing $s$ has length one. Thus $\mu(s)=a_s/A$ is a symmetric probability measure whose support is exactly $S$.

For a real function $f$ and uniform $\pi$, the independent uniform-pair identity is

$$\operatorname{Var}_\pi f=\frac1{2|G|^2}\sum_{z,x\in G}(f(zx)-f(z))^2.$$

Telescope along the chosen word for $x$ and use Cauchy?Schwarz. For each occurrence of $s$, translating the summation variable $z$ by the preceding prefix leaves the uniform sum unchanged. Therefore

$$\operatorname{Var}_\pi f\le\frac12\sum_s a_s\,\mathbb E_{z\sim\pi}(f(zs)-f(z))^2=A\,\mathcal E_\mu(f,f).$$

The variational characterization of the gap gives $\tau_2\le A\le D^2$. This is the continuous-time/rate-one spectral convention $\tau_2=(1-\lambda_2)^{-1}$; it is not a claim about absolute discrete-time eigenvalues when the graph is bipartite. Adding one-half holding makes aperiodic discrete-time mixing and changes the relaxation bound by a factor two.

## Second check and limits

The Aldous?Fill comparison theorem 7.16, with comparison increments uniform on the whole group, gives $\tau_2\le\max_s a_s/\mu(s)=A$. It independently reproduces the direct Dirichlet-form argument. The inversion randomization is necessary to justify symmetry in a noncommutative group; a deterministically chosen word table need not give symmetric counts.

This derivation was written before the Pak source was found in the campaign's later-literature check. Discovery order does not imply novelty. The open-problem record is now excluded and the argument survives only as a provenance-labelled mathematical contribution.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:fa4eb0186ec9e6a4a54c5d0dce5c1c32bd0f2b21885951bb5ed32afb6346b693","revision_digest":"sha256:cea26777a2a19a0f2adb6f3a07be69884f76ea61dd4f12f51eb176db0a2690ff","source_id":"owner-authored-probability-notes-20260907:weighted-canonical-diameter","source_revision":"private-author-checked-2026-09-07T00:56:03Z","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Defn Inner product on standard module of arXiv:2506.01306, 'Asymptotic of Coulomb gas integral, Temperley-Lieb type algebras and pure partition functi'] Let $x, y \in V_{n,m}$ be two $(n,m)$-link states and $\delta \in \mathbb{C}$. Define $\langle x, y \rangle_{n,m}$ as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Reflect $x$ across a vertical axis (mirror image).
    \item Glue $x$ to $y$ vertically, forming a closed link diagram.
    \item If all defects pair, and $l(\alpha,\beta)$ closed loops are formed, then
    \[
    \langle x, y \rangle_{n,m} := \delta^{l(\alpha,\beta)}.
    \]
    \item Otherwise, if any defects remain unpaired, then $\langle x, y \rangle_{n,m} := 0$.
\end{enumerate}

[Lem 50 of arXiv:2604.03777, 'Equilibrium fluctuations for a multi-species particle system with long jumps'] For $r>1$, let $\phi\in\cC^r$ be a scaling function and $\psi$ the associated mother wavelet. 
Then, there exists a constant $C=C(\phi,\psi)>0$ 
such that for any $p\in\NN$, $p<r$, all $z\in\Lambda_0$, $m\geq 1$, $x\in\Lambda_m$ and $v\in\R$, we have 
\begin{equ}[e:BoundsWavelets]
\|\partial_y^p\phi^z(\cdot-v)\|_{L^2(\R)}\leq C\,,\qquad\text{and}\qquad \|\partial_y^p\psi_m^x(\cdot-v)\|_{L^2(\R)}\leq C 2^{\frac{mp}{2}}\,.
\end{equ}
Let $h$ be a smooth and compactly supported function. Then, for $v\in\R$, 
$\langle h(\cdot-v), \phi_z\rangle_{L^2(\R)}$ and 
$\langle h(\cdot-v), \psi_m^x\rangle_{L^2(\R)}$ are 
non-zero for at most finitely many $z\in\Lambda_0$ and $O(2^m)$ $x\in\Lambda_m$, $m\geq 1$, 
where in both cases the exact number is independent of $v$. 
Furthermore, there exists a constant $C=C(h, \phi,\psi)>0$ such that 
for all $z\in\Lambda_0$, $m\geq 1$, $x\in\Lambda_m$ and $v\in\R$, and any $j\in\NN$, $j<r$, we have 
\begin{equ}[e:BoundSmooth]
\big|\langle h(\cdot-v), \phi^z\rangle_{L^2(\R)}\big|\leq C\,,\qquad \text{and}\qquad \big|\langle h(\cdot-v), \psi_m^x\rangle_{L^2(\R)}\big|\leq C 2^{m-mj}
\end{equ}
title: Lem 50 of arXiv:2604.03777

[Lem taylorcoeff of arXiv:2412.00593, 'A new approach to strong convergence II.\\The classical ensembles'] Let $f:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic in a neighborhood of 
$\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|\le r\}$. Then $f(z)=\sum_{k=0}^\infty a_k 
z^k$ is absolutely convergent for $|z|<r$ with
$$
	|a_k| \le r^{-k} \max_{|z|=r} |f(z)|.
$$

[Definition 66 of arXiv:2607.18104, '2607.18104'] Fix $M\in \N$ and let $T>0$. Assume that for all $i\in \lbr M\rbr$, we have some $\hfix^{\per,(i)}_0 \in \UCp$. Consider the random function $(y,t) \mapsto \hfixpa(\mathfrak{h}^{\per,(i)}_0;y,t)$, where for all $y\in \mathbb{T}$, all $t \in [0,T]$, and all initial data $\mathfrak{h}^{\per,(i)}_0$,
    \begin{equation}
         \hfixpa\big(\hfix^{\per,(i)}_0;y,t\big) :=  \sup_{x\in \mathbb{T}} \big(\hfix^{\per,(i)}_0(x) + \Lpa(x,0;y,t)\big). 
    \end{equation} Here, $\Lpa$ is a wrapped patched directed landscape from Definition~\ref{def:PatchedDLExt}. 
    We refer to  $(y,t) \mapsto \hfixpa(\mathfrak{h}^{\per}_0;y,t)$ as a \textbf{patched KPZ fixed point} of scale $n$ and with periodic initial data $\hfixp_0$.
title: Definition 66 of arXiv:2607.18104

body: In decision theory and estimation theory, Stein's example is the observation that when three or more parameters are estimated simultaneously, there exist combined estimators more accurate on average than any method that handles the parameters separately. It is named after Charles Stein of Stanford University, who discovered the phenomenon in 1955.
title: Stein's example

body: [Proposition resampling uniform of arXiv:2603.09008, 'On the statistics of random-to-top shuffles'] Suppose that after $r$ random-to-top shuffles of an $n$-card deck, exactly $k$ unique cards have been moved to the top. Then, the cards which have been selected are in the first $k$ positions of the deck, and they form a uniformly random $k$-permutation of $[n]$. The cards that have not been selected are in the last $n-k$ positions of the deck in the same relative (increasing) order.

body:
[Defn H marginal of arXiv:2505.16093, 'Multiple chordal SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Moser system'] The locally commuting n chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$ is a compatible family of measures $\mathbb{P}_{\left(\Omega; z_1, z_2,\ldots,z_n,u\right)}^{\left(U_1, U_2,\ldots,U_n\right)}$ on $n$ tuples of continuous non-self-crossing curves $\left(\eta^{(1)}, \eta^{(2)},\ldots,\eta^{(n)}\right)$ for all simply connected domain $\Omega$ with $\left(z_1, z_2,\ldots,z_n,u\right)$, and $\left(U_1, U_2,\ldots,U_n\right)$ as above that satisfy additionally the conditions below. 

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Conformal invariance}: If $\varphi: \Omega \rightarrow \Omega^{\prime}$ is a conformal map fixing 0, then the pullback measure
$$
\varphi^* \mathbb{P}_{\left(\Omega^{\prime} ; \varphi\left(z_1\right), \varphi\left(z_2\right),\ldots,\varphi\left(z_n),\varphi(u)\right)\right)}^{\left(\varphi\left(U_1\right), \varphi\left(U_2\right),\right)}=\left(\mathbb{P}_{\left(\Omega ; z_1, z_2,\ldots,z_n,u\right)}^{\left(U_1, U_2,\ldots,U_n\right)}\right) .
$$

Therefore, it suffices to describe the measure when $\left(\Omega ; z_1, z_2,\ldots,z_n,u\right)=\left(\mathbb{H}; z_1,z_2,\ldots,z_n,0\right)$.
We can extend our definition to arbitrary simply-connected domain $\Omega$ with a marked interior point $u$ by pulling back via a conformal equivalence $\phi:\Omega \rightarrow \mathbb{D}$ sending $u$ to $0$.

\item
\textbf{Domain Markov property}: Let $\left(\gamma^{(1)}, \gamma^{(2)},\ldots,\gamma^{(n)}\right) \sim \mathbb{P}_{\left(\mathbb{H} ; x_1, x_2,\ldots,x_n\right)}^{\left(U_1, U_2,\ldots, U_n\right)}$ and we parametrize $\gamma^{(j)}$ by their own capacity in $\mathbb{H}$. Let $\mathbf{t}=\left(t_1, t_2,\ldots,t_n\right)$, such that $t_j$ is a stopping time for $\gamma^{(j)}$ and $\gamma_{\left[0, t_j\right]}^{(j)}$ is contained in the interior of $U_j$. Let
$$
\tilde{U}_j=U_j \backslash \gamma_{\left[0, t_j\right]}^{(j)}, \quad \tilde{\gamma}^{(j)}=\gamma^{(j)} \backslash \gamma_{\left[0, t_j\right]}^{(j)}, \quad j=1,2,\ldots,n; \quad \tilde{\Omega}=\mathbb{H} \backslash\left(\gamma_{\left[0, t_1\right]}^{(1)} \cup \gamma_{\left[0, t_2\right]}^{(2)} \cup \ldots \cup \gamma_{\left[0, t_n\right]}^{(n)}\right) .
$$

Then conditionally on $\gamma_{\left[0, t_1\right]}^{(1)} \cup \gamma_{\left[0, t_2\right]}^{(2)} \cup \ldots \cup  \gamma_{\left[0, t_n\right]}^{(n)}$, we have
$$
\left(\tilde{\gamma}^{(1)}, \tilde{\gamma}^{(2)}, \ldots, \tilde{\gamma}^{(n)}\right) \sim \mathbb{P}_{\left(\tilde{\Omega} ; \gamma_{t_1}^{(1)}, \gamma_{t_2}^{(2)},\ldots,\gamma_{t_n}^{(n)}\right)}^{\left(\tilde{U}_1, \tilde{U}_2, \ldots,\tilde{U}_n\right)} .
$$

\item \textbf{Absolute continuity with respect to independent SLE($\kappa$)}:
 In $\mathbb{H}$-uniformization, let $\left(\gamma^{(1)}, \gamma^{(2)},\ldots,\gamma^{(n)}\right) \sim \mathbb{P}_{\left(\mathbb{H} ; x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n,u\right)}^{\left(U_1, U_2,\ldots,U_n)\right.}$. 

We assume that there exist smooth functions $b_j: \mathfrak{X}^n(\boldsymbol{x},u) \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$, where the chamber: $$\mathfrak{X}^n(\boldsymbol{x},u)=\left\{(x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n,u) \in \mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{H} \mid x_1<x_2<\ldots<x_n, u \in \mathbb{H} \right\}$$ 
such that the capacity parametrized Loewner driving function $t \mapsto \theta_t^{(j)}$ of $\gamma^{(j)}$ satisfies
\begin{equation} 
\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{~d} x_{j}(t)=\sqrt{\kappa} \mathrm{d} B_{j}(t)+b_j\left(x_{1}(t),x_{2}(t),\ldots,x_{n}(t),u\right) \mathrm{d} t \\
\mathrm{~d} x_{k}(t)=\frac{2}{x_{k}(t)-x_{j}(t)} \mathrm{d} t,  k\neq j
\end{array}\right.
\end{equation}
where $B_{j}$ is one-dimensional standard Brownian motion. 

\end{itemize}
title: Local multiple chordal SLE($\kappa$)

[Lemma l.xi-infnity of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Let $\xi :\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K} \times \hat\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K}} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a stabilizing marking function satisfying  $R^\xi_\infty(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}})<\infty$ a.s. for all $\tilde{x}\in\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$ and consider $\xi_\infty$ as defined in (equation scoreconvergence of the paper). The following statements hold.

\begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),  labelindent=0pt]
\item   There exist (finite) random variables $n_0:= n_0(\tilde{x}, \tilde{\mathcal{P}})$  such that for all $k \geq n_0$  we have  $R^{\xi}_{W_k}(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}}_k)=R^\xi_{\infty}(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}} )$  and $ \xi(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}}_k)=\xi_{\infty}(\tilde{x}, \tilde{\mathcal{P}})$. In particular, a.s. for all $\tilde{x}\in\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$, we have that $\xi_{\infty}(\tilde{x}, \tilde{\mathcal{P}}) = \lim_{n \to \infty} \xi(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}}_n) \ $ i.e., the equivalence (equation e:xi-to-infty of the paper) holds.
\item   $R^\xi_\infty$ is a.s. an upper bound for the radius of stabilization for $\xi_\infty$ as in Definition~(def.Stab.Radius of the paper), i.e., $R^{\xi_{\infty}}(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}}) \leq R^\xi_\infty(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}})$ a.s..
\item  If $\xi$  satisfies the $p$-moment condition~(equation e:xinpmom of the paper) on finite windows then ~(equation e:xinpmom of the paper) also holds
  for $\xi_\infty$ (i.e., replacing $\xi_{i,n}$ 
  by  
$\xi_\infty(\tilde x_i,\tilde{\mathcal{P}}))$  with the same moment bound $M_p^\xi$.
For this implication to hold, it is enough that $\xi_{\infty}$ is defined as a limit as in (equation e:xi-to-infty of the paper), without requiring that $R^\xi_\infty(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}})<\infty$.  
\item  If $\xi$ is translation invariant  then is so $R^\xi_\infty$ and hence $\xi_\infty$.
\end{enumerate}

Suppose now that $\xi$ is defined on  $\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K} \times
  \mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K}}$ and satisfies stopping set stabilization on $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$ ~(equation stab-infinite of the paper)  with $p=1$. Then 
\begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),  labelindent=0pt]
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\item  $R^\xi_\infty(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}})<\infty$ for all $\tilde{x}\in\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$, a.s.. Consequently all properties (i)--(iv) hold  and moreover $R^\xi_\infty=R^\xi$ and $\xi_\infty=\xi$ for all $\tilde{x}\in\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$, a.s. 
\end{enumerate}

[Proposition 10 of arXiv:2609.01594, '2609.01594'] Let $a\in\N$. 
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If $a\in\Acal$, then the witnesses may be chosen with
\[
 f>0,\quad b\in\Sq(\Z),\quad b\in2\uparrow ,\quad
 b\leq g<\Cscr,
 \quad
 Y\mid\binom{2X}{X}.
\]
They may in fact be chosen arbitrarily large.
\item If
\[
 f\neq0,\quad 0\leq g<2\Cscr,
 \quad b\in\Sq(\Z),\quad b\in2\uparrow ,
 \quad Y\mid\binom{2X}{X},
\]
then $a\in\Acal$.
\item Whenever $a\in\N$, $f\neq0$, $b$ is a square and
$0\leq g<2\Cscr$, one has
\begin{equation}
 X>3b\ \ \t{and}\ \ Y>\max\{b,2^8\}.
\end{equation}

[Theorem 18 (Keyl--Werner) of arXiv:2609.03736, '2609.03736'] Let $\tau$ be a density matrix on $\CC^m$ with decreasing eigenvalue list
$s$, and let $\Pi_\lambda^{(N)}$ be the $\mathfrak S_N$-isotypic projection
of shape $\lambda$ in $(\CC^m)^{\otimes N}$.  The numbers
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P_{\tau,N}(\lambda)
 =\tr\bigl(\tau^{\otimes N}\Pi_\lambda^{(N)}\bigr)
 
\end{equation}
form a probability measure on partitions of $N$ with at most $m$ parts.
View $\lambda/N$ as an $m$-vector by appending zero parts.  For every
$\varepsilon>0$,
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{\substack{\lambda\vdash N\\
        \|\lambda/N-s\|_1>\varepsilon}}
 \tr\bigl(\tau^{\otimes N}\Pi_\lambda^{(N)}\bigr)
 \longrightarrow0.
 
\end{equation}
Equivalently, the normalized row-length vector $\lambda/N$ converges in
probability to the spectrum $s$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:lcp-nonlocal-square-identity of arXiv:2608.02459, 'Response Calculus for Spectral Simplicity\\ and Joint Eigenvalue Densities'] The square $\phi^2$ belongs to $V_x$ and satisfies
\begin{equation}
 A_0(\phi^2)
 =2\Lambda\phi^2M_x^\partial-\Gamma_J(\phi)m
 \qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\mathbb T).
\end{equation}
Both terms on the right are finite Radon measures, and
$\Gamma_J(\phi)m\ll m$.  Equivalently, for every real
$\zeta\in C^\infty(\mathbb T)$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E(\phi^2,\zeta)
 =2\Lambda\int_{\mathbb T}\zeta\phi^2\,dM_x^\partial
  -\int_{\mathbb T}\zeta\,\Gamma_J(\phi)\,dm.
\end{equation}

body:
[Openquestion 35 (Stability near fairness at fixed length) of arXiv:2601.16580, 'Coin flipping and waiting times paradoxes \\ Why fair coins are exceptional'] Fix an alphabet size $s$ and a length $k\ge 2$, and consider i.i.d.\ sources with probabilities $(p_1,\dots,p_s)$.
(Here the \emph{uniform} distribution means $p_i=1/s$ for all $i$.)
For patterns of length $k$, orient the complete directed graph by
$A\to B$ iff $\Pr(A\!>\!B)>\tfrac12$ under \emph{independent} sources and \emph{random tie-break}.
Does there exist $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(k,s)>0$ such that whenever $\max_i |p_i-1/s|<\varepsilon$,
this head-to-head tournament on $\mathcal{A}^k$ has \emph{no directed $3$-cycles} (equivalently, is transitive as a tournament)?
More generally, what is the largest neighbourhood of the uniform distribution on which the length-$k$ head-to-head relation is cycle-free? (Stated as a question by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Stability near fairness at fixed length

[Lemma 14 (Matrix concentration inequalities) of arXiv:2608.22595, 'Sparse Additive Off-Policy Evaluation for Reinforcement Learning with Potentially Limited '] Let \(p_1,p_2\geq1\) and write \(D=p_1+p_2\).

\begin{itemize}
\item
Let \(\{\boldsymbol{Z}_j\}_{j=1}^m\) be independent, mean-zero
random matrices of dimension \(p_1\times p_2\). Suppose that
\(\|\boldsymbol{Z}_j\|_2\leq R\) almost surely, and define
\[
\nu^2
=
\max\left\{
\left\|
\sum_{j=1}^m
\mathbb{E}
\left(
\boldsymbol{Z}_j\boldsymbol{Z}_j^\top
\right)
\right\|_2,
\left\|
\sum_{j=1}^m
\mathbb{E}
\left(
\boldsymbol{Z}_j^\top\boldsymbol{Z}_j
\right)
\right\|_2
\right\}.
\]
Then, for any \(u>0\),
\[
\Pr\left[
\left\|
\sum_{j=1}^m\boldsymbol{Z}_j
\right\|_2
>
\sqrt{2\nu^2\{u+\log D\}}
+
\frac{2R}{3}\{u+\log D\}
\right]
\leq
\exp(-u).
\]
In particular, if \(\nu^2\leq mR^2\), then
\[
\Pr\left[
\left\|
\sum_{j=1}^m\boldsymbol{Z}_j
\right\|_2
>
R\sqrt{2m\{u+\log D\}}
+
\frac{2R}{3}\{u+\log D\}
\right]
\leq
\exp(-u).
\]

\item Let \(\{\boldsymbol{X}_j,\mathcal{F}_j\}_{j=1}^m\) be an adapted
sequence of random matrices of dimension \(p_1\times p_2\) satisfying
\(\mathbb{E}(\boldsymbol{X}_j\mid\mathcal{F}_{j-1})
=\boldsymbol{0}\). Suppose that
\(\|\boldsymbol{X}_j\|_2\leq R_j\) almost surely, where
\(R_1,\ldots,R_m\) are deterministic. Then, for any \(u>0\),
\[
\Pr\left[
\left\|
\sum_{j=1}^m\boldsymbol{X}_j
\right\|_2
>
\sqrt{
8\{u+\log D\}
\sum_{j=1}^m R_j^2
}
\right]
\leq
\exp(-u).
\]
In particular, if \(R_j\leq R\) for all \(j\), then
\[
\Pr\left[
\left\|
\sum_{j=1}^m\boldsymbol{X}_j
\right\|_2
>
R\sqrt{8m\{u+\log D\}}
\right]
\leq
\exp(-u).
\]
\end{itemize}

[Theorem lazyGinf of arXiv:2604.07227, 'Transition probabilities of step-reinforced random walks'] Let $S=(S_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ be an irreducible generalized SRRW on a countably infinite group $G$ with parameter $\alpha \in [0,1)$ and step distribution $\mu$ such that $\mu(e_G)\geq \mu_0$ for some $\mu_0\in (0,1/2]$. Then for any $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$, one has
$$
 \max_{x \in G} \mathbb{P}(S_n=x) \leq \varepsilon \quad \text{if } n \geq \frac{C(\mu_0)}{1-\alpha} \int_{4}^{8 / \varepsilon}\frac{1 }{u \Phi^2(u)} d u, 
$$
  where $C(\mu_0)$ is a positive constant that depends only on $\mu_0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem thm:convbls of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Consider a bounded simply-connected domain $D$ and sequence $(\widetilde D_m)_{m\geq 1}$ of approximating metric graphs via the lattice $\frac{1}{m}\mathbb{Z}^2$. 

In these domains consider the Brownian loop soup 
$\mathcal{L}_D$ at the critical intensity 
($\alpha=1/2$ or central charge $c=1$) and the metric graph loop soup $\widetilde \mathcal{L}_{\widetilde D_m}$ also at the critical intensity. 
Let $\widetilde \Xi^a_{\widetilde D_m}$ denote the PPP of Brownian boundary to boundary excursions of intensity $a \geq 0$ on the metric graph $\widetilde D_m$, 
and $\Xi^a_{D}$ the corresponding PPP of Brownian boundary to boundary excursions in the continuum.

Finally, let $(\widetilde C_k^m)_{k \geq 1}$ be the clusters of 
$\widetilde \Xi^a_{\widetilde D_m} 
\cup \widetilde \mathcal{L}_{\widetilde D_m}$, 
and $(C_k)_{k \geq 1}$ the clusters of 
$\Xi^a_{D} \cup \mathcal{L}_D$,  listed say by the order of decreasing diameter. 
Denote by $\widetilde \gamma, \gamma$ closed paths on the metric graph and in the continuum respectively.

Then for any $z_1,\dots, z_n \in D$ distinct points, and any $\varepsilon_1, \dots, \varepsilon_n \geq 0$, we have that the probabilities
$$\tilde p_{a,m} := \mathbb{P}\left(\nexists \widetilde C_i^{m}\text{ with }\widetilde \gamma \in \widetilde C_i^{ m}\text{ such that} \sum_{j=1}^{n}
\indx_{\widetilde \gamma}(z_j)
\text{ odd}
 \: \& \: \widetilde C_i^{m} \cap \bigcup_{j=1}^n\mathbb{D}(z_j, \varepsilon_j) = \emptyset\right)$$ 
converge, as $m \to \infty$ to 
$$p_a := \mathbb{P}\left(\nexists C_i\text{ with }\gamma \in C_i\text{ such that} \sum_{j=1}^{n}
\indx_{\gamma}(z_j)
\text{ odd}
 \: \& \: C_i \cap \bigcup_{j=1}^n\mathbb{D}(z_j, \varepsilon_j) = \emptyset\right).$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:convbls of arXiv:2604.15146

[Definition of arXiv:2609.00163, 'Decompositions and diagrams of symplectic surfaces in Weinstein domains'] Let $\mathcal{T}=(H_1,H_2,H_3;\tau_1, \tau_2,\tau_3)$ be the spine of a $b$-bridge bisection with divides and consider $\hat\phi_{i,i+1}$ be the pointed mapping class group of the tangle $\tau_i$. Let $\tau'_1$, $\tau'_2$, $\tau'_3$ be ($b+1$)-stranded braided tangles corresponding to the pointed monodromies:
\[\hat\phi'_{12}=ATB, ~ \hat\phi'_{23}=\hat\phi_{23}, \text{ and } \hat\phi'_{31}=\hat\phi_{31}, \text{ or }\]
\[\hat\phi'_{12}=\hat\phi_{12}, ~ \hat\phi'_{23}=\hat\phi_{23}, \text{ and } \hat\phi'_{31}=AT^{-1}B,\]
where $A,B$ are pointed mapping class group elements, $\hat\phi_{12}=AB$ or $\hat\phi_{31}=AB$, and $T$ is a positive half-twist involving the $(b+1)$-st puncture of the page. The resulting tuple of braided tangles $\mathcal{T}'=(H_1,H_2,H_3;\tau'_1,\tau'_2,\tau'_3)$ is called a \emph{positive braided perturbation} of $\mathcal{T}$.

Own work, proof (unaudited), W719-T295-C010 v1; conditional route calculation, no novelty claim. The exact omitted-row GD perturbation satisfies Delta_next=(I-eta Q_minus)Delta-(eta/m)((a_i^T x)^2-g_i^2)(a_i^T x)a_i, with explicit symmetric polynomial secant matrix Q_minus. Assuming row norm/projection bounds, same-rate perturbation contraction rho=1-eta mu, and an error envelope R0 rho^t, the norm-only forcing bootstrap yields normalized envelope coefficient at most D0+(eta B/rho)(d/m)(log d)t. Its scalar inequality admits equality; at t=ceil(1/eta), eta=c/log d, linear m leaves a log d deficit. This is a proof-strategy obstruction, not an actual GD lower bound. Let ell=log d and assume ||a_i||<=A sqrt(d), |g_i|<=G sqrt(ell), ||h_t||<=r, |a_i^T h_t|<=K sqrt(ell)||h_t||, ||I-eta Q_minus||<=rho, and ||h_t||<=R0 rho^t. Here B=A K(2G^2+3GKr+K^2r^2) and D0=sqrt(d/ell)||Delta_0||/R0. Then sqrt(d/ell)||Delta_t||/(R0 rho^t)<=D0+(eta B/rho)(d/m)ell*t. No relative-error bound follows without comparing R0 rho^t to actual ||h_t||. At m of order d log d this particular coefficient is bounded after t of order 1/eta, but all trajectory assumptions still need proof. No actual divergence or oversampling necessity is established.

[Thm 12 (Convergence of root statistics and their expectations) of arXiv:2608.06576, 'The Resultant Distribution Method: Universality for $p$-adic Random Matrices and Polynomia'] Fix an integer $m\geq 1$. Let $K_1,\ldots,K_m$ be finite extensions
of $\Q_p$, and let
$$
U\subseteq\mc{O}_{K_1}^{\new}
\times\cdots\times\mc{O}_{K_m}^{\new}
$$
be clopen. Let $P_1^S,P_2^S,\ldots$ be random elements of $\mathscr{P}^S$
satisfying the assumptions of
\Cref{thm: resultant distribution convergence introduction}, and let
$P_\infty^S\in\mathscr{P}^S$ be the limiting random polynomial provided
by that theorem. Suppose that
$$
\mathbf{P}\left(P_\infty^S\text{ has a repeated root}\right)=0.
$$
Then $Z_U(P_n^S)\overset{d}{\longrightarrow}
Z_U(P_\infty^S)$. If, in addition, the degree tightness assumption is strengthened to moment tightness, i.e.,
$$
\lim_{D\to\infty}\sup_{n\geq 1}
\mathbf{E}\left[(\deg P_n^S)^m
\mathbf{1}_{\{\deg P_n^S>D\}}
\right]=0,
$$
then
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbf{E}\left[
Z_U(P_n^S)\right]=\mathbf{E}\left[
Z_U(P_\infty^S)\right].
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Convergence of root statistics and their expectations

[Defn 1 (Markov Kernels) of arXiv:2510.22155, 'Random walks in space-time random media in all spatial dimensions: the full subcritical fl'] Fix $d\ge 1$. Let $I$ be any locally compact additive subgroup of $\mathbb R^d$, for example $I=\mathbb R^d$ or $I=A \mathbb Z^d$ where $A$ is some nonsingular $d\times d$ matrix. Let $\mathcal B(I)$ denote the Borel $\sigma$-algebra on $I$. 
A \textit{Markov kernel} on $I$ is a continuous function from $I\to \mathcal P(I)$, where $\mathcal P(I)$ is the space of probability measures on $(I,\mathcal B(I))$ equipped with the topology of weak convergence of probability measures. 

Any Markov kernel $K$ on $I$ shall be written as $K(   x,A)$, which is identified with the continuous function from $I\to \mathcal P(I)$ given by $x\mapsto K(   x,\cdot)$. We denote by $\mathcal M(I)$ the space of all Markov kernels on $I$.

We equip $\mathcal M(I)$ with the weakest topology under which the maps $T_{f,   x}:\mathcal M(I)\to \mathbb R$ given by $$K\stackrel{T_{f,   x}}{\mapsto}  \int_I f(   y)\;K(   x,\mathrm d   y)$$ 
are continuous, where one varies over all $x\in I$ and all bounded continuous functions $f:I\to \mathbb R$. This topology endows $\mathcal M(I)$ with a Borel $\sigma$-algebra which allows us to talk about random variables taking values in the space of Markov kernels. For $   a\in I$ define the translation operator $\tau_a:\mathcal M(I)\to \mathcal M(I)$ by $(  \tau_{   a} K)(   x,A):= K(x+   a,A+   a)$ which is a Borel-measurable map on this space.
title: Markov Kernels

[Lemma 18 of arXiv:2608.14802, 'Dynamical Gibbs-non-Gibbs transitions for finite-alphabet models on trees'] Let $i\in \{2,3\}$ and $R_i>0$ the threshold given in Corollary \ref{cor: differential normalized potts map}. Then, for each $r_i\in (0,R_i)$ there exists $t^{(i)}_2=t^{(i)}_2(r_i)<\infty$ 
and a unique family $\left(l^{(i)}(t)\right)_{t\geq t^{(i)}_2}$ 
such that the following holds. 

The family defines a continuation of $l^{(i)}_+$, i.e. it satisfies $\lim_{t\rightarrow \infty}l^{(i)}(t)=l^{(i)}_+$ and $l^{(i)}(t)\in U_{r_i}$ for all $t\geq t^{(i)}_2$. Here, $l^{(i)}(t)$ are the limits of Proposition \ref{prop: Total Badness q=3 Potts model} part a) and $U_{r_i}$ the local trapping region of Corollary \ref{cor: differential normalized potts map}.

[Definition 12 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] A limiting point \(\xi=(\mu_t)_{t<T}\) is \emph{based at \(q\)} with
respect to the limiting morphism \(\pi\) if
\(\pi_*\mu_t\rightharpoonup\delta_q\).  Such a \(q\) is unique when it
exists, and we denote it by \(q_\pi(\xi)\).  It is
\emph{Type-I based at \(q\)} if there is \(C_\xi<\infty\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \int_Xd_\eta(\pi(x),q)^2\,d\mu_t(x)\le C_\xi(T-t)
 \qquad\text{for every }0\le t<T.
\end{equation}
If \(q\in Y^{\rm rv}\) and \(\rho_q\) is a localized
squared-distance barrier from \cref{def:squared-distance-barrier},
compactness and the defining comparisons for \(\rho_q\) show that this
is equivalent to
\[
 \int_X\rho_q\circ\pi\,d\mu_t\le C'_\xi(T-t).
\]
For an arbitrary holomorphic map, qualitative basing alone need not
imply this rate.  For the semiample K\"ahler--Ricci flow considered here,
\Cref{lem:automatic-label} proves that every limiting point is based at
a unique point \(q_\pi(\xi)\) and is Type-I based there.  Thus
\eqref{eq:label-moment} is never an additional hypothesis below.  When
\(q_\pi(\xi)\in Y^{\rm rv}\), we simply say that \(\xi\) is based at
the regular value \(q_\pi(\xi)\).
title: Definition 12 of arXiv:2609.02878

[Theorem 23 of arXiv:2608.30549, '\vspace{-1cm}Maximally Spread Out Measures and Implications\\{} for Phase Transitions in A'] Let $(\XX,\norm{\cdot})$ be a quasi-normed space with modulus of concavity $C_2 \ge 1$.
    Assume that $\SC$ satisfies {\ConditionZetaTextAlphaC{(\alpha,C_0)}} for some constants $\alpha, C_0>0$.
    Let $s\ge0$, $t\in \RR$ (with $t>0$ if $s=0$), and let $c_1>0$. 
    Let $(\SC_n)_{n\in\NN}$ be a sequence of finite $2^{-n}$-separated subsets $\SC_n \subset \SC$,
    and let $n_0\in \NN$ such that
    \begin{equation}
        \num\SC_n \ge \exp\bigl( c_1 \cdot 2^{ns}n^{t}\bigr)
        \quad \text{for all $n\ge n_0$.}
        
    \end{equation}
    Then the measure $\mu$ given in \cref{definition_measure_SC_n} satisfies the following:
    There exist $r_0>0$ and $c>0$ such that
    \begin{equation}
        \om{\mu}\bigl(\ball(x,r)\bigr) 
        \le \exp\biggl( - c  
        \cdot \Bigl(\frac{1}{r}\Bigr)^{s} \cdot \Bigl( \log_2 \Bigl(\frac{1}{r}\Bigr)\Bigr)^{t-\alpha s}\biggr)
        
    \end{equation}
    for all $r\in (0,r_0)$ and all $x\in \XX$.
title: Theorem 23 of arXiv:2608.30549

[Definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The moments of a variable $f:X\to\mathbb R$ are the numbers
$$M_k=E(f^k)$$
which satisfy $M_0=1$, then $M_1=E(f)$, and then $V(f)=M_2-M_1^2$.

[Definition def:disagree-polymer-len-energy-decor of arXiv:2509.04333, 'The limiting law of the Discrete Gaussian level lines'] Let $(\gamma,\{D_i\},\{h_i\})$ be a labeled disagreement polymer. Its \emph{length} ${\ensuremath{\mathscr N}}(\gamma)$ and \emph{energy} 
		${\ensuremath{\mathscr E}}_\beta(\gamma)$ are defined as
		\[{\ensuremath{\mathscr N}}(\gamma)=\sum_{e\in\gamma}|(\nabla \phi)_e|\quad,\quad 
		{\ensuremath{\mathscr E}}_\beta(\gamma) := \beta\sum_{e \in \gamma} |(\nabla \phi)_e|^2\,.\]
		To describe the law of the disagreement polymer, we will use a family of decoration functions $\Phi$ on subsets ${\ensuremath{\mathsf W}}\subset \mathbb Z^2$---each referred to as a cluster if it is also connected---
        satisfying the following properties.
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item  If ${\ensuremath{\mathsf W}}$ is not connected, then $\Phi({\ensuremath{\mathsf W}}) = 0$.
			
			\item 
			The function $\Phi$ is translation invariant, as well as invariant under a rotation by $\pi/2$ or reflection with respect to one of the axes.
			
			\item There exists a constant $C > 0$ such that for every ${\ensuremath{\mathsf W}}$, we have 
			$
			|\Phi({\ensuremath{\mathsf W}})| \leq \exp(-(\beta - C){\ensuremath{\mathbf d}}({\ensuremath{\mathsf W}}))
			$, 
			where ${\ensuremath{\mathbf d}}({\ensuremath{\mathsf W}})$ is the size of the smallest connected set of bonds in $(\mathbb Z^2)^*$ containing all the boundary bonds of ${\ensuremath{\mathsf W}}$.
		\end{enumerate}
title: Energy, length and decorations of a disagreement polymer

[Lemma reductiontoA2 of arXiv:2507.16188, 'The noisy voter model with general initial conditions'] Let $\{W_i\}_{i=1}^m$ be subsets with $|W_i|\leq 3$ and $\operatorname{dist}_G(W_i,W_j) \geq \frac{1}{2}(\log n)^{1+\beta}$, and let $\Delta$ denote the maximum degree in $G$. Then for every $t\geq 0$,
\[
\sum_{i=1}^m d_{\textsc{tv}}^{\mathsf{x}_0}(W_i,t)^2 \leq 18q\Delta n \left( t^2\mathcal{A}^{(2)}_t(\mathsf{x}_0) + (t+1)e^{-4 \theta t}\right) + O(n^{-9})\,.
\]
title: Lemma reductiontoA2 of arXiv:2507.16188

[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2606.31455, 'Discrete time-multidimensional renewal theory and applications'] Fix $k\in\mathbb{N}^d$. Then for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
\[
\overline{F}_{N(k)}(n):=\mathbb{P}(N(k)\ge n)=F_n(k),
\]
and consequently

\begin{eqnarray*}
F_{N(k)}(n)&:=&\mathbb{P}(N(k)\le n)=1-F_{n+1}(k),\\
f_{N(k)}(n)&:=&\mathbb{P}(N(k)=n)=F_n(k)-F_{n+1}(k).
\end{eqnarray*}

metric in \eqref{ds}.

[Theorem Th_degrees of arXiv:2607.14792, 'On the degree distribution of large tentacular Bienaymé--Galton--Watson trees'] Let $d \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 2}$. Assume that $k_n = o(n)$, $k_n\rightarrow \infty$ and $\mu(2)>0$.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item If $k_n=o( n^{\frac{d-1}{d}})$, then \[\mathbb{P}\left(\mathrm{deg_{max}}(T_n^{k_n}) \leq d  \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.\]
        \item Let $c>0$. If $k_n\underset{n \to \infty}{\sim} cn^{\frac{d-1}{d}}$, 
        \[\phi_{d+1}\left(T_n^{k_n}\right) \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{(d)} \mathrm{Poi}\left( c^d\frac{\mu(d+1)\mu(1)^{d-1}}{\mu(2)^d} \right). \]
        \item If $k_n^d/n^{d-1} \rightarrow + \infty$ as $n\rightarrow +\infty$, then for every $p \geq 1$ 
\[ \frac{n^{d-1}}{k_n^d}\phi_{d+1}\left(T_{n}^{k_n}\right) \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{L^p} \frac{\mu(1)^{d-1}\mu(d+1)}{\mu(2)^d}.\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:CPRE-BDS of arXiv:2507.00329, 'Oriented bond-site percolation in random environment and contact processes with periodic r'] Let $\varDelta>0$ be a random variable, with $\mathbb{E}[\varDelta^{1+\varepsilon}]<\infty$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, and fix $\delta>0$ and $p\in(0,1)$. Let $(\varDelta_x)_{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}}$ be an i.i.d.\ family of random variables distributed according to $\mathcal{L}(\varDelta)$, the law of $\varDelta$. Consider the generalised contact process on $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}$ with $\mathbb{X}\sim\mathrm{PPP}(1)$ and recovery times  $(\mathbb{Y}_x)_{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}}$ given by independent copies of the following Cox point processes:
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item With probability $p$ (independent of everything else), let $\mathbb{Y}_x\sim\mathrm{PPP}(\delta)$.  
        \item Otherwise, let $\mathbb{Y}_x\sim\mathrm{PPP}(\varDelta_x)$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then, there exists some $\delta_c:=\delta_c(p,\mathcal L(\varDelta))>0$ such that, for every $\delta<\delta_c$, the generalised contact process has a positive probability of survival. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Contact process in (spatial) random environment

body:
[Theorem thm:module-stability of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Fix a declared global circuit state $\tau$.  Let $\mathcal T$ be any finite
composition of correlated same-$C$ distance-hereditary pair combs,
signed-$K_5$ pair combs, safe word decorations, and normalized boundary
operations.  Let $m$ be the total $C$-degree of
$\mathcal T\mathfrak q_C$, counting the incoming token as its two
underlying coefficient occurrences.  If no new smoothing carrier is
adjoined, the raw tangle has a finite circuit-anchored presentation
$\zeta_{\mathcal T,\tau}\in\mathscr P_\tau$ satisfying
\[
  \|\zeta_{\mathcal T,\tau}\|_{\mathscr P_\tau}
  \le C_0^mK^{m-2}h^2,
\tag{2.4.6}
\]
where $C_0$ is numerical and independent of $n$, $m$, and $E$.  In
particular, arbitrarily many interleaved combs still pay $h^2$ only once.
Every declared port and context occurs once, token degree remains one,
and the circuit-base normalization is deferred to (eq:2.3.17 of the paper).  No ordinary
open-component norm is asserted for a $K_5$ branch.

[Definition def:valid of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix $\lambda \in (0,1)$ and a send sequence $\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$. Fix an initialising state~$\Psi_0$. Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be a transition rule on
a set of high-level states which includes~$\Psi_0$. Let $\Psi^{*}$ be the $\Psi_0$-closure of $\mathrm{hls}$. The transition rule~$\mathrm{hls}$ is 
\emph{\newsym{Psi-valid}{validity condition for hls - Definition~(def:valid of the paper)} {\Psi^*\mbox{-valid}}}  if 
for every $\psi \in \Psi^*$ and every integer $t > \tau^\psi$, the following holds.
\begin{itemize}
\item  { Let $\overline{X}(\psi,t) \sim \mathsf{Po}(F_{[j^\psi]}^\psi(t))$.}
Let $\Psi'$ be the random high-level state 
$\Psi' = \mathrm{hls}(\psi, { \overline{X}(\psi,t)}, t)$.
For every high-level state $\psi'$ 
such that $\mathbb{P}(\Psi' = \psi')>0$, 
let $A(\psi,\psi',t) = \mathrm{dist}({ \overline{X}(\psi,t)} \mid \Psi'=\psi')$.  
Then for all $\psi'$, $A(\psi,\psi',t) \gtrsim \mathsf{Po}(F_{ [j^\psi]}^{\psi'}(t))$. 
\end{itemize}

Fix a $\Psi^*$-valid transition rule 
$\mathrm{hls}$. 
Recall the function~$\phi_{\cdot,\cdot}$ from Definition~(def:phi of the paper).
For any high-level states
$\psi,\psi' \in \Psi^*$ 
and $t> \tau^{\psi}$,  we define 
\newsym{phi-2}{stochastic domination 
map determined by hls $\psi$ and $\psi'$ - see Definition~(def:valid of the paper)}
{\phi_{\psi,\psi',t}} as follows.
If $A(\psi,\psi',t) \gtrsim 
\mathsf{Po}(F_{ [j^\psi]}^{\psi'}(t))$ then
$\phi_{\psi,\psi',t} = \phi_{A(\psi,\psi',t),
\mathsf{Po}(F_{ [j^\psi]}^{\psi'}(t)) }$.
Otherwise $\phi_{\psi,\psi',t}$ is the identity.

body:
[Defn def:main-func of arXiv:2412.03415, 'Critical first passage percolation on random graphs'] For any pair of vertices $u\neq v \in [n]$, let $\mathscr{P}_n(u,v)$ denote the collection of all (self-avoiding) paths from $i,j$. For any path $\boldsymbol{\pi} \in \mathscr{P}_n(u,v)$ let the total passage time using this path be given by $T(\boldsymbol{\pi}) = \sum_{e\in \boldsymbol{\pi}} t_e$ and let $|\boldsymbol{\pi}|$ denote the number of edges in $\boldsymbol{\pi}$.  Let $T_n(u,v) = \min_{\boldsymbol{\pi} \in \mathscr{P}_n(u,v)} T(\boldsymbol{\pi})$ denote the optimal passage time between these two vertices and 
\[\mathscr{P}_{\opt}(u,v) = \left\{\boldsymbol{\pi} \in \mathscr{P}_n(u,v): \boldsymbol{\pi} = \arg \min T(\boldsymbol{\pi}) \right\},\]
denote the collection of optimal paths. Let 
$H_n(u,v) = \min \set{|\boldsymbol{\pi}|: \boldsymbol{\pi} \in \mathscr{P}_{\opt}(u,v) },$
denote the hopcount, namely the minimal number of edges amongst all optimal paths between $u,v$.
title: Main functionals of interest

[Lem app-hilbert-cocycle of arXiv:2608.27939, 'Entropy and domination for quasi-Hitchin representations'] For every nontrivial $\gamma\in\Gamma$, and the H\"{o}lder cocycle $c_H$ as above,  the period  of $\gamma$ with respect to $c_H$ is precisely the 
Hilbert length with respect to the Hitchin representation $\rho_0$:
\begin{equation}
  \ell_{c_H}(\gamma)
  :=c_H(\gamma,\gamma^+)
  =\ell^H_{\rho_0}(\gamma).
\end{equation}
In particular, all nonzero periods of $c_H$ are positive.

body:
[Proposition 20 of arXiv:2609.03831, 'On flows generated by square-integrable vector fields'] Let $\v \in L^2(\R^d)$ be a compactly supported divergence-free vector field.
	Suppose that the operator $B_0(\rho) := \d_t \rho + \v \cdot \nabla_x \rho$
	with $D(B_0) = C^\infty_c(\R^{d+1})$ is essentially skew-adjoint in $L^2(\R^{d+1})$.
	Then for any open interval $I\subset \R$ the vector field $\v$
	has the renormalization property in the class $L^2(I \times \R^d)$.
title: Proposition 20 of arXiv:2609.03831

[Definition of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] A \textbf{norm} on a vector space $V$ over $K$ is a function $\|\cdot\|\colon V\to[0,\infty)$ such that
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
    \item $\|v\|=0$ iff $v=0$,
    \item $\|av\|=|a|\cdot\|v\|$ for all $a\in K$, $v\in V$,
    \item $\|v+w\|\leq \max(\|v\|,\|w\|)$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'

body: [Definition 11 of arXiv:2609.01574, 'A linear bound for Fujita's freeness conjecture'] Let $Z$ be a normal variety. We use $b$-divisors as in \cite[Section~2]{FH23}. If $\mathbf D$ is a $\mathbb Q$-Weil $b$-divisor over $Z$ and $Z'\to Z$ is a birational model, we denote its trace on $Z'$ by $D_{Z'}$. If $F$ is a prime divisor over $Z$, we set $\mult_F\mathbf D:=\mult_F D_{Z'}$, where $Z'$ is any model on which $F$ appears. If $D_{Z'}$ is $\mathbb Q$-Cartier, we denote by $\overline{D_{Z'}}$ its Cartier closure. Its trace on every birational model $h\colon Z''\to Z'$ is $h^*D_{Z'}$. We say that $\mathbf D$ \emph{descends to $Z'$} if $\mathbf D=\overline{D_{Z'}}$. We denote the canonical $b$-divisor over $Z$ by $\mathbf K_Z$.

[Theorem thm:LMTparallel of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] {LandryMinskyTaylor2025_TransverseSurfacesAndPseudoAnosovFlows_PUB}}]
Let \(\varphi\) be a pseudo-Anosov flow on \(M\), and let \(S_{1}\) and \(S_{2}\) be two isotopic embedded subsurfaces in \(M\) which are almost transverse to \(\varphi\).
Let \(N\) be a \(I\)-bundle cobounded by \(S_{1}\) and \(S_{2}\). (Such \(N\) is unique if \(S_{i}\) is not a fiber of \(M\).)
If \(S_{1}\) and \(S_{2}\) are minimally transverse to blowup \(\varphi^{\sharp}_{1}\) and \(\varphi^{\sharp}_{2}\), respectively, then \(\varphi_{1}^{\sharp}\) and \(\varphi_{2}^{\sharp}\) has same combinatorial type.

Furthermore, if the surfaces are transverse to a single blowup \(\varphi^{\sharp}\), then \(N\) is a product sutured manifold \(S_{1}\times I\) endowed with product flow, and hence \(S_{1}\) and \(S_{2}\) are isotopic along flowlines of \(\varphi^{\sharp}\).

body:
[Theorem 24 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let \(\iota\colon X\to S\) be a smooth representable morphism of fpqc algebraic \(\F_p\)-stacks of relative dimension \(d\).
Assume that  $F^{\dR}_{X/S}$ splits. 
Then there is an isomorphism
\[
F_{X/S,*}\Omega_{X/S}^{\bullet}
\simeq
\bigoplus_{i=0}^d
\Omega_{X^{(1)}/S}^i[-i]
\]
in $\mcalD_{\qcoh}(X^{(1)})$.
This isomorphism is canonically obtained from a given retraction
\[
(\varphi \colon F_{X/S,*}\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}
\longrightarrow
\mcalO_{X^{(1)}},\, \varphi \circ F^{\dR}_{X/S} \simeq \id_{\mcalO_{X^{(1)}}})
\]
in \(\mcalD_{\qcoh}(X^{(1)})\).

In particular, if \(\iota\) is projective, then, for every
\(\iota\)-ample line bundle \(L\) on \(X\), we have
\[
R^i\iota_*
\bigl(\Omega_{X/S}^j\otimes L^{-1}\bigr)=0
\qquad
(i+j<d) \quad \text{and} \quad R^i\iota_*
\bigl(\Omega_{X/S}^j\otimes L\bigr)=0
\qquad

[Corollary cor_convergence of arXiv:2608.09105, 'Longest convex chains with i.i.d.\ points'] For any $\mu\in\mathcal{M}$ and any sequence $(\mu_n)_{n\geqslant1}$ in $\mathcal{M}$, the following statements are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]

\item 
$d(f_{\mu_n},f_\mu)\to0$ as $n\to\infty$.

\item 
$f_{\mu_n}(x)\to f_\mu(x)$ as $n\to\infty$, for every $x\in[0,1)$.

\item 
$\mu_n[0,t]\to\mu[0,t]$ as $n\to\infty$, for every continuity point $t\in(0,1)$ of $\mu$.

\end{enumerate}

PRIVATE AUTHOR-CHECKED DRAFT, no independent review. If indicators I_x on N sites have deterministic sum k, then Var(sum over B of I_x)=Var(sum over the complement of B of I_x)<=min(|B|,N-|B|)^2/4. In particular a window omitting one site has variance at most 1/4, so a positive size-uniform lower bound proportional to its volume is impossible as N grows. This does not rule out linear variance on genuinely small windows, and global covariance cancellation does not prove mesoscopic hyperuniformity.

metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:5bd16760a5ae06001bdb31c94de2c044cc910609eb166a6aab5ad45688c43ae2","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/5b/5bd16760a5ae06001bdb31c94de2c044cc910609eb166a6aab5ad45688c43ae2.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:927afb676ae68f04ff269bf2890ea471aa6c7d98f43063cd34f03e1dbddf9ae5","bundle_entry_key":"fixed","bundle_id":"population.probability-variance-joint-laws-and-voronoi-partials-007","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"codex-probability-01a07a40/bundle_007.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.stochastic:fixed-mass-complement-window-variance-obstruction","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Fixed mass and the ARW window-variance questions

Status: author-checked scope counterexample only. No independent review or novelty claim. The intended mesoscopic hyperuniformity problems remain unsolved.

Source: Levine and Silvestri, *Universality Conjectures for Activated Random Walk*, arXiv:2306.01698v2, Conjecture 27 and Question 28, PDF pages 15-16. Corpus entries P0389 and P0390. The two questions concern different laws, but share the following necessary correction to the observation-window quantifier.

## Deterministic complement identity

Let T be a finite set with N sites, and let I_x be zero-one occupation indicators with exactly k occupied sites almost surely. For every B contained in T,

$$S_B=\sum_{x\in B}I_x=k-S_{T\setminus B},\qquad \operatorname{Var}(S_B)=\operatorname{Var}(S_{T\setminus B}).$$

Both counts are bounded by their respective window sizes. The variance bound for a variable in an interval of length a is a squared divided by four. Thus

$$\operatorname{Var}(S_B)\le\frac14\min\{|B|,N-|B|\}^2.$$

This proof uses only fixed total mass, which holds after every free-chain addition and throughout each fixed-particle-number wake chain.

## Proper boxes already contradict the unrestricted lower bound

Take d=1 and T the cycle with L vertices. Fix any positive subcritical density rho, and put k=floor(rho L). Take the proper interval B consisting of L-1 vertices. If x is the omitted vertex, S_B=k-I_x, so its variance is at most 1/4. It cannot be at least c(L-1) for any positive c independent of L.

Uniform free driving is translation equivariant. For the wake chain, the unique stationary law is translation invariant because the transition kernel commutes with translations. Therefore each single-site mean is rho_L=k/L in both ensembles, and the variance of this proper box is exactly rho_L(1-rho_L). The whole torus gives the even simpler value zero, but the proper interval shows that requiring merely a strict subset does not repair the claim.

At zero density the configuration is empty and has variance zero for every window, giving another boundary exception. The positive fixed-density argument above does not rely on that exception.

## Global cancellation is not mesoscopic hyperuniformity

Under any fixed-mass law,

$$\sum_{y\in T}\operatorname{Cov}(I_x,I_y)=\operatorname{Cov}(I_x,k)=0.$$

Consider, only as a comparison model, a uniformly chosen k-subset of T. For x distinct from y,

$$\mathbb E I_x=\frac{k}{N},\qquad\mathbb E I_xI_y=\frac{k(k-1)}{N(N-1)}.$$

For a window with b sites, expansion of the variance gives

$$\operatorname{Var}(S_B)=b\,\rho_N(1-\rho_N)\frac{N-b}{N-1},\qquad\rho_N=k/N.$$

When b grows but b/N tends to zero and rho_N tends to a number strictly between zero and one, this is asymptotic to b times rho(1-rho). Therefore exact finite-volume covariance cancellation is compatible with volume-order mesoscopic fluctuations. Passing a finite-torus zero sum to an infinite-volume covariance sum requires additional uniform tail control.

## What remains

The natural next version restricts windows away from full volume, or takes the thermodynamic limit before the window limit. Neither restriction is asserted to have been prescribed by the source. Proving the ARW transition and its exponent in such a regime remains the actual mathematical problem. These elementary identities do not show that either actual ARW law is a uniform subset law, negatively associated, or hyperuniform.

## Second check

An exact rational enumeration of all k-subsets for small N independently checks the comparison variance and complement formula. The enumeration is a finite arithmetic control, not evidence that an unbounded ARW conjecture is solved. Then Lambda_epsilon(A) is the set of eigenvalues of all A + E with ||E|| <= epsilon, and for epsilon > 0 and z not in the spectrum of A, z is in Lambda_epsilon(A) exactly when ||(zI - A)^-1|| >= 1/epsilon. A witness: if (zI - A) v = s u for unit singular vectors with s = sigma_min(zI - A), then E = s u v* has norm s and makes z an eigenvalue of A + E.

[Definition 16 of arXiv:2609.02017, 'Optimal girth-dependent bounds for the Bethe approximation of the permanent'] For every $e\in E$, define
\begin{align*}
  \mathsf J_e^+
  &:=
  p_e\KL\bigl(
    \mc{L}(X_\star\mid E_e=1)
    \,\big\|\,
    \mc{L}(X_\star)
  \bigr),\\
  \mathsf J_e^-
  &:=
  (1-p_e)\KL\bigl(
    \mc{L}(X_\star\mid E_e=0)
    \,\big\|\,
    \mc{L}(X_\star)
  \bigr).
\end{align*}
We set $\mathsf J_e^+=0$ when $p_e=0$ and
$\mathsf J_e^-=0$ when $p_e=1$; the formulas below are interpreted
using the same convention.
Thus, recalling \eqref{eq:mutual-information}, we have
\[
  I(X_\star;E_e)=\mathsf J_e^++\mathsf J_e^-.
\]
For every $v\in V$, define
\[
  \mathsf J_v^+
  :=\sum_{e\ni v}\mathsf J_e^+,
  \qquad
  \mathsf J_v^-
  :=\sum_{e\ni v}\mathsf J_e^-.
\]
title: Definition 16 of arXiv:2609.02017

[Theorem thm:domregime of arXiv:2606.01866, 'Phase Transition of a Semiflexible Membrane in Two Dimensions'] For $d=2$, let $\{\phi_x\}_{x\in V_N}$ be as in (thm:compregime of the paper). Fix $\delta\in(0,1)$. Then the following holds for $x,y\in V_N^\delta$:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
        \item(DGFF domination regime) If $\lambda<0$, then
            \[\operatorname{Cov}(\phi_x,\phi_y)=\operatorname{Cov}^\nabla_N(\phi_x,\phi_y)+O(N^\lambda).\]
        \item(MM domination regime) If $\lambda>2$, then
        \[\operatorname{Cov}(\phi_x,\phi_y)=N^{-\lambda}\operatorname{Cov}^{\Delta}_N(\phi_x,\phi_y)+O(N^{4-2\lambda}\log N).\]
    \end{enumerate}
    Here, $\operatorname{Cov}^{\Delta}_N(\phi_x,\phi_y)$ denotes the covariance of the two-dimensional MM with zero boundary conditions. It coincides with the Green function $G^{\Delta}_N(x,y)$ of the following boundary value problem: for any fixed $y\in V_N$,
    \begin{equation}
        \begin{aligned}
            \Delta^2 G^{\Delta}_N(x,y)&=\delta_y(x),&&\quad \forall x\in V_N,\\
            G^{\Delta}_N(x,y)&=0,&&\quad \forall x\in\partial_2 V_N.
        \end{aligned}
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Covariance calculation for dominant regime

body: [Theorem 4 of arXiv:2511.05218, 'On the Color Discrepancy of Spanning Trees in Random and Randomly Perturbed Graphs'] For any $\alpha\in(0,1)$, there exists a constant $\lambda=\lambda(\alpha)$ such that the following statement holds. For any graph $G_{\alpha}$ on $n$ vertices with $\delta(G_{\alpha})\geq\alpha n$, and a probability function $p=p(n)$ with $\frac{1}{n^{2}}\ll p(n)\ll\frac{1}{n}$, with high probability, the randomly perturbed graph $H=G_{\alpha}\cup G(n,p)$ contains a spanning tree $T$ with $\left|\sum_{e\in E(T)}\chi(e)\right|\geq\lambda pn^{2}$ under any coloring $\chi:E(H)\rightarrow\{+1,-1\}$.

[Defi 1 (Indistinguishability) of arXiv:2512.02766, 'Fine-Graining and Continuous Space Scaling Limit of the $H^{2|2}$ Model on the Hierarchica'] Given a finite weighted graph $\mathcal{G}=(V,E,W)$, we say that a subset $U\subset V$ is \emph{indistinguishable from outside} if
\begin{equation*}
    \forall i,j\in U, \forall k\notin U,\quad W_{ki}=W_{kj}.
\end{equation*}
If additionally a boundary condition $\eta\in \mathbb{R}_{+}^{V}$ is given, $U$ is indistinguishable from outside if additionally
$$\forall i,j\in U,\ \eta_{i}=\eta_{j}.$$
In words, for a given vertex $k$ not in $U$, it is connected to all vertices in $U$ with the same weight.
title: Indistinguishability

$D(-p^2)$-tuple satisfies the same bound as in the positive case. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:FP of arXiv:2609.00636, 'Forcing monochromatic subdivisions'] Let $d \ge 1$ and $n \ge 1$. If $H$ is a non-empty graph satisfying
\[
  |N_H(X)| \ge (d+1)|X|
\]
for every $X \subseteq V(H)$ with $|X| \le 2n-2$, then $H$ contains
every tree with at most $n$ vertices and maximum degree at most~$d$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
