# Relative attractor construction for exact-band rigidity
Supplement to T421-W706-021 v5 Section6. Kind:special; target1.
Status: proof (unaudited). This verifies an abstract implication, conditional
on the full-path classification and strict end ordering of021 Section5.
It is not an independent proof of those source-dependent inputs.

HYPOTHESES. K is a nonempty compact metric space, R a closed subset of K times K,
and every point has at least one incoming and outgoing R-edge in K.
A continuous H:K->R is nondecreasing on edges. There are finitely many
critical periodic orbits. Every full doubly infinite path approaches one
such orbit at each time end. If a full path is not itself critical, its
forward critical end has STRICTLY larger H value than its backward end.
Each critical state has a unique outgoing edge, its ordinary successor.
The R-chain convention is true edges followed by small jumps, including
a final small jump to the desired endpoint, as in021 Section3.

CONCLUSION. If K is internally chain transitive, it is one critical orbit.

1. Closed relations and nested images.
For compact C subset K, R(C) is compact as the projection of the compact
set R intersect (C times K). Moreover for nested nonempty compact C_n,
 R(intersection_n C_n)=intersection_n R(C_n).
The forward inclusion is immediate. For the reverse, fix y in every
R(C_n). Its possible predecessors in C_n form nested nonempty compact
sets. Their intersection supplies a predecessor in intersection C_n.
No lower semicontinuity or continuous selection is used.

Choose h_max, the largest critical H value in K, and h<h_max above all
smaller critical values. At least one critical orbit exists by taking a
full path through any point; compactness supplies the stated end orbits
in K. Set U={H>=h}, with interiors always relative to K. It is nonempty,
compact and positively invariant. C_n=R^n(U), n>=0, are nested nonempty
compact sets: R(U) subset U by monotonicity, and every point has an outgoing
edge. Their intersection A satisfies R(A)=A by the preceding identity.
In particular each point of A has incoming and outgoing edges in A, and
one can recursively choose a full path in A through it. Positive-time
choices remain in A; predecessor choices use R(A)=A.

Every such full path has both end orbits in U, necessarily at level
h_max. Strict end ordering excludes every noncritical full path. Thus
A consists exactly of the union of critical orbits at level h_max.
Conversely each such orbit is contained in every R^n(U), because it has
arbitrarily long predecessors in that orbit. Therefore A subset int_K U,
since its H value is strictly greater than h.

2. Finite entry into the interior and one-step trapping.
Some N>=1 satisfies C_N subset int_K U. Otherwise the nested nonempty
compact sets C_n intersect (K minus int_K U) have a common point, which
would belong to A outside int_K U. If K!=A then some x in K lies outside
U: if U=K, seriality in both directions gives R(K)=K and A=K. Since U
is compact and x is outside, its distance from x is positive.

We use the following upper-neighborhood fact: if C is compact and
R(C) subset O for an open O, then a sufficiently small closed metric
neighborhood N_eta(C) in K satisfies R(N_eta(C)) subset O. Otherwise
choose eta_n->0 and edges with source tending to C and target outside O.
A convergent subsequence and closedness give an edge from C to K minus O,
contradiction. Closed metric neighborhoods are compact here.

If N=1 use W=U. If N>1, work backward j=N-1,...,1. Given an open
neighborhood O of C_(j+1), the upper-neighborhood fact permits a compact
neighborhood W_j of C_j with R(W_j) subset O and excluding x. Start
with O=int_K U and subsequently use O=int_K W_(j+1). Each C_j is a
subset of U, so x can always be excluded. Taking W_0=U gives
 R(W_(N-1)) subset int_K U,
 R(W_j) subset int_K W_(j+1), 1<=j<N-1,
 R(U)=C_1 subset int_K W_1.
Thus W=union_(j=0)^(N-1) W_j is compact, contains A, excludes x, and
 R(W) subset int_K W.
U itself need not be a neighborhood of all of U; only its interior
containing C_N and A is used. This avoids a hidden openness assumption.

3. Chains cannot escape.
R(W) and K minus int_K W are disjoint compact sets and both are
nonempty when needed; their distance gamma is positive. A relation
chain whose first source is in A remains in W when every jump is less
than gamma: an edge with source in W has target in R(W), and any such
jump lands in int_K W. The same gap prevents its final jump from reaching
x outside W. This contradicts internal chain transitivity. Hence K=A.
On A, true edges follow the unique critical successors. The finite set
of distinct critical orbits has positive separation; chains with smaller
jumps cannot switch orbits. Internal chain transitivity leaves one orbit.

APPLICATION / LIMITS. The closed compact relation, monotone H and unique
critical edges in021 meet the structural hypotheses only subject to their
own proofs. The hardest input still to audit is Section5: all full path
end limits are the nine critical states, with strict ordering for a
noncritical path. This note closes neither that input nor the entire
frontier target. The finite three-state check exercises a strictly
specified discrete analogue; it is not a certificate for the continuum.


# End-limit extraction and the boundary of the023 audit
Supplement to T421-W706-021 v5 Section5. Kind:special; target1.
Status: supporting proof (unaudited). Claim023 v1 itself has reviewer PASS;
that PASS does not extend to the implication below or to021.

1. Work and dissipation are different hypotheses.
In021 write W_i=(q_i')^2-2*y_i*q_i' and
Psi_i=phi_i'-phi_i-W_i. For an exact-band edge sum_i lambda_i W_i=0,
so H'-H=sum_i lambda_i Psi_i, with Psi_i>=0.
An end-limit path has constant H and hence each Psi_i=0, because every
lambda_i>0. This is zero DISSIPATION, not a proof that each W_i=0.
The product work constraint alone permits cancellation between channels.
For example (lambda1,lambda2)=(1,1),(W1,W2)=(1,-1) satisfies the constraint.
This arithmetic example is not asserted to be an Adam relation edge.

Audited023 assumes scalar exact zero WORK at every integer time:
 X_t^2*(1/(sqrt(V_(t+1))+rho)-1/D)=0.
It applies to bounded full raw physical paths at positive rho in its
stated interval. It does not assert a classification of zero-Psi paths,
and it does not cover rho=0 by its own statement. Invoking its PASS for
all021 end-limit paths would require an additional bridge. In particular,
the source H.5 equality-case analysis in021 Section4 remains necessary,
especially at the singular origin and rho=0 compactification.

2. A precise compact extraction lemma.
Let K be compact metric, R closed in K times K, H continuous and
Psi_i continuous nonnegative on R, with fixed positive weights lambda_i.
Suppose H(y)-H(x)=sum_i lambda_i Psi_i(x,y) on R, and (z_n) indexed by
all integers is a full R-path. Bounded monotonic H(z_n) has limits h_minus
and h_plus as n tends to negative and positive infinity.

For ANY accumulation point w at either time end, choose n_j tending to
that end with z_(n_j)->w. Compactness and a countable diagonal subsequence
make z_(n_j+k) converge to w_k simultaneously for every integer k, with
w_0=w. Closedness gives (w_k,w_(k+1)) in R. For each fixed k,
H(w_k)=lim_j H(z_(n_j+k))=h_end by continuity. Thus
sum_i lambda_i Psi_i(w_k,w_(k+1))=0, and positivity forces EACH term zero.
Every end accumulation point therefore lies on a full zero-dissipation
path. This is a finite-sum argument, not an interchange of a limit with
an infinite sum; the diagonal subsequence preserves every finite edge.

3. What the missing classification would imply.
IF every full zero-dissipation path consists of one of the finitely many
critical periodic orbits, the previous lemma puts both end accumulation
sets in that finite critical set. Compactness then implies distance of
the original path to that set tends to zero at each end. With the unique
critical-successor and robust separation of065, each tail stays in one
critical orbit group and approaches its correct phases. The two H end
limits are its respective critical values.
If the full path is not itself critical, the assumed zero-dissipation
classification implies that some edge has some Psi_i>0. Consequently
 h_plus-h_minus >= H(z_(n+1))-H(z_n)
                  =sum_i lambda_i Psi_i(z_n,z_(n+1))>0
at that edge. This supplies the strict end ordering required by066.

4. Audit boundary and next unpaid step.
The compact extraction and conditional ordering are supplied above as
written arguments,not independently checked proofs. The hardest remaining
input is021 Section4's classification of bounded full ZERO-DISSIPATION
paths on the broad closed relation,including rho=0. Claim023's audited
zero-work theorem is useful once its different hypotheses are obtained;
its PASS alone is not the missing equality-case bridge.

edge. This note does not present that calculation as new or rerun it.

on physical states V>=0, with s=sqrt(V)+e and primed analogues:
 V'=d*V+(1-d)*y^2, z'=y, q'*s'=y,
 u*s'=s, u>=0,
 y'=y+b*u*(y-z)-(1+b)*q', q*s=z.
A full path indexed by all integers with uniformly bounded V cannot
contain a state (y,z,V,q)=(0,0,V0,0) with V0>0. Branch labels are arbitrary
subject to their own restrictions; the argument uses neither label.

backwards yields V_(-k)=V0*d^(-k) for every integer k>=0.

boundedness. This is a full-history obstruction, not a claim about a
one-sided orbit: positive pure variance has a perfectly valid forward

from positive variances; u>0 follows from u*s'=s; and b>0 is a hypothesis.

constant positive pure variance is a bounded full path. If boundedness
or full negative-time history is removed, the forward orbit above is
not excluded. The lemma does not exclude limit states reached by
one-sided paths unless a full bounded limiting history has been obtained.

Together with070 this handles the regular labelled threshold interfaces,

# Regular-threshold exclusion and a finite-window dissipation barrier
Supplement to T421-W706-021 v5; kind special; target1.
Status: proof (unaudited). No new frontier score or full021 promotion.

HYPOTHESES, NOT CONCLUSIONS OF COMPACTNESS
Use the compact labelled lifted relation R of021, or any compact closed
relation with the following properties. Parameters are constant along
paths and range in a compact set with0<=e_i<=e_max<1/2 and positive
weights lambda_i bounded below. Physical variances are nonnegative and
bounded. All scalar edges obey069's equations with b=.9,d=.999.
The lifted scalar dissipations Psi_i are continuous nonnegative on R,
and the labelled threshold formulas are those of070/074. Every bounded
full path satisfies the F3 lower bound w>=c needed by074 at a regular
high-source/low-target threshold. These are structural/source hypotheses;
they have not been independently checked for the entire021 relation.
Let s_i=sqrt(V_i)+e_i and similarly s_i_prime, with physical curvature
variables p_i=1/s_i,w_i=1/s_i_prime whenever these speeds are positive.
Fix sigma>0. Let C_sigma be the closed subset of R on which at least one
coordinate has s_i,s_i_prime>=sigma and either s_i=1 or s_i_prime=1.
All labels are retained as distinct copies, as in070/074.

1. NO BOUNDED FULL ZERO-DISSIPATION PATH MEETS C_sigma.
Suppose a full R path has every Psi_i=0 at every integer time and a
central edge in C_sigma. Choose a coordinate witnessing membership.
If both speeds are1,070 makes its Psi strictly positive. Otherwise074
makes it strictly positive except for the explicit low-source target-
threshold pure-variance equality. That exception has y=z=q=0 and
V=(1-e)^2/d>0 at its source. The relation q*s=z implies q=0 since
s>0. Lemma069 excludes this state on any bounded full physical path.
All cases contradict zero dissipation. This argument uses no assertion
that individual work terms W_i vanish, and uses no023 audit.

The regularity trim is essential to this statement's scope. No claim is
made here for s_i=0 or s_i_prime=0; those singular edges still require
the main021 origin analysis. Nor does this classify full zero-Psi paths
that stay in the interiors of the labelled branches.

2. UNIFORM FINITE-WINDOW PAYMENT.
Put D(edge)=sum_i lambda_i*Psi_i(edge)>=0, continuous on compact R.
There are an integer N>=1 and epsilon>0 such that every finite R path
(z_n) for -N<=n<=N+1 whose central edge lies in C_sigma satisfies
 sum_{n=-N}^N D(z_n,z_(n+1))>=epsilon.                    (1)
If there is no such finite path, the assertion is vacuous.

Otherwise, if no N,epsilon exist, for each integer j>=1 select an
R path on[-j,j+1] with central edge in C_sigma and total D<1/j.
Compactness of the state and auxiliary edge spaces and a countable
diagonal subsequence yield a full limit R path on all integers. Every
fixed edge has0<=D<=1/j on sufficiently long selected windows, hence
has limiting D=0. Since each lambda_i>0 and each Psi_i>=0, every
Psi_i on that limit edge is zero. Closedness keeps its central edge
in C_sigma. This contradicts Section1, proving(1). This is a finite-sum
positivity argument followed by a diagonal limit, not a product of
conditional probabilities or an independence assertion.

3. ROBUST PAYMENT NEAR THE TRIMMED THRESHOLD.
For the fixed N above the space of all length(2N+1)-edge R paths is
compact. There exist delta>0 and epsilon_prime>0, for example a possibly
shrunk epsilon/2, such that central-edge distance to C_sigma<=delta
implies total window D>=epsilon_prime. Otherwise choose windows with
central-edge distance tending to zero and total D<epsilon/2. A convergent
subsequence has central edge in C_sigma, contradicting(1). If C_sigma
is empty there are no near-threshold assertions needed.

4. APPLICATION TO MONOTONE FULL EXACT-BAND PATHS.
Additionally suppose H is continuous on the compact state space and
 H(z_(n+1))-H(z_n)=D(z_n,z_(n+1)).
Then a full exact-band path visits the delta-neighborhood of C_sigma
only finitely often in each time direction. Indeed, infinitely many
visits permit infinitely many pairwise disjoint windows of length2N+1;
Section3 makes their total D infinite, contradicting the telescoping
bound sup H-inf H<infinity. Equivalently every end-limit full path from
068 has zero dissipation and avoids C_sigma. This conclusion is for
exact relation paths only. Passing it to corrected iterates requires a
separate approximation/error argument; it is not asserted here.

UNPAID PIECE
The regular threshold interfaces are excluded under the displayed
structural hypotheses. The remaining main021 task is the full zero-
dissipation equality classification on the interior branches and at
singular s=0 edges, including e=0, followed by the existing global
confinement/capture argument. Source F3 and nonnegative-continuous lifted
Psi on the full relation remain hypotheses to be independently audited.
The finite-graph check is only a checkable analogue of Sections2--4;
it does not certify compactness or the full Adam relation.

FINITE ANALOGUE VALIDATION: scripts/check_finite_threshold_barrier.py
enumerates all19,683 three-vertex directed graphs with absent/zero/unit-
cost edges using exact integer min-plus arithmetic. For78,345 marked
edges excluded from bounded full zero-cost paths,72,549 have positive
length-seven window cost and5,796 have no such window. The39,753
full-zero-path control edges have window cost0 and would violate the
barrier if its exclusion hypothesis were omitted. Radius N=3 and gap1
are finite-graph facts only. They supply no numerical constants for the
compact Adam relation. Full record:logs/finite_threshold_barrier_exact.json.

# Zero variance on a full zero-dissipation lifted path
Supporting clarification of T421-W706-021 v5, Section4 of056.
Kind: special; target: 1. Status: proof (unaudited).
This spells out an existing boundary argument; no new frontier score or novelty claim.

Fix b=9/10, d=999/1000 and constant e>=0. Let a path indexed by every
integer satisfy the state constraints and edge equations of056(2),(4):
 V>=0, s=sqrt(V)+e, q*s=z,
 V'=d*V+(1-d)*y^2, z'=y, q'*s'=y,
 u*s'=s, 0<=u<=1/sqrt(d),
 y'=y+b*u*(y-z)-(1+b)*q'.
Assume Psi=0 on every edge, using the labeled potential of056(3).
If V_t=0 at any time, then (y,z,V,q)=(0,0,0,0) at every time.
Boundedness is unnecessary for this implication. Constant e and full
negative-time history are hypotheses, not consequences of one-sided data.

PROOF. Shift the given time to0. Nonnegativity and 0<d<1 in the variance
recursion imply V_-1=y_-1=0. Induction gives V_j=y_j=0 for all j<0.
Since z_j=y_(j-1), z_j=0 for all j<=0.

If e>0, s_j=e for j<=0, so q_j=0 for j<=0. On edge -1 to0,
0=y_-1=z_-1=q_0 forces y_0=0 by the position recursion. Thereafter,
V'=0, s'=e, q'=y/e=0, and z'=0 imply y'=0 and u=1. Induction proves
the claim forward; all negative-time coordinates were already zero.
This case needs no dissipation identity.

If e=0, every edge with source y=z=V=0 has s=s'=0 and high labels
at both endpoints. The EXISTING identity056(6) is
 Psi=99*(q')^2/200+q^2/2.
Zero dissipation forces q=q'=0 and the position equation gives y'=0,
regardless of the permitted u. Applying this first to every negative-time
edge gives q_j=0 for all j<=0 and y_0=0. Applying it successively forward
gives all remaining y,z,V,q zero. This uses the already derived identity,
not a new derivation or an independent audit of the whole compact relation.

PHYSICAL PROJECTION. At e=0, u*s'=s reduces to0=0. Every choice of u
in [0,1/sqrt(d)] is consistent with the zero physical edge; u can vary
between edges. Thus the physical projection is fixed, but an edge decorated
with u is not uniquely determined. Do not substitute uniqueness of the
entire decorated relation for physical uniqueness in an ICT argument.
At e>0 the two branch copies can coexist when e=1; the physical conclusion
still holds. In021's e<1/2 range only the high label occurs at this origin.

LIMITS / CONTROL. A one-sided path with V_0=0 and y_0!=0 can have
V_1=(1-d)*y_0^2>0. Its existence does not contradict the lemma: such a
state has no nonnegative full backward history satisfying the variance
and position constraints plus the zero-dissipation condition. For e=1,
y_0=1,z_0=q_0=V_0=0 gives an explicit regular forward edge (the exact
checker below supplies it). This control is not asserted to have Psi=0.

CHECK. scripts/check_zero_variance_full_path.py checks the rational
positivity coefficients, the deductions at the two origin branches, and
both distinct auxiliary choices u=0 and u=1 at the singular origin.
Its forward countercontrol is represented exactly with s_1=1+sqrt(1/1000).
These finite algebraic checks support the written induction; they do not
certify all full paths or independently audit021. No Lean certificate.

REMAINING FRONTIER BURDEN. Together with069 this removes zero-variance
and positive pure-variance boundary alternatives on bounded full zero-Psi
paths. The regular interior zero-Psi classification, compatibility of
threshold labels, and the complete compact-relation argument remain
separate obligations. This note does not establish typical tracking,
existence of tracking starts, or the full021 theorem.

# Corrected lifted edge limits and omega-set chains
Kind: special; target:1. Status: proof (unaudited).
Supporting argument for056 Section3, with a direct F3 derivation.
It does not independently audit the source potential inequalities or021.

1. The exact corrected recurrence and its limiting edge.
Fix eta>0, positive lambda_i and r=epsilon/eta>0. In one coordinate
use056's normalization c=1/19,b=9/10,d=999/1000,nu=1-d,
 y_t=x_t/(c eta), mu_t=m_t/(c eta lambda),
 V_t=v_t/(c eta lambda)^2, e=r/(c lambda)>0,
 z_t=y_(t-1), s_t=sqrt(V_t)+e, q_t=z_t/s_t.
Assume the actual tail and raw moments lie in a fixed bounded box;
this note does not re-prove the absorbing box. For t>=1 put
 kappa_t=(1-b^t)*(sqrt(V_t/(1-d^t))+e).
The position update at the PREVIOUS step gives exactly
 mu_t=-c*kappa_t*(y_t-z_t).
The raw recurrences mu_(t+1)=b*mu_t+(1-b)*y_t and
 V_(t+1)=d*V_t+nu*y_t^2 therefore imply
 y_(t+1)=y_t+b*(kappa_t/kappa_(t+1))*(y_t-z_t)
              -(1+b)*y_t/kappa_(t+1).                 (1)
Here (1-b)/c=1+b exactly; the clocks in kappa_(t+1) have index t+1.
On the bounded box kappa_t-s_t tends uniformly to zero at fixed e>0.
Indeed the sqrt clock factor tends to1, and its uncorrected argument
is uniformly bounded. For all sufficiently large t, kappa_t>=e/2.
All divisions in (1) thus pass to adjacent-pair limits. Every limiting
edge satisfies
 V'=dV+nu*y^2, z'=y, q'*s'=y, u=s/s',
 y'=y+b*u*(y-z)-(1+b)*q'.                             (2)
Also V>=nu*z^2, qs=z, u>=0 and d*u^2<=1, since
 s'>=sqrt(d)*sqrt(V)+e>=sqrt(d)*s.
Labels are part of a finite discrete coordinate: low at s>=1, high at
s<=1. At s=1 the two copies remain distinct. Label limits satisfy
these closed constraints; continuity of a single-valued label map is
neither asserted nor needed.

2. F3 from the bounded full gradient history.
Through any adjacent-pair limit, diagonal extraction of shifted raw
(y,mu,V) histories supplies a bounded doubly infinite uncorrected path.
Its moment recurrences unroll to the absolutely convergent formulas
 mu_t=(1-b)*sum_(j>=0) b^j*y_(t-1-j),
 V_t=nu*sum_(j>=0) d^j*y_(t-1-j)^2.                   (3)
Boundedness makes the discarded remainders b^n*mu_(t-n) and
d^n*V_(t-n) tend to zero. The past-step position equation is
 y_t=y_(t-1)-mu_t/(c*s_t).
Write B=1+b, s=s_t, V=V_t. In this linear functional of the past
positions the coefficient for j=0 is 1-B/s and for j>=1 is
 -B*b^j/s. Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz, with positive weights d^j and
b^2<d, gives
 nu*y_t^2 <= V*[1-2B/s+B^2*d/(s^2*(d-b^2))].          (4)
The bracket is the sum of squared functional coefficients divided
by d^j; in particular it is nonnegative. This is a deterministic
Hilbert-space inequality, not a concentration or independence argument.
The geometric series used is sum_(j>=1)(b^2/d)^j=b^2/(d-b^2).
Adding dV to (4), using V=(s-e)^2<=s^2 and positivity of the
resulting coefficient, yields
 V_(t+1) <= (1+d)*s^2-2B*s+B^2*d/(d-b^2).
For a high source 0<s<=1 and 1+d<2B, so its first two terms have
nonpositive sum. Consequently
 s'<=B*sqrt(d/(d-b^2))+e <3B+1/2=31/5                 (5)
whenever e<1/2. The square-root comparison uses d/(d-b^2)<9.
All constants in (5) are independent of the positive lower bound on e.
At e=0 singular source states are not derived by dividing by s here:
when parameters later tend to that boundary, the closed bound s'<=31/5
is inherited from these fixed-positive-e limiting edges instead.

3. Passing the active band without dividing at zero gradient.
With the post-variance-update convention in056, define
 qbar_i=y_i/(sqrt(V_i'/(1-d^(t+1)))+e_i),
 Dbar=sum_i lambda_i*y_i*qbar_i.
When the active quotient is defined its width-delta inequality is
 |sum_i lambda_i*(qbar_i^2-2*y_i*qbar_i)|<=c*delta*Dbar.
At fixed positive e_i, qbar_i-q_i' tends uniformly to zero on the
bounded box. Thus adjacent-pair limits obey the same multiplied band
with q_i'. This passage remains valid when the limiting gradient is
zero: no division by a limiting D is made. The statement here uses
exactly this timing convention; a different preconditioner timing
requires its own identification before applying this formula.

4. A compact-sequence lemma: restricted edge limits are chain transitive.
Let a_n be ANY sequence in a compact metric space, K its nonempty omega
set and G the set of all limits of pairs (a_n,a_(n+1)) as n->infinity.
Then G is compact and contained in K times K. Every point of K has an
incoming and an outgoing G-edge, by extraction of its predecessor or
successor along a subsequence. Also dist((a_n,a_(n+1)),G)->0; otherwise
a counterexample subsequence has a convergent pair limit belonging to G.

Fix x,y in K and epsilon>0. Choose h>0 with 2h<epsilon. Along a
subsequence a_n->x also extract a_(n+1)->v, giving the TRUE edge (x,v).
Choose n sufficiently late that dist(a_(n+1),v)<h and every later pair
is within h of G in the max product metric. Choose a later m>=n+2
with dist(a_m,y)<h. For j=n+1,...,m-1 replace the pair
(a_j,a_(j+1)) by an edge (A_j,B_j) of G within h.
Begin with (x,v). Its jump to A_(n+1) is <2h. Consecutive replacement
edges have jumps dist(B_j,A_(j+1))<2h, as does the last target's jump
to y. Thus this is an epsilon-chain with first source EXACTLY x,
all true edges and endpoints in K, and an allowed final jump to y.
There is no accumulated error and no uniform bound on m-n is required.
Therefore K is internally chain transitive for G and for every closed
relation restricted to K that contains G. This does not require
continuity of the label lift or of an underlying map.

5. Application boundary: what is CLEAN and what remains separate.
CLEAN for the compact-sequence lemma and the corrected algebra/F3
calculations above: their hypotheses, indices, inequality directions
and constants re-derive. For the actual lifted sequence, Sections1-3
place G in the physical and band constraints of056, assuming its
bounded box and its stated active-curvature timing convention.
The FIRST additional assertion not re-derived in this note is
 Psi_i=phi_i'-phi_i-W_i>=0 for every limiting labeled branch edge.
That is the source-potential inequality and all branch-closure cases;
it is not supplied by chain transitivity or Cauchy-Schwarz. Assuming
that inequality, G lies in056's restricted relation, and Section4 gives
all of056 Section3's seriality, full-path extraction, pair approach
and internal chain transitivity conclusions. The potential claims
074/079/083-086 and038 remain under independent audit. Neither a
reviewer PASS nor the global021 conclusion is asserted here.

[Definition 18 (Parabolic and hyperbolic THP) of arXiv:2608.03575, '2608.03575'] Let \(P\) be an infinite THP, and let \(P^{\rm trun}\) be the polyhedron
obtained by truncating all ideal and hyperideal vertices. Let
\(\{K_n\}_{n\geq 1}\) be an exhaustion of \(\mathbb H^3\) by compact sets.

\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
    \item \(P\) is called \emph{parabolic} if
    \(P^{\rm trun}\setminus K_n\) tends to a single point in
    \(\partial_\infty\mathbb H^3\). Equivalently, the set of accumulation
    points of the boundary faces of \(P\) consists of one point.

    \item \(P\) is called \emph{hyperbolic} if
    \(P^{\rm trun}\setminus K_n\) tends to a half-sphere in
    \(\partial_\infty\mathbb H^3\). Equivalently, the accumulation points of
    the boundary faces form a circle in \(\partial_\infty\mathbb H^3\), and
    all faces of \(P\) lie in one of the two half-spaces bounded by the
    hyperbolic plane determined by this circle.
\end{enumerate}
title: Parabolic and hyperbolic THP

[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2608.27708, 'Proof of the Lyons--White Conjecture'] For every symmetric rate collection $\blam$ and every $t\geq 0$, we have
\[h_t^{\blam}=\sum_{g\in G}P_t^{\blam}(g)g.\]
Moreover, $a_t^{\blam}$ is positive, and
\[\left(a_t^{\blam}\right)^\theta=e^{-\theta t\Delta_{\blam}}(e-\pi)\]
for every $\theta>0$.

body: [Definition 24 (Feasible independent set) of arXiv:2608.07239, 'Unified framework for asymptotically uniform iterative construction of generalised random '] Given a graph $G=(V,E)$ with a set $F\subset V$ of forbidden vertices and an equivalence relation $R\subset V^2$ of forbidden pairs of vertices, an independent set $S$ of $G$ is called \emph{feasible} (with respect to $F$ and $R$) if it is disjoint from $F$ and no two of its vertices are $R$-equivalent. The abbreviation \emph{FIS} stands for feasible independent set. An \emph{FMIS} (feasible maximum independent set) is an MIS that is feasible. An FIS is \emph{maximal} if it is not a strict subset of another FIS.
title: Feasible independent set

body: In probability theory, the de Moivre–Laplace theorem, which is a special case of the central limit theorem, states that the normal distribution may be used as an approximation to the binomial distribution under certain conditions. In particular, the theorem shows that the probability mass function of the random number of "successes" observed in a series of independent Bernoulli trials, each having probability of success, converges to the probability density function of the normal distribution with expectation and standard deviation , as grows large, assuming is not or .

body:
[Lemma lem:local-max of arXiv:2608.23135, 'Graph distance and effective resistance of the random walk trace in four and five dimensio'] There exist constants $C_1,C_2<\infty$, depending only on $\varepsilon$ and $\delta$, such that
\begin{equation}

\mathbb{P}\left(
\exists 1\le j\le M:
\max_{u_{j-1}\le r\le s\le u_j}X[r,s]> C_1\mathbb{E}[\Delta_n]
\right)
\le C_2(\log n)^{-1}.
\end{equation}
Consequently, outside an event of probability $O((\log n)^{-1})$,
\begin{equation}

\max_{u_{j-3}\le r\le s\le u_j}X[r,s]
\le C'_1\mathbb{E}[\Delta_n]
\qquad\text{for all }3\le j\le M.
\end{equation}
Moreover, if we fix $l,q>0$,  
then for every $p>0$ there is
$K=K(p,l,q,\varepsilon,\delta)$ such that
\begin{equation}

\mathbb{P}\left(
\exists r\le M:
\max_{u_r- l a_n^{(q)} \le s\le t\le u_r+{ la_n^{(q)}}}
X[s,t]
> K\mathbb{E}[X_{l a_n^{(q)}}]
\right)
\le (\log n)^{-p}.
\end{equation}
title: Lemma lem:local-max of arXiv:2608.23135

body:
[Lemma lem:vector-second-moment of arXiv:2606.25976, 'Gaussian rigidity for infinite exchangeable sequences'] Let \((X_i)_{i\ge1}\) be an exchangeable sequence of \(\mathbb{R}^d\)-valued random
vectors with de Finetti directing measure \(\eta\).  Suppose that
\(\mathbb{E} |X_1|^2<\infty\).  Then
\[
        M_\eta:=\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}x\eta(\,\mathrm{d} x)
\]
is well-defined a.s. and belongs to \(L^2\).  Moreover, with
\(\Sigma:=\operatorname{Cov}(X_1)\) and \(C:=\operatorname{Cov}(X_1,X_2)\) (which is symmetric by exchangeability), we have
\[0\preceq C\preceq\Sigma.\]
Here and below, \(A\preceq B\) means that \(B-A\) is positive semidefinite.

body: [Proposition prop:bounded_hausdorff of arXiv:2411.13133, 'Connectivity of the adjacency graph of\\ complementary components of the $\SLE$ Fan'] Fix $\kappa \in (0,4)$ and $a,b \in \mathbf{R}$ with $a+b > -2\lambda$.  Suppose that $h$ is a GFF on $\mathbf{H}$ with boundary conditions given by $-a$ on $\mathbf{R}_-$ and $b$ on $\mathbf{R}_+$.  For each $\theta \in \mathbf{R}$ we let $\eta_\theta$ be the flow line of $h$ from~$0$ to~$\infty$ with angle $\theta$.  Then~$\eta_\theta$ converges to~$\mathbf{R}_+$ in probability in the bounded Hausdorff metric as $\theta \downarrow -(\lambda+b)/\chi$. Furthermore, for any $\delta_0, p \in (0,1)$ and $R > 0$, there exists $\theta_0 > -(\lambda + b)/\chi$ (depending only on $\kappa$, $R$, $\delta_0$, $p$, $a$, and $b$) such that for any $\theta \in (-(\lambda+b)/\chi, \theta_0)$ the following holds with probability at least $1-p$: for each $x \in [0,R]$, there exists $y \in \eta_\theta \cap [0,R]$ such that $\n{x-y} \leq \delta_0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 47 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let \((U,h)\) be a smooth Riemannian manifold, and let
\(H_i,H:U\to\R^k\) be smooth maps with
\(H_i\to H\) in \(C^\infty_{\rm loc}\).  Suppose that \(0\) is a regular
value of \(H\), and set \(S=H^{-1}(0)\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.4em]
\item If \(K\Subset\operatorname{int}K^+\Subset S\) are compact
domains, then, for all large \(i\), \(H_i^{-1}(0)\) contains a small
normal graph \(K_i\) over \(K\), and \(K_i\to K\) smoothly.
\item If \(S\) is compact and is the entire zero set of \(H\) in a
precompact tubular neighbourhood \(U_0\Subset U\), then, for all large
\(i\), \(H_i^{-1}(0)\cap U_0\) contains a compact boundaryless normal
graph \(S_i\) over \(S\).  Moreover, \(S_i\to S\) smoothly and
\(S_i\cong S\).
\end{enumerate}
If Riemannian metrics \(h_i\) on \(U\) converge smoothly to \(h\), the
induced metrics and volume forms on these graphs converge smoothly. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Openquestion 34 (Reversal amplitude) of arXiv:2601.16580, 'Coin flipping and waiting times paradoxes \\ Why fair coins are exceptional'] Fix a tie convention.  Among all pairs with $\mathbb{E}[\tau_U]\ge \mathbb{E}[\tau_V]$, how large can the head‑to‑head advantage of $U$ over $V$ be?  Define the \emph{reversal gap}
\[
\Delta_{L_1,L_2}(p)\;:=\;\sup_{|U|=L_1,\,|V|=L_2,\ \mathbb{E}[\tau_U]\ge \mathbb{E}[\tau_V]}\Bigl(\Pr(U\!>\!V)-\tfrac12\Bigr).
\]
Determine (or bound) $\Delta_{L_1,L_2}(p)$ and its maximisers; relate them to border polynomials.
In particular, for fixed $(L_1,L_2)$ and $p$, can $\Delta_{L_1,L_2}(p)$ be bounded away from $1/2$, or can it approach $1/2$ (i.e.\ can a ``slower'' string win with probability arbitrarily close to $1$)? (Stated as a question by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Reversal amplitude

  Let $A$ be a random Hermitian matrix of size $N$
  and $0 < \theta < 1$. Assume that for every finite $r$ we have
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{N^{\theta}} \log \mathbb{E} [H

    (A))] = \sum_{i = 1}^r \Psi (x_i),

  where $\Psi$ is a smooth function in a complex neighborhood of $0$ and the above
  convergence is uniform in a complex neighborhood of $0^r$. Then, for every $k \in

  1}^N \delta \left( N^{- 1} \lambda_i (A) \right)$ converges in
  probability to $\dfrac{\Psi^{(k)} (0)}{(k - 1)!}$, as $N \rightarrow \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop Sgn of arXiv:2609.00672, 'Deciding superellipticity and computing the Weierstrass normal form'] Let $g\ge 2$.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $\mathcal S_{g,n}=\emptyset$ for $n>2g+2$.
\item For $g+2<n\le 2g+2$, the locus $\mathcal S_{g,n}$ is empty unless $n\in\{2g+1,2g+2\}$, and then it consists of the single point $y^n=x^2-1$, which lies in the hyperelliptic locus.
\item Let $3\le n\le g+2$ and $\mathcal S_{g,n}\ne\emptyset$. Then the datum $\mathbf C_{g,n}$ has $m\ge 3$. If $3\mid g+2$, then $\mathcal S_{g,g+2}$ contains the non-hyperelliptic curve $y^{g+2}=x^3-x$.
\end{enumerate}

There exist $c,C>0$ such that for all $m\in\N$ and $u\geq0$, we have
\begin{align}
        \P\Big(
        \max_{0\le k\le m}\|S_k\|_\infty>u
        \Big)
        \le
        Ce^{-cu^2/\sigma_m^2}\,.
\end{align}
where we use the convention that $1/\sigma_m^2 \coloneqq 0$ when $\sigma_m = 0$.
Moreover, for all $\lambda,K>0$, there exists $C_\lambda<\infty$ (also depending on $K$) such
that whenever $\sigma_m \in [0,K]$, we have
\begin{align}
        \E\big[\exp( \lambda \max_{0\leq k\leq m} \|S_k\|_\infty)\big]-1
        \leq
        C_\lambda\sigma_m .
\end{align}

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Asymptotic total length of finite SIRSN samples structural attempt Result: A local truncation argument gives the lower bound liminf E length/k>=ell. Tile the bulk of the large square by unit cells. For fixed R and M, retain in each cell only the length, truncated at M, of routes between sampled endpoints within distance R of that cell. Its local binomial point configuration converges in total variation to the corresponding rate1 Poisson configuration. The retained length is bounded by M, so its expectation converges. Summing disjoint unit-cell contributions and then taking k to infinity gives the Poisson local truncated expectation as a lower bound. Let M and then R increase: monotone convergence recovers the full sampled-network intensity ell. Check: Only a bounded endpoint region is used before taking k to infinity; its binomial count tends to a Poisson count and conditional positions have the same uniform law. Truncation avoids any unproved uniform-integrability step. Boundary cells are an asymptotically negligible fraction for fixed R. Obstruction: This proves no upper bound on total length. Rare paths can leave the sampling square by a large distance, and their exterior contribution is absent from the local lower-bound argument. Controlling those excursions remains necessary for equality.

[Lemma lem:finite-type-one-cycle-convergence of arXiv:2607.04264, 'Macroscopic Feynman Cycles and Poisson--Kingman Universality in Bose Condensation'] Assume (equation eq:finite-type-band-parameter-convergence of the paper).  Then, for every
\(0<\delta<R<\infty\) and every
\[
  F\in
  C_b\bigl([0,1]\times[\delta,R]\times\mathsf M_{\mathrm{ft}}\bigr),
\]
one has
\[
  \sup_{x\in[\delta,R]}
  \Bigg|
  \int_0^1
  \int_{\mathsf M_{\mathrm{ft}}}
  F(u,x,m)\,
  \mu_{L,\lfloor xV_L\rfloor}^{\mathrm{ft}}(dm)\,du
  -
  \int_0^1
  \int_{\mathsf M_{\mathrm{ft}}}
  F(u,x,m)\,
  \eta_x^{\mathrm{ft}}(dm)\,du
  \Bigg|
  \longrightarrow0 .
\]
Moreover,
\[
  \sup_{L\ge1}\sup_{j\ge1}
  q_{L,j}^{\mathrm{ft}}
  \le
  \sum_{r=1}^Q\theta_r
  <\infty .
\]

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Explicit calculation or obstruction with source-specific scope Result: An annulus semigroup with a self-adjoint generator would yield an abstract spectral resolution, but the spectral theorem alone does not identify the multiplicity or the W-algebra descendant states required in a bootstrap integral. A diagnostic is multiplication by x on L2([0,1]) versus multiplication by x on L2([0,1]) direct-summed with itself: both have spectrum [0,1], identical semigroup norm exp(0)=1 for positive times, and different spectral multiplicity. Check: The second operator has two orthogonal spectral channels over every interval of positive measure. Equality of spectral sets and operator norms therefore cannot imply a complete one-channel expansion. Obstruction: A proof needs the actual Toda scattering transform, its Plancherel measure and multiplicities, identification of descendants, and justified sewing integrals. Neither an abstract existence theorem for the path integral nor a conjectural structure constant resolves these completeness and integrability requirements.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0299-probabilistic-conformal-bootstrap-for-toda-theory

[Definition 12 (Truncated extended generator) of arXiv:2607.17192, 'Geometric Regime--Switching Diffusions on Stratified Riemannian Spaces with an Application'] A measurable function $V:E\to\mathbb R$ is said to belong to the domain
		$D(A^\ast_m)$ if there exists a measurable function
		$G_m:E\to\mathbb R$ such that
		\[
			\mathbb E_x[V(X_t^{(m)})]
			=V(x)+\mathbb E_x\!\left[\int_0^{t \wedge T_m} G_m(X_s)\,ds\right],
			\qquad t\ge 0,\ x\in E
		\]
		and $\E_x [\int_{0}^{t\wedge T_m}|G_m(X_s)|\, ds]<\infty$
		for all $t\ge 0$.
		In that case we write $A^\ast_m V:=G_m$ on $O_m$.
title: Truncated extended generator

[Lemma G-global-spectra-tensoring of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] The smash product $\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*\times\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}\to\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}$ is a left Quillen bifunctor for the $\mathchoice{\hbox{\hfuzz=20pt\hbox{$\mathcal A\kern-.3pt$}\setbox0=\hbox{$\ell\kern-.75pt\ell$}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern-.075pt\unhcopy0}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern.075pt\unhcopy0}\box0\kern.05pt}}{\hbox{\hfuzz=20pt\hbox{$\mathcal A\kern-.3pt$}\setbox0=\hbox{$\ell\kern-.75pt\ell$}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern-.075pt\unhcopy0}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern.075pt\unhcopy0}\box0\kern.05pt}}{{\mathcal{A}}\kern-.3pt\ell\kern-.6pt\ell}{{\mathcal{A}}\kern-.3pt\ell\kern-.6pt\ell}$-model structure on $\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*$ and the $G$-global model structure on $\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}$. Moreover, if $X\in\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*$ is $\mathchoice{\hbox{\hfuzz=20pt\hbox{$\mathcal A\kern-.3pt$}\setbox0=\hbox{$\ell\kern-.75pt\ell$}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern-.075pt\unhcopy0}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern.075pt\unhcopy0}\box0\kern.05pt}}{\hbox{\hfuzz=20pt\hbox{$\mathcal A\kern-.3pt$}\setbox0=\hbox{$\ell\kern-.75pt\ell$}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern-.075pt\unhcopy0}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern.075pt\unhcopy0}\box0\kern.05pt}}{{\mathcal{A}}\kern-.3pt\ell\kern-.6pt\ell}{{\mathcal{A}}\kern-.3pt\ell\kern-.6pt\ell}$-cofibrant, then $X\smashp{-}$ is fully homotopical, and if $Y\in\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}$ is flat, so is ${-}\smashp Y\colon\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*\to\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}$.
    \begin{proof}
        The pushout product axiom for cofibrations follows from Lemmas~(lemma:restr-gl-sp-right-Quillen of the paper) and~(lemma:restr-inj-gl-sp-left-Quillen of the paper) as in the proof of Lemma~(lemma:G-Top*-tensored of the paper). Moreover, if $X\in\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*$ is $\mathchoice{\hbox{\hfuzz=20pt\hbox{$\mathcal A\kern-.3pt$}\setbox0=\hbox{$\ell\kern-.75pt\ell$}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern-.075pt\unhcopy0}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern.075pt\unhcopy0}\box0\kern.05pt}}{\hbox{\hfuzz=20pt\hbox{$\mathcal A\kern-.3pt$}\setbox0=\hbox{$\ell\kern-.75pt\ell$}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern-.075pt\unhcopy0}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern.075pt\unhcopy0}\box0\kern.05pt}}{{\mathcal{A}}\kern-.3pt\ell\kern-.6pt\ell}{{\mathcal{A}}\kern-.3pt\ell\kern-.6pt\ell}$-cofibrant, then $X\smashp{-}\cong\Sigma^\infty X\smashp{-}$ is homotopical by Proposition~(prop:gl-flatness of the paper), as is ${-}\smashp Y$ for any flat $Y$. With these established, the pushout-product axiom for acyclic cofibrations then follows as in the proof of Proposition~(prop:smash-gl-left-Quillen of the paper).
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma G-global-spectra-tensoring of arXiv:2608.28504

[Lemma l:palm_conc of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a simple point process satisfying the Palm correlation bound (equation e:bd_palmcorr of the paper). Then for a bounded Borel set $B \subset \mathbb{R}^d$,

\begin{align}\nonumber \sup_{x_1,\ldots,x_p \in \mathbb{R}^d} \mathbb{P}_{\bk x1p} \bigl(\mathcal{P}(B) \geq \hat{\kappa}_p|B| + p + t \bigr) \le
& \exp\Bigl(-t\Bigl(\log(1+\frac{t}{\hat{\kappa}_p|B|})-1\Bigr)\Bigr), \ \ \ p \in \mathbb{N}, \ \ \ t > 0.
\end{align}

[Lem prob expression of arXiv:2505.11700, 'Distribution of the cokernels of determinantal row-sparse matrices'] Let $\underline{n}=(n_a)_{a \in G}$ and $q \in S(\underline{n})$. Then
$$
\mathbb{P}(A_nq = 0) = \frac{1}{k_n}n^{-(k_n-1)n} \det(M) \prod_{a \in G_+} (n(k_n-1)_a^{n_a -1}). 
$$
Moreover, the matrix $M$ is positive semi-definite.

[Corollary cor:lower_bounds of arXiv:2607.22908, 'Epidemic Phase Transitions in the Zero-Range Process'] For any relative deviation $\delta \in (0, 1)$ and corresponding absolute deviation $\varepsilon = \rho\delta \in (0, \rho)$:
  \begin{equation}
    \mathbb{P}(\bar{X} \le \rho(1-\delta)) \le \exp\braces*{ -n \frac{\rho \delta^2}{2\Gamma}},
    \qquad 
    \mathbb{P}(\bar{X} \le \rho - \varepsilon) \le \exp\braces*{ -n \frac{\varepsilon^2}{2 \Gamma \rho} }.
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2607.22878, 'Clustering of large deviations in heavy-tailed moving averages: the catastrophe principle '] For every $M> \max(|a_0|, |a_L|)$, 
$0<\eps<\min_{l=0,\ldots, L+1}(a_l-a_{l-1})$ and $0<\delta<\delta_0$, 
\begin{align} 
  &\limsup_{n\to \infty} \, \bigl(n P(h^{(n)} \|Z\| > \lambda_
    n)\bigr)^{-1}\left[ \sum_{|i| 
          \leq Mn}E\bigl( e^{-g(i/n,    G_i^{(n)}Z_i/\lambda_n)}
  \one_{\Psi}(H_i^{(n)} Z_i/\lambda_n)\bigr) \right.\\
 \notag &\left. \hskip 0.05in - n\eps \sum_{l=0}^{L+1} \sum_{a_{l-1}/\eps\leq
                 k<a_l/\eps} \sum_{j=1}^{m_l} e^{-b_{lj}}P\bigl(
                 H_{[kn\eps]}^{(n)}Z_i/\lambda_n \in  \Psi^{\delta},  G_{[kn\eps]}^{(n)} Z_i/\lambda_n \in A_{lj}^\delta \bigr)\right] 
\leq f(\eps)  
  \end{align}
  and
\begin{align} 
  &\liminf_{n\to \infty}  \, \bigl(n P(h^{(n)} \|Z\| > \lambda_
    n)\bigr)^{-1}\left[ \sum_{|i| 
          \leq Mn}E\bigl( e^{-g(i/n,    G_i^{(n)}Z_i/\lambda_n)}
  \one_{\Psi}(H_i^{(n)} Z_i/\lambda_n)\bigr) \right.\\
 \notag &\left. \hskip 0.05in - n\eps \sum_{l=1}^L \sum_{a_{l-1}/\eps\leq
                 k<a_l/\eps} \sum_{j=1}^{m_l} e^{-b_{lj}}P\bigl(
                 H_{[kn\eps]}^{(n)}Z_i/\lambda_n \in \Psi^{-\delta}, G_{[kn\eps]}^{(n)} Z_i /\lambda_n \in A_{lj}^{-\delta} \bigr)\right] 
\geq -f(\eps)  
  \end{align}
  for a nonnegative function $f$ with $f(\eps)\to 0$ as $\eps\to
  0$. Here $a_{-1}=-M, \, a_{L+1}=M, \, m_{-1}=m_{L+1}=1$ and

body:
[Corollary 7 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] Assume $q\equiv c>0$ and $V\in C_b(\R)$. Then
\[
\alpha d\,\cH\!\left(\frac{c}{\alpha d}\right)-\sup_\R V
\le\Lambda_D^\R(\alpha)\le
\alpha d\,\cH\!\left(\frac{c}{\alpha d}\right)-\inf_\R V.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac{\Lambda_D^\R(\alpha)}{|\log\alpha|}\longrightarrow\frac{c}{R_+}
\qquad(\alpha\downarrow0).
\]
Under the edge hypothesis of Theorem~\ref{thm:heteroHamiltonian},
\[
\Lambda_D^\R(\alpha)
=\frac{c}{R_+}\left[\log\frac{c}{\alpha d}
+p\log\log\frac{c}{\alpha d}-p\log R_+-\log(R_+A)-1\right]+O(1).
\]
If, in addition, $V\equiv a_0$, then
\[
\Lambda_D^\R(\alpha)=\alpha d\,\cH\!\left(\frac{c}{\alpha d}\right)-a_0
=\sup_{s\in\R}\{cs-\alpha d(M(s)-1)\}-a_0.
\]
If $s_\alpha>0$ is the optimizer, then $\alpha dM'(s_\alpha)=c$ and
\[
(\Lambda_D^\R)'(\alpha)=-d(M(s_\alpha)-1)<0,\qquad
(\Lambda_D^\R)''(\alpha)=\frac{c^2}{\alpha^3dM''(s_\alpha)}>0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\Lambda_D^\R(\alpha)=-a_0+\frac{c^2}{2\alpha dD_2(J)}
-\frac{D_4(J)c^4}{24\alpha^3d^3D_2(J)^4}+O(\alpha^{-5})
\qquad(\alpha\to+\infty),
\]
and, under the edge hypothesis,
\[
\Lambda_D^\R(\alpha)=\frac{c}{R_+}\left[\log\frac{c}{\alpha d}
+p\log\log\frac{c}{\alpha d}-p\log R_+-\log(R_+A)-1+o(1)\right]-a_0
\]
as $\alpha\downarrow0$. Finally, for
$\cA_{\sigma,m,\R}u=\sigma^{-m}(J_\sigma*u-u)+cu'+a_0u$,
\[
\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,\R})=\sigma^{-m}\cH(c\sigma^{m-1})-a_0.
\]

body: [Definition of arXiv:2412.02777, 'How to quantify the coherence of a set of beliefs'] Two coherent credence bases $(V, \boldsymbol q)$ and $(V', \boldsymbol q')$ are \textit{content equivalent} if $\langle\bar V\rangle=\langle\bar V'\rangle$ and the credence base $((V, V'), (\boldsymbol q, \boldsymbol q'))$ is coherent.

[Theorem thm:Push-TASEP-multipoint of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] The dressed edge weights satisfy the mixed diamond
equation
\begin{align}
& (\partial_t \mathcal{M}_{t,\mathbf{a},
\mathbf{n}+\mathbf{1}})
\mathcal{M}_{t,\mathbf{a},
\mathbf{n}+\mathbf{1}}^{-1}
- (\partial_t \mathcal{M}_{t,\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{1},
\mathbf{n}})
\mathcal{M}_{t,\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{1},
\mathbf{n}}^{-1} \notag \\
& \qquad + \mathcal{M}_{t,\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{1},
\mathbf{n}}
\mathcal{M}_{t,\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{1},
\mathbf{n}+\mathbf{1}}^{-1}
- \mathcal{M}_{t,\mathbf{a},
\mathbf{n}}
\mathcal{M}_{t,\mathbf{a},
\mathbf{n}+\mathbf{1}}^{-1} = 0
\end{align}
at every $(t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n})$ with $t > 0$,
$1 \le n_1 < \cdots < n_m$, and
$a_i < y_{n_i+1} - 1$ for all~$i$.

body:
REFUTED AUXILIARY CLAIM: every density-one periodic force-balanced configuration for the repulsive three-dimensional Riesz potential |r|^{-s}, s>3, has nonnegative second variation under every finitely supported displacement. The sc-compact entry is a counterexample: Z^3 is force balanced and has a finite-support negative second variation. This false universal bridge is distinct from P0309 and from a properly conditional harmonic calculation.
This entry records a false auxiliary statement with its counterexample
It must not be used as a theorem
title: Refuted auxiliary bridge: force balance implies Hessian positivity

body:
[Lem L1L2 of arXiv:2504.19942, 'The edge-averaging process on graphs \\ with random initial opinions'] Fix a vertex $o\in V$. Then, for every $t>0$,
$$\|f_t(o)\|_1\leq \|f_0(o)\|_1\, .$$
If $\mathrm{Var}(f_0(o))<\infty$, then we also have
$$\mathrm{Var}(f_t(o))=\mathbb{E}[Q_t]\mathrm{Var}(f_0(o)).$$
title: Lem L1L2 of arXiv:2504.19942

[Theorem 10 (Classical central-section extremizers; see \cite{MeyerPajor,Koldobsky1998,Eskenazis,ChasapisNayarTkocz}) of arXiv:2605.11451, '2605.11451'] Let $0<p<2$ and $n\ge2$. For every $\theta\in\sphere$,
\begin{equation}
 A_{p,n,0}(\diag)
 \le
 A_{p,n,0}(\theta)
 \le
 A_{p,n,0}(e_1).
\end{equation}
The right equality occurs exactly for coordinate directions $\{\pm e_i\}$, and the left equality occurs exactly for diagonal directions
\[
 \left\{\frac1{\sqrt n}(\pm1,\ldots,\pm1)\right\}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Thm LSS of arXiv:2507.09120, 'Chemical distance in graphs of polynomial growth'] Fix $\hat{D}, K' < \infty$. Then there exists a function $\sigma: [0,1] \to [0,1]$ (depending on $\hat{D}$ and $K'$)
   such that $\lim_{q \to 1} \sigma(q) = 1$
   with the following property. Let $\hat{G}$ be any graph with degree at most $\hat{D}$ and let
   $X$ be a random subset of sites of $\hat{G}$ which has ``dependence range $K'$'' in the sense that
   for any $K'$-separated subset $S \subset \hat{G}$, the collection of events
   \[
      \left \{ \{ s \in X \} : s \in S \right\}
   \]
   is mutually independent.
   Suppose also that for some $q \in [0,1]$, $\mathbb{P}( v \in X ) \ge q$ for all $v \in \hat{V}$.
   Then there exists a coupling of $X$ and $\hat{G}_{\sigma(q)}$ such that
   \[
      \hat{G}_{\sigma(q)} \subset X
   \]
   almost surely,
   where $\hat{G}_{\sigma(q)}$ is independent Bernoulli site percolation on $\hat{G}$ with parameter 
   $\sigma(q)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{LSS} Corollary 1.4

[Prop MDPcppp of arXiv:2412.09471, 'On the moderate deviation principles in the sparse multi-type Erd\H{o}s R\'enyi random gra'] Under the Assumption~(assump1 of the paper), for any sequence $a_n$ such that $1\ll a_n\ll\sqrt{n}$, suppose that $|\mu^n-\mu|=O\left(\frac{1}{n}\right)$ and $\alpha\in{\mathbb R}_+^d$ satisfy $\alpha_r\le\mu_r$ for all $r\in{\mathcal S}$. Let $\{\alpha^n\}\subset{\mathbb R}_+^d$ be a sequence such that $\alpha^n\rightarrow\alpha$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$ and $0<\alpha^n_r\le\mu^n_r$ for all $r\in{\mathcal S}$. Under condition $X_{i,r}^n\leq \alpha^n_r n$ for all $i\geq 1$ and $r\in{\mathcal S}$, 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item [(i)]  the sequence of random vectors 
        $$\frac{1}{a_n\sqrt{n}}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N(Z_n n)}X_i^{n}-c^n n\right)$$
        satisfies the moderate deviation principle in ${\mathbb R}^d$ with speed $a_n^2$ and the rate function  
        $$j_1(x)=\frac{1}{2}\<x, \Phi^{-1} x\>,$$
        where $\Phi^{-1}=D_{c}^{-1}-\kappa$;
        \item [(ii)] the sequence of random vectors 
        $$\frac{1}{a_n\sqrt{n}}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor(|c^n|-\frac12\langlec^n,\kappac^n\rangle)n+a_n\sqrt{n}x\rfloor}X_i^{n}-c^n n-\frac{c^n a_n\sqrt{n}x}{|c^n|-\frac 12\langle c^n, \kappac^n\rangle}\right)$$
        satisfies the moderate deviation principle in ${\mathbb R}^d$ with speed $a_n^2$ and the rate function 
        $$
       j_2(x)= \frac12 \bigg\langle x,\left(\Phi-\frac{cc^T}{|c|-\frac12\langlec,\kappac\rangle}\right)^{-1}x \bigg\rangle;
        $$
        
      \item [(iii)]the sequence of random vectors 
        \[\frac{1}{a_n\sqrt{n}}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N(Z_n n)}X_i^{n}\mathbbm{1}_{\{X^{n}_i\neq k\}}-(c^n-kh(k)) n\right)
        \]
        satisfies the moderate deviation principle with speed $a_n^2$ and rate function  
        \[
        j_3(x)=\frac{1}{2}\<x,(\Phi-kk^Th(k))^{-1}x\>.
        \]
        
        
    \end{enumerate}
title: Prop MDPcppp of arXiv:2412.09471

body:
Let n>=2, K>0, and let x=(x_1,...,x_n) and y=(y_1,...,y_n) be real random vectors whose 2n coordinates are mutually independent, each with a Lebesgue density bounded almost everywhere by K. Let Z be a deterministic real n by n matrix, u,v deterministic real n-vectors, and w a deterministic real scalar. Write sigma_1(Z)>=...>=sigma_n(Z)>=0 for its singular values, and assume r=rank(Z)>=2. Then Q=x^T Z y+x^T u+v^T y+w has a Lebesgue density satisfying ||p_Q||_infinity <= 2(C_RV K)^2 sqrt(2e*pi) min_{2<=j<=r} [j^(-1/2) (product_{i=1}^j sigma_i(Z))^(-1/j)], where C_RV is the universal constant in the Rudelson-Vershynin bounded-density projection theorem. Equivalently one may minimize over 2<=j<=n, interpreting terms with zero singular-value product as infinity. This is the k=1 corollary of Banks, Garza-Vargas, Kulkarni and Srivastava, arXiv:2005.08930. No bounded-density bound is available in general at rank one: if U,V are independent uniform(0,1), UV has density -log(t) on 0<t<1, which is unbounded near zero. Independence only between the two vectors is insufficient even at rank two: x=(U,U), y=(V,V), Z=diag(1,-1) gives Q=0 almost surely. A quadratic-form application must independently verify the coordinate independence and rank hypotheses.
n>=2 and K>0
All 2n coordinates of x and y are mutually independent and each has a Lebesgue density bounded a.e. by K
Z,u,v,w are deterministic real coefficients
rank(Z)>=2

[Proposition prop:c2fail of arXiv:2608.28007, 'Exact Risk Ratios for Weighted Data Selection in Linear Regression'] For $\varepsilon>0$ define directions in $\mathbb{R}^4$
\[
\begin{aligned}
d_0&=-\varepsilon(e_1+e_2), & d_1&=e_1,\ d_2=e_2,\\
d_3&=-\varepsilon(e_3+e_4), & d_4&=e_3,\ d_5=e_4,\\
d_6&=-\varepsilon(e_1+e_3), & d_7&=-\varepsilon(e_2+e_4),
\end{aligned}
\]
with masses $s_0=s_3=s_6=s_7=\frac1{4(1+2\varepsilon)}$ and
$s_1=s_2=s_4=s_5=\frac{\varepsilon}{2(1+2\varepsilon)}$, realized as a
whitened system through Lemma~(lem:realize of the paper). Exactly the four points
$d_0,d_3,d_6,d_7$ are strictly $4$-generated, and the four side points
$d_1,d_2,d_4,d_5$ are not generated by the other rays at all. The exact
Mahalanobis norms are
\[
\lVert v\rVert^2=\frac{2\varepsilon(3\varepsilon+2)}{\varepsilon+1}
\ \text{(generated points)},\qquad
\lVert v\rVert^2=\frac{\varepsilon^2+4\varepsilon+2}{\varepsilon(\varepsilon+1)}
\ \text{(side points)} .
\]
For $0<\varepsilon<\frac{\sqrt{33}-3}{12}\approx0.2287$, all generated
points have $t=1/\lVert v\rVert^2>1$ and all side points have $t<1$: no point is
simultaneously cheap and generated. At $\varepsilon=\frac1{100}$ the values
are exactly $t=\frac{5050}{203}$ and $t=\frac{101}{20401}$.

body: In computability theory, Rice's theorem states that all non-trivial semantic properties of programs are undecidable. A semantic property is one about the program's behavior, unlike a syntactic property. A non-trivial property is one that is neither true for every program, nor false for every program.
title: Rice's theorem

body: In mathematics, the pigeonhole principle states that if n items are put into m containers, with n > m, then at least one container must contain more than one item. For example, of three gloves, at least two must be right-handed or at least two must be left-handed, because there are three objects but only two categories of handedness to put them into. This seemingly obvious statement, a type of counting argument, can be used to demonstrate possibly unexpected results. For example, given that the population of London is more than one unit greater than the maximum number of hairs that can be on a human head, the principle requires that there must be at least two people in London who have the same number of hairs on their heads.
title: Pigeonhole principle

Status: proof (unaudited); owner-work claim T410-w739-C005 version 1; independent review pending. A single polynomial-time instance-uniform oracle sampler for all positive-normalizer {0,1,4}-weighted oracle circuits at TV accuracy 1/10 implies NP^O subset RP^O subset P^O/poly; this sampler-interface route cannot establish T410 Target 2. No Target 2 common oracle is constructed, and no novelty priority is claimed.
Uniform polynomial running-time/randomness bounds in the arbitrary weight-circuit description length, including hardwired instances
metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:cd7babe876c3357d888afeb8ef19c6394e317abef58a458426469b0be2afe042","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/cd/cd7babe876c3357d888afeb8ef19c6394e317abef58a458426469b0be2afe042.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:5d544a0cbc0f2ffed98a3664ea50e70ceeb525f95c42c1200e5418673643b262","bundle_entry_key":"instance_uniform_weighted_sampler_barrier","bundle_id":"population.t410-oracle-sampling-barriers-protected-blocks-003","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"computational complexity; conditional sampling; relative entropy; autoregressive scoring","draft":"w739/bundle_003.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:complexity.cryptography:instance_uniform_weighted_sampler_barrier","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Instance-uniform sampling is incompatible with Target 2 circuit hardness

Claim C005 v1. Status: proof (unaudited). Kind: route-failure. Target: 2.
No novelty priority is claimed. This is an elementary necessary restriction
on an oracle construction, not a separation or an impossibility of C003 A.

## Exact hypothesis

Fix an oracle O. Suppose there is one randomized oracle algorithm U which,
given an explicit description of any deterministic oracle circuit C on m bits,
with output in {0,1,4} and positive total weight, samples a distribution within
total variation 1/10 of the law assigning probability C(z)/sum C to z.
Its time and randomness are bounded by one polynomial in the description
length and m. The quantifier includes circuits containing a fixed input x as
constants. Ordinary polynomial-size circuits may use O gates, in the usual
bit-query model. This is an INSTANCE-UNIFORM sampler interface.

Then NP^O is contained in RP^O, and consequently NP^O is contained in P^O/poly.
It is therefore incompatible with the circuit-hardness requirement of Target 2.

## Verifier reduction

Let A be any NP^O language, with a polynomial-time oracle verifier V(x,w)
and exactly p(|x|) witness bits after padding. Given x, construct in polynomial
time a circuit C_x with m=1+p(|x|) input bits. It assigns weight 1 to 0^m,
weight 4 to 1w when V(x,w) accepts, and zero to all other strings. The circuit
is polynomial-size: unroll the bounded verifier, with oracle gates for its
queries, and hardwire x. Its normalizer is 1+4 Z_x, where Z_x counts witnesses.
No normalizer computation is used by the reduction.

Run U on C_x. Accept only if the sampled word is 1w and V(x,w) actually
accepts. On a no input this never accepts. On a yes input the target event has
mass 4Z_x/(1+4Z_x)>=4/5. Total variation at most 1/10 leaves acceptance
probability at least 7/10. This proves A is in RP^O. The running time is
polynomial in |x| because U has one polynomial bound uniform over descriptions.

## Relativized randomized-to-advice step

For each input length n, repeat the preceding test independently k=n+2 times
and accept if any run accepts. A yes input is rejected with probability at
most (3/10)^k; a no input is never accepted. The union bound over all 2^n
inputs of length n gives probability of any mistake at most

    2^n (3/10)^(n+2) = (9/100)(3/5)^n < 1.

Thus there is one fixed polynomial-length collection of k random tapes that
works simultaneously for EVERY length-n input. Hardwire those tapes as advice
and unroll the oracle computation into a polynomial-size oracle circuit.
Only the independent repetitions on a single input were multiplied; inputs
need no independence. This proves A is in P^O/poly. The tape collection may
depend on n and O, exactly as the circuit model permits.

## Why this does not contradict C003

C003 A has quantifier form: for every fixed uniform weighted family W, there
exists a uniform polynomial-time sampler S_W. It supplies neither a computable
compiler W to S_W nor a polynomial bound uniform over weight descriptions.
In the reduction above x varies with the INSTANCE, not just with the length.
Replacing the family-specific samplers by a single sampler accepting C_x would
be an extra assumption, which is precisely what the theorem rules out.

C004 encoded a unary input into a polynomially related output length and so
did not require this additional uniformity. Encoding every binary x into its
own length requires exponentially many lengths; it does not yield a polynomial
time reduction and cannot silently convert C003 A into this stronger property.

Therefore an oracle construction for C003 must achieve family-specific
sampling without a polynomial-time instance-uniform weight-circuit interface.
It must also preserve hardness after all sampling/inversion interfaces are
available. Neither this proof nor C004 proves such a construction exists.
The joint oracle consistency problem for binary NP circuit hardness is OPEN.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:a709e45865929b025dd7f8ab22e9a633f013cb492fed61e532bf39a91f8c0201","revision_digest":"sha256:d9fe42072d4cba052697690bd26cd19d3d236739c096685e652aa411c85317b6","source_id":"own-work:T410-w739-C005-v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20T21:39:37.775816+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}
title: Instance-uniform weighted sampling forces NP into RP and P/poly (unaudited)

body:
[Theorem thm:CD_schur_averaging of arXiv:2603.14906, 'Four Levels of Thermodynamic Convergence of Singularly Perturbed Markov Semigroups'] Suppose that (ass:fundamental of the paper) holds and $A^\varepsilon$ is constant.
Denote the Jacobian of the unscaled drift by
\[
\mathcal Jb(z)=
\begin{pmatrix}
\nabla_x b_1(z) & \nabla_y b_1(z)\\
\nabla_x b_2(z) & \nabla_y b_2(z)
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Define
\[
\mathsf S(z)
:=\mathrm{diag}(a_1,a_2)^{1/2}\,\mathrm{Sym}\!\bigl(-\mathcal Jb(z)\bigr)\,\mathrm{diag}(a_1,a_2)^{1/2}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\mathsf S_{11}(z) & \mathsf S_{12}(z)\\
\mathsf S_{21}(z) & \mathsf S_{22}(z)
\end{pmatrix},
\]
and assume that there exist $\varepsilon_0>0$ and $\kappa\ge0$ such that for all $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$ and all $z\in E$,
\[
\mathsf S_{11}(z)\succ 0,
\qquad
\lambda_{\min}\!\Bigl(\mathrm{Schur}(\mathsf S_{11})(z)\Bigr)\ge -\kappa,
\]
where $\mathrm{Schur}(\mathsf S_{11})(z):=\mathsf S_{22}(z)-\mathsf S_{21}(z)\mathsf S_{11}(z)^{-1}\mathsf S_{12}(z)$.
Then (ass:CDkappa of the paper) holds uniformly in $\varepsilon$, i.e.\ $(P_t^\varepsilon)_{t\ge0}$ satisfies $CD(-\kappa,\infty)$ for all $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$.
title: Schur-type criterion for uniform $CD(-\kappa,\infty)$ in the averaging model

&\quad + \int_0^t \int_{\mathbb{R}_0} \left[ \frac{\partial \theta}{\partial x}(t,s,e)\dot{X}(s) + \frac{\partial \theta}{\partial x_1}(t,s,e)\dot{X}_1(s) + \frac{\partial \theta}{\partial u}(t,s,e)\beta(s) \right] \tilde{N}(ds,de),
\end{align*}
where $\dot{X}_1(t) = \dot{X}(t-\delta)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Theorem thm:McCann of arXiv:2605.10491, 'Zero-couplings of infinite measures with cyclically monotone support and multivariate regu'] Let $P,Q \in \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$. There exists a coupling measure $\pi \in \Pi(P,Q)$ with cyclically monotone support contained in the graph of the subdifferential of a closed convex function $\psi$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$. If $P$ vanishes on all sets of Hausdorff dimension at most $d -1$, then $\psi$ is differentiable $P$-almost everywhere, $(\nabla\psi)_{\#}P=Q$, and the map $\nabla\psi$ is uniquely determined $P$-almost everywhere. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Brenier's Theorem, Main Theorem in \citet{McCann1995}

\(C^2\) Jordan curve if \(\gamma\) is a \(C^2\) embedding and satisfies
 \[
     \inf_{t\in\mathbb T}|\gamma'(t)|>0,
     \qquad
    \inf_{t\in\mathbb T}
     |\det(\gamma'(t),\gamma''(t))|>0.
 \]
When derivatives are written, \(\gamma\) is represented by the associated
\(1\)-periodic \(C^2\) map
\(\bar\gamma=\gamma\circ\pi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^2\), where
\(\pi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb T\) is the quotient map; the notation
\(\gamma'(t)\), \(\gamma''(t)\) refers to the derivatives of
\(\bar\gamma\) at any representative of \(t\in\mathbb T\).

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2505.21774, 'The friendship paradox for trees'] {\bf [Densities of vertex types for infinite trees]}

\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] 
Let $\mathcal{T}_\infty$ be the infinite Galton-Watson tree with offspring distribution $p$ satisfying \eqref{eq:pcond}. Then, for each $\chi \in S$, there exists $f^\chi$  such that 
\[
\lim_{m\to\infty} \frac{N_m^\chi}{N_m} = f^\chi \quad \PP\text{-}\mathrm{a.s.}
\] 
\item[(b)] 
For $k \in \N$, let $S_k= \sum_{l=1}^k X_l$, where $(X_l)_{l=1}^k$ are drawn independently from $p$, and let $\tilde{X}$ be drawn independently from $\tilde{p}$. Then
\[
f^\chi = \sum_{k \in \N_0} p_k\,\PP\Big({\rm sign}\big[\tX+S_k-k(k+1)\big] = \chi\Big).
\]
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own-work draft, C006 version 2, proof (unaudited); priority not established. Fix L>=3, d>=1, H=L-1, equal hidden widths m, a C2 activation with |sigma|, |sigma prime|, |sigma double prime|<=1, and data ||x||<=1, |y|<=1. Let h1_i=sigma(w_i dot x), hl_j=sigma(m^(-1)sum_i B^l_ji h(l-1)_i) for 2<=l<=H, and f=m^(-1)sum_j a_j hH_j, with half-squared population loss. Initialize two independent runs with w_i iid in [-1,1]^d, a_i iid in [-1,1] and entries of every B^l iid in [-1,1]; arrays are mutually independent and each array law is common across runs. Train all parameters by simultaneous fresh-sample SGD or finite minibatch averages, using multipliers m for a,w and m^2 for every middle matrix, with deterministic nonnegative steps summing to T<infinity. Set S2=sum eta_k^2, A=2exp(T), define M_l=1+2A^2 T product_{s=l+1}^H M_s backwards for l=H,...,2, W=sqrt(d)+2A^2 T product_{s=2}^H M_s, R=max(1,A,W,M_2,...,M_H), and r=6sqrt(d)m^(-1/(d+2))+6m^(-1/3)+6(L-2)m^(-1/2). A compatible tuple of hidden-layer permutations, selected only from the initial boundary arrays, has expected population loss-chord barrier <=8R^L exp(64L^2 R^(2L)T)[r+4L R^L sqrt(S2)]. Thus eta_max<=m^(-2/(d+2)) yields O_{L,d,T}(m^(-1/(d+2))) for every fixed depth. The boundary matchings and identity internal permutations suffice: each middle cut error adds linearly at initialization, and deterministic transpose cut estimates handle trained dependence. No bound uniform in growing depth, ReLU theorem, fixed-step independent-data limit, low-risk endpoint guarantee or independent audit is established.
All stated bounded smooth fixed-depth, fixed-horizon and independent iid initialization hypotheses
Fresh iid SGD data; deterministic steps; small-step condition required for width vanishing

body: [Theorem complete feedback optimal strategy of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] Suppose a deck of $n$ cards is given a shelf shuffle with a single shelf, and the player is given complete feedback. Once one of card $n-1$ or $n$ is first shown, the player should guess the remaining cards in descending order, and is guaranteed to get these correct. body:
[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2609.02267, 'Locally Conformally Flat Manifolds with Positive Scalar Curvature: Kleinian Groups, Moduli'] Let \( (M^n, g) \) be a closed, connected, oriented, smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension \( n \geq 3 \), which is locally conformally flat with positive scalar curvature. Assume further that \( H_1(M^n; \mathbb{Z}) = 0 \) and that the fundamental group \( \pi_1(M) \) is finite.

\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] If \(n\) is even or \(n\equiv1\pmod4\), then \((M^n,g)\) is conformally equivalent to the standard sphere \((S^n,g_{st})\).

\item[(ii)] If \(n\equiv3\pmod4\), then \(\pi_1(M)\) is trivial or isomorphic to the binary icosahedral group \(I_{120}^*\cong\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb F_5)\); accordingly, \((M^n,g)\) is conformally equivalent to \((S^n,g_{st})\) or to a spherical space form \(S^n/\Gamma\) with \(\Gamma\cong I_{120}^*\). The congruence restriction is optimal: for every \(n\equiv3\pmod4\), both alternatives occur.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 7 of arXiv:2609.02267

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2609.00483, 'On Embedding Hamming Spheres with Applications to Positive Curvature'] Let $p$ be a prime and $k\ge2$, and set $m=(p^k-1)/(p-1)$. Let $\mathcal C_V$ be a projective code associated to $\mathrm{PG}(k-1,p)$. Then every $x\in\mathcal C_V$ has weight $w=p^{k-1}$, any two distinct $x,y\in\mathcal C_V$ satisfy $d(x,y)=b=p^{k-1}$, and
$$
|\mathcal C_V|=\gamma(p,b,w,m)=p^k-1.
$$
In particular,
$$
\gamma(p,b,w,m)<(p-1)m+1.
$$

body: Let (X, Sigma_X, mu) and (Y, Sigma_Y, nu) be sigma-finite measure spaces and let f be measurable on the product sigma-algebra of X times Y, with values in R or C. If the double integral of |f| over X times Y with respect to mu times nu is finite (f is integrable), then for a.e. x the slice y -> f(x,y) is integrable, for a.e. y the slice x -> f(x,y) is integrable, and integral_X integral_Y f dnu dmu = integral_Y integral_X f dmu dnu = integral over X times Y of f d(mu times nu). Tonelli's theorem gives the same conclusion for f merely nonnegative and measurable, integrals allowed to be +infinity.

[Lemstar lem:eigenfunctions of arXiv:2605.06488, 'Continuous-state branching processes with L\'evy-Khintchine drift-interaction: Laplace dua'] Let $\Psi$ be a  branching mechanism. Recall $\rho\in [0,\infty]$ its largest zero.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Assume $\Psi$ supercritical: $\Psi'(0+)\in [-\infty,0)$ and $\rho\in (0,\infty]$.  Let $u_0\in (0, \rho)$ be fixed. Define for all $\theta\in \big(0,-\Psi'(0+)\big)$,
\begin{equation}f(x):=\int_0^{\rho} (1-e^{-xu})\frac{\theta}{-\Psi(u)}e^{-\int_{u_0}^{u}\frac{\theta}{\Psi(v)}\mathrm{d} v}\mathrm{d} u,\quad x\in (0,\infty).
\end{equation}
This is a well-defined increasing function, in $\mathrm{C}^2((0,\infty))$, which satisfies $x\mathrm{L}^{\Psi}f(x)=\theta f(x)$ for all $x\in (0,\infty)$.
Moreover, 
\[f(x)\underset{x\rightarrow \infty}{\longrightarrow}\infty \Longleftrightarrow \int_0^{x_0}\frac{\mathrm{d} u}{-\Psi(u)}=\infty \text{ for some } x_0\in (0,\rho).\]
\item Assume $\Psi$ non-immortal (not necessarily supercritical): $\rho\in [0,\infty)$. Let $u_0\in (\rho,\infty)$ be fixed. Define for all $\theta\in (0,\infty)$, \[f(x):=\int_{\rho}^{\infty}e^{-xu}\frac{1}{\Psi(u)}e^{\int_{u_0}^u\frac{\theta}{\Psi(v)}\mathrm{d} v}\mathrm{d} u,\ x\in (0,\infty).\]
This is a well-defined decreasing function, in $\mathrm{C}^2((0,\infty))$, which satisfies $x\mathrm{L}^{\Psi}f(x)=\theta f(x)$ for all $x\in (0,\infty)$. Moreover, \[f(x)\underset{x\rightarrow 0}{\longrightarrow}\infty \Longleftrightarrow
\int_{x_0}^{\infty}\frac{\mathrm{d} u}{\Psi(u)}=\infty \text{ for some } x_0\in (\rho,\infty).\]
\end{enumerate}

body:
Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); independent mathematics/priority/scope audits pending. Let d>=1,N>=2d+1,K>=2,1<=r<K,F=K-r,gcd(r,F)=1. The source has d unknown A/S context pairs, one arbitrary r-support A and one all-K S each, and N-2d known S contexts; it selects contexts uniformly then truths uniformly. Independently receive uniform ell-subsets of truths in BOTH variable contexts,ANY0<=ell<=r, and n actual iid untagged facts. Every realized generator must be source Mis_infinity<=c at exact score bins in ALL data-compatible worlds,0<=c<1/(2NrK),rational c. For each FIXED alphabet bound K0, C026 true-posterior native branch frontier and an attaining randomized robust policy are polynomial-time computable in growing d,n,N and rational budget bit size, for every verifier fraction in the coprime small-budget paired actual-iid model. Low whole contexts separate; whole choices are posterior prefixes per h; sorted-coefficient marked multiset DP solves allocation. No uniform polynomial-in-K, efficient global expectation or classical ERM/PAC claim. The C026 conditional Bayes minimum beta is min_branches,partitions(sum f*p/m-c*max f/m), where unresolved h=min union chooses paired residual (2(K-h),F,(2-h/r-h/K)/N), or F units(2,1,1/(NK)) at h=r, OR BOTH posterior-weighted whole contexts(K,F*pi,1/N),(K,F*(1-pi),1/N). Resolved A union j<r contributes(K-j,F,(r-j)/(Nr)),otherwise none. pi is the true original-data posterior defined by L(u,j)=(K/r)^u*binom(K-j,r-j)/binom(K-ell,r-ell). All lower-posterior whole contexts can be isolated. For any number of whole choices among pairs with the same h, keep the largest max(pi,1-pi) values. Enumerate those per-h prefix lengths. Remaining native types are at most2K-1. Sort selected high false counts, and candidate cell signatures by coefficient [lambda*m(s)-p(s)+e*c]/[m(s)+K*q],lambda=1/(NK),where q high whole objects and donor mark e are included. An ordered unbounded resource DP allocates contiguous high-count blocks with exactly one mark. Rearrangement and exchange arguments prove equality. This gives a polynomial-time estimator for every fixed K0 with growing VC d; polynomial degree depends on K0. Learning-policy symmetrization attains C026 global minimax E beta, without averaging generator laws. The global oracle penalty formula is unchanged. Dependence on the earlier unaudited characterization is explicit.
All C026 v2 coprime paired actual-iid hypotheses, every0<=ell<=r
0<=c<1/(2NrK), rational input budget; each fixed alphabet bound K0
