{"artifact_digest":"sha256:5208e10004d7396a52346d2bb633bafbd297218510eef09131d67126a1334a78","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/52/5208e10004d7396a52346d2bb633bafbd297218510eef09131d67126a1334a78.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:b791b63988aaae0045775ffa65f3b4205213a6c1d0a6735105d0e4292eec4c2c","bundle_entry_key":"posterior-prefix-sorted-dp","bundle_id":"population.t379-posterior-prefix-fixed-alphabet-efficient-20261020","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"calibrated generation; efficient estimation; posterior prefixes; multiset dynamic programming","draft":"w709/bundle_019.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.calibration:kalai-vempala-posterior-prefix-fixed-alphabet-efficient-minimax","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Growing-VC efficiency at fixed alphabet via posterior prefixes

T379-C027 v2, proof (unaudited); exact checks PASS. Target1, secondary target2.
Depends on C026 v2 and all its hypotheses. No new global law is assumed.

Aim: polynomial-time evaluation/attainment of beta_c(D) for every fixed
K0 and K<=K0, allowing d,n,N to grow. This is NOT uniformly polynomial
in K and NOT a polynomial-time exact evaluation of its global expectation.

Write lambda=1/(NK). For each native object put deficit A=lambda*m-p>=0.
Every partition objective is lambda*total_false_count minus

 sum_cells f_S*A_S/m_S + c*max_cells f_S/m_S.             (1)

Each whole branch has posterior probabilities pi,1-pi. Call the larger
one t>=1/2. Its lower whole-context object has risk F*(1-t)/K<=F/(2K),
whereas every other high whole object and EVERY native paired/unit/A
object has risk>=F/(2K). All whole objects have zero deficit. Removing
all low whole objects from risk-bearing pools and keeping them separate
weakly increases f_S/m_S on remaining pools, so increases (1); splitting
them does not reduce maximum risk because all remaining risks dominate.
Hence the low objects need not participate in pooling or be budget donors.

Now group unresolved pairs by h. For a fixed number k_h of whole
branches in group h, one may select the k_h largest t values:
exchanging a selected smaller t for an unselected larger t leaves the
remaining paired-native multiset unchanged. It increases the high whole
false count in its pool, decreases only the isolated low false count and
preserves total false count F. Every benefit coefficient A_S/m_S and
the marked-donor coefficient c/m_S is nonnegative. The old maximum risk
cannot decrease. Thus the exchange cannot worsen the objective.

Enumerate all k_h in0..D_h; at most product_h(D_h+1), polynomial in d
for fixed K. For each selection there are:
* T<=2r+1<=2K-1 fixed native types with counts v_t<=dF;
* H<=d high whole objects, all size K, deficit0, variable false counts;
* isolated low objects, already included in the constant
  lambda*F*(#unresolved+#resolved-unsaturated-A).

Sort the H high false counts f_1>=...>=f_H and their prefix sums.
A potential pooled cell consists of a native submultiset s<=v and q
high whole objects, not both empty, plus mark e in{0,1}. The single
marked cell receives the c discount. Its BENEFIT is

       [f(s)+sum_assigned f_i] * b(s,q,e),
 b(s,q,e)=[A(s)+e*c]/[m(s)+K*q].                         (2)

For a fixed collection of cell signatures, rearrangement assigns the
largest high false counts to the largest b values, each with capacity q.
Hence after ordering cells by decreasing b, each cell receives a
contiguous block of the sorted high list. Equal b cell types can be put
in any fixed order: the variable-count contribution is unchanged.

Enumerate all signatures (s,q,e), sort by decreasing b, then run an
unbounded knapsack DP in that order. State: used native count vector,
number of high whole objects consumed and whether the donor is marked.
Choosing a cell consumes s,q and adds (2), using the next q false counts.
At a given signature, repeated choices are allowed; every choice consumes
at least one resource, so increasing total-resource order is acyclic.
A marked signature can only be used while the flag is0 and sets it1.
Skipping to the next signature is allowed. End with all resources used
and one mark. All finite partitions have a sorted representation by
rearrangement, and every DP path is a valid partition, proving equality.

There are at most2*(H+1)*product_t(v_t+1) signatures and at most
2*(H+1)*product_t(v_t+1) states per signature. Including prefix selections
gives a polynomial in d for each FIXED K0, of degree depending on K0.
Posterior rationals have bit length polynomial in explicit sample size;
sorting, benefits and DP sums use exact rational arithmetic. Backpointers
recover the actual partition; C026 supplies the robust generator and
finite-group policy symmetrization (efficient random permutations).

## Proof details, exact evidence and limits

Low-context removal can be performed in increasing risk order: the
smallest low object in a cell has risk no larger than the mean of the
remaining components. Removing it increases the remaining mean risk
and leaves deficit A fixed. The isolated low object has deficit0.
Repeating yields all lows isolated. If a remaining pool is nonempty,
its components all have risk>=F/(2K), so the maximum risk is attained
among nonlow cells. A whole branch always supplies a high counterpart.
Thus low cells need not be marked even at positive c.

For the prefix exchange keep the old high object's pool assignment:
increasing its expected false count increases both its nonnegative
deficit benefit and its risk. Only an isolated low count decreases.
The multiset of unselected native components is identical for equal h,
including the F-unit saturated branch. Therefore neither budget nor
baseline invalidates the exchange.

For rearrangement, expand each cell coefficient b into q identical
slots. Swapping inverted high counts x>=y between coefficients b>=a
changes benefit by(x-y)*(b-a)>=0. This elementary identity proves the
needed assignment step without trusting an external formula. It also
applies to the single marked coefficient. Exactly one cell is marked;
optimizing its identity is equivalent to c*maximum risk. Native-only
cells have q0 and do not constrain the high order. Whole-only cells
have s0,q>0 and remain allowed.

For repeated knapsack choices, each step strictly increases
sum_t used_v_t+used_high. Processing resource states in that order
permits all repetitions of the current signature. Moving to the next
signature prevents decreasing coefficient order. Equal-coefficient
types may be canonically grouped because their total high contribution
does not depend on which of their equal-b slots receive particular
counts. This proves both directions of the DP correspondence.

The fixed-K type bound and polynomial cardinalities above concern
explicit data and rational c. Posterior numerators/denominators have
O(n log K+K) bits before common reductions. Rational DP path sums have
at most O(Kd) summands of polynomial bit size; exact comparisons and
sorting therefore preserve polynomial bit complexity. Uniform draws
of context swaps and atom permutations implement C026 policy
symmetrization in polynomial time. Backpointers reconstruct native
components, high-count slots and the marked cell; low whole objects
are isolated. C026 supplies the actual robust generator.

scripts/posterior_prefix_dp.py is a guarded exact prototype:
before resource allocation it bounds signature-times-state work by
two million per prefix choice. Reconstruction of the resource path
checks counts, contiguous high slots, single donor mark and benefit.
These box limits are not an asymptotic algorithm restriction.

logs/posterior_prefix_dp_check.json compares the sorted algorithm to
C026's UNRESTRICTED branch and multiset partition solver in1933 games,
including1340 below-half,529 saturated and1679 mixed-h cases.
It checks5510 prefix choices and200384 bounded state/signature products.
Cases include the C025 unit-splitting and internal budget-crossing
witness, plus three different true repetition posteriors at the same h.
This is a cross-check of different optimizations; it is not an
independent mathematical audit of their common C026 model reduction.

logs/posterior_prefix_controls_check.json uses genuine K3,r2,N7 data:
t_high=27/35,t_low=9/13. Keeping the lower posterior instead of the
higher at a fixed one-whole count loses1/13720; reversing high-count
assignment between two real native cell coefficients loses6/22295.
These strict controls show that the pruning and sorting are material.

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2511.09280, 'Random Walk conditioned to stay above a non-flat floor: curvature effects'] Let \(p\geq 1,\beta>0\). Let \(S\) be the random walk with i.i.d.\ steps of law \(\calN(0,\beta)\). There are \(c>0, n_0\geq 1,\lambda_0\geq 0\) such that, for any \(\lambda\geq \lambda_0\) and \(n\geq n_0\),
    \begin{equation*}
        P\bigl(S_0 \geq n + \lambda n^{\alpha_p} \given S_{-n}=S_n =0,\, S\geq h_n\bigr) \leq
        e^{-c \lambda^{(2p-1)/p}}.
    \end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 16 of arXiv:2511.09280

[Prop prop_smooth_fit_2d of arXiv:2606.23648, '\textsc{Optimal Stopping for a Diffusion with Unobserved Bernoulli Drift}'] Let \(x\in\mathcal I\). Then \(U(x,\cdot)\) satisfies smooth fit at the
    upper boundary:
    \[
        \lim_{y\uparrow b(x)} D_y U(x,y)
        =
        \lim_{y\downarrow b(x)} D_y U(x,y)
        =
        k'(x+b(x)).
    \]
    If \(a(x)>-x\), then \(U(x,\cdot)\) also satisfies smooth fit at the lower
    boundary:
    \[
        \lim_{y\uparrow a(x)} D_y U(x,y)
        =
        \lim_{y\downarrow a(x)} D_y U(x,y)
        =
        k'(x+a(x)).
    \]

    Suppose, in addition, that the boundaries are \(C^1\) on an open interval \(J\subset\mathcal I\). Then \(U\) satisfies horizontal smooth fit as well. More precisely, if \(a(x)>-x\) on \(J\), then
    \begin{equation}
        Q'(x)G(a(x))+R'(x)=k'(x+a(x)),
        \qquad
        Q'(x)G(b(x))+R'(x)=k'(x+b(x)).
    \end{equation}
    If \(a(x)=-x\) on \(J\), then we have the upper-boundary identity
    \[
        Q'(x)G(b(x))+R'(x)=k'(x+b(x)), \qquad x \in J.
    \]

[Lemma lem:1 of arXiv:2607.22291, 'Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declum'] For $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ set
$$  h_{n}(k)= \mathbb{E}\!\left[ f_{n}\big( 1 +\sum_{j=1}^{n-2M_{n}+1} I^{(M_{n})}_j\big) \;\Big|\; S_{n-M_{n}} = -1-k\right], \quad \Delta_{n}(k) = h_{n}(k) - h_{n}(0).$$
Let $f_{n}$ be a function with $||f_{n}||_{\infty} \leq 1$. Assume that $(n \pi_{n})$ is bounded. Then
$$n\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[(I_1^{(M_n)} - q_{n})\,\Delta_{n}(S_{M_n}) \mid S_n = -1\right]  \quad \mathop{\longrightarrow}_{n \rightarrow \infty} \quad0.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:1 of arXiv:2607.22291

[Proposition 3 of arXiv:2609.03248, 'Connections between colored restricted $b$-ary and ordinary partitions'] Given positive integers $k$ and $n$, the following are identical:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] The number of partitions of $n$ with parts not exceeding $k$.
\item[(b)] The number of $k$-color binary partitions in which a part with
color $i$ has multiplicity $i$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 15 of arXiv:2506.11918, 'Central limit theorems for the Euler characteristic in the Random Connection Model for hig'] Let $K$ be a connected simplicial complex on $r\in\N$ vertices and assume that (\ref{Integrabilitaet:esssup}) holds.
Then, for any sequence $(W_n)_{n\in\N}$ in $\K^d$ with $r(W_n)\rightarrow\infty$, we have
\begin{align*}
&\frac{1}{|W_n|} \int_{W_n^r} \int_{\AA^r} f_K\big((x_1,a_1),\dots,(x_r,a_r)\big) \; \Theta^r (\d {(a_1,\dots,a_r)}) \; \d {(x_1,\dots,x_r)} \\
&\qquad \xrightarrow{\;\;}\; \int_{(\R^d)^{r-1}} \int_{\AA^r} f_K\big((\0,a_1),\dots,(x_r,a_r)\big) \; \Theta^r (\d {(a_1,\dots,a_r)}) \; \d {(x_2,\dots,x_r)} \,<\, \infty
\end{align*}
for $n\rightarrow\infty$.

 is uniformly absolutely continuous, that is, for every $\eps>0$, there exists $\delta> 0$ such that for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and for all pairwise disjoint segments $\{[x_i,y_i]\}_{1 \leq i \leq N }$: if

[Prop PropCarlo-Levy of arXiv:2506.08202, 'Stochastic dissipative systems in Banach spaces driven by L\'evy noise'] Let $d\in{\mathbb N}$, $H=L^2([0,1]^d)$ and $A$ be the realization of the Laplacian operator with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Assume that $\nu(H\backslash H_{1/4+\delta})=0$ and
\begin{equation}
\int_H {\left|z\right|}_\delta^2+{\left|z\right|}^4_{1/4+\delta}\nu(dz)<+\infty.
\end{equation}
The following two assertions hold true.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\{L_A(t)\}_{t\geq 0}$ is a càdlàg process in $H_\gamma$ with $\gamma<1/4+\delta$.
\item Let $\delta>\frac{d-1}{4}$. Then $\{L_A(t)\}_{t\geq 0}$ is a càdlàg process in $C([0,1]^d)$ and
\[
{\mathbb E}\left[\sup_{t\in [0,T]}{\left\|L_A(t)\right\|}^q_{C([0,1]^d)}\right]<+\infty,\qquad T>0,\, q\in [1,4).
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

TECHNIQUE CARD. Exponential approximation by Stein's method: couple a non-negative variable with a variable having its equilibrium law; when the two are close, the variable is close to the exponential law. Ross, Definition 5.2: for W ≥ 0 with E[W] = μ, W^e has the equilibrium distribution with respect to W if E[f(W)] − f(0) = μE[f'(W^e)] for all Lipschitz f. Theorem 5.4: if W ≥ 0 with E[W] = 1 and E[W²] < ∞, and W^e has the equilibrium distribution with respect to W and is coupled to W, then for Z ~ Exp(1), d_W(W, Z) ≤ 2E|W^e − W|. Proposition 5.5 builds W^e from the size-bias law: if W ≥ 0 with E[W] = μ, W^s has the size-bias distribution of W, and U is uniform on (0,1) and independent of W^s, then UW^s has the equilibrium distribution of W.
W ≥ 0 with E[W] = 1 and E[W²] < ∞ (Theorem 5.4)

[Theorem thm:main-Airy-Laplace of arXiv:2609.03532, 'Airy limit for the Jack process and topological expansion'] For every $\beta\ge 1$, $m\geq1$, and $k_1,\ldots,k_m>0$, set
$b=2/\beta-1$. We have
\begin{equation}
  \mathbb E\left[
    \prod_{p=1}^m
    \mathcal Z_\beta\left(\frac{k_p}{\mu_+\mathfrak c_2}\right)
  \right]
  =C_2^m\mathbf L_b[\boldsymbol k].
  
\end{equation}
Equivalently, for $s_1,\ldots,s_m>0$,
\begin{equation*}
  \mathbb E\left[\prod_{p=1}^m\mathcal Z_\beta(s_p)\right]
  =C_2^m\mathbf L_b[\mu_+\mathfrak c_2\boldsymbol s].
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 249 (Half-spectral curve) of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Given $\boldsymbol{v} \in \amsmathbb{R}^H$ non-zero with bipartite $\mathfrak{G}$-orbit, we define $\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}}^{\textnormal{half}}$ to be the image in the quotient $\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ (\textit{cf.} Definition~\ref{def:spcurv1}) of
\[
\bigcup_{\boldsymbol{w} \in \mathfrak{G}.\boldsymbol{v}} \widehat{\amsmathbb{H}}^{\epsilon(\boldsymbol{w})}.
\]
where $\epsilon$ is the unique bipartition of $\mathfrak{G}.\boldsymbol{v}$ such that $\epsilon(\boldsymbol{v}) = 1$. This is a bordered Riemann surface, whose boundary is the closure of the set of real points, that is the image in $\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ of
\[
\bigcup_{\boldsymbol{w} \in \mathfrak{G}.\boldsymbol{v}} \big(\widehat{\amsmathbb{R}}^{\epsilon(\boldsymbol{w})} \setminus \amsmathbb{B}_{\boldsymbol{w}}^{\epsilon(\boldsymbol{w})}\big).
\]
See Figure~\ref{Fig:Half5} and \ref{Fig:Half7} for an example.
title: Half-spectral curve

[Corollary 69 of arXiv:2606.11758, '2606.11758'] Let \(W\) be in the minimal Kahane--Peyri\`ere regime, and set
\(\chi=1-\mathbb E[W\log_2 W]\). In each of the following two settings---the fixed-arc setting of
Theorem~\ref{T:arc-main-endpoint} and the fixed-Jordan setting of
Theorem~\ref{T:jordan-main-endpoint}---the corresponding pushforward cascade
measure is Salem almost surely on the relevant non-extinction event if and
only if there exists \(a\in[1,2)\) such that
\[
    \mathbb P(W=a)=a^{-1},
    \qquad
    \mathbb P(W=0)=1-a^{-1}.
\]
Here Salem means that the Fourier dimension of the measure equals its
Hausdorff dimension.

Let M>=1 finite linear-regression tasks have matrices X_m in R^(n_m by d) and labels y_m. Suppose X_m*w_star=y_m for every m, put R=max_m||X_m||_2>0, and define L(w;m)=||X_m*w-y_m||^2/2 and L(w)=M^(-1)*sum_m L(w;m). Initialize w_0=0 and sample tau_1,...,tau_k independently and uniformly from{1,...,M}, with replacement. Scheme1 performs the exact update w_t=argmin_w {L(w;tau_t)+(lambda_t/2)*||w-w_(t-1)||^2}. Write D2=||w_0-w_star||^2. For a known integer horizon k>=3, choose lambda_t=lambda=R^2*(ln(k)-1)>0 and keep it fixed for all k rounds. Then E L(w_k)<=5*D2*R^2*ln(k)/k. Thus the coefficient is constant within a run and changes with the chosen horizon.
Finite jointly realizable linear tasks; R is the largest task-matrix operator norm and R>0.
Independent uniform task indices sampled with replacement; exact Scheme1 updates; w_0=0.
Known horizon k>=3; lambda=R^2*(ln(k)-1) used throughout the run.

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Estimate the number of near-maximal configurations and compare with the connectivity threshold of the level set on the hypercube. Result: In the NK model with K = O(1) the fitness is a sum of n local terms each depending on K + 1 bits, so the field is a sum of n independent contributions (for the standard model with random neighbourhoods) and the level set at height M_n - delta_n with delta_n = o(n) but delta_n >> sqrt n contains exp(c delta_n^2/n)... the number of configurations within delta of the maximum is, by a large-deviation count, about exp(n I(delta/n)) for a rate I; bridges exist if this level set percolates on the hypercube, and a level set of density rho on the n-cube contains a giant connected component when the local structure allows, roughly when each configuration in the set has on average more than one neighbour in the set: the expected number of neighbours in the level set of a typical level-set point is n times the conditional probability that flipping one bit stays within delta of the maximum, which is n times (probability that the change of the K+1 affected local terms is at most delta), of order n delta/n = delta when delta is small compared to the local term scale... so bridges exist (heuristically) when delta_n >> 1, i.e. the level set within a constant deficit of the maximum is connected in the giant-component sense for deficits growing to infinity, while for bounded deficits the peaks are isolated. This suggests the answer depends on the deficit scale: bridges at deficit delta_n -> infinity, islands at bounded deficit. The argument is a branching heuristic (neighbour counts) without control of dependencies; making it rigorous would need a second-moment argument on the number of level-set paths, which I did not carry out. Key identity: Expected number of level-set neighbours of a level-set point is of order delta (the deficit); bridges expected iff the deficit tends to infinity. Obstruction: Second moment for level-set paths on the hypercube not done.

[Lemma 27 (Critical product lower divisor law) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Fix \(r\geq1\).  Suppose that, for every integer \(L\), compact
operators \(A_{j,L}\), \(1\leq j\leq r\), satisfy
\[
 s_k(A_{j,L})\geq\frac{c}{k},
 \qquad 1\leq k\leq L.
\]
For \(T_L=A_{1,L}\otimes\cdots\otimes A_{r,L}\), there are constants
\(b_r,B_r>0\), independent of \(L\), such that
\begin{equation}
 s_N(T_L)\geq b_r\frac{(\log(e+N))^{r-1}}{N}
 
\end{equation}
whenever
\[
 B_r\leq N\leq b_rL(\log(e+L))^{r-1}.
\]

body:
[Definition 64 (Critical second-order entrance) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] A stochastic source has a \emph{critical second-order entrance} in a real
separable Hilbert space \(H\) if its perfected degree-two anchor is an
adapted c\`adl\`ag path in \(\mathscr G^+_{\mathrm{crit}}(H)\), its
finite-rank spatial projections converge ucp in the critical metric, and its
relative increments are obtained from the anchor by the stopped causal law.
A \(\beta\)-controlled entrance additionally satisfies, for a control
\(\omega\),
\[
 \|X_{s,t}\|\lesssim\omega(s,t)^\beta,
 \qquad
 \|A_{s,t}\|_{1,\infty}\lesssim\omega(s,t)^{2\beta},
 \qquad \beta\in(1/3,1/2).
\]
The source-specific analysis ends at this entrance.  Higher ancestry and
spectral conclusions are supplied by the normal and response theories.

body:
[Lemma 3 (Chain-compatible cutoffs) of arXiv:2607.19752, 'Weak Equilibrium Measures and Capacity--Hitting Identities\\ for the Hypoelliptic Third-Or'] Let $\mathsf O\subset\R^{3d}$ be a bounded smooth open set.  After the
reordering
\[
    x^1=r,\qquad x^2=p,\qquad x^3=\theta,
\]
there exist cutoff drifts, indexed by $0\le\delta\le1$,
\[
    B_1^{\mathsf O},B_2^{\delta,\mathsf O}
        \in C_b^\infty\left(\R^{3d};\R^d\right),
    \qquad
    B_3^{\delta,\mathsf O}
        \in C_b^\infty\left(\R^{2d};\R^d\right),
\]
with
\[
    B^{\delta,\mathsf O}(x)
    =\left(
        B_1^{\mathsf O}(x),
        B_2^{\delta,\mathsf O}(x),
        B_3^{\delta,\mathsf O}\left(x^2,x^3\right)
    \right),
\]
such that, for every $x\in\mathsf O$,
\begin{equation}
    B^{\delta,\mathsf O}(x)
    =
    \begin{pmatrix}
        -\gamma x^2-\gamma x^1\\
        -L^{-1}\nabla U(x^3)+\gamma x^1-\delta Lx^2\\
        x^2-\delta\nabla U(x^3)
    \end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
Moreover, for every $k\ge0$,
\begin{equation}
    \sup_{0\le\delta\le1}
    \left(
        \left\|B_1^{\mathsf O}\right\|_{C_b^k}
        +\left\|B_2^{\delta,\mathsf O}\right\|_{C_b^k}
        +\left\|B_3^{\delta,\mathsf O}\right\|_{C_b^k}
    \right)<\infty.
\end{equation}
On $\mathsf O$,
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
    J_{x^1}B_2^{\delta,\mathsf O}=\gamma I_{d},
    \qquad
    J_{x^2}B_3^{\delta,\mathsf O}=I_{d}.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The same assertions hold for cutoff drifts $B^{\delta,\mathsf O,*}$ of the
adjoint dynamics, with
\begin{equation}
    B^{\delta,\mathsf O,*}(x)
    =
    \begin{pmatrix}
        \gamma x^2-\gamma x^1\\
        L^{-1}\nabla U(x^3)-\gamma x^1-\delta Lx^2\\
        -x^2-\delta\nabla U(x^3)
    \end{pmatrix},
    \qquad x\in\mathsf O,
\end{equation}
and hence with chain links $-\gamma I_d$ and $-I_d$.

[Lemma 25 of arXiv:2609.04033, 'From configuration spaces to graph complexes via $\mathbf{FA}$-modules'] For $d$ odd there is an isomorphism of graded $S_n$-modules
	$$ 
H^\ast(\mathsf{T}_\Gamma(n)_d)\cong \bigoplus_{a+b=d-1} u_{(a,b)}\Sigma^{d}\Phi[n,(a,b)^\ast],
	$$
where
	$$u_{(a,b)} =
	\begin{cases}
		\left\lfloor \ds\frac{a-b-2}{4}\right\rfloor - \left\lfloor \ds\frac{a-b}{6}\right\rfloor+
		\delta_{a,b} & \text{ if }  a\equiv b \equiv 0 \text{ mod } 2 \\ 
		& \\
		\left\lfloor \ds\frac{a-b-2}{4}\right\rfloor - \left\lfloor \ds\frac{a-b}{6}\right\rfloor+
		1 & \text{ if }  a\equiv b \equiv 1 \text{ mod } 2 \\ 	
		& \\
		0 & \text{ else.}
	\end{cases}
	$$
title: Lemma 25 of arXiv:2609.04033

body:
[Proposition 6 of arXiv:2605.09706, 'A dyadic construction of a three-dimensional attractive point interaction Markov family'] Fix $T,\beta,\varepsilon>0$ and $0\le s<t\le T$. The map 
$\widehat{\mathsf K}^{T,\beta,\varepsilon}_{[s,t]}$ given by~\eqref{EqDefGlobalDyadicLimitKernel_Inf} is well defined and satisfies the following:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $\widehat{\mathsf K}^{T,\beta,\varepsilon}_{[s,t]}:\;
E_\varepsilon \times \mathcal B(E_\varepsilon)\to [0,1]$ is a sub-probability kernel on $E_\varepsilon$.

\item If $0\le r<s<t\le T$ with $r,s,t\in\mathbb D_T$, then for every $x\in E_\varepsilon$ and every $A\in\mathcal B(E_\varepsilon)$,
\begin{align}
\widehat{\mathsf K}^{T,\beta,\varepsilon}_{[r,t]}(x,A)
\,=\,
\int_{E_\varepsilon}
\widehat{\mathsf K}^{T,\beta,\varepsilon}_{[r,s]}(x,dy)\,
\widehat{\mathsf K}^{T,\beta,\varepsilon}_{[s,t]}(y,A)\, .
\end{align}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm MT_Lips of arXiv:2411.09640, 'Random Lipschitz functions on graphs with weak expansion'] There is a constant $c>0$ for which the following holds. Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices. Fix $v_0 \in V(G)$, and let $f$ be chosen uniformly at random from $\mbox{\rm{Lip}}_{v_0}(G;\infty)$. Then for any $r$ that satisfies $\max\{|B_r(v)|:v \in V(G)\}<c\log n$,
    \[\mathbb{P}\left[R(f)< \frac{r}{2}\right] =o_n(1).\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [campaign status: candidate_full_solution - author-checked, unrefereed] Aldous and Fill, Open Problem 4.30 (p. 137) asks whether there is an explicit function psi(b,s) tending to 0 as s tends to infinity, not depending on the chain, with sup_x |P(S_t/(sigma sqrt t) <= x) - P(Z <= x)| <= psi(||g||_inf, t/tau2) for standardized g and continuous-time reversible chains. Our result (id P0209, 2026-09-08): NO such psi exists. Take two independent reversible chains: Y two-state with rates epsilon and 1 - epsilon (spectral gap exactly 1) and Z a fair sign flip at rate R/2; set epsilon = s^-2, R = s^4, A = 2 epsilon + sqrt((1-epsilon)(1-4 epsilon)), B = (2-A)/(1-epsilon) and g = A Z + B (Y - epsilon). Then exactly, at every s: E g = 0, E g^2 = 1, ||g||_inf = 2 and tau2 = 1. Taking t = s sends t/tau2 to infinity with the sup norm pinned at 2, yet normality fails: S_t is compound Poisson with vanishing intensity (the mean number of visits to the rare state is epsilon t = 1/s, tending to 0), so with probability 1 - O(1/s) no visit occurs and S_t sits near the deterministic value -B epsilon t while the whole variance is carried by one rare excursion. Verification as the source words it: the identities were checked to seven decimals at every s, and the measured Kolmogorov distance to N(0,1) is 0.478, 0.505, 0.509, 0.506 at s = 30, 100, 300, 1000 - flat at about 1/2, not decreasing, while t/tau2 rises from 30 to 1000. Prior art not cleared. two independent reversible chains as specified (four states in total) g standardized: E g = 0, E g^2 = 1, sup norm 2, tau2 = 1 t = s, epsilon = s^-2, R = s^4

[Proposition 10 of arXiv:2605.13512, '2605.13512'] Let $c(x,y)$ satisfy Assumptions \ref{ass:c}, \ref{ass:c2}, \ref{ass:c0} and consider the discretisation 
$c^n(i,j) = c(in^{-1}, jn^{-1})$. Consider further (not necessarily deterministic) sequences of vectors $(a_n, b_n)$ and $(s_n, t_n)$ which satisfy 
\[
n^{-1}(a_n, b_n) \to (a,b) \text{ and }  n^{-1}(s_n, t_n) \to (s,t),
\] 
with $(s_n,t_n)-(a_n, b_n) \in \R^2_+$.

\lim_{n\to \infty} \frac{1}{n}G^{(n)}_{(a_n, b_n), (s_n, t_n)} = \Gamma_c((a,b),(s,t)) = \Gamma_{T_{a,b}c}(s-a,t-b).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary 12 (Recovery of known regimes and strict extension) of arXiv:2609.01116, 'Vector-Carleson, Calder\'on, and Poisson--Atomic Criteria for\\ Generalized Hilbert Operat'] Put
\[
 B_{2,p}(\phi)
 =|\phi(0)|+
 \left(\sum_{j\ge0}
  \bigl(2^{-j/p'}\|\Delta_j\phi\|_2\bigr)^t\right)^{1/t}.
 \tag{4.9}
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item $\|T_\phi:H^p\to H^2\|\asymp_p B_{2,p}(\phi)$, and
 boundedness of $T_\phi:H^p\to H^p$ implies
 $B_{2,p}(\phi)<\infty$.
 \item If $\operatorname{supp}\widehat\phi$ is contained in an analytic
 $\Lambda(p)$-set $E\subset\mathbb N_0$, then
 \[
  T_\phi:H^p\to H^p\text{ is bounded}
  \iff B_{2,p}(\phi)<\infty,
 \]
 with
 \[
  \|T_\phi:H^p\to H^2\|
  \le\|T_\phi:H^p\to H^p\|
  \le C_{E,p}\|T_\phi:H^p\to H^2\|.
 \]
 In this sector boundedness is equivalent to compactness.
 \item Hadamard-lacunary symbols are a special case of \textup{(ii)}.
 For a one-frequency-per-block symbol the test $h=1$ exactly norms the
 vector criterion, up to constants depending only on $p$.
 \item The blockwise condition
 \[
  \bigl(2^{-j/p'}\|\Delta_j\phi\|_{H^p}\bigr)_j\in\ell^t
 \]
 is sufficient in general and is not necessary, even for symbols with
 a consecutive interval occupying half of every sufficiently large hard
 block.
\end{enumerate}

[Prop x_n-decreasing of arXiv:2505.24821, 'Asymptotics for the harmonic descent chain and applications to critical beta-splitting tre'] Let $x_1, \ldots, x_{k-1} = 0, x_k > 0$ and 
    \[ x_n = \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} p(n, i)x_i \ \text{ for $n > k$}. \]

    unique solution in $C([0,T];L^2)$ given by
    \cref{prop:well_posed_averaging_limit}. For each

    process ${\xi}$ with paths in

   \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition 19 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let \(\iota \colon X \to S\) be a morphism of $\F_p$-stacks.
Let
\[
X^{(1)} \defeq X\times_{S,F_S}S
\]
be the relative Frobenius twist, and let
\[
F_{X/S}\colon X \to  X^{(1)}
\]
be the relative Frobenius.
  \begin{itemize}
      \item   The \emph{(absolute) de Rham stack} of \(X\) is defined as a functor
  \begin{equation*}
    X^{\dR} \colon \CAlg^{an}_{\setF_p} \to \Ani; \  R \mapsto X(W(R)/^L p),
  \end{equation*}
  where \(W(R)\) is the ring of Witt vectors of \(R\), \(-/^L p\) is the derived quotient by \(p\), and \(X(W(R)/^L p)\) is the mapping space \(\Map_{\dSch_{\setF_p}}(\Spec(W(R)/^L p), X)\) in the \(\infty\)-category of derived schemes over \(\setF_p\).
  Since this is isomorphic to the relative Hodge--Tate stack \((X/\setZ_p)^{\HT}\) of \(X\) relative to the crystalline prism \((\setZ_p, (p))\) introduced in \cite{bhatt2022Prismatization}*{Construction 7.1}, this is a stack on \(\CAlg^{an}_{\setF_p}\) (\cite{bhatt2022Prismatization}*{Lemma 7.3}).

  This is equipped with natural morphisms
  \begin{equation*}
    \pi_{X} \colon X \to X^{\dR} \quad \text{and} \quad \nu_X \colon X^{\dR} \to X
  \end{equation*}
  of \(\setF_p\)-stacks: For each \(R \in \CAlg^{an}_{\setF_p}\), each morphism is given by precomposition of morphisms
  \begin{equation*}
    R \xrightarrow{\Phi_R} W(R)/^L p \quad \text{and} \quad W(R)/^L p \xrightarrow{\res} R,
  \end{equation*}
  where \(\Phi_R\) is the animation of the morphism \(a \mapsto [a^p] \bmod p\) and \(\res\) is the restriction morphism.
  Note that the composition \(\nu_X \circ \pi_X\) is the absolute Frobenius morphism \(F_X \colon X \to X\) of \(X\).
\item The \emph{de Rham stack} of $X$ over $S$ is defined by
\[
(X/S)^{\dR} \defeq X^{\dR} \times_{S^{\dR},\pi_S} S.
\]
We define natural morphisms
  \begin{equation*}
    \pi_{X/S} \colon X \to (X/S)^{\dR} \quad \text{and} \quad \nu_{X/S} \colon (X/S)^{\dR} \to X^{(1)}
  \end{equation*}
  of \(\setF_p\)-stacks as follows:
The morphism $\pi_{X/S}$ is defined by
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
X \arrow[r,"\pi_{X/S}"'] \arrow[rd,bend right,"\iota"] \arrow[rr,bend left,"\pi_X"] & X^{\dR} \times_{S^{\dR}} S \arrow[r,"\pr_1"] \arrow[d,"\pr_2"] & X^{\dR} \arrow[d,"\iota^{\dR}"] \\
& S \arrow[r,"\pi_S"] & S^{\dR}.
\end{tikzcd}
\]
The morphism $\nu_{X/S} \colon (X/S)^{\dR} \to X^{(1)}$ is induced by the following commutative diagram
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
X^{\dR} \times_{S^{\dR}} S \arrow[r,"\pr_1"] \arrow[d,"\pr_2"] & X^{\dR} \arrow[d,"\iota^{\dR}"] \arrow[r,"\nu_X"] & X \arrow[d,"\iota"] \\
S \arrow[r,"\pi_S"] \arrow[rr,bend right,"F"] & S^{\dR} \arrow[r,"\nu_S"] & S.
\end{tikzcd}
\]
\item We assume that $\iota$ is smooth representable.
Then the cotangent complex \(L_{X/S}\) is a locally free \(\cO_X\)-module concentrated in degree \(0\).  
We set
\[
\Omega^1_{X/S} \defeq L_{X/S},
\qquad
\Omega^i_{X/S} \defeq 
\bigwedge_{\cO_X}^i\Omega^1_{X/S}.
\]
The universal \(S\)-derivation
\[
d_{X/S}\colon \cO_X \to  \Omega^1_{X/S}
\]
extends uniquely to the relative de Rham complex
\[
\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}
=
\left[
\cO_X
\xrightarrow{d_{X/S}}
\Omega^1_{X/S}
\xrightarrow{d_{X/S}}
\Omega^2_{X/S}
 \to \cdots
\right].
\]

We define a morphism of complexes of $\cO_{X^{(1)}}$-modules
\[
F^{\dR}_{X/S} \colon \cO_{X^{(1)}} \to F_{X/S,*}\Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}
\]
as follows:
We have
\[
d_{X/S}\circ F_{X/S}^{\sharp}=0
\]
by checking smooth locally on \(X\).  
Therefore, the morphism
\[
F_{X/S}^{\sharp}\colon
\cO_{X^{(1)}} \to  F_{X/S,*}\cO_X
\]
defines a morphism of complexes
\[
F_{X/S}^{\dR}\colon
\cO_{X^{(1)}}
 \to 
F_{X/S,*}\Omega^\bullet_{X/S},
\]
whose degree \(0\) component is \(F_{X/S}^{\sharp}\) and whose
positive-degree components are zero.
\end{itemize}

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The central moments of the binomial law are
$$M_1'=0$$
$$M_2'=np(1-p)$$
$$M_3'=np(1-p)(1-2p)$$
$$M_4'=np(1-p)(1+(3n-6)p(1-p))$$
$$\vdots$$
with the computation in general being possible by recurrence.

[Theorem disintegration of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] Let \(\Omega\)  and \(\mathcal{X}\) be Polish spaces, and let \(\nu \in \mathcal{P}(\Omega)\). Consider any
	\(\mu \in \mathcal{P}_{\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times \Omega)\). Then, there exists a unique (up to \(\nu\)-a.e. equality)
	Borel family \((\mu^{\omega})_{\omega \in \Omega}\subset \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})\) such that 
     	\[
     		\int_{\mathcal{X}\times \Omega} \varphi(x,\omega)d\mu(x,\omega)=\int_{\Omega} \int_{\mathcal{X}} \varphi(x,\omega)d\mu^{\omega}(x)d\nu(\omega),
     	\]
	for every bounded and measurable function \(\varphi:\mathcal{X}\times \Omega\to \mathbb{R}\). Conversely, given any Borel
	family \((\mu^{\omega})_{\omega \in \Omega}\subset \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})\), we can associate a unique fibered probability
	measure \(\mu \in \mathcal{P}_{\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times \Omega)\) so that the above formula holds true, and it will be denoted
	by \(\mu(x,\omega)=\mu^{\omega}(x)\otimes d\nu(\omega)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:dg of arXiv:2410.23509, 'Dynkin Games for L\'evy Processes'] Let 
$G_1(x)\leq G_2(x)$
be two real continuous payoff functions.
Consider a L\'evy process $X$ and a discount factor $r>0$, 
such that conditions (equation eq:ic of the paper) and (equation eq:limit of the paper) above hold.
Given two stopping times $\sigma$ and $\tau$, define the expected payoff

$$
{\operatorname{\mathbf{M}}_x}(\sigma,\tau)=\operatorname{\mathbf{E}}_x\left(
e^{-r\tau}G_1(X_{\tau})\mathbf{1}_{\{\tau\leq\sigma\}}
+
e^{-r\sigma}G_2(X_{\sigma})\mathbf{1}_{\{\sigma<\tau\}}
\right).
$$

The Dynkin game (DG) problem consists
in finding the value function $V(x)$ and two optimal stopping rules ${\sigma^*}$ and ${\tau^*}$ such that
\begin{align}
V(x)&=\inf_{\sigma}\sup_{\tau}{\operatorname{\mathbf{M}}_x}(\sigma,\tau)=\sup_{\tau}\inf_{\sigma}{\operatorname{\mathbf{M}}_x}(\sigma,\tau)={\operatorname{\mathbf{M}}_x}(\sigma^*,\tau^*).

\end{align}
title: Dynkin game

[Definition 10 (Weighted deterministic maximal $L^p$-regularity) of arXiv:2606.15425, 'Well-posedness of stochastic parabolic equations with gradient nonlinearities and applicat'] Let $\mathcal B_1 \coloneqq D(A) \subset \mathcal B$. Given $p \in (1,\infty)$ and $\beta \in (-1,p-1)$, we say that $A$ has \textit{weighted deterministic maximal $L^p$-regularity} on $[0,T]$ if for every
$f\in L^p_\beta([0,T];\mathcal B)$ and $u_0\in (\mathcal B,\mathcal B_1)_{1-(1+\beta)/p,p}$
there exists a unique
$$
u\in W^{1,p}_\beta([0,T];\mathcal B)\cap L^p_\beta([0,T];\mathcal B_1)
$$
such that $u(0)=u_0$ and
$$
u'(t)+Au(t)=f(t)\quad \text{for a.e. } t\in(0,T),
$$
and moreover, there is a constant $C_{MR}>0$ independent of $f$ and $u_0$ such that
\begin{equation}
\norm{u}_{W^{1,p}_\beta([0,T];\mathcal B)}+\norm{u}_{L^p_\beta([0,T];\mathcal B_1)}
\leq C_{MR}\left(\norm{f}_{L^p_\beta([0,T];\mathcal B)}+\norm{u_0}_{(\mathcal B,\mathcal B_1)_{1-(1+\beta)/p,p}}\right).
\end{equation}
title: Weighted deterministic maximal $L^p$-regularity

[Theorem 6 (\cite{DHKBrown},\cite{HoZhong2020Brown}) of arXiv:2511.10535, 'Eigenvalues of Brownian Motions on $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$'] Let $b_{0,1}(t)$ be a free multiplicative Brownian motion, and let $u_0$ be a unitary operator freely independent from $b_{0,1}$.  Denote by $\mu_{u_0}$ the spectral measure of $u_0$, a probability measure on the unit circle $\mathbb{T}$.

Define $T(u_0,\cdot)\colon\C\to\R_+$ by
\begin{equation}  T(u_0,z) = \frac{\log |z|^2}{|z|^2-1}\left(\int_{\mathbb{T}} \frac{\mu_{u_0}(d\xi)}{|\xi-z|^2}\right)^{-1}.
\end{equation}
Also, for each $t>0$, define the open precompact set $\Sigma(u_0,t)$ by
\begin{equation}  \Sigma(u_0,t) = \{z\in\C\colon T(u_0,z)<t\}. \end{equation}
The Brown measure $\mu_{u_0b_{1,0}(t)}$ has support equal to $\overline{\Sigma(u_0,t)}$.  The Brown measure is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure, and has density on $\overline{\Sigma(u_0,t)}$ that is real analytic in $\Sigma(u_0,t)$.  The density has the form $z=re^{i\theta}\mapsto w_t(\theta)/r^2$, with the radial function $w_t$ bounded by $w_t(\theta)<\frac{1}{\pi t}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{DHKBrown},\cite{HoZhong2020Brown}

If \(S\neq\varnothing\), choose \(b_0\in S\) and define

   U=\Span(S-b_0).

Owner draft: independently checked proof (C006 v1). For d>=1, the signed radial line law on [-1,1] with density f_d(t)=(d/2)|t|^(d-1) can be (2k+1)-CM only if (k/(k+1))^d>=1/(2k+1). A zero-sum tuple cannot have every |t_i|>k/(k+1), since at least k+1 share a sign and cannot be canceled by k bounded terms. Thus F_2 is not 3-CM (1/4<1/3) and F_4 is not 5-CM (16/81<1/5). These are the uniform disk/four-ball conditional laws on unoriented lines through the center. The full balls are mixable, so this refutes componentwise centered radial-needle mixing, not the convex-body conjecture. Projection onto a fixed line has a different marginal.

Let $\lambda$ be a partition, $k$ an integer such that $l(\lambda)\leq k$, and $\mathcal C$ be a positively-oriented simple contour encircling $0,\mathfrak a$ and $\mathfrak b$ and leaving $x_i^{-1}$ outside. Then
$$
G_\lambda^{(\mathfrak a,-\mathfrak b)}(x_1, \dots, x_n)=\oint_{\mathcal{C}}\cdots\oint_{\mathcal{C}} \frac{du_1}{2\pi \mathbf i}\dots \frac{du_k}{2\pi \mathbf i}\prod_{i<j}(u_i-u_j)\prod_{i=1}^k\left( \frac{1}{(u_i-\mathfrak a)^{\lambda_i}(u_i-\mathfrak b)^{k-i+1}}\prod_{j=1}^n\frac{1-\mathfrak b x_j}{1-u_ix_j}\right).
$$

body:
[Corollary 2 of arXiv:2607.29534, 'Expected signatures via partial integration, coordinate change and symmetrization'] There exists a graded invertible linear map
    $\widehat{\Psi}:
        T_{\mathcal{A}^{\prime\prime}}((\mathbb{R}^{d}))
        \to
        T_{\mathcal{A}^{\prime\prime}}((\mathbb{R}^{d}))$
    such that, for every smooth path $Y=(A,X)$ and any word
    $w\in\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{A}}$ with decomposition as in \eqref{eq:decomp_intro}, it holds that
    \[
        \left\langle
            [w_0]\blue{i_1}[w_1]\cdots\blue{i_k}[w_k],
            \widehat{\Psi}\circ\Sigsym{Y}_{s,t}
        \right\rangle
        =
        \frac{X_{s,t}^{[w_k]}}{[w_k]!}
        \int_{s<t_1<\cdots<t_k<t}
        \prod_{j=1}^{k}
        \frac{X_{s,t_j}^{[w_{j-1}]}}{[w_{j-1}]!}
        \dd A^{\blue{i_j}}_{t_j},
    \]
    where, for $v\in\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{A}^{\prime\prime}}$,
    \[
        X_{s,t}^{[v]}
        :=
        \prod_{\orange{i}\in\mathcal{A}^{\prime\prime}}
        \left(X_{s,t}^{\orange{i}}\right)^{\alpha_{\orange{i}}},
        \qquad
        [v]!
        :=
        \prod_{\orange{i}\in\mathcal{A}^{\prime\prime}}
        \alpha_{\orange{i}}!,
    \]
    with $\alpha_{\orange{i}}$ denoting the multiplicity of
    $\orange{i}$ in $v$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem thm:limit-law of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] Let $K$ be the Koenigs linearizer of $A$ at $\tfrac12$: the unique
		increasing solution of the Schr\"oder equation
		$K(2u) = A(K(u))$, $K(0)=\tfrac12$, $K'(0)=1$; then $K$ extends to a
		real-analytic increasing bijection $\mathbb{R}\to(0,1)$ and is the
		distribution function of a symmetric law $\mathcal{K}$ with analytic
		density. For every $f \in \mathcal{D}_{+}$,
		\begin{equation}
			2^{n} f(m)\,(X_{n} - m) \;\xrightarrow{\ d\ }\; \mathcal{K},
			
		\end{equation}
		and if $\mathbb{E}|X|^{\varepsilon} < \infty$ for some
		$\varepsilon>0$, all moments converge; in particular
		\begin{equation}
			\operatorname{Var}(X_{n})
			\;\sim\; \sigma_{\mathcal{K}}^{2}\, f(m)^{-2}\, 4^{-n},
			\qquad \sigma^{2}_{\mathcal{K}} \approx 0.166.
			
		\end{equation}
		Moreover, with $g = 1-K$, the symmetry of $A$ gives the exact tail
		recursion $g(2u) = A(g(u))$, whence
		\begin{equation}
			-\log\big(1 - K(u)\big)
			= u^{\log_{2}3}\,\Theta(\log_{2}u)\big(1 + O(u^{-\log_{2}3})\big)
			\qquad (u \to \infty)
			
		\end{equation}
		for a positive continuous $1$-periodic $\Theta$: the tails of
		$\mathcal{K}$ are compressed-exponential with exponent
		$\log_{2}3$, lighter than exponential and heavier than Gaussian, the
		exponent being the ratio of the logarithms of the endpoint degree and
		the interior multiplier; consistently, the excess kurtosis of
		$\mathcal{K}$ is positive ($\approx 0.164$). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Universal limit law

body: In mathematical analysis, the alternating series test proves that an alternating series is convergent when its terms decrease monotonically in absolute value and approach zero in the limit. The test was devised by Gottfried Leibniz and is sometimes known as Leibniz's test, Leibniz's rule, or the Leibniz criterion. The test is only sufficient, not necessary, so some convergent alternating series may fail the first part of the test.
title: Alternating series test

where $g_P$ is the side of $P$ separating $P$ from $Q$ and $g_Q$ is

finite approximant from
Corollary~(cor:slithering-networks of the paper), and define

 T\bigl(t_\rho(Q)\bigr)^\delta
 S_{\rho,N}(g_Q,g_P)
 E\bigl(e_\rho(P,Q)\bigr).

\(n\times n\) random matrix with independent real entries.  Assume that
\begin{align}
   \sup_{x\in\R}\PP\{A_{ij}=x\} &\leq b<1
   \qquad (1\leq i,j\leq n), \\
   \PP\{\rank A<n\} &\leq C_0\exp(-c_0 n)
   \qquad\text{for all }n\ge n_0 
\end{align}
for some constants \(C_0>0\), \(c_0>0\), and \(n_0\ge1\).  Then there exists
\(c_{5.1}=c_{5.1}(b,C_0,c_0,n_0)>0\) such that for all \(n\ge1\) and all
\(1\leq k\leq n\),
\begin{equation}
   \PP\{\rank A\leq n-k\}\leq \exp(-c_{5.1}nk).
\end{equation}

body: Load-bearing hypothesis: Omega bounded. The proofs use boundedness twice - the auxiliary function exp(gamma x_1) must be bounded on Omega, and the maximum must be attained on a compact set. On unbounded domains the conclusion is false even for harmonic functions with zero boundary data. Unbounded counterexample: on the half-space {x_n > 0} the function u(x) = x_n is harmonic and vanishes on the whole boundary, yet u > 0 inside; sup u = infinity while sup over the boundary of u = 0. Bounded counterexample (so boundedness of u does not rescue the statement in general): for n >= 3 let Omega = {|x| > 1} and u(x) = 1 - |x|^{2-n}. Then u is harmonic in Omega, continuous up to the boundary, bounded with 0 <= u < 1, u = 0 on the boundary sphere, and sup over Omega of u = 1 > 0 = sup over the boundary of u^+. In the plane, u(x) = log|x| on {|x| > 1} is an unbounded version of the same phenomenon. What restores the principle: treat infinity as a boundary point, i.e. assume limsup of u(x) as |x| tends to infinity is <= 0 (then the principle holds on any unbounded Omega, by exhausting with large balls), or impose a Phragmen-Lindeloef growth restriction adapted to the geometry. The admissible growth is set by the opening of the domain, and a thinner domain permits faster growth, not slower: in a plane sector of opening pi/a the threshold is exp(|x|^a), so a narrow sector allows faster growth than a half-plane, and in a strip of width d the threshold is exp(pi|x|/d), the extremal being exp(pi x_1/d) cos(pi x_2/d). The same caution applies to the H^1 weak maximum principle: its proof uses the Sobolev inequality together with the fact that the level sets have finite measure.
title: Pitfall: The Weak Maximum Principle Needs a Bounded Domain (or Control at Infinity)

[Lemma 24 (Fifth-chaos kernels) of arXiv:2608.29726, '\LARGE A Priori Estimates for Singular Fractional Stochastic Burgers Equations'] In the regime \eqref{eq:sbe-tree-response-regime}, the fifth-chaos
kernels of the three response coordinates are
\begin{subequations}
\begin{align}
 G_{\XoneFourB,5}^\eps
 &=
 \operatorname{Sym}_5\left[
  \chi_\odot(k_5,k_{1234})
  M_{12345}M_{1234}M_{12}M_{34}
  \prod_{i=1}^5H_i^\eps
 \right],
 \\
 G_{\XtwoThree,5}^\eps
 &=
 \operatorname{Sym}_5\left[
  \chi_\odot(k_{12},k_{345})
  M_{12345}M_{12}M_{345}M_{34}
  \prod_{i=1}^5H_i^\eps
 \right],
 \\
 G_{\XoneFourC,5}^\eps
 &=
 \operatorname{Sym}_5\left[
  \chi_\odot(k_5,k_{1234})
  M_{12345}M_{1234}M_{123}M_{12}
  \prod_{i=1}^5H_i^\eps
 \right].
 
\end{align}
\end{subequations}
Moreover, uniformly in \(\eps\),
\[
 \mathcal C_{G_{\XoneFourB,5}^\eps}(\zeta)
 +\mathcal C_{G_{\XtwoThree,5}^\eps}(\zeta)
 \lesssim
 \langle\zeta\rangle_\gamma^{
  -(\gamma+1)-2(5q-\delta)+},
\]
and
\[
 \mathcal C_{G_{\XoneFourC,5}^\eps}(\zeta)
 \lesssim
 \langle\zeta\rangle_\gamma^{-(\gamma+1)-4q+}.
\]

THE PROBE'S CONTENT, CONFIRMED BY P3 AND UNCHANGED: monotonicity Var(X_{n+1}) >= Var(X_n) for planar FPP reduces exactly to a signed-covariance statement through the identity Var(X_{n+1}) - Var(X_n) = Cov(X_{n+1} + X_n, Delta) with Delta := X_{n+1} - X_n bounded by an O(1) triangle bound, equivalently monotonicity iff Cov(X_n, Delta) >= -Var(Delta)/2; and FKG/Harris positive association is structurally inapplicable, because Delta is not environment-monotone - the two-route gadget is constructible with bounded weights and raising a weight on X_n's geodesic makes Delta strictly fall. Let X_1, \dots, X_n be independent Bernoulli random variables with \mathbb{P}(X_k = 1) = p_k = 1 - \mathbb{P}(X_k = 0). Let S_n = \sum_{k=1}^n X_k and \lambda = \sum_{k=1}^n p_k. Let Y \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda). Then the total variation distance between the distribution of S_n and Y satisfies d_{TV}(\mathcal{L}(S_n), \text{Poisson}(\lambda)) = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{k=0}^\infty |\mathbb{P}(S_n = k) - \frac{\lambda^k e^{-\lambda}}{k!}| \le \sum_{k=1}^n p_k^2.
X_k independent Bernoulli(p_k)

body:
[Lemma lem:moving-bump of arXiv:2609.00794, 'On operators whose adjoints or second adjoints attain their norms'] Let
\[
u:=\left(\frac1{2^n}\right)_{n=1}^\infty\in S_{\ell_1},
\qquad
b_n:=\frac12(e_{n+1}-e_{n+2})\in S_{\ell_1},
\]
where $(e_n)$ denotes the standard coordinate basis for $\ell_1$. 
Let $0<\kappa<1$, and let $S\in\mathcal L(\ell_1,\ell_1)$.
Suppose that there exist a set $A\subset\mathbb N$, a mapping
$\nu\colon A\to\mathbb N$, and scalars $(\lambda_j)_{j\in A}$ such that

\begin{enumerate}
\itemsep0.25em
\item  $Se_j=\kappa u+(1-\kappa)\lambda_j b_{\nu(j)}$ for every $j \in A$, and $|\lambda_j|\leqslant 1$ for every $j \in A$;

\item there exist $(j_n)\subset A$ and a sequence $(s_n)$ tending to
infinity such that
\[
Se_{j_n}=\kappa u+(1-\kappa)b_{s_n};
\]

\item $\sup_{j\notin A}\|Se_j\|<1$.
\end{enumerate}

Then $\|S\|=1$ and $S^*$ does not attain its norm.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Zero speed on every bounded-degree subexponential-growth subgraph Result: Let H be a connected subgraph of a bounded-degree graph G with |B_G(x,n)|=exp(o(n)). The Carne-Varopoulos bound gives P_x(X_n=y)<=2 sqrt(deg_H(y)/deg_H(x)) exp(-d_H(x,y)^2/(2n)). Summing over reachable vertices yields P(d_H(x,X_n)>=epsilon n)<=C exp(o(n)-epsilon^2 n/2), which is summable. Thus the intrinsic speed on H is zero almost surely. Check: Reachability in H implies membership in B_G(x,n), but distances in the exponential bound remain intrinsic to H. Bounded degrees control the prefactor. This is a consequence of the classical heat-kernel bound, not a novelty claim. Obstruction: It settles the zero-speed equivalence for subexponential-growth Cayley graphs and their clusters only. Exponential-growth cases need different information.

[Lemma lem:asymptotic-product-app of arXiv:2609.00556, 'Higgs--Demailly System and Positivity of Higgs Bundles'] Let $x_{a,j}>0$, $1\leq a\leq r$, be functions on a compact space.  If
\[
 \prod_{a=1}^r x_{a,j}\to1
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \max_{a,b}|x_{a,j}-x_{b,j}|\to0
\]
uniformly, then $x_{a,j}\to1$ uniformly for every $a$.

body: [Defn def:hugging of arXiv:2604.12963, 'Shocks, instability, and the twenty networks\\ of infinite geodesics in the Directed Lands'] For $\theta\in\Theta^\omega$, a point $(x,s)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ is a \emph{$\theta+$ hugging shock} if $(x,s)\in\IG\theta$ and $\Gamma_{{(x,s)}}\dir{L}{\theta}{-}\cap\Gamma_{{(x,s)}}\dir{L}{\theta}{+}\ne\{(x,s)\}$. Similarly, $(x,s)$ is a \emph{$\theta-$ hugging shock} if $(x,s)\in\IG\theta$ and $\Gamma_{{(x,s)}}\dir{R}{\theta}{-}\cap\Gamma_{{(x,s)}}\dir{R}{\theta}{+}\ne\{(x,s)\}$.
title: Defn def:hugging of arXiv:2604.12963

Own-work draft, proof (unaudited), T280-w716-C9 v1, kind route-failure, Target 3. For every k>=1, the prepared aligned finite scale law supported on 1,...,k+1, with zero output weights and biases and exp activation, has a positive risk threshold whose first hitting time for the normalized degree-k sphere harmonic tends to infinity with d. Thus k+1 occupied scales with fixed positive separation do not alone imply O(1)-in-d small-risk learning. For k=1 and scales 1,2 the Gaussian squared approximation floor exceeds 2/5, so risk 1/4 cannot be attained in dimension-uniform bounded time. For any fixed finite horizon T and positive minimum atom mass, d/dt E a^2<=1/2 implies pointwise bounded output coefficients and O(1/d) aligned-scale drift; the actual nonlinear output remains O(1/d) from its initial exponential span. The degree-k sphere harmonic has a strictly positive limiting Gaussian projection distance from the span at scales 1,...,k+1. For scales 1,2 and target Z the squared distance is 1-(1-4 exp(-2)+4 exp(-3))/(exp(1)-1)>2/5. This is a full-risk obstruction; no claim is made about a single harmonic projection hitting time. No novelty claim or independent certification.
Uniform unit sphere, ordinary all-parameter population mean-field flow, known axis and sqrt(d)-scaled initialization
Fixed finite positive atom masses, fixed scales, zero output and bias initialization
Threshold depends on k; assertion concerns full residual energy, not a claimed general mixing or frequency lower bound

[Theorem thm:highdimEinstein of arXiv:2609.01464, 'Removability of non-isolated singularities for Einstein metrics and RCD spaces'] Let $n\geqslant 2$ be an integer, and $a>0$. There exists $0<\varepsilon:=\varepsilon(n,a)<1$ such that the following holds.
  
  Let $(M^n, g)$ be a closed $L^\infty$-Riemannian manifold, and $S\subset M$ a closed subset of Assouad codimension greater than $2+a$; see (def:Codimension of the paper). Suppose that $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = Kg$ on $M\setminus S$ for some $K\in\mathbb R$, and in addition suppose that one of the following conditions holds:
  \begin{itemize}
      \item[(a)] Either $(1 - \varepsilon)h \leqslant g \leqslant (1+\varepsilon) h$ for a smooth metric $h$ on $M$,
      \item[(b)] Or $g$ is continuous. 
  \end{itemize}
    Then $g$ extends to $M$ as a smooth Einstein metric, perhaps for a different smooth structure. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:highdimEinstein of arXiv:2609.01464

PRIVATE REDUCTION, author-recorded. By Aizenman's random-current identity the four-point Ursell function is expressed through the probability that the currents from x_1 to x_2 and from x_3 to x_4 share a cluster; non-triviality (nonvanishing renormalised coupling) is equivalent to inf over scales L of P(two independent random-current clusters at scale L intersect) > 0. The 4D case is now trivial (Aizenman-Duminil-Copin 2021); in 3D the heuristic is favourable because the current-cluster dimension (5 - eta)/2 = 2.48 exceeds 3/2, so independent fractals of that dimension would intersect with positive probability. A second-moment argument on the number of intersection points reduces the uniform lower bound to (a) a two-point function lower bound with exponent 2 - eps in d = 3 (Duminil-Copin's Conjecture 5, PIMS lectures) and (b) a variance bound on the intersection count, which involves six-point correlations beyond the Lebowitz inequality. Both inputs are open; (b) is the genuinely new obligation.

[Lemma 57 (A curve meets an ellipsoid in at most $2D$ points) of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Let $V\subset\R^d$ and $C\subset\mathbb P^d_{\mathbb C}$ be as above,
		with $\deg C=D$.  For $R\succ0$ and $\rho>0$, set
		\[
		E_{R,\rho}:=\{x\in\R^d:x^\top R x=\rho\}.
		\]
		If $C$ is not contained in the projective quadric obtained by
		homogenizing $x^\top R x-\rho$, then
		\begin{equation}
			
			\#\bigl(V\cap E_{R,\rho}\bigr)\le 2D.
		\end{equation}
		In particular, this holds for every centered ellipsoid if $V$ is not
		contained in any centered ellipsoid.  A sufficient condition is that
		$V$ be unbounded.

[Thm 2 of arXiv:2605.07059, 'Modified ruin probability for a Cram{\'e}r-Lundberg model driven by a compound mixed Poiss'] Fix $\ell\in(0,c/\mu)$. Assume that
\[
\psi_{\rm cl}(u,\ell)\sim c_\ell e^{-R_\ell u},\qquad u\to\infty,
\]
for some constants $c_\ell,R_\ell>0$. If $\psi$ is continuous or monotone on $(-\infty,0)$, then
\[
\psi_\ell(u)\sim C_\ell\,\psi_{\rm cl}(u,\ell),\qquad u\to\infty,
\]
where
\[
C_\ell:=\int_{(-\infty,0)}\psi(y)\,\nu_\ell(\rmd y)
\]
and the probability measure $\nu_\ell$ is determined by
\begin{align*}
&\nu_\ell(( -\infty,-x])
\\
&=\frac{1}{c-\ell\mu}\Bigl(ce^{-R_\ell x}
\\
&\qquad\qquad-\ell\int_0^x e^{-R_\ell(x-z)}\bar F(z)\,\rmd z
\\
&\qquad\qquad-\ell\int_x^{\infty}\bar F(z)\,\rmd z\Bigr),
\end{align*}
for $x\ge0$.

[Definition gsp of arXiv:2608.30777, 'Inhomogeneous nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation \\ in Fourier-Lebesgue and modulation space'] Let $1\leq p_{0} \leq 2.$
 Consider a pair of exponents $(Q_{p_{0}}(r),r)$ satisfying 
\begin{align*}
&\frac{2}{Q_{p_{0}}(r)} + \frac{1}{r} = \frac{1}{p_{0}} \\
  \text{either}\quad 
& 0 < \frac{1}{Q_{p_{0}}(r)} < \min \left( \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{r},\; \frac{1}{4} \right) \quad  \text{and}\quad
  0 < \frac{1}{r} < \frac{1}{2}\\
&  \text{or}\quad 
(Q_{p_0}(r), r)= (4, r) \quad  \text{and}\quad r > 4.
\end{align*}
The set of all such pairs is denoted by 
$\widehat{\mathcal{X}}(p_{0}).$
title: Generalized Strichartz pair, \cite{hyakuna2012existence, CFeffermanAM,grunrock2004improved}

[Lemma 43 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let
\[
 (X,g_i(s))\longrightarrow(\widehat X,\hat g_s),\qquad s<0,
\]
be smooth spacetime convergence on an exhaustion of a complete smooth
limit, with time-preserving convergence embeddings \(\psi_i\) defined
on domains \(U_i\Subset\widehat X\times(-\infty,0)\).  Write
\(U_{i,t}=U_i\cap(\widehat X\times\{t\})\) and \(\psi_{i,t}\) for the
time-\(t\) maps.  Fix \(t_0<0\), \(D>0\), an integer \(k\ge0\), and
\(\varepsilon>0\).  If \(p_i\to p_\infty\) in the correspondence at
time \(t_0\), then there is a relatively compact smooth domain
\(\Omega\Subset\widehat X\) such that, for all large \(i\),
\[
\overline{B_{g_i(t_0)}(p_i,D)}
\Subset
\psi_{i,t_0}(\Omega)
\Subset
\psi_{i,t_0}(U_{i,t_0}),
\]
\[
\left\|
\psi_{i,t_0}^{*}g_i(t_0)-\hat g_{t_0}
\right\|_{C^k(\overline\Omega,\hat g_{t_0})}
\leq\varepsilon.
\]

Let p>0. Let X_n be real random variables in L^p on one probability space, and let X be a finite real random variable on that space. Then X is in L^p and E|X_n-X|^p tends to zero if and only if X_n converges to X in probability and {|X_n|^p:n>=1} is uniformly integrable. For 0<p<1, L^p convergence here means convergence of the pth absolute moments of the differences; no norm or Minkowski inequality is asserted.

X_n in L^p for every n
X finite and real; all variables on one probability space

[Proposition 47 (Local comparison for the one-step tilted spine law) of arXiv:2604.25877, 'Asymptotic height of Plancherel random trees'] Fix $t>1$ and let $\nu_t=\mathrm{Beta}(t,\theta)$ on $(0,1)$, with density
$
f_t(x)$.
We set
\[
I_j^{(m)}:=\left(\frac{j-1}{m},\frac{j}{m}\right],\qquad 1\le j\le m.
\]
With the same notations as in 
Proposition~\ref{prop:ewens_onestep_beta}, 
the following estimates hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \textbf{Uniform cell-wise comparability.}
There exist constants \(0<c_t\le C_t<\infty\) such that for all sufficiently large \(k\) and all
\(1\le j\le m\),
\begin{equation}
c_t\,
\nu_t\!\left(I_j^{(m)}\right)
\le
\mu_{k,t}\!\left(\left\{\frac{j}{m}\right\}\right)
\le
C_t\,
\nu_t\!\left(I_j^{(m)}\right).

\end{equation}

\item[(ii)] \textbf{Sharp comparison in the bulk.}
There exist constants $C,\gamma>0$ such that for
every $\eta\in(0,\frac12)$, 
\begin{equation}
\sup_{\eta m\le j\le (1-\eta)m}
\left|
\frac{\mu_{k,t}(\{j/m\})}{\nu_t(I_j^{(m)})}-1
\right|
\le
C\,\eta^{-1}m^{-\gamma},

\end{equation}
for all sufficiently large $k$.
\end{enumerate}

[Defin 55 of arXiv:2604.00635, 'Large deviations of the periodic Toda chain'] Let $\op{s}_{\rho}$ be the dilation with scale $\rho > 0$: $\op{s}_{\rho}(x)=\rho x$. Given $\mu \in \mathcal{M}_1(\mathbb{R})$, its pushforward by $\op{s}_{\rho}$
is the unique probability measure $\op{s}_{\rho \#}\mu$  such that

$$\Int{\mathbb{R}}{} f(x) \, \mathrm{d}\op{s}_{\rho \#}\mu( x)  \, =  \, \Int{\mathbb{R}}{} f(\rho  x) \,  \mathrm{d}\mu(x) \, .$$

Note that $\mathrm{supp} \big[ \op{s}_{\rho \#} \mu \big] \,  =  \,  \rho \, \mathrm{supp} [ \mu ]$. For a probability measure $\mu$ and $\tau>0$, we denote by $\mu_\tau$
the probability measure obtained by the convolution

\begin{equation}

\mu_\tau=\frac{1}{2\tau} \mathbbm{1}_{[-\tau;\tau]} \ast \mu\,.

\end{equation}

body: Let X be a smooth projective curve of genus g over an algebraically closed field, equivalently a compact Riemann surface, and let D be a divisor on X. Write l(D) for the dimension of the space of meromorphic functions on X whose poles are bounded by D and which have no other poles, and let K be a canonical divisor of X. The Riemann-Roch theorem states l(D) - l(K - D) = deg(D) + 1 - g, where deg(D) is the sum of the coefficients of D. Once deg(D) > 2g - 2 this gives l(D) = deg(D) + 1 - g exactly, since l(K-D) then vanishes. Proved by Riemann and Roch in the 1850s-60s; vastly generalized by Hirzebruch and Grothendieck.
title: Riemann-Roch theorem

[Definition 28 of arXiv:2607.29495, 'Fast Mixing for Low-Temperature Potts Models via Poisson Trees'] Let $\Downg$  be the distribution of  $X\sim\Poisson(dp_\good)$.
Let $\Downgbig$ be the distribution of $X$ conditioned on $X\geq D$ and let $\Downgsmall$ be $\Downg$ conditioned on $X<D$. Let $\Downb$ be the distribution $\Poisson(dp_\bad)$.  The rooted random tree $\cT^{\down}$ is defined as follows.

\begin{itemize}
\item The root is set to be \emph{down-good} with probability $p_\good$ and \emph{down-bad} otherwise (with probability $p_\bad$).

\item From every down-good vertex, the number of down-good children is sampled independently from $\Downgbig$ and the number of down-bad children is sampled independently from $\Downb$.

\item From every down-bad vertex, the number of down-good children is sampled independently from $\Downgsmall$ and the number of down-bad children is sampled independently from $\Downb$.
\end{itemize}

[Cor scaling-exponent-distance of arXiv:2604.14122, 'The scaling limit of random walk and\\ the intrinsic metric on planar critical percolation'] Let $S_n$ be the geodesic distance (resp.\ effective resistance) between the left and the right side of $\Lambda_n$ which we denote by $\partial_L \Lambda_n, \partial_R \Lambda_n$, respectively. Let $\beta \in \{\beta^{\mathrm {geo}},\beta^{\mathrm {res}}\}$ be the scaling exponent of the CLE$_6$ geodesic (resp.\ resistance) metric defined in [my2025metric,my2025diffusion]. For each $q \in (0,1)$, we have
    \[
    \mathbf{E}[S_n \mid \partial_L \Lambda_n \leftrightarrow \partial_R \Lambda_n ] 
    \asymp \operatorname{quant}_q[S_n \mid \partial_L \Lambda_n \leftrightarrow \partial_R \Lambda_n ]
    \asymp {\mathfrak{q}}_n
    = n^{\beta+o(1)} 
    \quad\text{as } n \to \infty ,
    \]
    where $\operatorname{quant}_q$ denotes the $q$-quantile, ${\mathfrak{q}}_n$ denotes ${\mathfrak{q}}_n^{{\mathrm {geo}}}$ (resp.\ ${\mathfrak{q}}_n^{{\mathrm {res}}}$), and the multiplicative constants in~$\asymp$ depend on $q$. Method: Equal level growth does not determine branching number Result: A geodesic spanning tree has exactly the Cayley graph sphere sizes at each level. But growth can exceed branching number for a bounded-degree tree: take a single infinite spine and at its nth vertex attach a finite b-ary tree of height n. Its level sizes have exponential rate sqrt(b)>1, while its only infinite ray is the spine and arbitrarily deep singleton cutsets give branching number one. Check: At level m the largest attached contribution starts around n=m/2 and has order b^(m/2), up to constant factors and a geometric sum. Every attachment is finite, so no additional infinite ray appears. Obstruction: This is not a geodesic Cayley spanning-tree counterexample. It proves that matching sphere counts alone cannot establish the conjectured branching number.

body: [Lemma lem:excess-chernoff of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Let $n$ be an integer, and let $Z_1,\dots,Z_n$ be components of a generalised multinomial  random variable. Let $\overline{\mu} \in (\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n$, and suppose $\mathbb{E}(Z_k) \le \mu_k$ for all $k \in [n]$. Fix $\delta \ge e$, and for all $k \in [n]$, let $Z_k^+ = \max\{0, Z_k - \delta\mu_k\}$. Let $Z^+ = \sum_{k=1}^n Z_k^+$. Then for all $z\geq 0$, $\mathbb{P}(Z^+ > z) \le 2^n\delta^{-z}$.
title: Lemma lem:excess-chernoff of arXiv:2602.21315

body:
[Lemma main_lemma of arXiv:2604.05921, 'Simplicity of random hypergraphs'] Let $\delta_1,\delta_2 \in \mathds{N}$. Given (possibly non-unique) vertices $v_1,v_2,\hdots,v_{\delta_1} \in V$, let the unique vertices be denoted by $v'_1,v'_2,\hdots,v'_{u(\vb*{v})}$, for some $u(\vb*{v}) \in \mathds{N}$. Similarly, let the unique vertices in $w_1,w_2,\hdots,w_{\delta_2}$ be denoted by $w'_1,w'_2,\hdots,w'_{u(\vb*{w})}$. Let $D(\vb*{v})=\frac{\delta_1!}{\prod_{i=1}^{u(\vb*{v})} m_{v'_i}(\vb*{v})!}$ and $D(\vb*{w})=\frac{\delta_2!}{\prod_{i=1}^{u(\vb*{w})} m_{w'_i}(\vb*{w})!}$. Let $\hat{R}(\cdot)$ be as in (equation def:B_hat of the paper) and let $U$ denote a uniformly chosen vertex in $V$. For any functions $f_1^{(i)}(v):V \rightarrow \mathds{N}$, $f_2^{(i)}(v):V \rightarrow \mathds{N}$ and $w \in \mathds{N}$,
    \begin{align}
        
        &\sum_{\vb*{v} \in V^{\delta_1}}  \sum_{\vb*{w} \in (V\backslash\{v_1,\hdots,v_{\delta_1}\})^{\delta_2}} (D(\vb*{v})D(\vb*{w}))^w \prod_{i=1}^{u(\vb*{v})} f_1^{(m_{v'_i}(\vb*{v}))}(v'_i) \prod_{j=1}^{u(\vb*{w})} f_2^{(m_{w'_j}(\vb*{w}))}(w'_j) \nonumber \\
        &=\sum_{\substack{\vb*{a} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_1}:\\ \sum_{i=1}^{\delta_1} ia_i = \delta_1}}  \frac{\delta_1!^{1+w}}{\prod_{k=1}^{\delta_1} k!^{(1+w)a_k}} \sum_{\substack{\vb*{b} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_2}:\\ \sum_{i=1}^{\delta_2} ib_i = \delta_2}}  \frac{\delta_2!^{1+w}}{\prod_{k=1}^{\delta_2} k!^{(1+w)b_k} } \nonumber \\
    &\hspace{1cm} \times \sum_{\gamma(\cdot) \in \hat{R}(\vb*{a},\vb*{b})} (-1)^{\sum{\vb*{g} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_1}, \vb*{h} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_2}}( \sum_{i=1}^{\delta_1} g_i + \sum_{j=1}^{\delta_2} h_j -1) \gamma(\vb*{g},\vb*{h})} \nonumber \\
    &\hspace{1cm} \times  \prod_{\substack{\vb*{y} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_1}\\ \vb*{z} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_2}}} \Bigg( \frac{1}{\gamma(\vb*{y},\vb*{z})!} \Big(\frac{n\mathds{E} \big[\prod_{i=1}^{\delta_1} (f_1^{(i)}(U))^{y_i} \prod_{j=1}^{\delta_2} (f_2^{(j)}(U))^{z_j} \big] \big(\sum_{i=1}^{\delta_1} y_i + \sum_{j=1}^{\delta_2} z_j-1 \big)!}{\prod_{i=1}^{\delta_1} y_i! \prod_{j=1}^{\delta_2} z_j!} \Big)^{\gamma(\vb*{y},\vb*{z})} \Bigg).
    \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma main_lemma of arXiv:2604.05921

[Lemma lem:class-number-reduction of arXiv:2609.00777, 'Universal murmuration and Hecke augmentation'] Let $P\nmid N$, with $P$ odd, $N$ squarefree, and $PN>4$.  For $m\geq1$, whenever the arguments are discriminants, one has
\[
h(-P^{2m}N)=P^{m-1}h(-P^2N),
\qquad
h(-4P^{2m}N)=P^{m-1}h(-4P^2N),
\]
and
\[
h(-P^{2m+1}N)=P^mh(-PN),
\qquad
h(-4P^{2m+1}N)=P^mh(-4PN).
\]

[Definition Type forest, type rays and paths of arXiv:2607.16911, 'Multipartite random graphs with given degrees: local limit, revisiting the giant, distance'] Consider the \emph{Ulam-Harris forest} $\mathscr{F}_S$ on the set of types $S$. That is to say, $\mathscr F_S$ is an infinite forest, consisting of $|S|$ many infinite tree components $\{\mathscr T(s):s\in S\}$. For any fixed $s_0 \in S$, the root of the tree $\mathscr T(s_0)$ is $s_0$, and for any $v\in \mathscr T(s_0)$, it has $|S|$ many offspring $\{vs:s\in S\}$. Observe that any $v\in \mathscr T(s)$ has the form of a word $v=s_0s_1\dots s_k$. We call the forest $\mathscr F_S$ the \textit{type forest} corresponding to the set of types $S$. 
    
    Furthermore any directed infinite path $\pi=(s_0\rightarrow s_0s_1 \rightarrow s_0s_1s_2\rightarrow \dots)$ starting at the root $s_0$ is called a \emph{type ray} in $\mathscr T(s_0)$, and a finite directed path of the form $(s_0\rightarrow s_0s_1 \rightarrow \dots \rightarrow s_0s_1s_2\dots s_k)$ is called a \emph{type path} started at $s_0$. By $|\pi|$ we denote the length of $\pi$. Thus, if $\pi$ is a type ray, $|\pi|=\infty$, while for $\pi=(s_0\rightarrow s_0s_1 \rightarrow \dots \rightarrow s_0s_1\dots s_k)$, $|\pi|=k$.
title: Type forest, type rays and paths

[Proposition 2 of arXiv:2604.00642, 'Quantitative central limit theorem for an integrated periodogram via the fourth moment the'] Let
\[
f_\alpha(\lambda)=|\lambda|^{-\alpha}L(\lambda),
\qquad \lambda\in(-\pi,\pi),\quad \alpha\in\mathcal A,
\]
where $\mathcal A=[a,b]\subset[0,1)$, and assume that the true parameter value $\alpha_0$ belongs to $\mathcal A$. Suppose that $L\in \mathcal C^1([-\pi,\pi]\setminus\{0\})$ is positive on $[-\pi,\pi]$ and slowly varying at $0$.

Define the Whittle contrast by
\[
Q_n(\alpha)
=
\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}
\left[
\log f_\alpha(\lambda)+\frac{I_n(\lambda)}{f_\alpha(\lambda)}
\right]\dd\lambda,
\qquad \alpha\in\mathcal A.
\]
Let
\[
\widehat\alpha_n\in \arg\min_{\alpha\in\mathcal A} Q_n(\alpha)
\]
be any measurable minimizer of $Q_n$ over $\mathcal A$. Then
\[
\widehat\alpha_n \xrightarrow{\mathbb P} \alpha_0,
\]
and
\[
\sqrt n\,(\widehat\alpha_n-\alpha_0)
\;\Rightarrow\;
\mathcal N\!\left(0,\frac{4}{\sigma_0^2}\right),
\]
where
\[
\sigma_0^2
=
\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} \bigl(\log|\lambda|\bigr)^2\,\dd\lambda.
\]

[Corollary cor:mass-no-killing of arXiv:2608.11931, '\texorpdfstring{Nonlinear parabolic characterizations of stochastic completeness at infini'] Let $G$ be a graph with $\kappa=0$ and \(\mu(X)<\infty\).
Let $\phi\in\mathcal{I}$ with $\phi^{-1}(\mathbb R_+)\neq\emptyset.$ Then \(G\) satisfies
\hyperref[def:SC]{\textup{(SC)}}{} if and only if one, and hence all, of the
statements {\rm(ii)}--{\rm(iv)} of
Theorem~(thm:generalized-mass-characterization of the paper) hold, with the
generalized mass identity~\hyperref[eq:nonlinear-generalized-mass]{\textup{(MB)}}{} reducing
to the conservation of mass:
\[
    \mathsf M_u(t)=\mathsf M_{u_0}
    \qquad \text{for } t\in[0,T].
\]

Moreover, if \(G\) does not satisfy \hyperref[def:SC]{\textup{(SC)}}{}, then, for every \(T>0\)
and every \(c \in \mathbb R_+\) such that $0<\phi(c)<\sup_{\mathbb R}\phi,$ there exist bounded positive pointwise solutions
\(u_-\) and \(u_+\), both with initial datum \(u_0= c\), and times
\(t_-,t_+\in(0,T]\) such that
\[
    0\le u_-\le c\le u_+
    \qquad\text{on }[0,T]\times X
\]
and
\[
    \mathsf M_{u_-}(t_-)<c\,\mu(X)<\mathsf M_{u_+}(t_+).
\]
Thus, failure of \hyperref[def:SC]{\textup{(SC)}}{} allows for both loss of mass to infinity and
creation of mass from infinity.

[Lemma lemmawi of arXiv:2412.02087, 'The spectral distribution of random graphs with given degree sequences'] [Properties of $w_i$]
    
    If $w_i = 1$, then $\sum_l d_l^{w_i} = D$. If $w_i =0$, then $\sum_l d_l^{w_i } = n$. If $w_i \leq -1$, then $\sum_l d_l^{w_i}  = o(n(n/D)^{|w_i|/2})$.\\
    Additionally, if $w_i$ increases by $1$, then $\sum_l d_l^{w_i}$ increases by a factor of $\omega (\sqrt{D/n})$.

[Theorem CPLT of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a compactly supported positive measure $\rho$, of mass $c=mass(\rho)$, the following compound Poisson limits converge,
$$p_\rho=\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(\left(1-\frac{c}{n}\right)\delta_0+\frac{1}{n}\rho\right)^{*n}
\quad,\quad 
\pi_\rho=\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(\left(1-\frac{c}{n}\right)\delta_0+\frac{1}{n}\rho\right)^{\boxplus n}$$
and if we write $\rho=\sum_{i=1}^sc_i\delta_{z_i}$ with $c_i>0$ and $z_i\in\mathbb R$ we have the formula
$$p_\rho/\pi_\rho={\rm law}\left(\sum_{i=1}^sz_i\alpha_i\right)$$
where the variables $\alpha_i$ are Poisson/free Poisson$(c_i)$, independent/free.

Let A be an N-by-n real random matrix whose rows a_i^T are independent, with integers N,n>=2, common uncentered second-moment matrix Sigma=E[a_i a_i^T], and Gamma=E max_i||a_i||_2^2<infinity. Put r=min(N,n). There is an absolute C such that, for delta=C sqrt(Gamma log(r)/N), E||A^T A/N-Sigma||_op<=max(||Sigma||_op^(1/2)delta,delta^2). With an absolute constant C, enlarged if necessary, the same hypotheses give (E||A||_op^2)^(1/2)<=sqrt(N||Sigma||_op)+C sqrt(Gamma log(r)). These are both conclusions of Vershynin1011.3027v7 Theorem5.48 p30. Sigma may be singular; zero row means, identical row laws and independence of coordinates are not assumed. The dimension restriction excludes the literal zero-log singleton endpoint.

body: [Definition 3.2 (δ-hyperbolic (Gromov, 1987) of arXiv:2606.10238, 'Hyperbolic Neural Population Geometry Benefits Computation'] ). A geodesic metric space (X , d) is δ-hyperbolic if every geodesic triangle in X is δ-thin. Equivalently for all x, y, z, w ∈X , d(x, z) + d(y, w) ≤ (3.1) max {d(x, y) + d(z, w), d(y, z) + d(x, w)} + 2δ, which is called the 4-point condition. In general, low δ means the geodesic metric space is more tree-like, as tree triangles (Chiswell, 2001) are 0-hyperbolic.

[Thm 7 (Universality of resultant distributions) of arXiv:2608.06576, 'The Resultant Distribution Method: Universality for $p$-adic Random Matrices and Polynomia'] Let $Z\in\Z_p[x]$ be a fixed monic polynomial of degree $d$, whose constant term lies in $\Z_p^\times$. Then there exists a random variable $\mathcal{R}_Z\in\Z_{\geq 0}\cup\{\infty\}$ such that
$$
\val(\Res(P_n,Z))
\overset{d}{\longrightarrow}
\mathcal{R}_Z,\qquad n\rightarrow\infty.
$$
Furthermore, the sequence $\val(\Res(P_n^{\Haar},Z))$ also weakly converges to the same limit, i.e.,
$$
\val(\Res(P_n^{\Haar},Z))
\overset{d}{\longrightarrow}
\mathcal{R}_Z,\qquad n\rightarrow\infty.
$$

[Prop 12 of arXiv:2605.25762, 'Brownian Convergence of Planar Domains and Stability of the Planar Skorokhod Embedding Pro'] Let $(x^{[n]}_{k})_{0\leq k\leq n}$ be a mesh.
Define
\[
\mu_{n}:=F(a)\delta_{a}+\sum^{n}_{k=1}\big(F(x_{k})-F(x_{k-1})\big)\delta_{x_{k}},
\]
and let $q_{n}$ be the quantile function of $\mu_{n}$. Then for
any $p\ge1$,
\[
\|q-q_{n}\|_{L^{p}(0,1)}\le\max_{1\le k\le n}(x_{k}-x_{k-1}).
\]
In particular, for the uniform mesh $x_{k}=a+\frac{b-a}{n}k$,
\[
\|q-q_{n}\|_{L^{p}(0,1)}\le\frac{b-a}{n}.
\]

body:
[Lem 237 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $\alpha,L,\epsilon,K>0$ and any sequence of $\epsilon$-approximate $L$-Lipschitz algorithms $(\cA_N)_{N\ge 1}$,
	\[
		\lim_{N\to\infty} \bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_{N[K]}), \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)\Big) 
		= \lim_{N\to\infty} \bbW_2\Big(\mu_{\sym}(\cA_{N[K]}), \cM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha;\epsilon)\Big)
		= 0\,.
	\]

\begin{proof}
	We only prove that the first limit is zero, as the second limit is proved analogously.
	Suppose for contradiction that there exists $\delta > 0$ such that $\bbW_2(\mu(\cA_{N[K]}), \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)) \ge \delta$ for infinitely many $N$.
	By \eqref{e:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound.l4} from Lemma~\ref{l:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound}, there exists $C = C(\alpha,L,K) > 0 $ such that for sufficiently large $N$, $\mu(\cA_{N[K]}) \in \cP_4(\R,C)$.
Then, for infinitely many $N$, we have
	\[\mu(\cA_{N[K]})\in
		S_\delta 
		\equiv \Big\{ \mu \in \cP_4(\R,C) : \bbW_2(\mu, \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)) \ge \delta 
		\Big\}\,.
	\]
	By Lemma~\ref{l:confinement.cPp.compact.Wq}, the space $\cP_4(\R,C)$ endowed with the $\bbW_2$ metric is compact.
	The set $S_\delta$ is closed with respect to the $\bbW_2$ metric, hence also compact. Therefore
 we may find $\mu \in S_\delta$ and a subsequence $(N_j)_{j\ge 1}$ such that
	\[
		\lim_{j\to\infty} \bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_{N_j[K]}),
		\mu\Big) = 0\,.
	\]
	As noted in Definition~\ref{d:truncated.lip.alg}, we have $\mu^{\Ising}(\cA_{N_j[K]}) = \mu^{\Ising}(\cA_{N_j})$: thus, since each $\cA_{N_j}$ is an $\epsilon$-approximate $L$-Lipschitz algorithm, so is each $\cA_{N_j[K]}$. It follows by omitting finitely many $j$'s that we have
	\[
	\WERR(\cA_{N_j[K]},\mu)
	=\max\bigg\{
	\bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_{N_j[K]}),
		\mu\Big),
	\bbW_2\Big(
		\mu^\Ising(\cA_{N_j[K]}),
		\cP(\{\pm1\})
		\Big)
	\bigg\}\le\epsilon
	\]
for all $j$. Recalling the definition \eqref{e:cM.Lip} of  $\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;L,\epsilon)$, this implies
	\[
		\mu \in \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;L,\epsilon) \subseteq \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)\,,
	\]
	which contradicts that $\mu \in S_\delta$.
\end{proof}

[Defn of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] Let $\gamma:[0,T]\rightarrow V$ be a continuous path with bounded
variation. The \textit{signature transform} of $\gamma$ (or simply
the signature) is the formal tensor series defined by 
\[
S(\gamma)\triangleq\big(1,\gamma_{T}-\gamma_{0},\int_{0<s<t<T}d\gamma_{s}\otimes d\gamma_{t},\cdots,\int_{0<t_{1}<\cdots<t_{n}<T}d\gamma_{t_{1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes d\gamma_{t_{n}},\cdots\big),
\]
where the path integrals are defined in the Lebesgue-Stieltjes sense.
The tensor series $\log S(\gamma)$ is known as the \textit{logarithmic
signature} of $\gamma$.

[Cor 10 of arXiv:2608.05185, '\large\bf ON THE HEAT FLOW CONJECTURE FOR RANDOM MATRICES'] Let \((\mathbf{G}_N)_{N\geq1}\) be any sequence of complex Ginibre
matrices: for each \(N\), its entries are independent centred complex
Gaussian variables satisfying
\[
 \E\!\left[|(\mathbf{G}_N)_{ij}|^2\right]=\frac1N,
 \qquad
 \E\!\left[(\mathbf{G}_N)_{ij}^2\right]=0.
\]
Let us set
\[
 p_N(z)=\det(z\mathbf{I}-\mathbf{G}_N),\qquad
 q_N(z)=\exp\!\left(-\frac{1}{2N}\partial_z^2\right)p_N(z).
\]
Then, almost surely,
 $\nu_{q_N}\overset{\mathrm{w}}{\longrightarrow}\mathfrak{sc}_1$.

body:
Every unbounded open convex set in finite-dimensional Euclidean space contains an infinite straight ray starting at each of its points. If such a set is a mirror-complement component, that ray never collides with a mirror and is an escaping launch direction. The assertion needs convexity and does not settle the general all-reflected-rays trapping problem.
All hypotheses and scope restrictions in the statement apply.

Lemma 1. Every unbounded open convex set C in R^d contains an unbounded straight ray starting at each x in C. Therefore, if a mirror-complement component is unbounded, open and convex, an origin in it has an unobstructed escaping launch direction and cannot have every reflected ray bounded.

Eventually this radius exceeds 3r/4 and the center is within r/4 of x+t*d, so B(x+t*d,r/2) is in C. This holds for every fixed t with the same subsequential direction d, proving the entire ray stays inside C. No collision occurs along it.

Lemma 2. C={(x,y): x>0 and |y-x^2|<1} is open, connected and unbounded but contains no unbounded straight ray.

Thus all possible directions leave C in finite time.

This gives an explicit algebraic version of the previous spiral-corridor obstruction: unbounded connected vacancy alone does not supply a straight ray. The corridor is not represented as a permitted mirror arrangement, and absence of straight rays does not establish trapping of reflected rays. We write $(A, B) \in \mathcal{SMR}^\bullet_p$ if for every $f\in L^p(I_T\times \Omega, X_0)$, $u_0 \in L^p_{\mathcal{F}_0}(\Omega; X^{\operatorname{Tr}}_p)$ there exists a strong solution $u$ to the linear Cauchy problem 
    $$\mathrm{d}u - Au\mathrm{d}t = f_t\mathrm{d}t  + B(u)\mathrm{d}W_t,\qquad  u(0)=u_0.$$
    such that $u \in  L^p(\Omega ; H^{\theta, p}(I_T; X_{1-\theta}))$ for every $\theta \in [0, 1/2)$ and for all stopping times $\tau : \Omega \rightarrow I_T$ it holds 
    $$\|u\|_{L^p( \Omega; H^{\theta, p}(I_T; X_{1-\theta}))} \lesssim \|f\|_{L^p(I_T \times \Omega ; X_0)} + \|u_0\|_{L^p_{\mathcal{F}_0}(\Omega; X^{\operatorname{Tr}}_p)}$$
    and in particular 
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{t\in[0, T]} \|u_t\|^p_{X^{\operatorname{Tr}}_p}\right]  +\expt{\int_0^t\|u_s\|^p_{X_1}\mathrm{d}s}  \lesssim \expt[]{\int_0^t \|f_s\|^p_{X_0}ds} + \expt{\|u_0\|^p_{ X^{\operatorname{Tr}}_p}}.
    \end{equation}

[Proposition 4 of arXiv:2607.11283, 'Markov Properties of $k$-Record Processes via Order Statistics'] The process $(Y_n)_{n\ge k}$ is a time-homogeneous Markov chain with respect to the filtration $(\mathcal{F}_n)_{n\ge1}$. More precisely, for every bounded Borel function $g:\mathcal{E}_k\to\mathbb{R}$ and every $n\ge k$,
\[
\mathbb{E}\bigl[g(Y_{n+1}) \mid \mathcal{F}_n\bigr]
=
\int_{\mathbb{R}} g\bigl(\psi_k(Y_n,x)\bigr)\, dF(x)
\quad \text{a.s.}
\]
In particular,
\[
\mathbb{P}(Y_{n+1}\in A \mid \mathcal{F}_n)
=
\int_{\mathbb{R}} \mathbf{1}_A\bigl(\psi_k(Y_n,x)\bigr)\, dF(x),
\quad A\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{E}_k).
\]

body:
[Lemma of arXiv:2604.24914, 'SPDEs with time-independent\\ L\'evy colored noise'] Under Hypotheses A to D, for any $(t,x)\in \mathbb{R}_{+} \times \mathbb{R}^d$,  $\{Y^{(t,x)}(s)\}_{s \in [0,t]}$ and $\{Z^{(t,x)}(s)\}_{s \in [0,t]}$ have jointly measurable modifications denoted by $\{\widetilde{Y}^{(t,x)}(s)\}_{s \in [0,t]}$, respectively $\{\widetilde{Z}^{(t,x)}(s)\}_{s \in [0,t]}$, and with probability 1,
\[
\int_0^t |\widetilde{Y}^{(t,x)}(s)|ds<\infty \quad \mbox{and} \quad \int_0^t |\widetilde{Z}^{(t,x)}(s)|ds<\infty.
\]
Moreover, for any $(t,x)\in \mathbb{R}_{+} \times \mathbb{R}^d$,
\[
v(t,x):=\int_0^t \widetilde{Y}^{(t,x)}(s)ds=\int_0^t \widetilde{Z}^{(t,x)}(s)ds \quad \mbox{in $L^2(\Omega)$}.
\]
The process $\{v(t,x); t\geq 0,x\in \mathbb{R}^d\}$ is the random field solution of equation (equation lin-eq of the paper).

[Definition def:fk_current of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Let $U\in C^1_b(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^d)$ be a bounded, continuously
differentiable vector field with bounded derivatives, and $k\in\mathbb{R}$.
The \emph{Feynman-Kac semigroup} associated with $U$ is the family
$(P_t^{k,J})_{t\geq 0}$ on $L^2(\mu)$ defined by
\begin{align}
  \bigl(P_t^{k,J} f\bigr)(x)
  \equiv
  \E^x\left[
    f(X_t)\exp\left(k \int_0^t U(X_s)\circ\mathrm{d} X_s\right)
  \right],
  
\end{align}
for $f \in L^2(\mu)$, $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, $t \geq 0$, where $\circ$ denotes
Stratonovich integration and $U(X_\tau)\circ\mathrm{d} X_\tau=\sum_i U_i(X_\tau)\circ\mathrm{d} X^i_\tau$.
