[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2608.22534, 'Entropy power inequalities in compact groups'] Let $G$ be a compact and metrizable topological abelian group
equipped with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and let $\mu$ denote the Haar 
probability measure on $G$. 
For any $G$-valued random variables $X, Y$ with finite entropies 
there is a non-empty, closed subset $S$ of $G$ of positive Haar 
measure such that, if $U_S$ is uniformly distributed on $S$, then,
for any constant $C\geq 4$,
\begin{equation} 
\dR(U_S, Y) \leq (C+2)\dR(X, Y) + H_2(1 - 2/C), 
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
\log \frac{\mu(S-S)}{\mu(S)} \leq (2C+4)\dR(X, Y) + 2H_2(1 - 2/C).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:main-explosion of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] \phantomsection
Let $\sigma=1+2d\zeta$, where $(\zeta(x))_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}$ are i.i.d.\ with $\mathbb{E}\zeta(0)=0$ and $0<\Var(\zeta(0))<\infty$. In parts~\textup{(i)}, \textup{(ii)}, and~\textup{(iii)(a)--(b)}, assume additionally that
$\mathbb{E} e^{\theta_0|\zeta(0)|}<\infty$ for some $\theta_0>0$.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \underline{\textup{Dimensions one, two, and three.}}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item The rescaled mean converges:
$\lim_{t\to\infty}t^{-(4-d)/4}\mathbb{E} u_t(0)$
exists and lies in $(0,\infty)$.
\item The parabolic scaling limit is a Brownian optimal-stopping value. Let
$\mathcal W$ be white noise on $\mathbb{R}^d$, let
\[
    Z(t,x)\coloneqq \sqrt{\Var(\zeta(0))}
    \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}g_t^{\rm BM}(x,y)\,\mathcal W(dy)\, ,
\]
with $g_t^{\rm BM}$ the finite-time Green kernel of Brownian motion (defined in Section~(sec:rw-rep of the paper)), and let
\[
    \mathcal U(T,x)\coloneqq
    \sup_{\tau\leq T}\mathbf E_x^{\rm BM}
    \bigl[Z(T,x)-Z(T-\tau,B_\tau)\bigr]\, ,
\]
where the supremum is over stopping times for Brownian motion. Then, for every $T>0$,
\[
    R^{-(2-d/2)}\,u^{(R)}_{\lfloor TR^2\rfloor}
    \Longrightarrow
    \mathcal U(T,\cdot)
    \qquad\text{in }C_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^d)\, ,
\]
where the field on the left denotes the multilinear interpolation from $R^{-1}\mathbb{Z}^d$ of the values
$x/R\mapsto R^{-(2-d/2)}u_{\lfloor TR^2\rfloor}(x)$.
\end{enumerate}

\item \underline{\textup{Dimension four.}}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item The mean odometer is of logarithmic order at each site: as $t\to\infty$
\[
    \mathbb{E} u_t(0)\asymp\log t\, ,
\]
and, for every fixed $x\in\mathbb{Z}^4$, $u_t(x)/\mathbb{E} u_t(0)\to1$ in $L^2$ and
almost surely.
\item The centered odometer $u_t(0)-\mathbb{E} u_t(0)$ has Gaussian fluctuations:
\[
    \frac{u_t(0)-\mathbb{E} u_t(0)}{\sqrt{\log t}}
    \Longrightarrow
    N\left(0,\frac{4\Var(\zeta(0))}{\pi^2}\right)\, ,
\]
and $\Var(u_t(0))/\log t\to4\Var(\zeta(0))/\pi^2$.
\item For every $T>0$ and $s>0$, the fields
$\bigl(u_{\lfloor TR^2\rfloor}-\mathbb{E} u_{\lfloor TR^2\rfloor}(0)\bigr)^{(R)}$ for
$R\geq1$ are tight in $H^{-s}_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^4)$. Moreover, for every
$\alpha>2$, the fields $\bigl(u_{t_R}-\mathbb{E} u_{t_R}(0)\bigr)^{(R)}$ at the
superdiffusive times $t_R\coloneqq\lfloor R^\alpha\rfloor$ converge, modulo additive constants, to the four-dimensional membrane model $\mathcal G_4$ in $H^{-s}_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^4)$.
\end{enumerate}

\item \underline{\textup{Dimensions five and higher.}}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
	\item The odometer is deterministic to first order at every fixed site. For
	each fixed $x\in\mathbb{Z}^d$, $u_t(x)/\mathbb{E} u_t(0)\to1$ in $L^2$ and almost surely.
	Moreover, the mean diverges: there is $c>0$ such that $\mathbb{E} u_t(0)\geq c(\log t)^{2/d}$ for all large $t$.

[Lemma lem:delta of arXiv:2608.05089, 'Correlation decay in area-tilted line ensembles'] Under any coupling between $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$, we have
\begin{align}
    \mleft|
        \operatorname{Cov}[X^i(0), X^j(t)]
    \mright|
    &\leqslant
    2 \sqrt{
        \mathbb{E} \mleft[ X^i(0) (X^i(0) - Y^i(0)) \mright] \cdot
        \mathbb{E} \mleft[ X^j(t) (X^j(t) - Y^j(t)) \mright]
    } \\
    
    &\qquad + \mathbb{E} \mleft[ Y^i(0) (X^j(t) - Y^j(t)) \mright]
        + \mathbb{E} \mleft[ (X^i(0) - Y^i(0)) Y^j(t) \mright] \\
    
    &\qquad + \mathbb{E}\mleft[Y^i(0)\mright] \mathbb{E}\mleft[ X^j(t) - Y^j(t) \mright]
    + \mathbb{E} \mleft[ X^j(t) \mright] \mathbb{E} \mleft[ X^i(0) - Y^i(0) \mright].
\end{align}
Moreover, both factors appearing under the square root in (equation decom4631 of the paper) are nonnegative.

chains $P_{\delta,N}$ (parameterized by $\delta\in(0,1)$ and integer

\[
  \lim_{N\to\infty}\;\lim_{\delta\to 0}\;L(P_{\delta,N})\;\le\;2\varepsilon,

AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. Near-square Gaussian extensive-rank reference has a C1 information limit and pointwise limiting MMSE at every fixed positive SNR, proof unaudited. For independent real standard Gaussian U of size N by M and V of size P by M, B=UV^T/sqrt(N), M/N->beta in (0,infinity), P/N->1, the per-entry MI tends to i_beta(s)=Sigma(dilation_sqrt(s)(mu_beta) free-plus semicircle_1)-Sigma(semicircle_1), where mu_beta is the compact symmetric limiting singular law of UV^T/N in the square model and has second moment beta. For s>0, i_beta is C1 and normalized Gaussian-reference MMSE converges to 2 i_beta_prime(s)=1/s-Phi(mu_beta free-plus semicircle_(1/s))/s^2. Input zero atoms are allowed. A real conditional population-Wishart theorem, exact random-profile density calibration021 and free-heat regularity020 pay the observation law, MI limit and derivative separately. Column-padding chain-rule bounds extend the square result to every P/N->1 sequence. With existing finite-fourth-moment spectral coupling008 and Haar comparison006, every centered fixed iid unit-variance finite-fourth-moment pair of factors has limsup normalized product-MMSE excess over the Gaussian reference <=0 at every fixed s>=0. Novelty unestablished; full rectangular aspect !=1 is not settled.
Real centered iid Gaussian reference factors, independent between arrays and of Gaussian channel noise.
M/N->beta>0 finite, P/N->1.
Per-entry risk for UV^T/sqrt(N); raw UV^T risk divided by N.
Iid-prior MMSE consequence uses fixed centered unit-variance finite-fourth-moment laws and unaudited claims006/008.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:4c3e0cbd1ab022f1c5a21624256d0762ba0994785c484f1778108a7bfc71f042","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/4c/4c3e0cbd1ab022f1c5a21624256d0762ba0994785c484f1778108a7bfc71f042.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:f7ee46a2e3388a11ce13fc89ccd7a2a712259b34ba37615dbe0afe0e0398d634","bundle_entry_key":"gaussian-product-near-square-mi-c1-mmse-w718","bundle_id":"population.t287-near-square-c1-and-finite-variance-comparison-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian channels and extensive-rank matrix inference","draft":"w718/bundle_008.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.gaussian_channels:gaussian-product-near-square-mi-c1-mmse-w718","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Gaussian extensive-rank reference: a C1 information limit near the square aspect

Target 2 partial result, proof draft, unaudited. Novelty is unestablished.
The hardest remaining part of full Target 2 is the corresponding reference
entropy differentiability at rectangular aspect bounded away from one.
Target 1's dimension-uniform high-noise remainder also remains open.

## Statement and normalization

Let n->infinity, M_n/n->beta in (0,infinity), and P_n/n->1. Let U_n and
V_n be independent real standard Gaussian arrays of sizes n by M_n and
P_n by M_n. Put B_n=U_n V_n^T/sqrt(n), let G_n have independent standard
Gaussian entries, and define

 i_n(s)=I(B_n;sqrt(s)B_n+G_n)/(n P_n),
 m_n(s)=E||B_n-E[B_n|sqrt(s)B_n+G_n]||_F^2/(n P_n).

There is a compact symmetric probability law mu_beta, of second moment
beta, such that, for every s>=0,

 i_n(s)->i_beta(s)
   =Sigma(dilation_sqrt(s)(mu_beta) free-plus sigma_1)-Sigma(sigma_1).

The interpretation at s=0 is zero. For s>0 the limit is C1 and

 lim m_n(s)=2 i_beta'(s)
   =1/s-Phi(mu_beta free-plus sigma_(1/s))/s^2.        (1)

Here Sigma is logarithmic energy, sigma_t is the variance-t semicircle
law, and Phi is scalar free Fisher information as in claim020.
This applies to all positive finite beta, including beta<1 when the
input singular law has a zero atom. No finite input logarithmic energy
is assumed. At s=0, m_n(0)=M_n/n->beta.

Together with unaudited claims006 and008, this gives, for centered iid
unit-variance fixed finite-fourth-moment factor laws at the same sizes,

    limsup [m_iid,n(s)-m_n(s)]<=0 for every fixed s>=0.               (2)

It is a near-square partial Target2 result, not a full rectangular
answer. Raw UV^T loss must be divided by n before comparing these limits.

## 1. The primary real population-Wishart theorem

Silverstein, *Strong convergence of the empirical distribution of
eigenvalues of large dimensional random matrices*, J.Multivar.Anal.55
(1995),331-339, DOI10.1006/jmva.1995.1083, Theorem1.1 and equation(1.4).
The author's PDF is papers/silverstein1995_primary.pdf, with provenance
and SHA in SOURCES.jsonl. The theorem allows independent random PSD
population matrices with almost-sure weak empirical convergence. Its
entries may be complex with unit centered variance; iid real standard
Gaussians are a special case. No condition E Z^2=0 is imposed.

At square sample aspect one, if the population spectral law is K on
[0,infinity), the limiting squared-singular-value transform m, with
m(lambda)=integral(x-lambda)^-1 dF(x), satisfies

    m(lambda)=integral[-t*lambda*m(lambda)-lambda]^-1 K(dt).

The Stieltjes branch is specified by the theorem. For the symmetric
singular law, put g(z)=-z*m(z^2), z in the upper half-plane. Analytic
continuation from Re z>0 gives

    g(z)=integral[z-t*g(z)]^-1 K(dt),                 (3)

where Im g<0 and g(z)~1/z at infinity. This explicitly fixes the opposite
sign convention from m. All populations used below are PSD, independent
of the sample Gaussian matrix, and have almost-sure deterministic weak
limits, as the theorem requires.

First take C_n=U_n U_n^T/n. Applying the same theorem with identity
population and sample aspect n/M_n, then rescaling by M_n/n, gives a
deterministic limit tau_beta. Gaussian norm tails give compact support.
The normalized trace converges to beta, so tau_beta has mean beta.

## 2. Exact conditional covariance and the observation law

Initially set P_n=n and S_n=B_n/sqrt(n)=U_n V_n^T/n. If H_n is an
independent n by n standard real Gaussian matrix, then, conditional on U_n,

    S_n has law C_n^(1/2) H_n/sqrt(n).

Indeed its columns are independent centered Gaussians with covariance
C_n/n. For independent Z_n with entry variance1/n, the normalized
observation Y_n=sqrt(s)S_n+Z_n similarly has conditional law

    (I+s C_n)^(1/2) H_n/sqrt(n).                    (4)

The sample H_n in each distributional representation is independent
of C_n. Silverstein's theorem therefore applies both to the input
population C_n and to the output population I+s C_n. It gives a compact
symmetric input singular law mu_beta and an output law nu_s. With
g_s=G_(nu_s) and h_s=G_(dilation_sqrt(s)(mu_beta)), equation(3) reads

 h_s(w)=integral[w-s*c*h_s(w)]^-1 tau_beta(dc),
 g_s(z)=integral[z-(1+s*c)*g_s(z)]^-1 tau_beta(dc).    (5)

These equations are only used for s>0; s=0 is pure Gaussian noise.
Put w(z)=z-g_s(z). It lies in the upper half-plane, and g_s(z) solves
the first equation at w(z). For Im z sufficiently large, that equation
has at most one solution in the lower half-plane: for two candidates,
the difference of the integral maps is bounded by
s*sup(supp tau_beta)/(Im w)^2 times their difference. This factor is
less than one. Hence g_s(z)=h_s(w(z)) there, and analyticity extends
the equality to the entire upper half-plane.

This is the semicircular subordination equation with variance one. To
check the branch rather than assume it, H(w)=w+h_s(w) satisfies H(w(z))=z.
Moreover

 Im H(w)=Im w*[1-integral |w-x|^-2 d(dilation_sqrt(s)mu_beta)(x)].

Since Im z>0, w(z) is in Biane's domain Omega_(dilation_sqrt(s)mu_beta,1).
Biane1997 Lemma4, journal p710, makes H conformal from that domain onto
the upper half-plane; Proposition2, p711, identifies its inverse as the
semicircular subordination map. Therefore

    nu_s=dilation_sqrt(s)(mu_beta) free-plus sigma_1.                (6)

This uses a primary real Wishart theorem, not a unitary-to-orthogonal
extension of the rectangular-addition theorem. By Biane Corollaries1-3,
nu_s has a bounded continuous density and compact support; its positive
singular law eta_s has density twice that symmetric density on x>0.
Thus eta_s is compact with bounded density, including at the hard edge.

## 3. Expected W2 convergence, including the moment passage

We record the upgrades beyond weak convergence because they are needed
by the calibration theorem. For an n by M Gaussian U, a pair of sphere
1/4-nets gives

 P(||U/sqrt(n)||op>K)<=2 exp((n+M)log9-n*K^2/8).

The bounded ratio M/n permits a fixed sufficiently large K. The tails
are summable in n, and their integrated versions give uniformly bounded
moments of every fixed order of these norms. The same holds for the
square noise and H_n. Consequently S_n and Y_n have uniformly bounded
fourth operator-norm moments, and almost-sure eventual norm bounds.

For A_n=||Y_n||_F^2/n, the exact conditional moments from(4) are

 E[A_n|U_n]=tr(I+s C_n)/n,
 Var(A_n|U_n)=2 tr((I+s C_n)^2)/n^3.

The expected conditional variance is O(n^-2), by the uniform norm
moments. Also Var(tr C_n/n)=2(M_n/n)/n^2. Total variance is therefore
O(n^-2), and E A_n=1+s M_n/n. Chebyshev and Borel-Cantelli give
A_n->1+s beta almost surely. The same argument with population C_n
gives ||S_n||_F^2/n->beta.

Weak convergence from the primary theorem plus these second moments
gives empirical singular W2 convergence almost surely. The uniform
fourth operator-norm bounds make its square uniformly integrable:
W2(eta_n,eta_s)^2<=2 m2(eta_n)+2 m2(eta_s), and
m2(eta_n)<=||Y_n||op^2. Thus

    E W2(eta_(Y_n),eta_s)^2->0.                     (7)

The same reasoning fixes the second moment beta of mu_beta. Distributional
representations may be realized on a common probability space; the
expected-W2 and information conclusions depend only on their marginals.

## 4. Pay the unbounded-input truncation

Choose C large enough that E_n={||S_n||op<=C} has probability tending to
one exponentially fast, using the product bound for the two Gaussian
factor norms. Let S_n^E have the conditional law of S_n given E_n.
This is still biorthogonally invariant and has operator norm at most C.

Construct a coupling by setting S_n^E=S_n on E_n and, on its complement,
drawing an independent sample from that conditional law. It has the
claimed marginal. With a_n=||S_n||_F^2/n,

 d_n^2:=E||S_n-S_n^E||_F^2/n
       <=2 E[a_n 1_(E_n^c)]+2 P(E_n^c)E[a_n|E_n]->0.              (8)

Uniform operator fourth moments and Cauchy-Schwarz pay the first term;
the second is bounded because P(E_n)->1 and E a_n=M_n/n. They also give
E||S_n^E||_F^2/n->beta.

Share the noise between the coupled observations. Hoffman-Wielandt gives
expected squared singular-law W2 distance at most s*d_n^2. Hence(7)
holds for the conditioned prior too. Claim021 now applies and proves
its normalized MI limit Sigma(nu_s)-Sigma(sigma_1).

The dimension-uniform Gaussian entropy/W2 estimate of claim006 transfers
back to the original prior:

 |I(S_n;Y_n)/n^2-I(S_n^E;sqrt(s)S_n^E+Z_n)/n^2|<=sqrt(s)*d_n.

The right side tends to zero. We obtain the stated square-reference
information formula, with no input-density or finite input-energy
assumption and no use of the disputed oracle-to-Bayes step in2403.04615.

## 5. Differentiability and limiting MMSE

By dilation and(6), for s>0 the limit is

 i_beta(s)=Sigma(mu_beta free-plus sigma_(1/s))
                         +(1/2)log s-Sigma(sigma_1).

The compactness of mu_beta verifies claim020, including when it has atoms.
That claim proves positive-time C1 energy with derivative Phi/2. Thus

    i_beta'(s)=1/(2s)-Phi(mu_beta free-plus sigma_(1/s))/(2s^2).

The finite normalized information functions are concave and differentiable,
with derivative m_n/2 by I-MMSE. Their pointwise convergence to this C1
limit forces derivative convergence by the two-sided concave secant
inequalities. This proves(1) for exactly square dimensions.

## 6. Extend the reference limit to P_n/n->1

At fixed n,M, couple all column sizes by sharing U and the existing rows
of V. Adding k observed columns increases unnormalized MI by an amount
between zero and

    n*k*c_n(s), c_n(s)=(1/2)log(1+s M/n).

The chain rule gives the increase as conditional MI. Its upper bound
uses conditioning reduces entropy, the independent new Gaussian noise,
and the scalar maximum-entropy bound for each new entry of variance
1+s M/n. No independence between signal columns is assumed.

Both the smaller matrix's normalized information and the extra-column
information per new entry lie in [0,c_n(s)]. The larger normalized
information is their dimension-weighted average. Therefore

 |i_(n,P)(s)-i_(n,n)(s)|
       <=|P-n|/max(P,n) * c_n(s)->0 when P/n->1.      (9)

The reference limit remains i_beta and is C1. The same concave secants
give its MMSE limit(1) for every such near-square sequence.

Finally, claim008 supplies expected ordered spectral coupling to this
Gaussian reference for centered fixed finite-fourth-moment iid factors,
at every positive finite aspect ratio. Claim006's Haar-risk and
information/secant comparison applies now at every positive s, since
the near-square reference limit is C1. This proves(2). At s=0, both
risks are exactly M_n/n, so the comparison includes zero directly.

## Scope and least-trusted step

All new proof dependencies017,019,020,021 and old006,008 remain unaudited.
The least-trusted new step is the spectral identification(5)-(6), especially
the square-root Stieltjes convention and analytic branch continuation;
the explicit primary equations and Biane inverse-domain check expose it
for line-by-line review. Full rectangular aspect !=1 and Target1's
uniform remainder are not claimed. This statement concerns fixed SNR
after the dimension limit and does not contradict the existing finite-n
counterexample on an SNR interval shrinking with dimension.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:686964a520b560babff49b2d3c712ffe188ecb5df9287b91721884bf39c60f66","revision_digest":"sha256:dbc2109a02b1bca692e4d6c35194e860836da22ede9d76fed8f8cfbddcd756dd","source_id":"owner:w718:T287:gaussian-product-near-square-mi-c1-mmse-w718","source_revision":"2026-10-21 claim w718-T287-022 version1, proof unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2604.15152, 'The Multinomial Allocation Model and the Random Box Load'] Define
\[\Phi_n(r,t)=\binom{n}{r,t,n-r-t}
\Big(
 \rE\!\left[q_X^r q_Y^t (1-q_X-q_Y)_+^{\,n-r-t}\right]
- N^{-1} \rE\!\left[q_X^{r+t}(1-2q_X)_+^{\,n-r-t}\right]\Big)-\rE[\hat q_r]\rE[\hat q_t],\]
where $q_Y$ is an independent copy of $q_X$, and $(a)_+ := \max(a,0)$. 
Then for all $r \ne t$, 
\begin{align*}
\rE[\hat q_r]
&= \binom{n}{r}\, \rE\!\left[q_X^r (1-q_X)^{n-r}\right],\qquad
\rV[\hat q_r]
= \Phi_n(r,r)+N^{-1}\rE[\hat q_r],\qquad
\rC[\hat q_r ,\hat q_t]= \Phi_n(r,t).
\end{align*}
title: Lemma 4 of arXiv:2604.15152

[Lemma Generic Morse property of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[lemma]{lem:Morse}
For fixed \(N,p\), the set of coefficient tensors for which the restriction of \(H_N\) to \(\mathbb S_N\) is not Morse is contained in a proper real algebraic subset of \(\mathbb R^{N^p}\).  Consequently, if the joint coefficient law is absolutely continuous, the field is almost surely Morse.
The same conclusion holds when the coefficient law is absolutely
continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on the space of symmetric
degree-\(p\) tensors.

[Proposition 7 (Conditional unique limit at infinite time) of arXiv:2609.00501, 'Uniqueness of Finite-Time Varifold Limits for the M\"obius-Invariant Willmore Flow'] Let $F\colon[0,\infty)\times\Sigma\to\Sph^3$ be a smooth MIWF of a
compact torus.  Assume that there is one constant $c_0>0$ such that
\[
 \inf_{t>0}\min_{x\in\Sigma}|A_{F_t}^0(x)|^2\geq c_0,
\]
and, in addition, that
\begin{equation}
 
 \int_0^\infty\sqrt{-W'(r)}\dd r<\infty.
\end{equation}
Then there are positive Radon measures $\mu_\infty$ on $\Sigma$ and
$\lambda_\infty$ on $\Sph^3$ and a unique integral two-varifold
$\Var_\infty$ in $\R^4$, possibly the zero varifold, such that
\[
 \mu_t\longrightarrow\mu_\infty\quad\text{in total variation},
 \qquad
 \lambda_t\longrightarrow\lambda_\infty
 \quad\text{in }d_{\BL},
 \qquad
 \Var_t\rightharpoonup\Var_\infty
\]
as $t\to\infty$, and $\lambda_\infty=\lVert\Var_\infty\rVert$.
Writing $W_\infty:=\lim_{t\to\infty}W(t)$, one also has
\[
 H_{\Var_\infty}^{\R^4}
 \in L^2(\lVert\Var_\infty\rVert;\R^4),
 \qquad
 \frac14\int_{\R^4}|H_{\Var_\infty}^{\R^4}|^2
 \dd\lVert\Var_\infty\rVert\leq W_\infty.
\]
title: Conditional unique limit at infinite time

[Definition Costly steps of arXiv:2510.26724, 'Sharp Fuss-Catalan thresholds in graph bootstrap percolation'] The $i$th step of the REA is called a {\it costly step} 
if it is neither a TS nor an IntR. 
The associated {\it cost} $\kappa_i$ to the step 
is $r=v(H)$ plus the number of vertices 
(if any) 
outside $H_i$
that are in at least 
two of the components being merged
with $H_i$. 
If the $i$th step is not costly (i.e., TS or IntR)
then we 
put $\kappa_i=0$. 
The {\it total cost} of $W$ is 
\[
\kappa(W)=\sum_{i=1}^m \kappa_i. 
\]
title: Costly steps

[Conjecture conj:threshold of arXiv:2601.05361, 'Noise sensitivity in last-passage percolation'] Consider planar last-passage percolation with geometric weights. The transition from stability to noise sensitivity occurs at $t\asymp n^{-1/3}$ in the sense that, as $n\to\infty$,
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item for $t\ll n^{-1/3}$ we have $\Corr \big(T_n(\omega), T_n(\tilde\omega^t) \big)=1-o(1)$;
    \item for $t\gg n^{-1/3}$ we have $\Corr \big(T_n(\omega), T_n(\tilde\omega^t) \big)=o(1)$.
    \end{enumerate} (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Conjecture conj:threshold of arXiv:2601.05361

[Lemma 24 (Many macroscopic children) of arXiv:2604.25877, 'Asymptotic height of Plancherel random trees'] Let $\theta>0$ and $m:=n-1$. Fix any $\delta\in(0,1)$ and set
\[
J:=\left\{\left\lceil m^{1-\delta}\right\rceil,\dots,\left\lfloor
    m^{1-\delta/2}\right\rfloor\right\},
\qquad
\widetilde N_0:=\sum_{j\in J} C_j,
\]
where $C_j$ is the number of parts of size $j$ in an $\mathrm{Ewens}(m,\theta)$ partition.
Then $\widetilde N_0\to\infty$ in probability as $m\to\infty$. In particular,
$N_0\to\infty$ in probability.

We say that the $\mathfrak{G}$-orbit of $\boldsymbol{v}$ is bipartite if there exists a function $\epsilon : \mathfrak{G}.\boldsymbol{v} \rightarrow \{\pm 1\}$ such that $\epsilon(T^{(h)}(\boldsymbol{w})) = - \epsilon(\boldsymbol{w})$ for any $\boldsymbol{w} \in \mathfrak{G}.\boldsymbol{v}$ and $h \in [H]$.

body:
[Lemma h11A-lem of arXiv:2608.30747, 'Compact homogeneous complex manifolds'] $\sigma=\sigma_\ag+\sigma_\qg\in\Ker\partial\overline{\partial}|_{\Lambda_T^{1,1}}$ if and only if 
\begin{enumerate}[{\rm (i)}] 
\item $h|_{\underline{\ag}_f\times\underline{\ag}_f}=0$.  

\item $h|_{\overline{\ag}\times\overline{\ag}}=-(z_{u+1}\kil_{\ggo_{u+1}}+\dots+z_s\kil_{\ggo_s})|_{\overline{\ag}\times\overline{\ag}}$, for some $z_{u+1},\dots,z_s\in\RR$. 

\item $x_{\alpha+\beta}=x_\alpha+x_\beta-z_i$, for all $\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta\in\Delta_{\qg_i}^+$ and $i=1,\dots,s$, where we set $z_1=\dots=z_u=0$. 
\end{enumerate}
In particular, 
$$
\dim{\Ker\partial\overline{\partial}|_{\Lambda_T^{1,1}}}=\dim{\zg(\hg_f)}+\dim{S}, 
$$ 
where $S$ is the subspace of all symmetric bilinear forms $h:\ag\times\ag\rightarrow\RR$ such that $h$ is compatible with $J_\ag$ and satisfies conditions (i) and (ii). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2608.27249, 'Torus actions, almost non-negative curvature and fundamental groups'] Let \(M\) be a connected manifold on which a torus \(T\) acts.
  Assume there is a point \(x\in M\) whose isotropy group \(T_x\) is finite.
  Then a subgroup of index \(|T_x|<\infty\) of the fundamental group of the orbit \(Tx\) of \(x\) acts trivially on \(\pi_2(M)\).

body:
[Lem lem for 4.1 of arXiv:2505.11700, 'Distribution of the cokernels of determinantal row-sparse matrices'] Let $\{a_n\}$ and $\{b_n\}$ be sequences of positive integers and $c$ be a real number.  
Suppose that 
$$
\lim_{n \to \infty}\frac{a_n b_n}{n} = 0. 
$$
Then
$$
\left(n + ca_n \right)^{b_n} - n^{b_n} = O\left( n^{b_n-1}a_nb_n \right). 
$$
title: Lem lem for 4.1 of arXiv:2505.11700
Hoffman exponential

[Proposition 36 of arXiv:2606.14564, 'Upper tails for irregular graphs \\ beyond the mean-field regime'] Suppose that  $(J_0, J)$ is an optimal pair and let $d \coloneqq \dim_{J_0}J$.
  There are $J_1, \dotsc, J_d \in \cJ^*$ such that $J_1 \cup \dotsb \cup J_d = J$, $\dim_{J_0} J_i = 1$ for each $i \in \br{d}$, and $J_i \cap J_j = J_0$ for all distinct $i, j \in \br{d}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Thm rehyp of arXiv:2609.03033, 'An Overview of Einstein $4$-Manifolds'] Let $M^4$ be a smooth compact isometric quotient of 
hyperbolic 4-space ${\cal H}^4=SO_+(4,1)/SO(4)$,
 and let $g_0$ be its tautological  metric of constant sectional curvature. 
 Then the moduli space $\mathscr{E}(M)$ of Einstein metrics
 on $M$ consists of a single point, represented by $g_0$. 
That is, 
every Einstein metric $g$  on $M$   is of the form 
$g=\Psi^*(cg_0)$ for  some self-diffeomorphism  $\Psi$ of $M$ and some positive constant 
   $c$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem thm:IS6V-diamond of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] Suppose that $K_u$ is trace class and that
$(I + K_u)^{-1}$ exists at all relevant lattice
vertices.  Then for any two distinct divisors
$p, p' \mid \Pi_{x,y}$ with
$1 \leq \deg p, \deg p' < \deg \Pi_{x,y}$,
the dressed edge weights
satisfy the mixed diamond equation
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{M}_p(u) \Lambda_{p'}
+
\Lambda_p \mathcal{M}_{p'}(S_p u)
-
\mathcal{M}_{p'}(u) \Lambda_p
-
\Lambda_{p'} \mathcal{M}_p(S_{p'} u)
= 0.
\end{equation}

body:
[Theorem main representable of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Suppose $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Z}$ are smooth separated Deligne--Mumford stacks of dimension $n$, and there is a representable contraction $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Z}$ where the exceptional $\mathcal{E}$ is a smooth irreducible Cartier divisor. 
    Moreover, suppose there is a smooth closed irreducible Deligne--Mumford substack $\mathcal{Y} \subseteq \mathcal{Z}$ such that $(f^{-1}\mathcal{Y}) \simeq \mathcal{E}$ set-theoretically, and $f : \mathcal{X} \setminus \mathcal{E} \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathcal{Z} \setminus \mathcal{Y}.$    
    Then $f$ is an ordinary blowup of $\mathcal{Z}$ along smooth center $\mathcal{Y}$. In particular, $f|_{\mathcal{E}} : \mathcal{E} \to \mathcal{Y}$ is a projective bundle, and $\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{X}}(\mathcal{E})|_{\mathcal{E}} \simeq \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{E}}(-1) \otimes f^*\mathcal{L}$ for some line bundle $\mathcal{L}$ on $\mathcal{Y}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem main representable of arXiv:2609.04023

[Theorem 31 of arXiv:2608.25785, 'Proper Actions on Homogeneous Spaces of the Upper Triangular Matrix Group via Coarse Geome'] Fix $n\in \Z_{\geq 1}$.
    Then the following holds:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item For each $\lambda\in \Lambda_1(n)$, the map $\mu_{\lambda}$ is controlled.
        Here, $\rmB(n)$ is equipped with the LR-coarse structure and $\R^{\{\lambda\}}\cong \R$ is equipped with the bounded coarse structure (see Example \ref{example:coarse}).
        \item The map $\mu_0$ is coarse.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 31 of arXiv:2608.25785

[Proposition prop:no-reappearance-old-shapes of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] Suppose a shape \(\sigma\) is first added to the ground set \(\mathcal{B}(Q_i)\) at
iteration level \(i\). Then \(\sigma\) does not appear in any subsequent update:
for every \(j\ge i\),
\[
    \sigma \notin \mathcal{B}(Q_{j+1})\setminus \mathcal{B}(Q_j).
\]
Consequently, the coefficient of \(\sigma\) remains unchanged throughout all
later iterations.

body:
[Theorem 34 (Finite spectral reduction) of arXiv:2608.15805, 'Spectral duality structures and the Fisher--Rao geometry of reset distributions'] The reduction space, \emph{in symmetrised coordinates}, is exactly
the odd sector:
\begin{equation}
\widetilde V:=D^{-1}V = E_{\mathrm{odd}},
\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
V = D\,E_{\mathrm{odd}} .

\end{equation}
The distinction matters: $D$ does not commute with $S$ unless
$p=q$, so $D\,E_{\mathrm{odd}}\neq E_{\mathrm{odd}}$ for a biased
walk --- consistently with the fact, noted above, that it is
$\widetilde\psi$ and not $\psi$ that is antisymmetric. The space
admits the canonical decomposition
\begin{equation}
\psi(\gamma)=\sum_{k\ \mathrm{even}} f_k(\gamma)\,\mathbf m_k,
\qquad
\mathbf m_k := D\,P_k\,D^{-1}\xi = D\,P_k\,\widetilde\xi,
\qquad
f_k(\gamma)=\frac{t}{1-\lambda_k t},
\quad t=1-\gamma .

\end{equation}
The directions $\mathbf m_k$ are nonzero and linearly independent.
As for canonicity, the symmetrised directions $P_k\widetilde\xi$ are
determined by $(\widetilde P,S,\widetilde\xi)$; their
original-coordinate images are determined by $(P,S,\xi)$ alone. For
the present irreducible tridiagonal $P$ the positive diagonal
symmetriser is unique up to an overall scalar --- the ratios
$D_{z+1}/D_z$ being fixed by the neighbour relations --- and the
conjugation $D P_k D^{-1}$ is unchanged under $D\mapsto cD$; so no
normalisation of the symmetriser need be fixed. In particular $\dim V = r$, and all $\gamma$-dependence is
carried by the elementary scalars $f_k$.

The notation is deliberate: these $\mathbf m_k$ are \emph{not} the
normal directions $\mathbf n_\nu$ of Section~\ref{sec:finite-reduction}.
There are $N$ of the latter, one per spectral mode, spanning a space
of dimension $r$ and therefore dependent; there are exactly $r$ of the
former, indexed by the even $k$ alone, and they are independent. Both
families span $V$, which is all the two routes are claimed to share.

body: Load-bearing hypothesis: 'the solution at (t,x) depends only on the data on the sphere ∂B(x,t)', i.e. sharp propagation on the light cone with no tail, holds only in odd space dimensions n ≥ 3. Finite speed of propagation (support in {|x| ≤ t + R}) holds in every dimension; the sharp inner edge does not. Counterexample n = 1: with u0 = 0 and u1 = 1_{[−1,1]}, d'Alembert's formula gives u(t,x) = (1/2)∫_{x−t}^{x+t} u1, so u(t,0) = 1 for every t ≥ 1 — the disturbance never leaves the origin. Counterexample n = 2: with u0 = 0 and u1 = 1_{B(0,1)}, Poisson's formula gives u(t,0) = (1/2π)∫_{|y|<1} (t² − |y|²)^{−1/2} dy > 0 for every t > 1 — a decaying tail behind the wavefront (this is why a splash on a pond is felt long after the front passes, while a sound pulse in three dimensions is heard once). Practical consequence: statements like 'the data inside B(x,t) do not matter' or 'the solution vanishes after the front passes' are valid only for odd n ≥ 3, and any argument that tacitly extends them to n = 1, 2 or to even dimensions (or to variable-coefficient / curved-background wave equations, where strong Huygens generally fails even in odd dimensions) is unsound.
title: Pitfall: Strong Huygens' Principle Needs Odd Dimension n ≥ 3

body:
[Lemma lemstable of arXiv:2607.12459, 'Renormalisation of Inhomogeneous Random Graphs'] {\bf [Invariance property for positive stable weights]}

Let $\gamma\in(0,1)$, and let $Y_1,\ldots,Y_m$ be i.i.d.\ standard positive $\gamma$-stable random variables, with Laplace transform
\[
\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda Y_1}] = \mathrm{e}^{-\lambda^\gamma}, \qquad \lambda\geq 0.
\]
Then
\[ 
m^{-1/\gamma}\sum_{i=1}^mY_i \stackrel{d}{=}Y_1.
\]
Consequently, for every $\delta\in(0,\infty)$ and $\eta\in[0,\infty)$, the inhomogeneous random graph with connection functions
\[
g^{\neq}_\delta(x,y)=\delta xy, \qquad g^{=}_\eta(x)=\eta x,
\]
and i.i.d.\ standard positive $\gamma$-stable weights is invariant in distribution under the renormalisation transformation, provided the aggregated weights are rescaled by $m^{-1/\gamma}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lemstable of arXiv:2607.12459

[Corollary 4 (Fixed-horizon first-order accuracy) of arXiv:2608.19762, '2608.19762'] Consider the scaled perturbation $\alpha\xi_t$ and a fixed horizon $H$.
Suppose that, in a neighborhood of the control trajectory,
$D\psi_t$ and $D\widetilde f_s$ are locally Lipschitz,
the finite-horizon propagators are uniformly bounded,
the probe objectives have locally Lipschitz gradients, and the switching
defects satisfy
\[
    \|r_s^{\mathrm{sw}}\|
    \leq
    C_s^{\mathrm{sw}}
    \|\delta x_s\|^2,
    ~~
    1\leq s-t<H.
\]
Then, for every $1\leq h\leq H$,
\[
    \delta F_{t+h}(\alpha)
    =
    \alpha
    c_{t+h}^{\top}
    \Phi_{t+h,t+1}
    B_t\xi_t
    +
    O(\alpha^2),
    ~~
    \alpha\rightarrow0.
\]
The $O(\alpha^2)$ constant may depend on the fixed horizon and control
trajectory but not on $\alpha$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Fixed-horizon first-order accuracy

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Controlled generators, exact finite-state diagnostic, coupling, renewal reward or capacity comparison Result: A single idle-gap diagnostic is exact: for next-arrival gap G~Exp(Lambda), the chance the server becomes cold is exp(-Lambda*gamma), and expected on-idle duration is E[min(G,gamma)]=(1-exp(-Lambda*gamma))/Lambda. If a cold arrival triggers deterministic setup beta, that arrival incurs beta*exp(-Lambda*gamma) expected setup delay. The local marginal tradeoff follows by differentiation, but a full renewal cycle also includes later arrivals during setup, active service and possible setup cancellation. Check: Integrate P(G>t)=exp(-Lambda*t) over [0,gamma]. Separately condition on G>gamma for the cold-arrival delay. Both formulas have correct gamma=0 and gamma->infinity limits. Obstruction: The idle-gap calculation is not a stationary many-server mean or a globally optimal grace period.

Own-work draft, proof (unaudited), T280-w716-C11 v2, kind special, Target 3. For every compact nontrivial interval J, probability scale law mu supported on J with mu>=ell Lebesgue on all of J (ell>0), fixed k>=1 and q in (0,1), there are T,d0,eps>0 independent of d and of the unit-norm degree<=k polynomial target such that every d>=d0 ordinary all-parameter population exponential mean-field flow on uniform S^(d-1), initially within coupled essential-sup distance eps in (a,b,p=w/sqrt(d)) of (0,0,gamma*u), gamma~mu and u known, has full residual energy <=q by T. The continuous frozen-scale reference is uniformly bounded on every finite horizon: I(a)=<integrated residual,exp(gamma Z)> and integral c(a)I(a) controls coefficient L1 norm; positive interval density converts reciprocal Gaussian-tail growth into a uniform pointwise bound. Explicit continuation and O(1/d) full-flow transfer constants are given. Write I(a)=integral_0^a exp(-s^2/2)ds, S=I(infinity), c(a)=a exp(a^2/2). In the frozen-scale zero-start reference v(gamma)=I(a_gamma)=<h_t,exp(gamma Z)>, h_t=-integral r_s ds. The exact nonnegative identity integral c(a)I(a)dmu=<h_t,f_t> bounds integral |c(a)|. The transformed variable v is uniformly Lipschitz on the compact scale interval. For |a|>=1, |c(a)|>=exp(-3/2)/(S-|v|). A one-sided interval-density integral then forces a positive gap from |v|=S. This supplies the pointwise bound absent from an averaged potential alone; comparison to the reference gives original-clock full-flow error O(1/d). The prepared axis remains assumed. No general law outside the lower-density interval, rotational direction learning, fixed-joint-objective phase separation, novelty, independent audit or Lean certificate is claimed.

Entire initial scale law supported on one compact interval J with a positive Lebesgue density lower bound on that whole interval; atoms within J allowed
Zero output/bias reference; arbitrary sufficiently small coupled measurable perturbations, including nonzero signed output weights and biases and off-axis first-layer weights, are covered
C8 static approximation and C6 operator derivative estimates used as unaudited dependencies; their proofs remain part of the review chain

[Lemma 42 (Sublevel regular neighborhoods) of arXiv:2609.02267, 'Locally Conformally Flat Manifolds with Positive Scalar Curvature: Kleinian Groups, Moduli'] Let $T$ be a finite triangulation of the fixed PL sphere $S^n$, let $L$
be a nonempty, proper, full subcomplex of $T$, and let
$f_L:|T|\to[0,1]$ be the simplicial map that takes value $0$ at the
vertices of $L$ and value $1$ at all other vertices.  Then
$f_L^{-1}(0)=|L|$.  Define the simplicial complement of $L$ in $T$ by
$C(L,T):=\{\Delta\in T:|\Delta|\cap|L|=\varnothing\}$.
Then $C(L,T)$ is a nonempty, proper, full subcomplex of $T$, and its
$0$--$1$-level function is $f_{C(L,T)}=1-f_L$.  Moreover, for every
$c\in(0,1)$, the set $N_c:=f_L^{-1}([0,c])$
is a closed regular neighborhood of $|L|$ in $S^n$ and a compact PL
$n$-manifold, with $\partial N_c=f_L^{-1}(c)$.  Its topological
interior in $S^n$ is $\operatorname{int}N_c=f_L^{-1}([0,c))$.
There is also a homeomorphism of pairs
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_c:
 \bigl(N_c\setminus|L|,\partial N_c\bigr)
 \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }
 \bigl(\partial N_c\times(0,1],
       \partial N_c\times\{1\}\bigr)
\end{equation}
whose restriction to $\partial N_c$ is $z\mapsto(z,1)$.  Consequently,
$\partial N_c$ is a strong deformation retract of $N_c\setminus|L|$.

[Lemma 23 ({Fenchel conjugate formula for singular-value functions}) of arXiv:2608.26288, 'Muon with Finite Newton--Schulz: The Smoothing Benefit in Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization'] Let $\phi\colon[0,\infty)\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper and convex, and write $\phi^*(a)\coloneqq\sup_{x\geq0}\{ax-\phi(x)\}$.
Then the Fenchel conjugate of $S\mapsto\sum_{i=1}^r\phi(\sigma_i(S))$ is $W\mapsto\sum_{i=1}^r\phi^*(\sigma_i(W))$.

[Thm 3 of arXiv:2608.21090, 'Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process conditioned to have restricted $L_2$-norm'] Let $0<\theta<\frac{1}{2\gamma}$. Then, for any $\delta\in(0,1)$, $\beta\in(0,\frac12)$ and $K>0$, there exists a $T_{\delta,\beta,K}>0$, such that for all $T\geq T_{\delta,\beta,K}$ and any $x\in\R$, $y>0$ with
    \[\abs x\abs\leq T^{\beta/2}\quad\text{and}\quad \left|y-\theta T\right|\leq K\,T^\beta\]
    it holds
    \begin{equation*}
        (1-\delta)\,C_\theta\,A(T)\leq\P_x(Z_T\leq y)\leq (1+\delta)\,C_\theta\,A(T),
    \end{equation*}
    with
    \[C_{\theta}:=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi}}\frac{4\sqrt{\theta}}{\left(1+2\gamma\theta\right)^{3/2}\left(1-2\gamma\theta\right)},\]
    and
    \[A(T):=T^{-1/2}\,\exp\left(-\frac{1}{8\frac{y}{T}}\left(1-2\gamma \frac{y}{T}\right)^2T-\frac{x^2}{4\theta}\left(1-2\gamma\theta\right)\right).\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 3 of arXiv:2608.21090

[Thm th:wp of arXiv:2603.29711, 'Strong Feller property, irreducibility,\\ and uniqueness of the invariant measure\\ for st'] Let $\alpha\geq2$, $\beta\geq1$,
    $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, 
    $\sigma\in[0,\frac12)\cap[\frac d4-\frac12, \frac12)$,
    and $\delta>\frac d4+\sigma$.
    Assume also that:
    \begin{itemize}
  \item if $\sigma\in\left(\frac d4, \frac12\right)$, then $\gamma\in[1,+\infty)$;
  \item if $\sigma=\frac d4$, then 
  $\gamma\in[1,+\infty)$, with also
  $\alpha>2$ if $\gamma>\alpha+\beta$;
  \item if $\sigma\in[0,\frac d4)$, then 
  $\gamma\in\left[1,\frac{\alpha - 8 \sigma/d}{1- 4\sigma/d}\right]
  \cup
  \left[1,\min \left\{\alpha+ \beta, 
    \frac{\alpha - 8 \sigma/d +4\beta\sigma/d}{1- 4\sigma/d} 
    \right\}\right]$.
\end{itemize}
    Then, for every 
$x$ satisfying (equation init of the paper), there exists 
a unique variational solution $X^x$ to
(equation eq_ast of the paper), in the sense of Definition~(def_sol of the paper), and
it holds, for every $T>0$ and $\ell\geq2$, that
\begin{align*}
  &X^x\in L^\ell_\mathscr{P}(\Omega; C([0,T]; H)\cap L^2(0,T; V)),\\
  &\Psi_\gamma(X^x(t))\in L^\ell(\Omega;L^1(\mathcal O))\quad\forall\,t\in[0,T].
\end{align*}
Moreover, for every $T>0$ and $\ell\geq2$,
there exists a constant $C>0$, only depending on
$\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta,\sigma,\ell,T$,
such that for every 
$x_1,x_2$ satisfying (equation init of the paper), it holds that
\[
  \norm{X^{x_1}-X^{x_2}}_{L^\ell_\mathscr{P}(\Omega; C^0([0,T]; H)\cap L^2(0,T; V))}
  \leq C\norm{x_1-x_2}_H.
\]
Eventually, when $d=1$,
if $\gamma\geq\beta$ it holds for every 
$\xi\in[0,\frac12)$ that
\[
X^x\in L^\ell_\mathscr{P}(\Omega; C([0,T]; V_{2\xi}))
  \quad\text{if } x\in V_{2\xi},
\]
while if $\gamma\geq2\beta$ it further holds
for every $\xi\in[\sigma,\frac12+\sigma)$ that
\[
X^x\in L^\ell_\mathscr{P}(\Omega; C([0,T]; V_{2\xi})\cap 
L^2(0,T; V_{2\sigma+1}))
  \quad\text{if } x\in V_{2\xi}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Differentiate the magnetisation lace expansion at the critical point. Result: The bounded-ratio statement beta = 1 follows from the triangle condition via the Barsky-Aizenman differential inequality dtheta/dp >= c theta - C theta^2 together with the mean-field upper bound; an asymptotic statement needs the limit of theta(p)/(p - p_c), i.e. a differentiable extension of theta at p_c from the right with a computable derivative. With the magnetisation M(p,h) (ghost field h), the lace expansion for the two-point function gives an expansion of the susceptibility chi(p,h) = dM/dh whose coefficients are analytic in p near p_c for fixed h > 0; theta(p) = M(p,0+) is the h -> 0 limit, and the interchange of the h -> 0 and p -> p_c limits is exactly where asymptotic control is lost: the expansion converges uniformly for h >= h_0 > 0 but the coefficients' h-dependence near h = 0 is only bounded, not differentiable. A candidate route: the scaling relation beta = gamma - Delta with gamma = 1 asymptotically (Hara-Slade) and Delta = 2 asymptotically (gap exponent, known asymptotically in the sense of the ratio only) would give beta = 1 asymptotically if the gap exponent were known asymptotically; I checked that the gap exponent's asymptotic form is equivalent to the asymptotic form of the ratio M_3/M_2^2 ... in the source's notation, which is itself not derived. Reduction: asymptotic beta = 1 <=> asymptotic gap exponent Delta = 2 via the magnetisation differential inequality with sharp constant. Obstruction: The h -> 0 and p -> p_c limits do not commute in the lace expansion; the sharp constant in the gap-exponent inequality is missing.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0063-critical-exponent-beta-1-in-the-asymptotic-sense-for-high-dimensional

[Proposition proposition duality of arXiv:2412.05064, '\textbf{Sample path central limit theorem for the occupation time of the voter model on a '] For any integer $m\geq 1$, $y_1, y_2,\ldots, y_m\in \mathbb{Z}^d$, $0\leq t_1\leq t_2\leq \ldots\leq t_m$, $\eta\in \{0, 1\}^{\mathbb{Z}^d}$ and function $G$ from $\{0, 1\}^m$ to $\mathbb{R}$, we have
\begin{align}
&\mathbb{E}_\eta G\left(\eta_{t_1}(y_1), \eta_{t_2}(y_2),\ldots, \eta_{t_m}(y_m)\right)\\
&=\hat{\mathbb{E}}G\left(\eta\left(\mathcal{X}_{t_m, m}^{x_m, s_m}\right), \eta\left(\mathcal{X}_{t_m, m-1}^{x_{m-1}, s_{m-1}}\right),\ldots, \eta\left(\mathcal{X}_{t_m, 2}^{x_2, s_2}\right), \eta\left(\mathcal{X}_{t_m, 1}^{x_1, s_1}\right)\right),\notag
\end{align}
where
\[
\left(x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_m\right)=\left(y_m, y_{m-1},\ldots,y_1\right)
\]
and
\[
\left(s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_m\right)=\left(t_m-t_m, t_m-t_{m-1}, \ldots, t_m-t_2, t_m-t_1\right).
\]
Consequently, for given $0<p<1$,
\begin{align}
&\mathbb{E}_{\nu_p} G\left(\eta_{t_1}(y_1), \eta_{t_2}(y_2),\ldots, \eta_{t_m}(y_m)\right)\\
&=\int_{\{0, 1\}^{\mathbb{Z}^d}}\left(\hat{\mathbb{E}}G\left(\eta\left(\mathcal{X}_{t_m, m}^{x_m, s_m}\right), \eta\left(\mathcal{X}_{t_m, m-1}^{x_{m-1}, s_{m-1}}\right),\ldots, \eta\left(\mathcal{X}_{t_m, 2}^{x_2, s_2}\right), \eta\left(\mathcal{X}_{t_m, 1}^{x_1, s_1}\right)\right)\right)\nu_p(d\eta).\notag
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition proposition duality of arXiv:2412.05064

[Defi 25 of arXiv:2608.02103, '$p$-Adic Diffusion and Random Walks on $[0,1]$'] Let $A_n$ as in (\ref{partition}) be the $n$-regular partition of the unit interval $[0,1]$. For a given kernel function $w\in L^1([0,1]\times[0,1])$, define the average transition-rate matrix $W_n^a$ attached to the pair $(A_n,w) $ as
\[ 
w^{(n),a}_{I,J}:=[W_n^a]_{I,J}= \frac{1}{n^{2}}\int_{I\times J}w(x,y) dxdy,
\]
\begin{comment}
and
\[
w^{(n),a}_{J,I}:=[W_n^a]_{J,I}=\frac{1}{n^{2}}\int_{I\times J}w(y,x) dxdy
\]
\end{comment}
for $I,J\in A_n$.
The function defined by 
\[w_n^a(x,y):=\sum_{I,J\in A_n}w_{I,J}^{(n),a}\chi_{I}(x)\chi_J(y),\]
is called the \emph{$n$-th step average kernel} attached to the pair $(A_n,w)$. \newline

\begin{comment}
We define the sample rate-transition matrix $W_n^s$ attached to the pair $(A_n,w)$ by
\[w_{I,J}^s:=[W_n^s]_{I,J}=w(x_I,y_J)\]
and 
\[w_{J,I}^s:=[W_n^s]_{J,I}=w(y_J,x_I),\]
where $x_I\in I$, $y_J\in J$ are elements of $\mathcal{S}$. The function \[w_n^s(x|y):=\sum_{I,J\in A_n}w_{I,J}^{(n),s}\chi_{I}(x)\chi_J(y),\]
is the $n$-step sample kernel attached to the pair $(A_n,w)$. 
\end{comment}

[Lemma lem:soft-active-clustering of arXiv:2606.19763, 'Optimal Sparsification of Gaussian Processes'] Suppose $T \sse \R^n$ is finite and non-empty and let $\eps > 0$. 
	Additionally suppose $S \sse \R^n$ and the map $\Pi : T \to S$ satisfies $\|t - \Pi(t)\|_2 \leq \eps$ for every $t\in T$. 
	For $t \in T$ and $\theta \in [0,1]$, define 
	\[
		u_t := t - \Pi(t) 
		\qquad\text{and}\qquad 
		v_t(\theta) := t - \theta u_t\,. 
	\]
	Finally, fix $\beta > 0$. 
	Then there exist absolutely continuous functions $a_t : [0,1] \to \R$ with $a_t(0) = 0$ such that the softmax function $H_\theta : \R^n \to \R$ defined as 
	\begin{equation}

LASSO ((eq:matrix-lasso of the paper)) with linear map $\mathcal{A}$ and noiseless
measurements $b=\mathcal{A}(X_{\star})$ admits a unique solution $X_{\lambda,r}$
with a common SVD as the ground truth
\[
X_{\star}=U\operatorname{diag}(x_{\star})V^{T},\quad X_{\lambda,r}=U\operatorname{diag}(x_{\lambda,r})V^{T}
\]
where $U\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{1}\times d}$ and $V\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{2}\times d}$ have
orthonormal columns. Define the matrix $A$ by 
\[
Ax=\mathcal{A}\!\left(U\operatorname{diag}(x)V^{T}\right),\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}.
\]
Then $Ax_{\star}=b$ and $\normtwo{x_{\star}}=\normF{X_{\star}}$,
and the sparsity-restricted vector LASSO ((eq:vector-lasso of the paper))
with linear map $A$, and measurements $b$ has unique solution $x_{\lambda,r}$
satisfying $\normtwo{x_{\lambda,r}-x_{\star}}=\normF{X_{\lambda,r}-X_{\star}}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Method for the bounded-density-of-a-quadratic-form conjecture. Write the density by Fourier inversion p(y)=(1/2pi) integral e^{-ity} phi(t) dt with phi(t)=E[e^{itQ(X)}] the characteristic function; then ||p||_inf <= (1/2pi) integral |phi(t)| dt, so a bounded density follows from an L^1 bound on phi. phi(t) is an oscillatory integral integral e^{it Q(x)} prod f(x_i) dx with quadratic phase Q. Per large-eigenvalue direction, van der Corput / stationary phase gives decay |t lambda_j|^{-1/2} uniformly over amplitudes with density <=1 (since x^2 has nonvanishing second derivative); three eigenvalues with |lambda_j|>=1 give |phi(t)| <~ min(1,|t|^{-3/2}), which is integrable at infinity -> bounded density. The coupling between eigen-directions and the coordinate variables (Q not diagonal in the X_i) and degenerate phases are handled by resolution of singularities / Newton polyhedra (Varchenko oscillatory-integral asymptotics; the x^2-y^3 cusp is the model degenerate case), and Bai-Yin controls the eigenvalue configuration. The squaring/decoupling identity |phi(t)|^2=E_{X,X'}[e^{it(Q(X)-Q(X'))}] lowers the smoothness demanded of the densities. Related area: anti-concentration and local limit theorems for quadratic forms (Costello-Tao-Vu, Nguyen-Vu, Rudelson-Vershynin, Gotze-Sudakov-Tikhomirov).
title: Method for the bounded-density-of-a-quadratic-form conjecture. Write the density by Fourier inversion p(y)=(1/2pi) integral e^{-ity} phi(t)

For every n>=2 and fixed b_i,k_i>0, 0<a_i<b_i, let shared scalar v,p minimize average logistic loss on signed margins v[a_i+b_i tanh(k_i p)]. For EVERY fixed eta>0, the open regions v>0,p>max_i p_i* and v<0,p<min_i p_i*, p_i*=atanh(-a_i/b_i)/k_i, are forward invariant; their GD trajectories escape to matching-sign infinity, with p/v->0 and loss->0. Limiting normalized minimum margins are respectively min_i(a_i+b_i) and min_i(b_i-a_i), with the latter strictly smaller than the attainable global supremum min_i(a_i+b_i). Thus an open positive-measure suboptimal joint basin persists for arbitrarily many distinct examples. The family embeds exactly in scalar cross-attention with arbitrary labels y_i, fixed tokens y_i(a_i+-b_i), and fixed queries y_i k_i/b_i; it includes a distinct two-example mixed-label witness. The same open-region conclusions hold for gradient flow. Define the joint normalized minimum margin as lim_t min_i v_t h_i(p_t)/sqrt(v_t^2+p_t^2). Q_-= {v<0,p<min_i atanh(-a_i/b_i)/k_i} is a sufficient open region inside the inferior basin. Full-plane classification is not asserted here.
Shared scalar head and unfactored scalar attention weight; fixed scalar cross-attention data and queries; average logistic loss; simultaneous Euclidean GD; any positive constant eta. Global basin exhaustion is not claimed.

# Target 1 extension: arbitrarily many distinct examples, jointly trained head and attention

Version 1, proof unaudited. Literature comparison was completed in LITERATURE_STATUS.md before this extension. The hardest remaining piece is the basin classification for general coupled, multidimensional data; the theorem below supplies an infinite family of coupled multi-example obstructions, not that classification.

## Theorem

Let n>=2, b_i,k_i>0, and 0<a_i<b_i for i=1,...,n. Define h_i(p)=a_i+b_i tanh(k_i p) and signed margins m_i(v,p)=v h_i(p). Train the SAME scalar head v and SAME scalar attention parameter p on all examples, using

  L(v,p)=(1/n) sum_i log(1+exp(-m_i(v,p))).

For every fixed eta>0, ordinary simultaneous Euclidean GD has two forward-invariant open regions

  Q_+={v>0, p>max_i p_i*},
  Q_-={v<0, p<min_i p_i*},
  p_i*=atanh(-a_i/b_i)/k_i.

Every orbit initialized in Q_+ has v,p->+infinity and p/v->0. Every orbit initialized in Q_- has v,p->-infinity and p/v->0. Both have L->0. Their asymptotic joint normalized minimum margins are respectively

  Gamma_+=min_i(a_i+b_i),   Gamma_-=min_i(b_i-a_i).

The global supremum attainable asymptotic joint normalized minimum margin is Gamma_+, and Gamma_-<Gamma_+. Thus Q_- is a nonempty open positive-measure set of strictly suboptimal joint token-selection initializations, for every positive fixed step size. Any initialization law with positive density on all of R^2 assigns it positive probability. This theorem also holds for Euclidean gradient flow on the same loss.

No claim is made that Q_+ and Q_- exhaust the full basins. In particular, this multi-example theorem does not classify every finite critical point or every initialization. It proves robust suboptimal escaping selections on a whole parameter family and arbitrary sample counts.

## Exact scalar cross-attention embedding, with both labels

Choose ANY labels y_i in {+1,-1}, including both signs, fixed scalar token pairs

  x_i1=y_i(a_i+b_i), x_i2=y_i(a_i-b_i),

and fixed input queries z_i=y_i k_i/b_i. Let the trained scalar key-query product/matrix be the single unfactored parameter p. The prediction is

  F_i(v,p)=v sum_{tau=1,2} x_i,tau softmax((x_i1 p z_i,x_i2 p z_i))_tau.

The logits differ by 2k_i p, and y_i F_i=v[a_i+b_i tanh(k_i p)]=m_i. Therefore the displayed loss is exactly the usual labeled logistic cross-attention loss, jointly trained in its attention weight p and head v. Fixed queries are part of this constructed dataset, not parameters inferred from unknown labels during training. This is a counterexample family of fixed labeled data. It includes mixed-label data; it does not claim an arbitrary label-query distribution. If all labels are positive and k_i=b_i, it also lies in the simpler common-query prompt-attention model with W=1.

## Proof for GD

Write g_i=(1+exp(m_i))^{-1}>0. The updates are

  Delta v=(eta/n) sum_i g_i h_i,
  Delta p=(eta/n) v sum_i g_i h_i',
  h_i'=b_i k_i sech^2(k_i p)>0.

In Q_+, every h_i and v is positive, so both coordinates increase, remain in Q_+, and all h_i(p_t)>=c:=min_i h_i(p_0)>0. Put H=max_i(a_i+b_i) and M=max_i b_i k_i.

First v cannot remain bounded: otherwise all m_i are bounded above, all g_i have a common positive lower bound, and Delta v has a positive lower bound. Hence v_t->infinity. If p_t were bounded, each h_i' would have a common lower bound d>0 on its compact monotone range. Then

  Delta p / Delta v
   =v [sum_i g_i h_i']/[sum_i g_i h_i] >= (d/H)v.

Summing gives an unbounded p increase as v grows without bound (for v>=1, sum v Delta v >=sum Delta v). Contradiction. Thus p_t->infinity.

For the normalized direction, put k0=min_i k_i>0. We have g_i<=exp(-cv), so 0<Delta p<=eta M v exp(-cv)->0. For sufficiently late t, p>=0 and Delta p<=1. Also

  sum_i g_i h_i' <=4M exp(-2k0 p) sum_i g_i,
  sum_i g_i h_i >=c sum_i g_i.

Consequently Delta p <=(4M/c) v exp(-2k0 p) Delta v, and the mean-value theorem yields

  Delta[exp(2k0 p)]
   <=(8k0 M exp(2k0)/c) v Delta v.

Since 2v Delta v <=Delta(v^2), telescoping proves exp(2k0 p)<=C(1+v^2) and p<=log(v)/k0+O(1). Thus p/v->0. This proof needs no common first integral, no product of conditional bounds, no Hessian bound, and no small-step restriction. All iterates remain finite at finite step number because the update is finite everywhere.

For Q_-, set w=-v,r=-p and t_i(r)=b_i tanh(k_i r)-a_i=-h_i(-r)>0. The updates in (w,r) have exactly the positive form above, with t_i increasing and bounded, derivative b_i k_i sech^2(k_i r), and the same exponential tail. Hence w,r->infinity and r/w->0. The limits of m_i/sqrt(v^2+p^2) are a_i+b_i in Q_+, and b_i-a_i in Q_-, proving the asserted minimum margins and zero loss.

To see strict suboptimality, set a0=min_i a_i>0. For every i, a_i+b_i=(b_i-a_i)+2a_i>=Gamma_-+2a0, and therefore Gamma_+>=Gamma_-+2a0>Gamma_-. For ANY finite parameters, |h_i|<=a_i+b_i and |v|<=sqrt(v^2+p^2), giving min_i m_i/sqrt(v^2+p^2)<=min_i(a_i+b_i)=Gamma_+. The upper bound is attained as a limit in Q_+, so is the global supremum. Q_- is open and nonempty, hence has positive Lebesgue measure. All initializations there select the second token asymptotically. The full basin containing it need not be determined for this conclusion.

For gradient flow the same derivative signs, boundedness argument, and derivative ratio work. The exponential estimate follows by differentiating exp(2k0 p), bounding its derivative by (8k0 M/c) v dv/dt, and integrating. There is no finite-time blow-up: |dv/dt|<=H and |dp/dt|<=M|v|. The negative region follows by the same sign change.

## Explicit distinct two-example witness, both labels and equal optimal endpoint

Take (a_1,b_1,k_1)=(1/2,1,1), (a_2,b_2,k_2)=(1/4,5/4,5/4), labels (+1,-1), and fixed queries z=(+1,-1). The raw token pairs are (3/2,-1/2) and (-3/2,1). Both signed optimal endpoints are 3/2. The signed inferior endpoints are -1/2 and -1. Hence Gamma_+=3/2, Gamma_-=1/2. Every point

  v<0, p<min(atanh(-1/2),(4/5)atanh(-1/5))=atanh(-1/2)

lies in the invariant suboptimal region, for every eta>0. The observations have different token pairs, different roots, and different nonlinear scales. They are not repeated copies of the scalar example.

The old sample-1 invariant is genuinely lost. Let C_1=v^2-G_1(p), with G_1'=2h_1/h_1'. Along the TWO-example flow,

  dC_1/dt=v g_2 [h_2-h_1 h_2'/h_1'].

At (v,p)=(1,0), h_1=1/2,h_1'=1,h_2=1/4,h_2'=25/16, so dC_1/dt=-(17/32)/(1+exp(1/4))!=0. Thus proof 002's conserved quantity cannot be reused. This does not assert nonexistence of every conceivable first integral.

Finally this witness also satisfies the strict optimal-token margin-shrinkage geometry of 2306.13596 Assumption C, in the natural fixed-query extension: Gamma=3/2 and nu=1/2. For softmax first-token weights s_i, |h_i|<=3/2-(1/2)(1-s_i), hence min_i|h_i|<=3/2-(1/2)max_i(1-s_i). If signed features are not jointly separable, the achievable nonnegative unit-head label margin is zero and the same upper bound remains valid. If they are separable, it is min_i|h_i|. The attention separator of all first tokens is feasible since all logit gaps are positive multiples of p. body: Define the Fourier transform on L^1(R^n) intersect L^2(R^n) by f-hat(xi) = integral over R^n of f(x) e^(-2 pi i x.xi) dx. This map extends uniquely to a unitary isomorphism of L^2(R^n) onto itself, i.e. a bijective linear map preserving the L^2 norm: integral over R^n of |f-hat(xi)|^2 dxi equals integral over R^n of |f(x)|^2 dx for every f in L^2(R^n). More generally the Plancherel/Parseval identity gives integral of f times conjugate(g) equals integral of f-hat times conjugate(g-hat), for f, g in L^2(R^n).
title: Plancherel theorem

body: Let U be an open subset of R^n, f in L^1_loc(U) (locally Lebesgue integrable), and alpha a multi-index. A function g in L^1_loc(U) is the alpha-th weak (distributional) derivative of f, written g = D^alpha f, if integral over U of f(x) D^alpha phi(x) dx = (-1)^{|alpha|} integral over U of g(x) phi(x) dx for every test function phi in C_c^infinity(U) (infinitely differentiable with compact support in U). When it exists, the weak derivative is unique up to a set of Lebesgue measure zero, and it agrees with the classical derivative whenever f is continuously differentiable. [standard, e.g. Evans, Partial Differential Equations]
title: Weak Derivative of a Locally Integrable Function

\label {thm5.2}
Suppose $X := (X_k, k \in \mathbb Z)$ is a (not necessarily Markovian)
strictly stationary sequence of random variables such that
the following conditions (a), (b) hold: \hfil\break
(a) $E[X_0^2] < \infty$ and $E[X_0] = 0$; and \hfil\break
(b) $\sum_{n=1}^\infty 
\int_0^{\alpha(n)} Q_{|X(0)|}^2(u)\, du < \infty$. \hfil\break
Then the following three statements hold: \hfil\break 
(1) $\sigma^2 := E[X_0] + 2\sum_{n=1}^\infty E[X_0X_n]$
exists in $[0, \infty)$, with the sum being absolutely convergent;
\hfil\break
(2) $\lim_{n \to \infty} n^{-1} \textrm{\rm Var}(\, \sum_{k=1}^n X_k) = \sigma^2$; and \hfil\break
(3) if also $\sigma^2 > 0$, then
$[1/(\sqrt n\, \sigma)] \sum_{k=1}^n X_k$ converges in 
distribution to $N(0,1)$ as $n \to \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

On undirected nearest-neighbor Z^d, d>=2, assign iid Uniform[1,2] weights. T(x,y) is the minimum total weight over paths from x to y. For an induced finite box C containing a straight n-edge route from x to x+n e_1, T_C is the analogous constrained minimum. The unique unrestricted geodesic exists almost surely. Its deviation D(x,y) is the maximum Euclidean distance from the segment [x,y]. Along these axis endpoints n<=T<=T_C<=2n, and T_C-T vanishes whenever the geodesic is contained in C.

[Corollary 2 of arXiv:2608.26618, 'A Unified Descriptive-Complexity Framework for Model Selection under Correlated Designs'] Let $\{C_k\}_{k=1}^q$ be nonnegative atomic code lengths satisfying
$
\sum_{k=1}^q e^{-C_k}\le 1 .
$
For each model $S\in\mathcal M_n$, define its descriptive complexity by
$
C_S:=1+\sum_{k: U_k\subseteq S} C_k .
$
For every $\lambda\ge \lambda_{\rm sel}$,
if assumptions \textnormal{(\romannumeral 2)}--\textnormal{(\romannumeral 3)} of
Theorem~\ref{thm:complexity} hold, then
\[
\Pr\left(
\min_{S\in\mathcal M_n,\ S\neq S^*}
\mathrm{DCIC}(S)>\mathrm{DCIC}(S^*)
\right)\to 1
\qquad \text{as } n\to\infty .
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 2 of arXiv:2608.26618

body:
[Lemma lem:critM of arXiv:2607.22291, 'Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declum'] Set $
  \P_k(\,\cdot\,)
  \coloneqq
  \P(\,\cdot\mid G_k(\mathcal T)=1)$ and $  \mathbb{E}_k[\,\cdot\,]
  \coloneqq
  \mathbb{E}[\,\cdot\mid G_k(\mathcal T)=1]$. Assume that
there exist nonnegative integer-valued random variables $C_k,L_k$ such that
one can construct copies $\mathcal T^{(1)},\mathcal T^{(2)},\ldots$ which,
conditionally on $(C_k,L_k)$, are independent and each have the same law
as $\mathcal T$, with
$$
  |\mathcal T|
  =
  C_k+\sum_{i=1}^{L_k}|\mathcal T^{(i)}|
  \qquad\text{under }\P_k \qquad  \textrm{and} \qquad 
  \mathbb{E}_{k_n}[C_{k_n}+L_{k_n}]
  =
  n^{o(1)}.
$$
Then, for every $\eta\in(0,1-1/\alpha)$, Assumption (hyp:S of the paper) holds for
$(G_k)$ along $(k_n)$ with respect to $
  M_n=\lfloor n^{1-\eta}\rfloor$.

body:
[Theorem thm:KPZ of arXiv:2511.08479, '\Large From disordered systems to the Critical 2D Stochastic Heat Flow'] \ 
Let $h^\varepsilon$ be the solution of the mollified 2D KPZ equation (equation eq:2DKPZ of the paper) with disorder strength $\beta_\varepsilon=(\hat\beta+o(1)) \sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{\log \frac{1}{\varepsilon}}}$ for some $\hat\beta\in (0,1)$. Then for any test function $\phi\in C_c(\mathbb{R}^2)$, we have
\begin{align}
\frac{1}{\beta_\varepsilon} \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \phi(x) \Big(h^\varepsilon(t,x)-\ensuremath{\mathbf  E}[h^\varepsilon(t,x)] \Big) {\rm d}x
\xrightarrow[\,\varepsilon\to 0\,]{d} \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \phi(x) v(t, x) {\rm d}x,
\end{align}
where $v(t, x)$ is the solution of the Edwards-Wilkinson equation (equation linearSHE of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Edwards-Wilkinson fluctuations \cite{CSZ20, G20}

[Lemma 17 of arXiv:2608.18075, '2608.18075'] Let $u:\Omega_\tau\to\mathcal H$ be Borel and suppose that
\begin{align*}
 u\in\mathbb D^{1,p}(\mathcal H)
 \qquad\text{for every finite }p,
\end{align*}
where $\mathbb D^{1,p}(\mathcal H)$ is the usual Malliavin Sobolev space \cite{Bogachev10}.
Define
\begin{align*}
 \mathbf u(\omega)(t)=\int_0^t u(\omega)_r\,\dd r,
 \qquad
 T_u(\omega)=\omega+\mathbf u(\omega).
\end{align*}
Suppose moreover that, for some $d\ge0$,
\begin{align}
 \|u\|_{\mathcal H}\le Cd,\qquad
 \|D_{\mathcal H}u\|_{\HS}\le Cd,\qquad
 \|D_{\mathcal H}u\|_{\rm op}\le\frac12
\end{align}
$\mathbf P$-almost surely. Then $(T_u)_\#\mathbf P\sim\mathbf P$
and
\begin{align*}
 \operatorname{Ent}\bigl((T_u)_\#\mathbf P\mid\mathbf P\bigr)
 \le C_{\rm Ram}d^2,
\end{align*}
where $\operatorname{Ent}(\cdot\mid\cdot)$ denotes relative entropy and
$C_{\rm Ram}$ depends only on the fixed constant $C$ in
\eqref{eq:Ramer-small}.

\begin{equation}
    \hL_{\lambda}(h_0;x,y) := \sup_{u \in \lambda} \big( h_{0}(u) + T_{u,(x,y)}\big) 
\end{equation} for all $x,y \in \Z$ with $(x,y) \succeq u $ for some $u\in \lambda$. . The \textbf{periodic height function} $\hLp_{\lambda}$ is defined as in \eqref{eq:LPPRecursion}, but with respect to the periodic last passage times $\Tper$ from Definition~\ref{def:LastPassageTimes} and a down-right path $\lambda=\lambda^{\per}_N \in \Lambda_{N,k}$.

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2608.13631, 'The classical discrete laws near the mode:\\ complete local expansions for the negative bi'] Let $t_c$ be the vertex of the quadratic part of $A_1$ of \eqref{eq:hyp-Am}.  Then
	\begin{equation}
	\begin{gathered}
		t_c=-\frac{(N-2n)(N-2K)}{2N^{2}},\\
		\mu+t_c+\tfrac12-\frac{(n+1)(K+1)}{N+2}
		=-\frac{(2K-N)(2n-N)}{N^{2}\,(N+2)} .
	\end{gathered}
	\end{equation}
	and the discrepancy satisfies
	\[
		\Bigl|\mu+t_c+\tfrac12-\frac{(n+1)(K+1)}{N+2}\Bigr|<\frac1{N+2} .
	\]
	Consequently, whenever $(n+1)(K+1)/(N+2)\notin\Z$, the unit window
	$\bigl(\mu+t_c-\tfrac12,\,\mu+t_c+\tfrac12\bigr]$ contains exactly one integer and it is
	the mode \eqref{eq:hyp-mode-classical}; when $(n+1)(K+1)/(N+2)\in\Z$ the window boundary
	falls within $1/(N+2)$ of the tied pair, and the integer it selects is one of the two
	modes.

body:
[Defi 17 (Elliptical Brownian motions) of arXiv:2511.10535, 'Eigenvalues of Brownian Motions on $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$'] Let $\rho>0$ and let $\zeta\in\C$ with $0<|\zeta|\le\rho$.  Define
\begin{equation}
    
    \theta = \frac12\arg \zeta \qquad a = \sqrt{\frac12(\rho+|\zeta|)} \qquad b = \sqrt{\frac12(\rho-|\zeta|)}. 
\end{equation}
Then $a^2+b^2=\rho$ and $e^{2\i\theta}(a^2-b^2)=\zeta$, so that $(a,b,\theta)$ satisfy \eqref{eq.rho.zeta}.  This yields a bijective mapping
\begin{equation} \{(\rho,\zeta)\colon 0<|\zeta|\le\rho\}\mapsto\{(a,b,\theta)\colon a>b\ge 0, \theta\in[0,\pi)\}. \end{equation}
We may extend the definitions of $a,b$ to allow $\zeta=0$, in which case $a=b$; here $\theta$ is undefined.

Let $(X^N(t))_{t\geq 0}$, $(Y^N(t))_{t\geq 0}$ be independent Hermitian Brownian motions of size $N$. 
We define the general {\bf elliptical Brownian motion} $(W^N_{\rho,\zeta}(t))_{t\ge0}$ by
	\[ W^N_{\rho,\zeta}(t) = e^{\i \theta} \left(aX^N(t) + \i b Y^N(t)\right). \]
    Similarly, if $(x(t))_{t\geq 0}$ and $(y(t))_{t\geq 0}$ are freely independent free semicircular Brownian motion, the {\bf free elliptical Brownian motion $(w_{\rho,\zeta}(t))_{t\ge0}$} is defined as
    \[ w_{\rho,\zeta}(t) = e^{\i \theta} \left(a x(t) + \i b y(t)\right). \]
In both cases, when $a=b$ (i.e.\ $\zeta=0$), all values of $\theta$ yield the same distribution for the right-hand-side, so we may take canonically $\theta=0$ in this case.

Note that the laws of $W^N_{\rho,\zeta}(t)$ and $w_{\rho,\zeta}(t)$ are invariant under $a\mapsto-a$, $b\mapsto-b$, and $(a,b,\theta)\mapsto(b,a,\theta+\frac{\pi}{2})$.  It then follows from \eqref{eq.bijection} that $\rho>0$, $|\zeta|\le\rho$ paramaterize the laws of all possible elliptical Brownian motions.

To lighten notation we will often drop the subscripts $\rho,\zeta$ if there can be no confusion.
title: Elliptical Brownian motions

For x in X and radii R > r > 0, the open annulus is A(r, R, x) = {y in X : r < d(x, y) < R}. For Gamma in Pi(X), N_{r, R}^x(Gamma) denotes the total number of crossings between the inner boundary {d(x, .) = r} and outer boundary {d(x, .) = R} made by curves in Gamma. X is a metric space

[Lemma l.moments-cumulants of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] For a fixed  collection of integers $k_1,\ldots,k_p$, $p\ge2$,
 assume that  for all $J\subset[p]$,
 \begin{equation}
     
 \sup_{(x_j)_{j \in J} \in\mathbb{R}^{d|J|}} 
 m^{(k_j:j \in J) }( x_j : j \in J)<\infty.
 \end{equation}

 The following statements are equivalent:
 \begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),  labelindent=0pt]
\item There exist fast decreasing functions $\tilde\phi=\tilde\phi_{k_1,\ldots,k_p}$
and constants
	$\tilde C=C(k_1,\ldots,k_p)$, such that
  for any subset  of integers  $J\subset [p]$, $|J|\ge2$, a nonempty, proper subset
  $I\subsetneq J$, and all configurations $\{x_j:  j \in J \}, x_j \in\mathbb{R}^d$, of distinct points
	we have

\begin{equation}
	\Bigl|m^{(k_j : j\in J)}(x_j : j\in J)-
	m^{(k_j: j\in I)}(x_j:j\in I)\, m^{(k_j: j\in J\setminus I)}(x_j:j\in
	 J\setminus I)\Bigr|\le
	\tilde C\tilde\phi(s)\,,
	\end{equation}
	
	where  $s:=d\bigl(\{x_j:j\in I\}, \{x_j:j\in  J\setminus I\}\bigr)$.
      \item  	 There exist fast decreasing functions $\tilde\phi_\top=\tilde\phi_\top^{k_1,\ldots,k_p}$ and constants
	$\tilde C^\top=\tilde C^\top(k_1,\ldots,k_p)$, 
        such that for any subset  of integers $ J\subset [p]$, $|J|\ge2$ and all configurations  $x_j\in\mathbb{R}^d$, $j\in J$ of distinct points
	we have

	\begin{equation}
	|m_{\top}^{(k_j:j\in J)}(x_j : j\in J)|\le
	\tilde
	C^\top\tilde\phi_\top\bigl(\mathrm{diam}(x_j : j\in J)\bigr)
	\,,
	\end{equation}

where $\mathrm{diam}(x_j : j\in J):=\max_{i,j\in J}(|x_i-x_j|)$.
 \end{enumerate}
 Moreover, the bound~(equation e.Usell-clustering-bound of the paper)  for $J=[p]$ implies
 	\begin{equation}
\sup_{x_1\in \mathbb{R}^d}\int_{
(\mathbb{R}^d)^{(p-1)}}|m_\top^{\bk k1p}(\bk x1p)|\,\mathrm{d} x_2\cdots \mathrm{d} x_p< \infty.
	\end{equation}

Further, $\tilde\phi_\top$ and $\tilde C^\top$ in (ii) depend only on $\tilde \phi$, $\tilde C$, the dimension $d$ and the bound in (equation e.moments-uniformly-bounded of the paper) and similarly the $\tilde\phi$ and $\tilde C$ in (i) depend only on $\tilde \phi_\top$, $\tilde C^\top$ and the bound in (equation e.moments-uniformly-bounded of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\[

\]

\[
    L(P)=\bigl(L_f(P): f\in F(P)\bigr).
\]

body: In the mathematical field of graph theory, Kirchhoff's theorem or Kirchhoff's matrix tree theorem is a theorem about the number of spanning trees in a graph. It states that this number can be computed as any cofactor of the graph's Laplacian matrix. This shows in particular that the number of spanning trees can be computed from the graph data in polynomial time. Kirchhoff's theorem is a generalization of Cayley's formula which provides the number of spanning trees in a complete graph. The theorem is named after the German mathematician Gustav Kirchhoff, who published it in 1847. An English translation of Kirchhoff's paper was published in 1958.
title: Kirchhoff's theorem

body:
[Lemma 11 (Parametric weighted lattice-corner expansion) of arXiv:2609.03466, 'Least-Favorable Location for Binomial Top-$t$ Selection'] Let $U$ be a compact interval. For each $p\in U$, let $Z_p$ be a random vector supported by a fixed finite subset of $\Zz^d$, with masses that are positive and $C^{r+2}$ in $p$. Assume that the additive group generated by differences of support points is $\Zz^d$. Put
\[
 M_p(\lambda)=\Ee e^{\langle\lambda,Z_p\rangle}.
\]
Suppose there is a $C^{r+2}$ map $\lambda:U\to(0,\infty)^d$ satisfying
\[
 \nabla_\lambda\log M_p(\lambda(p))=0.
\]
Let
\[
 I(p)=-\log M_p(\lambda(p)),
 \qquad
 \Sigma(p)=\nabla_\lambda^2\log M_p(\lambda(p)).
\]
Let $w:\Zz_+^d\to\Rr$ be bounded and define
\[
 W(p)=\sum_{z\in\Zz_+^d}
 w(z)e^{-\langle\lambda(p),z\rangle}.
\]
For independent copies $Z_{p,1},\ldots,Z_{p,n}$, put $S_{n,p}=\sum_{i=1}^nZ_{p,i}$ and
\[
 \mathcal T_n(p)=\sum_{z\in\Zz_+^d}w(z)\Pp(S_{n,p}=z).
\]
Then, for $\varepsilon_n=n^{-1/2}(\log n)^{3r+6}$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal T_n(p)
 =\frac{e^{-nI(p)}n^{-d/2}}
 {(2\pi)^{d/2}\sqrt{\det\Sigma(p)}}
 \left[W(p)+O_{C^r(U)}(\varepsilon_n)\right].
 
\end{equation}
If $r\ge1$ and $I'(p_0)\ne0$, then
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal T_n'(p_0)
 =n^{1-d/2}e^{-nI(p_0)}
 \left\{-I'(p_0)
 \frac{W(p_0)}{(2\pi)^{d/2}\sqrt{\det\Sigma(p_0)}}+o(1)\right\}.
 
\end{equation}
If in addition $W(p_0)\ne0$, this may equivalently be written with a relative factor $\{1+o(1)\}$. If $r\ge2$, $I'(p_0)=0$, $I''(p_0)>0$, and $W(p_0)>0$, then
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal T_n''(p_0)
 =-I''(p_0)
 \frac{W(p_0)}{(2\pi)^{d/2}\sqrt{\det\Sigma(p_0)}}
 n^{1-d/2}e^{-nI(p_0)}\{1+o(1)\}.
 
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Parametric weighted lattice-corner expansion

[Openquestion 30 (Does every non-uniform die admit a non-transitive $3$-cycle?) of arXiv:2601.16580, 'Coin flipping and waiting times paradoxes \\ Why fair coins are exceptional'] Fix an $s$-sided i.i.d.\ source with probability vector $(p_1,\dots,p_s)$ that is not uniform (i.e.\ not all $p_i=1/s$).
Must there exist finite strings $A,B,C$ over the alphabet $\{1,\dots,s\}$ such that, for
\emph{independent} copies of this source and \emph{random tie-break},
\[
\Pr(A\!>\!B)>\tfrac12,\qquad \Pr(B\!>\!C)>\tfrac12,\qquad \Pr(C\!>\!A)>\tfrac12\ ?
\]
Equivalently: is exact fairness the only obstruction to the existence of non-transitive head-to-head races under independent sources? (Stated as a question by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)

body: [Proposition prop:fullconf of arXiv:2608.23638, 'Replicable Conformal Prediction'] Consider full conformal prediction with the $1$-nearest-neighbor score, calibration size $n\ge2$, and data law $P$ absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^{2}$. For a rank cutoff $m$, let $\widehat\mathcal{C}^{(m)}_\mathcal{D}(x)$ be the set of labels whose full-conformal rank among the $n{+}1$ scores is at least $m$ (Appendix~(app:twolist of the paper) fixes the tie convention). For every nonendpoint cutoff $m\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, two independent runs satisfy $\mathbb{P}[\widehat\mathcal{C}^{(m)}_\mathcal{D}\equiv\widehat\mathcal{C}^{(m)}_{\mathcal{D}'}]=0$ (map equality read in the completed law); with any shared seed $U$ and measurable cutoff $M(U)$, the agreement probability equals $\mathbb{P}[M(U)\in\{0,n{+}1\}]$ exactly. The usual rule $\{\widehat p_\mathcal{D}>\alpha\}$, where $\widehat p_\mathcal{D}$ is the full-conformal $p$-value, is the cutoff $\lfloor\alpha(n{+}1)\rfloor$, so agreement is zero for every $\alpha\in[1/(n{+}1),1)$, with no integrality condition, and trivially one below; $n\ge2$ is sharp. This covers exactly the sample-independent, seed-dependent monotone transformations of the $p$-value grid followed by a strict threshold; within this class, stabilizing the refitted training map is the remaining route [ilps2022,eaton2026]. (Full statement, conventions, and proof: Appendix~(app:twolist of the paper).) (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Full conformal is not rescuable by rounding

Let Q be uniform product law on [0,1]^2 and D=Law(U,U), U uniform on [0,1]. Define F(s)=s^2/2 for 0<=s<=1 and F(s)=1-(2-s)^2/2 for 1<=s<=2. The map T(u,r)=(F(u+r),F(u+r)) pushes Q to D and is optimal for squared Euclidean cost. W_2^2(Q,D)=1/10; each coordinate contributes 1/20. T is the gradient of a convex potential Phi(u,r)=H(u+r), where H(s)=s^3/6 for s<=1 and H(s)=-s^3/6+s^2-s+1/3 for s>=1. Source: Ansari arXiv:2609.23940v1, Corollary 1.4 p.4, Proposition 3.1 p.7, Corollary 3.2 p.8.

[Theorem Invariance principle of arXiv:2505.05921, 'Limit Theorems for step reinforced random walks\\ with regularly varying memory'] {}
         Let $\{S_n\}_{n\geq 0}$ be the SRRW-RVM with the zero mean innovation sequence $\{\xi_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ satisfying $\mathbb{E}\xi_1^2=1$. Then, for all $p\in \left[0,p_c\right)$, we have 
         \[
            \left( n^{-1/2} S_{\lfloor{nt}\rfloor}: t\geq 0\right)\to_{\rm{w}} \left(\mathcal{G}(t): t\geq 0\right),
        \]
        in $(D([0, \infty)), \mathcal D)$, where $\left(\mathcal{G}(t): t\geq 0\right)$ is a continuous and centered Gaussian process, starting from the origin, with the covariance kernel given by, for $0\leq s\leq t$,
        \begin{equation}   \mathbb{E}\left(\mathcal{G}(s)\mathcal{G}(t)\right)=
            \begin{cases}
            \frac{s}{(1-p)(\gamma-p(\gamma+1))}\left(\gamma - \frac{p((2-p)(\gamma+1)-1)}{(2(1-p)(\gamma+1)-1)}\left(\frac{s}{t}\right)^{\gamma-p(\gamma+1)}\right), &\text{for $p\ne\widehat{p}$,}\\    s\left(\gamma^2 +(\gamma+1)^2 - \gamma(\gamma+1) \log \frac{s}{t}\right), &\text{for $p=\widehat{p}$.}           
            \end{cases}
        \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 16 (The separatrix is the cone of square roots) of arXiv:2608.15805, 'Spectral duality structures and the Fisher--Rao geometry of reset distributions'] Suppose, as in Remark~\ref{rem:pi-mu}, that the underlying chain
is $(\sigma,\kappa)$-reversible with reversible measure
$\mu\propto\kappa^{-1}$. Then
\[
\Sigma\cap\Delta_{m-1}
=\Bigl\{\pi:\ \pi|_O\propto\sqrt{\mu}\,\bigl|_O\ \text{on each
orbit }O,\ \text{neutral weights free}\Bigr\},
\]
and the per-orbit constants (together with the neutral weights,
modulo normalisation) are global coordinates on $\Sigma$. Note that
the two pictures are of different kinds: in the $\pi$-coordinates
$\Sigma$ is an affine slice of the simplex, not a cone; it is in the
coordinates $x=2\sqrt\pi$ that it becomes a genuine cone, and the
name is to be read there. On the sphere, correspondingly,
\[
\Phi\bigl(\Sigma^\circ\bigr)
=\operatorname{cone}_{+}\bigl\{\mu^{1/4}\big|_O,\ \text{neutral
axes}\bigr\}\cap S^{m-1}_+(2),
\]
the \emph{positive} cone --- positivity and normalisation are part
of the statement, not decoration. The spectral square root
$\mu\mapsto\sqrt\mu$ and the geometric square root $\Phi$ thus
compose, and the separatrix is generated, in spherical coordinates,
by the fourth roots of the reversible measure.
