Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). After the optimism reading was refuted (P20), the gain was located row by row: the per-evaluation-row relative-score gain of the long-only stack over least squares against the bootstrap variance of the least-squares stack at that row. P22 (a) REFUTED at the pre-registered 0.2: the within-cell median Spearman between a row's gain and the least-squares variance load at that row is 0.13 over the 40 EMIT cells (positive in 36 of 40; 0.37 on Y2, 0.01 on Y1); (b) HELD on Y2, REFUTED as an every-group claim: the top-decile-load rows carry 47 pct of Y2's gain (a uniform spread gives 10) but only 11 pct on Y1 (20 on Y3, 32 on Y4); (c) HELD: across the 40 EMIT cells the gain rank-correlates 0.54 with the variance-load share of least squares' error, and 0.65 with the share the constraint removes (least squares minus nn1) - the between-cell statistic that optimism (P20) failed to be; (d) REFUTED as written: the OCO-2 top-decile share reaches 0.40 on sco2, but as the share of a gain of -0.55 pct it is the ratio of two near-zero numbers and does not test the clause; falsifier (within-cell correlation at or below zero) not triggered. Reading: where the gain is large (Y2, +18) it sits where least squares is uncertain - row-level rank correlation 0.37, 47 pct of the gain on the tenth of rows with the largest variance; where it is modest (+5 to +6) it is spread over the rows; between cells the variance-load share of least squares' error predicts the gain (0.54) and the variance the constraint removes predicts it better (0.65). The calibration and evaluation rows share the same target-norm distribution, so this is not a split shift; the gain leans toward the small-norm evaluation rows the reported metric weights most. Cell level: the variance the constraint removes (least squares' bootstrap variance share minus the long-only stack's) predicts the gain within every output group (Spearman 0.79, 0.87, 0.54, 0.43 on Y1-Y4; 0.69 across 40 cells with the group effect removed), while the L1 norm of the least-squares weights does not survive the group adjustment (0.02): the constraint pays what it saves in estimation variance at the rows it is scored on. Fresh-split replication (split C, SPLIT_SEED 11): P23 (a) REFUTED at the per-group 0.5, HELD in the aggregate: on split C the within-group Spearman between the gain and the variance removed is +0.59, +0.49, +0.64, +0.22 on Y1..Y4 and +0.74 across the 40 cells with the group effect removed (split B: +0.69); (b) REFUTED: the split-B variance-removed share predicts the split-C gain only on Y1 and Y2 (+0.72, +0.47; Y3 +0.09, Y4 -0.24; demeaned +0.17), and the split-B gain itself predicts the split-C gain only weakly (Y1 +0.82, Y4 +0.47, Y2 +0.15, Y3 -0.14); (c) HELD: the long-only stack beats least squares on 35 of 40 split-C cells (mean +9.59 against +8.83 on split B); falsifier (any group at or below 0.2, or the demeaned correlation at or below 0.3) not triggered. Fresh-split check of the calibration-side correlates (P32, the P20 driver on split C): P32 (a) HELD: on split C the between-cell Spearman of the gain with the least-squares L1 is +0.55 and with n_eff -0.44; (b) REFUTED: group-demeaned, L1 +0.29 and members kept +0.21; (c) HELD: the nn0 RMSE gain with the smallest relative eigenvalue +0.29 and with the condition number -0.31; falsifier (L1 above +0.3 after the group adjustment) not triggered.

AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. Finite-second-moment extension of Gaussian product spectral coupling and Target2 comparisons, proof unaudited. Let independent real factor arrays U(N by M),V(P by M) have fixed centered iid unit-variance laws, possibly different, with finite second moments only; P/N->alpha>0 and M/N->beta>0 finite. Ordered product singular profiles of X=UV^T/sqrt(N) and an independent Gaussian-factor reference B satisfy E sum_j(sigma_j(X)-sigma_j(B))^2/(NP)->0. Centered normalized bounded truncations give the exact error E||X-X_K||_F^2/(NP)=2(M/N)(1-c_U,K*c_V,K), where c_A,K=E[A A_K]->1. Apply existing finite-fourth-moment convergence008 at fixed K, then K->infinity. Haar/channel comparison006 gives limsup per-entry MI_X-MI_B<=0 at every fixed s>=0 for ALL positive finite aspect ratios. For P/N->1, the C1 reference limit022 also gives limsup normalized MMSE_X-MMSE_B<=0 at EVERY fixed s>=0, with no exceptional SNR set. Non-unit centered variances follow by rescaling; noncentered or dimension-dependent priors are not asserted. Novelty unestablished.
Independent arrays with fixed centered iid unit-variance real factor laws and finite second moments.
Positive finite limits P/N and M/N; near-square P/N->1 required only for the all-SNR MMSE conclusion.
Independent standard Gaussian channel noise and per-entry Frobenius loss.
Existing finite-fourth-moment spectral coupling008, Haar comparison006 and new reference proof022 remain unaudited dependencies.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:ff286e93f6c37c0dad47334ff8bfca3e8d96473b830ffac93cbb560093e9e5e2","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/ff/ff286e93f6c37c0dad47334ff8bfca3e8d96473b830ffac93cbb560093e9e5e2.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:f7ee46a2e3388a11ce13fc89ccd7a2a712259b34ba37615dbe0afe0e0398d634","bundle_entry_key":"finite-variance-product-gaussian-mi-mmse-extremality-w718","bundle_id":"population.t287-near-square-c1-and-finite-variance-comparison-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian channels and extensive-rank matrix inference","draft":"w718/bundle_008.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.gaussian_channels:finite-variance-product-gaussian-mi-mmse-extremality-w718","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Finite-variance iid factors: spectral coupling and near-square MMSE comparison

Target 2 partial result, proof draft, unaudited. Novelty is unestablished.
This extends the moment scope of the existing spectral coupling and
uses the new near-square C1 reference limit. It is not an additional
isolated numerical case or a dimension-uniform Target1 expansion.

Let N->infinity, P/N->alpha in (0,infinity), M/N->beta in (0,infinity).
Let U and V be independent real arrays of sizes N by M and P by M.
Each array has iid entries from a fixed centered unit-variance law;
only finite second moments are assumed. The two laws may differ.
Set X=UV^T/sqrt(N), and let B be the same product with independent
standard Gaussian factors. Define ordered-singular-profile distance

 D_N(X,B)^2=E sum_j(sigma_j(X)-sigma_j(B))^2/(NP),

where B is independent of the original arrays. Then

    D_N(X,B)->0.                                    (1)

Consequently, for every fixed s>=0,

 limsup [I(X;sqrt(s)X+G)-I(B;sqrt(s)B+G)]/(NP)<=0.    (2)

If in addition P/N->1, then for every fixed s>=0,

    limsup [mmse_X,N(s)-mmse_B,N(s)]<=0,             (3)

where each Bayes risk uses its own Gaussian observation and Frobenius
loss divided by NP. The Gaussian risk has the explicit limit in
gaussian_reference_near_square_c1.md. This includes N=P=M and all fixed
positive hidden-rank ratios in the near-square aspect. Gaussian factors
maximize the limiting comparison for BOTH MI and product MMSE, with
the latter conclusion here restricted to P/N->1.

## 1. Centered, normalized truncations with exact covariances

For a centered variance-one random variable A define, for sufficiently
large K,

 b_K=E[A 1_(|A|<=K)],
 v_K=E[A^2 1_(|A|<=K)]-b_K^2>0,
 A_K=(A 1_(|A|<=K)-b_K)/sqrt(v_K),
 c_K=E[A A_K]=E[A^2 1_(|A|<=K)]/sqrt(v_K).

Then A_K is bounded, centered and variance one. Finite second moment
gives b_K->0, v_K->1 and c_K->1. Cauchy-Schwarz gives |c_K|<=1; its
displayed numerator shows c_K>=0. Thus 0<=c_K<=1, and
E(A-A_K)^2=2(1-c_K)->0. These facts require no higher moments or tail
decay rate. Thresholds with zero v_K are simply omitted; sufficiently
large thresholds have v_K>0.

Apply this construction separately to the U and V laws, with
covariances c_U,K,c_V,K. Couple every entry with its own normalized
truncation, preserving independence across entries and between arrays.
The resulting U_K,V_K have fixed bounded iid laws, and
X_K=U_K V_K^T/sqrt(N).

For a single product summand, independence between factor arrays gives

 E(U_ia V_ja-(U_K)_ia(V_K)_ja)^2
                  =2(1-c_U,K*c_V,K).

Different hidden indices a have zero cross terms: each difference is
centered and the entry pairs at distinct a are independent. Summing
over the M hidden indices and then the NP entries yields the exact
dimension-independent normalized error

 E||X-X_K||_F^2/(NP)
                  =2(M/N)(1-c_U,K*c_V,K).           (4)

No conditional probabilities or independent error events are multiplied.
The required independence is explicit in this entrywise computation.

## 2. Transfer the bounded-law spectral coupling

Hoffman-Wielandt bounds the ordered singular-value distance between
X and X_K by their Frobenius distance. Fix K. The bounded factor laws
meet every finite-fourth-moment hypothesis of existing unaudited
claim008. With the same independent Gaussian reference B, that claim
gives D_N(X_K,B)->0. Minkowski and the pointwise ordered-profile triangle
therefore give

 limsup_N D_N(X,B)
       <=sqrt(2 beta(1-c_U,K*c_V,K)).                (5)

First take N->infinity with K fixed, then K->infinity. The right side
tends to zero, proving(1). This is a two-limit approximation argument;
no unproved interchange or dimension-dependent truncation law is used.
It also avoids assuming that weak spectral convergence alone implies
expected W2 convergence for the original heavy-tailed factors.

## 3. Information and MMSE consequences

Claim006's finite Haar-mixture comparison and Gaussian information/W2
bound apply under finite second moments, which are present here. The
Gaussian reference is biorthogonally invariant. The spectral coupling(1)
therefore gives the information limsup(2) at every positive fixed s,
without requiring an information limit for the original iid prior.
At s=0 both mutual informations are zero.

For MMSE, Haar-randomizing the signal's left and right frames can only
increase its Bayes risk: revealing those independent frames reduces
the problem to the original Gaussian channel by rotating its noise.
Claim006 also gives two-sided information closeness between the
Haarized signal and B from the shared-frame spectral coupling(1).
When P/N->1, the Gaussian reference has a finite C1 information limit
by the full proof in gaussian_reference_near_square_c1.md. Concave
secant bounds and I-MMSE consequently give the same limiting risk for
the Haarized signal and the Gaussian reference. The original signal's
risk is bounded above by its Haarized risk. This proves(3) for every
s>0, with no exceptional SNR set. At s=0, both product-entry variances
are exactly M/N, proving the zero-SNR comparison directly.

Non-unit positive variances follow by multiplying the signal by the
product of the factor standard deviations and rescaling s accordingly.
The centered zero-variance cases are identically zero. Noncentered or
dimension-dependent prior laws are not asserted here.

## Dependencies and remaining scope

The all-aspect finite-fourth-moment profile convergence in claim008 and
the Haar/channel comparison in claim006 remain unaudited dependencies.
The new near-square reference proof depends on unaudited claims017,
019,020,021 and primary Silverstein/Biane results. None is independently
checked without an exact-version reviewer PASS.

The hardest remaining Target2 piece is pointwise reference regularity
at general rectangular aspect P/N->alpha!=1. Existing averaged and
off-corner statements remain separate. No finite-N Gaussian-factor
extremality is claimed: the old finite-size shrinking-SNR reversal is
compatible with these fixed-SNR dimension-limit conclusions. Target1's
dimension-uniform explicit remainder and Target3's larger-size numerical
correction are not settled by this argument.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:686964a520b560babff49b2d3c712ffe188ecb5df9287b91721884bf39c60f66","revision_digest":"sha256:e3d78694f87f7026224d1fe3fa92818d46f022d5d286d995e6edc50744cfd430","source_id":"owner:w718:T287:finite-variance-product-gaussian-mi-mmse-extremality-w718","source_revision":"2026-10-21 claim w718-T287-023 version1, proof unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Theorem 37 of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] Suppose that $p$ is odd, $\chi$ is injective, $m$ is even, and the morphism $X\rightarrow X/G$ is an HKG cover. Let $l_1<\cdots<l_s$ be the lower jumps and let $u_1<\cdots<u_s$ be the upper jumps of the wild cyclic subgroup $H=C_{p^s}$ acting on the completion of the local ring of $X$ at the ramified point. For each $j\in\llbracket0,s\rrbracket$ let $H_{s-j}$ and $Y_j$ be as in Corollary \ref{C4} and, if $j\ge 1$, let 
$$\l_j:=l_j-1.$$ Then the following properties hold. 

\medskip
{\bf (1)} We have $\textup{g}_{Y_0}=0$ and for each $i\in\llbracket1,s\rrbracket$ we have
\[
\textup{g}_{Y_i}=\frac{p-1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^i \l_jp^{i-j}.
\]

{\bf (2)} For each $i\in\llbracket1,s\rrbracket$, $p-1$ divides $\textup{g}_{Y_i}$.

\smallskip
{\bf (3)} Let $\mathcal R_X$ be the $B_0[H]$-module of Proposition \ref{P5}(2). Then we have identities 
$$\frac{\textup{g}_{Y_i}-\textup{g}_{Y_{i-1}}}{p^i-p^{i-1}}=\frac{\l_i+(p-1)\sum_{j=1}^{i-1}\l_jp^{i-1-j}}{2p^{i-1}}=\frac{u_i-1}{2}$$
for each $i\in\llbracket1,s\rrbracket$ and hence a $B_0[H]$-linear isomorphism 
$$\mathcal R_X\cong\oplus_{i=1}^s \frac{\l_i+(p-1)\sum_{j=1}^{i-1}\l_jp^{i-1-j}}{2p^{i-1}}\mathcal B_i= \oplus_{i=1}^s \frac{u_i-1}{2}\mathcal B_i.$$

{\bf (4)} Let $\mathcal X$ be a smooth projective curve over $\Spec R$ whose reduction modulo $\upsilon$ is $X$ and such that there exists a homomorphism $\varrho:G\rightarrow\Aut(\mathcal X)$ that lifts $\rho$. Then the following properties hold.

\medskip\noindent
{\bf (4.a) (de Jong)} For each subgroup $\Delta$ of $G$, the quotient curve $\mathcal X/\Delta$ is smooth projective over $\Spec R$ with geometrically connected fibers.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (4.b)} For each subgroup $\Delta$ of $G$, the special fiber $(\mathcal X/\Delta)_k$ of $\mathcal X/\Delta$ is naturally identified with $X/\Delta$.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (4.c) (Chinburg--Guralnick--Harbater)} The KGB obstruction for the HKG cover $X\rightarrow X/G$ vanishes.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (4.d)} We have $B[H]$-linear isomorphisms
$$H^0(\mathcal X,\Omega_{\mathcal X})\otimes_R B\cong H^1(\mathcal X,\mathcal O_{\mathcal X})\otimes_R B\cong\oplus_{i=1}^s \frac{u_i-1}{2}\mathcal B_i.$$

[Lem graph-to-weighted-jordan of arXiv:2607.21428, 'Subcritical percolation and network archaeology on random recursive tree substrate network'] Suppose the conclusion of Lemma~(lem:singly-attached-decorations of the paper) holds.
		Write \(X_u:=|D_u|\) for \(u\in\mathcal{B}_n^{\operatorname{root}}\), and
		\(X(A):=\sum_{u\in A}X_u\).  Put
		\[
		\Delta_n:=\max_{u\in\mathcal{B}_n^{\operatorname{root}}}|D_u|.
		\]
		Then for every skeleton vertex \(v\in\mathcal{B}_n^{\operatorname{root}}\),
		\begin{equation}
			
			0
			\leqslant
			\psi_{\mathcal{C}_n^{\operatorname{root}}}(v)
			-
			\psi_{\mathcal{B}_n^{\operatorname{root}}}^X(v)
			\leqslant
			\Delta_n .
		\end{equation}
		Moreover, fix a skeleton vertex \(v_{\mathrm{skel}}\), an integer \(L\geqslant1\), and
		\(\delta>0\).
		If
		\begin{equation}
			
			\Delta_n\leqslant \frac{\delta}{4}X(\mathcal{B}_n^{\operatorname{root}}),
			\qquad
			\psi_{\mathcal{B}_n^{\operatorname{root}}}^X(v_{\mathrm{skel}})
			\leqslant
			(1-\delta)X(\mathcal{B}_n^{\operatorname{root}}),
		\end{equation}
		and
		\begin{equation}
			
			\#\left\{
			v\in\mathcal{B}_n^{\operatorname{root}}:
			\psi_{\mathcal{B}_n^{\operatorname{root}}}^X(v)
			\leqslant
			\psi_{\mathcal{B}_n^{\operatorname{root}}}^X(v_{\mathrm{skel}})+\delta X(\mathcal{B}_n^{\operatorname{root}})
			\right\}
			\leqslant L,
		\end{equation}
		then \(v_{\mathrm{skel}}\in \operatorname{TopJ}_L(\mathcal{C}_n^{\operatorname{root}})\).

body:
[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2606.01881, '2606.01881'] Let $T$ be an a.s. finite stopping time for $(\mathcal F_n)$, and condition on $\mathcal F_T$.  Let $\mathcal B=\{B_r:r\ge1\}$ be a partition such that, for every $k>K_T$, the block containing $k$ is the singleton $\{k\}$ (since the occupied tables at time $T$ have labels $[K_T]$, this amounts to grouping the tables present at time $T$, while leaving all later labels as singletons).  Put
\[
        M_r^{(T)}:=\sum_{\ell\in B_r}N_\ell^{(T)},
        \qquad r\ge1.
\]
Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The aggregated seating sequence after time $T$ is again a Simon-type Chinese restaurant process with parameter $p$, started from the block occupancies $(M_r^{(T)}:r\ge1)$.  Equivalently, for $s\ge T$, an already occupied block $B_r$ is chosen with probability $pM_r^{(s)}/s$, while the next new singleton block is opened with probability $1-p$.
\item Conditionally on the aggregated seating sequence $(C_k^{\mathcal B}:k>T)$, the within-block sequences $C_{B_r}^{(T)}$ over blocks $B_r\subseteq [K_T]$ are independent.  For each such block, $C_{B_r}^{(T)}$ is the fixed-table restaurant on $B_r$ started from the occupancies $(N_\ell^{(T)}:\ell\in B_r)$.
\end{enumerate}

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2607.17662, 'On the Strong Law of Large Numbers under Sublinear Expectations'] A \textit{sublinear expectation} $\mathbb{E}$ on $\mathcal{H}$ is a functional $\mathbb{E}\colon \mathcal{H} \to \overline{\mathbb{R}} := [-\infty, +\infty]$ satisfying the following properties for all $X, Y \in \mathcal{H}$:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item[(a)] \textit{Monotonicity.} If $X \geq Y$, then $\mathbb{E}[X] \geq \mathbb{E}[Y]$.
			\item[(b)] \textit{Constant preserving.} $\mathbb{E}[c] = c$, $\forall\, c \in \mathbb{R}$.
			\item[(c)] \textit{Positive homogeneity.} $\mathbb{E}[\lambda X] = \lambda\,\mathbb{E}[X]$, $\forall\, \lambda \geq 0$.
			\item[(d)] \textit{Subadditivity.} $\mathbb{E}[X + Y] \leq \mathbb{E}[X] + \mathbb{E}[Y]$, provided that $\mathbb{E}[X] + \mathbb{E}[Y]$ does not take the form $\infty - \infty$ or $-\infty + \infty$.
		\end{enumerate}

For a vertex a set h=g-2g(a)1_{z=a}, F(z,+1)=g(z), F(z,-1)=h(z), and s_g(a)=#{j:g(a)!=g(a+e_j)}. Then I(F)=m/2+(m+1-2s_g(a))/N; each s=0,...,m is attainable by a character twist of the canonical quadratic bent base. Put R=sqrt(N), K_+=(N+R)/2, K_-=(N-R)/2 and phi(t)=t log_2(1/t), phi(0)=0. H(F)=E_m=K_+phi((R-1)^2/N^2)+K_-phi((R+1)^2/N^2)+Nphi(1/N^2), independent of g and a. At fixed m the sharp class maximum H/I is E_m/[m/2-(m-1)/N], attained by the full-parity twist flipped at zero. At m=4 this example has I=29/16 and H>469/128>2I, so a canonical constant-2 bound does not extend to all bent splices. Every such splice still satisfies H<=3I. [Def 39 of arXiv:2609.01389, 'K-stability and birational rigidity of Fano 3-fold weighted complete intersections'] Let $m < n$ be positive integers and $a_1, \dots, a_n, b_1 \dots b_n$ be integers.
Let $R = \mbC [x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be the polynomial ring endowed with a $\mbZ^2$-grading defined by the $2 \times n$ matrix
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
a_1 & \cdots & a_n \\
b_1 & \cdots & b_n 
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
This means that the bi-degree of the variable $x_i$ is $(a_i, b_i) \in \mbZ^2$.
We denote by 
\begin{equation} 
\mbT \begin{pNiceArray}{ccc|ccc}[first-row]
x_1 & \dots & x_m & x_{m+1} & \dots & x_n \\
a_1 & \dots & a_m & a_{m+1} & \dots & a_n \\
b_1 & \dots & b_m & b_{m+1} & \dots & b_n
\end{pNiceArray}
\end{equation}
the toric variety whose Cox ring is $R$ and irrelevant ideal is 
\[
I = (x_1, \dots, x_m) \cap (x_{m+1}, \dots, x_n).
\]
In other words, this toric variety is the geometric quotient
\[
(\mbA^n_{x_1, \dots, x_n} \setminus V (I))/(\mbC^*)^2,
\]
where the $(\mbC^*)^2$-action is defined by
\[
(\lambda, \mu) \cdot (x_1, \dots, x_n) = (\lambda^{a_1} \mu^{b_1} x_1, \dots, \lambda^{a_n} \mu^{b_n} x_n).
\]
For a point $\msp$ of the toric variety \eqref{eq:deftoricT}, which we denote by $\mbT$, we pick a point $\msq = (\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_n) \in \mbA^n$ in the preimage of the natural projection $\mbA^n \setminus V (I) \to \mbT$ over $\msp$.
In this case we express $\msp$ as $\msp = (\alpha_1\!:\!\cdots\!:\!\alpha_m;\alpha_{m+1}\!:\!\cdots\!:\!\alpha_n) \in \mbT$.
title: Definition 39 of arXiv:2609.01389

[Theorem thm:centrality of arXiv:2606.02472, 'Correlated uniform attachment trees'] Let $T_{n} \sim \mathrm{UA}(n)$ and let $A_{K}(n)$ be the set of the $K$ most central vertices of~$T_{n}$. Fix $c > 1$, $\delta > 0$,
and set 
\[
c^{\prime} := c \left(1 - e^{-1/c} \right) - \delta.
\]
Then there exists a constant $C < \infty$ that depends only on $c$ and $\delta$ such that for every 
$\varepsilon > 0$, 
the following holds for all $K \geq (C/\varepsilon) \log(1/\varepsilon)$ 
and all large enough $n \geq n_{0}(K,\delta, c )$: 
\[
\mathbb{P} \left( \left| A_{\ceil{c K}}(n) \cap \{ 0, 1, \ldots, K-1 \} \right| \geq c^{\prime} \,   K \right) 
\geq 1 - \varepsilon.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: FIRES WHEN you are about to prove a convex-order dominance for a Markov-modulated inter-event time by conditioning on the modulating state and calling the result a mixture of exponentials. THE ROUTE: conditionally on the chain's stationary sojourn structure the inter-event time is exponential with a state-dependent rate, and a MIXTURE of exponentials always dominates the matched exponential in the convex order by Jensen applied to t -> E[exp(-lambda t)]. WHERE IT FAILS: only when the chain does NOT move during the inter-event interval. A general MMPP lets it move, and then the law of T is PHASE-TYPE, not a mixture of exponentials, and phase-type laws are not automatically above the exponential in the convex order. MINIMAL WITNESS that the simplest sufficient condition also fails: the source's own four-state example has a NON-MONOTONE hazard rate, so the decreasing-hazard-rate criterion does not apply either. CONDITION OF FAILURE: any modulating transition inside an inter-event interval. The route that worked instead was Palm inversion - see the E0078 result node.

[Proposition 45 (Invariance of frequencies) of arXiv:2504.02435, 'Poisson-Voronoi percolation in higher rank'] Let $(R_k)_{k=1}^\infty$ be random walk on $X$. Let $Z$ be a closed subset of $X$ such that $\beta(Z)$ exists a.s.~and does not depend on the random walk.
    Then, for every isometry $\tau$ of $(X,d_X)$,
    $$\beta(\tau(Z)) = \beta(Z).$$
    In particular, if $\mathcal{Z}$ is a $G$-invariant enough random closed subset of $X$ which is independent of $(R_k)_k$, then $\beta(\mathcal{Z})$ is an isometry invariant measurable function.

For any $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $c=c(\varepsilon)$ such that if $\omega>c$ then the following holds with probability at least $1-\varepsilon$ provided $n$ is large enough. 

Let $G \in \mathcal{G}(n,k,p,q)$ with the planted partition $\mathcal{P}$. 
For any $d \in \left[0,\frac{1}{k}\right]$, 
let 
$$H(d) = \max_{\mathcal{A}: |\mathcal{A}|\le k} \left\{ q_\mathcal{A}(G) : d - \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \le d(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{P}) \le d + \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \right\}.
$$
Then,
\begin{equation*}
\left| H(d)  - \frac {a-b}{a+(k-1)b}\cdot h(d) \right| \le \varepsilon,
\end{equation*}
where 
\[h(d)= 1 - \frac {1}{k} - 2d\big (1-d(k-1)\big). \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 7 (Admissible analytic resolution) of arXiv:2609.01116, 'Vector-Carleson, Calder\'on, and Poisson--Atomic Criteria for\\ Generalized Hilbert Operat'] Let
\[
 I_k=\{n\in\mathbb N:2^k\le n<2^{k+1}\},\qquad k\ge0.
\]
A family of scalar sequences
$\sigma=(\sigma_j)_{j\ge0}$ on $\mathbb N$ is called
$(L,M,p)$-admissible if:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
 \item $\sigma_j(n)=0$ for $n\in I_k$ whenever $|j-k|>L$;
 \item $\sum_{j\ge0}\sigma_j(n)=1$ for every $n\ge1$;
 \item for every $|\ell|\le L$, the patched sequence
 \[
  m_\ell(n)=\sigma_{k+\ell}(n)\qquad(n\in I_k),
  \tag{3.8}
 \]
 with $\sigma_j=0$ for $j<0$, is an $H^p$ coefficient multiplier of
 norm at most $M$.
\end{enumerate}
Put
\[
 W_j^\sigma\phi(z)=\sum_{n\ge1}\sigma_j(n)\widehat\phi(n)z^n,
 \qquad
 \mathscr S_{\phi,p}^{\sigma}a
 =a_{-1}\phi(0)+
  \sum_{j\ge0}a_j2^{-j/p'}W_j^\sigma\phi.
 \tag{3.9}
\]
The hard resolution is $\sigma_j=\mathbf1_{I_j}$ and has $L=0$.

[Dfn 5 (Large deviations principle) of arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy'] The sequence $(\mu_n)_{n\ge 1}$ obeys the \textbf{large deviations principle} (`\textbf{LDP}') with \textbf{rate function} $I$ if the following hold:
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[i.] (Upper bound) If $x \in \X$ and $a < I(x)$, then there is a neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that
		\[\mu_n U \le e^{-an + o(n)}.\]
		\item[ii.] (Lower bound) If $x \in \X$ and $I(x) < a < \infty$, then any neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ satisfies
		\[\mu_n U \ge e^{-a n - o(n)}.\]
		\item[iii.] (Exponential tightness) For every $a > 0$ there is a compact subset $K$ of $\X$ such that
		\[\mu_n (\X\setminus K) \le e^{-an + o(n)}.\]
	\end{itemize}
title: Large deviations principle

[Theorem 21 of arXiv:2608.31070, 'Sub-Laplacians on Compact Lie Groups: Heat Kernels, Distance, and Zeta Determinants'] For every $R>0$ there are $\varepsilon_R,C_R>0$ such that, whenever $\mathfrak F_{G,K}(Z)\le R$ and $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_R$,
		\begin{equation}
			\left|
			d_{\sr}(e,\exp(\varepsilon Z))^2
			-\varepsilon\mathfrak F_{G,K}(Z)
			\right|
			\le C_R\varepsilon^{3/2}.
		\end{equation}
		The lower estimate has the stronger remainder
		\begin{equation}
			d_{\sr}(e,\exp(\varepsilon Z))^2
			\ge
			\varepsilon\mathfrak F_{G,K}(Z)-C_R\varepsilon^2.
		\end{equation}

[Definition def:drift of arXiv:2411.04773, 'Meeting of squared Bessel flow lines and application to the skew Brownian motion'] An $\mathcal F$-predictable process $\overline{\delta}:{\mathbb R}\to{\mathbb R}$ is called a drift function if there exists a deterministic vector $(\delta_i)_{1\le i\le n} \in {\mathbb R}^n$ and $\mathcal F$-stopping times $-\infty=\tilde{t}_1<\tilde{t}_2<\ldots<\tilde{t}_{n+1}=\infty$ such that $\overline{\delta}=\delta_i$ on $A_i:=(\tilde{t}_{i},\tilde{t}_{i+1})$.
    
    
    If $\overline{\delta'}$ is another drift function and $r_1$ is an $\mathcal F$-stopping time, we write $\overline{\delta}\,|_{r_1}\, \overline{\delta'}$ for the drift function $\overline{\delta}(x)\mathbbm{1}_{(-\infty,r_1)}(x)+ \overline{\delta'}(x)\mathbbm{1}_{[r_1,\infty)}(x)$.
title: Definition def:drift of arXiv:2411.04773

body:
[Proposition 23 (Conditional Rees face maps) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] Let \(S\subset T\subset K\), and set the direction parameters indexed by
\(K\setminus S\) equal to zero before localising those indexed by \(S\).
With the conditional blocks from \eqref{eq:conditional-blocks}, define
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf W^\rho_{K\to T}f(\boldsymbol u_T)
 =
 \left.
 \exp\!\left(
  \frac{\rho^2}{2}
  \Delta_{C_{K\setminus T\mid T}}^{(\boldsymbol v)}
 \right)
 f\bigl(
  \boldsymbol u_T,
  L_{K\setminus T\mid T}\boldsymbol u_T+\boldsymbol v
 \bigr)
 \right|_{\boldsymbol v=0}.
 
\end{equation}
Then \eqref{eq:conditional-Rees-Wick} induces an isomorphism
\[
 \mathbf W^{\rho,S}_{K\to T}:
 \mathcal L_{K\mid S}
 \xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ }
 \mathcal L_{T\mid S},
 \qquad
 [f\operatorname{vol}_K]
 \longmapsto
 [\mathsf W^\rho_{K\to T}f\operatorname{vol}_T],
\]
where determinant orientation lines are identified as in
\cref{thm:gaussian-face-cube}.  For \(S\subset T\subset K\subset L\), the
polynomial operators satisfy strictly
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf W^\rho_{K\to T}
 \circ\mathsf W^\rho_{L\to K}
 =
 \mathsf W^\rho_{L\to T}.
 
\end{equation}
and, with the determinant-line convention above, so do the induced lattice
maps.  Moreover, after localisation at \(\rho\), these maps intertwine the
cohomological radial connections in the Gaussian-normalised gauge:
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf W^{\rho,S}_{K\to T}
 \nabla_{\rho,K}^{\mathrm{phys}}
 =
 \nabla_{\rho,T}^{\mathrm{phys}}
 \mathbf W^{\rho,S}_{K\to T}.
 
\end{equation}
Thus \eqref{eq:physical-face-horizontality} is an identity from
\(\mathcal L_{K\mid S}[\rho^{-1}]\) to
\(\mathcal L_{T\mid S}[\rho^{-1}]\).  Equivalently, after multiplication
by \(\rho^3\), it is an identity of the unlocalised lattices.
title: Conditional Rees face maps
\cite{ACK10}

body:
[Proposition prop:Wishart.integrated.deBruijn of arXiv:2606.04859, 'Stein's method for the Wishart distribution'] Under the assumptions of Proposition~(prop:Wishart.deBruijn of the paper), we have
\begin{equation}
\mathrm{Ent}(\mu \, \| \, \xi)
= \int_0^{\infty} J_{\mathcal{W}, \Sigma}(\mu_t \mid \xi) \, \mathrm{d} t
= \int_0^1 \frac{1}{2\tau} J_{\mathcal{W}, \Sigma}(\mu_{\tau} \mid \xi) \, \mathrm{d} \tau.
\end{equation}
Assume furthermore that $\mu$ is the law of a random matrix $\mathfrak{X}$ and that this law has Lebesgue density $f_{\mathfrak{X}}$, that is, $\mu(\mathrm{d} X) = f_{\mathfrak{X}}(X) \, \mathrm{d} X$. Equivalently, if $f_{\xi}$ denotes the Lebesgue density of $\xi$, then the initial relative density is $g(X) = f_{\mathfrak{X}}(X)/f_{\xi}(X)$. Assume also that $\mathfrak{X}$ has finite differential entropy
\[
H(\mathfrak{X}) \vcentcolon= -\int_{\mathcal{S}_{++}^d} f_{\mathfrak{X}}(X)\log(f_{\mathfrak{X}}(X)) \, \mathrm{d} X.
\]
If $\mathsf{E}[\mathfrak{X}] = \mathsf{E}[\mathfrak{W}_{\infty}] = \alpha \Sigma$ and $\mathsf{E}[\log(|\mathfrak{X}|)] = \mathsf{E}[\log(|\mathfrak{W}_{\infty}|)]\in \mathbb{R}$ with $\mathfrak{W}_{\infty}\sim \xi$, then
\begin{equation}
H(\mathfrak{W}_{\infty}) - H(\mathfrak{X})
= \int_0^{\infty} J_{\mathcal{W}, \Sigma}(\mu_t \mid \xi) \, \mathrm{d} t
= \int_0^1 \frac{1}{2\tau} J_{\mathcal{W}, \Sigma}(\mu_{\tau} \mid \xi) \, \mathrm{d} \tau.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Integrated De Bruijn identity for the Wishart measure and entropy jump

[Theorem thm:sle of arXiv:2607.18070, 'The Brownian loop-catcher'] For \(\lambda=-c/2\in(0,1]\), let
\(\kappa\in[2,\frac83)\) be in~(equation eq:c-kappa of the paper).  
Let $\eta_-$ and $\eta_+$ be the lower and upper boundaries of \(K_\lambda^{D;a,b}\), respectively (i.e.~$\eta_\pm=\overline{\partial D_K^\pm\setminus \partial^\pm D}$). Then \(\eta_-\) is chordal
\(\SLE_\kappa(\kappa-2)\) in \(D\) from \(a\) to \(b\), with force point
at \(a^+\); conditionally on \(\eta_-\), \(\eta_+\) is chordal \(\SLE_\kappa(\kappa-4)\) in the component adjacent
to \(\partial^+D\),
with force point at \(a^-\).\footnote{At \(\kappa=2\), the law of the second curve
can be viewed as the \(\rho\downarrow-2\) limit of chordal \(\SLE_2(\rho)\) with force
point at \(a^-\); equivalently, $\eta_\pm$ are the two prime-end sides
of a chordal \(\SLE_2\) trace.} As a consequence, we have the following coupling between $\SLE_\kappa$ and Brownian excursion:
\[
 \eta_-\cup\eta_+\subset\gamma_{\mathrm{BE}}^{D;a,b}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Boundary identification

body:
[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2604.20617, 'Structured random perturbations of \\ tridiagonal twisted Toeplitz matrices'] Fix a compact set $K\Subset \C\setminus \Sigma$, where
\[
\Sigma:=\left\{z\in\C:\exists x\in[0,1]\text{ such that }|\xi_1(x,z)|=|\xi_2(x,z)|\right\}
\cup
\left\{z\in\C:\exists x\in[0,1]\text{ such that }\xi_1(x,z)^2=1\right\},
\]
and for each $x\in[0,1]$ the numbers $\xi_1(x,z),\xi_2(x,z)$ are the roots of
\[
\lambda^2-\frac{z-b(x)}{c(x)}\lambda+\frac{d(x)}{c(x)}=0
\]
ordered so that $|\xi_1(x,z)|>|\xi_2(x,z)|$ on $K$.

Then, for every fixed block index $j$ and every $\varepsilon>0$,
\[
\prob\!\left(
\left|
\frac{\det(R_{k-1}^{(j)}-zI)}{\det(R_k^{(j)}-zI)}
-\frac{1}{c(jk/n)\,\xi_1(jk/n,z)}
\right|>\varepsilon
\right)=o(1),
\]
and
\[
\prob\!\left(
\left|
\frac{\det(R_k^{(j)'}-zI)}{\det(R_k^{(j)}-zI)}
-\frac{1}{d(jk/n)\,\xi_1(jk/n,z)}
\right|>\varepsilon
\right)=o(1),
\]
uniformly for $z\in K$.

Consequently,
\[
\Theta_k^{(j)}(z):=
\frac{c(jk/n)d(jk/n)\det(R_{k-1}^{(j)}-zI)\det(R_k^{(j+1)'}-zI)}
{\det(R_k^{(j)}-zI)\det(R_k^{(j+1)}-zI)}
\]
satisfies
\[
\Theta_k^{(j)}(z)\longrightarrow
\frac{1}{\xi_1(jk/n,z)^2}
\qquad\text{in probability, uniformly for }z\in K.
\]
In particular, there exists $\delta_K>0$ such that
\[
\prob\!\left(|1-\Theta_k^{(j)}(z)|\ge \delta_K \right)=1-o(1)
\qquad (z\in K).
\]

body:
Let b ∈ C^1(R^n × R; R^n) with sup_{(x,t)} ||D_x b(x,t)|| < ∞, and let g ∈ C^1(R^n). For (x,t) let s ↦ X(s;x,t) be the solution of d/ds X = b(X,s), X(t;x,t) = x; by the global Lipschitz bound in x this flow exists for all s ∈ R and is C^1 in (s,x,t). Then u(x,t) := g( X(0;x,t) ) is the unique C^1 solution of the Cauchy problem u_t + b(x,t)·Du = 0 in R^n × R, u(x,0) = g(x). In particular, for constant b the solution is u(x,t) = g(x - tb), and solutions are constant along the characteristic curves s ↦ X(s;x,t). With a source term, u_t + b·Du = f(x,t) with f continuous, the unique C^1 solution (when it is C^1) is u(x,t) = g(X(0;x,t)) + ∫_0^t f( X(σ;x,t), σ ) dσ.
b ∈ C^1 with globally bounded x-derivative (this gives a globally defined C^1 flow; without a growth restriction characteristics can blow up in finite time and the formula only holds locally)
g ∈ C^1 (a merely continuous g gives the same formula but only a weak/viscosity solution)
the equation is linear in u: the characteristics do not depend on the solution, which is why no shocks form

[Lemma lem:mesoscopic-descendant-independence-paper of arXiv:2606.08683, 'Exact Fourier dimensions of dyadic Mandelbrot cascades under minimal integrability'] Fix \(0<m\le k\), and let \(G\subset[1,2]\) be finite.  For \(|u|=m\), set
\[
    Z_u(\eta)
    =
    e^{-2\pi i a_u2^k\eta}H^{(u)}_{k-m}(\eta),
    \qquad \eta\in G.
\]
Conditional on \(\mathcal F^X_m\), the family
\[
    \{Z_u:|u|=m\}
\]
is independent.  Each \(Z_u\) is independent of \(\mathcal F^X_m\), has the law
of
\[
    \{H_{k-m}(\eta):\eta\in G\}
\]
up to deterministic unimodular phases, and satisfies
\[
    \mathbb{E}[Z_u\mid\mathcal F^X_m]=0
\]
coordinatewise.

[Definition of arXiv:2609.00636, 'Forcing monochromatic subdivisions'] Let $0<\alpha<1$ and $t\ge 1$. A graph $F$ on $q$ vertices is an

\[
|N_F(X)|\ge t|X|
\qquad\text{for every }X\subseteq V(F)
\text{ with }|X|\le \frac{\alpha q}{t}.
\]
A graph is $m$-\emph{minor-universal} if it contains every graph with at
most $m$ vertices and at most $m$ edges as a minor.

body: [Defn of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] If $\mathcal{G}_1$ and $\mathcal{G}_2$ are two foliations on $\mathbb{T}^2$, then say that $\mathcal{G}_1$ has \textbf{lower slope} than $\mathcal{G}_2$ at a point $x\in \mathbb{T}^2$ if positively oriented tangent vectors in $T_x\mathcal{G}_1$ and $T_x\mathcal{G}_2$ combine to form a positively oriented basis of $T_x\mathbb{R}^2$. We say that $\mathcal{G}_1$ has \textbf{pointwise lower slope} than $\mathcal{G}_2$ if $\mathcal{G}_1$ has greater slope than $\mathcal{G}_2$ at every point in $\mathbb{T}^2$. In this case, we write $\mathcal{G}_1 \prec \mathcal{G}_2$. Note that $\prec$ is a partial order when restricted to $\Phi$-horizontal foliations.

[Lemma 39 (Negligibility of integrals compared to the pole) of arXiv:2512.09136, 'On the Green's functions and Martin boundary structure of a planar diffusion in a disconti'] Suppose $x^* \in (0, \M)$. Let $z_0 \in \R^2$, $\alpha_0 \in [0,\alpha^*_+)$, and let $x_c$ be such that $x^* < x_c < \min(x(\alpha_0),\M)$. body:
[Lem 29 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] The function $V$ defined by \eqref{e:freeprob.V} is strictly convex on the interval $(z_0,+\infty)$, with $V(z)\to\infty$ as $z\to\infty$.
As a consequence, $V$ has a unique minimizer on the interval $[z_0,+\infty)$, which we denote $z_{\min}$.

\begin{proof} For $z>z_0$, we calculate
    \beq
        
        V'(z)
        = 1 - \alpha \frac{m_2(z)}{m(z)^2} \sum_{j=1}^r \lambda_j
            \bigg(\frac{\hv_j m(z)}{\alpha - \hv_j m(z)}\bigg)^2\,.
    \eeq
Recall that $m:(\hw_1,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ is strictly decreasing, and we have
$\alpha - \hv_j m(z) > 0$ for all $z>z_0$. It follows that, on  the interval
$(z_0,\infty)$, the function
    \[
    \frac{m(z)}{\alpha-\hv_j m(z)}
    = \frac{1}{\alpha/m(z)-\hv_j}
    \]
is strictly decreasing, \emph{regardless of the sign of $\hv_j$}. Consequently, in \eqref{e:fp-V-pr}, each term
    \[      \bigg(\frac{\hv_j m(z)}{\alpha - \hv_j m(z)}\bigg)^2\]
is strictly decreasing on $(z_0,\infty)$, again \emph{regardless of the sign of $\hv_j$}. In the special case $s=1$, we have $m_2(z)=m(z)^2$, so we conclude in this case that $V'$ is strictly increasing on the interval $(z_0,\infty)$. For $s\ge2$, we note that $m_2(z)/m(z)^2$ is positive, and
    \[
        \frac{d}{dz}\bigg[ \frac{m_2(z)}{m(z)^2}\bigg]
        = \frac{2}{m(z)^3} \Big(m_2(z)^2 - m(z)m_3(z)\Big)
        < 0
    \]
by the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality. It therefore follows in this case as well that $V'$ is strictly increasing, and so $V$ is strictly convex, on the interval $(z_0,\infty)$.
Finally, as $z\to\infty$, $m(z) \to 0$. Therefore the first term of $V(z)$ tends to $\infty$ while the second term remains bounded, and so $V(z) \to \infty$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 29 of arXiv:2608.29416

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2608.24552, 'Asymptotic Rounding Laws for Optimal Thresholds in Secretary Problems'] Under the hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{thm:general_threshold_principle}, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
r_n^{\mathrm{opt}}\in\{\lfloor\ell n\rfloor,\lfloor\ell n\rfloor+1\}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\{\ell n\}<1-c-\frac{\varepsilon_n}{|A|}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
r_n^{\mathrm{opt}}=\lfloor\ell n\rfloor,
\]
whereas
\[
\{\ell n\}>1-c+\frac{\varepsilon_n}{|A|}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
r_n^{\mathrm{opt}}=\lfloor\ell n\rfloor+1.
\]
Consequently, whenever
\[
\left|\{\ell n\}-(1-c)\right|>\frac{\varepsilon_n}{|A|},
\]
the optimal threshold is unique and satisfies
\[
r_n^{\mathrm{opt}}
=
\lfloor\ell n+c\rfloor.
\]

Choose a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ of $W$ and extend it to a basis
\[
  e_1,\ldots,e_n,e_{n+1},\ldots,e_m
\]
of $H$.

We first prove that $j$ is injective. If $S_1,S_2\in\Gr(q,W)$ and
$j(S_1)=j(S_2)$, then $S_1$ and $S_2$ are equal as linear subspaces of $H$,
and hence $S_1=S_2$. Thus $j$ is injective.

We next describe its image. Define
\begin{equation}
  Z=\left\{
  S\in\Gr(q,H):
  p_J(S)=0\text{ for every }J\nsubseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}
  \right\}.
\end{equation}
Here $J\nsubseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ means that $J$ contains at least one index
greater than $n$. We prove that
\begin{equation}

Own work, proof (unaudited), W719-T295-C002 v1. For every fixed alpha>=1024 and c>0, m=ceil(alpha d), iid a_i~N(0,I_d), and fixed unit x_*, use f(x)=(1/(4m)) sum_i ((a_i^T x)^2-(a_i^T x_*)^2)^2 and eta=c/log d. With probability tending to one there is a sample-dependent point x_0 with ||x_0-x_*||=1/10 whose unmodified GD iterates diverge in norm. Take x_0=x_*+(1/10)u, where u is the signed unit direction of a_1 aligned with its signal projection. Its first update has norm Omega_(alpha,c)(d/log d). Writing S=A^T A/m and B=H_*/2, on S>=I/2 and ||B||=O_alpha(log d), every x of norm R satisfies ||x-eta grad f(x)|| >=eta R^3/4-(1+eta||B||)R. The first update enters the region where this lower bound is at least 2R. The logarithmic bound on B uses C001. This refutes a simultaneous guarantee for every point in the fixed ball; it does not refute random independent starts or convergence along incoherent trajectories.
fixed alpha>=1024 and c>0
iid real standard Gaussian rows
fixed deterministic unit signal
sample-dependent initialization allowed
unconstrained unmodified GD

[Lem Duality Lemma of arXiv:2411.07671, 'Long Time Behavior of General Markov Additive Processes'] Consider a MAP $( (\xi,\Theta),\mathbb{P})$ such that there exists a MAP $( (\xi,\Theta) ,  \tilde{\mathbb{P}})$ with weak reversibility property. Let $\hat{\mathbb{P}}_{0,\theta}$ be the law of $(-\xi,\Theta)$ under $\tilde{\mathbb{P}}_{0,\theta}$. Then, for every $t>0$, we have \begin{enumerate}
    \item for $x\in\mathbb{R}$, the process 
    $(\xi_{(t-s)-}-\xi_t,\Theta_{(t-s)-})_{0\leq s \leq t}$  under $\mathbb{P}_{x,m}$ has the same law as $(\xi_s,\Theta_s)_{0\leq s \leq t}$ under $\hat{\mathbb{P}}_{0,m}$.
\item $(\Theta_0, t-\Bar{g}_t, \Theta_t, \Bar{\xi}_t-\xi_t, \Bar{g}_t, \Bar{\Theta}_t, \Bar{\xi}_t)$ under $\hat{\mathbb{P}}_{0,m}$ is equal in distribution to\\ $(\Theta_t,\Bar{g}_t,\Theta_0,\Bar{\xi}_t,t-\Bar{g}_t,\Bar{\Theta}_t,\Bar{\xi}_t-\xi_t)$ under $\mathbb{P}_{0,m}.$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 8 (Lead-change survival bound) of arXiv:2605.09641, 'The Ballot Event for Two-Player Coupon Collection: A Renewal--Catalan Asymptotic'] Fix $g_0\ge0$, and define
\[
        \tau_a:=\inf\{n:S_n\ge a\}.
\]
For every integer $a$ with $\max\{s_0,1\}\le a\le d$ one has the trivial bound
\[
        \Prob_{s_0,g_0}(\tau_a<\tau)\le 1.
\]
Moreover, there is a constant $C_{g_0}$ such that, whenever
\[
        a\ge 4\max\{s_0,\lceil\sqrt d\rceil\},
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
        \Prob_{s_0,g_0}(\tau_a<\tau)
        \le
        C_{g_0}\frac{\sqrt d}{a}.
\end{equation}

[Lemma lem.inv_lo of arXiv:2603.11043, 'An asymptotically optimal bound for the concentration function of a sum of independent int'] Let $N$ be a fixed positive integer, $c > 0$ and $\epsilon > 0$.
    Then there exist $r=r(N, c, \epsilon)$ and  $v=v(N, c, \epsilon)$ such that the following holds.
    
    For any sequence $X_1, \dots, X_n$ of independent random variables on $\mathbb{Z}$
    such that $\mathbb P(X_i = j) = \frac {a_{i,j}} N$ where $a_{i,j} \in \mathbb{Z}$, 
    $\mathcal{Q}(X_i) = \max_{j} \frac{a_{i,j}} N \le \frac 1 2$
    and $\mathcal{Q}(X_1 + \dots + X_n) \ge \frac c {\sqrt n}$
    there
    exists a symmetric GAP ${\bf A}$
    of rank at most 
    $r$ and volume at most $v$
    such that all but at most $\epsilon n$ of random variables $X_i$
    have their support contained in ${\bf A}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Let G be a finite simple graph on n >= 3 vertices. The closure cl(G) is obtained from G by repeatedly adding an edge between any two non-adjacent vertices u, v with deg(u) + deg(v) >= n, until no such pair remains; the resulting graph cl(G) does not depend on the order in which edges are added. Then G is Hamiltonian if and only if cl(G) is Hamiltonian. [Bondy and Chvatal (1976); see Diestel, Graph Theory]
title: Bondy-Chvatal Closure Lemma

Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). After the optimism reading was refuted (P20), the gain was located row by row: the per-evaluation-row relative-score gain of the long-only stack over least squares against the bootstrap variance of the least-squares stack at that row. P22 (a) REFUTED at the pre-registered 0.2: the within-cell median Spearman between a row's gain and the least-squares variance load at that row is 0.13 over the 40 EMIT cells (positive in 36 of 40; 0.37 on Y2, 0.01 on Y1); (b) HELD on Y2, REFUTED as an every-group claim: the top-decile-load rows carry 47 pct of Y2's gain (a uniform spread gives 10) but only 11 pct on Y1 (20 on Y3, 32 on Y4); (c) HELD: across the 40 EMIT cells the gain rank-correlates 0.54 with the variance-load share of least squares' error, and 0.65 with the share the constraint removes (least squares minus nn1) - the between-cell statistic that optimism (P20) failed to be; (d) REFUTED as written: the OCO-2 top-decile share reaches 0.40 on sco2, but as the share of a gain of -0.55 pct it is the ratio of two near-zero numbers and does not test the clause; falsifier (within-cell correlation at or below zero) not triggered. Reading: where the gain is large (Y2, +18) it sits where least squares is uncertain - row-level rank correlation 0.37, 47 pct of the gain on the tenth of rows with the largest variance; where it is modest (+5 to +6) it is spread over the rows; between cells the variance-load share of least squares' error predicts the gain (0.54) and the variance the constraint removes predicts it better (0.65). The calibration and evaluation rows share the same target-norm distribution, so this is not a split shift; the gain leans toward the small-norm evaluation rows the reported metric weights most. Cell level: the variance the constraint removes (least squares' bootstrap variance share minus the long-only stack's) predicts the gain within every output group (Spearman 0.79, 0.87, 0.54, 0.43 on Y1-Y4; 0.69 across 40 cells with the group effect removed), while the L1 norm of the least-squares weights does not survive the group adjustment (0.02): the constraint pays what it saves in estimation variance at the rows it is scored on. Fresh-split replication (split C, SPLIT_SEED 11): P23 (a) REFUTED at the per-group 0.5, HELD in the aggregate: on split C the within-group Spearman between the gain and the variance removed is +0.59, +0.49, +0.64, +0.22 on Y1..Y4 and +0.74 across the 40 cells with the group effect removed (split B: +0.69); (b) REFUTED: the split-B variance-removed share predicts the split-C gain only on Y1 and Y2 (+0.72, +0.47; Y3 +0.09, Y4 -0.24; demeaned +0.17), and the split-B gain itself predicts the split-C gain only weakly (Y1 +0.82, Y4 +0.47, Y2 +0.15, Y3 -0.14); (c) HELD: the long-only stack beats least squares on 35 of 40 split-C cells (mean +9.59 against +8.83 on split B); falsifier (any group at or below 0.2, or the demeaned correlation at or below 0.3) not triggered.

\[
 x_1=(-2,-2),\qquad x_2=(-2,-1),
\]
and define
\begin{equation}
 X=N_1x_1+N_2x_2-(x_1+x_2).
\end{equation}
Then \(\Sigma\) is positive definite, but for
\[
 t_1=(-2,1),\qquad t_2=(-1,2),
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 C_X(t_1)=\frac{35}{39},\qquad
 C_X(t_2)=0,
 \qquad C_X(t_1+t_2)=1.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 C_X(t_1+t_2)>C_X(t_1)+C_X(t_2).
\end{equation}

[Definition ATTRACTOR of arXiv:2603.12774, 'Synchronization by noise for stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Browni'] Let $\Phi$ be an RDS. A random compact set $\mathcal{A}$ is { called pullback attractor} if 
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item [1)] $\mathcal{A}$ is invariant under \( \Phi \).
		\item [2)] For every compact set $K\subseteq  \mathcal{X}$ 
		we have
		\[ \lim\limits_{t\to\infty} \sup\limits_{x\in K} d(\Phi^t_{\theta_{-t}\omega}(x), \mathcal{A}(\omega)  )=0~~~\mathbb{P}-a.s. \]
	\end{enumerate}
	We call $\mathcal{A}$ a {weak attractor} if the convergence in 2) holds in probability instead of almost surely. The set $\mathcal{A}$ is called a {(weak) point attractor} if it satisfies the properties stated above, assuming that the compact set $K$ in condition 2) consists of a single point.~A (weak) point attractor is said to be {minimal} if it is contained in every other (weak) point attractor.

 |D\chi_{F_j}|&\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}|D\chi_G|
 
\end{align}
and
\begin{equation}
 G=H\setminus L,
 \qquad
 |D\chi_G|=\HH^n\llcorner P+|D\chi_L|.
\end{equation}

 Let also $\mathcal{H}$ be a set of functions $h : \R \to \R$ such that $\esp[\vert h(W) \vert] < \infty$ for every $h$, the Stein solution $g_{h}$ exists, is absolutely continuous and satisfies \eqref{H_1} 

 for almost every $x > 0$,
 for some $\beta \in (-\infty, \alpha)$ and $C_{1} > 0$ independent of $h$.
 Then, we have

\underset{h \in \mathcal{H}}{\sup} \ \vert \esp[h(W)] - \esp[h(Z)] \vert \leq \underset{h \in \mathcal{H}}{\sup}\ \vert &\esp[h(W)\ind_{\lb W \leq K \rb}] - \esp[h(Z)]F_{W}(K)\vert\\

body:
Let X and Y be Banach spaces and T : X -> Y a bounded linear operator that is surjective. Then T is an open map: the image of every open subset of X is open in Y; equivalently there is c > 0 such that the image of the unit ball of X contains the ball of radius c in Y. Corollaries: a bounded linear bijection between Banach spaces has a bounded inverse (the bounded inverse theorem), and two complete norms on one vector space that are comparable in one direction are equivalent. Completeness of BOTH spaces is needed: the identity from (C[0,1], sup norm) to (C[0,1], L^1 norm) is bounded and bijective and its inverse is unbounded, the target not being complete.
X and Y Banach (complete normed) spaces
T bounded, linear and surjective

[Dfn 3. dfn: Polish functor of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{Polish functor}] 
  We say that a functor $\tau$ is \textit{Polish} if there exist a functor $\tilde{\tau}$
  and, for each $(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}$,
  a sequence $(\tilde{\tau}_{k}(S))_{k=1}^{\infty}$ of open subsets in $\tilde{\tau}(S)$
  satisfying the following conditions.
  \begin{enumerate} [label = (P\arabic*), leftmargin = *]
    \item 
      The functor $\tilde{\tau}$ is complete, separable and continuous. 
    \item 
      The functor $\tau$ is a topological subfunctor of $\tilde{\tau}$.
    \item 
      For every $(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}$,
      it holds that $\tau(S) = \bigcap_{k \geq 1} \tilde{\tau}_{k}(S)$.
    \item 
      Let $f: S_{1} \to S_{2}$ be a root-and-distance-preserving map
      between $(S_{i}, d^{S_{i}}, \rho_{S_{i}}) \in \mathfrak{M},\, i=1,2$.
      Then, $\tilde{\tau}_{f}^{-1}(\tilde{\tau}_{k}(S_{2})) = \tilde{\tau}_{k}(S_{1})$
      for each $k \geq 1$. 
      In particular,
      $\tilde{\tau}_{f}^{-1}(\tau(S_{2})) = \tau(S_{1})$.
  \end{enumerate}
  We call $(\tilde{\tau}, (\tilde{\tau}_{k})_{k \geq 1})$ a \textit{Polish system} of $\tau$.
title: Dfn 3. dfn: Polish functor of arXiv:2412.08236

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Universal leading cover-time upper bound under transitivity structural calculation Result: For continuous-time rate-one random walk on the cycle, tau0=(n^2-1)/6 while E C=n(n-1)/2. To see the latter, when exactly k consecutive vertices have been visited the walker is at an endpoint, and the mean time to enlarge the range is k, by gambler-ruin exit-time calculation on a path of length k+1. Summing k=1,...,n-1 gives E C. Hence E C/(tau0*log n) is asymptotic to3/log n and tends to0 even though tau2/tau0 stays positive. Check: Poissonizing the jump chain preserves the mean duration because the holding means are one. The cycle explicitly shows that failure of the source sufficient condition does not imply failure of the desired upper bound. Label: proof of an elementary inversion and a conditional process-transfer lemma, not a solution of Problem 6.4. Current literature status is unverified offline.

The earlier C0135-A001 says both that a clock has size m^2 log(m) and that its inverse is sqrt(t)/log(t), and later uses the different scale sqrt(t) log(t). These cannot be equivalent scales.

Let f(x)=x^2 log(x), x>=1. It is strictly increasing for x>1. If a deterministic increasing clock T_m is asymptotic to m^2 log(m), its generalized inverse is asymptotic to sqrt(2t/log(t)). Indeed put u(t)=sqrt(2t/log(t)). Then log(u(t))=0.5(log(t)+log(2)-log(log(t))), so f(u(t))/t tends to one. For every fixed eps>0, T_floor((1-eps)u(t))/t tends to (1-eps)^2<1 and T_ceil((1+eps)u(t))/t tends to (1+eps)^2>1, which brackets the inverse. max_{k<=floor(nT)} |S_k-X_k| / a_n -> 0 in probability,

and S_floor(nt)/a_n converges in distribution in the Skorokhod J1 topology to a continuous process Y, then X_floor(nt)/a_n converges to Y in J1. The uniform norm bounds their J1 distance by using the identity time change; convergence in probability of this distance and the metric-space Slutsky lemma give the result. A uniform O_P(sqrt(n)) backtracking bound would suffice, since sqrt(n)/a_n=1/log(n) tends to zero.

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2506.18834, '\large\bf On the random-time and finite-time ruin probability for widely dependent claim s'] Let $\xi_{i},i\geq1$ be WUOD random variables with a common distribution $V$ on $(-\infty,\infty)$
such that $E\xi_1s_1(\xi_1)<\infty$ for some positive even function $s_1(\cdot)$ on $(-\infty,\infty)$
satisfying $s_1(x)\underline{\uparrow}\infty$.
Then the following three conclusion hold.

(1) There exists a positive even function $s_2(\cdot)$ on $(-\infty,\infty)$ such that
\begin{eqnarray}
s_2(x)\underline{\uparrow}\ \infty,\ \ s_2(x)s_1^{-s+1}(x)\overline{\downarrow}\ 0\ \ \ \text{for any}\ \ \ s>1\ \ \
\text{and}\ \ \ E\xi_1s_1(\xi_1)s_2(\xi_1)<\infty.
\end{eqnarray}

(2) Write $s(\cdot)=s_1(\cdot)s_2(\cdot)$ and $V_{s(\cdot)}^+(x)=s^{-1}(x)\int_{0\le y\le x}ys(y)V(dy)+x\overline{V}(x),\ x\ge0$, then
\begin{eqnarray}
V^+_{s(\cdot)}(x)=o\big(s^{-1}_1(x)\big)\ \ \ \ \ \text{and}\ \ \ \ \ s_1^{-l}(x)=o\big(V^+_{s(\cdot)}(x)\big)
\ \ \ \text{for any}\ \ l>1,
\end{eqnarray}

(3) If $E\xi_1=0$ and there is an integer $m\ge1$ such that
$$x^ms^{-1}(x)\underline{\uparrow}\ \infty\ \ \ \ \text{and}\ \ \ x^{m-1}s^{-1}_1(x)\overline{\downarrow}\ 0,$$
then for any $\gamma>0$, $v>0$ and $0<\theta<1$, there exist $x_0=x_0\big(v,\gamma,m,\theta,V,s_1(\cdot),s_2(\cdot)\big)\ge 1$
and $C=C(x_0)>0$ such that for each integer $n\ge1$,
\begin{eqnarray}
P\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\xi_i>x\Big)\le n\overline{V}(vx)+Cs_{U,V}(n)\big(V_{s_{(\cdot)}}^+(vx)\big)^{(1-\theta)v^{-1}}
\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \text{for all}\ \ x\ge \max\{\gamma n,x_0\}.
\end{eqnarray} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Derive d_s in d = 2 from known exponents via the Einstein relation and locate what is rigorous. Result: On the IIC of two-dimensional critical percolation (which exists, Kesten) the walk is subdiffusive with d_s = 2 d_f/d_w where d_f = 91/48 is the fractal dimension of the IIC and d_w is the walk dimension; the Einstein relation d_w = d_f + zeta with zeta the resistance exponent gives d_s = 2 d_f/(d_f + zeta), and the conjectured resistance exponent of the 2D IIC is zeta ~ 0.98 (numerically the backbone resistance exponent), giving d_s = 2 x 1.896/(1.896 + 0.98) = 1.318, matching the numerics quoted by the source; the rigorous status: Kesten proved subdiffusivity with d_w > 2, and the resistance exponent is only known to lie in an interval (zeta > 0 from Kesten; zeta <= something from the one-arm/backbone dimension). A rigorous upper bound: d_s <= 2 d_f/(d_f + zeta_min) where zeta_min is any rigorous lower bound on the resistance exponent; with zeta >= (d_f - d_backbone)?? no, the rigorous lower bound of Kesten for the resistance across an annulus of the IIC uses the number of disjoint crossings (the backbone), giving resistance >= (log n)^c at least... Kesten's bound is R(0, B(n)^c) >= n^{epsilon} for some small unexplicit epsilon. So no explicit rigorous bound on d_s beyond d_s < 4/3?? not even that. Recorded: d_s in 2D is determined by the resistance exponent through d_s = 2 d_f/(d_f + zeta) (rigorous given that the Einstein relation holds, which is a theorem for strongly recurrent graphs with the volume and resistance exponents, Barlow-Coulhon-Kumagai), so the open content is the value of zeta; for 3 <= d < 6 the existence of the IIC is the first obstacle. Key identity: d_s = 2 d_f/(d_f + zeta) on the 2D IIC (Einstein relation); d_f = 91/48 known, zeta unknown (numerically about 0.98). Obstruction: Resistance exponent of the 2D IIC unknown; IIC existence unproved for 3 <= d < 6.

If Assumption~\ref{ass:perron-excitation} holds, then \(\rho(\Top)<1\).

body:
[Corollary 10 (Exhaustive finite-time breakdown alternative) of arXiv:2609.00501, 'Uniqueness of Finite-Time Varifold Limits for the M\"obius-Invariant Willmore Flow'] Let $F\colon[0,T_{\max})\times\Sigma\to\Sph^3$ be a maximal smooth
MIWF with
\[
 T_{\max}=T_{\max}(F_0)<\infty,
 \qquad W(0)\leq8\pi.
\]
Then exactly one of the following mutually exclusive alternatives
holds:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\Alph*)}]
 \item there are $t_j\nearrow T_{\max}$ and $x_j\in\Sigma$ such that
 \[
  |A^0_{F_{t_j}}(x_j)|^2\longrightarrow0;
 \]
 \item uniform nonumbilicity holds and the unique limit is zero:
 $\Var_{T_{\max}}=0$;
 \item uniform nonumbilicity holds, $\Var_{T_{\max}}\neq0$, and
 $\spt\Var_{T_{\max}}$ is a closed embedded orientable Lipschitz
 surface of genus zero;
 \item uniform nonumbilicity holds, $\Var_{T_{\max}}\neq0$, and
 $\spt\Var_{T_{\max}}$ is a closed embedded orientable Lipschitz
 surface of genus one.
\end{enumerate}
In alternatives \textup{(C)} and \textup{(D)}, the limit has unit
density.  No assertion made here excludes alternative \textup{(D)}.

[Theorem 2 (Large deviations principle) of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] Let \(a>1\) and \(I_a=[1,a]\). Then \(N_a(L)/L\) satisfies a large deviations principle on \([0,\infty)\) with speed \(L\) and good rate function
\[
J_a(x):=\sup_{\theta\in\mathbb{R}}\{\theta x-\Lambda_a(\theta)\},
\qquad x\geq0.
\]
That is, for every Borel set \(A\subset[0,\infty)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
-\inf_{x\in A^\circ}J_a(x)
&\le \liminf_{L\to\infty}\frac{1}{L}\log\mathbb{P}\left(\frac{N_a(L)}{L}\in A\right) \\
&\le \limsup_{L\to\infty}\frac{1}{L}\log\mathbb{P}\left(\frac{N_a(L)}{L}\in A\right) \le -\inf_{x\in \overline{A}}J_a(x),
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(A^\circ\) and \(\overline A\) denote the interior and closure of \(A\) in the relative topology of \([0,\infty)\). Moreover, \(J_a\) is strictly convex on \((0,\infty)\) and vanishes only at \(\lambda_a=\frac{1}{4\pi}\left(1-\frac{1}{a}\right)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Large deviations principle

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:c9be99a48552ce7792d95452efe3dd94a94a66b949407b7a7f28edb9260d64bd","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/c9/c9be99a48552ce7792d95452efe3dd94a94a66b949407b7a7f28edb9260d64bd.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:918cd3c546d66c2f7525a6b902166f5b62c3ae08f13f6c01f9aaccf300b49373","bundle_entry_key":"operator-contraction","bundle_id":"population.t419-julia-dilation-operator-contraction-all-scale-flat-20261020","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"LoRA convergence and Julia operator dilation","draft":"w705/bundle_013.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.lowrank:factor-gd-small-step-operator-residual-contraction-dilation","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T419-C024 v2: small-step operator-norm residual contraction

Kind:moved. Target:1. Status:proof (unaudited). No novelty claimed.

## Statement

Let E be any real m-by-p matrix, B any m-by-r matrix and A any r-by-p matrix. Set e=||E||op and h=||B||op^2+||A||op^2. For any eta>0 with eta(e+h)<=1/2, put

 Phi(E,B,A)=E-eta(BB^T E+E A^T A)+eta^2 E A^T B^T E.

Then ||Phi(E,B,A)||op<=||E||op. In particular, when E=BA-Delta, Phi is exactly the residual after one simultaneous GD step for ||BA-Delta||F^2/2. No rank assumption, Gaussian assumption, balance or commutation is required. The lemma gives a sufficient small-step condition, not an optimal one. It does not claim spectral monotonicity at an arbitrary loss-decreasing step.

The hardest point is that orthogonal dilation commutes with this particular nonlinear update after compression. The proof explicitly checks the quadratic term. The algebraic dilation is the classical Julia/Halmos construction; its primary provenance is P. L. Robinson, "Julia operators and Halmos dilations", arXiv:1803.09329, Theorem0 p.1 and Theorem1 p.2. The rectangular block here is the Julia operator with its column blocks switched; Theorem2 concerns the square-space special case. The construction and its properties are proved below from an SVD rather than assumed from a named theorem. The primary source gives the classical dilation, not this GD contraction. Literature overlap and independent correctness remain unaudited.

## 1. Orthogonal residuals

First suppose m=p=N and E=eQ for an orthogonal N-by-N matrix Q, with e>0. Multiplying Phi/e on the right by Q^T gives

 (Phi/e)Q^T=I-eta(DD^T+CC^T)+eta^2 e C D^T,

where D=B and C=Q A^T. Indeed E A^T B^T E/e=e Q A^T B^T Q, which becomes e C D^T after right multiplication by Q^T. This checks the order of the quadratic term.

Let W=[D C] be N-by-2r and set

 H = [[I_r,0],[-eta e I_r,I_r]].

The preceding matrix equals Z=I-eta W H W^T. Direct expansion gives

 I-Z^T Z = eta W[H+H^T-eta H^T W^T W H]W^T.

Now ||W||op^2<=||D||op^2+||C||op^2=h,

 H+H^T >=(2-eta e)I, and ||H||op<=1+eta e.

The first bound follows either from the 2-by-2 scalar block eigenvalues 2+eta e and 2-eta e, or the quadratic-form inequality 2|x^T y|<=||x||^2+||y||^2. The second follows by writing H=I+N, where the sole nonzero off-diagonal block of N has operator norm eta e. Consequently

 H+H^T-eta H^T W^T W H
 >=[2-eta e-eta h(1+eta e)^2]I
 >=[2-1/2-(1/2)(3/2)^2]I
 =(3/8)I>=0.

Only eta e<=1/2 and eta h<=1/2 are used in this estimate; they follow from the stated sufficient condition. It follows that Z^T Z<=I and ||Z||op<=1. Right multiplication by Q^T preserves the norm, so ||Phi||op<=e in this orthogonal case.

## 2. Explicit orthogonal dilation of an arbitrary rectangular contraction

Suppose e>0 and let F=E/e, so ||F||op<=1. The matrices I_m-FF^T and I_p-F^TF are positive semidefinite. Their positive semidefinite square roots define the (m+p)-by-(p+m) real matrix

 Q = [[F, (I_m-FF^T)^(1/2)],[(I_p-F^TF)^(1/2),-F^T]].

This is square because m+p=p+m. It is orthogonal. For a direct verification, take an SVD F=U Sigma V^T. It gives the exact intertwining identity

 F(I_p-F^TF)^(1/2)=(I_m-FF^T)^(1/2)F,

since each paired singular direction contributes the scalar sigma_i sqrt(1-sigma_i^2) on both sides, and the unmatched zero singular directions contribute zero. Multiplying Q Q^T therefore gives identity diagonal blocks and zero cross blocks. Thus Q Q^T=I, which for a finite square real matrix also implies Q^T Q=I. In particular the upper-left m-by-p compression of eQ is E. This proof also covers rectangular F with singular value1; no inverse of a defect square root is used.

## 3. Compression preserves the nonlinear update

Use the orthogonal residual Etilde=eQ, the padded factor Btilde=[B;0_(p-by-r)], and Atilde=[A,0_(r-by-m)]. These are compatible factors in the enlarged N=m+p dimensional problem, with ||Btilde||op=||B||op and ||Atilde||op=||A||op. The step condition is unchanged, so section1 gives ||Phi(Etilde,Btilde,Atilde)||op<=e.

Consider its first m rows and first p columns. The linear terms compress to BB^T E and E A^T A because Btilde Btilde^T and Atilde^T Atilde are zero off their leading diagonal blocks. For the quadratic term, the first m rows of Etilde Atilde^T equal E A^T, and the first p columns of Btilde^T Etilde equal B^T E. Hence the leading m-by-p block of

 Etilde Atilde^T Btilde^T Etilde

is exactly E A^T B^T E, not a block contaminated by the defect square roots. Therefore the full compressed residual is exactly Phi(E,B,A). Compression by orthogonal coordinate projections cannot increase operator norm, proving the lemma. If e=0, every term of Phi is zero, completing the missing degenerate case.

## Relation to GD and limitations

Multiplication of B_next=B-eta E A^T and A_next=A-eta B^T E gives the displayed Phi with its positive quadratic term. Thus the lemma applies to ordinary simultaneous GD without replacing it by alternating updates, a continuous flow, or a split contraction. At larger steps the proof does not give monotonicity. It provides no statistical-risk or convergence theorem without a separate factor bound and positive-margin argument. The application is saved separately as C025. body:
[Lemma lem6.5 of arXiv:2411.03528, '\textbf{On a boundary of the central limit theorem for strictly stationary, reversible Mar'] Suppose $\phi: [1,\infty) \to (-\infty, 0]$ is a function
that satisfies the following conditions: \hfil\break
(a) $\phi$ is strictly decreasing and convex on $[1, \infty)$; and \hfil\break
(b) one has that
\begin{equation}

\lim_{x \to \infty} \phi(x)\ =\ -\infty 
\indent {\rm and} \indent
\lim_{x \to \infty} \frac {\phi(x)} {x}\ =\ 0.
\end{equation}

   Let $\Gamma$ denote the set of all points $x \in (1, \infty)$ (the open half line) 
such that $\phi$ is {\rm not} differentiable at $x$.
Refer to Notations (nt6.4 of the paper)(A)(B).   
For each $y \in (1, \infty) - \Gamma$, let 
$L^{(y)}: \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$ denote the affine function whose graph is tangent to that 
of $\phi$ at the point $(y, \phi(y))$ --- that is, the affine function that satisfies
\begin{equation}

L^{(y)}(y)\ =\ \phi(y) \indent {\rm and} \indent 
L^{(y)}(x)\ \leq\ \phi(x)\ \ {\rm for\ all}\ x \in [1, \infty). 
\end{equation}
 
   Then the following statements (I) and (II) hold:
\medskip

   (I) The following statements hold: \hfil\break 
(i) For each $x \in (1, \infty)$, $\phi(x) < \phi(1) \leq 0$. \hfil\break 
(ii) For each $y \in (1,\infty) - \Gamma$,  
$[{\rm slope\ of}\ L^{(y)}] = \phi'(y) < 0$. \hfil\break   
(iii) The function $x \mapsto \phi'(x)$ for $x \in (1,\infty) - \Gamma$, 
is nondecreasing. \hfil\break  
(iv) One has that $\lim_{x \to \infty,\, x \notin \Gamma} \phi'(x) = 0$. 
\medskip

   (II) For any negative number $D$ and any positive number 
$s$, there exists a number    
$T = T(\phi, D, s) > 1$ with the following property:

   For each $y \in [T,\infty)  - \Gamma$, the affine function 
$L^{(y)}$ in (the entire sentence of) eq.\ ((eq6.502 of the paper))
satisfies 
\begin{equation}

-s\ \leq\ [{\rm slope\ of}\ L^{(y)}]\ =\ \phi'(y)\ <\ 0 
\indent {\rm and} \indent
L^{(y)}(0)\ \leq\ D. 
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem6.5 of arXiv:2411.03528

[Lemma lem:chemical_easy of arXiv:2508.18809, '{\bf Critical long-range percolation III: The upper critical dimension}'] Let $G=(V,E,J)$ be a transitive weighted graph. The following inequalities hold for every $0\leq \beta<\beta_c$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathbb E_\beta \sum_{x\in K} d_\mathrm{chem}(o,x)\leq (\mathbb E_\beta|K|)^2$.
\item $\mathbb E_\beta|K|^2\leq \mathbb E_\beta|K|\mathbb E_\beta \sum_{x\in K} (1+d_\mathrm{chem}(o,x))$.
\item $\frac{d}{d\beta}\mathbb E_\beta|K| \leq \sup_e \frac{J(e)e^{-\beta J(e)}}{1-e^{-\beta J(e)}}\mathbb E_\beta \sum_{x\in K} d_\mathrm{chem}(o,x)$. 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:chemical_easy of arXiv:2508.18809

body:
Let X and Y take finitely many values with joint pmf p and marginal p_X, entropies in natural logarithms with 0 ln 0 = 0. For each x choose a pmf K_x on the values of Y with K_x(y) = p(x, y)/p_X(x) whenever p_X(x) > 0, and K_x arbitrary when p_X(x) = 0. Then H(X, Y) = H(X) + sum over x of p_X(x) H(K_x), and this sum, the conditional entropy H(Y | X), equals -sum over (x, y) with p(x, y) > 0 of p(x, y) ln(p(x, y)/p_X(x)) whatever the choices at zero-probability x. Hence H(Y | X) >= 0 and H(X, Y) >= H(X). By induction, H(X_1, ..., X_k) = sum over j of H(X_j | X_1, ..., X_{j-1}) for finitely-valued X_1, ..., X_k. Dividing every term by ln 2 gives the statement in bits.
X and Y take finitely many values
natural logarithms with 0 ln 0 = 0
K_x the conditional pmf where p_X(x) > 0 and any pmf where p_X(x) = 0

[Thm large_time_limit_non_L1 of arXiv:2605.29073, 'Volterra clocks and their pure-jump limits: \\hitting times of curved boundaries'] Assume $K \in L^1_{loc}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+\,,\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+)$ is completely monotone with $\int_0^{\infty}\,K(s)\,ds = + \infty\,$, and $\lambda > 0\,$. Then the following hold:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item If $\widetilde{G_0}(t) \to G_0^* \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+$ as $t \to + \infty\,$, then $(W^n \,, X^n) \Rightarrow (W^*\,, X^*)$ in $D^{\circ}[0\,,T]\,$, where $W^*$ is standard Brownian motion, and $X^*$ is the constant process
        $$
        X^*_t := \inf\{s \geq 0 \,:\, \lambda s - \nu W^*_{f(s)} > G_0^* \}\,, \quad t \leq T\,.
        $$
        \item If there exists a sequence $c_n \downarrow 0$ such that, defining
        $$
        \widetilde{G_0}^n(t) := c_n\,\widetilde{G_0}(nt)\,, \quad f^n(x) := c_n^2\,f(x / c_n)\,, \quad \widetilde{W}^n_t := c_n\,W^n_{t / c_n^2}\,, \quad t\,,x \geq 0\,,
        $$
        we have $\widetilde{G_0}^n \to G_0^*$ pointwise on $[0\,,T]$ for some continuous $G_0^*\,$, and $f^n \to_{l.u.} f^*$ on $\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+\,$, then $(\widetilde{W}^n\,, c_n\,X^n) \Rightarrow (W^*\,, X^*)$ in $D^{\circ}[0\,,T]\,$, where $W^*$ is a standard Brownian motion, and
        $$
        X^*_t := \inf\{s \geq 0\,:\, \lambda s - \nu W^*_{f^*(s)} > G_0^*(t) \}\,, \quad t \leq T\,.
        $$
    \end{enumerate}

PRIVATE REDUCTION, author-recorded. Via the Kruskal/invasion coupling the MST on T_{n,d}, d > 6, is governed by the critical window p = p_c(1 + O(V^{-1/3})): the V^{1/3} diameter (Heydenreich-van der Hofstad Open Problem 16.3) follows from (a) a window cluster of size V^{2/3} with intrinsic diameter V^{1/3} existing with positive probability (torus plateau plus the Kozma-Nachmias intrinsic one-arm exponent applied on the torus), (b) subcritical clusters at p_c(1 - eps) having intrinsic diameter O(eps^{-1} log V), summable over the geometric ladder of levels, and (c) uniqueness and concentration of the giant just above the window (Open Problem 13.2), the same three ingredients as in the complete-graph proof of Addario-Berry, Broutin, Goldschmidt and Miermont. The scaling limit (Open Problem 16.4) additionally needs metric-space (Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov) convergence of the window clusters and the product merging rule, both unproved on the torus and both consequences of the wrapping mechanism if it could be made quantitative.
Uniform i.i.d. edge weights on T_{n,d}, d > 6
Kruskal/invasion coupling between the MST and percolation
title: Diameter and scaling limit of the minimal spanning tree on high-dimensional tori reduce to supercritical uniqueness and the geometry of window clusters

[Lem 49 (Polynomial tail control on the random sum) of arXiv:2506.19123, 'The longest increasing subsequence of Brownian separable permutons'] The random sum 
\[
\sum_{k=1}^\infty (\sttm_k)^{\frac{1}{2}-\alpha }\left(\sum_{n=\sttm_k}^{\sttm_{k+1}-1} r(n) f(T_n)\right)
\]
is almost surely finite.
Furthermore, there exists $\eps>0$ such that almost surely, for $k_0$ large enough,
\begin{align*}
\sum_{k=k_0}^\infty (\sttm_k)^{\frac{1}{2}-\alpha }\left(\sum_{n=\sttm_k}^{\sttm_{k+1}-1} r(n) f(T_n)\right) \leq k_0^{-\eps}.
\end{align*}
title: Polynomial tail control on the random sum

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2605.05864, 'Classification and Metrization of Classes of Smooth measures'] Assume that $\mu\in{\cal S}$ and its $\alpha$-potential
    $R_\alpha\mu$ belongs to $L^\infty(E;m)$ for  all $\alpha>0$. 
    Let $\{F_\ell\}$ be a (compact) nest attached 
    to $\mu$, namely, $1_{F_\ell}\mu \in {\cal S}_0$ for all $\ell \in{\mathbb N}$.
    Then for any compact set $K$ and $\alpha>0$,
    there exists a $C=C(\alpha, K)>0$ such that
    the following hold for all $\ell \in{\mathbb N}:$ 
    \begin{equation} 
      \mu(K\cap F_\ell) \le
      C \sqrt{\form_\alpha(U_\alpha(1_{F_\ell \cap K}\mu), U_\alpha(1_{F_\ell \cap K}\mu))}
    \end{equation}
    and 
    \begin{equation} 
      \form_\alpha(U_\alpha(1_{F_\ell \cap K}\mu), U_\alpha(1_{F_\ell \cap K}\mu))
      \le \Big(1+\frac{|\alpha-1|}{\alpha} \Big) \|R_1\mu\|_{\infty} \mu(K \cap F_\ell).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 16 of arXiv:2605.05864

[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2609.00988, 'Covering Projective Height Balls by Subspaces in Rigid Adelic Spaces'] There is a constant $c_7>0$, effectively computable from $d, r_2, |D_K|$, with the following property. For every nonzero prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset\cO_K$, with
$q=\Nm\mathfrak p$, and every $R\ge1$, there is a subset
$S(R,\mathfrak p)\subset\cO_K/\mathfrak p$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)]
\[
|S(R,\mathfrak p)|\ge c_7\min\{q,R^d\};
\]
\item[(ii)] every class in $S(R,\mathfrak p)$ has a representative
$a\in\cO_K$ with $\|a\|_\infty\le R/2$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 8 of arXiv:2609.00988

[Definition 1 (GOE Matrix) of arXiv:2606.16018, 'A non-asymptotic bound on the TV distance between a \\Wishart matrix and an appropriately '] A random matrix \(\mG\in\bbR^{n \times n}\) is drawn from the \emph{Gaussian orthogonal ensemble} if it is a symmetric matrix with independent entries on the upper triangle such that for any \(i < j\)
	\[
		[\mG]_{ii} \sim \cN(0,2)
		\qquad
		\text{and}
		\qquad
		[\mG]_{ij} \sim \cN(0,1).
	\]
	We will denote this random matrix as \(\mG \sim \mathrm{GOE}(n)\).
	A GOE matrix is also distributed as \(\mG = \frac1{\sqrt 2} (\mH + \mH^\top)\) where \(\mH\in\bbR^{n \times n}\) has iid \(\cN(0,1)\) entries.

[Proposition 46 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Fix a limiting point \(\xi=(\mu_t)_{t<1}\) based at
\(q\in Y^{\rm prod}\), let
\(\tau_i\searrow0\), and set
\[
 g_i(s)=\tau_i^{-1}g(1+\tau_i s).
\]
Choose \(H_{2m+2}\)-centres \(p_i\) of the time-\((-1)\) measures
\(\mu_{i,-1}:=\mu_{1-\tau_i}\) with respect to \(g_i(-1)\).
After passing to a subsequence realizing a tangent space at \(\xi\), fix
a finite \(A\ge0\) and any \(q_i\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
 d_\eta(q_i,q)\le A\sqrt{\tau_i}.
\end{equation}
There is \(D_A<\infty\) such that
\begin{align}
 \operatorname{diam}_{g_i(-1)}F_{q_i}&\le D_A,
 \\
 F_{q_i}&\subset B_{g_i(-1)}(p_i,D_A).
 
\end{align}
For every finite \(B\ge0\), there is \(C_{A,B}<\infty\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{B_{g_i(-1)}(p_i,D_A+B)}
 |\Rm(g_i(-1))|_{g_i(-1)}\le C_{A,B}.
\end{equation}
The constants may depend on the fixed limiting point and the realizing
subsequence, but not on \(i\).

[Defn 2 of arXiv:2608.12804, 'Scaling Limits for Ising Models on Inhomogeneous Random Graphs and Applications'] Let $H$ be a Hilbert space, and let
$\{s_j(T)\}_{j\geq1}$ denote the singular values of a compact
operator $T:H\to H$, that is, the eigenvalues of
$(T^*T)^{1/2}$, counted with multiplicity. The operator $T$ is
called \emph{trace--class} if
\[
    \sum_{j\geq1}s_j(T)<\infty,
\]
and \emph{Hilbert--Schmidt} if
\[
    \sum_{j\geq1}s_j(T)^2<\infty.
\]
If $T$ is self-adjoint, then its singular values are the absolute
values of its eigenvalues $\{\lambda_j(T)\}_{j\ge 1}$, and hence these conditions are equivalent
to
\[
    \sum_{j\geq1}|\lambda_j(T)|<\infty
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \sum_{j\geq1}\lambda_j(T)^2<\infty,
\]
respectively.

body:
[Df 34 of arXiv:2609.03836, 'Koszul Orlik--Solomon Algebras from Non-supersolvable Arrangements'] Let $E$ be a finite set.
    Let $E = E_0 \sqcup E_1 \sqcup E_2$ be a tripartition of $E$.
    Write $E_{01} = E_0 \cup E_1$ and $E_{12} = E_1 \cup E_2$.
    Suppose $M$ is a matroid on $E_{01}$ and $N$ is a matroid on $E_{12}$ such that
    $E_1$ is a modular flat of $M$ and
    $M|_{E_1} = N|_{E_1}$.
    
    One defines the \textbf{generalized parallel connection} of $M$ and $N$ along $E_1$---denoted $P_{E_1}(M, N)$---to be the unique matroid on $E$ whose flats are the subsets $F \subseteq E$ such that 
    $F \cap E_{01}$ is a flat of $M$ and 
    $F \cap E_{12}$ is a flat of $N$.
    The rank of this matroid is $\rk P_{E_1}(M, N) = \rk M + \rk N - \rk_M E_1$.
    When $E_1$ is modular in $N$ also, we say (following Ziegler) that $M$ is the \textbf{modular join} of $M$ and $N$ along $E_1$.
    In this case, $P_{E_1}(N, M)$ also exists and is equal to $P_{E_1}(M, N)$.

Iterating CRUX 9.3's Var(X_Mn) <= (beta/2) M Var(X_n) from n_0 with n_j = M^j n_0 gives the exponent 2 chi = 1 + log(beta/2)/log M, so M is a FREE DESIGN PARAMETER selecting which exponent is proved rather than an obstruction; at beta = 1 it takes M = 8 to deliver 2 chi = 2/3 exactly. If Var ~ n^(2 chi) exactly then Var(X_Mn) = M^(2 chi) Var(X_n), so the inequality is tight precisely when beta = 2 M^(2 chi - 1): at chi = 1/3 that is 1.587 at M=2, 1.260 at M=4, EXACTLY 1.000 at M=8, 0.794 at M=16. So 'beta <= 1 at M = 8' is not a sufficient condition for chi <= 1/3 that some other route might reach - it IS the statement chi <= 1/3, with zero slack. An inequality that is an equality at the truth cannot be established by an argument that loses constants, and every technique in reach loses constants somewhere. This also explains BETA_MEASURED_20260815's numbers: beta falling 1.76, 1.58, 1.45, 1.38 toward about 1.22 is, against beta = 2 M^(-1/3), the tight value at M near 4.4, consistent with KPZ holding and the block geometry sitting near M = 4.
