[Lemma lem:longinequali of arXiv:2512.12124, 'A discontinuous percolation phase transition on the hierarchical lattice'] Let $\varpi \in \Lambda_{M_g+jr,\infty}$ for some $jr \in \{r,\ldots, \bar{r}_{g+1} - r\}$. Then
    \begin{align}
        &\notag \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varpi \textnormal{ bad} \right)  
        \\
        & \notag 
        \leq
        \sum_{\varphi, \varphi^\prime \in \chi_{r}(\varpi)} \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varphi \textnormal{ not good} \right) \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varphi^\prime \textnormal{ not good} \right) 
        \\
        & \notag \hspace{7mm}
        + \sum_{\varphi \in \chi_{r}(\varpi)} \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varphi \textnormal{ not good} \right) \mathbb{P}_{\bar{J}} \left( G^{\mathrm{bl}} \left( \chi_{r}(\varpi) \setminus \{\varphi \} \right) \textnormal{ not connected} \right)
        \\
        & \notag \hspace{7mm}
        + \sum_{\gamma \in \{L^{-r}, \ldots, 1- L^{-r} \} }  \sum_{\varphi \in \chi_{r}(\varpi)} \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varphi \textnormal{ is $\gamma$-mediocre} \right) \sum_{A \subset \chi_{r}(\varphi) : |A|\geq \gamma L^r } \mathbb{P}_{\bar{J}} \left( A \nsim \chi_{r}(\varpi) \setminus \{ \varphi \} \right) 
        \\
        & \hspace{7mm}
        +
        \sum_{m \in \{0,r,\ldots, jr - r \} } \left( L^{jr - m} \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \Lambda_{M_{g}+m}(0) \textnormal{ bad} \right) \right)^N
    \end{align}
    and, for every $\gamma \in \{L^{-r},\ldots,1-L^{-r} \}$,
    \begin{align}
        \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varpi \textnormal{ is $\gamma$-mediocre} \right)
        \leq
        \mathbb{P}_{\bar{J}} \left( G^{\mathrm{bl}} \left( \chi_{r}(\varpi) \right) \textnormal{ has a cluster of density at most $\gamma$} \right).
    \end{align}
    If $\varpi \in \Lambda_{M_{g+1},\infty}$, then, for every $\gamma \in \{ L^{-r},\ldots, 1-L^{-r} \}$,
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varpi \textnormal{ is $\gamma$-mediocre} \right)
        \leq
        \mathbb{P}_{\bar{J}} \left( G^{\mathrm{bl}} \left( \chi_{r}(\varpi) \right) \textnormal{ has a cluster of density at most $\gamma$} \right),
    \end{equation}
    and
    \begin{align}
        
        &\mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varpi \textnormal{ bad} \right)  
        \\
        & \notag \leq
        \sum_{\varphi, \varphi^\prime \in \chi_{r}(\varpi)} \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varphi \textnormal{ not good} \right) \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varphi^\prime \textnormal{ not good} \right) 
        \\
        & \notag \hspace{4mm}
        + \sum_{\varphi \in \chi_{r}(\varpi)} \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varphi \textnormal{ not good} \right) \mathbb{P}_{\bar{J}} \left( G^{\mathrm{bl}} \left( \chi_{r}(\varpi) \setminus \{\varphi \} \right) \textnormal{ not connected} \right)
        \\
        & \notag \hspace{4mm}
        + \sum_{\gamma \in \{L^{-r}, \ldots, 1- L^{-r} \} }  \sum_{\varphi \in \chi_{r}(\varpi)} \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varphi \textnormal{ is $\gamma$-mediocre} \right) \sum_{A \subset \chi_{r}(\varphi) : |A|\geq \gamma L^r } \mathbb{P}_{\bar{J}} \left( A \nsim \chi_{r}(\varpi) \setminus \{ \varphi \} \right) 
        \\
        & \notag \hspace{4mm}
        +
        \sum_{m \in \{M_{g}, M_{g}+r,\ldots, M_{g+1} - r \} }  \hspace{-12mm} \left( L^{M_{g+1} - m} \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \Lambda_{m}(0) \textnormal{ bad} \right) \right)^N
        \\
        & \notag \hspace{4mm}
        +
        \sum_{m \in \{M_{g-1}, M_{g-1}+r,\ldots, M_{g} - r \} } \hspace{-12mm} \exp \left( e L^{\bar{r}_{g+1}} L^{M_{g}-m} \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \Lambda_{m}(0) \textnormal{ bad} \right) - \log(g)^3 \lceil L^{\bar{r}_{g+1} + M_{g} - m} g^{-1-\varepsilon} \rceil \right) .
    \end{align}

[Theorem Polynomial approximation to $C^k$ functions of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] Suppose that $f:\RR\to \RR$ is a $k$-th order differentiable function with $|f^{(k)}|\le M $. 
  Let $\mu$ be a distribution on $\RR$. 
  Then there exists a polynomial $p$ of degree 
  
  
  \begin{enumerate}
    
    
    \item $O(\mathrm{poly}(1/\varepsilon)) $ under strictly sub-exponential $\mu$; 
    \item $O(\exp\{\mathrm{poly}(1/\varepsilon)\})$ under sub-exponential marginal $\mu$.
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Polynomial approximation to $C^k$ functions

[Def $G$-gerbe of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Let $G$ be a finite group scheme, and suppose $\mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{Z}$ is a morphism between two smooth separated Deligne--Mumford stacks. 
Then, equipping $\mathcal{Z}$ with the \'etale topology, the morphism $\mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{Z}$ is a {\em $G$-gerbe} if there exists an \'etale covering $\{Z_i \to \mathcal{Z}\}$ such that there is an isomorphism $\mathcal{Y} \times_{\mathcal{Z}} Z_i \simeq BG$ over $\mathcal{Z}/Z_i$ for every $i$.
title: $G$-gerbe

[Definition 15 (Regularity used in this paper) of arXiv:2609.03361, 'Grassmann--Pl\"ucker Parametrization of Convolutional Filter Subspaces:\ Regularity and Cl'] Let $f:X\to Z$ be a morphism from a smooth algebraic variety $X$ to an
algebraic variety $Z$. If the differential
\[
  \dd f|_x:T_xX\longrightarrow T_{f(x)}Z
\]
is injective for every $x\in X$, then $f$ is called a \emph{regular
parametrization}. Equivalently,
\[
  \rank(\dd f|_x)=\dim X
\]
for every $x\in X$.
title: Regularity used in this paper

body:
[Lemma 36 of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{lem:tet}
 Let $w,w'>0$ and $u,u'\geq 0$, let $a^2 = w^2 + u^2$, $b^2 = (w')^2 + (u')^2$, and let $f - d = \delta = u + u'$. 
There is a unique positive solution in $x$ for the equation 
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\Delta_{abx}^2}{abx} \frac{\Delta_{xdf}^2}{xdf}
 =
 \left(\frac{9 \diamondplus_{abfd}^2}{4a b fd}\right).
\end{equation}
Denote it $c_*$. Then,
$$c_{**} := \lim_{\substack{f \rightarrow \infty\\ f - d = \mathbf{\delta}} } c_*$$ exists. 
Also,  for a target right-angled or obtuse triangle \((a,b,c_{**})\),  where $c_{**}^2 \geq a^2 + b^2$,     the required 
\(\delta^2\) is given by
\[
\delta^2
=
\frac{
2c_{**}^4(c_{**}^2-a^2-b^2)
}{
(c_{**}^2-a^2+b^2)(c_{**}^2+a^2-b^2)
}.
\]
Moreover, suppose
\[
a_n=a\sqrt n,\qquad b_n=b\sqrt n,
\]
and
\[
Q_n=n^{21}+O(n^{20}),\qquad
d_n^2=Q_n-2u'n^{11}+O(n^{10}),
\qquad
f_n^2=Q_n+2u n^{11}+O(n^{10}).
\]
If \(c_n\) is the maximizer of
\[
x\longmapsto
\frac{\Delta_{a_nb_nx}^2}{a_nb_nx}
\frac{\Delta_{xd_nf_n}^2}{xd_nf_n},
\]
then
\[
c_n=c_{**}\sqrt n+O(n^{-1/2}).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 36 of arXiv:2607.04138

[Definition 45 of arXiv:2512.07202, 'Hitting Probabilities for Hypoelliptic Differential Equations Driven by Fractional Brownia'] Let \( N \geqslant 1 \) be an integer. Suppose \( V = (V_1, \ldots, V_d) \) is a collection of vector fields on \( \mathbb{R}^N \), each of class \( \mathcal{C}^{N-1}(\mathbb{R}^N;\mathbb{R}^N) \). Let \( \mathbf{g} \in T^{(N)}(\mathbb{R}^d) \), the step-\( N \) free nilpotent group over \( \mathbb{R}^d \), and let \( y \in \mathbb{R}^N \). Then the (increment of the) step-\( N \) Euler scheme is defined by
\[
\mathcal{E}_{(V)} (y, \mathbf{g}) := \sum_{k=1}^{N} \sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_k \in \{1, \ldots, d\}} V_{i_1} \cdots V_{i_k} I(y)\, \mathbf{g}^{k; i_1, \ldots, i_k}.
\]
title: Definition 45 of arXiv:2512.07202

[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2606.14812, 'Joint convergence in Wiener chaos via transport hierarchy and Malliavin covariances'] Let $p\geq 2$ and let $(X_N=I_p(f_N),N\geq 1)$ satisfy 
	\eqref{c1}. Let $Y_N=I_q(g_N)$ with $p<q<2p$ and 
	$\sup_N\|g_N\|_{H^{\otimes q}}<\infty$  with the decomposition (\ref{decomp}). Assume that
	\begin{equation}
		(Y_N, Y_{1,N})
		\xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{(d)}(Y, Y_1).
	\end{equation}
	Then:

 $(X_N,Y_N)\xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{(d)}(Z,Y)$ 
		where $Z\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$ and $Y$ admits the decomposition 
		\begin{equation}
			Y = \frac{Z}{p\sigma^2}Y_1 + \varepsilon, 
		\end{equation}
		where $\varepsilon$ is independent of $Z$.  The characteristic function of $(Z,Y)$ is
		\begin{equation}
			\varphi(u,v) = e^{-\frac{\sigma^2 u^2}{2}}\,
			\mathbf{E}\!\left[e^{iv\varepsilon - \frac{uv}{p}Y_1 
				- \frac{v^2}{2p^2\sigma^2}Y_1^2}\right].
		\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 16 of arXiv:2606.14812

[Proposition 93 (Revealed c\`adl\`ag critical entrance) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Let $M$ be a square-integrable c\`adl\`ag $H$-valued martingale whose complete
predictable bracket path $R$ is revealed by $\mathcal G_0$ and satisfies
$\mathbb E\operatorname{Tr}R_T<\infty$.  Then its split anchor
\[
 (M_t,A_t,[M]_t)
\]
has a c\`adl\`ag version in $\mathscr G_{\mathrm{crit}}(H)$.  If
$P_k\uparrow I$ are finite-rank orthogonal projections, then
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{t\le T}d_{\mathrm{crit}}\!\left(
 (P_kM_t,P_kA_tP_k,P_k[M]_tP_k),(M_t,A_t,[M]_t)\right)
 \longrightarrow0
 \quad\text{in probability}.
 
\end{equation}
Consequently the anchor has the optional completion of
\Cref{cc:thm-critical-optional-quotient}.

[Prop Probability of hitting the origin, driftless case of arXiv:2606.06187, 'How to Study Reflected Brownian Motion in a Quadrant via Kernel Functional Equations?\\ \m'] When the drift is zero, i.e., $\mu=0$, we have
$$
\mathbb{P}[T<\infty]= \begin{cases}1 & \text { if } \alpha>0, \\ 0 & \text { if } \alpha \leqslant 0. \end{cases}
$$
If $\alpha \leqslant 0$, the vertex is not reached.  
If $0<\alpha<2$, the vertex is reached, but the amount of time spent at the vertex has zero Lebesgue measure.  
If $\alpha \geqslant 2$, the process hits the vertex and stays there. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Probability of hitting the origin, driftless case

Let sigma be a continuous sigmoidal function (sigma(t) tends to 1 as t goes to +infinity and to 0 as t goes to -infinity). Then finite sums of the form sum a_j sigma(<w_j, x> + b_j) are dense in C(K) for every compact K in R^n: any continuous function on a compact set can be uniformly approximated by a one-hidden-layer network. The width required may grow with the target accuracy; the theorem asserts density, not efficiency.

[Lemma Glem1 of arXiv:2411.06089, '{\Large \bf Averaging principle for semilinear slow-fast rough partial differential equati'] Let $T> 0$ and $\mathbf B \in \mathscr{C}^\gamma([0,T]; \mathbb R^d)$ for some $\gamma \in (1/3, \gamma_0)$. and

&\Big\| \int_0^{\cdot} S_{\cdot-u} G_1 (Y_u) d\mathbf{B}_u , G_1 (Y) \Big\|_{\mathcal{D}_{\mathbf B}^{2\gamma,\eta}}  \nonumber\\
 \lesssim & \|G_1 (Y)_0^\prime\|_{\mathcal H_{-2\gamma}^{d \times d}}+\|G_1 (Y)\|_{\infty,0}
+T^{\gamma-\eta}(1+|B|_\gamma+|B^2|_{2\gamma})\|G_1 (Y),G_1 (Y)^{\prime}\|_{\mathscr{D}_{S,\mathbf B}^{2\gamma,2\gamma,0}}.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Draft counterexample awaiting independent review: For the same parameter p=99/100 every finite-width strip S_k=Z x {-k,...,k} has no infinite Bernoulli bond cluster, while their increasing union Z^2 percolates. An enclosing closed dual circuit count gives theta_Z2(p)>=1-10557/2352250000>0.99999. Consequently unrestricted transfer of nonpercolation from every approximating graph to its union is false, even when every graph is infinite, connected, locally finite and quasi-transitive. This example is supercritical in the plane and the strip critical probabilities do not converge to the planar critical probability; it does not refute critical nonpercolation on higher-dimensional lattices or a bridge with additional threshold hypotheses.

[Proposition 17 of arXiv:2608.11637, '\bf Uniform Local Asymptotics for L\'evy Processes with Subexponential Jumps'] For any $ \theta>0$, $K\geq 0$ and $\delta_1\geq \delta_0>0$, we have as $n\to\infty$,
 	\beqlb
 	\sup_{x\geq \theta n} \sup_{|y|\leq Kb(x)}\sup_{\delta\in[\delta_0,\delta_1]}
 	\bigg| \frac{  \mathbf P\big(  \widetilde{S}_n \in x-y+\Delta_\delta\big)}{n\cdot \nu\big(x+\Delta_\delta\big)}-1
 	\bigg| \to 0.
 	\eeqlb
 	Moreover, there exists a constant $C>0$ such  that for all $n\geq 1$, $x\geq \theta n$ and $\delta \in [\delta_0,\delta_1]$, 
 	\beqlb
 	\sup_{|y|\leq Kb(x)} \mathbf P\big(  \widetilde{S}_n \in x-y+\Delta_\delta\big) \leq C\cdot n\cdot \nu\big(x+\Delta_\delta\big). 
 	\eeqlb (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 17 of arXiv:2608.11637

[Proposition prop:Lq-J-comonotonic of arXiv:2411.03609, 'Asymptotically optimal Wasserstein couplings for the small-time stable domain of attractio'] Pick $q \in (0,1]$. Assume that 
 the L\'evy measures of $\nu_{\bm{X}}$ and $\nu_{\bm{Y}}$ admit the radial decomposition in~(equation eq:radial_decomp of the paper)
and construct the processes $(\bm{L^X},\bm{L^Y})$ 
by~(equation eq:comono_coupling_2 of the paper).
For any $\varepsilon\in(0,\infty)$ (we may have $\varepsilon=\infty$ when $\bm{X}$ and $\bm{Y}$ are of finite variation), the coupling $(\bm{L^X},\bm{L^Y})$ satisfies 
\begin{equation}

\mathds{E}\bigg[\sup_{t \in [0,1]}\big|\bm{L^X}_t-\bm{L^Y}_t\big|^q\bigg]\leqslant  \int_{(0,\varepsilon)\times \mathbb{S}^{d-1}} |\rho_{\bm{X}}^{\leftarrow}(x,\bm{v})-\rho_{\bm{Y}}^{\leftarrow}(x,\bm{v})|^q \mathrm{d} x \otimes \sigma(\mathrm{d} \bm{v}).
\end{equation}
In particular, the following inequality holds
\begin{equation}

\begin{split}
\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X},\bm{Y})
&\leqslant |\bm{\varpi_X}-\bm{\varpi_Y}|^q
+\bigg(4\int_{[\varepsilon,\infty)\times \mathbb{S}^{d-1}}(\rho_{\bm{X}}^{\leftarrow}(x,\bm{v})-\rho_{\bm{Y}}^{\leftarrow}(x,\bm{v}))^2 \mathrm{d} x \otimes \sigma(\mathrm{d} \bm{v})\bigg)^{q/2}\\
&\qquad+2^qd^{q/2}|\bm{\Sigma_X}-\bm{\Sigma_Y}|^q
+\int_{(0,\varepsilon)\times \mathbb{S}^{d-1}} |\rho_{\bm{X}}^{\leftarrow}(x,\bm{v})-\rho_{\bm{Y}}^{\leftarrow}(x,\bm{v})|^q \mathrm{d} x \otimes \sigma(\mathrm{d} \bm{v}).
\end{split}
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:Lq-J-comonotonic of arXiv:2411.03609

body:
[Lemma lem:distinct-translation-budgets of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] After equal-time fusion, fix one relative weak order with $h\ge1$
ordered supernodes.  Reparametrize its physical translation orbit by the
first occupied time $a=t_1$.  If
$t_{j+1}-t_j=1+g_j$ with $g_j\ge0$, and $q$ is the total slack recorded
by the common one-variable Green series, admissibility in
$\{1,\ldots,m\}$ is
\[
 a+(h-1)+q\le m.
\]
Thus its Taylor budget is
\[
 M(a)=m-h+1-a,
 \qquad M(a+1)=M(a)-1.
\tag{3.2.10q$_{20}$}
\]
In particular distinct physical translations have distinct budgets.
If a root time was initially used to name the orbit, replacing it by
$t_1$ is a bijective reparametrization and changes no local state or
multiplicity.

[Theorem 39 (Convergence for a strictly positive density plus an atom) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Assume \hyp{A}{A} and \hyp{M}{M}. Then
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\ \sup_{A\in\XXA} \bigl| (T^{n}\circ\mu)(A) - \pi(A) \bigr| = 0
  \qquad\text{for every } \mu \in \Prob,
\]
and $\pi$ is the unique invariant probability measure of $T$. More precisely, the
singular mass is bounded by the probability that no move has yet been made:
\[
  \sing\bigl( T^{n}\circ\mu \bigm| \pi\bigr) \;\le\; \int_{\XX} r^{n} \dd\mu
  \qquad (\mu \in \Prob,\ n \in \Nz) ,
\]
and the right-hand side tends to $0$ for every $\mu \in \Prob$.

body:
[Theorem thm:min_sample of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Under the assumptions of Theorem~(thm:ci of the paper), 
we fix a desired accuracy (or tolerance)
$\varepsilon>0$ at a confidence level $1-\alpha$, with $\alpha\in(0,1)$, and introduce
\begin{align}
  \Theta_A(\varepsilon)
  \equiv
  \frac{1}{2\varepsilon^2}
  \left(\sqrt{\tilde\sigma_A^2} 
  + \sqrt{\tilde\sigma_A^2 + 2c_A\varepsilon}\right)^{2},
  
\end{align}
such that the minimal required time for a single trajectory (Theorem~(thm:tmin of the paper))
reads $t_{\textrm{min},A}(\varepsilon,\alpha) = \Theta_A(\varepsilon)\log(2N_\nu/\alpha)$. 

Then $\mathbb{P}^\nu(-\varepsilon \leq \widehat{A}_{n,t} - \E^\mu[\overline{A}_t] \leq \varepsilon) \geq 1-\alpha$, i.e., 
the confidence radius stays below the tolerance level, $r_A(\alpha,n,t) \leq \varepsilon$, with 
probability of at least $1-\alpha$, if and only if

\begin{align}
  nt \geq \Theta_A(\varepsilon)\left(\log\frac{2}{\alpha} + n\log N_\nu\right).
  
\end{align}
This fixes the minimal sample size and the minimal per-trajectory time as follows.

For fixed $t > \Theta_A(\varepsilon)\log N_\nu$, the
guarantee holds if and only if $n \geq n_{\min,A}$, where
\begin{align}
n_{\min,A}(\varepsilon,\alpha,t)
=\left\lceil\frac{\Theta_A(\varepsilon)\log(2/\alpha)}{t - \Theta_A(\varepsilon)\log N_\nu}
\right\rceil.

\end{align}
denotes the \emph{minimal sample size}. In the case that $t \leq \Theta_A(\varepsilon)\log N_\nu$, 
no finite number of independent trajectories is sufficient. 
At stationarity $N_\mu = 1$ we recover 
    \begin{align}
      n_{\min,A}(\varepsilon,\alpha,t)
      =\left\lceil\frac{t_{\textrm{min},A}(\varepsilon,\alpha)}{t}\right\rceil,
      
    \end{align}
and the required sample size is simple the minimal time of a single trajectory
(Theorem~(thm:tmin of the paper)) divided by the per-trajectory length, and any $t>0$ 
has a finite sample size.

For fixed $n$, Eq.~(equation eq:uq_full of the paper) holds if and only if $t \geq t_{\min,A}(n,\varepsilon, \alpha)$,
where
\begin{align}
  t_{\min,A}(n, \varepsilon, \alpha)
  =\frac{\Theta_A(\varepsilon)}{n}\left(\log\frac{2}{\alpha} + n\log N_\nu\right).
  
\end{align}
Notably, in the case $n=1$ this recovers $t_{\textrm{min},A}(\varepsilon,\alpha)$ from 
Eq.~(equation eq:tmin of the paper).
The corresponding one-sided guarantees hold under the same conditions with
$\log(2/\alpha)$ replaced by $\log(1/\alpha)$.

[Proposition 4 of arXiv:2606.16083, 'Eyring--Kramers asymptotics for infinite-dimensional stochastic gradient systems'] [NGS bound]

Let $g\in \mathrm{Lip}_b(B)$ with $\|g\|_{L^2(d\gamma_\beta)} =1$. Then 
\begin{align}

  \int_B
   \left[
      \frac1\beta\|\nabla g\|_H^2
      +V_\beta g^2
   \right]\,d\gamma_\beta
   \ge
   -\frac12\log\int_{\operatorname{supp}(g)} e^{-2V_\beta}\,d\gamma_\beta,
\end{align}
where $V_\beta$ is defined in \eqref{Eq:Def_V_beta}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

for some positive $p$ then 
\begin{enumerate}
\item the radial limit of $f$, say $f^{\ast}(\xi)$, exists a.e on $\mathbb{T}$

\item $\underset{r\rightarrow1^{-}}{\lim}\Vert f(r\cdot)-f^{*}\Vert_{p}=0$.
\item $\Vert f^{*}\Vert_{p}$ equals the $p^{th}$ Hardy norm of $f$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:two-vortex of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Let $\boldsymbol\kappa=(\kappa_1,\kappa_2)$ satisfy
$\kappa_1>0>\kappa_2$, and let
$(\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})\in\Lambda_2(D)$ be a strict local
minimum point of $W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}$.  Choose $\rho>0$ such that
\[
  B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,1})\times B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,2})
  \Subset\Lambda_2(D),
\]
and
\begin{equation}
  \begin{aligned}
  W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)
  &>W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}
  (\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})\\
  &\quad\text{for every }(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)\in
  \overline{B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,1})\times
  B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,2})}
  \setminus\{(\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})\}.
  \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Fix $M_i,R_i>0$ for $i=1,2$.  Then there exist positive constants
$C$, $\eta_0$, and $\varepsilon_0$, depending only on
$D,\rho$, and $\mathbf a_{*,i},\kappa_i,M_i,R_i$, $i=1,2$,
such that the following holds.

For every $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0$, let
$(\mathbf a_{1,\varepsilon},\mathbf a_{2,\varepsilon})
\in B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,1})\times B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,2})$, and let
$\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}\in L^\infty(D)$ be nonnegative and satisfy
\[
  \int_D\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}\,\mathrm d\mathbf x=|\kappa_i|,
  \qquad
  \|\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}\|_\infty
  \leq M_i\varepsilon^{-2},
  \qquad
  \operatorname{supp}\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}
  \subset B_{R_i\varepsilon}(\mathbf a_{i,\varepsilon}),
  \quad i=1,2.
\]
Set
$\omega_{\varepsilon,0}
:=\zeta_{1,\varepsilon,0}-\zeta_{2,\varepsilon,0}$.
Let $\omega_{\varepsilon,t}$, $t\in\mathbb R$, be the corresponding Yudovich
solution of (equation eq:euler-intro of the paper), and let
$\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,t}$ denote the transport of
$\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}$ by the associated Euler flow map.
If
\begin{equation}
  \eta^{(2)}_{\varepsilon,0}
  :=\sum_{i=1}^2\mathcal D(\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0})
  +\Bigl[W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}
  (\mathbf a_{1,\varepsilon},\mathbf a_{2,\varepsilon})
  -W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}
  (\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})\Bigr]
  +\varepsilon
  \leq\eta_0,
\end{equation}
then, for every $t\in\mathbb R$,
\begin{equation}
  \mathsf C(\zeta_{1,\varepsilon,t})
  \times\mathsf C(\zeta_{2,\varepsilon,t})
  \subset B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,1})\times
  B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,2}),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{align}
  &\sum_{i=1}^2\mathcal D(\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,t})
  +\sup_{(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)\in
  \mathsf C(\zeta_{1,\varepsilon,t})\times
  \mathsf C(\zeta_{2,\varepsilon,t})}
  \Bigl[
  W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)
  -W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}
  (\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})
  \Bigr] \leq C\eta^{(2)}_{\varepsilon,0}.
  
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Quantitative estimates: two opposite-sign vortices

[Definition 27 (Language relating to polymer models from \cite{ks}) of arXiv:2511.07350, 'Decoupling of clusters in independent sets in a percolated hypercube'] In these definitions, we use the notation $N(A)$ to denote the \emph{set of neighbors} of $A$ in $\Q$, rather than
the number of neighbors.
Additionally, $\cH$ denotes either $\cE$ or $\cO$.
\begin{itemize}
    \item
    A subset $A \sse \cH$ is said to be \emph{2-linked} if there is no decomposition $A = A_1 \cup A_2$ into
    nonempty sets $A_1$ and $A_2$ which satisfy $N(A_1) \cap N(A_2) = \emptyset$.

    \item 
    For a subset $A \sse \cH$, we denote by $[A]$ the \emph{closure} of $A$,
    defined to be the largest subset of $\cH$ with the same neighborhood set as $A$.
    In other words, $[A] = \{ v \in \cH : N(v) \sse N(A) \}$.

    \item
    A 2-linked set $\fp \sse \cH$ with $|[\fp]| \leq \fr{3}{4} 2^{d-1}$ is called a \emph{polymer}.

    \item
    Polymers $\fp_1$ and $\fp_2$ are said to be \emph{compatible} if $\fp_1 \cup \fp_2$ is not 2-linked.

    \item
		We denote by $\Sep[\cH]$ the set of pairwise compatible collections of polymers.
    
    \item
    The \emph{weight} of a polymer $\fp$ is $\omega(\fp) = \E[\phi_\fp]$, where $\phi_\fp = 2^{-\N(\fp)}$.
    We remind the reader that $\N(\fp)$ denotes the (random) number of vertices neighboring $\fp$
    in the percolated graph $\Qp$.

    \item
    We define \emph{clusters} and their weights as in the previous section, which is a general construction that
    works for all polymer models.
    The set of clusters will be denoted by $\cC^\cH$.
\end{itemize}
title: Language relating to polymer models from \cite{ks}

body:
[Corollary 17 (Global well-posedness for the periodic SBE) of arXiv:2608.29726, '\LARGE A Priori Estimates for Singular Fractional Stochastic Burgers Equations'] Let \((\gamma,\alpha)=(2,0)\), let \(u_0\in L^2(\T)\) have zero spatial
mean, and let \(\mathbb X_{0,2}\) be the canonical periodic Burgers
enhancement.  Then the canonical stochastic Burgers equation
\[
 (\partial_t-\partial_x^2)u
 =\partial_x(u\diamond u)+\partial_x\xi,
 \qquad u(0)=u_0,
\]
admits, almost surely, a unique global paracontrolled solution in the sense of
\cite{GubinelliPerkowski2017KPZReloaded}.  On every finite interval it has
the representation
\[
 u=X+\Xone+\ell+Jm^\Psi,
\]
where
\[
 m\in L^\infty_tL^1\cap L^\infty_tL^2\cap L^2_tH^1,
 \qquad
 m\in L^3_tB^s_{3,3}\quad\text{for every }0<s<\frac12.
\]
Moreover, for every \(\eps_n\downarrow0\) and every sequence of smooth,
mean-zero initial data \(u_0^n\to u_0\) strongly in \(L^2\), the full
canonical mollified solution sequence converges to \(u\) in probability in
the local solution topology of
\cite[Theorem~3.7]{GubinelliPerkowski2017KPZReloaded} on each finite interval.

[Corollary corollaryofthelcd of arXiv:2504.15992, 'Repeated singular values of a random symmetric matrix and decoupled singular value estimat'] Let $X,Y$ be uniformly sampled from an $(N,N_1,\kappa,\kappa',D_1,D_2,D_3)$ box pair with $N\geq N_1\geq 2$, and let $\alpha>0$ satisfy $\alpha d\geq 4,2^{16}B^2\kappa'Nd^{-1/2}/\alpha \leq 3^d$. Let $t_1=N^{-1}$ and $t_2=N_1^{-1}$. Then whenever $\log N$ is small enough relative to $\alpha$ in the sense that
$
\sqrt{\alpha c_0^2n/8}\geq (\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{\nu p}}+\frac{256\sqrt{2}B^2}{\sqrt{c_0}})\sqrt{\log_+\frac{c_{\rho,\delta}^2c_0^42^{-11}N}{\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{\nu p}}+\frac{256\sqrt{2}B^2}{\sqrt{c_0}}}}
$, the following probability estimate holds true: 
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{P}_{X,Y}(\operatorname{LCD}&^\mathbf{t}_{\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{\nu p}}+\frac{256\sqrt{2}B^2}{\sqrt{c_0}},c_{\rho,\delta}^2c_0^42^{-16}}(r_nX_D,r_nY_D)\leq 2^{11}B^2, \\&|\sin(X_D,Y_D)|\geq c_{\rho,\delta}^2c_0^2/128)\leq (10^{12}\alpha(2+\frac{4\kappa'}{\kappa})^2)^{d/4},
\end{aligned}$$
where we take $r_n=\frac{c_0}{32\sqrt{n}}$ and in the probability we take an intersection with the event where the lower bound on $|\sin(X_D,Y_D)|$ holds. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2609.01166, 'Nonparametric inference for density-dependent McKean--Vlasov diffusions'] Suppose that the assumptions of Lemma~\ref{lem:dnn} hold, and let \(\xi_m\), \(m\geq m_0\geq 1\), be the corresponding graded approximant. Define \(G_m(r)=g_{\xi_m}(r)-g_{\Xi_0}(r)\) 
and let \(\rho_t=(1-t)\rho_{\Xi_0}+t\rho_{\xi_m}\) and \(\xi_t(r)=(r\rho_t(r))^{-1}\) for \(0\leq t\leq1\). Finally, let \(\Pi_t\) be the stationary law for \(\xi_t\). Then it holds that
\begin{equation}
 \norm{G_m}_{\infty,[0,U]} =o(1), \quad
 \sup_{0\leq t\leq1}\norm{G_m}_{L^2(\nu_t)} \leq C_{\mathrm{path}} m^{-(\beta+1)},
\end{equation}
and, consequently, given~\eqref{eq:app_fwd}, 
\(\KL(\pi_0\Vert\pi_{\xi_m}) \leq C_{\mathrm{KL}} m^{-2(\beta+1)}\).
Here  
\(C_{\mathrm{path}},C_{\mathrm{KL}}\) are constants depending on \(\kappa\), K, as well as 
\(C_{\mathrm{app}},
C_{\mathrm{fwd}}\)
from Lemma~\ref{lem:dnn}, and independent of \(m\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 6 of arXiv:2512.08745, 'Variance strikes back: sub-game--perfect Nash equilibria in time‑inconsistent $N$‑player g'] Let {\rm\Cref{assumpDPP_NplayerGame}.\ref{Glip_NplayerGame}} and {\rm\Cref{assumption:borelMeasurability_Lip}} hold. Let $(\Y^N,\Z^N,\M^{\star,N},\N^{\star,N},\Z^{m,\star,N},\Z^{n,\star,N})$ be a solution to the following system of {\rm BSDEs}
\begin{align}
\notag Y^{i,N}_t &= g^i\big(X^i_{\cdot \land T}, L^N(\X^N_{\cdot \land T})\big) + G^i\big(\varphi^i_1(X^i_{\cdot \land T}),\varphi^i_2\big(L^N(\X^N_{\cdot \land T})\big)\big) \\
\notag &\quad+ \int_t^T f^i_s\big(X^i_{\cdot \land s},L^N(\X^N_{\cdot \land s},\hat\balpha^N_s),\hat\alpha^{i,N}_s\big) \d s - \int_t^T \partial^2_{m,n}G^i\big(M^{i,\star,N}_s,N^{i,\star,N}_s\big) \sum_{\ell =1}^N Z^{i,m,\ell,\star,N}_s \cdot Z^{i,n,\ell,\star,N}_s \d s \\
\notag &\quad- \frac{1}{2} \int_t^T \Bigg(\partial^2_{m,m}G^i\big(M^{i,\star,N}_s,N^{i,\star,N}_s\big) \sum_{\ell =1}^N \big\|Z^{i,m,\ell,\star,N}_s\big\|^2 +\partial^2_{n,n}G^i\big(M^{i,\star,N}_s,N^{i,\star,N}_s\big) \sum_{\ell=1}^N \big\|Z^{i,n,\ell,\star,N}_s\big\|^2 \Bigg)\d s \\
\notag &\quad- \int_t^T \sum_{\ell = 1}^N Z^{i,\ell,N}_s \cdot \d \big(W_s^{\hat\balpha^\smalltext{N},N}\big)^\ell, \; t \in [0,T], \; \P \text{\rm--a.s.}, \\
\notag M^{i,\star,N}_t &= \varphi^i_1(X^i_{\cdot \land T}) - \int_t^T \sum_{\ell =1}^N Z^{i,m,\ell,\star,N}_s \cdot \d \big(W_s^{\hat\balpha^\smalltext{N},N}\big)^\ell, \; t \in [0,T], \; \P \text{\rm--a.s.}, \\
\notag N^{i,\star,N}_t &= \varphi^i_2\big(L^N\big(\X^N_{\cdot \land T}\big)\big) - \int_t^T \sum_{\ell=1}^N Z^{i,m,\ell,\star,N}_s \cdot \d \big(W_s^{\hat\balpha^\smalltext{N},N}\big)^\ell, \; t \in [0,T], \; \P \text{\rm--a.s.} \\
\notag \hat\balpha^N_t &\coloneqq \mathfrak{a}^N\big(t,\X^N_{\cdot \land t},\Z^N_t,\M^{\star,N}_t,\N^{\star,N}_t,\Z^{m,\star,N}_t,\Z^{n,\star,N}_t\big),  \\
\frac{\d \P^{\hat\balpha^\smalltext{N},N}}{\d \P} &\coloneqq \cE\Bigg( \int_0^\cdot \sum_{\ell =1}^N b^\ell_t\big(X^\ell_{\cdot \land t},L^N\big(\X^N_{\cdot \land t},\hat\balpha^N_t\big),\hat\alpha^{\ell,N}_t\big) \cdot \d W^\ell_t \Bigg)_T.
\end{align}
In addition, for each $i \in \{1,\ldots,N\}$, there exists $p \geq 1$ such that 
\begin{align}
\notag &\sup_{\balpha \in \cA^\smalltext{N}_\smalltext{N}} \E^{\P^{\smalltext{\balpha}}} \Bigg[ \sup_{t \in [0,T]} \big|Y^{i,N}_t\big|^p + \bigg(\int_0^T \sum_{\ell =1}^N \big\|{Z}_t^{i,\ell,N}\big\|^2 \d t\bigg)^\frac{p}{2} \Bigg] \\
&+\esssup_{\balpha \in \cA^\smalltext{N}_\smalltext{N}} \Bigg\{\sup_{t \in [0,T]} \Big\{ \big| M^{i,\star,N}_t\big| + \big| N^{i,\star,N}_t \big| \Big\} + \sup_{\tau \in \cT_{0,T}} \E^{\P^{\smalltext{\balpha}\smalltext{,}\smalltext{N}\smalltext{,}\smalltext{\tau}}_{\smalltext{\cdot}}} \Bigg[ \int_\tau^T \sum_{\ell =1}^N \Big( \big\|Z^{i,m,\ell,\star,N}_t\big\|^2 + \big\|Z^{i,n,\ell,\star,N}_t\big\|^2 \Big) \d t \Bigg] \Bigg\} <+ \infty.
\end{align}
Consequently, it holds that $\hat\balpha^N \in \mathcal{N}\!\mathcal{A}_{s,N}$, and for any player index $i \in \{1,\ldots,N\}$, $J^i(t,\cdot,\hat\alpha_t^{i,N};\hat\balpha_t^{N,\smallertext{-}i}) = Y^{i,N}_t$, $\P\text{\rm--a.s.}$, for every $t\in [0,T]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2604.26026, 'Stochastic Ordering of Dependent Systems under Transformation Models and Archimedean Copul'] Let $m \ge 1$, let $g:\mathbb{R}\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}$ be $m$ times differentiable, and $h_1,\dots,h_m>0$. Define the iterated forward difference operator by
\[
\Delta_{h_1,\dots,h_m} g(a) :=	(\Delta_{h_m}\circ\cdots\circ\Delta_{h_1})g(a), \qquad	\Delta_h g(a):=g(a+h)-g(a).
\]
Then the following identities hold:
\begin{align}
\Delta_{h_1,\dots,h_m} g(a) &=
   \sum_{L\subseteq\{1,\dots,m\}} (-1)^{m-|L|}\, g\left(a+\sum_{r\in L} h_r\right),  \\[1.5ex]
\Delta_{h_1,\dots,h_m} g(a) &=
   \int_0^{h_1}\cdots\int_0^{h_m} g^{(m)}(a+u_1+\cdots+u_m)\,du_1\cdots du_m. 
\end{align}

$M,k,d,r_2,|D_K|$, such that for every $\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_k>0$ there is a

|\mathcal D|
\le
C_5

\|y_i\|_\infty\le M\nu_i

(Thm 1.4) Let X_1,...,X_n be independent random vectors in R^d, M(.) the essential supremum of the density, and Z_1,...,Z_n independent, Z_i uniform on an origin-symmetric Euclidean ball with M(Z_i) = M(X_i) (Z_i = 0 if M(X_i) = infinity). Then M((T \otimes I_d)X) <= M((T \otimes I_d)Z) for every linear map T: R^n -> R^k. For d = 1: every k-dimensional linear image of a vector with independent coordinates has maximal density at most that of the same image of independent centred uniforms with the same maxima. (Thm 1.1) For P a projection onto a k-dimensional subspace, M((P \otimes I_d)X) <= c(d,k) prod M(X_i)^{gamma_i}, gamma_i in [0,1], sum gamma_i = k, with c(1,k) = min{2^{k/2}, (n/(n-k))^{(n-k)/2}}. For d >= 2: M(sum X_i)^{-2/d} >= Gamma(1+d/2)^{2/d}/(1+d/2) sum M(X_i)^{-2/d}.

[Theorem punique of arXiv:2412.02777, 'How to quantify the coherence of a set of beliefs'] Given a credence base $(\mathtt E, \boldsymbol q)$ and a loss function $L$ of the form in ((eqn:lossfunction of the paper)), if there exists a coherent $\boldsymbol p\in C(\mathtt E)$ such that $L(\boldsymbol p, \boldsymbol q)$ is finite, then there exists a unique $\boldsymbol {p^*}$ such that

body:
Every nontrivial semantic property of programs is undecidable. Precisely: let P be any set of partial computable functions that is nontrivial, meaning some partial computable function belongs to P and some does not. Then the index set {encodings of Turing machines M : the partial function computed by M belongs to P} is undecidable. 'Semantic' is essential: the property must depend only on the function computed, not on the machine's text (syntactic properties such as 'has fewer than 100 states' are decidable). Only the two trivial semantic properties (satisfied by all machines, or by none) have decidable index sets. Examples of undecidable questions: does M compute the everywhere-zero function; does M halt on the empty input; is the language accepted by M empty, finite, or regular.
P is a set of partial computable functions
P is nontrivial: neither empty nor all partial computable functions

Reduce halting: given a pair (M, w), effectively construct a machine N(M, w) that on input x behaves as follows - first it simulates M on w, ignoring x; if and when that simulation halts, it runs M_f on x and returns that result. If M halts on w, then N(M, w) computes exactly f, which is in P. If M does not halt on w, then N(M, w) halts on no input, so it computes the nowhere-defined function, which is not in P. The map (M, w) -> N(M, w) is computable. A decider for the index set of P applied to N(M, w) would therefore decide whether M halts on w, contradicting the undecidability of the halting problem. [Corollary 11 of arXiv:2608.19744, 'Conditioned Brownian motion and local equivalence of path ensembles'] Let $X$ be the CIR process above, take
$A_T=\int_0^T \de s \, X_s$
and fix $0<\theta<\eta$.  With $r_{\beta_\theta}=\frac{\kappa\eta}{\theta}$ and $\beta_\theta
      =\frac{\kappa^2}{2\sigma^2}
        \left(\frac{\eta^2}{\theta^2}-1\right)$,
put
\[
    I_x^{\mathrm{CIR}}(\theta)
      =\frac{\kappa^2(\eta-\theta)^2}{2\sigma^2\theta},
    \qquad
    v_\theta
      =\frac{\sigma^2\theta^3}{\kappa^2\eta^2}.
\]
Then, for every fixed $x>0$ and $z\in\mathbb R$,
\[
\begin{split}
    \bbP_x^{\mathrm{CIR}}(A_T\leq\theta T+z)
    \sim{}&
    \frac{1}{\beta_\theta\sqrt{2\pi v_\theta T}}
    \left(
       \frac{2r_{\beta_\theta}}
            {\kappa+r_{\beta_\theta}}
    \right)^\alpha
    \exp\!\left(
       -\frac{(r_{\beta_\theta}-\kappa)x}{\sigma^2}
    \right)
    \exp\!\left(
       -I_x^{\mathrm{CIR}}(\theta)T+\beta_\theta z
    \right).
\end{split}
\]
On every fixed time interval, the conditioned process converges in total
variation to the CIR process
\[
    \de Y_t
      =r_{\beta_\theta}(\theta-Y_t)\,\de t
       +\sigma\sqrt{Y_t}\,\de B_t,
    \qquad Y_0=x.
\]
Its invariant law is Gamma with shape $\alpha$ and mean $\theta$.

body:
[Corollary 20 of arXiv:2609.01473, 'Keller sequences of exact $\infty$-categories'] Let $i\colon \cal{A} \hookrightarrow \cal{C}$ be a right-special inclusion and $\cal{E}$ some $\infty$-category which admits small colimits. 
Then the square
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep = 50pt]
\cal{A} \ar[r,"i"]\ar[d,"j_{\cal{A}}"'] & \cal{C} \ar[d,"j_{\cal{C}}"] \\
\pst(\cal{A}) \ar[r,"\pst(i)"] & \pst(\cal{C}) 
\end{tikzcd}
\]
satisfies the following Beck-Chevalley properties:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*]
\item
For every functor $\vphi\colon \C \to \cal{E}$ the Beck-Chevalley transformation
\[ (j_{\cal{A}})_!i^*\vphi \Rightarrow \pst(i)^*(j_{\cal{C}})_!\vphi  \]
is an equivalence, where $(-)^*$ denotes restriction and $(-)_!$ left Kan extension.
\item
For every presheaf $\vphi\colon \pst(\cal{A})^{\op} \to \cal{E}$ the Beck-Chevalley transformation
\[ i_!j_{\cal{A}}^*\vphi \Rightarrow j_{\cal{C}}^*\pst(i)_!\vphi \]
is an equivalence, where by abuse of notation we denoted by $(-)^*$ and $(-)_!$ also restriction and left Kan extension of presheaves.
\end{enumerate}

&=O(e^{-\frac{c_1}{2} L} ),\notag 
\end{align}

\noindent 
uniformly in $x_0\in \mathbb{T}_{L}$ and $\theta \in [0,2\pi]$, where $g_L(x)=L^{-\frac 12}g(L^{-1}x)$.

    <\infty.
    \end{eqnarray*}

[Theorem 2 (B\^ocher theorem for $-\Delta+(-\Delta)^s$) of arXiv:2609.01403, '2609.01403'] Let $B_1\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, and $s\in(0,1)$. Assume
$u\in\mathcal L^{2s}(\mathbb R^n)$ satisfies $u\ge0$ a.e. in $B_1$ and
\[
    \mathscr{L}_su+cu\ge0
    \qquad
    \text{in }\mathcal D'(B_1\setminus\{0\}),
\]
where $c\in L^\infty(B_1)$. Then there exist $a\ge0$ and a nonnegative
Radon measure $\mu$ in $B_1$, with $\mu(\{0\})=0$, such that
\[
    \mathscr{L}_su+cu
    =
    \mu+a\delta_0
    \qquad
    \text{in }\mathcal D'(B_1).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: B\^ocher theorem for $-\Delta+(-\Delta)^s$

body:
[Cor 6 of arXiv:2511.18861, 'Correlation Decay for Maximum Weight Matchings on Sparse Graphs'] Let $(G_n)$ be a sequence of random graphs and  let $(G_n,o_n)$ converge locally weakly to $(G,o)$ where $o_n$ is  chosen uniformly from $V(G_n)$. Assume  that 
$\sup_n \E \tfrac{|E(G_n)|}{| V(G_n)|} < \infty$ and $\E|w_e|^p<\infty$ for some $p>1$. Further assume that, almost surely under the law of $(G,o)$, the limit graph $G$ satisfies the correlation decay assumption. Then
	\[
	\lim_{n\to\infty} \E \frac{\W_{G_n}}{|V(G_n)|} = \frac{1}{2}\E \left[ \sum_{v: v\sim o}w_{(ov)} \mathbf{1}_{\{(ov) \in \M_G\}} \right],
	\]
    and 
    \[
	\lim_{n\to\infty} \E \frac{|\M_{G_n}|}{|V(G_n)|} = \frac{1}{2}\E \left[ \sum_{v: v\sim o}\mathbf{1}_{\{(ov) \in \M_G\}} \right],
	\]
    where $|\M_{G_n}|$ is the number of edges in the matching $\M_{G_n}$ and the expectation $\E$ is taken over both the randomness in the graph and the edge weights. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor 6 of arXiv:2511.18861

[Lemma lem:two-cross-lower of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Let $\kappa_1,\kappa_2\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, and fix $M_i,R_i>0$ for
$i=1,2$.  Let $K$ be a nonempty compact subset of
$\Lambda_2(D)$ and let
$\theta>0$.  Then there exist $\delta_{\rm cross},\varepsilon_{\rm cross},C>0$,
depending only on
\[
  D,K,\theta,|\kappa_1|,|\kappa_2|,M_1,M_2,R_1,R_2,
\]
such that the following holds.

Suppose that
$0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_{\rm cross}$,
\[
  f_i\in\mathscr R_{\varepsilon,|\kappa_i|,M_i,R_i}(D),
  \qquad \mathbf b_i\in\mathsf C(f_i), \qquad i=1,2,
\]
$(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)\in K$, and
\[
  \mathcal D(f_1)+\mathcal D(f_2)\leq\delta_{\rm cross}.
\]
\nopagebreak[4]
Then the cross interaction satisfies
\nopagebreak[4]
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal I(f_1,f_2)
  \geq|\kappa_1\kappa_2|G(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)
  -\theta[\mathcal D(f_1)+\mathcal D(f_2)]-C\varepsilon.
\end{equation}

such that 
\begin{itemize}[nosep]

every subgraph $S'\subset\mathcal{G}_{n,p}$
with $v(S')=v(S)$ has an $(S,F)$-extension  
in $\mathcal{G}_{n,p}$ (where  $V(S')$
is ordered by the natural order of the integers).

body:
[Lemma 9 (Wick index count for products of traces) of arXiv:2608.04824, 'Strong Convergence for a General Class of Random Matrix Models'] Fix \(h\geq1\) and \(p_1,\ldots,p_h\geq0\).  Expand
\[
 \prod_{a=1}^h\trn_{qn}G_n^{p_a}
\]
using the independent real Ginibre representation from the proof of
Proposition~\ref{prop:gaussian-limit}.  Consider a monomial containing
\(2e\) centered Gaussian matrix entries and a Wick pairing whose covariance
factors are nonzero.  After all covariance identifications, let \(v\) be the
number of free \(n\)-indices.  Then
\begin{equation}
 v\leq e+h.
\end{equation}
Consequently, the contribution of every fixed nonzero pairing to the product
of normalized traces is \(O(1)\), uniformly in \(n\).

Assume that there are $\alpha_1, \alpha_2 \in (0,1)$ such that $\tilde{\beta}(\mu) \ge \alpha_1$ and that there is some interdependence matrix $J$ such that $\lvert J \rvert_\mathrm{op} \le 1 - \alpha_2$.

\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Lemma le:cle_sle_domain_markov of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] Suppose that $\eta$ is an ${\rm SLE}_\kappa$ in $\mathbf{H}$ from $0$ to $\infty$ and (given $\eta$) $\Gamma$ is a ${\rm CLE}_{\kappa'}$ in the component of $\mathbf{H} \setminus \eta$ to the left of $\eta$. Let $W \subseteq \overline{\mathbf{H}}$ be a connected, relatively open set that intersects~$\mathbf{R}_-$, and let $\widetilde{W} \subseteq W$ be the union of connected components of $W \setminus \eta$ that intersect $\mathbf{R}_-$. Let $\Gamma(\widetilde{W})$ be the the collection of loops in $\Gamma$ that intersect $\widetilde{W}$. Let $\widetilde{\eta}$ denote the outer boundary of the union of loops in $\Gamma(\widetilde{W})$ (as seen from $1$, say). Given $\widetilde\eta$ and the set $\widetilde\eta \cap \eta$, pick two points $\eta(\tau), \eta(\sigma) \in \widetilde\eta \cap \eta \setminus \overline{W}$ such that $\eta((\tau,\sigma))$ is a connected component of $\eta \setminus \widetilde{\eta}$. Let $U$ be the component of $\mathbf{H} \setminus (\widetilde{\eta} \cup \eta)$ with $\eta((\tau,\sigma))$ on its right boundary, let $\widetilde{U}$ the component of $\mathbf{H} \setminus (\widetilde{\eta} \cup \eta([0,\tau]) \cup \eta([\sigma,\infty)))$ containing $\eta((\tau,\sigma))$, and let $\Gamma_U$ be the loops of $\Gamma$ that are contained in $\overline{U}$. Then the conditional law of $\eta|_{[\tau,\sigma]}$ given $\Gamma \setminus \Gamma_U$ and $\eta_{[0,\tau]}$, $\eta|_{[\sigma,\infty)}$ is that of an ${\rm SLE}_\kappa$ in $\widetilde{U}$ from $\eta(\tau)$ to $\eta(\sigma)$ and the conditional law of $\Gamma_U$ given $\Gamma \setminus \Gamma_U$ and $\eta$ is that of a ${\rm CLE}_{\kappa'}$ in $U$.

Let G in R^{m x n}, g in R^m and h in R^n have mutually independent standard Gaussian entries. Let S_x in R^n and S_y in R^m be nonempty compact sets and psi:S_x x S_y -> R continuous and deterministic. Define Phi(G)=min_x max_y [y^T G x+psi(x,y)] and phi(g,h)=min_x max_y [||x||_2 g^T y+||y||_2 h^T x+psi(x,y)]. Then for every c in R, P(Phi<c)<=2P(phi<=c). If additionally S_x,S_y are convex and psi is convex in x and concave in y, then for every deterministic mu in R and t>0, P(|Phi-mu|>t)<=2P(|phi-mu|>=t). The offset need not be Gaussian. A random offset may be conditioned on only when the Gaussian matrix and auxiliary vectors retain their stated independent Gaussian laws conditionally.
Nonempty compact index sets
Continuous deterministic offset
Independent standard Gaussian matrix and auxiliary vectors
For the two-sided comparison: compact convex sets and a convex-concave offset

\begin{equation}
\sup_{\pmark,\qmark\in \vmarkspace}\int_{\emarkspace}|G(\pmark,\qmark,\rmark)|^2\emarklaw(\dd \rmark)<\infty.

For any admissible probability measure $\mu$ on $\vmarkspace\times \cC_d$, we use the

$$
\Lambda_\mu(t,\pmark,x)=\int_{\vmarkspace\times \cC_d} \int_{\emarkspace\times \cC_1}

\mu(\dd \qmark,\dd y).
$$

[Definition 7 (Supermartingale $C$-monotonicity.) of arXiv:2603.27940, '\Large \bf Stability of supermartingale optimal transport problems'] The Borel set $\Gamma \subset \R \times \Pc_1$ is supermartingale $C$-monotone if and only if there exists $M_0, M_1 \subset \R$, such that for any $N \in \N$, any collection $(x_1, p_1), \cdots, (x_N, p_N) \in \Gamma$ and $q_1, \cdots q_N \in \Pc_1$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^{N} p_i = \sum_{i=1}^{N} q_i$ and 
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \int_{\R} y p_i(dy)= \int_{\R} y q_i(dy), \ \ \forall i \in \mathcal{I}_1; \\
& \int_{\R} y p_i(dy) \geq \int_{\R} y q_i(dy), \ \ \forall i \in \mathcal{I}_0,
\end{aligned}
$$
 we have
 $$
 \sum_{i=1}^N C(x_i, p_i) \leq  \sum_{i=1}^N C(x_i, q_i).
 $$
where, $\mathcal{I}_0=\{i : x_i \in M_0 \}$, $\mathcal{I}_1=\{i : x_i \in M_1 \}$. In the following, we say a coupling $\pi \in \Pi_S(\mu, \nu)$ is Supermartingale $C$-monotone if there exists a Supermartingale $C$-monotone set $\Gamma$ with 
$$
(x, \pi_x) \in \Gamma \ \ \mbox{for } \mu(dx) \mbox{-almost every }x,
$$ 
with $M_0, M_1$ defined as the martingale region of $\pi$ to the left and right of $x^*$ (recall that $x^*$ is defined in Section \ref{sec:irreducible})  {In addition, a probability measure $\P \in \Pc(\R \times \Pc_1$, which is supported on a martingale $C$-monotone set, is called supermartingale $C$-monotone. }
title: Supermartingale $C$-monotonicity.

body:
[Theorem 12 of arXiv:2608.26038, 'Rotated semicircle laws for permanental roots of Gaussian random matrices'] For the Gaussian weight \(w(x)=e^{-x^2/4}\), the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=2em]
\item
\begin{equation}
  \lim_{N\to\infty}t_N(w)^{1/N}=e^{-F_w}=e^{-1/2}.
\end{equation}

\item
Let \(M_N\) be a sequence of monic complex polynomials of exact degree
\(N\).  If
\begin{equation}
  \lim_{N\to\infty}\|w^NM_N\|_{\R}^{1/N}=e^{-1/2},
\end{equation}
then
\[
  \nu_{M_N}\weak\mu_{\mathrm{sc}}.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 12 of arXiv:2608.26038

body:
[Lemma prelim of arXiv:2608.12056, 'Deviation inequalities for U-processes of growing order, with applications to half-space d'] There exist absolute constants $c,C>0$ with the following properties. Assume that $\frac{\max(t,d)m}{N}\leq c$. Then 
\[
\hat \delta \leq C\sqrt{\frac{\max(d,t)}{N}}
\]
with probability at least $1-e^{-t}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma prelim of arXiv:2608.12056

[Proposition 2 of arXiv:2606.11389, 'Instability of a nonlinear oscillator with small friction and small additive noise'] For the system \eqref{add eps} and for all $(x_0,y_0,v_0)$ with $v_0 \neq 0$ the limit
      $$
       \lambda(\e^2 \beta,\e \sigma,1,1) = \lim_{t \to \infty} \frac{1}{t} \log \|v_t\|
      $$
exists almost surely and has the value

     \lambda(\e^2 \beta,\e \sigma,1,1) = \int \widetilde{Q}_\e(x,y,\theta)d\nu_\e(x,y,\theta)

body:
[Proposition 40 of arXiv:2607.10486, 'Weak martingale solutions to stochastic Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system with transport '] Assume that $(\Omega, \mathscr{F}, \mathbb{F},\mathbb{P})$ is a probability space satisfying the usual conditions and that    
$(\bu_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence of $\mathbb{F}$-adapted, $\mO$-valued continuous processes.
This sequence  satisfies the  \textbf{Aldous-Rebolledo} condition in the space $\mO$ if and only if the following condition is satisfied. \\
\item[\textbf{[A]}]
For every $\eps>0$, $\eta>0$, there exists a $\zeta \in (0,1]$  and $n_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for  every sequence $(\tau_n)_{n=1}^\infty$ of $[0,T]$-valued  stopping times,
          \begin{equation}
             \sup_{n \geq n_0} \sup_{ \vartheta \in [0,\zeta]} \mathbb{P} \left( \Vert \bu_n(\tau_n+\vartheta)-\bu_n(\tau_n) \Vert_{\mO} \geq \eta\right) \leq \eps.
         \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 40 of arXiv:2607.10486

[Lemma Wiener-intervals of arXiv:2505.04942, '\textbf{Randomized Routing to Remote Queues}'] Let $ \{\check{B}(t) : t \geq 0 \} $ be a standard Brownian motion and $ f: \mathbb{R}_{+} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}_{+} $ a nondecreasing function such that $ 0 < f(t) \leq t $ and $ f(t)/t $ is nonincreasing for $ t > 0 $. Then with probability 1,
	\[
	\limsup_{T \to \infty} \sup_{0 \leq t \leq T - f(T)} \sup_{0 < u \leq f(T)} \frac{|\check{B}(t+u) - \check{B}(t)|}{\sqrt{2f(T)(\log T - \log f(T) + \log\log T)}} = 1.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Thm 3 of arXiv:2607.06242, 'Exponential mixing and Freidlin--Wentzell large deviation principle for Markov cocycles'] Assume that the coefficients of either \eqref{e.intro.ns} or \eqref{e.intro.sg} satisfy the mild integrability, boundedness, and determining mode controllability conditions stated in Section~\ref{s.060701} or Section~\ref{s.060702}. Then the associated Markov cocycle admits a unique stationary family $\{\mu_\sigma\}_{\sigma\in\Sigma}$, and this family attracts transition probabilities exponentially both in pullback and forward time. Moreover, for the small noise stationary family $\{\mu_\sigma^\varepsilon\}_{\varepsilon\in(0,1]}$, the Freidlin--Wentzell upper bound holds: for $m$-a.e. $\sigma\in\Sigma$ and every closed set $F$ in the corresponding phase space, 
 \[ \limsup_{\varepsilon\to0} \varepsilon\log\mu_\sigma^\varepsilon(F) \leq -\inf_{u\in F}E_{\mathcal A(\sigma)}(u), \] 
 where $E_{\mathcal A(\sigma)}$ is the pullback quasipotential associated with the deterministic limiting equation. If, in addition, the deterministic pullback attractor is a random point, then the matching lower bound holds: for every open set $G$ in the phase space, 
 \[ \liminf_{\varepsilon\to0} \varepsilon\log\mu_\sigma^\varepsilon(G) \geq -\inf_{u\in G}E_{\mathcal A(\sigma)}(u). \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 3 of arXiv:2607.06242

body:
[Definition def:ribbon-majorant of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Fix a ribbon record $\Gamma$, a circuit state $\tau$, and a designated
set $\mathcal E$ of factored endpoint or packet resources.  Expand every
remaining coefficient component in its circuit-anchored projective
presentation and insert every prescribed fixed gate before closing the
original circuit bases.  Define $\mathfrak a_{\Gamma,\tau;\mathcal E}$
to be $|\omega_\Gamma|$ times the sum of the absolute scalar
coefficients multiplied by all remaining positive projective and
trace-class costs.  No endpoint weight or debit in $\mathcal E$ is
included.  In the monomer--dimer applications of (sec:moments of the paper), the
fixed recurrence scalar $(-\gamma)^a$ is also declared a factored
resource: it is not one of the ``scalar coefficients'' in this
definition and is restored exactly once by the resource ledger.
Local fold, transport, and projective-presentation coefficients do remain
inside the majorant.  When $\tau$ and $\mathcal E$ are clear we write
$\mathfrak a_\Gamma$; subscripts such as
$\mathfrak a_{\Gamma,\mathcal C}$ name the part of the record left open.

This is a positive presentation cost, not the possibly cancelling value
of an open contraction.  Consequently it dominates every compatible
partial trace-class contraction obtained from the same atoms.  The
operator-norm estimate needed for the Kac root-open specialization is the
separate, proved statement (lem:root-open-sinfty of the paper); it is not built
into this definition and no replica factorization is assumed.  The later
allocation argument specifies
which carriers are left bare and proves the corresponding Euler bound;
no second copy of this majorant is introduced there.
title: Positive ribbon majorant

[Lemma lem:bottle-events-pair-jammed of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix $\lambda \in (0,1/2)$. Let $\overline{p}$ be a send sequence with $p_0=1$. 
Let $i$ be a sufficiently large integer

Fix a non-negative integer~$\tau$. 
Let $\overline{z}\in (\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0})^j$ be a $j$-tuple such that, for all $x\in [j]$, $z_x \geq \lambda W_x/4$. 
Let $Y^A$ and $Y^B$ be independent
$j$-jammed processes with send sequence~$\overline{p}$, start time~$\tau$, birth rate~$\lambda$, and initial population size distribution~$\mathsf{Po}(\overline{z})$. 
Let $T = \tau + i \lceil  \exp((\log i)^{2/3} ) \rceil$.
Then $\mathbb{P}(
\mathcal{E}^{Y^A,\mathcal{N}}_{\leq T} \cap \mathcal{E}^{Y^B,\mathcal{N}}_{\leq T} \cap 
\mathcal{E}^{Y^A,\mathbf{s}}_{\leq T} \cap \mathcal{E}^{Y^B,\mathbf{s}}_{\leq T}
) \geq W_i^{-1/6}$.

  \]
  is an isomorphism of schemes.

[Thm 16 (Main Formula) of arXiv:2609.00974, 'On Algebraic Integrability\\ of Vector Fields \\ with Rational Function Coefficients\\ tha'] Let $k$ be a perfect field. Let $K= k(x)$.
    Let $f\in K$ be a nonzero element.
    Let $PFD(\frac{1}{f})=P+L+H$ be its partial fraction decomposition (over $\overline{k}$), see Theorem \ref{thm: PFD}.

    Let $e$ be the degree of $P$. Let $M$ be the highest order of pole in $H$. Let $p$ be a prime number such that $p-1>e$ and $p>M-1$.

    Let $D=f\frac{\partial}{\partial x}$.
    Then we have that
    \begin{equation}
        D^p= \mu D \hspace{1 cm} \text{, where } \mu=f^p\overline{L}=\frac{\overline{L}}{P^p+L^p+H^p}\in K^p
    \end{equation}
    and $\overline{L}=\sum_{i=1}^d \frac{c_i}{x_i^p-a_i^p}$ if ${L}=\sum_{i=1}^d \frac{c_i}{x_i-a_i}$.

body:
[Lemma lem : Topology/RegPD/HW_cvg/KeyLemma of arXiv:2412.03320, 'Large deviation principle at speed $n$ for the random metric in first-passage percolation'] Let $\gamma : \intervalleff0T \rightarrow X$ be a continuous path and $X_0\subseteq X$ be a compact set. There exists a countable family $\p{\intervalleff{s_p}{t_p}}_{p\ge 1}$ of pairwise disjoint segments of $\intervalleff0T$ such that

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Tightness via a Dirichlet-form argument and identification through conformal covariance. Result: The discrete process is a reversible diffusion with respect to the Liouville measure of the regularised field, with Dirichlet form (1/2) integral |grad f|^2 dx (the Dirichlet form is field-independent, only the speed measure depends on the field). Mosco convergence of the speed measures (the Liouville measures converge) gives convergence of the time-changed Brownian motion, i.e. the marginal law of X converges to Liouville Brownian motion; the joint law with the field converges by the same construction because the time change is a measurable functional of the field. But the process in Problem 16.13 is not the time-changed Brownian motion: it has a drift beta grad h_eps (Langevin), whose limit as eps -> 0 is a distribution and not a function, so the drift term does not converge as a process; the joint limit must be defined through an Ito-type renormalisation of the drift, as for the Liouville Brownian motion with drift. I could not find a formulation of the renormalised drift that is closable in eps; the Dirichlet-form route only gives the drift-free limit. Obstruction: The Langevin drift beta grad h_eps diverges; the problem needs a renormalisation scheme which the notes do not specify.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0013-existence-of-the-liouville-langevin-motion-as-a-joint-scaling-limit

body:
Let X = (X_1, ..., X_n) have independent coordinates with finite ranges, f a real function of X, and f = sum over S of f_S its Hoeffding (ANOVA) decomposition over subsets S of {1, ..., n}: f_S depends only on X_S, f_empty = E f, and E[f_S | X_T] = 0 unless S is inside T. Put w_S = E[f_S^2] and W_k = sum over |S| = k of w_S, the variance at interaction order k. Let T_p be a random set, independent of X, containing each coordinate independently with probability p in [0, 1], and J(p) = E over T_p of Var(E[f | X_{T_p}]). Then J(p) = sum over nonempty S of p^|S| w_S = sum_{k=1}^n p^k W_k. Hence J^(k)(0) = k! W_k >= 0 for every k, J(0) = 0, J(1) = Var(f), and J is nondecreasing and convex on [0, 1].

f real valued

[Prop primi_1 of arXiv:2607.10105, 'The four-dimensional Anderson model: a case study for critical SPDEs'] Fix $1\leq n\lesssim|\log\varepsilon|$, and functions $G_j(z)\in\mathcal E$ satisfying $|G_j(z)|\leq |z|^{-2}$ for $1\leq j\leq 2n-1$. Consider the following expression
\begin{equation}\mathcal J_{2n,\mathrm{prim}}(z-w):=\lambda_\varepsilon^{2n}\sum_{\kappa}\int_{(\mathbb T^4)^{2n-2}}\prod_{j=1}^{2n-1}G_j(x_j-x_{j+1})\prod_{\{i,j\}\in\kappa}\eta_\varepsilon(x_i-x_j)\,\mathrm{d}x_2\cdots\mathrm{d}x_{2n-1},
\end{equation} where $x_1:=z$ and $x_{2n}:=w$, and $\kappa$ runs over all \emph{primitive} full pairings of $[1,2n]$. Then the function $\mathcal J_{2n,\mathrm{prim}}(z)\in\mathcal E$, and satisfies the following estimate
\begin{equation}|\mathcal J_{2n,\mathrm{prim}}(z)|\leq(C\lambda)^{2n}\bigg(\frac{\varepsilon^{-4}}{|\log\varepsilon|}\cdot|z|^{-2}\mathbf{1}_{|z|\lesssim\varepsilon}+\frac{1}{|\log\varepsilon|^2}\cdot(|z|^2+\varepsilon^2)^{-3}\bigg).
\end{equation}
Moreover, if we change $\mathcal J_{2n,\mathrm{prim}}$ into $\widetilde{\mathcal J}_{2n,\mathrm{prim}}$ by inserting an additional factor $\varepsilon^2+\max_{i,j}|x_i-x_j|^2$ in the integrand in ((eq.primi_1 of the paper)), then we have
\begin{equation}|\widetilde{\mathcal J}_{2n,\mathrm{prim}}(z)|\leq(C\lambda)^{2n}\bigg(\frac{\varepsilon^{-2}}{|\log\varepsilon|}\cdot|z|^{-2}\mathbf{1}_{|z|\lesssim\varepsilon}+\frac{1}{|\log\varepsilon|^2}\cdot(|z|^2+\varepsilon^2)^{-2}\bigg).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In statistics, the Neyman–Pearson lemma describes the existence and uniqueness of the likelihood ratio as a uniformly most powerful test in certain contexts. It was introduced by Jerzy Neyman and Egon Pearson in a paper in 1933. The Neyman–Pearson lemma is part of the Neyman–Pearson theory of statistical testing, which introduced concepts such as errors of the second kind, power function, and inductive behavior. The previous Fisherian theory of significance testing postulated only one hypothesis. By introducing a competing hypothesis, the Neyman–Pearsonian flavor of statistical testing allows investigating the two types of errors. The trivial cases where one always rejects or fails to reject the null hypothesis are of little interest but it does prove that one must not relinquish control over one type of error while calibrating the other. Neyman and Pearson accordingly proceeded to restrict their attention to the class of all level tests while subsequently minimizing type II error, traditionally denoted by .
title: Neyman–Pearson lemma

[Definition 16 of arXiv:2608.29075, 'The 2-Monoidal Structure of Symmetric Sequences'] Let $(\catname{C},\square, I, \circ, J)$ be a 2-monoidal category. A \textit{bimonoid} in $\catname{C}$ is a quintuple $(H,\mu,\iota,\Delta,\epsilon)$ where $(H,\mu,\iota)$ is a monoid in $(\C,\square,I)$, $(H,\Delta,\epsilon)$ is a comonoid in $(\C,\circ,J)$, and the two structures are compatible in the sense that the following four diagrams commute.
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{(H \circ H)\square (H \circ H)} && {(H\square H)\circ (H \square H)} \\
	{H \square H} & H & {H \circ H}
	\arrow["{\zeta_{H,H,H,H}}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{\mu \circ \mu}", from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{\Delta \square \Delta}", from=2-1, to=1-1]
	\arrow["\mu"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["\Delta"', from=2-2, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}\]
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{H \square H} & {J \square J} && I & H \\
	H & J && {I \circ I} & {H \circ H}
	\arrow["{\epsilon \square \epsilon}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["\mu"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{\mu_J}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["\iota", from=1-4, to=1-5]
	\arrow["{\Delta_I}"', from=1-4, to=2-4]
	\arrow["\Delta", from=1-5, to=2-5]
	\arrow["\epsilon"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\iota \circ \iota}"', from=2-4, to=2-5]
\end{tikzcd}\]
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	& H \\
	I && J
	\arrow["\epsilon", from=1-2, to=2-3]
	\arrow["\iota", from=2-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{\iota_J = \epsilon_I}"', from=2-1, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}\]
    A morphism of bimonoids is a morphism of the underlying monoids and comonoids. 
    
    The category of bimonoids in $(\catname{C},\square, I, \circ, J)$ is denoted by $\text{Bimon}(\catname{C},\square, I, \circ, J)$.
title: Definition 16 of arXiv:2608.29075

body:
If a solution of the heat equation attains its maximum over $\overline{U_T}$ at an interior point $(x_0,t_0)\in U_T$, the conclusion is that $u$ is constant on $\overline U\times[0,t_0]$ -- the past of $t_0$ -- and nothing at all is claimed for $t>t_0$. Heat is not time-reversible, and the mean value property over heat balls only looks backwards. Counterexample: on $U=(0,\pi)$, $T=2$, let $h(t)=1$ for $t\le1$ and $h(t)=1-e^{-1/(t-1)}$ for $t>1$ (smooth, $h\le1$, $h<1$ for $t>1$), and let $u$ be the solution of $u_t=u_{xx}$ with $u(\cdot,0)\equiv1$ and $u(0,t)=u(\pi,t)=h(t)$. On $[0,1]$, $u\equiv1$ by uniqueness; the weak maximum principle gives $\max_{\overline{U_T}}u=1$, attained at the interior point $(\pi/2,1)\in U_T$; but for $t>1$, $u$ is not constant (its boundary values are $<1$ while, by continuity, $u$ stays near $1$ in the middle). So constancy holds exactly up to $t_0=1$ and fails afterwards. A second load-bearing hypothesis is connectedness of $U$: for $U=(0,1)\cup(2,3)$ the solution equal to $1$ on the first component and to $e^{-\lambda_1t}\phi_1$ on the second attains its maximum at an interior point of the first component and is not constant on $U$. Finally, the interior maximum must be attained in $U_T$, i.e. at a point with $x_0\in U$: a maximum on the lateral boundary says nothing about constancy (that is the Hopf lemma's domain, which asserts instead that the outward normal derivative is strictly positive there).
Conclusion is constancy on the closure of U x [0,t_0] only
U must be connected
The maximum must be attained at a point with x_0 in U and t_0 > 0
title: Pitfall: The Strong Maximum Principle gives constancy only in the past, and needs a connected domain

[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2608.11071, 'Scaling Laws for Majority-based Opinion Dynamics in the Presence of Stubborn Agents'] Fix $(\gamma_0, \gamma_1)\in \Gamma_{\text{crit}}^k$. The two possibilities are $\gamma_0=\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_0\neq\gamma_1$. For $\gamma_0=\gamma_1$, let $r$ be the unique root of $\Delta_k$ in $\mc S$ with multiplicity three and for $\gamma_0\neq\gamma_1$, let $r$ denote the root of $\Delta_k$ in $\mc S$ with multiplicity one. The following statements hold.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item If $\gamma_0 \neq \gamma_1$, then, for each sufficiently small $\delta>0$ and $x\in \mc S^n$, we have $\EE_{x}[T_{\text{enter}}^n(B_{\delta}(r))]= O(n^{1/3})$, and the mixing time of the process $X^n$ satisfies $t_{\text{mix}}^n =\Theta(n^{1/3})$.
        \item If $\gamma_0=\gamma_1$, then for any $x \in \mc S^n$, we have $\EE_x[T^n_{\text{enter}}(B_{1/n}(r))]= O(n^{1/2})$ and the mixing time of the process $X^n$ satisfies $t_{\text{mix}}^n =\Theta(n^{1/2})$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 2 of arXiv:2609.02703, 'A choice-free proof of the Erd\"os--Dushnik--Miller theorem'] Let $\langle P,\prec\rangle$ be a well-founded poset each of whose levels is finite.
Then there exists ${\prec_\omega}\subseteq{\prec}$ such that $\langle P,\prec_\omega\rangle$
is a gapless well-founded poset and $\rk_\prec(q)=\rk_{\prec_\omega}(q)$ for all $q\in P$.

\[
p\prec'q\iff p\prec q\wedge\forall\gamma(\rk_\prec(p)<\gamma<\rk_\prec(q)\rightarrow\exists r(p\prec r\prec q\wedge\rk_\prec(r)=\gamma)).
\]
Clearly, $\langle P,\prec'\rangle$ is a well-founded poset. We claim that, for all $q\in P$,
\begin{equation}
\rk_\prec(q)=\rk_{\prec'}(q).
\end{equation}

We prove \eqref{S003} by $\prec$-induction on $q$. Assume inductively that $\rk_\prec(p)=\rk_{\prec'}(p)$ for every $p\prec q$.

body:
Load-bearing hypothesis: in any uniqueness statement for u_t + H(Du) = 0 the solution must be a VISCOSITY solution (equivalently, for convex superlinear H, a Lipschitz a.e. solution satisfying the one-sided semiconcavity estimate). Satisfying the equation at almost every point plus the initial condition is far too weak. Counterexample (n = 1): H(p) = p^2, initial datum g ≡ 0. Both u ≡ 0 and v(x,t) := min(0, |x| - t) are Lipschitz on R × [0,∞), vanish at t = 0, and satisfy v_t + v_x^2 = 0 at every point of differentiability: for |x| < t one has v = |x| - t, v_t = -1, v_x = ±1; for |x| > t one has v ≡ 0. Only u ≡ 0 is the viscosity solution (it is also what the Hopf-Lax formula gives, since L(q) = q^2/4 and min_y ( |x-y|^2/(4t) ) = 0). Why v fails: at a point (0,t) with t > 0, v has a local minimum in x with a convex kink, so φ ≡ v(0,t) + c(t'-t) touches from below with φ_x = 0, φ_t = -1, and the supersolution inequality φ_t + φ_x^2 ≥ 0 reads -1 ≥ 0. Equivalently v violates semiconcavity: v(z,t) - 2v(0,t) + v(-z,t) = 2|z|, which is not O(|z|^2). Auditor's check: whenever a proof concludes 'u is the solution' from 'u is Lipschitz and solves the PDE a.e.', the argument is incomplete unless viscosity, semiconcavity, or a variational (Hopf-Lax) representation is verified.
The counterexample uses H(p) = p^2 (smooth, uniformly convex) and zero data, so no exotic Hamiltonian is needed
'Solution a.e.' means Lipschitz plus the equation at points of differentiability
Uniqueness is restored by the viscosity property or, equivalently for convex superlinear H, by the semiconcavity bound of the Hopf-Lax solution
title: Pitfall: Uniqueness for Hamilton-Jacobi Needs the Viscosity (or Semiconcavity) Condition, Not Just 'Solves a.e.'

[Proposition 21 of arXiv:2608.30752, '2608.30752'] The following statements hold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item
Assume that \(u_0:\Sigma\to(S,h)\) is an orientation-preserving 
covering map, and let \(Y=(\Sigma,u_0^*h)\) be the unique minimizing point
of the varying-domain energy. Let \(X_t\in\mathcal T(\Sigma)\), \(t\geq0\),
be any unit-speed Teichm\"uller ray and put
\(d_0=d_{\mathrm T}(X_0,Y)\). Then
there exists constant $A_{Y}$ and
\begin{equation}
  \frac{\eta_Y}{2}e^{-2d_0}e^{2t}
  \leq E_{u_0}(X_t)
  \leq A_Ye^{2d_0}e^{2t}
  \qquad (t\geq0).
  
\end{equation}
Consequently, \(E_{u_0}(X_t)\asymp e^{2t}\) and
\(\log E_{u_0}(X_t)=2t+O(1)\). If \(X_0=Y\), one may omit the factors
\(e^{\pm2d_0}\) in \eqref{eq:varying-domain-energy-ray-growth}.

\item
Assume that the varying-target energy \(\mathcal E_{u_0}\) satisfies the
filling hypothesis with filling system
\(\Gamma=\{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_N\}\). Let
\(q\in\mathcal Q^1(X_0)\) be Jenkins--Strebel and let
\(X_t=\gamma_q(t)\), \(t\geq0\), be the associated unit-speed ray. Define
\(\Theta(q,\Gamma)=\sum_{j=1}^N(\sum_{r=1}^m
i(\delta_r,\alpha_j))^2\). Then \(\Theta(q,\Gamma)>0\), and
there exist constants
$A_{\mathfrak F}$ and
$B_{\mathfrak F}$ such that
\begin{equation}
  16
  A_{\mathfrak F}\,
  \Theta(q,\Gamma)
  \leq \frac{\mathcal E_{u_0}(X_t)}{t^2}
  \leq 16
  B_{\mathfrak F}
  \,
  \Theta(q,\Gamma)
    \qquad (t\geq0).

\end{equation}
Consequently, \(\mathcal E_{u_0}(X_t)\asymp t^2\) and
\(\log\mathcal E_{u_0}(X_t)=2\log t+O(1)\).
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2604.22644, '2604.22644'] For $k \in \{1, 2, \dots, N-1\}$, let
$$G(k;p) = E\left[\left. \sum_{t=0}^{\tau_0 \wedge \tau_N - 1} I(X_t = k) \right| X_0 = 1, Z_1 = p \right].$$
Then $G(k;p)$ is given by:
$$    G(k;p) = \frac{S(N;p) - S(k;p)}{W(k;p) S(N;p)},
$$
where $S(k;p)$ is the scale function defined in Theorem \ref{thm1}, and $W(k;p)$ is defined as follows:
$$    W(k;p) = r^k p \prod_{j=1}^k \frac{1 - r^j p}{r^j p}.$$

[Definition 39 (Levi-Civita connections and associated differential operators) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] \hfill

\begin{enumerate}
\item We denote the Levi-Civita connection of $\gfour$ by $\Dfour$. 
\item We denote the Levi-Civita connection of $\gtorus$ by $\newangD$. In particular,
	for $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent tensorfields $\upxi$, we have $\newangD \upxi = \smoothtorusproject \Dfour \upxi$.
\item If $\upxi$ is an $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent one-form, then we define its $\ell_{t,u}$-divergence 
	to be the scalar function
	$\angdiv \upxi \eqdef \mytr_{\gtorus} \angD \upxi =  (\gtorus^{-1})^{AB}\cdot \newangD_A \upxi_B$. Similarly, if $Y$ is an $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent vectorfield, 
	then we define its $\ell_{t,u}$-divergence to be the scalar function $\angdiv Y \eqdef \gtorus^{-1} \cdot \newangD Y_{\flat}$.
	where $Y_{\flat}$ is the $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent one-form that is $\gfour$-dual to $Y$.
\item If $\upxi$ is an $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent one-form, we define its $\ell_{t,u}$-curl to be the scalar function given by $\in^{AB} \angD_A \upxi_B$, where $\in_{AB}$ are the components of the area form element of the Riemannian manifold $(\ell_{t,u},\gtorus)$ relative to an arbitrary frame $e_A$, $A = 2,3$.
\item If $\upxi$ is a symmetric type $\binom{0}{2}$ $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent tensorfield, 
	then we define its $\ell_{t,u}$-divergence 
	to be the $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent one-form with the following $\ell_{t,u}$-components for $A=2,3$:
	$(\angdiv \upxi)_A \eqdef (\gtorus^{-1})^{BC} \cdot \newangDarg{B} \upxi_{CA}$. 
\item We denote the covariant wave operator of $\gfour$ by $\Box_{\gfour} \eqdef \gfour^{-1}\cdot\Dfour^2
	= (\gfour^{-1})^{\alpha \beta} \Dfour_{\alpha} \Dfour_{\beta}
$. 
\item We denote the angular Hessian and angular Laplacian on $\ell_{t,u}$ associated to $\gtorus$ by $\angD^2$ and 
$\angLap \eqdef \gtorus^{-1} \cdot \newangD^2
=
(\gtorus^{-1})^{AB} \angDarg{A} \angDarg{B}
$, respectively.
\end{enumerate}
title: Levi-Civita connections and associated differential operators

For any $\lambda >0$,  $f\in \mathscr{S}_0^\lambda$ and $\gamma>0$,

and a random variable

body: [Definition def-markov-kernel of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] Suppose $(\Omega, \mathcal{F})$ and $(\Omega', \mathcal{F}')$ are measurable spaces. A function $\Lambda: \Omega \times \mathcal{F}' \to [0,1]$ is a \emph{Markov kernel} if $\Lambda(\omega, \cdot)$ is a probability measure on $(\Omega', \mathcal{F}')$ for each $\omega \in \Omega$, and $\Lambda(\cdot, A)$ is $\mathcal{F}$-measurable for each $A \in \mathcal{F}'$. If $\mu$ is some measure on $(\Omega, \mathcal{F})$ and $(X,Y)$ is a sample from $\Lambda(x, dy) \mu(dx)$, we say the \emph{conditional law} of $Y$ given $X$ is $\Lambda(X, \cdot)$.
title: Definition def-markov-kernel of arXiv:2411.19810

[Proposition 9 of arXiv:2608.08242, 'Bang--bang representation of $3\times 3$ embeddable stochastic matrices'] Each of the regions $R_n$, $\T$, $\V$, and $\NH$ is invariant under
transposition. For $A>0$, one has $A\in\V$ if and only if, for some
$B\in\T$, $i\neq j$, and $t>0$,
\[
A\sim BX_{ij}(t),
\]
and this is also equivalent to
\[
A\sim X_{ij}(t)B.
\]
Likewise, $A\in\NH$ if and only if $A\notin\T\cup\V$ and, for some
$B\in\V$, $i\neq j$, and $t>0$,
\[
A\sim BX_{ij}(t),
\]
equivalently, $A\sim X_{ij}(t)B$.

Convention $\hat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}dx$. (a) If $f\in L^1(\mathbb R^d)$ and $x_jf\in L^1(\mathbb R^d)$, then $\partial_{\xi_j}\hat f$ exists everywhere, is continuous, and equals the transform of $-2\pi i x_jf$. Iterating: if $|x|^kf\in L^1$ then $\hat f\in C^k$. (b) If $f\in C^1(\mathbb R^d)$, $f\in L^1$ and $\partial_jf\in L^1$, then $\widehat{\partial_jf}(\xi)=2\pi i\xi_j\hat f(\xi)$. Iterating: if $f\in C^k$ and $\partial^\alpha f\in L^1$ for all $|\alpha|\le k$, then $|\hat f(\xi)|\le C_{d,k}\big(\sum_{|\alpha|\le k}\|\partial^\alpha f\|_1\big)(1+|\xi|)^{-k}$, and by the Riemann-Lebesgue lemma $\hat f(\xi)=o(|\xi|^{-k})$. Slogan: decay of $f$ gives smoothness of $\hat f$, smoothness of $f$ gives decay of $\hat f$.
(a): f and x_j f are Lebesgue integrable on R^d
(b): f is continuously differentiable, and f and its partial derivative d_j f are Lebesgue integrable on R^d
for the k-fold decay bound: f in C^k with every d^alpha f integrable, |alpha| <= k

body:
[Definition def:RBG of arXiv:2510.13733, 'Internal Diffusion Limited Aggregation \\ with Critical Branching Random Walks'] Let $R_1 < R_2$ be two integer numbers,
set  $H = R_2 - R_1$. 
Let $\eta : \mathbb{Z}^d \to  \mathbb{N}$
be the initial particle configuration
with support in $\partial B_{R_1}$
and number of particles $N_1 = \sum_{z \in 
\partial B_{R_1}} \eta(z)$. 
Let further $Z_1, \ldots Z_{N_1}$ be i.i.d.\  random variables with distribution 
 supported in   $ \{1, \ldots,  H\} $  given by
\begin{equation}
P( Z_i = h) = \frac{ h^{d-1} }{\sum_{r =1 }^H  r^{d-1}},
\end{equation}
The $\{ Z_i\}$ represent the sequence of heights at which the BRWs will probe the space for settlement. 

The RBG consists of a discrete time
Markov chain  $(A_t)_{t \in \mathbb{N}}$
and a sequence of random variables 
$(  \tilde G_t,  \tilde R_t)_{  t \in \mathbb{N}_0  }$,
 defined as follows. 
We set $A_0 =  \emptyset$ 
and label the particles in $\eta$ with integers from $1$ to $N_1$ in some arbitrary order. 
At each step $t \in \{1, \ldots, N_1\}$, 
we start, from the $t$-th particle of $\eta$, an independent BRW
stopped on $\partial B_{ R_1 + Z_t  }$ 
and let $\xi_t$ be the configuration of pioneers  on $\partial B_{ R_1 + Z_t  }$.
We define the aggregate of the step $t$ as 
the union of the aggregate of the step $t-1$ and 
the support of the  pioneers configuration,  namely 
$$
A_t := A_{t-1} \cup \{ z \in \partial  B_{ R_1 + Z_t  } \, \, : \,   \xi_t(z) > 0     \}.
$$
After that we proceed as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)]
For each particle reaching $\partial B_{ R_1 + Z_t  }$ within 
$A_{t-1}$ we start an independent critical branching random walk stopped on
$\partial B_{ R_2  }$  and call $\tilde{G}_t$ the total number of pioneers 
on $\partial B_{ R_2  }$, which we dub \textit{green particles}.
\item[(b)]  
For each vertex 
 $ x \in \partial  B_{ R_1 + Z_t  } \setminus A_{t-1}$
 with $\xi_t(x)>0$,
 we let exactly one of the $\xi_t(x)$ particles at $x$ settle
 and  start 
 $(\xi_t(x) - 1) \1_{ \{ \xi_t(x)>0 \}  }$
  independent critical branching random walks
 stopped on $ B_{ R_2  }$ from $x$, 
 namely one critical Branching Random Walk from each particle which has not settled at $x$. 
 We call $\tilde{R}_t$ 
 be the total number of pioneers on $\partial B_{ R_2  }$,
 which we dub \textit{red particles}.
\end{enumerate}
We then move to the step $t+1$ and iterate the procedure
up to reaching $t = N_1$.
title: \textbf{Random Barrier Growth}

[Corollary 10 of arXiv:2608.29736, '2608.29736'] Let $(M^n,\omega)$ be a compact K\"ahler manifold of complex
 dimension $n\geq 2$. Let $\chi$ be another K\"ahler form.  Suppose that the $J$-semistable condition ~\eqref{topintegralnonnegative}--~\eqref{$J$-semistablecondition} holds. Then the set 
 \[
\operatorname{Dest}_{n-1}(\chi,\omega)
:=
\bigcup_{\substack{
Z\subsetneq M\ \mathrm{irreducible}\\
\dim Z= n-1,\; \int_ZF_{n-1}(\chi)=0
}}Z
\]
is an analytic subvariety of $M$. And there exists a uniform constant $\delta>0$ independent of the prime divisors, such that for any prime divisor $Y$  satisfying $\int_{Y} F_{n-1}(\chi)>0$, we have 
$$\int_{Y} F_{n-1}(\chi)\geq \delta\int_{Y}\omega^{n-1}.$$
title: Corollary 10 of arXiv:2608.29736

[Theorem 33 of arXiv:2605.03236, 'Stochastic It\^o Equations and Parabolic Second-Order Equations with singular Drift'] Let $\{\Pi_{x}\}$ satisfy condition 1)
and let $\xi^{0}_{\infty}[P,\omega]$
be $\{\Pi_{x}\}$-admissible. Also suppose that
for any $x\in E,P\in\Pi_{x}$, $\tau\in\frT$, $f\in C_{0}$, and $\alpha\geq0$ we have
$$
E^{P}|\xi^{\tau}_{\infty}[P]|<\infty,
$$
$$
E^{P}\Big\{\alpha\xi^{\tau}_{\infty}[P]
+\theta_{\tau}\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-t}f(x_{t})\,dt
\mid \frM_{\tau}\Big\}\leq w_{\alpha}(f,x_{\tau})
\quad P-(a.s.),
$$
$$
E^{P}\Big\{\alpha\xi^{0}_{\tau}[P]
+ \int_{0}^{\tau}e^{-t}f(x_{t})\,dt
+e^{-\tau}w_{\alpha}(f,x_{\tau})\Big\}\leq w_{\alpha}(f,x),
$$
where
$$
w_{\alpha}(f,x):=\sup_{P\in\Pi_{x}}E^{P}
\Big\{\alpha\xi^{\tau}_{\infty}[P]
+ \int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-t}f(x_{t})\,dt\Big\}
$$
(we will see that $w_{\alpha}(f,\cdot)\in\bB(E)$).

Then the system
$$
\big\{P\in\Pi_{x}: E^{P}\xi^{0}_{\infty}[P]
=\sup_{P\in\Pi_{x}}E^{P}\xi^{0}_{\infty}[P]\big\}
$$
is Markovian relative to $(\frT,\frM_{t})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Defn of arXiv:2606.24385, 'Gradient Mean-Field Dynamics with Measure-Valued States: Well-Posedness, Chaos, and Long-T'] Let $E$ be a generic Banach space, and denote by $\mathscr{B}(E)$ the Borel $\sigma$-field of $E$. A probability measure $\gamma$ on $(E,\mathscr{B}(E))$ is said to be Gaussian if $\gamma \circ f^{-1}$ is Gaussian measure in ${\mathbb R}$ for every $f\in E^{\ast}$ (the topological dual space of $E$ of linear and continuous functionals $f:E\rightarrow {\mathbb R}$). The measure is called centered (or symmetric) if all the measures $\gamma\circ f^{-1}$ are centered.

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2605.13512, '2605.13512'] (Hydrodynamic limit)
 For any $n \in \N$, let $z^n$ evolve using a field of independent Poisson processes $\{N^{(n)}_{i,j}\}_{(i,j) \in \Z^2}$ with rates $\{\lambda^n_{i,j}\}_{(i,j) \in \Z^2}$ given by 
\[
        \lambda^n_{i,j}=\tilde c(i/n,j/n)
        = c((i+j)/n,j/n),
\]
and let $\tilde c$ satisfy Assumption \ref{ass:pde-speed}.
Assume \eqref{eq:etaass}, \eqref{eq:in-cur} and \eqref{eq:z0lim} where the limits are assumed either ${\bf P}-$ a.s.~or in ${\bf P}-$probability. 

Then for any $x \in \bR$ and $t \in \bR_+$ we have the existence of a function $v(x,t)$ such that the limit 
\be 
\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n} z^{n}_{\fl{nx}}(nt) = v(x,t) 
\ee
holds in the same mode of convergence as for $t=0$, i.e. ${\bf P}-$ a.s.~or in ${\bf P}-$probability. 

Moreover, $v(x,t )$ satisfies the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item $v(x,t)$ is Lipschitz-1 in the $x$-variable.
\item  $v(x,t)$ is locally Lipschitz, jointly in $(x,t)$. 
\item $v(x,t)$ is differentiable in both $x$ and $t$ for a.e.\ $(x,t)$. 
\end{enumerate}
The a.e. $x$-derivative $\rho(x,t)$ is the density profile for the particle system, as given by the LLN
\be 
\lim_{n\to \infty} \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i = \fl{na}}^{\fl{nb}} \eta^n_i(nt) = \int_{a}^b \rho(x,t) \, dx.
\ee (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 4 of arXiv:2605.13512

Let (X_{n, k})_{1 \le k \le k_n, n \ge 1} be a triangular array of row-wise independent random variables. Let S_n = \sum_{k=1}^{k_n} X_{n, k}. For any truncation level b_n > 0, define Y_{n, k} = X_{n, k} \mathbf{1}_{\{|X_{n, k}| \le b_n\}}. If: (1) \sum_{k=1}^{k_n} \mathbb{P}(|X_{n, k}| > b_n) \to 0; and (2) b_n^{-2} \sum_{k=1}^{k_n} \text{Var}(Y_{n, k}) \to 0 as n \to \infty, then \frac{S_n - a_n}{b_n} \xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}} 0, where a_n = \sum_{k=1}^{k_n} \mathbb{E}[Y_{n, k}].

[Satz thm:partialLSITails of arXiv:2507.08692, 'Some notes on higher order concentration of measure'] Let $\mu$ be a measure on a product of finite sets satisfying a $\mathfrak{d}\mathrm{-LSI}(\sigma^2)$, and let $f \in L^\infty(\mu)$.
	\begin{enumerate}
	        \item Assuming that $\norm{\mathfrak{h}^{(j)} f}_{\mathrm{op},1} \le 1$ for all $j=1,\ldots,d-1$ and $\norm{\mathfrak{h}^{(d)} f}_{\mathrm{op},\infty} \le 1$, it holds that
	        \[
	        {\mathbb E} \exp\Big\{c |f(X)|^{2/d} \Big\} \le 2,
	        \]
	        where a possible choice of the constant $c$ is given by
	        \[
	        c = \frac{(\sqrt{2}-1)^2}{16 \kappa e}.
	        \]
	        \item For any $t\ge 0$, it holds that
	        \[
	        {\mathbb P}(|f(X)| \ge t)\le
	        2 \exp\Big\{- \frac{C}{d^2} \min\Big(\min_{j=1, \ldots,d-1} \Big(\frac{t}{\norm{\mathfrak{h}^{(j)} f}_{\mathrm{op},1}}\Big)^{2/j}, \Big(\frac{t}{\norm{\mathfrak{h}^{(d)} f}_{\mathrm{op},\infty}}\Big)^{2/d}\Big)\Big\},
	        \]
	        where a possible choice of the constant $C$ is given by
	    	\[
	    	C = \frac{\log(2)}{4 \kappa e^2} > \frac{1}{34}.
	    	\]
	 \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
